Very nice, staff has treated us with respect and dishes were very nice and even and good. Not best restaurant in the Nyc, but it has pleased my group very much and I will certainly eat again at this establishment.

This place is super adorable and has great food. Definitely recommend the poikilia as as starter but for some reason the hostesses that work there from the both times I have dined there and multiple times speaking to them on the phone, I am pretty certain that they hate their jobs and people (just fyi).

Definitely this is a pretty cheap place to eat. Â The food is good and it comes out quick. Â I had to try the duck sesame pancake sandwich, delicious. Â It is a must. Â Its only 3 dollars too! Come on! A STEAL!

This place is SO adorable! The interior was dimly lit and there was a beautiful chandelier in the middle of the restaurant. I really liked the atmosphere, they had party music playing pretty loud, but not to the point where it would be difficult to hold a conversation. We ordered the Pad Thai, Spicy Basil Noodle, Pumpkin Curry, a lychee mojito, and a pitcher of sangria. The mojito was a bit too sweet, but I liked the sangria a lot. All of our entrees were good, I can't pick out a favorite since they were all pretty different, but overall I was pleased with my meal. Service here was also quick, waited about 10 minutes for our food to come out. 4 stars for the great ambiance, service, and food. Would definitely come back.

A small, very quaint pizza place with a lot of "swag." A Jay-Z and Beyonce special, Lucali helps makes itself a sought after place of eatery. Open from only 6 pm . on, Lucali creates its own swag by becoming somewhat exclusive as its small venue and limited hours make for an extended wait even if arriving when the doors open. Although the wait is almost guaranteed to be at least an hour, they do take your number, which allows for you to do other things while you wait. Lucali also has a "bring-your-own-drink" Â policy which can be a good use of your waiting time as you go and purchase the accompanied dinner beverage. The venue itself, aside from being small, is everything you could want from a New York eatery-grungy, rustic, while also being very modern and upscale. Regarding, specifically Italian cuisine, Lucali gets it right. The place just feels like a carbon copy of what you would imagine getting a piece of pie from an early 1900's Italian establishment would look like. Even the waiters appear Italian. Food wise, I was disappointed. Not because of the food necessary, but because the rave reviews were almost too much to hold up to. All organic ingredients, and literally made "right before your eyes," the pizza cannot be more fresh. However, with that, it is hot, thin, and ultimately a somewhat runny pizza. The crust has a slight crunch, which is nice, but it is also kind of bland by itself. However, if you ask for a side of sauce, your waiter will bring you a nice spread of additional cilantro, mozzarella, and tomato sauce that helps assuage concerns about the pizza being too "bland." The side is also graciously free. In saying that, the pizza themselves are more on the pricey side with their basic running $24 and an additional $2-3 per topping after that. I did not get the calzone, but hear great things In conclusion, if you are looking for a high-end pizza establishment with a lot of notoriety, Lucali is your spot. If you like quality, organic ingredients, Lucali is where you want to be. If you don't mind paying around $25 per pizza, Lucali is your place. However, if you want a thicker, cheaper, pizza without the wait, as heralded as Lucali is, you might want to "go on to the next."

I have been trying the various Ramen noodle places in manhattan. Went to Totto ramen based on the reviews here. Waited for a couple of hours outside, but I thought- well I am sure it is worth it. Turned out to the worst of the many Ramen places I have been- left my bowl half-empty and left. Broth was non-descript. Still cannot figure how this place got 4 stars and the wait. Momofuku still reigns at the top of my list with Ippudo close behind. In terms of just the broth- Momo is hands down the best.

As a Venezuelan I can tell you this is one of the best spots for Venezuelan food in NYC. Tasty food, good portions, reasonable price. Try the cachapas, arepas (all are delicious), the empanadas, chicha, tres con leches for dessert. The main plates are good also! Oh and they do awesome traditional breakfast (brunch) too!! And don't forget to put that green sauce (guasacaca) everywhere! Its soo damn good. None of the friends I brought here left disappointed. I always come back with more friends! My only wish was that they had a bigger space.

Sunny afternoon. Chilled sangria. Corn. Veggie dog. Quesadillas slathered in canned jalapenos. Solar-powered. Truly a Brooklyn afternoon. My favorite place to sit in the sun and drink, people-watch, hear good music and watch some more.

Eataly is a great place. The restaurants in Eataly are awesome. The pasta was definitely worth it. Eataly is a place to check out. I went there with my boyfriend to get a bite to eat. Eataly is worth checking out.

This menu is really interesting to me as a Korean person because a lot of the items are fairly traditional, with one or two tweaks here and there. The names of the items are interesting though... like their "gnocchi" is really just ddukbokki and their "affogato" is really just patbingsu/shaved ice. It's not a bad thing but it was just amusing... Anyway, the galbi jjim is delicious. The flavors are somewhat traditional but the presentation is creative. The meat is so tender it literally just falls apart... it's kind of experience. It's that good. The Korean chicken wings are good but nothing special. I was hoping for something a little more extravagant (and a little more sauce) but these are basically the same as what you'd get at Bonchon or Kyochon. The kimchi pancake was good and bad. It had tons of kimchi in it which was good, but it fell apart really easily which made it kind of hard to eat. If you make a reservation it could be your lucky day -- they let you spin this wheel (think wheel of fortune) and you can win a glass of sangria, beer, kimchi, fries, etc. So if you remember.. make a res on opentable before you go! We had half of the restaurant to ourselves so the service was great. Friendly and competent staff. Would definitely go back if I'm in the area.

Super Taste is famed for their spicy beef noodle and the fact that they make their own noodles here. The main difference is they are hand-pulled noodles, but machine cut. In case you're wondering why every strand is so perfectly symmetrical. Service is your typical Chinatown service. A little loud and a little obnoxious. Â I came here with some friends and surprise surprise, despite them walking in first and asking for the table the lady looked right over them to me. Yup they were white. We had a good laugh about it, but hey that's Chinatown for you. Â It's a cheap meal and their beef noodle was delicious. The spice isn't the insane burn your tongue spice. It's more the lingering tingling that builds and builds as you continue with your meal. The portion is generous and it makes for a good no-nonsense meal.

Pepe Giallo to me has always been one of the best kept secrets in New York City for Italian. Amazing food, wonderful atmosphere, and prices that are incredibly reasonable. I couldn't give recommend this place highly enough. Go there and you'll see where I'm coming from

Thoroughly enjoyed dinner at the restaurant. The food and service were great and the atmosphere was the perfect level of casual with a noise level that was acceptable given the location. The modern interior decor, elegant with high vaulted ceilings, great lighting, and comfortable seating was marvelous and made me a happy camper instantly.
Twin Tartare, mussels with lemongrass, Angels on Horseback. All good. Watch out, it gets super busy on weekend nights. Expect to wait.

The food is certainly good, but what makes this place solidly 4 star is the fact that (unlike loads of good restaurants in the West Village) it is blessedly quiet... there is no loud music, as a result fewer people shout, and you can actually have a proper conversation with your friends. The black pasta was delicious.
Fries are good but falafel / rest could be better.
Bad service, average food. Two visits confirmed this.

Located in EV, Minca's a small place and a bit hard to find. But the narrow seating and quick service do make it feel like a legit ramen place. I've been to this place twice already and I wasn't really satisfied both time I went. First time I got the toroniku ramen, which is like pork broth with slowly cooked meat. The soup itself is kinda greasy and salty but one good thing is they put a lot of lettuce in there so it balances out. But the meat again is also really fat and greasy..I finished the entire thing and I felt kinda gross..But the overall taste and texture of the noodle is pretty good. If you are a meat person and are super hungry then I recommend getting this! Second time I went I got the basic (shio) pork broth with extra cha-shu and thin noodle because I was super hungry haha. Again he soup came out really thick, which I do like, but it's still a bit on the greasy and salty side. Maybe it's because I got the extra cha-shu.. I would've only given a three-star based on my two experiences. But since the overall taste is still pretty good, and the restaurant just have that authentic feel of Japanese ramen place, I decided to give it one more shot next time. I will prob get the shoyu or miso based chicken broth ramen, or even the spicy one.

I'm actually rate this place 3 1/2 but since there are no half ratings, I'm giving it 4 stars. I have been to Carmine's a couple of times. To summarize, its great for groups, reasonably priced, they serve decent and generous portions. The waiters are friendly but often very busy, but this really didnt bother us. I did have to wait a little while to get water from our waitress the last time I came here which was last night. But overall, not much to complain about.

The corn crab chowder was AMAZING. & we loved their signature dish, the Cioppino, as the broth was the perfect compliment to the seafood. Our food came out quickly, but we were never rushed. It's BYOB and our waiter came by frequently to refill our glasses. It's almost like having a catered dinner party when you have already purchased the alcohol. Â The staff is expert and friendly. We will defiantly be back ........ Merci Beaucoop Petite Crevette!

Solid ramen! As a ramen-goer in New York, I don't mind taking my friends to Totto ramen (especially out-of-towners who might not appreciate the 2-hour wait at Ippudo or the late-night hours of that midtown japanese-restaurant-turned-ramen-show-at-night locale). Be warned that there will however, on most days, still be a wait. My only gripe -- the chicken ramen broth is not as consistent as the other broths; I've had the pork and miso ramen a few times and have never been disappointed. Some days the chicken ramen is fine and other days it has that odd off-scent that sometimes chicken broth can have. Some of my friends have theorized that this comes from using older chickens instead of younger ones, but what do I know about poultry science? Overall, very solid ramen. Will definitely continue returning here in the future!

This place was strange to me. I went there without so much of an opinion and I left from there with a pleasant feeling. I would not say this place is my favorite here in the city but if ever somebody wanted advice on new things to try out: This would be my go-to restaurant! The environment over there is just super friendly, chilled and cosy. I ended up there with friends and it was hard for us to describe the premise we entered: It's a mix a south american food with a hispter-ish ambiance and in a wooden decor. Strange but really enjoyable combination! I'm not gonna give you the details of what I ate so I can focus more on what was a genuine revelation: The spicy beef jerky! You're probably thinking "That french guy must be going crazy", and you would probably be right. But what a foodgasm!

LOVE this place! Great pizza, decent prices, love love love. I love bringing my friends and family to Lombardi's. I've never had a bad experience here. I don't know why everyone else is complaining about having to wait forever for a table. Yeah, waiting sucks, but this is LOMBARDI'S, this place is famous. It's worth the wait in my opinion. If you don't want to wait, go to Olive Garden.
Great place for a quick cheap meal! The buffet bar is great, but only available during certain hours. It gets really crowded during lunch and dinner hours, also on weekend late nights.
Shame on them for charging 25 cents for chutney.

I went back and had the porkchop. It was like a taste explosion!!! (And I do not use the phrase 'taste explosion'. Ever.) The porkchop was juicy and had a flavorful crispy outside, and it went so perfectly with the sour sauerkraut and the sweet baked apples. The pancakes were perfect, as usual, but that porkchop pushed me over the edge!

Only street meat I will eat (chicken over rice). Line is generally pretty long. Go easy on the hot sauce (recommend taking a tiny cup and dripping it yourself, they put WAY too much on). Get extra white sauce. Chicken is better than the lamb/gyro meat, but both are serviceable.

My friend and I were roaming the streets of TriBeca looking for a place on Yelp Â to relax and have a drink. Â We walked past this gem of place and what caught my eye was the decorations. Â As soon as we walked in I knew it would be a great experience. Â Everything from the ambiance to the service is top notch. Â Everyone is friendly, professional, and knowledgeable. Â  What was intended to be a drink or two turned into a full dinner and a greater time than I could have imagined! Â  Anytime I am in TriBeca The Greek is my first choice.
A top notch Resturant worthy of praise. Enjoyed every aspect from cocktails, Appetizers, main to dessert. Those tempura green beans were a pleasant surprised. Definitely going on my favorites list.

I always get the extra spicy here, and while it certainly packs a punch it is far from an obnoxious test of Â fortitude. Â In short, it might be the most perfectly seasoned piece of chicken I've ever eaten. Â It's also nicely brined, so it's always perfectly moist and meaty. Points off only for: 1) Â Mac & cheese that's fair at best. Â Skip it, get the excellent butterbeans instead. 2) Â Service that's often haphazard, which is fine at a place like this as long as it's always is upbeat and friendly, which it is 80% of the time, but 20% of the time it can be attitude-y. Â (Probably if you go here a lot, or work here, you know exactly who I'm talking about...) 3) Portion size is small: you're charging $13, give me half a chicken, not 3/8ths of a chicken!
Went to Calle Ocho for the first time. Â The atmosphere is really nice. Â The service was great in that we didn't have a long wait, but the sangria and the food was ok.

We were trying to get in various spots last saturday night and managed to grab a table in Buttermilk channel. The food was full of flavor and the service was excellent. Very attentive and on point. I had the special which was ribeye. I'm usually not one for a steak if its not in a steakhouse but this was as good as any i've had. Full of flavor and cooked rare to perfection. Really enjoyed the place and would highly recommend. Â Next time the fried chicken will be mine !

this is one of those places that is hard to give a bad review. Â the price is good, the staff is friendly and helpful, the food is good too. Â but nothing is amazing. Â it's like one of those places you grow up eating with your family, but probably wouldn't want to go for a special occasion. Â  i stumbled on il corallo trattoria after meandering around the area looking for a place to eat. Â most of the area has expensive restaurants that are over crowded so rose and i were having trouble getting a seat. Â we even stumbled in a lesbian bar, yea i'm talking to you dalloway. Â  Â  anyway, we found this place. Â it was quaint. Â busy, packed, but still were accommodating. Â the portion sizes were very large and luckily the waiter stopped us from over ordering as we planned. Â the food was good, nothing amazing, but definitely filling and edible. Â if you're in the area and can't find anything else to eat, you can't go wrong with this place.

There really is a nonna in the back cooking. Â She came out and asked us how our meal was! Â So cool. Â SO the deal - they have two seatings.. 7:00 and 9:30. Â So you aren't rushed out after the meal.. you can have a nice relaxed meal ... the food is amazing. Â there are nightly specials that the nonna makes (my Italian friend said it tasted just like her nonna's meals) and some very cool inexpensive wines that the owner has picked out personally. Â great appetizers, great meals, great desserts. Â The place is very small.. but the food is amazing. I can't wait to go back and try another nonna's cooking.

Expensive but very good. Â We had the wonderful sheep's milk ricotta (agree you have to have it), beet salad, pumpkin ravioli, and scallops. Oh, and topped off with a chocolate cake. Â Loved it all and worth the $ for a special celebration.

A few weeks ago I wrote a rather scathing review of Almond on YELP, upon my first visit there. And while I stand by the accuracy of that experience, I must say I was pleasantly surprised when someone from Almond's management tracked me down, apologized and invited me back to Almond for another try. I tried it again last night with three friends and our experience could not have been more different. This time the food, service and attention to detail were exceptional - 5 stars! When we arrived, we were seated right away. Â The primary waiter serving us was amazing - great attitude and very attentive. Â The food was delicious; we mostly ordered seafood as I now realize that, that is Almond's strength. Â We were treated as royalty. Â I am impressed that the restaurant cared about our unpleasant prior experience and invited us to return so they could show their better side. Â And that better side, which I hope is their norm, is spectacular.
The best Italian American food for the regular guy in the United States. Â Any one who likes Italian food should eat there at least one time.

This review is for The Lounge at Atera. I made reservations several weeks in advance and they were ready for us when we arrived. There are no markings for the restaurant from the street and there's definitely a cool "speakeasy" feel to the place. The Lounge is one level below the street and accessible via elevator. It's a little fabulous jewel box of a space with two tables for couple and two sofa lounges for slightly larger groups. It's a very comfortable mod interior and the staff was very cool and friendly. The drinks were outstanding and the apps were straight from the tasting menu upstairs. Cool indie music soundtrack at the perfect volume for atmosphere. Fantastic spot for upscale hipster romance.

Awesome food, atmosphere and service. Â Only complaint was the insanely rude hostess. Â We were a party of 3 at the bar waiting for two more to arrive for dinner. Â When our table was ready she came over and was like you have to close out asap, but our bartender was busy talking to other patrons, we weren't just going to interrupt him. Â So i told her to give us the next table and she did. Â She didn't even want to wait two minutes. Â I would absolutely still go back but i will be sure to be a b*tch to her everytime.

Wait in the line, don't worry about being sat with other patrons...the crab dumplings will simply shut you up. Â Order up a few orders, get some Shanghai fried flat noodles, or an order of scallion pancakes and you're good to go. Â Living in LA now, this is without question the one food I miss most about New York. Â  If you only remember one thing, take a little nibble of the dumpling skin from the top so you can suck out the ample juices...do not make the freshman mistake of biting into it and having it explode all over your plate. Â I cringe and curse to myself when I see newbies make this mistake, because the meat/crab broth is a religious experience! Make sure you hit up the next block and go to the Chinatown Ice Cream Factory for exotic ice cream dessert...what a treat.
The food is good, but not worth the price.

I will admit that the pancakes are pretty good, but its a really long wait and the fact that they take cash only at brunch ( it was 80 for 2..not exactly cheap) and barely advertise that, yet they take credit cards for dinner, is kinda ridiculous..not even sure they ate allowed to do that. It is near my apartment so I was able to put my name down and go back when our table was ready so I am glad I tried it, but not sure I woukd trek there ftom elsewhere.

What a friendly waitstaff, entertaining and totally sold us on the food! Sizzling sisig app was very delicious... Fat never tasted so good! And the garlic rice! THE GARLIC RICE!!! I felt like I was cheating on my lifetime partner aka white rice, knowing I'll never look at it the same again... The real winner from the chicken and waffles is the waffles. The chicken is chicken but the waffles are the most fluffy, perfectly sweet, tiny bit crunchy things. And then... You try slather it in some of their coconutish magical syrup and by the Grace of God and the kitchenstaff you have the most delicious waffles I've ever tasted in my life. The butter on the waffles were a culinary twist I didn't particularly like: the butter has a but of fishy anchovy taste so beware! Pork ribs adobo was just good. Your breath will stink for a long time afterwords. Very large portion enough for two. Overall a great intimate way to try Filipino food!

The only reason I came here was because of the Red White and Blue. Â Just like every other reviewer here. Â 8 Dollars for 6 oysters and a drink (Red Wine, White Wine, or PBR). It's a great deal! Unfortunately the price was the only thing that I loved. The oysters were not chilled well. Â I'm not saying it was warm but it was definitely not chilled to a temperature where raw oysters can be enjoyed. Â Also a few of the oysters were lacking in size. Â I couldn't believe that it was counted!! but I guess for the price, you can't be picky. Fish and chips were a bit bland ($17), I enjoyed the fries more than the fish. Â Also got an order of Crab cakes ($14), we all enjoyed that a lot but. Loaded with a lot of crab meat. This was possibly the best out of all the items ordered. Â  The restaurant is cramped and we were put into a corner by the kitchen. Â Which made us have to reach over or under objects and maneuver around dishes and drinks to grab some food. Â We were all still very hungry so we decided to get the check and eat somewhere else to finish off the night. Â There is a wait in case you were wondering, we waited an hour to get in. Â  The staff is all very nice and everything but there are plenty of other places to go for some cheap oysters and the pleasure of dining in a more comforting setting.

3 words for Taqueria: Simple Tasty Fun Hands down the best chorizo tacos in the city! Â Everything is good here, from the chicken flautas, to every taco on the menu, the addicting chips, the decor, the old school movies playing and the mariachi music! Â  Sit down, enjoy a Sol beer, and get ready to eat food with some flavor!

I was excited that to hear about another banh mi addition to the East Village. Being one of my favorite foods, I couldn't wait to try it. When I went, I asked what was suggested and was told the coconut lamb if I wanted to be more adventurous. Having been my way around a traditional banh mi, I went with that. I also couldn't turn down the obvious compliment of a Vietnamese cie coffee. And the two come to just under $10. The coconut lamb was absolutely brilliant. It was thinly sliced like roast beef with a light coconut sauce. I would've preferred something extremely rich and creamy because I love coconut sauces, but this was still great. As for the traditional banh mi, while it was very good, I prefer Baoguette's because they have minced chunks of pork. The highlight is definitely the bread. I don't know if they make their own bread, but it sure tasted like it was right out of the oven. I initially couldn't even pick up my sandwich because it was so hot. The inside is light and soft, whereas the outside has a real fresh crunch, not the kind you get from staleness. So of my favorite banh mi places in the area, I can't decide if I like Xe May or Banh Mi Zon more. However, it really is a win win because the more banh mi in the East Village, the better.

Three-and-a half stars for the food, and half a star for the styling/decor/name. I was torn between trying Katsu-hama and this place in a recent trip to NYC and due to ease of take-out, went with Go Go Curry! I happened to visit on the 15th which means I got coupons to come back and claim a free topping. Unfortunately I'm from out of town (anyone want one)? The curry sauce was pretty tasty with a decent amount of spiciness and the katsu breading was done just right. The meat (I had pork) left a little to be desired as it was a bit chewy/tough in parts. Would go back, though next time I'll be trying Katsu-hama first. (Also - the story behind "Go Go": The number "five" in Japanese is "Go" so "Go Go" represents "5 5" = 55, Matsui's number for the Yankees.)

I am not a meatball fan but the sandwich I had here was bomb dot com, super succulent balls on warm and soft, fresh white bread. I may have been a little tipsy but i do recall a bit of heat in the balls and a stringiness to the cheese. I had already eaten a taco and mac n' cheese down the street but that didn't stop me from inhaling these ballin' meatballs! Went on Friday night around 3am and it was booming. This is the winter time and LES is noticeably less crowded, so I would imagine that it's crazy popping in the summer. All the customers in line and the staff managing the line were snippy and on edge. I have never seen a bouncer at a service couter before coming here. I guess that's what happens when you put belligerently good bar food in the middle of LES - aka one giant shit show - and stay open 'til the bars close. Turns out they gave us the wrong order. We came out with three extra sandwiches and some cake. Oops!
My wrap was completely underwhelming. Stay away! Expensive to top it all off for "fast food"

True authentic Italian food ----says the non- Italian ---ME!!!!!! My friend had her birthday dinner her on Sunday. Â Thank goodness for reservations b/c there had to be over 20+ people waiting w/o reservs...and the amount of people who actually had reservs was about the same... So that tells me this place has some serious food or drinks. So with everything being family style we ordered Sausage & meatballs, penne w/ broccoli, garlic & oil, Chicken Parmigiana (for the fake Itailan---ME), some other penne in a sauce, Tony's salad, and Sangria....everything....AMAZINGLY DELICIOUS!!!!!!! Price and service was great...couldn't ask for anything more!!!!

What else can I add to this review? Â Everyone pretty much nailed it on the spot. One thing I have to emphasize: Â Come here for the Chargrilled Burger...you can't go wrong. Will Chu "Real Food, Real Wine in The Real World!"

Best cappuccino my sister and I have ever had, and we have been to Italy, Paris, you name it, we've had it!!! The new barista chick was beyond sweet and friendly, and our almond milk caps were the best wake ups we have ever experienced. We actually walked back and thanked her for the heavenly goodness!!!!!

I had the famous Artichoke and Spinach pizza. Â The slice was humongous! Â The pizza was good, BUT I felt like it was heavier than what I would like. Â It is super creamy! Â It honestly was not the best pizza I've ever had, but I also prefer tomato sauce type pizzas more! Â You better be hungry when you eat this or share it with a friend!
the food was good, drinks were awesome, the bartender was accomodating and made my drinks as I had requested. space is a little tight but still a nice place to go with friends after a long day.

I came here for dinner one night last week to get my fried chicken fix. Â This place definitely hit the spot. I was happy to see that there wasn't a line. I've heard that this place usually has a wait. Â Maybe it wasn't as busy because we came on a weeknight. Â  I ordered the fried chicken (dark meat) with mac and cheese and coleslaw. Â Everything was delicious. Â I love their fried chicken. Â It was tasty without being overly greasy. Â I was so sad when I finished my chicken because I wanted more. Â I actually had to steal some of my boyfriend's chicken... which he willingly handed over. Â The service is fast and attentive. Â This was my first time at Amy Ruths and I would definitely come back.

A very good address : just surrounded by Asian people, it garantees authenticity. After few seconds, they brought us some hot tea and the order came within 2 min: beef rice noodle soup, dumpling flat noodle soup and spring rolls. All of it was very tasty. A filling meal with a healthy touch! Amazing for just 20$ for 2! The only dark point: they aren't nice at all with Caucasians or tourists...

Put it this way - I wore badge shorts and my waitress spilt a little Sangria on me while she was sturring at the table's edge (not to smart to begin with) and I am giving it a 5. Â The few dots did not remain and I was given club soda to apply. Â The Octopus for starters were amazing and the Empeladas as well. Â As far as the meat, well you can tell it is Argentinian steak - rib eye, skirt steak and shell steak - all amazing! Dessert - well let's just say you could consider this a dessert cafe if you happen to be in the neighborhood eating at a place that may not serve the best after dinner treats. Â Take a seat in the back garden underneath grape vines and an array of landscape that sets your night up to be a most memorable one and enjoy any of the desserts on the menu - may have been the best part!!

Good beer selection and food is what you expect it to be. Although you are first greeted by very noisy patrons when you enter in the front, but there is a more pleasant dining area tucked away in the back. But then again, it's what you expect during happy hour. From what I heard, they have really good burgers, and if you go during lunch they offer a $10 deal where you get burger with fries and a half pint of beer.
Solid food, great beer selection and creative cocktails. Â This place never disappoints.

Excellent food and service! I changed my reservation for 3 times back and forth, still they were able to accommodate and we were seated right away. I have read some bad reviews about the horrible service before I went there but I didn't have any problem at all. Paella is a must, both negra and the roast duck. We tried a few tapas and they were all good! Will definitely recommend to friends.

I love the atmosphere of this small French restaurant tucked away in Williamsburg but was not satisfied for what we came for -- crepes. They had a good array of crepes to choose from although they were lacking anything with strawberries and bananas. They just don't have strawberries at all which was disappointing. Ended up getting the pear and almond crepe with homemade chocolate. The chocolate was ehh-- nutella has spoiled me. The pear was a little mushy but still OK. The waitress had a cute French accent and was really sweet although we were only having takeout. The water they served us while waiting smelt like eggs and the guy who rang us up had to do the math incorrectly on a piece of paper. The bathrooms were charming tho -- postcards of France all over.
Great food, drinks, and bartenders! There's nothing more to say! Plus the atmosphere isn't so bad either for a casual night out.

Mmmmm, so super tasty. The hangtown fry was of course delicious, as was the bloody mary-- had I been feeling more tip top, I would have had multiple! Surprisingly affordable too, which I always appreciate. Lovely.

I'm tempted to give it 1 star so it stops being so full! Â I love this place and its mostly locals that know about it.... I see why. Â The truffle Pizza is do die for.... been here 5 times already and never had anything less than a stellar experience.

one of my favorite spots! good is always great and drinks are awesome. the mac attack is a must (like everyone else said). You can get held at the door late night so dress warm. I did see some people slip him some cash and they got in, but that's the way it rolls.

Good value for late-night drunk dining shenanigans. The slides and fries are good, and they have reasonably priced beers if you need a nightcap. Not much room to sit, though. Be sure to not be sober when you arrive.

Whoa, the Tonkatsu ramen was pretty out of this world. I've tried some really good ramen and this one is definitely on par with the best of them. While its slightly on the sweeter side. The soup was very flavorful and the ramen was tender and bouncy. Just the way I like them. And the decor and atmosphere was very chill. Felt like a really good time.

Finally, i took the pilgrimage to Grimaldi's after many tries. The line was expected so i didn't fault them for it. Plus taking a trip down to the dock and getting ice cream made the wait seem shorter. And once we finally reached the entrance, the hostess was extremely nice and apologized many, many times for the inconvenience. For new york coal pizza, i always compare it to my favorite, Lombardi's. And no doubt, it is up to par with the fresh mozzarella and basil. The peperoni was good but unlike Lombardi's, the experience was forgettable. The place was dirty and our table was not wiped down from the previous patrons. The prices were extremely fair ($6 less than Lombardis) but the menu only contains pizza or antipasto, nothing else food wise. The pizza came out within 5 minutes but half the slices' crust came out burnt. The unburnt slices were great and were not greasy. Some members of our party had committed blasphemy and stated that they liked Grimald's better than Lombardis. I respect their opinion and could see why they would, but Lombardis adds so much to the experience including salad on their menu. Grimaldi's is a place to definitely try because you might think this is your favorite pizzeria in NYC, and i hate when people say Grimald's is hands down the best pizza or Johns or Lombardi's or Joe's because they are all great and comparable to one another, there is no clear favorite, just a slight preference. My recommendation to grimaldis is to increase the price of the pizza by a dollar and save that money to renovate and buy the unnecessary store next to you to expand

We all have a different palate thats for sure! I have visited Il Corallo a few times with my gf who swears by it. The place is very cute, small, and homey. We have always been greeted well and seated as space allows. Â Did i say the place is small? The service has always been very courteous even when the place is completely full. Siting in the dining room you get to see the brick oven on the back, blasting with heat on freshly made personal pizzas with nicely toasted crust. Â The list of pastas in the menu is very nice, as for my experience they have always been very fresh and flavorful. Yes, i have to admit, it could be hit or miss, as most places are, but maybe i would add a bit of salt to my plate, but thats small compared to other places where you might feel like you can make the whole thing better. Wines are always good, they have a nice list as well as the house wine. The wines by the glass are limited to what they have open that day or night, but you are always advised which ones they are. All in all, fresh, flavorful, homey and courteous does it for me... 4 stars right there!

this $12 brunch gets 5 stars no matter what. Â i haven't eaten here for any other meal and don't know if the 5 stars would prevail, but at brunch ~ 5 stars it is. Â Coffee,tea and juice,bellini, or mimosa with an entree for $12. Â Mind you it is a mimosa with cheap bubbly, but there are costs to consider! Â Well, they show good intention by pouring a 95% bubbly to 5% oj ratio. Â Thanks! Â My spinach and goat cheese omelet was fresh, fluffy and stuffed with creamy goat cheese and supple well seasoned spinach. Â A side salad of mixed greens was bountiful and crisp with a perfect dressing of no more than S &P, olive oil and maybe lemon juice. Â the "home fries" were crisp little fried potato cubes. Â Not greasy, not mealy, just crisp and delish. Â I was so pleased. Yay for paprika!

Um, have I mentioned that brunch is my favorite meal of the day? Â My bf's friend couldn't make it to their reservation so they asked if we wanted it. Â Since we both had no brunch plans... SURE! (heard that they made reservations way ahead of time, so Â highly recommended to make reservations) Absolutely love the decor and vibe here. Â It felt like SF here with the organic, rustic, picked veggies from the back yard feel. Â We ordered the crab toast (MUST TRY!) and the benedict. Â Both was delicious. Â  Needless to say, I will be back!

Yes, my second 1 star of the weekend. Â Its just been a losing streak all around, down to the icky sandwich I just had working on night float. Â But again, I digress. Â Ew. Â This place is just well...ew. Â The dumplings are chewy and frankly kind of tasteless. Â The soup was cold. Â Hot and sour soup served cold. Â I think in a land where soup was hot and fresh this one may have been a winner, but helas the LES on a Sunday afternoon was no such land. Â The serracha sauce was watered down. Â The only 2 things I liked were the cucumber salad and the bubble tea. Â That's it. Â Actually, the sandwich and the pork buns our neighbor I coveted greatly, but not enough to come back...so the search for the perfect dim sum continues...
2 words: Â bespoke cocktails. Just avoid at all costs during happy hour. Â Way too packed for the type of venue this is. Â Stroll on over after 9 PM and you'll appreciate every second.

Toby's is a place that lives up to its Yelp reputation! Â It is a restaurant with a nice local feel. Â A long bar on the right, tables and chairs on the left, and the guys making and baking the pizzas in the wood burning oven in the back. I personally loved that they had basketball, soccer and the news on the large screens and decent background music that did not preclude listening in to the conversations at the tables adjacent to ours! But alas we came to eat! Â We began with a very fresh Arugula salad and followed with an excellent buffalo mozzarella pizza with a superior thin but tasty crust, fresh tomato sauce and a generous portion of cheese. Â  We only had water to drink but our server brought us a bottle to be sure we had enough and we did not have to ask for extra cheese and hot peppers because they were delivered with the pizza.. I do wish that restaurants who do not take credit cards would post so on the door, but otherwise it was a great first visit to Toby's and I am sure it will not be our last!

So after about two visits and multiple seamless orders, I finally decided to write my review. I always order the steamed fresh roll. I really like that they put real crab meat on top. Another one of my fave dishes is the crab and pork noodles. This time around I got the shrimp and calamari salad and jungle curry rice. Jungle curry rice medium spicy is not for the faint of heart, tongue or stomach. It left my tongue tingling and was good. The only downside was that the rice was a bit mushier than I would have liked. Â The shrimp and calamari salad with the lime dressing has tons of ginger goodness. If you don't like ginger as much as I do but want to try this salad, you should def ask the server for less. Â  It's nice that Pure Thai has a different style of Thai food choices from the rest of the many many many Thai restaurants in the neighborhood.

Notoriously long wait times as they don't take reservations of any kind, cramped seating, and not exactly cheap. Throw all that out the window, because once you try the melt in your mouth burger and delicious shoestring fries, you'll be transported to a land of milk and honey (that is actually meet and cheese). Your best bet is to show up early on in the evening or super late, put your name down and go for some cheap drinks in the neighborhood. Wait for your "table's ready" call and indulge. The burger is legendary and for good reason. Minor Critique: Thought the cheese was just a tad overwhelming, but maybe they put just a bit too much on mine. Also tried the skate (skippable, too salty, but tasty and filling for a white fish) and the roasted beets (awesome). Will go back soon for the other stuff, non-burger. Get a couple drinks--they make excellent cocktails--which are best if Â they're putting you in the high single digits for the night and then proceed to eat some delicious pub-food, that seems to have like started the whole gastropub thing in this wonderful city we live in. Thanks April, Now I can develop an eating disorder and alcoholism in the same place.

Genuinely amazing food -- the veggie curry in particular -- but pretty erratic service. I've tried to get the veggie curry a few times, and sometimes they don't have it at all, sometimes I have to wait for almost an hour (in a tiny, sweltering space). But, assuming you go in knowing not to expect a quick or simple experience, you'll leave happy, and stuffed.

Dos Toros was started by some dudes from my hometown who were unimpressed by NY's Mexican offerings and wanted to make something akin to Gordo's. Â For this I am eternally grateful to them. Â I would say that Dos Toros is about half a star down from Gordo's but, as New York is the antithesis of Mexican food I can't really blame them. Â Their burritos are good for two meals so the price is totally worth it, and definitely get guacamole.
'muttering retreats of one night cheap hotels, sawdust restaurants with oyster shells...' Don't ever go here.
The food was good. However, service was very slow. This will not be a good choice if your in a mood to get in and out. Also, it's a bit on the pricier side.

Amy's not sure what all the hype is about.... I had the chicken with potato salad and the Mac/ cheese. The potato salad was very good I must say the Mac:cheese was ok, the chicken was juicy and crispy:). The decor of the place was odd. I think overall Its alright. Â I can ck it off my list but wont Â be running back!
5 stars for a sandwich place. Great bread, great ingredients, and 2+ pounds sandwiches will leave you satisfied.
Best BBQ I have had since I left the south. The ribs melt in your mouth. Cool vibe. Could go dressy or casual and still feel comfortable. Sauce is AMAZING.

Haha, I had a good experience here. I came here after hearing about the pancakes which I was looking forward to trying. I was a bit dissapointed to get there and find that they weren't doing pancakes that morning. The guy suggested the french toast, so I said yeah great, I ordered some sausage aswell. What can I say? It was a really tasty, fat filled morning mover. I'd just started to tuck in when a group of business men came in, saw what I was having and said ''oh wow, french toast and sausage for me, that looks great!'' I laughed and said ''oh it is, it's just what you need on a morning''. The atmosphere in this place is really nice and welcoming. The old guy with the coffee pot was great and kept our cups filled up. Real friendly and genuine guys, I was glad to pay them for my breakfast.

Finally visited after months of people telling me how good it is. This ia a review on the bar only . Im yet to eat here but feel the urge is coming to try the best chicken in NYC. The bar is cool , not crazy busy but very civilised. Drinks were great , as was service. Great date spot and will definitely go back to try more drinks. I really want to add more but fear I was already 2 sheets to the wind from the flatiron room earlier.

This is just a lot of fun and good food on a summer day. Sitting out on the upper deck is like being at a great crab place on the Bay. OK, not exactly, but the food made us feel that way. We simply had crab bites, steamers and a dozen steamed (not boiled) blue crabs. If you love to get messy eating well prepared and tasty crabs, this is the place. It was all washed down with large quantities of Blue Point Summer beer. Save yourself a drive down to the Maryland shore if you are in the mood for blue crab. Â  Â Visited July 2013

I've eaten here before for brunch and had a lovely time. I came back for a special dinner and was extremely disappointed. I have a gluten intolerance and their website CLEARLY states that they can make food accommodations. If they didn't say that, then I wouldn't have made reservations for a specialty 5 course dinner. Once I got to the restaurant, I immediately mentioned my food allergy because there were going to be 2 courses I would not be able to eat. The waitress promised to ask but failed to tell me that NO accommodations would be made until after we had already received the first course. I only had 3 courses and they still put all the food in front of me, which is awful when you have a food intolerance! They proceeded to charge us full price for everything even though I didn't touch anything with gluten. I would have gone elsewhere for dinner if they only mentioned it before they bright us food! Super unprofessional to trap your guests in the restaurant. Mind you, i've had dozens of Â tasting dinners, and many in MUCH nicer places than this, and NEVER have I had a restaurant refuse to substitute for my food allergy! Even something cheap like a salad would have made me feel like they take allergies seriously. I'm extremely disappointed in the kitchen and the floor staff for their lack of communication. I would be careful about eating at Northern Spy if you have any food allergies. The kitchen obviously doesn't care. I did everything a guest is supposed to do and since no one cared, I will not be going back and I will definitely stop suggesting it to people like I used to. I really can't say how much it ruined my otherwise nice day.

I came here for a birthday dinner with 5 people, and they were very friendly and the 4 course tasting menu was DELICIOUS!!! The chef was very gracious and friendly. The tasting menu is something everyone should try - its from 5-8pm, $35/pp I think. The chef asked each person at the table their likes/dislikes, allergies, food restrictions, etc. I am vegetarian and its near impossible to find delicious, well-conceived dishes at good quality restaurants - so this was a HUGE treat. The atmosphere is romantic, dim lighting, rusting - Â great for a date.

Appetizers: Ordered octopus which was good although overly soft. Â  The pikilia, (4 spreads) Â 2 were tasty, 2 yuck. Â Main course: Â Shrimp Santorini - the sauce tasted like tin can with some spices and shrimp were overcooked. Btw, authentic shrimp Santonrini is made with chunks of tomato, not sauce. Â  Broiled Scallops also overcooked. Â Horta bland, potatoes , so-so. Â  Food was not horrible also not great. Â What gives it 2 stars is, the place is small & overcrowded. Â While eating, we were eyeballed to the point of being uncomfortable, they needed the table. Â When a host hovers over you for your table it makes a dining experience awful. Don't rush me!! Â It pisses me off! Â Plus, you never know which of your patrons understand the language you are speaking. Â Won't be returning here. Â I'll head over to the original instead.

What a crazy, ridiculous experience Artichoke Basille's is. It is a quirky little hole in the wall that fits its NYC neighborhood perfectly. And by quirky, I mean the Eddie Murphy oil painting they have on the wall. This was my first meal when visiting NY and I had no idea what to expect. What I got was really amazing pizza, a teeny tiny bathroom, giant styrofoam cups of beer, and "Happy 1st Birthday!" cocktail napkins for wiping up your thick, messy pizza. My husband and I split the "small" spinach artichoke pizza which was enough for 4 people to spit easily. It was thick, greasy, and super rich, with spinach and artichoke dip topping the pizza. What a unique pizza experience!

We have been going back for the years. Whenever we think about great pizza, this place comes to our mind. The owner is wonderful and always care about his customers as he comes over to greet us. I always takes my friends and families here for pizza and wine.

Dear Patrons that were sitting next to us on Saturday night, 8ish, 2nd table on the left, I didn't want to disrupt your dinner plans but when I looked over and you had placed your soup dumpling on your plates and then proceeded to break them open with your chopstick, I almost had a heart attack! How could you let the liquid goodness leak out like that??? Did no one teach you how to eat a soup dumpling??? I was saddened immensely!!!! Next time, please don't be so careless.... Broken-hearted, Dreamsrey

Came here for brunch on a Sunday and of course Â it was packed out. Â However, I was lucky enough to get seated at the bar. Â No wait. Â Woohoo. I had the veggie burger and my friend had the special of the day which was a pastrami hash. Â The veggie burger was great. Â The flavor of pesto on the burger was amazing and perfect. Â The burger also came with French fries that were delicious. Â Not oily at all. Â The pastrami hash was good. Â Probably wouldn't order it again but it was nice to try. Â  Service was very friendly.
Great dine-in experiences always. However, when I ordered delivery, it took over an hour and when I called, they hadn't even placed my order to be made yet. VERY disappointing.

Absolutely love this place. Â Been here several times and the experience had always been one of great food and service. Their 3 pasta all you can eat is the best deal in town. Their food is fresh, served promptly by an attentive staff and everyone seems concerned that you are enjoying yourself. Whether as a party of one or a group of 8 the experience was the same! It is best to make a reservation, especially if you are a larger party, but I dropped in once as a single during the dinner rush and was seated promptly. This is a very popular Italian restaurant in the Theater District and they have lots of pre-theatre patrons, so if you are going during the week getting there after the theater rush will make it more enjoyable. They don't rush you either, particularly for the 3-pasta all you can eat, they just keep coming back asking if you want more... Great all around and my first place to recommend to friends and out of town guests.

I went with some co-workers. We didn't have reservations and were told the wait would be about 1.5 hours but it was more like 2 hours. When we were seated at our table, the waiter came over right away and told us the specials and took our drink orders. The appetizers arrived (fried calamari & stuffed ardichokes) and they were delicious. Our main course was shrimp parm. with pasta. Some of the pasta wasn't quite done, but the shrimp were huge and tender. The waiter was very pleasant as well as the rest of the staff thru out the entire meal.This was the first time I ate at this location but I would defintely go back. I'll just make sure I have reservations.

I made a reservation for four but someone back out last minute so we were just three. They seated us at a table for two and just added a chair. It was ridiculously small but we were like whatever since it was so crowded. We ordereed a pitcher of white sangria. It wasn't anything special but it was $27 for one liter (Happy hour till 8pm). We ordered the guac (comes with chips and salsa), quesadilla de champigon (must order - the mushroom was so good), and the carnitas (meat heaven with rice&bean, spinach and yuca fries). It was so much food that we had a whole plate of leftover. If your food doesn't come with yuca fries then you have to order it. It was so fresh and hot when we had it.

Stopped in for an impromptu lunch / brunch after hearing about this spot opening up. Pleasantly surprised to see that it was wide open and had no trouble getting a table. A little bummed that they only serve their brunch menu until 4PM and I wasn't in the mood for breakfast given it was 2:00. All the wait staff was very attentive and super nice. The food was ok. We both had the fried chicken and waffles and although it was nice the chicken was off the bone there wasn't anything really thrilling about it. I love a jalapeno bloody but this was one was just ok to. However, the dinner menu sounds delicious so when I come back and I will be back, I'll update this! Cute space, try it out!

I never order delivery if i do not know the if it is clean or not restaurant , This restaurant is clean , tasty food , quick delivery and reasonable prices. Â You can ask them for Â low fat and msg free. Â I recommend this Great Chinese restaurant .
I went here for a late dinner with friends. Â We got fried chicken, ribs and several sides including biscuits, mac and cheese, baked squash and of course, pies! It was all terrific. Â I'll be back.

Currently sitting here for almost an hour waiting for my order. It's just a sandwich and a burger. People that have come after us have already gotten their food. Wth. Currently sitting here for almost an hour waiting for my order. It's just a sandwich and a burger. People that have come after us have already gotten their food. Wth. Minutes later: asked for the order to go. Don't have anymore time to sit around and eat. The woman says: the burger takes long. Uh.. Â I'm sorry, don't remember the last time I had to wait an hour for a Burger to cook. When we leave she says: you should've let me know you we're short on time. I would've had the burger come out with the soup. (Our appetizer) What..? Even if I wasn't short on time, no one wants to wait around for an hour for their burger and sandwich.

Decent. Not too impressed. Thought it would be way better but it was, like I said before, simply decent. Came here with a gigantic group of people on a Friday night (there were about 12 of us). We had no reservation or any handle of how long of a wait would be but it was only 30 minutes. Not bad! They seated us in the back dining room which was pretty nice. We ordered our respective dishes and none of us were too impressed. The chicken was overcooked and dry, which is a big no no in the restaurant world. Many of us ordered to trio of pasta sampler and only the ravioli was impressive. The seafood appetizer which came with it included octopus (which was surprising) but the seafood seemed a bit on the old side, like it was from the day before or sitting out from that morning. Some of my other fellow diners had the veal or steak and also weren't blown away. I thought it could have been a lot better considering the location, competition nearby on Restaurant Row, and prices. I probably won't be going back (maybe only for that ravioli).

Have you ever dreamt of a giant noodle wrapping itself around your neck and dragging you back to the lair of delicious amazing thai noodle heaven? I did after going to Tuk Tuk. The Pad-Thai here is addictive. For those of you that love Thai and are adventurous beyond the manhattan area, come to Vernon Jackson to sample their nutty, creamy, lime-y, flavorful, cheap Pad Thai. Every kind is great- their veggie duck is my favorite, surprisingly. Some of the other dishes are a little TOO flavorful- like their "roasted duck curry." I like spicy, but this was out of hand. And their duck was way overcooked. Their curry is ok. Their papaya salad is kind of gross. The spring rolls are spring rolls. And the dressing they serve with their normal green salad is practically just soy sauce. Ew. BUT on the plus side, service is fast and furious. You never have a wait for a table. And like I said, the pad-thai is worth getting over and over again. Morning, noon night, drunk, sober, christmas. . . .I could go on. But you can eat it for yourself and decide.

Good crepes! A little bit too fancy of a place for me though. Basically it's a tiny and dimly lit restaurant. I was going for dessert so I went for the sweet crepe. A friend recommended the one with fresh raspberries, white chocolate and whipped cream on top. Gotta say the place wins for presentation factor. The crepe was perfectly folded with a perfect scoop of whipped cream topped with a mint leaf. Â Taste wise it was okay for me. Â The raspberry sauce overpowered the taste of the white chocolate. Overall, pretty good. My crepe was $9 but with tax and tips came to about $12. A bit too pricey for dessert for me. I'd probably go to creperie and grab a quick large crepe to go for about $6.

As solid as any hamburger has ever been. I was very impressed. It was perfect. That's not to say that it is some unique taste, some revolutionary sandwich. It's just that in a world of many hamburgers, these guys made a flawless one. When you want just a regular hamburger, this one is perfect. There's nothing super special or unique about it, nothing that stands out. But you walk away impressed with how it's as solid as a regular burger has ever been made.
I wandered in there one morning for coffee and I tried the blueberry scones.... It was the best scone I ever had, and I can't wait to go back for brunch.

So The Halal Guys are the BEST halal stand anywhere. They don't need another 5 star review because you probably already know that they are THE BEST. They are a part of the NYC experience and every New Yorker knows they are the best, jeez, I'm getting temptations as I write this, so I'll keep it short. - Hottest hot sauce, which is why I go to them. Their red sauce is insane and it's what everyone mentions when they talk about The Halal Guys. P.S. Do not confuse the ketchup for the "red sauce" as one of my non-New Yorker friends mistakenly did. - The Lamb on rice is the way to go, but gyro is faaantastic, too. I usually get multiple orders to bring back for friends whenever I go. The lamb on rice comes with fluffy pita and the meat is plenty! -If you have not been, yet... shake my head.... Do yourself a favor and go now. You are welcome!

Apparently Joe's Shanghai has the best soup dumplings here. Maybe I'm a bit of a snob when it comes to soup dumplings, but these do not hold a candle to the soup dumplings I had out in San Francisco. The skins on the dumplings here are too thick, and the dumplings are too large. I like my dumplings smaller, closer to bite size, which is how they do them out west. Heck, I wouldn't even say these are the best soup dumplings in New York; the ones at Shanghai Cafe are better. The main reason I really am not a fan of the soup dumplings is that more than half of the ones I ordered with my girlfriend had little to no soup in them at all. If I wanted to order regular pork dumplings, I would've ordered it off the menu...but to say the least, it's a bit underwhelming. The dumplings that make it out intact are pretty good, but those are relatively few and far between. The rest of the food is pretty good; the moo shu pork is delicious, along with the clams in black bean sauce. It's a bit hard to enjoy the food if you go at peak hours, though; as it's a tourist hot spot, the restaurant gets packed, and when you're crowded around a group table, it's not a terribly enjoyable culinary experience. The service is lackluster by Chinatown standards; it took us a good 15 minutes or so for them to serve up our round of soup dumplings...at 10 PM at night when there were quite a few empty spots in the restaurant. All in all, Joe's is a decent restaurant, but it's a bit overrated in my book. Don't forget to bring cash either - they don't accept credit cards.

I scheduled a reservation for a Saturday night get-together here & was very impressed by the food, decor, and service. Â We had a larger group, they were very accommodating and our waiter made great recommendations for everyone at the table. Would go back in an instant!

I came here for brunch with my parents and sat at the front of the restaurant so my parents could have a view of the happenings on Cornelia St while we ate. Â I loved the decor of the restaurant from the wooden beams to the yellow/red roses. Â Our waitress was very attentive and polite - she even laughed at my dad's jokes! Â I liked the amount of time between appetizers and entrees. Â The artichokes were delicious. Â The bill was $100 for 2 appetizers, 3 egg entrees and a bottle of sparkling water. Â I guess this is on par with a lot of restaurants in NYC though. Â Anyway, I can't wait to come back here for date night and when I do, I will definitely try the garden.

Food: 5/5 I heard that the burgers were small, but when it came out it was a good sized classy burger. I ordered the umani burger and my friends ordered the slash burger and hatch burger along with some truffle fries. The burgers were well seasoned and rich in flavor, but not overwhelming. Â  Price: 3/5 It was a little more on the pricey side, but it was expected because truffle oil ain't cheap. Ambiance: 3/5 It has a nice bar. Customer service: 4/5 Our waiter was helpful with recommendations and was pretty prompt. They orders came out pretty quick Tip: It's typically very busy, but we went at 11am when they opened. There was no wait at that time.

This restaurant is amazing and the best part is its in Ridgewood! The food is great ...I had the chicken which was cooked to perfection. Â Friendly staff and great service . I look foward to going back and trying more things on the menu. Cant wait till they get thier liquor licence! What a Â great addition to the area!

Don't think I can say anything that hasn't already been said. Â Gramercy Tavern is a classic for a reason. Â It's not just a meal. Â It's an experience from the moment you walk in, get greeted warmly by the hostess and get seated. Â When the dishes start arriving, everything from service to the actual food could not be better planned/executed. Â I remember the peek toe crab as being just one of the most perfect combinations of sensations, the sweetness of the crab offset marvelously by the accompanying soup. Â The wine list is appropriate for an establishment of this stature. Â Bottles are opened as though they were long lost friends the sommelier is getting reaquainted with. Â And my favorite part is always the muffin you get sent home with. Â  Some might find this too stuffy but this is the perfect place for that special dinner.

Highly overrated!!! This place is mediocre at best. I don't know why people wait 45mins to an hr for Grimaldi's pizza - it is totally not worth the long wait. I've had much better pizza in NY. We got our table (group of 4) after over an hrs wait! They place inside is crammed, the service is not great and the pizza is mediocre. The pizza came out pretty fast and became cold even faster! It was cold and tasteless by the time we finished the first slice (and we finished that rather quickly since we were starving after the long wait). A complete waste of time!! Will never go back there again.

My well done burger was done well indeed! The food was great! I loved how they topped the onion rings on top of my juicy well done burger. The burger was too good to explain and the onion rings just melted in my mouth. To mention the tater tots...oh baby they were seasoned and began to just continuously pop into my mouth. I also love the cozy yet exotic atmosphere. A must go!

I have one word: the lobster stuffed with shrimp! Delicious. This place rivals many of my favorite Italian restaurants in Manhattan. Probably the most underrated restaurants I've ever been to, they never seem to disappoint. They also have a great wine list. The appetizers, the entree, everything was so fresh and wonderful. Can't wait to go back

Truffle egg salad and shaved speck crostini - this was my first time trying any kind of egg salad, now I think I'm spoiled because I cannot eat any other egg salad. They no longer make this crostini into a panini :( Also, everything else I've tried was good, but this crostini is my favorite.

I went last night to check this place out. Â It's only been open a couple of weeks but it is a well designed small bar/bistro. Â I had the Bronte Burger and Fries which were very tasty and I enjoyed them. Â Service was great and the Bartender was knowledgeable attentive very friendly and made everyone feel at ease and at home. Â I highly recommend this place especially if you are in the neighborhood. Â On a side note I met the proprietor of Brooklyn Gin and had a taste of this craft Gin. Â I have to say normally Gin is an acquired taste but this Gin had less the Juniper flavor and more of a clean citrus flavor. Â The bar uses it in some of their specialty cocktails. Â I recommend trying it if you ever see it.

Beautiful place with good food! Â Doesn't seem to be the easiest place to get a prime time reservation, so book ahead on open table! Â The homemade ginger lime soda was bubbly and refreshing and the calamari with 2 dipping sauces is hands down the best I've ever tasted.
everything's perf only one thing which is really annoying is the line is way too long. if they adjust the table inside practically they'll have more seats.

Five stars for the old Calle Ocho, three stars for the new. Calle Ocho recently moved into a new space in the Excelsior hotel, and a lot more changed than just the location. Instead of a self serve sangria bar with 8 choices at brunch, they now have seven and you have to order it through your server. It's still complimentary, but you can't just get up and get a new glass at your convenience. They also have drafted a list of rules such as one glass of sangria at a time, and you have to stay within their time limit, although they don't specify what that is but will "let you know if you are approaching it." They still give you the amazing assortment of breads with strawberry butter when you sit down, and the entrees are still pretty tasty and a decent price (esp since they come with free sangria). They have the same, latin-american menu, and I usually get the burrito with eggs, beans, and chorizo inside. It's always delicious but the cheese on top wasn't melted this time and they could have been a little heavier handed with the salsa. The sangria was decently strong and tasty as always but the new system posed a problem since our server wasn't the best. He would disappear for long periods of time, so we had to wait forever for a new glass, and they only put two pieces of the boozy fruit in each. We also asked him for several things which he said he would bring and just never did. This used to be a favorite for brunch but terrible service and new "rules" considered, I may take my business to one of the other hundreds of boozy brunches in the city.

The decor and staff have a very authentic feel and a good portion of the menu and sake list is in Japanese. Â Our waiter was very friendly and glad to give his recommendations in pairing the sake with food which were all on target. The food plates are on the smaller side but the quality and skill that goes into them really shows, even their onigiri is superb. Â Definitely one of my favorite Japanese restaurants.

I grew up eating plenty of Vietnamese food in flushing and various Chinatowns, and I must say this is absolutely the best Vietnamese food I've ever had. I ordered the chicken pho and the dish didn't need any additional sauces to bring out the flavor. The broth was perfect. The crab spring rolls are crispy and served with a great dipping sauce. I'd recommend getting the Bo luc lac with the tomatoe fried rice and an egg on top. Don't forget the tapioca pudding for dessert. I cried while eating it. The Vietnamese coffee is delicious, and so is the black cherry soda they have bottled

1st off i have no idea why everyone raves about this place. The drink menu was like 7 pages while the food on the menu took up 2 at most. The susie i must admit was excellent ,but that did not make up for the buns. They were very bad tasting and slimy to boot. Â The buns had terrible indredent mixtures and masked the actual flavor of the meat i am not a fan.

Nice and quick service which i really appreciate, but the food is just ok. I got the rancheros eggs dor sunday brunch and they Â are regular, dont underatand all the fuzz about how great the food is. Also dont expect ant free alcohol deink with the sunday brnch before 12, they should state in the menu

Ahhhh the Black Label Burger. Â  The burger has been hyped for at least a year. Â Every chef has raved about it. Â Bloggers wet themselves when discussing it... GF makes reservations for my birthday. Â 3 weeks in advance and we still only manage a 6pm reservation...on a Wednesday. Â So it's still way too busy. But entering the place, I felt like I was transported back to the 50s and early 60s. Â I was hoping to see Don Draper and Roger Sterling on their 7th old-fashioned at the bar. Â Instead, I got the dreamy Richard Gere dining at a table nearby. Â His silvery hair looked as luscious as ever. Now for the burger. Â Everyone has their burger standard. Â Having lived in California for much of my life, the cheap variety goes to In-n-Out. Â And now in NYC, the gourmet burger prize goes to ABC Kitchen's arugula mayo / pickled jalapeno burger. Â But how does the Black Label compare?!? Â Well it was damn good. Â But as I wolfed down the burger, I felt like the taste was very similar to something I've had before. Â I thought and thought and I realized that it reminded me a lot of the Persian kebab -- koobideh, which is typically made of ground beef and seasoning -- sometimes a combination of lamb and beef. Â The burger has a strong flavor to it, different than most burgers. Â And the delicious butter that it was prepared with was very evident. Â Mmmmm. Â Look I loved it. Â But, just like children, you always love one son or daughter more than the others. Â I love ABC Kitchen's more than Minetta's. As for the rest? Â Well the fries were great and reminded me a lot of McDonald's -- that's good, and I'm sure these ones are way healthier. Â I liked the two cocktails that I got. Â A maple sazerac which was nice and potent. Â Just what I needed for my bday. Â And then an old-fashioned, which was great as well, because everyone wants to be Don Draper (when he's not emo and depressed). The dessert? Â Grand Marnier souffle! Â In all its orangey goodness. Â It was puffy and creamy and perfect. Â Just the right dessert to follow that burger. Place was packed -- even by 630. Â It was Â crazy. Â Our waitress and busboys were WAY too attentive and it bordered on really annoying. Â The moment I put my spoon down from the dessert, the busboys would circle my table like vultures and asked me at least 4-5 times if I was done. Â NO! Â Is my plate empty?!? NO! Â I'll tell you when I'm done. Â Or at least when it's obvious. Overall, great birthday meal. Â Burger was ALMOST the best ever. Â My only regret is not asking Richard Gere's opinion. Â And to ask him why on God's green earth did he star in Dr. T and the Women.

I love that Cafe Katja has a separate asparagus dish menu when it's in season (now)! The cheesy Emmentaler sausage or the bratwurst are the way to go - they come with sauerkraut. And be sure to order the pretzels, you will not regret it. If you're starving go for the weiner schnitzel which even my Austrian friend calls legit. There's almost always a wait as they don't accept reservations but the friendly owners will find room for you to grab a beer while you wait. Fabulous neighborhood spot.

I was always skeptical of this place, it was tiny and I wasn't exactly sure what an Empanada was. At the 9th Ave Food Festival, they had a booth and I got to try it for the firs time. I tried a variety of different things and was not disappointed by anything! If you like anything breaded, stuffed and fried, you can NOT go wrong.

Possibly the best sliders I've ever had. Â The patty is juicy, full of flavor and sits in between perfectly toasted bun. Â The grilled mushrooms and melted cheese makes this slider incredibly delicious. The server was cool enough to share her fries with me. Â They are like steak fries but just not as thick. Â Long and crispy but not burnt. Â I love my fries with BBQ sauce. Â Try it with a mixture of BBQ and jalapeno sauce. Â  You must also try the chili. Â Big chunks of beef simmered with beans and whatever their special seasonings are..oh I think its pig fat!! Â I definitely felt like a pig after scarfing down all that with a glass of Rioja wine. Â Like spicy? Â Squeeze in some of their jalapeno sauce and mix in some of the sour cream. Â  Mark has a chic yet rustic decor with a sign that says "We grind our own meat" or something like that out front. Â That's what actually caught my attention and believe me, on St Marks Place, everything catches your attention so it can be hard to choose. Â  So $11.43 plus a nice tip for a well deserved server later, I was happy, full and ready to crash. Â 1st long day of 22 in NYC. Thanks for reading!

Last Friday, I left a message on the answering machine of the restaurant requesting a reservation for 2 people at 8:30pm. I received a return call from the restaurant at 7pm telling me that they could not accommodate a reservation, but that at 8:30pm that there should be a minimal wait for a table and that I should come down. Â Promptly at 8:30pm, my guest and I arrived. If this very tiny, cramped restaurant comfortably holds 30 people, there were at least 60 people at tables, in the aisles, and at the bar. To say that it was jammed packed was an understatement. We beat our way through the crowd to the dimwitted host, who I had spoken to earlier on the phone. He indicated that there would be a short wait. I had my doubts based on how obscenely crowded the space was but I was willing to give him the benefit of the doubt. While we waited, we watched the servers maneuver through the crowds trying to get to the tables. Patrons were sandwiched in like sardines. The bar crowd hovered over the dining space and in the aisles. Â So much for a pleasant dining experience. Â In addition, the crowd was primarily wannabe, twenty-somethings. The worst part was that what was being served looked marginal. The place was absolutely dismal. After about 20 minutes, I approached the same simple host, and asked him how much longer the wait for a table would be. He dully looked me in the eyes and said that it would be at least 45 minutes and that the best that he could do would be to get me a seat at the bar. Are you kidding me? My guest and I simply left and headed out to find a more civil dining experience. The last words heard from the dolt of a host was, "we don't want your business anyway". This struck me as funny since he told me to come right on down only an hour earlier because there would be ample seating. Trust me people, this place will be on Death Watch in the not so distant future. This restaurant is the typical NYC flyby night establishment that burns bright and fades fast. You heard it here folks!

One of the best bowls of Ramen I've had. Be prepared to wait a long time to get in. I won't fault the place for the hype. Just plan ahead and do something else in the wait time. The ramen here is VERY good. The noodles are made in house so it tastes very fresh. Loaded with flavour and not overly salty. I also shared the duck appetizer with my boyfriend. I thought it was extremely delicious and savory but he thought it was just OK. Highly recommended.
Lobster and shrimp tacos were good. Tilapia tacos were eh. Chips and guacamole were OK. Surprisingly, the time square/theater location is better.
Scarpetta spaghetti is fantastic as is the Carpretto fabulous.The service is just OK they seem Not to know the menu items.But this restaurant will not dissapoint You. Your in good hands.

The pork buns and ramen at Ippudo are to die for! I still have dreams about the food at this place. Not only is it simply delectable, it's also extremely cheap for New York. $15-$20 for dinner. And it seems a lot of folks know this since getting a table took a while and the place was packed on a weekday. When we left, there was still a considerable line waiting. Take that as an unequivocal endorsement! Try this place. You will not be disappointed!

Went for brunch. Drinks: - champagne - bloody Mary: watery, but fiery. Food: - Western omelet quesadilla: food was okay. I think my issue is that I ordered the wrong stuff. No one else in there had the western omelet quesadilla, a crisped large tortilla kind of encasing some scrambled up eggs... No flavors... - steak and eggs: liked this way better than my pseudo-omelet, but it was just okay. Service okay. Just very busy, serving staff walking by, easy to get their attention if needed.

Ugh so sad. Â Very steep inflation. Â I used to love coming here for dessert and will even wait in freezing cold weather for a table. Â Those are the good old days. Â Their menu is cut very much simplified now so you have limited tea options. Â And price went up quite dramatically. Â I went today for the dinner set. Â Yes it was decent and well executed but we left hungry. Â For $24 not sure if it was worthed. Â It included chef's dessert choice and both were disappointing. Â Some sponge cake that tasted like leftover cake and a lemon of lime pudding. Â  I guess they can charge this much since the line continues to be long. Â You won't find me waiting anymore though. Â I maybe at the Sobaya across the street or Ootoya a few blocks up.

The staff at Queens Kickshaw are perhaps the friendliest people in the world. Whenever I walk in to grab a coffee in the morning, I am greeted with a smile and genuine small talk, if there even is such a thing. I go in at least once a week (much to the chagrin of my wallet) and all the coffee drinks, from the iced lattes to the pour-overs to the drip of the day are delicious. Further, the innovative grilled cheeses are quite fantastic while the beer flights always introduce me to a new favorite. Overall, an excellent place to visit, whether you live in Astoria or are just visiting for a few hours.

Well lets start with the positives. 1) Awoesome Guacamole 2) Chicken Enchiladas were pretty good as was the mole sauce. 3) Prices were fairly reasonable. Unfortunaltey the restaurant was dredfully understaffed on a fri. night. Â Keeping in mind we were a large party it took forever to order and recieve our drinks. Â It must have taken 30 minutes to recieve the appys which were just guac and chips and my softshell crab appetizer came out ten minutes after my entree. Â I wouldn,t even have minded if it was good but it was terrible. Â ill concieved with root vegetable crust and what i think was an asparagus sauce. Â I got to take the hit on this one didnt see it tasting to great before I ordered it. Â Our server was really nice and maybe this was just an off night but a menu that really didnt excite me and small portions will probably keep me from coming back.
Great spot, you cannot go wrong. Everything is amazing from beers to all the grilled cheese sandwiches. Good spot for a date or just brunch. Highly recommended!

All I have to say is this: my beloved brother bought half a dozen macarons from here on Thursday. Â He gave them to me on Saturday.
