Â I didn't finish the last one until Tuesday (I was savoring each one sloooooowly)...and the very last one I ate (pistachio) was JUST as delicious as the very first one I tasted on Saturday. I can only imagine how much more delicious they would have been fresh. OH MY LORD. Not sure I would pay $3 per macaron (cause they are small)...but since my brother was treating...I can say unequivically that they were DELICIOUS and DELIGHTFUL. YUM. I can't wait for him to need another favor from me...cause they were super YUM!

I don't understand rave reviews about the Cuban Sandwich; maybe I just got a bad one. The bread was stale and tough on the outside and soggy on the inside, just gross. The cheese was processed Â and value store tasting, as well as the pickles. I'd expect a sandwich like this from a sketchy bodega, but not from such a popular restaurant at $9 a pop. The pork and chipotle mayo were really good, ended up scraping them off and eating them on the side. It's too bad they use such poor quality ingredients that ruin the sandwich otherwise. I really wanted to like this place because its Eco-friendly, has good links with the community and is just a nice spot to come and spend an afternoon. Maybe I'll give it a second chance someday. Maybe.

I was on a business trip to New York and had some time to kill in Manhattan on a Tuesday night. Found myself in the mood for a couple drinks and a bite to eat, so I stopped by, captivated by the name. I'm very glad to have come in. They have some great beers on tap and a well-varied Menu. Gerry (great bar tender!!) recommended the meat balls in marinara sauce - absolutely delicious. I left very satisfied with my overall experience & highly recommend a stop in if you're in the area.

Anella holds its own among the plentiful restaurants in the area. Warm rustic decor with a slight residential vibe. The service was spot on. The complimentary flower pot bread is so good it's hard not to spoil your appetite. The chicken breast dish was quality. The burger was good but not remarkable. Will definitely return to try their other dishes.

Food rule #107, fried runny egg on anything makes it better. So I have been here a few times and I am pretty happy with the Americanized Asian fusion sandwiches that they offer. I will admit, the sandwiches do come off on the sweet side though. The food: Lemongrass Chicken- It's grilled lemongrass marinated chicken thighs. This is probably my fav sandwich here, and the egg is a great addition. The lemongrass is so flavorful and the chicken thigh keeps it nice and juicy. Joju Monster- classic Vietnamese ham & headcheese, pate spread, BBQ pork with a fried egg. So this the perfect example of throwing a bunch of good shit together and the end product was really good. It is a large sandwich but everything kinda works together. This is definitely a sandwich to try. yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦ Classic- Slices of Vietnamese ham & headcheese with pate. This is their version of the Vietnamese sandwich called Banh Mi. It's a good dish, runny egg makes it better, but it was a tad too sweet for a sandwich. This is my 2nd fav. yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦ Loaded Joju Banh Mi Fries- Season & battered French fries topped w/ special house sauce, mild spicy mayo, spicy green sauce, pickled daikon & carrots, chopped cilantro & Jalapenos. This is awesome!! The fries are nice and crisp and the additions really make the dish awesome. The spiciness of the peppers counteract the sweet elements of the fries. This is a must get! yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦ Loaded Kimchi Fries- Season & battered French fries topped w/ mild spicy mayo, mild kimchi, chopped scallions, cilantro & jalapenos. I really wanted to like this dish since I like the Banh Fries so much, but this dish was just OK for me. First, these fries are drowned in the spicy mayo, the kimchi just felt like raw cabbage and the "spicy" mayo was so overwhelming sweet. It was so overwhelmingly sweet, I had to add ketchup to cut the sweetness from the spicy mayo. yelp.com/user_local_photâ€¦ Beef Bulgogi- thinly sliced rib eye of beef w/ Kimchi. I though this dish was OK, any Korean would scoff at this being a bulgogi dish. This dish comes off very sweet as well. Kakuni Pork Belly- Japanese slow-braised pork belly. I thought this dish was OK, I felt like the pork belly had a less fatty texture and wasn't as tender as I would want or think pork belly should be. Pork Spring Rolls- a very run of the mill spring roll. I would skip it, it's a sandwich shop not a full service restaurant. Crispy Chicken Wings- I wasn't crazy about this dish. The chicken was kinda bland.

I've been here a few times now, and this place never disappoints! From ordering to receiving the food, it was within 5mins! I've never seen this place so packed before, but even though the waiter/waitresses were storming back and forth, the quality of the food was perfect! The chicken and fries combo was so tasteful and tender. And even the fries was perfect crispy. Thanks for a wonderful meal! I will miss this place when I leave!

Went for brunch with my wife and mother. Â We all loved it . Â The ambiance was terrific. Â The brunch was fantastic and came with a blood orange mamosa. Â Three for breakfast with coffee and drink was only $45.00. Â We traveled from Mt Kisco NY (55 minutes) and it was well worth it. Â I will be back.
The corn = Â LOVE The margarita Â = LOVE The price = LOVE Tiny space = Â not so much Pretty solid choice. Minus one star for that table that is seated so oddly right in front of the bathroom!
Good, Fast, and Cheap. What more can you ask for? Space is very limited so beware if you are in a group.

I had one of the best dining experiences of my life at this at this restaurant. It's a pricy place and a reservation is hard to get. But for a special occasion I can't think of a better place to go. The restaurant is beautiful. The best way I can describe is, it's the type of place you might find a 40's movie star drinking a scotch. The bar tender was helpful in picking out cocktails, and the waiter was super helpful in helping us decide what to eat. He even engaged us while we talked about food and NYC, even though he was extremely busy. He talked us through the suckling pig entree. It was a big undertaking at 90 bucks, but he ensured us that it will feed the four of us. He also told us about how we can order a side of extra parts, like pork shoulder and cheak for an extra price. To me this was one of the best parts of the meal, and we wouldn't have thought to get it without his suggestion. Before it was brought out to us, a waiter brought the pig to the table before it was cooked, asking our approval as if it were an uncorked bottle of wine. I was very immpressed. When it was served, it turned out to be one of the best things I've ever tasted, it was one of those meals you will just never forget. The skin was so crispy and about an inch thick. Under that skin was the most tender, juicy pork I've ever eaten. I'm no chef but I swear it had to have been slow cooked for days, for weeks! For dessert we ordered one of my favorites- affogato, and the waiter came out to poor the espresso over the creamy vanilla gilato himself. Again, impressed. Another point to make about the service - I tweeted at the restaurantseveral times, expressing my excitement for the meal to come, and they responded almost immediatly each time, to the delight of me and my dining buddies. This was on a busy holiday weekend night. This may be a bit dramatic but at the end of the night I actually hugged the waiter. I will never forget this night, this meal and this restaurant. Between the service, the atmosphere, the drinks and the food, it's a NYC gem.

Came in hungry and a bit tipsy. Â Had pork belly buns, BBQ sandwich, apple/kim chee/bacon plate, Pork Shoulder Steak, Spicy Pork Sausage & Rice Cakes and Grilled Hanger Steak (no, not all by myself). Â I thought that the pork belly buns and the spicy pork sausage were the best, while the shoulder, hanger steak and the apple/kim chee were only fine. Â  The pork belly buns were served a la Peking duck, and I particularly liked the rice cakes, which were like Asian tater tots. Â  Also the "smoked jowl" in the apple kim chee looked and tasted suspiciously like good old bacon. Â Oh, and while I did not have the $200 pork butt, I cannot believe it is much different than the butt I marinated and slow roasted this weekend at a total cost of about $12. Â Bottom line: good and solid, but not worth great excitement.

Lunch is about $10 at this place! It's probably the only place around my job that is decently priced for what you get being that I do work on Fifth Avenue. The portions are huge and the food is pretty good. It's always packed during lunch hours though but they take care of you pretty quickly. Oh and make sure you don't forget the green sauce! Overall a nice grab & go spot if you work in the neighborhood.

This is one of my favorite restaurants IN THE WORLD. I first came when the restaurant was located a few blocks from their current location (and when they used to have the Bouley Bakery across the street), but I like their new location just as much (I think I like the down stair area the most). I always have a suburb meal and great time. The service is excellent and the decor just perfect - so inviting and so elegant. Update- made a reservation to go again and found out that for lunch the down stair area is only open during the weekend.

After a day a long day at work this restaurant truly hit the spot. The waitress and manager's service was attentive and helpful. The brick oven pizza was perfectly crunchy and filled with the freshest of vegetables. Â The cannolis were so fresh and delicious. Â The tiramisu was the best I have ever had. I will definitely be back.

I really want to give 3 stars, but if the definition of 2 stars is "Meh I've experienced better" than 2 stars it is. Â Presentation of the ramen was appetite enticing. Â I had the Minca salt broth with garlic, now that was VERY tasty broth. Â My friends had the shoyu broth, and theirs was too salty. Â The chasu (pork) was delectably delicious, nice and tender and fatty. Â But the point of ramen is the noodles, right? The sign said "ramen factory" Â but why did it taste like our noodles were not housemade???? Â I had thin, which was recommended, one friend had the thick. Â They both did not taste housemade. Â They did not have that freshly made springy chewy texture that you come to expect with a good bowl of ramen. Â In conclusion, if you're in NY and have a STRONG craving for ramen and you're in the neighborhood, then by all means.

Great new spot just a couple of blocks from my apartment. They have good food and good coffee (I haven't tried the smoothies yet) and play great music. There's a couch in the back and it's the perfect place to come study on a cold afternoon. They lose one star on three points: 1. the exhaust never seems to work and the place reeks of smoke, to the point that it burns the eyes. 2. they are closed on Mondays and close way too early the rest of the week.3. there's no sign and the places is usually mostly empty. I passed by a bunch of times without noticing it and only found out it was here because my neighbor told me. Hopefully they'll get these details sorted out, because this is exactly the kind of place this neighborhood needs.
what can i say, Freeman's has been excellent since day one...great atmosphere and great food.

I just happened to look for a restaurant to go to prior to the entertainment of the Robin Hood Foundation's benefit last week, and came across Scarpetta, and their 3 year anniversary menu. Â At first, I thought I wouldn't get a reservation, since the original 5:30 seating I saw was gone within 3 minutes, but after refreshing the page several times, it came back up, and of course I had to take it, since there wasn't an opening again until the end of the week. It was a little difficult to find, mainly because we were walking on the opposite side of the street, and the sign saying "Scarpetta" can really only be seen on the same side. Â However, they did have large numbers for the street address, which made it easier to find from the opposite side, after I had to look up the address. Â We came in and sat at the bar, and glanced at their drink menu. Â I wasn't really feeling a drink, but my bf got a captain and ginger, and I just got a soda, which ended up being about $18. We were seated in one of the booth/chair set ups. Â I didn't think the booth would be as comfortable as it was, since it appeared to be at a 90 degree angle, but it wasn't too bad. Â The decor was really nice and home-y; very comfortable to sit in. Â The best part was the sunroofs that were open, allowing fresh air and sunshine in. We chose from the 3 year anniversary menu, because we were able to try many items all at once. Â I had the creamy polenta, spaghetti, duck breast, and chocolate cake. Â He had the yellowtail, short rib and bone marrow agnolotti, black cod, and mango and white chocolate napoleon. Â Everything was absolutely amazing. Â  The creamy polenta was served separately from the mushrooms, which was nice because I was able to add as I ate, rather than mix all at once. Â The spaghetti was to die for...simple, but very tasty. Â The duck was cooked perfectly, and the chocolate cake was very rich too. Â I had a cup of coffee, which helped wash it down. The yellowtail was very nice, the salt on top gave a nice texture and taste contrast. Â The agnolotti was very smooth and rich in flavor. Â The black cod was great; crispy skin with a moist, tender texture to the fish. Â I saved the best for last. Â I think the napoleon was impeccable. Â The mango mousse was full of mango flavor, and they provided thin sheets of white chocolate, which balanced with the mango. I appreciated the fact that despite being a prix fixe menu, they did not mess up the quality of the food that came out. Â Everything was excellent. It was pretty quiet, even when the dining room was 3/4 full, which was nice, so we didn't have to yell across the table. Â It was also cool to see Bob Tuschman, from the Food Network, also in the restaurant. Â To me, it said that this restaurant is good, if he enjoys going there too. All in all, we will definitely be back. Â I cannot wait for the spaghetti and napoleon again!
The smoked mackerel with thinly sliced turnips and radishes and wheat berries. Â Stunning

oysters are my jam and upstates HH didn't disappoint. Their HH includes several choices for $1 oysters paired with a variety of craft brews. On the day I went, they had shigokus on the menu (my fave!!!), so I upstate already ha. A piece of my heart. Hahah. Cool vibe. Attentive servers. yummy oysters. Sold! PS Be especially nice to your server and they'll reward you with delicious slivers of the secret recipe whiskey cake. It's not on the menu so don't even try to order it

If you love spicy Jamaican food then this is the place for you! I think this is the best Island food in NY and it is worth the trip for authentic Jamaican food. I took my whoe family last week and there was something that we al ordered and enjoyed! Try the fish dishes and also the patties...ENJOY!

I just love this place. I came here awhile back with my sister and I met up with a friend last night for a quick bite to eat and it just gets better. I was slightly surprised that at 7:30pm on a Friday we were able to get seated really quickly and the place had a nice crowd to it. I like the decor and it's nicely lit inside. The host was super nice and our waiter was great and sharing his favorites, the specials and helping us make up our mind on what to order. I always start off with the Blackberry Lemonade and I could seriously drink that stuff by the gallon, it's so yummy! I got the turkey burger and it was one of the best I have had. There was a tasty cranberry aoili sauce and avocados on it with your typical American fries on the side. My friend got the steak and it looked good from across the table, but very filling. The portions are pretty large here. For dessert we got the fried oreos and they were so yummy. Cooked to perfection with a yummy espresso chocolate sauce and ice cream on the side. There were so many things on the menu that sounded delicious that I need to go back and try other things. I really wanted to try the Brussel Sprout Salad and I heard their Mac N' Cheese is really yummy. The BLT Salmon Sandwhich sounded pretty good. It's definitely a fun stop on a night out and the place is open 24/7 so it doesn't get much better than that. The service wasn't pushy at all. They let us stay and chat even after we payed the bill. I can't wait to go back again.

Come for the food. Tolerate the swelling masses of hungover hipsters who will wait hours on end for Orlin's pancakes and omelettes. The cafe's roomy interior allows for groups, but heaven forbid if you can't hear the hostess whisper-calling your party. My group and I ended up waiting an hour after she supposedly called our party twice. But once seated, everything was better. The pumpkin pancakes with cinnamon yogurt were excellent, if not a little dense, and the Mediterranean-inspired egg dishes cannot be missed. Â I ordered my poached eggs with a side of avocado (which at $4, seemed a bit rich). The food is indeed tasty, but the ordeal of waiting makes me hesitant to go back at peak hours.
good food, rustic ambiance, but wait is too long and very inefficient! if you have time to kill to make it to brooklyn and wait around, it's worth a trip.

First time ever dining there and I must say I left very satisfied..the restaurant isn't that big and you may feel like you're sitting on top of the people sitting next to you (can definitively hear every bit of their conversation.) wouldn't do a large party here, four people at most, any more then that is going to be somewhat uncomfortable. The service was very good...food very flavorful drinks yummy yummy yummy...would visit again and will recommend.

This is, by far, the best place been to in New York. I come to this restaurant on average, once a month. It never disappoints. The ingredients are always seasonal and fresh and the preparation is never over thought. Â Considering how often I go, you'd think they'd miss the mark at least once, but never have. The chef does amazing things lamb. And the gnocchi app, whatever preparation is always a winner. Fish dishes are always light and never to buttery, the way that fish should be. And the service is fantastic.

Went there today and it was really good!!! The service was great. Our server (I think his name was Aaron?) kept coming and refilling our drinks and making sure we were taken care of, even though the restaurant was fairly busy. I ordered a cheeseburger which was ok. My boyfriend ordered chicken (I tasted and it was really good). But the cheesecake now that was really good! I read some of the reviews prior to going so taking advice I ordered the original cheesecake with strawberry. I would definitely recommend this place.

One of Fort Greene's best new gems, and I keep wanting to bring everyone I know here with me because everyone should enjoy the deliciousness that is at Lulu and Po. The (very attractive) staff are really really nice, not at all pretentious, and really know their complex menu. The kitchen is open and the chefs seem to be enjoying their work, probably because they know everything they are making is incredible, and the small restaurant has a very chill vibe. I personally enjoy the whole open kitchen thing too, and so this makes the small space seem even more like a welcome and cozy place. The trout is so perfectly seared, and charred scallion bits cover the skin, mixing in well with capers and whatever else they put on it. The burger is always a home run, and the lentils mix a dollop of sour cream with enough spice to give them a kick, and make Â lentils all of a sudden become interesting again. I am also a huge fan of their cheese selections (all local) and their spanish octopus comes with a refreshing mint jalapeÃ±o sauce. I recently had the bone marrow tacos - this was actually my first time trying marrow, and I decided that I simply am not a fan of its texture really, although I could tell that the bones had been very well roasted and were packed with flavor, and the side topping of cilantro and pickled red onions was an appropriate complement to the marrow and the corn tortilla. Â Oh, and the fries are ridiculous (in the good way) and their house salad always has nice crisp greens, and lovely sugar coated walnuts to offset the more acidic dressing. I will also say that I love the tapas portions they offer, because I never leave too full, and have a personal dislike for the culture of excessive portions. However, between my boyfriend and I, we will easily finish 6 things, and still have room for dessert. So, the only down side is that it all adds up, and so I can't eat here every day, and instead have to limit my visits to once every 2 weeks or so. In the long run this is probably a good thing because it just wouldn't be fair for me to be able to eat food this delicious every day of my life. At first they were cash only, which annoyed me but I kept coming back, and eventually they figured this out and started to accept credit cards. Thank you Lulu and Po! Â This place definitely puts Fort Greene on the NYC foodie destination map.

Best restaurant not only in Williamsburg but in the whole world. Â I am lucky enough to live down the street, if I could afford it I would eat there every day. Â Over the past 2 years I have eaten there on average once a week and I have never had anything that wasn't amazing! Â Dinner is awesome Â but nothing beats the country breakfast and a large bloody mary on a sleepy Sunday afternoon!!! Â Also amazing are their other restaurants Romans and Marlow and Sons. Â Another win is Marlow and Daughters...when we BBQ we buy all of of the ingredients there..ground beef, cheese and buns and we have Diner burgers at home!

Four stars for the upscale Latin food and shic decor. Â 5 stars for the FREE SANGRIA BAR 8-DEEP ON SUNDAYS. Â And from my Barcelona days I am a sangria snob. Â Calle nails it. Tune ceviche was great. Â Sesame calamari was amazing and I swear there was some seafood below the four layers of sweet fried goodness. Â Empanadas were passable but I'd recommend passing. Â Bacon wrapped dates solid all around...let's face it, bacon wrap anything and you can't miss. Deconstructed Al Pastor tacos were very good, but not true Pastor...more like a Carnitas. Â But solid.

Awesome brunch place. Food is very very well prepared, service is great, but the wait sucks. Can't really blame them considering so many people want to eat there... Cheddar Waffles were amazing! I would Def come back here! Yum!

I never yelp but this place is something to talk about I had gnocchi and salmon steak both were really good not mention the live jazz band in the back ground was soothing to my ears... This place is a gem...

Finally tried a new dish and what a dish it was! Pork belly with pickled cabbage was TO DIE FOR!! The problem is that one can't eat this food too often, or one's heart with clog immediately, and one will have an aneurysm. The only reason why one can't try too many new things is because of the limited visits, one MUST have the dishes one craves leaving no stomach space for new items. Boo hoo.

I was craving for tapas for a looong time. The only problem was that I just could not find a place, which sounded tasty to me for a while. Finally I found Â Yuca Bar! I read a few reviews about the place and decided to give it a try on a Tuesday Loco Tapas Evening. When we got there there were still plenty of tables available however when we left there was a pretty big line there. So make sure and get there on time for your Loco Tapas Treat (around 5-6pm I guess would be the best time). Food: we got shrimp ceviche, Quesadilla de langosta(with lobster), Quesadilla de Champignon(wild mushroom), Mejillones al Tequila(tequila flamed mussel in a Chipotle Lobster broth.Served w/ garlic bread), Taquitos de Pollo (grilled chicken breast with Avocado & tomatilo salsa). For two of us 5 of those little dishes was plenty! Each dish was absolutely unique however they also matched each other pretty well at the same time. Shrimp ceviche was absolutely fantastic: I was thinking about getting a glass of sangria in the beg. but after tasting this shrimp with a wild mixture of exotic tropical flavors I completely forgot about it. So yes - my sangria was shrimp ceviche! Can you believe this?! :) Mussels were perfectly cooked: juicy but not raw accompanied by a wonderful sauce, which we literally almost licked from a plate. Our waitress was very kind and brought us a couple more pieces of garlic bread(also very good flavorful bread as american bread usually sucks) - she probably knows herself how good that lobster mussels sauce is!! Wild mushroom dish was exceptionally flavorful and had a rich mushroom taste - just how I like it. I found myself in the memories of my childhood when my mother used to cook some fresh mushrooms and aroma was all over the kitchen. YUM! Chicken accompanied with salsa and a guacamole with a little spice was wonderful and amazingly cooked - very soft and not oily at all. I can not say that lobster dish was that great - maybe it is because I did not enjoy a little bitter after-taste of it. But hey - making dish with a lobster is already a challenge so I prefer to eat it by itself :) I will sure go back and try more tapas dishes. Good night and good luck ;)
Perfect!! Seated right away, the white pizza is delicious!! The staff was friendly and very efficient. I loved everything about it!

I loved the Greek salad I order but was even better was seeing a youngster we were with devour a healthy pizza along with a blue berry muffin. Many times healthy version of good reliable staples turn kids off but this is one place where that did not happen at all! Just wish there was more seating for those that want to order and eat as opposed to take out.

It's all good! Â Four of us met at Upstate last Sunday night, they don't take reservations, but just after 7 pm with a few minutes wait we managed to nab a table and commence an evening of pure seafood bliss. Â Service was excellent from the moment we reached the door, not having to wait an hour while an empty table was being reset or cleared helped. Â  Starting with some West and Â East coast oysters we all discovered our preference for the latter, the waitress recommended several of her faves which we all agreed were at the top of our list too. Â I had the sword fish main knowing it's not one of my favorite fishes to consume because of it's heavier texture but found my meal to be extremely tasty and satisfying, I probably wouldn't get the swordfish again but that's just personal preference and nothing to do with the meal I had, which was delicious regardless of fish choice. My friends were pleased with the beer selection and I stuck to wine. Â My hubby had the seafood stew which he loved (not quite as good as Aquagrill he confessed) but definitely up there and very close. Â Upstate has a small menu but everything on it's well cooked and maintained at a high level of consistency. Â I'd like to return to sample more oysters and try something else off their menu. Â  I don't think you can go wrong Â with this place if you enjoy seafood.
For the first time, I must say it is GREAT!!! Â My mom had fried AND BBQ shrimp and she loved it!!

I am extremely jealous of the people that live near here. Seriously. Recently visited NYC on a whim, and luckily discovered this fabulous gem because I was hungry, and our hotel room wasn't ready yet. It's 2:30pm on a Saturday, and my friend and I are wandering around looking for a quick bite and maybe a drink (or two). Brunch until 4pm? $5 brunch cocktails? No wait? Sign me up. Â  The menu had a ton of awesome choices, mainly your usual suspects with a twist. They even have a section for pickled vegetables! Since it was my first time here, I went with the one of their benedicts: spinach and chorizo topped with sriracha hollandaise. Anything with sriracha is always a plus in my book. Home fries are included, probably added to sop all that eggy-goodness. Sold. As for brunch cocktails, my heart was set on the Bloody Mary. Probably not the best choice, since it really was quite different with the BBQ flavor in it. I switched over to the white sangria, while my friend stayed with the mimosa. Both of those were very good. The water was served in adorable mason glasses. Nice touch. While waiting for my meal, we decide to do picklebacks. Why not? It was recommended to do the pineapple mint habanero, but they were unfortunately out. So our lovely server, Nick, decides to do one with us. Even with the traditional flavor, the shot was divine. The meal was just as I had imagined it would be, and it was quickly eaten with just a few potatoes left as stragglers. Great meal, friendly service, cool vibe, and I'm smitten over this place. Sit by the window for some great people-watching!

Bo Ssam Lunch Group Dinning What TV Character Would Dine Here: Imagine if the Friends cast (Monica, Rachel, Phoebe, Ross, Chandler, Joey) lived real lives and didn't see each other 24/7. This is a great place to come in a large group and have a great meal to catch up. It reminds me of the last supper. Good For: Group dinning at brunch time Overall Quant Score: Please review quant profile in my profile. Pros: Simple, Straightforward, Large bang for your buck Cons: Table and hands can get a little messy as you are eating with your hands, New plates could have come quicker Food Wrap Up Summary: Arrived at 1:00pm on a Sunday for a late lunch. This place can get very busy and I would never head here without a reservation. Reservation were made 2-3 weeks ahead of time. Food Rundown (*Designated must try item): *Group bo ssÃ¤m - The bo ssÃ¤m (ssÃ¤m is korean for enclosed or wrapped) includes a slow cooked pork shoulder, a dozen oysters, and two bowls each of white rice, bibb lettuce, ssÃ¤m sauce (korean bbq sauce), kimchi and ginger scallion sauce. guests are encouraged to make wraps with the pork and condiments or eat as they please. The pork shoulder from niman ranch is cured overnight, then slow roasted for 6-8 hours with a brown sugar and kosher salt rub. $225 for your entire party, not including tax or tip. If you are carnivore like I am, the pork here is as tender and suckling as it comes. Grab a bunch of the inner core meat as it is the most tender. Between each wrap take a swig of wine to cleanse the pallet. For each new wrap grab a different sauce to try. *Pork Buns - Delicious fatty meat cut from the belly of the pig. It is wrapped in a white bun. However, watch out for the splash factor as the food is quite greasy and the pork belly has a tendency to fall out of the bun. Best bet is to eat this with a fork. Â  White Wine Sangria w/ Almonds - Thought this drink was quite plain. However, I like their touch with grinding up almonds in the drink. Tip: Reservation needs to be made in advance, Go last and get the inner core meat as it is the most tender and fatty, Grab enough meat for a few wraps and put it on your plate. It is difficult grabbing meat for each wrap.

The tacos are so good! The chicken and spicy pork tacos are highly recommend!! This is surely the best mexico food in Spanish harlem~* sometimes it may take them a while to make food, so I suggest you to order the food and go pick up.

The staff is very friendly and helpful. My sister and I shared the chopped salad with spicy grilled chicken and sweet potato fries with mango chutney. The order was just the right amount for 2 people and very reasonably priced. The chicken was perfectly grilled and the heat was great.

We visited this little restaurant while visiting NYC for the US Open. Â My wife had us traveling all over NYC for vegan restaurants. Â Not being a vegan or even a vegetarian, I had had enough. Â While in Brooklyn, I yelped for a close restaurant know for chicken. Â I went here and had the chicken sandwich (minus the avocado) with the fries, macaroni and cheese (to sample) and a brownie (for the road). Â Though it was way too much food, I tried my best to finish it all. Â The sandwich was just the right size, grilled, and very tender. Â It had Turkey bacon, which was new... but thoroughly enjoyed. Â  The staff knowing that I was a first time customer, went above and beyond to make sure I knew what to choose. Â I would definitely recommend this to anyone in the Brooklyn area.

This is definitely the best place for hotpot in the city. The ambiance is great! They dress it up for all the holidays and play great music. There's a small private room in the back for about 8-9 people that's great for a small party. Definitely always make a reservation! Aside from being one of our favorite places ever, they're great for parties. We have done birthday parties here and other large group events. We recently had some family in town for our wedding and took everyone here for dinner before things got started for the weekend. They loved it and the owner even came over to congratulate us and brought us a bottle of champagne! The food is incredible. You can do mixed bowls of 2 different kinds of soup side by side. The herbal and spicy are my favorites. We always tell everyone to order one protein and one veggie and we get a meat plate for the table. There's so much food and we love how much fun it is to see what everyone picks. Love this place!

This Brunch Rocks Random stop in on a Sunday with friend.......cool, chill vibe and dig that copper type bar....sat at bar since tables full at 1PM so a good sign: Great Bartender...Check Great Service....Check Chill Vibe...Check Stiff Drinks...Check Authentic Mexican Brunch Menu...Check 25$ Brunch special/ unltd bloodys/mimosas....bloodys are great..they put a tad of smokey chipolte sauce in them anda mix of salt t on rim and gives them a killer smokey flavor.....hibiscus mimosas also tasty. The food is plentiful, egg dishes rock and get the guac..yeah its 11$ but its awesome...simple well done authentic mexican food done correctly... I am going back soon...forget the crowds at POCO......Bartender told me original location was park slope...this is a newer outpost.... GO!

Completely average brunch. Due to past reviews and the ridiculous hour and fifteen minute wait, I was pretty sure we were going to be in for one slammin' brunch. Nope. If you know one thing about me, it's the fact that I finish everything that's on my plate. As long as it was good/great/amazing/phenomenal. My plate was 47% clean. Completely average. Nothing to write home about & certainly not worth going back a second time. Outdoor seating was THE highlight on such a nice day.

Cool adaptive reuse of an old school (hence the name Public) New Zealand food is delicious. Atmosphere and clientele is classy but relaxed. It's expensive, but very worth it, and probably less expensive if you aren't destroying bottles of wine with each course. Great for a date, birthday dinner, or any slightly special occasion. Â I love Public - they serve kangaroo which is extremely hard to cook properly and they did it wonderfully!

This place is the cutest! I had fish tacos and that delicious lemonade thing. The outdoor seating was so cute and I felt like I was in Cuba! Â Huge fan and the catfish was delicioso! I want to really sit there all summer, listen to the fountain and enjoy the sun.

We came here for my birthday not expecting much since everywhere in Brooklyn is usually overrated. However, this place was a wonderful surprise! We tried three different oyster plates, all fresh and so tasty! My husband got the brick chicken, AMAZING! Never knew chicken could taste so good. I got a pretty tasty fish sandwich, which I can't remember contained exactly what but I inhaled it nonetheless. Dessert was top notch as well. Service was quirky, but efficient!

Very anti-climatic after reading all the hype. Good for a one time gimmick, but not much more than that. The fries are OK; not bad, but not great either. The "double" frying thing really produced no noticible difference in the quality of the fries other than making quite a few of them overcooked. The sauces were very ordinary too. Halfway through the meal, we both said that the fries at a place like McDonalds would have been better. We also got a small poutine (a Canadian dish), which was very unique. Basically it's fries, gravy and fermented cheese. Very flavorful, but a tad on the heavy side. I wouldn't run back for it either now that I think about it. In the end, Pommes Frites is about average I guess. I suppose not every place is a life changing experience.

It was great living a stone's throw away from this place last summer. Â The vibe at this place is characteristic of the great atmosphere at Fort Greene. Â  There was always an interesting mix of people and it got crowded often, especially during film nights. Â I haven't tried too much of the food here, but they do have really good and cheap local brewed beers. Â The decoration is funky, and they have eco-friendly bathrooms and even a smoothie-maker bike. Â A nice place to hang out during the summer for a couple of drinks.

I started coming here when they only had one cart and the combos were $5. Once the halal guys started getting more business they added a second one right across the street which I keep telling people to go to since the line is shorter and the food is the same. I went back a month ago, my go to guy Ramin who's hooked me up by never having to wait in line apparently no longer works there so I had to wait like everyone else. I probably won't be going back as much since the food is only bearable after a night drinking. Everyone that I've brought here has gotten hooked.. they say its like crack. The yogurt sauce is the best and the hot sauce is extremely spicy so lay off if you can't handle it.

I don't know why, but I've been on a Thai craving spree lately, and the weekend hattrick began w/ this joint. It was either here or Kin Shop, so HD will have to take a back seat. I found the apps, well one of them, to be on the weaker side, but the mains and dessert more than compensated. Ouch on the doubling in prices of appetizers for dinner vs lunch. YMMV w/ the levels of spicyness, so be forewarned! Ditto w/ portion sizes. Case in point: our pork dish was bigger than our beef dish. Also, our pork was spicier than our beef dish, even though the beef dish had 3 spicy stars next to i vs 2. Dishes were cranked out in Santa Workshop fashion w/o sacrificing detail. The narrow space reminds me of Graffiti, but with elbow room. The major shocker was when the waitress announced that the dessert was on the house courtesy of the Chef. I had to Google him to see what he looked like, as I have never heard/seen DB before. This had me looking around for lurking eyes. Him being a JG alum and owning 2 other restys, shouldn't 'I' be the one doing the stalking?Now I know how Brad Pitt feels on a daily basis. Ordered: -Crispy Shrimp Sesame Crepe ($6) [shrimp mousse, sesame seed, lime wedge, kaffir lime curd] - almost like a Korean pajun, crispy, came out nice and hot, def made to order and lots of love in this, didn't taste too shrimpy though, loved how the chef celebrated the kaffir lime in this dish, tart and sweet, the sesame seeds made this dish SING! -Chicken Curry Puffs ($6) [caramelized chicken, onion, sweet potato, cucumber relish] - the weakest dish of them all IMO, tasted like an Asian empanada, nothing but mush inside -Ratchaburi Crab & Pork Dry Noodle ($9) [handmade egg noodle, roasted pork, lump crab meat, yu choy, scallion] - Chinese ppl would laugh and call this pork pork noodle a cheap dish, but alas, the subtlely of the handmade noodles was a stroke of pure genius here, kinda like HK noodles but chewier. -Wok Chili Turmeric w/ Beef ($10) [kaffir lime leaf, thai chili, seasonal vegetables, turmeric chili puree sauce] - not as spicy as I expected, flavors meshed well and overall solid dish, each herb and spice shined through here! -Wok Curry Paste w/ Pork ($10) [string bean, thai eggplant, bamboo shoot, basil, kaffir lime curry sauce] - way too spicy for me, had to go to the bathroom to brush my tongue, then take the rest home, loved the eggplant in this, which appeared to be dark green tomatillo slices, had me fooled, great textural contrast w/ the crunchiness of the bamboo shoots -Pork Cracklings ($2) [rec w/ Pure Thai Noodles] - did NOT go w/ the noodles, don't know what they are talking about -Sticky Rice w/ Yam Custard (free) - normally $6.50, came wrapped in a banana leaf pyramid held together w/ a bamboo toothpick, the star of the show, I'm still baffled as to how this arrived at our table gratis Total came out to $29/pp after everything P.S. Pics or it didn't happen, you say? Well, fair enough. Pic: i51.tinypic.com/2n6yf0h.â€¦ Pics are up on my FB...

I have heard/read SO many good things, so one lazy Sunday when I didn't feel like cooking, I ordered take away. Hot chicken, potato salad, collard greens, and Mac n cheese. I do believe the take away was not as good due to the fact that it wasn't eaten right away, piping hot, so I will factor that in... Overall: food was ok. I could have cooked the sides WAY better - not the best I've ever had, and I based my choices on yelp reviews. You guys let me down :( I do believe (my opinion) that those who find this place just to die for, haven't had this kind of cooking before. I grew up on collards and potato salad - and I have had better (much better - never appreciated how good it was till now, when everybody swears by collards and kale all of a sudden - but not everyone can cook them well). It's funny. Wish my grandmother was here to see this. She would love to see how everyone is eating kale and collards nowadays like out of nowhere... when I was small, this was solely for 'certain' households (I'll just leave it at that). Basically, the collards weren't seasoned well. Neither was the potato salad. And the Mac was boring. They should have added some interesting cheeses to it, or something. I've had far better Mac from my other grandmother. It must be baked. I've just never been a fan if it unless it's baked - with bacon, loaded with goodies. That's how I likes it :) Anyway: the chicken lived up to the hype-ish. Even as takeaway, it was still madd crunchy. Didn't lose it's yummy. Again, not my favorite fried chicken, but good nonetheless. Medium heat was spiced well. Also the cornbread was ok too. Try it for yourself. You may find it absolutely delish or just a good meal for the moment...

Mixed review: Â  I had the best waiter a girl could have, but honestly, I'm very disappointed in the quality of the food. Â  Not all the food though.I lived in Colombia on two different occasions, and cook colombian food frequently. Â Their empanadas were flavor less, and for $5 you would think you would get a little more. Â But what really shocked me was the lack of flavor that the steak (asado) had. Â I got the Bandeja Paisa a favorite at most Colombian restaurants, and the portions were more than generous for this, my daughter and I shared. Â  However, I was disappointed because the steak was flavorless. Â I tried to put "ahi" Â the colombian hot sauce and it was this watery vinegary mess that they "bottle" there. Â Why bother bottling it because it was crap. Â Anyone who has had aji know that its a little thicker, not watery of vinegary. Â I added salt and kept eating. The chorizo they have is delicious, amongst the best I've had. Â  The batido de Mora, Delicious and the plates that kept coming out were amazing. Â I think they are trying to merge too many different flavors and not really giving the best to anyone dish. Â I will be back though because the garlic chicken smelled like the most amazing thing I've ever smelled. Â  This was my second time there and the first time was better we were there on a Tuesday early so who know if maybe there was a different cook. It was odd too that this busboy got very offended that I spoke spanish to him it just came out, its a habit I admit but it wasn't that serious. Other than that, I love love love my waiter and he'd be a great waiter anywhere . Â Like I said the flavors were off, but the first time I went there it was amazing! Â  So I'll go back another time to enjoy something different.
This is honestly my favorite place in the slope/south slope. Great service, great atmosphere, and INCREDIBLE FOOD. I've gone here several times and not one complaint.

So relaxing, and the food has never disappointed. Perfect location, steps from my favourite cool down spot--Brooklyn Museum. Ambience: Casual cool. Communal farmhouse type Â table in the middle, with outlets for our ever present devices. Also a few tables lining the perimeter for more intimate dining. Service: Good. Food: Great. Fresh, fresh, fresh!
I will sum it up as this: multiple food orgasms in my mouth. see other reviews for food.

We'd been eyeing El Amacen for a while, and had the chance to go this weekend. Â We called about an hour before to make a reservation, and were seated at a cozy shared table when we arrived. Â We asked the waitress for recommendations for everything from the wine to the main meal, and were happy with everything. Â Steak dishes looked better than the others - I had the short rib, which is the house specialty and delicious. Â Try the avocado fries too. Yum.

The venue is pretty, very romantic setting. Â All dishes were elegantly present. Â However, I had a higher expectation in their food for the price tag I paid. Â After all, I was there to have a meal. Â All the sides were too salty. Â The over-seasoning had killed the fresh ingredients.

Seriously this was probably the BEST burger I have ever had!!! Â GO HERE AND ORDER THE BACON ROYAL!!!! Â So glad we were taken here, but then again - it was recommended by the YELP NY TEAM!! Â Such a great environment, service and place to hang out and talk. Â I will go back to this place when I am in New York again! Â The Onion rings ARE THE BEST!!!

Great deal if you're looking for a 10 course! This is Traif's sister restaurant, and it's just as good. I love love love Tapas! Traif is my top choice but Xixa is also great! Get the tasting menu for $40 per person. The foie gras al pastor and pineapple was one of my favorite dishes of the night. You're able to request a dish for the tasting. The rib, duck lettuce wrap, shrimp taco, were all one of my top choices. The edamame was GREAT too! Great snack, spicy and great flavor. The last dish we had was the octopus which I did not enjoy. They shouldn't have had that as the last dish! Other then that everything else was a win. We had two desserts as well. The carrot cake was amazing. I'm not a carrot cake fan either, but this carrot cake had me coming back for more. Our second dessert was some sort of green tea with coffee ice cream. At the end they also gave us all a piece of chocolate to finish the meal. Such a great deal for all this food, definitely can't get this within Manhattan.

Ok, 'yes' Eataly is so crowded sometimes that it makes it difficult to enjoy, and yes, there are often throngs of tourists which I find entertaining because often I hear them speaking Italian and wonder what they are thinking of our interpretation of their culture- however, the quality of food, the unlimited variety and transition from restaurant to piazza to shopping market are incredible. Â Though I wouldn't do weekly shopping here, I love picking up imported cheeses, fresh baked breads and good quality pastas for cooking at home. Â Totally worth the throngs of people in order to get some amazing food. Â I highly recommend the cafe as well, and love that everyone stands at the "bar" to drink their coffee-- for anyone who has gone to Europe, that is pretty authentic. Â So give credit where credit is due and eat up :)

Waited an hour and a half last Winter in 12 degree temps and suffered frostbite as a result. Â Bass-terds wouldn't let us in. Â Of course, there were no tables but whose fault is that? Â Not mine! Â  I just want a damn pizza! Scary wait on weekends - charming inside, not mind-blowing pizza but very good and fresh, great calzone which is quite large (like Lucali himself - from what I have heard). Spike likes it, Jigga likes it - you will like it too.

Totally worth the wait, or if you're smart you'll go early to avoid a long wait. The ramen is delicious, listen to their suggested toppings, and their pork buns live up to the hype. Great ambiance for any occasion, date, groups, casual lunch.
pizza was good but to be honest the plain the better i felt sometimes too much is too much for instance i dont like cherries on my pizza or limoncello on my pizza... other than that delicious!

Their truffle fries were incredible. I loved their ricotta too. I didn't have to wait for a table both times I went. Quick service, but their utensils were a little dirty. I found some food particles in my water cup, too.
I love this place. Delicious brunch menu - I crave the eggs Benedict all the time! - Stumptown coffee and great atmosphere means this is one of my new favorites!

Am I missing something here? I've been wanting to eat at Five Leaves for over a year. Considering the Yelp reviews I figured it was a guaranteed good time. Hmmm.... Ok first off this place is really tiny and the tables barely accomodate the food and beverage. Also, the chairs are REALLY uncomfortable. Not a very relaxing place... We ordered the meat and olive plate (dont remember the name) for an appetizer. It was OK. I think for the price, they could add some cheese to it. Plus, whats with the two skinny, flat breadstick-like things? What am I supposed to do with that? My friend and I split the Five Leaves burger with the infamous truffle fries. We both looked at each other and said "...it's OK...". I dont know what all the fuss is about. Yeah, the truffle fries are good but, really?? Worth all the fuss??? NO! The burger was good but I had a better burger at Paul's. I'm not being a hater...I REALLY wanted to like this place. Will I be back? meh, probably not.

Great Pizza!!! Â My roommate and I order pizza from here all the time. Â The Margherita is a favorite with san marzano tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, and fresh basil. Â The Toscana is also very good with fresh mozzarella, cracked egg, prosciutto, and black pepper. Â  The bar area is somewhat small. Â Great spot to go for lunch if you are dragging some "out of towners" down to see the Statue of Libery/Ellis Island. Â Walking distance from the Battery Park, just opposite the Ritza Carlton.

Public Enemy said it best "Don't Believe The Hype". haha. A bit overrated for me. Pizza was good, but I've had better. I went here with some peeps and had to wait outside in line 20-25 minutes. Service inside was ok and pizzas came out relatively quick. The place is kind of small for all the people. The pizzas itself though? ehhh...I prefer Pizza Hut Meat lovers and Stuffed Crust better than this place.

I came here with a Gilt City deal with a certain amount of trepidation. It's in my nature to be cautious of restaurants that need to advertise with coupons, and $150 for a 5-course meal for 2 seemed like red flag... We were pleasantly surprised. We were served: Portobello mushroom mousse in a pot Charcuterie Plate Hanger steak Boozy ice cream S'mores in a pot Bottle of cabernet ... all this for $150, which I think is a steal. The mushroom starter and the dessert were undeniably the best and has conditioned me to believe that the best food arrives in little glass pots. Also everything we got was part of their regular dining menu, and not some sort of lackluster, made-for-sub-patrons version. The space is also airy and large with space to accommodate groups. I've been here for brunch also and recall being impressed with their DIY Bloody Mary bar. If you do see another deal floating around on Gilt City - buy it! Def one of the better coupons I've purchased.
one of best roast chicken I've ever had! Great service. Clean & neat small authentic eatery next to penn station!

This place is wonderful! Very authentic Italian food. My dinner date (who recently went to Italy) said that this place is up to par to restaurants in Italy. The environment was nice although the tables were a little small. The waiters were very friendly. Our order included the following: - Steamed Mussels in a lightly spiced tomato sauce - it's not too hard to mess up mussels so I expected this to be delicious, and it was! - Warm Octopus Salad with potatoes, gaeta olives & capers - it was heavy on olives, but the flavor was a perfect compliment to the octopus. The octopus itself wasn't too chewy or rubbery... just right! - Squid Ink Tagliolini with fresh clams, white wine & cherry tomatoes - i thought this sounded interesting and didn't know what to expect of it but this was actually really good. The Tagliolini was a firm black-colored medium-thickness noodle. This is one tasty dish! These weren't my dishes, but they were also ordered: - Homemade Pappardelle with sweet sausage and truffle oil - had a bite of this and it was pretty good. I didn't get enough of it to give a better description. - Grilled Lamb Shank - The lamb was huge and the meat was nicely season.

I discovered this place a little over a year ago while searching for brunch places on the UWS. I love pickles, so needless to say I was excited to try this place out. They pickle a variety of different items, all delicious, and an excellent appetizer to your meal. Their food is as close to southern comfort style as we will get here in NY. I love fried chicken. And they serve excellent fried chicken atop biscuits and smothered in gravy. Their drinks are also excellent. I'm a bit sad that so many other people have discovered the place, because it means there is always a wait (if you don't have reservations). But it is delicious and well worth the wait!

Went to purbird today!!! Had half the free range and was the best I've ever had. My friend got the chicken burger and almost got another he loved it so much. The price is very reasonable for the quality of the food, we even got a parking spot outside. The location is awesome and going to be close to the new stadium

I chose Carmine's to celebrate my wife's birthday with some friends and boy did we have a great time! It was a Friday night (March 22nd) and the place was packed. We had an 8 pm reservation but all of my party wasn't there on time so we had to wait to be seated (they only seat complete parties). No matter, as soon as everyone was there they seated us shortly after. The waiter was great, he explained everything and told us that he would make sure that we didn't over order since the food was family style. There were 6 of us and we ordered the Calamari appetizer, Shrimp Parmigiana, Chicken Marsala and Penne Alla Vodka. EVERYTHING was delicious! There was more than enough for us all, as a matter of fact I took food home (yay). The food was fresh, plentiful and flavorful. The atmosphere was great , they had nice photos along the walls along with giant menu boards. It is ideal for large groups but just a few people will have a great time too. You get a sense of intimacy even though you are not alone. Feel free to dress up too. Everyone really enjoyed it and my wife's birthday was a hit. We went to a nearby lounge after wards to continue the celebration and to dance off that food lol. I'm definitely coming back.

Great bar. Chill but intimate... I was digging the motif. Behind the bar there was a wide selection of yummy drafts, including one of my favorite hard ciders. I was totally feeling it here and I look forward to a return trip!

They definitely weren't friendly but the pad thai was good. Not sure if the food was good enough for me to return when the service is so poor. I don't remember anyone speaking to me or asking if I was ok. Also, love the outside seating area. But then one of the workers came outside to put pillows into their storage area which was right next to my table. I think I must have been invisible because I had to move out his way numerous times so he would stop touching me and interrupting my meal. Very weird experience if I must say.

Living in NY I've been to this cart a dozen of times. BUT lately I've noticed that they don't give lettuce anymore. If any of you haven't heard SHENDY'S HALAL CART has been bought out by the halal guys so they are "apparently" the same now. Also yes they are open at 7:30pm - 4am BUT THERE IS Â a lunch time vendor that is open on the sw or se corner (not located at the original location). and yes he is legit. We got confirmation from the guys at 7pm while they were setting up before we bought our food. Point being - halal guys are amazing, their white sauce is creamier than others, their hot sauce is super hot....but they've been cutting back on their portions. Used to be a 5 now it became 3 because of no lettuce and their sparing portions...Just expect long lines from 7:30-4 and expect smaller portions bc of the high demand.
By far the best Korean place I have been too. Servers where courteous and prompt. The food was very tasty. Keep it up.
The owner/manager greeted us kindly right away. Romantic, cozy atmosphere for a date. Great food and the drinks were delicious and interesting. We were treated like family and had a great time.
Amazing mediterranean food. They had a grilled calamari special which u should order if they have it. Service was not too good altough the host was was very nice friendly and accomodating.

Oh. My. God. I wanna eat this ALL THE TIME. My man and I split a tray of brisket, pork belly, short ribs, and pulled pork. It was my first time trying pork belly, so I have nothing to compare it to, but I'm a new fan. The rub on the ribs was fabulous. I kept licking it. The beans might have been the best I've ever had. And the sauces were delightfully tomatoey and spicy. My one complaint? No corn bread! :(

one of the best sushi places i've ever ate in! now i moved to jersey, but when i get a chance to go there i always have a nice fresh meal Â with my husband . a big plus is that u don't have to wait for your food forever. Waitresses are really friendly. good place to have dinner

Overall, Degustation offers a pretty solid tasting menu. Â The start was a little rocky: the amuse-bouche consisted of a baby daikon and a light, airy, home-churned butter. Â The former had a nice kick, but as a whole, the two components did not marry well. Â The other plates were quite good save for the halibut (a substitute for the striped bass). Â Although it had a nice crispy finish, the fish was fairly dry rather than moist and flaky. Â Once I stuck my fork in that little square of fish, I already knew it was overdone. Â However, the roasted squab made up for this transgression. Â The meat was juicy, the skin crisp, and the flavor great. Â Generally speaking, it was a good dining experience. Â Also, as a side note, the service was phenomenal.

been dying to try these sandwiches ..ever since seen food network best sandwich i ever ate.. great sandwich. not your regular deli fare. bread was crunchy and meat was tender and flavorful....first time i order the classic and bbg and beef ..number 1,3,4 ..def get the egg on it... go for spicy .. to bad i live in Huntington ..i would go every day ..under 6 bucks tooo.

The concierge at our hotel recommended The Smith (east village) to myself and my daughter for her birthday and I am soooo glad we took her advice. Very cool! Very upbeat and happening. Great vibe. Easy to get to in the East Village. We had reservations and were seated within 10 mins of arrival. The place only sits MAYBE 150 and gets very crowded at dinner so highly recommend reservations. Service was prompt and attentive. We had Tuna Tartare, Brooklyn style calamari and a pot of Mussels for app. Swordfish and Tagliatelle for main course and dessert was complimentary! Great craft beer Great place to celebrate!
Small intimate dining area with a homey and inviting feeling. Food was fantastic from the tapas to the entrees, nothing was overly filling or seasoned.

Moved to the neighborhood last Summer and Benares quickly became our go to restaurant. Â We were initially lured in by half-price happy hour and now we return at least weekly for the amazing food, chic ambiance, and great service. We've put our palates into the very capable hands of the managers, Dipin and Diller, to recommend dishes because there are so many to choose from. Â Some favorites are Chili Chicken, Khasta Gobi, Crab Chettinadu, Makkai Ka Soweta, Goan Salmon Curry but every dish we've ordered has been fresh, flavorful and perfectly spiced. Â  It's the perfect place to be introduced to delicious Indian food if you've never tried it and if you're already a fan of the cuisine then this is the place you want to go for consistently amazing food with top quality service. Â Don't forget to try the Rose Ice Cream (yes, made with real Indian Red Roses and unexpectedly sublime).

Such a great dining spot! Small but quant and tasteful for the area in which it is located. The cider draft is the best beer I have ever tasted and the service was excellent, fast, and personable! I'd recommend this great place to everyone!
Insanely good, cheap Best bahn mi I've ever had. Quick and free delivery.
authentic thai food, just like on the street from thailand. Â tasty, fresh ingredients, fast service. Â the dining room is loud though and often a long wait, then feel a bit rushed at the table.

Good place for Maine lobster. I had their lobster roll and my favorite part was really yhe bread. Expensive for a small sandwich. The lobster filling was mediocre and that's why I would give it 4 instead of 5 stars.

Food was great, all flavors really well developed. Â Had the Tuna-Guac-Tar which was superb, the paper thin fried wonton skins were like air and the tuna was delicious. Â  Lamb meatballs were perfectly cooked although the tzatziki was a bit bitter and could have used more dill. Â Pork dumplings were great and super spicy which kicked things off well. Â  I had the pear salad which was quite good and my friend had the beet salad which she liked. Â  Pear & ice cream dessert was excellent as well. Â Only complaint is that the service started off great and then disappeared, left us with dirty plates and empty water and wine glass. I would have ordered another but no one ever came by until we flagged them down to order dessert. I watched the waitress come into the room, hand a bill to one table and then not even look at any other tables before she went back out to hang with the hosts. Even when we were paying the bill, it was as if they were done with us. Â I loved the place but the fall off in service seriously dampened the mood

Good lunch hour for quick semi special lunch in the FiDi. The crepes are really well made and it's quite hard to resist getting the savory AND sweet versions on same visit. Have sampled nearly all of them and my best bets are the chicken asparagus and prosciutto di parma ones for the savory, nutella banana (I mean come on) and crepes suzette for the sweet kind. Not doling out 4 stars as it's just a pain to get a seat here. The establishment is connected to another Nordic restaurant and me thinks it's the same owner. Last time I went they actually allowed Crepe fiends to cross-over for some seating, perhaps they should make this the norm especially during daytime.

My friend excitedly says to me, "DO YOU WANT CHICKEN AND RICE?" Â Only naturally was I confused, and asked, "What's that?" I'm glad I asked because I was pleasantly surprised with how it tasted. Â If some of you don't know what this place is, it's a blend of Mexican + Mediterranean + Persian all combined into one. Â I got the Combination place in which it has the pork and chicken. Â It's basically a dish filled with rice, meat, lettuce, and other ingredients. Â There are different sauces on the side of the cart that you have to put on! (at least I suggest so anyway). Â There's a white sauce that's relatively close to a ranch, but more of the Mediterranean sauce you would eat with Gyros. Â Other sauces are BBQ and hot sauce. Btw, feel free to share with a friend or two because this thing is loaded with CALORIES!!! Â The line was pretty long, but it seemed to move relatively quickly, and I got my food and started eating away. Â It's pretty good for food off a cart, and they seem to very efficient as well. *NOTE: Make sure you go to the right one. Â You can do this by looking for the cart with the longest line. Â There are other ones probably within a quarter-mile radius with no lines, and seem relatively shady.

Now having been to Sanford's Restaurant a multiple amount of times, as well as ordering in on several occasions, I now feel that this review will be as accurate as it gets. Firstly, my favorite appetizer is the Butternut Squash Ravioli, my favorite entree is the Sesame Chicken Teriyaki, and my favorite dessert is their fried cheesecake. Now let's go on to the review: Environment/Appearance: Sanford is a beautiful and modern looking restaurant. The music is usually soothing and calming, which is very enjoyable while you eat your meal and talk. The seating is also very comfortable. You have a choice of a booth, a regular table, to sit at the bar, or outside. Service: Well, the first thing I absolutely think I need to say is that the staff is very friendly. The owner(s) always come and say hi to me when I am there. The waiters/waitresses are also all very friendly. Even the bus boys are friendly. However, in my opinion, I feel the service is generally a little too slow when it comes to your actual meals, but they do give you the bread the second you sit down which is nice. I always seem to get into a conversation with the staff there, which is always nice. Food: Now the most important part of any restaurant: the food. The food here is fantastic. I have no complaints about the food here. Yes, like any restaurant, 1 out of 100 steaks are going to be overcooked it happens, I am sure most of us understand. Never has my food been under-seasoned, over-seasoned, undercooked, etc. My overall thoughts: This restaurant is great to take your kids, family, friends, or even co-workers. The menu is well thought out and the prices are not too shabby. Also I would like to mention that the prices for the liquor are not too bad for NY as well. I hope you found this review helpful!

a haiku review by sixgirlsonebathroom.com two bottles of wine for me and my hipster date b.y.o. booze cruise kewt petite venue for a romantic dinner quiet, intimate a curried salad wait, how do avocados grow in a mountain range? no matter, delish. aphrodisiac dumplings totes sparked make-out sesh
Solid. Nice ambience with pleasant, attentive service. The split pea soup was excellent. The risotto decent.

Painfully Pretentious and not at all worth it. I had wine with a couple of good friends last Friday, July 12, 2013. Â It was an unmitigated disaster of customer service for Jane. Â We waited for 15 minutes from 5pm until 5:15pm while no other customers had yet arrived, and there were an number of staff members milling about speaking to one another. Two of them stood behind the bar organizing cocktail garnishes in a way I can only describe as completely neurotic, arranging and rearranging little glasses of fruit 10 plus times in a row. Â Finally after three attempts to get the attention of the bartender verbally, I had to get up and ask the hostess to act as an intermediary between me, the customer, and the bartenders. Â Reluctantly and rolling his eyes, a bartender finally sauntered up and asked what we wanted. Â After such a production, I anticipated a great deal of sommelier knowledge and expertise, but he was completely ignorant of wines in my estimation. Â He characterized an Austrian wine I was drinking at demi-sec when it was quite sweet by Austrian standards. Then he offered to let me try a Riesling which he said would be drier than the "Grooner" wine I had originally ordered. Â It was a step away from koolaid. Â This place is such a complete joke service-wise - it really motivates me not at all to try their food. Â What's the point? Â More horrible, rude, holier-than-thou staff people? Â No thanks...

The food was good. Not great considering I am from the south. I thought the banana pie had a little artificial after taste. Next time I will try the pulled pork because everyone around me seemed to really enjoy it. I had the fried chicken.

I had a 5-star experience at Print to celebrate my 30th (shhhh!) birthday. The atmosphere, service, and especially the food were all top-notch. Â This farm-to-table restaurant is fresh, creative, and beyond tasty. Â As one of my girlfriends reflected at the end of the night as we were eating dessert, "I can't choose a favorite dish, they were all just so good!" Â  As a table, we ordered the following highly recommended dishes: - burrata, tomato basil salad - goat cheese gnocchi - stuff quail - asparagus salad - crispy duck - fresh ravioli - rhubarb galette - marsala cream puff - chocolate bread - whipped chocolate flan They also had an excellent selection of wines and fun cocktails!
We tried Da Kine pizza, amazingly good! Fresh ingredients and right combination of spicy, sweet, salty. Will def come back!!! Staff is very corteous.

I've been here a few times. The food is consistently mediocre and the service is consistently attentive. There are definitely better brunch options here, but if you want something hearty and not too much of a wait, it's not a bad choice.

So when I read the reviews, I thought, ok, these are going to be good tacos surely they aren't as great as people say. Yes, they are THAT good. The fried avocado and jalapeÃ±o taco and hanger steak along with the margarita made for a perfect stressed out Tuesday night fix.

A monthly regular at Corner Bistro. This place is a no frills bar serving some damn good burgers. On a paper plate, your choices are limited with a hamburger, cheeseburger (add cheese) or bistroburger (add bacon + cheese) or a chicken sandwich. All are really good and well done. Also they have McSorleys on tap, so it's a winner either way given the price vs quality. Would highly recommend, even though Regis doesn't (HIMYM).

This place is a hole in the wall, I've passed by it plenty of times before and never once thought to go in. Finally decide to give it a try when we were close by and was too lazy to venture off further, for food. My friend and I shared the prosciutto panini and the meatball dish. The panini was crunchy and was sooooo good. The meatball dish was delicious as well. Gaia brought us the food and was really nice. We struck up a conversation about Italy and the futball that that was going on that day. I would definitely come back here again to try the other stuff.
returned again 5/7/11. still solid great pizza & service.
ok food, too much cheese for me in my grilled cheese. the salad was better than the sandwich, which, i guess, says something. I love how in tune the restaurant is with the community

Disaster. I asked for sour cream on the side. They still haven't brought it to me. I'm expecting it to turn up in the mail. Also, I had the worst stuffed cabbage in my life. Stuffed cabbage is always a comforting, soulful experience, regardless of whether it's made by my grandmother or by industrial agribusiness. Yet, Lomzynianka has found a way of ruining what I thought was an unruinable dish... by making it extremely bland. But the red borscht with dumpling was exemplary.

When a good friend brings you out to dinner and drinks at a place they like in a restaurant/bar-infested neighborhood like Astoria, Queens, you better believe it's going to be good. If it's not- maybe you need some new friends. Sweet Afton (and my friend) nailed it. Aesthetics are a huge part of what makes a place hang-out-able and I was blown away when I walked inside. My bar-loving side was attracted to the plentiful variety of seating, vintage wood-style furniture, delicious bar food and great beer selection, while the clean, dimly-lit ambiance, cozy back-room booths and fun drinks appealed to me as a female (or perhaps the girl you're looking to impress on a date). I was there on a Tuesday night in November for an early dinner and as it crept into the evening, the place went from cool and quiet, to packed and uppity. But let's face it, we went there for the food and booze, right?? So, here's the DL on the food... Although limited, the menu has a few staple "comfort" foods and a unique edge- great for an indecisive, Libra like myself. There are four or five cheese options for the grilled cheese that they serve with Brooklyn pickles and yummy spicy mustard and the burger was juicy and flavorful. It's definitely not a boring, bar burger. I was also impressed that they had a cheese plate and a decent wine selection to accompany it! I've had better fries, but they ARE hand cut, so that's a plus in my book. And the booze!? Along with about a dozen interesting beers on tap, I was so excited to see they served one of my favorite seasonal, local beers, Greenport's Leafpile. It's the little things, right? Also, because of the season, the owner had a pot of hot cider that he gladly mixed with spiced rum for a warming, unique drink which was a fantastic alternative to my usual vodka-soda. I would bring someone here to eat a casual dinner, to snack on some comfort food or to hang and have drinks with a group of friends. A great find! Oh- and don't forget to have a Brooklyn pickle juice pickle back shot! Yum.
It's a nice restaurant. Â It's clean, neat and without any funky smell. The service is good, too. We ordered braised beef noodle soup. Â It's awesome! ! I'll definitely go there again.

- Good For Date and Small Group Gathering - Tomato Pickles is nice & unique!!! every single thing like burger, every appetizer, desserts, and cocktail is sophisticated. The portion is for 1 or 2 people. Â  Besides foods, the bar have a good atmosphere & super cool design of the interiors which focused on industrial & antique chair and sofas. Check the toilet (sink!), you will be surprised by this little entertainment. Â Fun. The space is based on very small square and nice size for calm & warm mood. It is difficult to find out here. Tricky place. Bring your careful eyes.

This place was amazing! We had the kitchen sink salad, mac n cheese, shepards pie, and bread pudding and it was all beyond delicious! Washing it down with a crispin helped greatly as well. Â And we took a growler of cider to go. Â One of the best places I've been to in a long time. SOOOOO TASTY!

Simply awesome. By far best Thai in the neighborhood with dishes that are comforting, clean, and some even delightfully complex within a well knit combination of ingredients, like the flavorful and unique Tom yum soup. Just try it

Up to now I haven't found a place with a better tasting burger. There are bigger burgers, or places with better french fries, but there I have yet to find a burger that tastes better. Also, they have good cheap beer. Depending on when you get there you may end up waiting a while for a table but just get some beers in the meantime.

A great place for a snack when you are on the go. Â I've been here a few times now and I think their falafal is really great! Â For $3 it comes in a huge pita that is probably 2 regular orders at another place. Â Service is really fast and the guys behind the counter are really friendly. Â  I noticed that they have flat pitas that are sorta like mini pizzas. Â You can order them with zaatar, which is am amazing Middle Eastern herb mixture than I fell in love with when I was in Jordan. Â So excited that I found a place that has this! Â You can also get them with lamb and spinach and a few other options. Â They are cheaper than the falafel! Â Can't wait to try them out!

Like: good selection of dishes, delicious, friendly service, food turn up quickly, good value Dislike: little space and long queue, can not make reservation and cash only. You only get seated when you get everyone arrive at the restaurant, so you might loss your table and ended up waiting for 30 mins when one of your friends runs 3 mins late. I have been trying to come here for month and month, but the waiting time was just terribly long, so I always ended up going to other places in the area. But I was really lucky this time that I pass by here at 1pm on a beautiful Saturday afternoon with my brother and there was no queue. My hubby was on his way to meet us and there were another 2 group of people were also waiting for one last person to join them, so we were all waiting for the only available table. It was very stressful. We ordered: scramble eggs, apple pancake, french toast and sear tuna salad. They were all delicious, I especially like the smash potato that came with the eggs. Apart from the potential queuing time, it is perfect for brunch.
I really, really like this neighborhood seafood place. Â Oysters are A+, the fish is always super fresh and the service is great. Try the brussels sprouts and lobster mac app

This place seems to be quite a scene. Â When I arrived at 7pm on a Friday, it was completely packed and deafeningly loud. Â We tried to order the smaller pitcher of sangria for $23, but were given the large one for $40, which we couldn't believe since it filled less than 4 glasses. Â However, the bartender felt bad that we were disappointed and only charged us $23 for the $40 pitcher. Â And I would like to note, the purpose for the high price was made clear about 1/3 through the first glass when we tipsily made our way to our table. We had fish croquettes that were a bit dry, which came with some strong yet not quite delicious sauce. Â The redeeming factor of the meal that brought this experience up from 2 stars to 3 was the baby back rib dish. Â Literally falling off the bone (and all over the place after the sangria), these were so rich and delicious. Â So all in all, the place is a bit commercial, and way too much of a scene for me, but we got free drinks and great ribs. Â I won't be back, but I'll remember it fondly.

I've been here a number of times, and every single time i've gone, I've been respected by the bouncer, the cafe, the staff and waiters. The music (live) is always spot on, my cuban wife approves :) we were last here when we just got engaged and our server (so sorry I forgot his name) came back over to our table with congratulatory shots of rum on the house!!!! What other place does such personal and kind things on top of all the other standard hallmarks of a GREAT establishment?? FEW

Just started school at NYU and found this little spot, it was blaaaah. The jambalaya was okay but the waitress said it was pre made when I asked for no sausage. The cornbread was ok but I've had better. I wouldn't come here again though sorry

Roberta's gets three stars because the pizza is pretty good. Â Otherwise, I'm not as impressed with them as they are with themselves. Â They're a little pretentious here. Â I asked for a side of anchovies, since I wanted anchovies on my pizza but the other people I was with did not (anchovies are listed on the menu under "sides"). Â The waiter initially told me that this wouldn't be possible because "the chefs don't like the way it looks," but we asked him to go back and see if they'd do it because it sounded so ridiculous.
