Â When the pizza came, they had refused to give me anchovies in a small dish, and instead compromised and put anchovies on half of the pizza. Â The waiter again clarified, and said that they didn't like the way the anchovies would look if served to me in a Â small dish. Â That might make sense in some really bougy place in the Manhattan but this is a pizza place that tries to appear to not be pretentious, or at least that was my impression. Â The pizza is good though, so I guess if you don't mind the long wait and the hipsters you should go there.

I was majorly disappointed when I heard that Union Picnic closed, but Jimmy's Diner fills UP's shoes nicely in the southern food department. I've eaten in once and by the time my bowl of Tater Heaven came, I was too full to eat most of it because I'd been filling up on the free donuts and oh my god they just had to go and fry their deviled eggs, didn't they? Our waiter was absolutely the nicest I've ever had in Brooklyn. The place has southern hospitality to go along with their southern inspired menu, which is hard to come by in this great state of New York. I've ordered out twice and the first time I got the Cowgirl veggie burger which was out of this world and a side of Â fries which were nice and crunchy and perfect. The second time I was violently hungover and ordered the cheese grits and tater heaven once again. Being a GRIT (girl raised in the south) myself, I know there is a right way and a wrong way to make grits. And Jimmy's does them up right. The tater tots in the tater heaven are very interesting, almost more like hush puppies than taters, but still delicious. For dessert, Â I would definitely recommend splurging on their mocha malted milkshake because it is definitely worth the $5.

So after attending 1st Saturday's at the Brooklyn Museum my friends and I were dying of hunger looking for somewhere to eat in the area. We ask a group of strangers and they recommended this Jamaican restaurant and stated how the food was goooood and how they serve big portions too. Yes the food was gooooood and the portions were good...... ......................................But the wait was loooong if you want to eat upstairs. The dining area upstairs is VERY TIGHT it seems like you're in an attic, even the downstairs is very tight as soon as you walk in the restaurant you're in the kitchen. You can see everything that is being prepared. The Island Â is more of a takeout spot but if you do choose to eat upstairs be prepare to wait as there are only about 5 tables. And the stairs are steep. Coming down after eating I experience vertigo. A hole-in-a-way with some kick ass food! I would definitely go back its worth the wait as long it's not cold because there isn't much standing room inside while you're waiting for a table. Do try the BBQ chicken. The chicken was so tender, falling off its bone and the rice and peas and cabbage was on point. Ya belly will be full I tell ya! with a doggie bag to go home with too.

Cute authentic Italian restaurant. I've been there a couple of times. Â The first time I had the gnocchi which was only okay. Â The second time I made them give me some truffle oil on the side to go with my pasta and the begrudgingly agreed, but hey at least it tasted good!

I love this place because the food is cheap and good :D Though, sometimes me and my brother stay there to eat and they don't have air conditioning- at least i don't think they do. During lunch hours it gets pretty crowed.

One of the best restaurants in the city. Anyone you ask, will agree. I had the price fixed menu $85 per person. The waiter kept bringing us Amuse-bouche so make sure you go with an empty stomach. I tasted foods and spices I've never tasted (ie: Foie gras). We were pampered all evening ... the service was impeccable. Â Will go back again for a special occasion!

Falafel...Thats what this place is all about. Â Lets be clear about some things: This place is not about seats...so dont look for one...chances are, they are taken..after all there are only like 6. Go there, order the falafel sandwhich...get two and you will still be in a $5 range or so...avoid the other over priced falafel places. Â You want a falafel right? Â This is the place to get it. Â Otherwise, go around the corner and pay like 6 dollars for one. Â I just saved $4 BEYATCH! Â I guess you are walking home...
Veggie and chicken tacos are just as good as fish tacos.

Travel to Maine in Financial District NY. Loved the places' decor. A small place but so cute. Went in on a saturday morning and was not full so we got great seating ONE -6 seater shared high table. I am a big fan of lobster but had never tried a lobster roll since all the ones I would see were basically a bunch of mayo with hints of lobster in an enormous roll. However, I am now officially a lover of lobster rolls. Small rolls but with so much fresh lobster. Shrimp rolls also great. Will defnintely be coming back. These guys did it right.
Incredibly delicious burgers and great beer. Went for a quick dinner with my friend Geoff and it was a great success.

Super yummy. Music is playing really really loud, and the restaurant itself is quite small and squished. It's not a big deal though, typical for NYC. I got the drunken noodles or pad kee mao, that were supposed to be medium spicy but they were definitely pretty spicy for me. It was really, really good though and hit the spot. Really flavorful with lots of vegetables. My friend got the ratchaburri noodles with crab and pork, it was really good too. We had the chicken curry puffs to start, which were okay. Next time I'm going to try the papaya salad. Overall super affordable and fresh, hot noodles!

Cramped, isn't the word. This place is tiny. Â But they say the best things come in small packages right? This place reminds me of your best friends cramped East Village apartment. Â That is if your best friend made amazing Indian influenced creative food. Â It's tapas style and I have dreams about the ginger scallop dish. Â Seriously, it is one of the most interesting delicious scallop dishes I have ever tried. Â In fact I could eat this dish every day for the rest of my life and be the happiest girl on the earth--yes, it is that good. Come here with only one, maybe two other people and prepare to be greeted by the super friendly chef and eat food that will delight and challenge your tastebuds.

This place is absolutely FANTASTIC. The main reason why I keep coming back is that it makes me travel back in time every time I come through those doors. They've managed to create something magical that activate your imagination and creativity which is obviously not what you would except form a restaurant. There is a little bit of wait to get your food, but the service is so first class that it did not matter to me.
I loved the black bean veggie burger, though for the price, thought I would get fries. Â My friend got a po boy and he said it was great!

My friend and I woke up way too early on a Saturday morning and decided to hit Cafe Orlin close to its opening hours. We arrived there and surprisingly found a few tables already filled up. Service was ok, nothing out of the ordinary but the food was really deliciouos. My veggie sandwich was pretty good and satisfying. Would definitely recommend it; enjoy!

This restaurant is definitely a ton of fun and they have the food to make the detective work worth it. Â I would say 4.5 stars is accurate as I feel people are probably giving this place 5 stars because of the whole "I found this 'secret' restaurant" pretentiousness. It is part of the fun and anyone who thinks about it enough and given all the clues littered about people's reviews it can be found with some quick searching. Â That's the thing, you really can't hide from the Internet or the government...I'll try to respect the secrecy of this establishment whilst I drop hints throughout, because I think you guys should really try this place out. When I first read up on the reviews here on Yelp I was expecting a super spendy dinner given the three $ rating on the listing. Â My party and I went for the prix fixe tasting menu which is $55 and yes fits within that 3 $$$ range. Â However I would rate this restaurant more at two $$, as most of their individual dishes range between $10-$25. Â There are only a few that are on the high end at $30. The interior living room feel that has been mentioned in numerous locations is due to the comfy couches, loungers and coffee table leveled tables on one side of the restaurant. The furniture here is certainly a focal point and will appeal to any of those into modern takes on retro design. The bathroom is equipped with those fancy Japanese toilets with the remote controls. (Be careful, you can tell the toilet to close the seat while you're going...err not that that happened to me....yeah.) You're greeted immediately when you enter since you have to ring the bell to get in and once you've been seated you get the warm towel to wipe off the NY grime from your hands. Service for the most part is available when you need it and invisible when you don't. They have a decent wine list here that will compliment your food quite nicely. For the food that my party and I had as part of our tasting, we were all surprised at how delicious the vegetables were. They definitely use high quality ingredients in all their dishes. The only thing we found a little overpowering was the Sake Pannacotta dessert. Â It left us all reeking like we had been hitting the sake bottle quite heavily, despite having it along with the brown sugar syrup. The fish was cooked perfectly and as I mentioned earlier the vegetables were great. Case in point: I don't eat brussel sprouts but was asking if others wanted theirs because I would have gladly taken them. Overall a fun experience. Some people find the 2+ hours too long, but honestly it's a tasting along with the laid back feel of being in someone's private home. Â Take the time to just hang out and have fun with your company and enjoy food while you're at it. Â At no point did we feel like the food came out too slowly. Things were timed quite perfectly and spent about 3 hours by the time we realized. They have a bar area which on busy nights they end up using as additional dining area, so they recommended calling ahead to ensure there is room if you're looking at just dropping by for a drink. Of course part of the fun is you have to first find the number. Â Best of luck with your detective work!
The burger is awesome. Very noisy restaurant but this burger and French fries are amazing
half hour wait but the chinese waitress was a witch,so we left,overcrowded filthy hole

While I am tempted to give this place a 5, I am gonna go ahead and give this place four stars. My only complaint is that the deals are so great and the drinks so tasty that everytime I go for their daily happy hour it's packed. Other than that this place is solid. Great Sangria and their Lyhcee martinis are the bomb. Great spot to hit before a night out on the LES. Next time I go Ill actually try the tapas. Stay tuned...

In general, I love Grey Dog. I love the massiveness of space in this particular location, and even the special little nook (you know the nook, past the bathroom, hidden in the back left corner of the restaurant) that my friends and I always try to get dibs on. However, they are definitely still working on the kinks with their delivery situation over there. Their delivery area is teeny tiny. They messed up on an order and gave me "heartache" (I say this, because I love grey dog) about not holding up their end of the order. Overall, I love the Grey Dog chain, we do catered company meals here, and I love their location on University Place, but this particular location greatly disappointed me and I'd much rather spend an extra 15-20 minutes out of my day to go to the one on University Place than the one on 16th. I wish things had worked out differently. I feel like I'm breaking up with a boyfriend or an old friend.

Flavortown BABY! Had the most wonderful meal here. Fiance and I split the octopus and scrambled eggs for appetizers. GET THE EGGS! Tied for the most unique bite of the night. Super creamy and flavorful, and perfect with the grilled bread. Â Entrees were the halibut and kale/mushroom paella. Paella had a wonderful crust/crunch to the bottom of it. But the other most unique bite of the night goes to the saffron-tomato-cous cous broth the halibut came in. I took a large spoon and drank up the rest of that broth; there was no way I was letting the waiter take it away. For dessert we had the cheesecake (yum!) and espresso bread pudding (similar to a tiramisu). Â Complimentary sherry and biscotti topped off the meal, which was made even more enjoyable by the fantastic, caring waitstaff. Will definitely be back here again, and will be dreaming about that broth in the meantime...
Delicious brunch! Â I got the farm scramble. Â it was so delish. Â Coffee was very strong (I like that!). Â My husband got the lobster eggs benedict, he LOVED it. Â Great brunch!
Great meal and fun ambience! -1 star because of a not so nice bus boy. Dropped a fork on me then told me I was lying!!

The feeling of contentment emerges within me as I finish my last bite of this truly crafted masterpiece. The taste of this work of genius created a thrill upon my taste buds and emotions, as happiness took over me like a child trying candy for the first time. The ingredients were truly unified and the quality emulated excellence. The bread and meat were soft as clouds; both were flavorful and concise, practical and effective to each other. Made for each other, one cannot simply exist without the other, and if one did exist without the other, life would be unfair, unjustifiable; this masterpiece would be incomplete. The manner of which this burger was intended and the basis for which it was created, is perfect the way it is, as simple as that. I guess what I'm trying to say is, the burger was really good.
I was very disapointed about this restaurant!!! The soup is tastless and nothing special. Plus the service is very very bad, and they did not respect the customer.

I have a rule of never Â going to the same place more than once while on vacation. This little joint was good enough that I ate there twice this past week. Usually I'm just a ketchup and vinegar guy when it comes to fries but I decided to go with the Especial which is mayo, ketchup and raw onions. The thought of mayo on fries didn't seem appealing but it really works. Their mayo container says Hellman's, but it tasted different to me. A regular, their smallest, is $4.50 but is plenty for one person. They fry their potatoes twice, first an initial blanche in oil to cook them after which they let them rest until ordered. The second fry is to heat them up and make them crisp. Delicious, and will visit again the next time I'm in the neighborhood.

Good, hot, fresh, crispy empanadas. That's what they serve at Empanada Mama. I ordered a selection of three different empanadas, each a bit different from the rest: cheesesteak, cuban, and spicy chicken. They were all delicious and I was very pleased.

This is a lovely, welcoming neighborhood place with outstanding, authentic food that knonws what it's about. Fantastic assortment of margaritas, many kinds of tequila, and a super friendly staff - most formerly of Bonita. Â Don't miss the special of stuffed zucchini flower - ridiculously good.

They haven't disappointed me yet! After my third trip to Beyoglu, I have tried many dishes. The hummus is amazing! The people I've brought here, some more pros of hummus, agreed it's great. Also, the octopus is phenomenal. If you're a little scared to try it - don't be. You won't be dissatisfied. My friends will surely return to the UES just for this spot.

CASH ONLY. I could eat the lamb gyro or lamb plate from here every single day. Â It's perfecly seasoned, cooked, and cut. Â The staff is all very friendly and a little bit clueless .... so , you may have to get their attention a couple of times if you dine in the back. Â It's a pretty small place so I didn't mind too much.

This is such a welcome change in the theater district. The food is fresh and delicious. I've been here a couple of times and had a great experience each time. The ambience is cozy. The staff is friendly and service AMAZING. I have tried the fettuccine Alfredo here love the sauce. The tortellini here is a bit over cooked so would pass on that. The chicken pillars is exceptional. It was recommended by our server and I'm hooked. I love they serve the caprese salad here. They plate it and drizzle it with balsamic, olive oil and pepper on the table. Very fresh! The cappuccino is the best I've had in an Italian restaurant. All this for a very reasonable price! I'll be back.
This was my favorite place with the corn that was a must eat, but the last time it was just so so, and the cuban sandwich that was just okay.
Great family place. We really enjoyed the country atmosphere. House made sodas, housed made sausage, , jam and juice. Food was very good and pretty sizeable portions. Our waitress was awesome.

Fantastic Restaurant! So to begin with, very easy in terms of transportation! Â I took the R train (don't take the D train or you'll end up in Coney Island before you know it!!!) and a few blocks later I saw the lights to this wonderful, comfortable looking restaurant on Prospect Avenue. The decor is lovely. Â It doesn't feel cramped, but still achieves a homey, warm feeling. The staff at the restaurant are super friendly and extremely knowledgeable about the menu, which is surprisingly extensive for such a new restaurant. I started out with the carpaccio. I love carpaccio but find that a lot of times it's either too chewy or too thickly cut. Â This was done to perfection Â with arugula, shaved parmigiano & capers. I almost ordered a second dish of the carpaccio but knew I had a lot more food coming. . . . which brings me to another point about this restaurant. Â The appetizers are a deal. Â Ranging from $8-$10, the portions are amazingly generous. Â Someone in my group ordered the sardines, which were delicious, and I couldn't believe the amount of food they received! I have to admit that I'm not a big risotto fan but apparently this place is known for risotto so I ordered the nero risotto with squid ink. Â Unbelievable. Â It was cooked perfectly and was actually pretty cool looking. Â The squid was tender. Â A+ Continuing to stuff myself, I had the tiramisu dessert. Â That was a highlight. Â Light and tasty, done to perfection. Â All the breads and pastas and desserts are made on premises every day. I will definitely be going back and am intrigued by pasta dishes and the steak, so I will be trying them next time. For anyone living in the area, a great neighborhood restaurant that also does take-out and delivery (there were several take out orders while we were there). Â Bravo Piccoli - Amazing meal!

As the Indian place closest to my office, i visit there often. The price is right (in fact on the cheap side considering the location), and the take out meal options are great. Couple of downsides are that, unlike the name, the place is not a Bengali food joint, and that they never change the takeout menu. I really like variety and wish they rotated their menu a bit. That being said, the food is very tasty and authentic in their recipe. There is a marked difference in taste and spice level in the dishes and any Indian would definitely enjoy eating here. I would definitely say this place is worth at least 4 out of 5 stars. Once point i took out cause of the 2 downsides i mentioned. The seating, though not good, is appropriate for a joint like this.

Despite previous good experiences, we had a REALLY awful one yesterday. Obviously, they think they have such good ratings so they don't need to make any effort any more for their customers. We had a 15 minute wait time which was quite ok, and were seated. Then the waiting started. After almost 20 minutes the drinks arrived. Then a new guests sat down to our left, ordered, were served, ate and left within about one hour. We did not receive our food although we asked in between for it and it was reassured it would come. The guests on our right, who had been there before us (!!) also still waited for their food. After 1.5 hours we asked if they had lost our order. Yes, they had lost our order and we re-ordered our brunch and appetizers, being re-assured it would come soon. The guests on our right were told that their food would come soon and that their order was not lost. However, around 3:40pm (just as they received 2 appetizers as "compensation" for the wait-time) they left because they had an appointment at 4pm (they thought arriving at 1 pm would be enough for brunch but it was not). We waited until 4:15pm for our brunch and then they forgot our appetizer (we had to order it a third time) an the poached egg was fully boiled (?!) - no apology, no compensation, and they charged us the full amount. I believe that this cafe can make good food, but their service is really bad and they are certainly not worth the wait time. They really need to make an effort to maintain their ratings. We were very disappointed.
You feel welcomed the moment you walk in. Â Genuine hospitality and cozy decor. Â Loved the honey cake! Â Definitely will be back.

Used Yelp to find this place after wrapping up a business meeting nearby. Â Nice open air dining area but not many tables. Â Got there after lunch crowd had dispersed so didn't have to wait. Â Order the Bun (vermicelli plate) and it arrived in no time at time. Â Serving size was quite large and it was reasonably priced for NYC food. Â The Bun was very good. Â Would definitely recommend Saigon Shack if you are ever that area of NYC.
still the best cappuccino in nyc. what can i say, always a pleasure stopping in for a drink.

Quirky little hipster burger joint. The food was good and cheap and staff friendly and all seemed to love their jobs and the place. Atmosphere is perfect for location and clientele. I really enjoyed my entire experience here right down to the cute little mouse running around the dining room. Â Yes this might bother some people, but those people should probably not be eating on St. Marks.
Delicious sandwiches - but TINY the people sitting next to us were having a heated debate and we could not escape their conversation! Pricey, but good

I had heard a lot about this place, and the food was good, but I don't think that it was worth the really long wait time and the less-than-stellar service. Plus, don't even think about going to the bathroom. Â There's only one, so there was a huge line for it when I tried to go. Â Then three different members of the waitstaff hollered at me to get out of the way when I was waiting on line for it. Â I would have liked to stay and try the dessert but I had to leave so I could go elsewhere to use the restroom.

It took guts for the owner of this establishment to put it where they did. You first need to understand that Panino Rustico is not in the ideal location, there are no other restaurants around it and it's surrounded by a mostly residential area that also has distributors, a 99 cent store and a tax preparer. To put a fantastic little cafe/Italian restaurant in this area was genius, and hopefully this will be the start of better surrounding establishments! Panino Rustico is done right, it's small but has a charm like no other place in the area besides Mona Lisa cafe about 6 blocks away. My wife had gone here a few times with friends and raved about it so i gave it a shot. Before i get to the food, keep in mind the place is small so seating during prime hours could take a while, and they do have outdoor seating too. It's safe to say i love everything about Panino Rustico! The menu is simple and at the same time extensive. There's a small list of antipastos, soups and salads... I started with a "small" option Caesar salad that was huge so my wife and i shared. The lettuce was fresh and crispy and the Caesar dressing was creamy but not too rich. There were also a ton of croutons and cheese shavings to top it off. The 'bread and butter' of the restaurant is basically a laundry list of panini or wrap options! Fortunately there's a "make your own" option so i went with that. I constructed a wrap with avocado, fresh mozzarella, sun dried tomato, basil, lettuce, oil and regular tomato. It was served with a side of greens and was fabulous! The wrap was put together well and toasted properly so i have zero complaints. Dessert is the other main attraction at this charming establishment! A vast selection of crepes, shakes, smoothies, coffee and gelato makes Panino Rustico a great destination for a date or an after dinner snack. Once again the "make your own" option comes into play for the crepes so i went all out! I went with the banana and nutella crepe with caramel drizzle and whipped cream, it was so good that i attempted to order a second until my wife stepped in and said otherwise. Once again, i have to commend the person who put this place here because it's perfect in every way and adds a great food destination for people in the neighborhood. It can't be understated how important it is to have a cool new place to go to where you can fill up on fantastic food and not break the bank! Our salad, sodas, wraps and crepes came out to $35, can't beat that! Highly recommended! One of the best in the area for sure.

I have been coming here for several years now and I consider Alta one of my top 10 favorites in Manhattan! Truly tasty food, helpful and friendly staff and the decor makes you feel warm and cozy. Try their brussel sprouts, spaghetti (it is not your typical!) even their BLT is not your average. Everything is delicious!!

I cant get enough of this place! Â I have been dining here for over 12yrs and can be found here at least 4x a week. Â The staff is awesome and treat me like gold! Â I feel like I'm a part of the family. Â They let me hang out and never make me feel rushed or unwelcome. Â Love just relaxing with a good coffee and some awesome french toast and people watching on their front patio. This place somehow has withstood the test of time in this ever-changing city...it is one of the few places in earnest. Â I hope it continues to thrive and doesnt change or sell-out to nouveau chelsea riche and the horrific highline tourism! Â  We used to be lucky enough to have these laid-back, family-run joints, like Grainne's, scattered all over the city, but they are becoming more and more scarce. Â  Hope this place is around as long as I am!

The Spotted Pig really knows what its doing and big props to them for that. It really surprised me that an eatery this crowded can be so smooth (maybe I've just been going to the wrong places all this time). Service was never a problem, food came on time at well paced intervals in the appropriate order, and although it looked so crowded and cramped, things were well arranged so I still definitely had a lot of personal space. I didn't order the burger (GASP). The small plates looked more interesting so between a friend and I, we shared: the deviled eggs, chicken liver toast, seared fluke, speck, pork rillette, and the ricotta gnudi. The deviled eggs weren't anything special, needs more spice. Don't know what the hype is all about. The chicken liver toast on the other hand was the best dish of the night. Incredible flavors and texture. I'd go back just for that. Worst dish of the night was the seared fluke with creme fraiche and mint vinaigrette. Absolutely horrible. My friend told me last time he was here, it was mackerel instead of fluke and since he liked it so much, he wanted me to try it. But fluke is a much more delicate fish with more subtle flavors and the creme fraiche and strong mint flavors just really killed the light flavors of the fluke. Horrible horrible horrible. Really disrupted the otherwise nice dinner. The speck was normal (aka boring). Pork rillette and ricotta gnudi were both very interesting and flavorful but also a little too rich for my too used to Japanese food palette. Pretty big portions, for small plates. Creme caramel for dessert was delicious. Would come back next time to try the famous burger and have some more of that addictive chicken liver toast.
The food was good. Â The mushroom bruschetta and the artichoke pizza was excellent in appetizers. Â The pastas were fantastic too.

Flavor-wise, I would give this a 3 star. But it's MAD cheap. 5 dumplings (fried or boiled) for $1... That's right 1 dollar!!! You can even buy the frozen ones to go. You gotta eat them with the hot sauce provided in the table! The place's extremely small, don't even bother trying to eat in there (there are like 4 stools), just eat it outside. Warning: this place only takes cash only. But yeah, if you're low on money and want pretty good dumplings, definitely stop by here!

After taking a boat tour at CenterLine, we stopped by for an early dinner prior to going to a show. Great people and service. Loved the old time atmosphere and learning the history (one of the oldest bars in New York). I had a black and tan along with fish and chips. Good sized portions and tasted very good. The only reasons that I didn't give it a five was the beer selection could have been better.

Food was really good, but kind of a small portion (even for a little lady like me). I got the asparagus w/ salami and runny egg with some sort of white sauce. The asparagus was perfectly grilled and the egg was just the right amount of boiled. The salami tasted like bacon (same thing?), but nevertheless, it was delicious! My friend got the biscuit with eggs and a side of their kale -- which he thought had way too much lemon. The staff was really friendly, but if it wasn't for the open outside tables I think I would have really disliked sitting inside. There are two rooms - the one in the front near the register when you walk in and another in the back. The front room is tiny with people walking in and out constantly and the back room looked really dark. I don't like eating my lunch in the dark - not a nice atmosphere. Â Lucky for us, we did grab an open table, albeit really tiny, outdoors. It started to rain right as we were leaving, so yay for good luck! The lack of nice indoor seating and small portions (I don't need a lot, but c'mon) makes me want to give this place 4 stars.

Went in there 2 mornings ago for a quick breakfast and a little introspection. Â I love how small it is. Â The two people working there were cool and calm. Â No pressure and not overzealous with the order taking. Â I loved their chicken, avocado, egg salad. Â It was delicious. Â I think it's almost impossible to find a good, satisfying salad that doesn't feel like some romaine lettuce was chopped with yesterday's carrots. Â Salads are an art form of good food. Â It takes effort. Â Great salad. Â  Also, HUGE note, I'm a big tea drinker and they brought the extra saucer for the tea bag without asking. Â Thank you! Â  I wonder if they have french fries...
The saddest looking and dullest tasting tortillas from here to Korea squeeze all joy and life out of any meats or vegetables inserted into them. Not returning.
Good food, but the service is almost nonexistent after ordering. Took over 45 minutes for a BLT and a salad.

Great place. Good staff, great food. I found this place on a very cold sunday night just looking to grab a quick bite. What followed was a great dining experience. I highly recommend you try some greek wine and the cheesecake here no matter what else you order. I had the chicken kota which was excellent.

The service at this place is awful enough to get them one star. The wings are actually pretty tasty but not so much that you should have to endure the Â most unpleasant service. This is not based on a single experience but rather many different visits and finally we gave up trying. The waiters have been rude to our kids, they screw up your orders all the time and they don't apologize for it. They make you feel bad about expecting decent service. Most notably, I ordered a large order of wings with two different sauces and rather than explaining before hand that ordering two is qualified as two small orders, they charged me for two small orders and refused to change it to one large order when I told them that I had ordered a large order. Im done with Bonnies.
This was a great place. Much better than Momofuko . Fun upbeat atmosphere and great food. Good price point as well.

The food is delicious. I like everything I have tried here and have been here more than several times. I recently went with my mom, whom I've been dying to take for a year, and the owner (yes the owner, not the waiter) was EXTREMELY rude to my mother and my sister. The service was awful, we asked 4 times to get pepper and no one came. My mom expressed her disappointment with the attitude of the place to the owner, after the owner had yelled at us for getting our own pepper, and the owner told her she appreciated her input and she can leave now. I will reconsider coming here and giving business to such a rude person in the future. There's something to be said about people who think they are so amazing and their restaurant is so good, that they can easily do without the $90 check and numerous people and families being brought in to eat at their restaurant and help put food on THEIR tables.

I almost don't want to write this review so I can have Emily all to myself! It's my happy place. Food: The Colony (red sauce, cheese, pepperoni, pickled chili's and honey) is AMAZING. I could easily eat this everyday. Their other pies are good too, but it's hard not to just get the colony every time. My bf and I get a pizza and then something else (app, pasta, etc) every time and it's a perfect meal. There pastas are great too, they frequently change em up so be sure to check them out. Drinks: Great. Love the goodybags... Some kind of amaretto, bourbon and egg white concoction that is just right. Atmosphere: Perfection. On a Friday night expect to hear our neighborhood boy Biggie and the like. Some nights is indie, equally great. Staff: Totally awesome, everyone's really friendly. Overall: I'm happy to go every weekend and unwind with great food, drinks, music and awesome staff. It's a perfect way to end the hectic work week.

Amazing, amazing. Â I went here when it first opened and have been a fan ever since. Â Lots of great, tasty options. Â Only problem is how popular it has gotten, which makes getting a table a nightmare!

Technically, I could give this place 5 stars (within its price range), but we have dined at the very best restaurants in NYC. Â I really cannot say anything bad about the place, and I highly recommend it. Â One particularly nice aspect of this palce is that we can drop in without reservations if we're willing to eat at the bar. Â Food made from fresh products, high quality, and great service.

Another fun Irish pub where the music comes to you "live and direct" on Tuesday nights. Â Grab a bench, grab a booth and grab some eats--it makes for a lovely evening. Lupa is my go-to neighborhood Italian spot. Always good. Always. I dont think I've had a bad dish here and the service is on point. Well, since this is my first pizza experience in NY, I can't shout "The best pizza in NY!!!" but I have to say it's the BEST PIZZA I had in my ENTIRE life!!!!! There are a lot of reasons to love this place--the decor, the drinks and the courtyard are great--but I am really put off by the way the owner treats his customers (via his servers, who are made to be the bearers of his message). Despite offering free internet, and presenting themselves as a coffee shop during the day, this place doesn't actually seem to welcome laptop use. A friend of mine--after buying a sandwich and a coffee and reading a book for a while--was told "If you're not going to buy anything else, I'm going to have to ask you to leave" by a server, upon taking out his laptop. The same thing happened to the person next to him, who had just arrived and bought a coffee fifteen minutes before. I understand that businesses don't want people loitering with their laptops for hours on end, but there are more tactful ways to discourage laptop use (block power outlets; limit internet to certain hours or days, or get rid of it altogether; limit laptop use to certain tables). Given the amount of cafe options in the neighborhood, this place should treat their customers with more courtesy, or risk never seeing them again.

The cocktails were delicious. Â In fact, my sister swears it's the best bloody mary she's ever had. Â To top that off, they serve it with a chaser (a few oz of beer). Â Amazing. I ordered the lamb bolognese with poached eggs. Â It was unique and delicious, and the serving size was more than I could eat. Â My sides included delicious cheesy grits and a biscuit. Â My sister ordered the sweet potato omelette (with egg whites, which is slightly less exciting than regular eggs). Â It was a little bland, but really - what can you do with egg whites? Â It could have used some sort of cheese or something in it, though. Â She was pleased with the home fries, which were the perfect blend of crunchy and fluffy. Â  We left stuffed and happy. Â The price isn't cheap, but you know that going into it. Â However, I wouldn't consider it more expensive than any of the comparable brunch restaurants in the neighborhood. Â I will certainly go back.

Tried the Maple Bacon on a Stick at the Landhaus stand @ Smorgasburg. Didn't disappoint! 3 sticks for 8 bucks i believe and my friends and I were sold. It's not a meal but a great snack and a quite tasty one. Before they serve it to you, i believe they add some mild spices and spread some maple sauce. They somehow cooked it to perfection where you cannot tell the difference from the layer of fat from the meat. Definitely one of the better things to try at Smorgasburg.

Pretty damn good. Came for brunch and may now be my favorite brunch spot in the city. Their merguez is just the right touch of spicy and flavor. The poached eggs were perfectly cooked and their bread is fantastic. Surprisingly their french fries are also amazing. Another plus - went in with two young kids and they were really accommodating and very friendly.

The line is like Black Friday every night but it is worth the wait! Lamb...chicken...rice...lettuce...yogurt sauce....hot sauce.....delicioussss. It's only $6...I think it's more food than a chipotle burrito bowl. You can't go wrong. The line moves quickly too so get your ass in line and try some Halal Guys.

I am French, was in a need of good French tasty food and by luck I found this place. I ordered the traditionnelle, which, believe me, tastes the same as in France. It was a pure moment of joy, plus the French owner (maybe not owner ? But French guy working in this place) was very friendly, smiling and helpful. I will definitely go there again. Thanks la tarte flambÃ©e !!!

Gather round now! The town crier has an overly comprehensive breakdown of their group dinner at Vesta. Among four of us we ordered a glutinous 3 apps, 4 entrees, and 3 desserts to share. Some things were right on but there were some things that made no sense. Â Consider this the consensus view of 4 folks (and before I sound like king critical/talks out his a$$ but 3 restaurant workers, 1 wine rep). Apps: Yogurt Soup, melon, walnuts - It's cold which to me is a bit of a turn off, but it's a very different soup, the walnuts are quite pronounced, the melon comes through well and despite sounding weird it's a good item to share as the portion is quite large (though even among 4, yes 4! it was too much) it's one of those things where you only want so much. + Salad of onions, nectarines & vinaigrette - This was tasty enough but nothing crazy. = Mussels: Not really my deal but I was told by the others they were "alright" hah sorry that's all I got for that one. = Entrees: Potato, pancetta, caramelized onions, apple & goat cheese pizza - The best entree we had, just a burst of flavors, ample size. Â This I would def order again. + Penne with cream sauce - This was the most leftover/abandon entree pasta, the least interesting or impressive entree. Just kind of heavy, flat and too pasta-y. - Linguini, peas, ricotta - Considering the dud of the Penne, this pasta dish was actually quite good. Â The amount of peas and cheese was better balanced to the amount of pasta. Â The peas were also good and the dish tasted brighter, cleaner, fresher than the Penne. + Steak & vegetables - The steak was good, cooked as ordered, not a ton of smokey flavor but a good, clean cut of meat. Â What was most puzzling was underneath the steak was a paste, very much like, tomato paste--we were quite certain that's what it was. Â I didn't get why one would want that or why it was there at all. = Desserts: Baby Jesus Cake - I thought it was alright, others seemed more keen on it than I. It had nice flavor but I didn't especially care for the texture. + Fresh fruit & mascarpone - This dessert was just weak. Â It was basically a bowl of sliced grapes and mascarpone cheese. Not cohesive, not good. - Strawberry short-cake - Just as disappointing as the fruit/cheese above. Â The cake part was said to be biscuit-like and it was...it was way too biscuity. Â Too crusty and too dense, not pleasant nor well executed dessert either. - Can't believe I just became the long post yelper but it was only because we tried so much I had to Pay It Forward. Overall, 4 good items, 3 average, 3 disappointments. The alcohol list has a nice selection of beers and there are some interesting mid-range by the bottle wines. Â I think their by the glass cheaper end could find better stuff however, it's not hard to find things beyond a mediocre Trebbiano. Alright, that's all I got, hope the specifics help someone.

I've been on the hunt for NYC's best pizza lately and since today was a nice day, I made the trek out to Old Fulton Street to experience Grimaldi's for the very first time. The line was about 30-40 people strong but moved relatively quickly. Once inside, we were seated in very tight quarters. The people sitting on the left were German tourists and the people to the right were debating last night's poker game moves. THAT closely seated. Reactions once pizza came: Mom: "It tastes like Matzah." Brother: "It only tastes good because I've been standing an hour to try it." I happen to agree with them. If you're looking for delicious pizza, you're better off going to Di'Fara's in Brooklyn or Joe's in the city. P.S. The ice cream shop on the waterfront where many patrons go for dessert is closed on Mondays, plan accordingly.

We (5 adults) went for a special occasion dinner last month on a Thursday night. Â We got a reservation (8:30ish) pretty easily just a day or two beforehand. Â The table was ready for us upon arrival. Â  The signature cocktails were all quite yummy, though when a friend ordered a Manhattan (not a signature drink) with bourbon, he was unimpressed by all three bourbon choices, which is weird, given this is such a classy restaurant. Hungry, we ordered a cheese appetizer as well as a charcuterie tray, and both were delicious. Â The server took the effort to explain to us what each meat and cheese was, and even where some of the cheese was from. Â  I was impressed by our waiter, who was very familiar with each menu item and when I asked, "Would you get X or Y?" he instantly gave me his feedback, which I LOVE in a waiter. Â I hate when servers say, "Oh, well, it really depends what you like." Â I wouldn't have asked your opinion if I wanted to go with what I like. Â  Anyway, I got a local fish dish (can't remember what kind now) and my friends got short ribs. Â Everyone was pleased with their dinners, and unlike some of the other reviewers, I thought the portions were quite sizable and appropriate. Â My meal was a little on the salty side, but I'm super sensitive to salt, so I probably should have told the waiter ahead of time. Â  We didn't get any dessert, but I can say the restaurant was awesome in terms of food quality, selection, and service. Â I would definitely go back.

I loved this place! I only had drinks, but every drink I had was AMAZING. I am a Lychee Martini connoisseur and I must say, their lychee martinis are a close second to Sunda's in Chicago. This is the perfect place to unwind, have drinks and chat with friends. A very diverse crowd which I liked very much. Will defintely be giving them repeat business when I am back in town.

Rose Water has always been a favorite brunch place of mine, but I only recently tried their dinner and was sadly disappointed to have it fall short of my high expectations. I had dinner there with the Park Slope Dinner Club, a group of proud Brooklynites that gathers monthly to eat our way through the neighborhood. We loved the atmosphere and our waiter Wolf was super nice. We all ordered from the Market Menu. The bread was superb and was my favorite part of the meal. Others really enjoyed the shaved fennel salad, creamy polenta, and the roasted chicken. The tile fish failed to impress, as did the soup, which were both too salty. The most disappointing part of all was the dessert. The meyer lemon treat was not at all what we envisioned from its description and the pear cobbler could have used some more time in the oven. Both were OK and a far cry from the delight we hoped for.

One of my long time favorites, I guess I never managed to review them because I've been going here since before I was yelping. Â Wow, time flies! Salad warmup: apple + cheddar Pizza: classica with minced fresh garlic Waiting for a few minutes just in from out of the cold, so we grab a couple of glasses. Â For me a montepulcianno and a rose for my friend. Â She looking all lovely in her hoody & thug vest. Â Don't mess with her! When it comes time to pay the bill, that's when my sugar mama steps in. Â She grabs it quickly, giving me no chance to step up to the plate. Â Damn, that's hot. Â Everyone talks about sugar daddies so much these days, who knew there were hot sugar mamas hiding about. Â  Don't hate, this is fo shizza!

Had an official beer club event here last night and it was awesome. Â Lynn was our server and she was phenomenal. Beer selection was outstanding. Â I'm now officially hooked on Keegan's Mother Pucker. Â I don't know why I was so reluctant to try sours for so long! This place has a cool design, a super friendly staff and they just do everything right. Â I'm almost scared to recommend this place so highly because then it will be too crowded for me to get in, but you know what, they deserve all the success in the world. Really love this place.

small sandwich shop tucked into the side of a small brooklyn street - definitely out of the way unless you live in this area. i've tried the vietnamese wonder sandwich, and it was good, but i wouldn't order it again - not enough pork, too much bread. knife is definitely a good lunch spot, but it's out of the way (unless you work in nearby in retail).

Delicious Latin food in Hell's Kitchen. It is giving Toloache a run for its money! The owner was very nice in greeting us and he gave us some great recommendations. I had this passion fruit cocktail that was delicious. For appetizer, my boyfriend and I shared the lobster tacos. These were flavorful but way too small. I think it would have been nice to have at least another taco since they are tiny. For entree, I had the fish ribs. This was such a unique dish and it had great flavors. It definitely was hard to eat though given that the bones were still there. It would be nice if it was de-boned. The portion size was pretty big and I loved the side of coconut rice. My boyfriend enjoyed his short ribs. I would come back!

The food was relatively good being Colombian I have slightly higher expectations. The largest fault was the service was just plainly the worst I've ever seen. We waited 30 minutes for the coffee and 30 more for the actual food. The most astonishing part was that for the whole restaurant there was only one espresso machine.
Yum! Great job here Great service and delicious pizza. Definitely a go to in the neighborhood.

This place is a good spot for happy hour drinks and snacks. Â Had their watermelon soju and white wine sangria during a girl's night out and extremely enjoyed it. Their oysters are $1 all night, but I'm going to stay away. Â The oysters were big and plump, but I felt they were more frozen than fresh.

My dining experience at the Little Owl has made me quite sad. Â The lamb t-bones at the Little Owl have spoiled any previous conceptions I've ever had as to what I most enjoy eating. Â I cannot imagine ever being quite satisfied with a rib-eye steak again. Â I am not kidding, it is depressing me greatly. Â Well, moving on, the Long Island duck appetizer was also tremendous, if a bit scant, and the meatball sliders were very, very good. Â Now I'm going to try to erase the memory of this meal from my head, else I won't be able to look forward to dining out again. Oh, the waitstaff was exceptionally courteous and patient. Â I'm sorry to disagree with other posters.

The papaya salad with the lime juice was light and tasty. I liked the flavor of the crispy pork but some of the pieces were too hard and I was afraid of chipping a tooth. Maybe I just got a bad batch. But my friend loved her pad see ew so 4 stars overall.

I'm from San Francisco, and I THOUGHT we had good macarons here...that is until I tried macarons from Maison Laduree. Â OMG. Â Practically melted in my mouth. Â Oddly, I did not have a problem with the price point of $3/macaron because they were JUST SO FREAKING GOOD. Â I have never had a macaron that was that creamy in the middle and full of flavor. Â Chocolate was my favorite (It's my favorite everywhere). Â Next time I am in New York I am coming here right away!

Oh my... this place was beyond my expectations. Â  One day I passed by and saw people waiting out front, so I knew it had to be popular someway or another, right? I made reservations (they only take reservations for 6:00!) and I'm glad I did. Although the restaurant seemed empty when we first walked in, by 7:00 it was packed and there was a wait by the door. Â My husband, friend, and I sat on the mezzanine with a great view of the sushi chefs and bar. We ordered 3 dinner sets and the homemade tofu appetizer. The tofu was okay, but it changed the way I will eat tofu with its 3 unique seasonal salts - plum salt, lemon salt, and wasabi salt! Â My husband ordered the washu beef bowl while I got the silky pork belly hot pot... both were phenomenal. You can tell right away that the quality of the meats were high and they were as fresh as you can get them. It was not at all oily, dry, too salty, none of the above. It was pure freshness! And of course... the best was the egg custard that comes with the set you order. I dont know WHAT that sauce on top was, but the whole thing simply melts in your mouth. Â It's super flavorful, smooth, and warm when it arrives in front of you. You just have to try!!

THE ABSOLUTELY BEST BBQ. The staff is phenomenal. The food is amazing. The ambiance is very chill. My only critique is I wish they had a better variety of sides, although their beans are TO DIE FOR. I love their small beer selection and did I already mention the food is amazing? Easily one of my favorite restaurants by far.
cheap, delicious, korean food...definitely better than some of the other korean restaurants on the block .

Went for brunch today. Even when you make reservations, be prepared to wait a bit. Â This is a nondescript bourbon bar. Â Menu is a little over-priced with entrees ranging from $12-24 and drinks from $8-10. Â Food was good, but not tastebud-blowing. Â I had the goat cheese red pepper omelette, but the egg was more rubbery flat than fluffy. Â The roasted potatoes were nice and crispy and the homemade hot sauce was flavorful, though lacking kick. Â My $4 buttermilk biscuit side took the form of cornbread and was tiny. Â Skip the fried cheese and meat appetizers...they are bland and meant more for curing hangovers. Â The best thing going here are the courteous servers, and that will keep me coming back.

A group of 6 of us went to Nai for my brothers birthday party. Wow! What a fantastic time. The foot was superb, the waitstaff was on point, and the flamenco was fantastic (just like I remember it in Spain)! Since it was my brothers birthday they invited him up on stage to dance. It was a great night that we will always remember. Thank you to all the staff and dancers for an unforgettable evening!

every single time i get the pork chop & cheddar waffles & every single time i leave blissfully happy. start off with the grapefruit & endive salad. so good. get there early for brunch if you don't want to wait for 2 hours.

I went there for my birthday which I invited a few friends. Â A total of six people, a little tight for this restaurant to accommodate this number but doable. Â The owner was so nice to hold a few tables in order to fit my friends as we waited next door while we were having drinks. Â We didn't mind the wait at all; in fact, we didn't notice the wait while our table was ready. When we sat in our table the waitress was very kind and the food was amazing! Great experience, affordable, awesome ambience, cozy, and warm for any occasion. Ever since then, I have been going there and have become a loyal customer. Don't think twice about coming to this humble place.
Great food and location.

There is a reason everyone talks about Vanessa's Dumplings...they are really good and cheep. Living in Chinatown there are a lot of little hole-in-the-wall places that sell dumplings. But Vanessa makes the best, in my opinion. And the sesame pankcake are very good too...not so much the pork ones. Now they have a location on 14th street too.

I love deep dish, so that probably had something to do with my love for Spumoni's Sicilian pizza. Â The dough is so fluffy and chewy. Â I loved the texture of the square slice. Â The sauce and the cheese were delicious, but it was the slightly-crispy and also doughy crust that did it for me. Â The pizza is so simple, but it's so good! I'd return to Brooklyn for L&Bs (and DiFara... my two favorite NY pizza joints).

Back when I still lived in Los Angeles, I always drove to BCD with friends. Their soup and meet combos are all tasty. So when the New York one reopened, I was extremely happy. It's definitely one of my fav. Always have seafood soon dobu.

I went in solo on weekday around 6 pm just to have a quick eat. I sat on a counter seat and had a miso ramen with pork, the price was $12 or $13, it was good, quick, and reasonably priced. The noodle was a but thicker than some other ramen place, a little bit on chewy side. Â The place quickly got busy around the time, but I would imagine you probably do not need to wait too long for a counter seat--people do not take long to finish a ramen (at least I don't).

Great space, amazing food (the Kale salad is reason enough to go but everything is a win), really wonderful staff.... But why the college frat music? This is really my only complaint but its kinda a big one as it really changes the whole vibe of the space. Â We have enough cheesy sports bars in the hood and this place has incredible potential to be much more hip and cool. Â Speaking of potential... could we work on the patio a bit? Picnic tables and smelly kegs? Again, not into the whole frat vibe but if you are, this is your place. Jeffrey, please reconsider your playlists and investing a little more in that patio space. Â Im counting on you to be the only place in the UES to have good taste. Saying that, Im still a fan though.... truffle popcorn... Yum!

space: low ceilings and tight seating made for a claustrophobic evening. even at 7pm on a tues, it was packed! this place feels like a 70s-era establishment even tho it's only a couple years old! food: - bacon peanut brittle -- no hard sheet of candied bacon.. more like roasted peanuts w/smoky bacon bits. totally addicting tho! - fried chicken -- crunchy skin and moist white meat = great! not the BEST fried chicken i've had, since i prefer more of a flavor bomb like UFC. it came with a light and crumbly chunk of cornbread and a huge spinach salad w/strawberries & almonds. nice touch! - gnocchi w/morels, peas and artichoke -- loved the morels, fluffy gnocchi had a golden crust, and that note of tarragon in the cream sauce was just right. - passed on dessert, but they gave us individually wrapped chocolate chip cookies to go! chewy with lots of brown sugar and full of chips. i'll be back to try more of their menu! but only with 1-2 other people tops...

Great, cheap vegetarian menu. Super flavorful - I had a potato dish accompanied by some bread that was out-of-this-world good. The chai I ordered, however, tasted a bit like a diet or protein shake. All in all, I'd go back!

My least favorite of the Michael Whites. Too casual and fast paced for me. Cant recall all of what I ate except one pasta. The dish I wholeheartedly recommend is the Cappelletti. Truffled ricotta and melted butter? Cant help but love you.
Shepard's pie was tasty. Good beer selection. As everyone else said historical factor. Don't get the corned beef, it's dry and tasteless. We like it more as a happy hour spot than a lunch spot.

It's like Banh mi, taken to the next level that is! This is the perfect shop for a grab and go. I've tried a majority of what they have on their menu and the top prize definitely goes to . . . well all of them. If I had to choose a favorite though, it'll be either the pork belly or coconut shrimp. Nowadays, I come here once or twice a week for lunch, as I work nearby. I can no longer make it through my week without one of their glorious sandwiches anymore. Their sandwiches are just that damn good. Oh and there's some seating up a spiral flight of stairs if you fancy.

I thought this place was gonna be all theme parked the fuck out, but it was not. I'm not sure if I was disappointed or relieved, but I guess it doesn't matter, because the food was yum. The cocktails! I had the one that said rhubarb, because you know, anywhere that serves rhubarb is for fancy people, and me, having heard of rhubarb felt fancy ordering it. I'm a fancy bitch, if you can't tell. Ok, I'm not a bitch, but anyway--the cocktail was really good. They have complimentary bread that was soft and warm. The plates are the correct size, I mean there's no doggy bagging here. I did the corned beef hash. OMFG. That's my review of the dish. Service was friendly. And well informed. The atmosphere is a true New York (no couch dancing here, sorry, not sorry) brunch, because well, you have to wait, it's lively, but everyone is in jeans and a T.

I love Lomzynianka and like to stop by for their soups, especially. Their pierogis are delicious, or rather - the best in Greenpoint! It is a small place with chaotic "decor", so if you need a calming ambiance, it may not be for you (unless Grandma's place is your style), but it is authentic, fresh, good and so cheap... As for the selective comments below about the waiter - I genuinely think he is a nice man. Whenever I need something, I simply let him know and he brings it over (makes sense?), but again - if you're high maintenance and need a waiter that is on top of you & making you feel special, you may need to go to a different place, with less competitive prices, BUT with waiters always ready to offer you a big, fake smile. Your choice. I'm staying with Lomzynianka!

I really like this place. Â I went here for a late Sunday dinner and the atmosphere was just chill. Â Not too busy so it was perfect. Â Had fresh oysters and fish soup and both were great! Â Service was excellent! Â Pricey but worth it. Â Highly recommended.

The options in which you can enjoy your meatballs here are vast: choose to have them on their own, atop pasta, with the market greens (usually some type of fresh salad), in a hero or as sliders. There are unique types of meatballs including a vegetarian one. I usually go for the daily ball to keep things interesting. The beer selection at Meatball Shop is pretty legit too, but the best thing served here is the homemade ice cream sandwiches. Mint ice cream is so fresh it has sprigs in it (!).

No frills - ....Certainly a whole in the wall location, just happen to drop by never expected a place like this in a semi-industrial location nevertheless the food was great....Make Sure to bring Wet Napkins.
Great food and awesome service. We did brunch and it was surprisingly good. So worth the time and effort to get over there.
Went for Happy hour and really enjoyed it. Looking forward to the next visit.

Cuba was a fantastic restaurant. Â We went for the unlimited mimosa brunch on Labor Day, and we really got our money's worth! Â (They had more than mimosas, BTW.) Â I believe that the time limit was two hours, but the restaurant was really relaxed about it. The waiters were attentive, the food was outstanding, the prices couldn't be beat, and the atmosphere was perfect-- not too formal but not too casual. Â I cannot believe that I didn't find this place until I had been in the city for two and a half years. Â This is by far the best AYCD brunch spot ever.

I SHOT FISH IN A BARREL! I didn't expect much coming in here, as I randomly chose this restaurant for lunch based on 4.5 yelp stars. Especially since it was located in the Theater District, I was skeptical. Did it live up to the hype? A resounding FUCK YEAH is my response to that. Why was the food and customer service SO DAMN GOOD? Was it because the Manager thought we were repeat customers and asked us? Was it because the Manager saw me taking pictures and thought I was a food critic? Whatever the case, THEY DELIVERED! Note to self: Never stray from what they are known for. Stick to the pasta in an Italian joint! 2 COURSE PRIS FIXE LUNCH w/ soda/tea/coffee ($18.95) APPETIZER -Calamari Marinati Alla Griglia (Grilled calamari marinated in EVOO, lemon & oregano served over arugula - 5pcs of delicious squid, tasted the grill in this, came w/ a netted half lemon, WOW! -Guazzeto Di Cozze (Sauteed Mussels in a light tomato broth served w/ toasted bread) - we counted 18 of these bad boys, the mussels and broth were tasty, more than ample appetizer portion, i tried this ENTREE -Pesce Del Giorno (Daily Fish Special: Striped Bass) - came w/ roasted baby carrots which tasted like sponge, green beans which were undercooked, and mash potato croquette which reeked of butter, green and black olives, all accompanied by a fillet of bland striped bass. I sent this back. -Fettuccine con funghi e spinaci (Homemade fettuccine w/ wild mushrooms & spinach leaves in a garlic & olive oil sauce) - I ended up ordering this instead, the infused mushroom flavor was evident upon simply smelling it, yes that aromatic. This dish was nothing short of amazing, the pasta was al dente just the way I like it, huge portion -Maccheroni alla chittara con ragu' di agnello (Homemade spaghetti chitarra w/ lamb ragout sauce topped w/ pecorino romano cheese) - the pasta was spectacular, w/ A LOT of lamb ragout sauce, super generous w/ the meat here, tender to the touch, generous portions, i tried this DOLCI -Panna Cotta (free) - traditional italian 'cooked cream' - comped due to mishap..on the menu for $8, topped w/ a sprinkle of cinnamon over it, so good! Decor: Modest, bistro style Service: We left a 30% tip due to stellar customer service. Water was always refilled promptly without asking. The manager Alek really lives up to his bio of great hospitality, generosity, and dedication to the table. He was in the trenches walking back and forth and went above and beyond the call of duty, exceeding our expectations. Food: 5 Service: 6 out of 5...yes, that good! Total came out to $26/pp after everything Pics: meetup.com/teamfoodie/phâ€¦

L & B is always a fun place to stop off. Â It's best feature is the super low stakes - you can always find a table in the outside seating area and the line for squares moves nice and fast, so you are pretty much guaranteed to be stuffing your face within a few minutes of arrival. Â  Now, let's be honest here -- describing the Sicilian squares as "the best in the city" or anything like that is misleading. Â It's total junk food and somewhat inconsistent. Â However, the way they've flipped the standard formula by dumping the sauce on top the cheese is brilliant, so what you get is a chewy, gooey, saucy mess. Â Usually, it hits the spot, and if your piece sucks you can always toss it, get back in line, and try again. The counter inside for heros and salads and such can be pretty frustrating. Â On a busy day you might end up waiting a half hour for their (delicious) pear salad or some other item you didn't realize would be back-ordered. And since everybody goes here the people watching is absolutely superb.
Love this place! Love the fun, cute bartender and the potato chip nachos. Great half bottles of Sancerre, too.

Came by for dinner the other night and was surprised by the line out the door around 8:30 pm on a Friday evening. The restaurant is pretty small and maybe seats ~40 at max? Managed to squeeze in without a wait and ordered the Ratchaburi Crab and Pork Dry Noodles that the waitress and Yelpers raved about. To my surprise, it was pretty good! The noodles were supposedly handmade and didn't have an odd aftertaste to them. There were huge chunks of crab and the pork was fresh and lean. There was just a tiny bit of broth at the bottom that made the dish super tasty. The Chicken Curry puffs that Yelpers raved about also hits the spot. The puffs were fresh and delicately made. At $6.5 for 4, it was pretty tasty! The Thai Iced Tea was also pretty tasty. Not too sweet or creamy! Due to the long lines out the door, the staff was pretty attentive...all at the same time hinting for you to leave as soon as you're done...

Food was okay and service was lackadaisical at best. Â We became so bored waiting for our meal that we were compelled to order too many drinks. When the meal finally arrived, we couldn't send back the hideously bitter broccoli rabe because no one bothered to check on us. Â The trout arrived with nary a potato/lentil/grain of rice to lend it substance. Â Meanwhile, the customers at the table next to us arrived after we did and received their food sooner. Â The server apologized profusely for the lapse in service by bringing out a comped dessert. Â Alas, we were offered nothing even though we arrived earlier, departed later, and ran up a significantly larger tab. Â Never again.
The best restaurant in NYC after about 25 years eating around. Had lunch over there, food, service, atmosphere , I just cannot find what I can complain about!

Went on a wednesday night with three friends. One friend was a tad bit late and the maitre d' told us we could "absolutely not sit" unless our entire party was he, so he gave up our table and we had to wait about 35 minutes for an empty table. we went upstairs to the first come first serve seating to get drinks, those took about 20 minutes to get after we ordered and by the time we got our drinks our table was ready. we ordered the grilled cheddar toast which had a really really sharp taste, more tough to eat then appetizing. We also ordered the artichoke dip which was the best thing i found on their menu. Â I ordered the lentil salad which everyone ended up eating from my plate because the 5 cheese mac and cheese was too cheesey and the autumn salad was actually just lettuce. My one friend did enjoy the trout and we were glad someone enjoyed their meal. We figured we might as well order dessert because it was the one and only time we would be there so we got the sticky toffee cakes which i was the only one who enjoyed them. The atmosphere was good for a wednesday night, but nothing to go crazy over. Do NOT suggest you eat here, spend your money somewhere worth while !!

If you have a hungry man right next to you, take him to the Empire Dinner! Pork on a pork, bun less Lamb Burger, Â short ribs Monday night special... It was the best dinner we had in a while... Do not hesitate to join this excellent establishment asap! Bon appetite :)

I've been wanting to try this place for a while after discovering it on Yelp and decided last minute to come here for dinner tonight. I was not able to get a reservation on OpenTable so we decided to try our luck by just walking in. We were seated at the communal table because we were told a lot of people have reservations and it would be packed soon, which is fine by us. We ordered the appetizer for two (consists of chiang mai fries, spring rolls, grilled squid, and a kale salad) and the dark night entree (squid ink pasta with fried calamari) to share between the two of us since we weren't that hungry. The food came out in less than 10 minutes. The appetizer is large enough for three people in my opinion. The sauces that came with the chiang mai fries were quite delectable and it was a fun change in fries. The spring rolls and kale salad were just okay. The grilled squid was the best of the appetizers; it tastes the most "Thai" and actually seems healthy compared to its fried counterparts. The squid ink pasta was the highlight of the meal for us. It packs a nice punch of heat to it and has great flavors. As much as I am a fried calamari lover though, I did not think it works well with the pasta. I found the spring rolls and calamari to be too oily. Overall it was a pretty okay meal, but I don't see myself coming back... New York City has too much to offer in terms of food. Service was okay.
If there is one star option I'm doing it. Such rude crew in New York's restaurant is outrageous. AVOID THIS PLACE!

Jeepney has quickly become a name that's synonymous with NYC's growing Filipino food scene due to it's popular Kamayan Night, attracting both Filipino cuisine lovers and newbies alike. I fall into the newbie category, having only had Filipino food a handful of times in my life, and thus Jeepney's Kamayan night was both enlightening as well as challenging; just getting the rice from the table to my mouth with my hand shovel proved to be no easy feat. But shovel I did, because everything I tried was delicious. Here's the break down of Jeepney's Kamayan Night: - Wed and Thurs only - reservations required (4 people minimum) - no utensils, no plates - eat with your hands over banana leaves - prix fixe includes: salad, puto, longanisas, veggies, rice, your choice of 2 apps & 3 entrees, halo halo for dessert - starting price of $40/person Our group chose the warm pinkabet salad and banana ketchup ribs as appetizers. The ribs was the winner of the two - fall off the bone tender with a really rich and tangy glaze. Out of our entrees, I loved the menudo (delicious pulled lamb shank) and bicol express (pork shoulder roasted in coconut milk) - both packed with flavor and perfect paired with rice. Our third entree, the whole fried red snapper, was also good but nothing out of the ordinary and not worth the extra $$/person. As fun and delicious as it was, I wouldn't go for Kamayan night again anytime soon because of the price. Dinner came out to be over $70/person because of additional costs, one drink per person, and automatically added gratuity - way over the amount I had imagined prior to the dinner. That said, I'll definitely return for the menudo and bicol express from the regular dining menu, which is probably for the best anyway because spoons are much more effective in transporting food than my hands.
Friendly service, amazing shrimp bisque soup, very reasonable prices. Worth leaving the city to experience a true Irish pub!

The quality of the food dishes, decor and intimate setting made for the perfect dinner date at Benares. Â We arrived around 6:00 PM on a weeknight and were immediately seated. Â  The giant booth space could've easily fit 6-8 adults and seemed a tad unnecessary for just the two of us. Â My honey and I snuggled onto one side of the table and were amazed by the amount of privacy the tall booths provided. Â He kept trying to push the "chef's special" of Tandoori Hen on us. Â We declined, but he repeated that he REALLY recommends ordering that because it's the chef's special. Â Dude, we already toldya no. Â  Keep in mind that the Tandoori Hen is actually a regular menu item. Â I was quite skeptical to order it (especially after that pushy recommendation) since I read in an article somewhere that the specials are the ingredients that are going bad soon so they need to use it up (makes sense, yeah?). Â  If you're a fan of seafood, the Crab Chettinadu was quite good. Â Very difficult to describe the flavoring since there's so much happening in every bite. Â They definitely could've let the spices dissolve a bit more before plating though, some bites did not go down as smoothly as others. Â  We also ordered the Garlic Naan, Chicken Tikka Masala and the Lamb Vindaloo. Â Most memorable was the Garlic Naan which was oily, but packed with flavor. Â I found the Chicken Tikka Masala style to be a bit different than what I'm accustomed to at other Indian restaurants - less creamy so the taste was not as heavy. Â The Lamb Vindaloo had a super-strong kick to it - not my preference. Â  As others have noted, the food does take longer to come out, but they clearly do not aim to be a fast food delivery spot. Â This much is clear if you actually step into the restaurant itself. Â The chefs are carefully preparing each dish as its ordered so it's going to take time and the prices reflect the time and care that goes into each dish.

Boyfriend and I came here prior to seeing a show on a Wednesday night. Â (He paid for tickets, I picked up dinner, he's a lucky guy.) Â Without an appetizer, you could easily spend under $100 for two even with the wine. Â We would come back here again. Â I'd definitely recommend this as a pre-show restaurant.

I'm so lucky to have people like Heather H in my life who continue to introduce me to some of the best restaurants around. Â She's been raving about Gramercy Tavern for some years now, and I had the pleasure of joining her for a Restaurant Week lunch date last Friday. Â And Gramercy lived up to the hype in spades. One of my dining pet-peeves is restaurants that try way too hard. Perhaps the reason I liked Gramercy Tavern so much is that it makes everything seem effortless. Â It also has the distinction of successfully combining elements of old school upscale dining (synchronous food arrival, swarms of busboys swapping plates and silverware, etc.) with a friendly relaxed feel. Â I feel like you'd be just as comfortable here in a suit as you would in jeans and flip-flops. Â That's a hard balance to strike. Finally, the food is just excellent. Â Classic yet innovative, balanced portions, and very well executed. Â I started with a calamari and carrot salad, fresh light and yummy and had the sirloin for my main dish - the highlight of which was the three buttery ravioli underneath. Â Dessert deserves a special mention as the most delectable, rich, and ridiculously good bread pudding I have ever had. This is a great meal for an expense account or a place to take your parents if you're not eating here during Restaurant Week (but thank god we were! Â All that for $40? Yes please). But still, it's nice when the legendary places live up to expectations. Â Well done.

Borscht also amazing I love a bar where you can also order steak tartar and oysters! And both deliciously fresh! Overrated and pricey, the Zagat hyped Sushi Yasuda serves tiny sushi that is composed of thinly sliced fish glued to the rice by overly large portion of wasabi. Â Perhaps I just can't quite appreciate what makes this restaurant unique, its wide selection of domestic fish and its specially prepared domestically grown sushi rice. Â  Obviously not serving to the Japanese clientele, the English only menus are confusing (main menu, sushi a la carte menu, special set sushi menus with pencil marks everywhere) and do not offer any guide to their proud selection of non-traditional domestic fish. Â Don't expect much help from the waitress as she would only point to the red pen circled "today's recommendation" from the a la carte menu and in my case, she provided the wrong information about the ingredients included in the chirashi. Â The fish is indeed very fresh (as you would expect from any restaurant charging this price) and selection unlike any I had before. Â However, I agree with Larry that none of these special sushi were memorable. Â As for the Yasuda's "scientifically" precisely prepared sushi rice, it's decent but not as impressive as the restaurant has claimed. Warning, stay away from the miso soup. Â For $6, I expected the soup base to be made from exquisite dashi and of decent portion. Â Instead, the only ingredient worth mentioning was the few tiny pieces of nameko mushrooms and the soup was served in a tiny chawanmushi sized cup. Yasuda's decor is clean, nontraditional and upscale and its atmosphere business like. Â The chef and staff is another very distinct characteristic of Sushi Yasuda as some of its Maitre D's and sushi chefs somehow slightly resemble the yakuza (dress code, hair style, attitude, choice of words, etc.) which certainly makes an awkward but interesting dining experience. Â Overall, my recommendation is, if you are willing to pay this price for sushi and looking for upscale service, go to Ichimura or Sushiden.
