One day, my big sis Michelle W. (yes we have different last names) decided to take me down a typical Chinatown street. It was a street I had seen before back in my youth league basketball days - Rivington, the one that lead to the park on Chrystie. Completely unaware of what to expect, I thought we were just going to chill by the park until she figures out a place to grab dinner. As usual, her eyes were glued to her blackberry, meticulously texting away...or so I thought. I could almost see the park and all the ah yi's that that chill on the side with you as you watch the best of Chinatown basketball. Then a hand grabs my arm...my big had stopped texting and started backtracking. She mutters..."I think its down this way..." I'm totally lost as I get dragged into an alley. I could only think of the eventual steel pipe I might feel across my face and wonder WHAT THE HELL DID I DO WRONG? As it turns out, there was no ambush, my big was just trying to google map the damn place and at the end of the alley stood Freemans. The overall experience was amazing. The ambiance is unlike any other restaurant I've been in NYC with stag heads and other wild game scattered across the walls. The service was top notch and the food was delectable. There's not much to expand on cuisine-wise as the menu has changed since the last time I went. The best dish I've ever gotten there was the glazed fried chicken. I can safely venture out and say it would give any other fried chicken dish a run for its money. Actually, it was the best I ever had and I don't know why it's not on the menu anymore, which makes me sad. The one thing that has been constant on the menu is the artichoke dip, which is highly recommended by other Yelpers, including me. This place is a great date place, especially if you keep it a surprise until the very end. My friends were amazed this restaurant was in the midst of Chinatown, which is even better when your date expects you to take her to some cash-only Chinese restaurant for chow fun once you tell her to meet you on Rivington and Bowery or Chrystie. There's a lively bar and as with all "speakeasies" (yes I consider this a speakeasy), the bars are staffed by "mixologists," instead of "bartenders", shaping up unique concoctions unheard of at other places. The hours would be a caveat. Although Yelp has them open 10am-12am, I don't think they serve food at all times, but it has been a long time since I went.

Had 2 chicken roti today. Asked for little spicy, it still came out quit spicy ! :-) Great spicy mixture of meat and vegetables rolled in Indian flat-bread. Very good presentation (high class food impression) with food presentation and packaging. The place is simple (still under renovation). Long line during lunch hours (11:30 to 1:00)

Dreamy, dreamy brunch. The french toast with bourbon and bananas was fluffy and not too sweet, the scrambled eggs were light and buttery, the bacon was salty and crisp. Arrive before noon and if there is a wait, head up the stairs to the "column" on the second floor - a less crowded place to order a cup of their kick-ass french-pressed coffee, balance the NYT on your knee, and survey the always interesting W. Village crowd. Or give them your cell number and take a walk around the nabe. The wait staff (cute gay girls galore) went out of their way to make a crazed brunch time seem smooth as, well, butter. Which I had a week's supply of and loved every second.

Having been a Manhattan-ite, I almost never went to Queens, but this restaurant is more than worth the subway ride! Â Fantastic food, very old school, prices are more than reasonable for the quantity and quality. Â For a white girl from L.A. the closest I ever lived to Cuba was Miami, but this place has even the restaurants on Calle Ocho beat!

super crowded, kind of detracted from the experience. tables VERY close. Family style is good, but being closer to the next family then your own is problematic. Â  I thought I posted a review but it seems to be lost. Â Foods were awesome and while we knew large even just order 2 entrees and 2 apps for 3 people we left with two sizable doggy bags. Â Linguini Seafood was very nice.

Class act. Everything from service, ambiance, drinks, etc was exceptional. I had an old fashioned with some kind of citrus twist to it which was spot on. For mains, I had a steak which was exceptional. It came presliced which is not really my preference but was cooked to perfection and sauce definitely had the wow factor. My wife had a duck dish which was very nice. For desert we had Apple tarte tatin which was amazing.

While the food and ambiance of this restaurant is pretty good, I don't understand why it is always so crowded here and why service is always pretty disappointing. The live music is also pretty obnoxious and not very entertaining.

Service 1 Star, Food 4 Stars. The service was so so so so so bad. Everything our server did was rude and condescending, he treated us like trash because we weren't drinking a lot and spending a lot of money. I worked in the restaurant industry for 7 years, and while usually I am very understanding I almost wanted to ask for a different server. My fiance's mother and father split a pizza and he was fighting with them telling them how unacceptable it was to split a pizza. They had to go back-and-forth 3 times with the server, after which he said "There's no yeast in the pizza, you're gonna to leave hungry" then walked away. He then, for the rest of the meal, didn't come back once. He ordered their pizza like an appetizer, to which it came out 10 minutes before our entrees did. So it just sat there and got cold. He never once checked back on us after our food arrived, even though he walked by 5 or 6 times. We ordered dessert, and he dropped off the check with the dessert, as if he was trying to kick us out. I wanted to like Tavola. I live right around the corner, I was hoping to come here often. But this service was so bad that I have no desire to ever return. The food, however, was pretty good. Not amazing or delicious, but clearly it was good authentic Italian food.

First thing that ran through my mind when we arrived: 'Are Jay-Z and Beyonce here??' I know I've read that they frequent this spot a lot (including the night of the Grammy's) so I had to see what all the HOVA hype was about myself! We anticipated a long wait so we decided to go backwards and eat dessert nearby before pizza so that we could get there right before they were open. As a group of three we arrived at 5:50 PM and we were immediately seated at the last available table. I would say Lucali is pretty on par with Di Fara's pizza as both are neopolitan style and use super fresh ingredients (and also cost you an arm and a leg for just pizza). But Lucali gives you the atmosphere in addition. It's rustic with wooden tables, open kitchen, and lighting by candlelight. There's no menu except the one written on a chalkboard. Every pizza's the same size and you just choose your toppings. Be prepared to pay at minimum $24 for a pie though and it's CASH ONLY. It's also BYOB. They don't sell any drinks except for soda so if you're fiending for some alcohol make sure you make a pitstop at the beer and wine. At the end of the day, I still think pizza can only get so good. Lucali probably has a pizza that is definitely as fresh as it gets and I'm glad I had it at least once, but I honestly also get the same satisfaction from 99 cent pizza down the block. Perhaps if I made as much money as jiggaman and his lady I'd get my chaeuffer to drive me down here every time I had a pizza craving, but alas this is reality and I am just a poor peasant media planner living in an overpriced (yet wonderful) city. Definitely recommend trying at least once though, it's worth it!

This place is the best dumpling house in the city! The dumplings are at a nice size and it's crispy with just the right amount of juice! This is way better than Vanessa's Dumpling. They even have an A rating. Also the people behind the counter are actually pretty friendly. I mean what can really go wrong because after all the dumplings are $1 for 5.

Delicious food. Â Great champagne & wine. Â Wonderful service. Â Warm atmosphere. Â All tables filled but no major lines. Â Manager came to introduce himself. Â Chef came out to tables. Â  My friends and family are such that it's not really where we are or what we're doing that matters, but it's who we're with, so we were already off to a great start. Â However, when we're surrounded by such warm energy like I've listed above, we're guaranteed to have a wonderful time. Â  Definitely will be going back again. Â Thanks Basso!

I love this place!!!! Â Definitely the bee's knees. I have been here for dinner, brunch, lunch, all countless times. Â It is consistently amazing! Â The drinks are a mixologists dream, the food is a game-y heaven, and the ambiance is a hipster hunter's paradise. Â It took me forever to convenience my parents to go down a dark alley at night to eat there, but they loved it as much. Key things to get: Everything! Â Just go you will love it!

I've been here twice -- once for drinks with munchies at the bar, and once for weekend brunch. The first time was incredible. The second time was meh. But on balance, this place is so pretty that I want to believe that the third time will be the charm. Now about the drinks...we sat at the bar, where, instead of beer nuts, there were big bowls of fresh, cut red radishes that we dipped into little bowls of sea salt. To my surprise, this was the perfect accompaniment to my equally perfect glass of Cote du Rhone. We also really enjoyed our exquisitely prepared appetizers, starting with the Yellowtail Crudo ($16). FYI, "crudo" is the Spanish word for "raw" in what was basically a pretty presentation of yellowtail sashimi with orange slices, pickled kohlrabi and fennel slaw. Â  We also had the Chicken Liver Terrine ($14) with apple chutney and crostini (toast). This was delicious too. Then a few weeks later, I went back for a Saturday brunch. I should've ordered the terrine again, which was on the menu. Instead I had the Quick Saute of Zucchini ($11) which was basically zucchini and not very interesting. If I go back again for dinner, I will report back.

I came here around noon and it was pretty packed, although I only had to wait 15 minutes to get a seat for 2. Our waiter kinda seemed mindless, but that might just be due to the high number of tables he have to wait. I ordered the cheeseburger with fries and onion rings. The burger was fat and filling, but was not juicy. It's just an average burger. I liked the fries, but the onion ring was just terrible. They overloaded the onion rings with batter. I also ended up getting a red velvet cheesecake from their bakery next door. It was filled with more cheesecake then the cake, but I enjoyed eating it (even 5 hours later).

A real find in the restaurant wasteland that is Midtown West., OCabanon is a place you'd walk right past if you weren't looking. We were greeted by a French accented man and that set this transportive moment straight to Paris. The food was delicious and the wine list is impressive and OH, THE BREAD. Delicious coffee too. I real find for lunch...I plan to go back for dinner. The decor is modest but homey. I love OCabanon. Jo NYC

Yes, it's that good. Â The wait was awful (1hr total), it's relatively expensive ($34 for a Sicilian with toppings), and a 40m trip down the Q from Union Square. But, this is the BEST pizza I've ever had. Â Better than Keste, better than Joe's, better than Motorino's, better than Artichoke (though very different). Â The crust was made to perfection, even though some might call it a bit burnt. Â The cheese was solid, and the sauce was fantastically sweet and chunky. Â We got onions and roasted red peppers, both good. Â Apparently the artichokes and the porcini mushrooms are what's famous, so it sounds like you can't go wrong. Di Fara is worth the adventure. Â Just know the time commitment you're going into before you get there. Â You will be in a food induced heavenly coma when you leave.
Delicious ribs and pulled pork! Unfortunately, they were out of brisket when I got there. The rice side is great as well, and the cornbread.

Anyone giving this place anything above a star does not know what NY pizza is. Â As a New Yorker I felt robbed paying money for the garbage they served. Â I would have been better off going to Sbarro's.

This BBQ joint is smokin good. I ordered the St Louis Ribs and it was out of this world good. The meat falls of the bone, with perfect level of smokiness. This place gives all of the restaurants on Franklin Avenue a run for their money. The owners and staff are super nice. A wonderful addition to the Brooklyn food scene.
Such a lovely experience from the cocktails at the bar to the very last bite of your entree. Â Gluten free friendly and the wait staff is superb!

Not a whole lot more than I can add to the many rave reviews about this place, but the Maine Blueberry Pancakes are every bit as AMAZING as everyone has noted! Â There's just the right amount of delicate crispiness on the outside that gives way to unbelievable fluffiness within. Â i also loved how fresh and sweet the blueberries were b/c it's pretty unpleasant to get tart ones in your pancakes that just ruin the entire dish (as I have on a couple of occasions in the past...) Â The maple butter complemented them perfectly and it was mouthgasm after mouthgasm with each bite =D Def come as early as you can and go on a weekday if at all possible. Â My friend and I lucked out like no other when we arrived at around 10 am on Monday - a mere 5 minute wait right before another half dozen or so people came in through the door!

Good food, great ambiance and despite sharp critics that compare it to Dell'Anima, a good place to eat. If you are looking for the Dell'Anima experience with easier reservations, this you will not get because the fact of the matter is that although the menus are similar in theme, the feel of it is different. Louder, less intimate, and more spacious L'Artusi has a different ambiance. Similarly, the staff, while still knowledgeable, also seem perhaps slightly less confident (or it could have been our luck of the draw). If you stop comparing it to Dell'Anima, however, it is a good place to eat. Tasty, simple pastas and seafood. Although I do not love everything on the menu (escarole salad was just boring to me), in general it still scored high points for me in terms of the quality, simplicity, and taste of the food. Again, not the best you'll ever have, but a safe bet for neighborhood eats.
Love everything about this place and the food is amazing! Loved the lentil burger and the vegetable bun, the cauliflower mash was fantastic and the coconut pudding to die for!

When this place opened early 90's, this place was my kitchen, breakfast, lunch and dinner. I was still single then. I always enjoyed their Croque Monsieur. It reminded of CafÃ© next to my apartment in Paris. Croque Monsieur ($14) It tasted exactly how I remembered but a size had gotten one third smaller than before and they charge extra for French fries ($3) that is if you want to substitute from salad. It used to be free and no home fries. My friend had lunch special and it was way better than my choice, choice of appetizers and main. The onion soup was tasty. The melted cheese was so yummy with sweetness of onion and a bit salty broth took me back to Paris, again. This soup was my choice after late night clubbing. Coq au Vin Wow! when this plate brought to our table, it was presented nicely with a mount of meat on the center with baby carrots and potato around. The Coq au Vin sauce poured over the dish and was only $15 with an appetizer but unfortunately, the sauce needed more seasoning (salt). I also wish it was cooked in a better wine.
Simple food, great execution--just what a trattoria should be. Â This place is my go-to in this neighborhood. Â Never fails to disappoint, and without breaking the bank.

Right out of the gate, I must attest to their excellent bartenders: Â the cocktails, including one the the top 3 Bloody Marys I've ever had, are right on the money. Â They have a solid list of classics (some that people may have forgotten) which are well-executed and memorable. I've had brunches and dinners there, and as far as the food, as with the drinks, it is not about inventiveness (which has its place)- it's about high quality, straightforward dishes that deliver what they promise. Â I've never had anything bad here. Â  Additionally, this is the kind of place that feels just right no matter what the season- breezy, well organized patio in the warmer weather, and cozy indoors when it's chilly. Â  This is sort of a no-fail pick, in my opinion. Â You could bring anyone and they could find something appealing. I highly recommend the Belgian waffles at brunch!
Good prices. Â Great taste. Â Family friendly too. Â Some foods were a bit bizarre for my taste - but the food we ordered was just fabo.
This place is making me write my first review on Yelp. Â  Five stars period. :D Can't wait to go backkk!!!

Had a really nice meal at walter foods this weekend Delicious fig sidecar, a bit dangerous didn't taste much alcohol Had a great (but expensive) surplus of oysters, although the waiter gave my husband an awful wine recommendation to go with (the muscadet, we would have much preferred the viognier, but on his recommendation choose otherwise, he never came back to check on us.) Â I had the sea bass entrÃ©e witch I felt was well seasoned, although I had hoped the lobster panzanella salad would have been warm. Â I had a 'Solera 1847' Oloroso Dulce after dinner drink which I chose and was great, but once again the waiter disappointed and told me it was a port, when it was a sherry. Great food, poor service, expensive price tag

What do you get when you take the following food items and grill them between two slices of sourdough? Perfectly fried chicken breast. Creamy pepper jack and blue cheese spread. Spicy buffalo sauce. You get a crazy delicious sandwich. Â Sure, I've had chicken sandwiches before with buffalo sauce; maybe the chicken was even fried. Â But there was something about this sandwich, I don't know specifically what did me in, but this meal has probably ruined all future buffalo chicken sandwiches for me. Â I'm serious. Â 4 stars alone for the sandwich. The sandwich I loved. But, alas, there were a few things I didn't love. Like the Shop Tots. Â I mean, the tots themselves were good, butttt what makes them "shop tots"? Â The parm cheese sprinkled over top? I kinda wish they were tossed around a little before being served... hot tots + melted parm cheese has the potential to be fantastic. I also didn't care for the price. Â After the sandwich + tots + a bottle of water (I curse myself for not bringing one and having to pay $2 for a silly Poland Springs bottle!) I was up to about $15. Â Ugh. Â I wish there was a lunch special here... or at any of the locations. Â The price won't deter me from returning at some point but it won't be a regular spot. Â Despite the crazy delicious buffalo sandwich! ----------------------- A couple additional notes- - This location is outside! Â There are a bunch of tables but its not ideal if its a colder day. Â  - The day I went there was a sign saying "no cash, credit only." Â Not sure if this is an everyday thing...so make sure you go prepared.

This place was packed and with good reason. Â Not wanting to wait, we ordered to go and ate in the car. Â I got the spicy pork balls with spicy meat sauce on a hero with provolone. Â First the bread was perfect, crunchy on the outside, chewy on the inside. Â It is the perfect match. Â The meatballs were tender and the spice gave it a mild kick. Â My brother would tell you it is very hot, but he is a wuss when it comes to heat. Â Can't wait to go back.
Thought it was charming. Â Lots of atmosphere. Food was delicious. Â I had the lamb chop. A great find for lunch in the theater district. Service was a little slow.

Had brunch here with a couple of friends on a Saturday afternoon. Â Incredibly delicious place that was packed. Â I wish I had gotten some photos of our food but this trip was marked with our daughter's first trip to Manhattan. Â So we were kinda focused on that. Â However... a few tidbits, the Julie's tea is incredible. Â My friend got the lowdown from the bartender how they infuse the bourbon so I'll be using that this summer. Â The drink itself is worth the visit to Bubby's. Â Seriously. I could sit at that bar and just have a few of those. Â However with my daughter there I had to behave. Â On to the food... I was pretty hungry so I had the griddle special or some version of it. Â Sunnyside up eggs, bacon and pancakes. Â All soooooo yummy!! So the wives did not want any breakfast meats. Â The waitress was an angel as she suggested to both of the lady's at our table to not cancel their meat orders but in turn order it and pass it along to their husbands. Â People go straight to heaven for making such wonderful suggestions. Â Excellent place. Â Definitely worth the higher prices.

We got seated at table #48... Â It's by the window, and quite intimate for a table for two. $12.00 Mushroom Pot $08.00 Fries $08.00 Shishito Peppers $07.00 Brussels $08.00 Cup o Punch $08.00 Bell Pepper Lemonade $51.00 + $4.53 tax = $55.53 Out of the food and drinks that we ordered... Â Shishito peppers were our favorite! (And, I also liked our mushroom pot.)

I came here a few weeks back on a Sunday night, I was very excited as I had heard this place was a "secret" and reservations could only be made if someone passes along the number to you. My friend had eaten here and highly recommended it. First, I liked the unidentifiable entrance (I will keep it a secret even though other Yelpers haven't). Once inside, you're welcomed to what resembles a Japanese living room. Small room with 5-6 tables and couch style seating and a Japanese style garden on the side. I opted for the $55 5-course tasting menu of which consisted of 3 fantastic appetizers, one LARGE entree (for two) followed by a second smaller plate, followed by dessert. The standouts were: 1) Mushroom (i think) croquette with sea urchin - absolutely amazing. Sea urchin on top of anything makes for a delightful dish. 2) Vegetable fondue - was a little hesitant about this one as I'm not huge on raw vegetables but the taste of these organic veggies dipped in warm fondue was amazing. I couldn't help but finish off the radishes, turnips, carrots and whatever else was in the fantastically presented bowl. 3) Branzino pot (for two) - you get a whole branzino served in a large pot with vegetables and potatoes. Very fresh and tasty fish, had trouble with the bones. 4) Kobe sliders - loved this one, wanted to order one on the side. 5) Sake pannacotta - great, light end to the meal. 6) Vast sake list for you sake lovers. I would highly recommend this place, very comfortable setting and great food, very very good date spot. The $55 tasting is the way to go.
THEY ARE OPEN!!!! Â Most amazing food I have had in a long time!! Food is VERY reasonably priced and the service is awesome!!! Â  I will definitely be going back!!!

Sunday night, 9pm. Busy with the well-dressed locals and other equally well-attired. Nothing formal, just a relaxed, casual atmosphere at this difficult-to-score-a-table venue. Deviled eggs had a nice touch with the fresh anchovy. Chicken liver crostini was familiar and delicious. Fried artichoke was a wee bit salty with the sauce. Cacio e Pepe was again familiar and delicious. Pigs Trotter was better than the nearby Les Halles. Desserts were very good but the Chocolate Bread and Butter pudding a clear winner. Tables were well spaced and comfortable. Service from our young social waiter was excellent, as was the Sangiovese ($70) that he recommended. All in all, super and fun. Maybe try the bar, which has most appetizers at smaller potions and prices. Ah, yes familiar...it is Bellavitae from Minette Lane back from the dead, but with a better vibe..

I don't get all the hype. Â It's okay food. Â I do not like that they add the 15% tip to the bill.My friend and I went on a Sunday at noon and there was no line. The soup dumplings tasted like other places to me. Â The Szechuan beef tendon noodle soup was good. Â I liked how soft the noodles were. Â The Singapore chow mai fun was yummy and had lots of fun. Â I liked how fluffy the eggs were. Â  I think sharing the table with an annoying couple took away from my experience. Â The couple was annoying and the guy had to ask his wife every time he if he was allowed to eat something. Â They wouldn't stop asking us what we ordered and how do we eat our soup dumplings.
Delicious Banh Mi, great vibe to the restaurant, and it's within walking distance to my office. mmmmm....

We came here before a Broadway show on a Thursday night. Service was spectacular! Very quick, friendly, and attentive. Wine was delicious and decently priced for Manhattan. We recommend the Tempranillo. It was only about $34 for the bottle. Food was great. We ordered the chicken parmesan, chicken alfredo, and my favorite was the seafood risotto. Ambience was delightful. Lighting was perfect, not too dark. The place was packed for a Thursday night so be sure to make reservations!

Eh... I have had better. Â I tried like 4 sauces and not that impressed. Â I rather have garlic fries at the Yankee's stadium. Â The sauces are something I can recreate at home and the fries were not crispy as I prefer.

Went there for dinner last night. We have been going there for years and never had a bad experience. We ate in the restaurant . First we ordered wine and two appetizers to start. They came in about 2 minutes. We had not forks and it took us 3 waiters to finally get forks. The sauce for the calamari was terrible. It had no taste. We had no salt and pepper on the table and the only way to get a waiter was to jump him. We had just started to eat out appetizers and the main course came. I felt like the food was just thrown at us. I waited for grated cheese and then they gave us salt and pepper. We ended up taking food home because we felt rushed. They kept coming and trying to clean our table while we were still eating. Â We were looking to have a nice relaxing dinner instead we felt rushed. Â Also the sauce for out main sauce also was terrible. It tasted watered down. I don't think Â we will be going there again any time soon. We have been going there since we were kids but I think it changed a lot and not for the better. We usually leave a generous tip but last night we did not.

Why doesnt every brunch spot serve you complimentary carrot cake, warm rasin toast and chocolate crossiants while you wait for your food? Hungry people are never happy people. Never again would you here, " im sorry for what i said when i was hungry". What a great world. After eating at LIC Market, do you.... Leave incredibly full? YES. Happily chuckling from all the gluten? YES Complaints?? NO Everything at LIC Market is done right. The service is the best ive witnessed in a long time. You are greeted with smiles and your coffee cup will never be empty. Ummmmmmm and can we talk about the pumpkin butter they serve here? I could put that stuff on anything! Lets just say the pancakes i had here were enhanced 10x by that pumpkin salty goodness. Those pancakes were so fluffy and flavorful that i didnt think they needed anything else but i was wrong. The "bullseye eggs" are also a great choice if you are brunching and want a tasty mix of sweet and savory. You get two pieces of whole grain toast with an egg in each and home fries on the side. Perfect for sharing and a tiny pit of maple syrup on top just makes it the perfect! Their home fries are also some of the best ive ever had. They were cooked just right with just the right amount of seasoning. Not many places get home fries right! After all the rave reviews i can see why LIC market is so loved. They deserve all the praise they can get. This little spot may seem like nothing special from the outside but i promise i great expereince once you settle in.

I went to this bar last night based on reviews I read on Yelp. I was NOT disappointed! Â This place is such a find! Â  Being part of the 30 something crowd I really enjoyed the atmosphere and the selection (both wine and food). Jed took care of me and my entire party. Â We weren't planning on eating, we just wanted to go somewhere to have some nice French wine. Â The food looked and smelled so good, we just couldn't resist. Â I was there early enough in the evening to see they made everything FRESH! Â And, the prices are so reasonable. This is my new favorite place in the Lower East Side. Â Thank you, Jadis!

What do you need in a bar? Â Good selection of beer? Check. Â Friendly bartenders? Check. Â Fun and interesting crowd? Â Check. Yummy Pub food? Check. You get the picture, this bar is a fun time. Whenever I am in the area, I stop by and get a pint and enjoy the dark surroundings. Â My favorite location is at the front in the window or at the bar, it's fun to people watch too!
It was such good experience, their trout was the best I've ever have, strongly recommend it!!

I'm a huge fan! Â I've eaten here multiple times (and I was re-introduced to my current boyfriend here *bonus points*). Â  The food is great, service is quick... what more can you ask for? Â I'm still trying to get past the 'mild' stage of the world of spice, but I hear that this food can get insanely spicy. Â I've seen the slow burning spice bring tears and sweat to people who "say they can handle spicy food". Â The noodles are cooked perfectly with a lot of flavor. Â This is definitely my favorite go-to Thai restaurant. Â  The last star is saved for when I'm able to handle the rest of the menu and its spicyness. Â ;)
Sobaya prepares traditional Japanese food simply, creatively and deliciously! Â Every time I go to New York it is a must stop. Â The service is great and the food fresh and wonderful.

Went to Balthazar this past Sunday for brunch. Â Food was great, especially the pastry/bread basket. Â No complaints about the food, but the service SUCKED. Â My boyfriend's sister was slammed in the head by a busser's dish bin to the point of tears on her part and there was hardly an apology. Â  Every single member of the wait staff was slammed and definitely did not want to be there on a Sunday morning. Â Dirty dishes sat on our table for way too long and our server was extremely inconvenienced by having to take our orders and respond to requests of things that we needed. Â With so many great places to go in the city why would I go back? I won't. Â These people need some staff meetings to learn about hospitality at the very least.

Excellent quality of French macaroons. Always fresh, always delicious in particular the vanilla andvpraline. They could be bigger. The staff is mostly friendly although a bit standoffish. But it's a great place for French macaroons.

First visited the Dosa Man in 2007 with my daughter while visiting colleges. Just returned to NYC during Spring Break with my wife and made it a point to take her as well. She was not disappointed and we still wonder how he is able to serve such large and amazingly tasty portions. We also are I impressed with the amount of time he must put in preparing his "appetizers" in advance. If you are in lower Manhattan, treat yourself to the Dosa Man's cart!

This was one place I overlooked in the addiction that is Yelp. And now I shall place a review rehashing all 70 previous reviews. Its a no frills dark wooded pub, musical conversation abound, cheap mug beer flows like a continuously running toilet, and people are sitting, eating, drinking, cursing or drinking. My best friend's ex, before she was his ex, stayed in the city for a week and we decided to take her to corner bistro because well, its a good a place as any. She ended up getting hammered and tried to bring these three girls from this other table over to talk to me but they thought she was hitting on them. So that worked out okay. The other times I've been here I've either been debating how long it would take for the greasy goodness of the tasty tamturger to go apepoopy on my insides. Or I would strike up a conversation with a random stranger and say to myself, "this woman who i've been talking to doesn't know her shit, she said that Renee Zellweger was in Love Actually and that she knew a producer on Love Actually when really she's wrong because she's been in the Bridget Jones movies". Oh don't have two burgers here. you'll want to. But refrain. Your taste buds may want seconds but your arteries don't.

Bomb.com Who would have thought street food would be that good!! I was quite scared the first time having it cause I didn't now what to expect! I always thought street food would be dirty and gross...but yet again my moto is "the dirty the better the food!", but I didn't expect this place to be as GREAT as it was. WARNING: SPICY red sauce is ACTUALLY SPICY! and trust me, I am they type to can handle spicy!!! THE line is super long!!! but worth the wait. If you are ever visiting NYC or just need a midnight snack...This is the place to go!!! Price: for $6 its worth the wait!!!! I can't even finish the whole thing! Dish: I usually get Half chicken, Half Lamb! try it! I usually don't like chicken but this chicken is actually juicy!
The only thing better than the Prosciutto pizza is the cute brunette waitress. Nicest staff we've had in a while

Always get the brunch on the weekends. Staff is very friendly and delivers great service. Bloody Mary's are great with the brioche French toast. Everything is organic and fresh and it really shows in the taste! Haven't had the dinner yet, but if it's anything like the brunch I bet it's fantastic!

Nice place.Came here with 4 in group on Sat. Late afternoon. The place was jumping with 3 separate tables of 6 or more having family parties but we were seated quickly and treated warmly.Sangria was great,Beef Empanadas two large ones to the order tastey,Cheese filled Pappas crisp and gooey yummy.Cubanwich done just right,Lechon platter w/rice & yucca was a huge portion of meat.Arroz con Pollo more managable portion and nice combo.Tres Leche coco cake was lite moist and not sickly sweet although the bomb lava cake was as it should w/ some ice-cream.2 apps 4 entrees 2 desserts 5 sangrias 2 upscale tea $113 not bad for NYC Village.Only gripe,the parking garage has cars coming out continuously with headlights on but not a big deal.

We finally went to check out the aestethically enticing Spritzenhaus in Greenpoint last Thursday after work. The minute I walked in, I thought I would love it. The decor is fantastic, the more you look, the more there is to discover. The designer definitely has an amazing appreciation for pulleys and now, so do I. But, 2 things: Although we planned on only having a drink each, within an hour we spent well over $100 and, no buybacks! Maybe we just got used to The Whiskey because they are great with buybacks, but we were a little surprised and disappointed that this new possibly awesome place was in this case, not so awesome. THEN, as we were leaving, I literally barely had my foot out the door when this guy, a bouncer??, started demanding that we move along and not "congregate" at the door. Uh, there were 3 of us, and we were not "congregating", we were WALKING out of the establishment which we just heavily financially patronized. And like I said, I wasn't even through the doorway when he started pushing us along. Might I mention that it was also POURING RAIN at that moment. Really. We were stunned. I'm only sorry that I didn't go right back in and mention this to management. They might as well have stood behind us and kicked us down the stairs into the rain. The decor of this place really is great. The atmosphere, on the night we went, was pleasant. I really wanted to like this place. But wow what a crappy way to end our night, and our impression of the place.

I really don't know how these guys stay in business. Â Yes, it's a hole in the wall, so they don't pay that much in rent. Â Yes, they have to update their menu (and their prices) with black sharpies since they refuse to buy a sign to replace the one they opened with. Â No, they do not seem to skimp on the quality of their dumplings which are excellent. Â It's absolutely a steal. Â I ordered a cornucopia of food, handed the guy a Hamilton and laughed at the ridiculous amount of change I got back (ok, slight hyperbole, but I did laugh). Â  The pork dumplings had a great ratio of chives and pork and just the right amount of oil. Â  If I ever get laid off I'm just going to eat all my meals here until I get back on my feet. Â It's the only place where an unemployment check can get stretched in Manhattan.

The atmosphere is lovely. Cool and elegant without feeling stuffy. I enjoyed the risotto balls as well as the homemade gnocchi. Dessert was solid. If in the area, it's definitely a good option. Solid food; a nice atmosphere; reasonable prices; relaxed environment without long lines/crowds. It may not blow you away, but there is really nothing not to like.
There are some things in life that just can't be made better. If the artichoke dip is not the best you've ever had, it's just as good as the best!

Our server (tall, slim, brunette--I presume her name was Jana by the name on our receipt) was awesome, the food was fantastic, the atmosphere cozy and cool. We had the ceviche de hamachi, spinach cheese corn empanadas, bone in steak and cheese platter to finish. For drinks, we shared a pitcher of Sangria followed by a couple great glasses of red recommended by our server. I hope to try other items on my next visit but that overall combination might be tough to beat. (sorry I'm just posting this now! It was so long ago when I started to rate this and just neglected to complete!)

Really delicious chicken sausage that comes in a pretzel bun. I wish I knew it did or I wouldn't have accidentally ordered an extra pretzel, which was ok, kinda oily. I like the open airiness of the place with plenty of places to sit and Jenga to play.

Go to this place for their bread! Yum...their ciabatta bread is awesome. It doesn't matter what sandwich you get as long as you get it with the ciabatta bread, you are good to go. Don't remember which ones I got....I just remember it's all about the bread.

Can I swear on here?!!? These tacos are f*cking stunning! Oopps excuse my mexican! Get your butt here, these tacos are earth shattering, fresh goodness that you will dream about every night! I ordered 2 of the steak, pork and chicken and I really thought the pork was going to be my favorite it turned out that the chicken was the best. So, that being said i went up and got more! Absolutely in love with this place. Like i said before get your butt there! P.S. Service is superb!

I usually go to Tasty Noodle around the corner and probably should have just stuck with my regular. Â My chicken noodle soup had a LOT of ginger in it and really no vegetables. Â The dumplings were kind of tasteless.

Small and cozy with gastropub fare in a laid back atmosphere. It gets busy on the weekends, but the area is cute for walking around while you wait. I don't find most of the food to be anything special, but I do absolutely love the chicken liver toast. The burger is also very good- perfectly cooked and so juicy! Great beer selection as well.

finally an amazing ramen place not in the village!! it was DELICIOUS. on a monday night at 9:00PM, the wait was just about 30 minutes - not bad and definitely worth the wait. i tried the chicken paitan ramen since it had the word totto in it. i'm not a huge fan of chicken but the soup was the best chicken broth i have ever had. it was like chicken noodle soup, japanese style. however, i wish i had gotten the spicy ramen because i tried a little and it was SOOOO good. the broth is so thick and flavorful. i am dying to try the EXTRA spicy ramen now - i was a little afraid to try it with the number of chili peppers next to its name on the menu but now i definitely need to go back. one of the best parts of the menu was the uni with rice. that rice was the most perfect rice i have ever had in my life. i would love to try the spicy tuna with rice as well. the service is SO fast and the food came out so fast too. the menu is small but what they do have, they do it well. (and cheaper than ippudo). this is definitely one of those places where i will crave all the time now!

BLUEBERRY PANCAKES! Hands down, best from a restaurant ever! I have a friend that makes better ones, but you can't just walk up to her everyday and ask her to make them on demand! Don't get a sandwich, don't get their overpriced slices of pies, get the BLUEBERRY PANCAKES. Comes with this maple, butter syrup. I'm salivating just thinking of this goodness. If you don't want to wait 2 hours, forget coming on the weekend, and don't bring a large party to this limited seating establishment. Come on a non-holiday weekday, bring cash (no credit accepted) and make sure your entire party is present to be seated. Oh, want their recipe for these amazing BLUEBERRY PANCAKES? They have a freaking recipe book! Here's the recipe (the secret is folding in egg whites and milk!): leitesculinaria.com/6916â€¦ Yummers! Get the BLUEBERRY PANCAKES!!!!

Not all rolls were created equal. The unda shammi rolls are easily the most authentic tasting, but can be a bit dry considering the minced nature of the kabab. I love the menu, it reminds of my childhood and the random posters you could buy at the local stationary store. The Big-B posters are rather unnecessary considering he is not a very good actor.

Spotted Pig is so trendy and crowded, I'm a little mixed on how I feel about the place. On the one hand, I have had only good experiences with the staff, so that's a good thing. But I've visited a handful of times for drinks, on various nights, at different times, and every time, it's been packed, both upstairs and down. Insanely packed. That's a sign of its popularity, but it's a little uncomfortable to be pushed around by other girls' purses (or elbows or butts), knocked in the head, or constantly squished up against my friends. Anyway, everyone raves about the burger, and I have to say, it's pretty darned good. I've seen a lot of Yelpers Â comment on the burger being too salty, but I think it's the cheese, cuz to me, the burger itself was just fine, in fact, it was perfectly cooked. Anyway, I really liked it, and the shoestring fries with fried slices of garlic and fried rosemary are fantastic. I Â would love to try to gnudi next, since I've read a lot of compliments about that too. Overall, I've always had a good time here, I just wish it weren't so crowded!

Mezetto came out of nowhere to deliver a surprisingly solid fusion Mediterranean light dinner. Great for sharing: the cheese plate, the dips (spicy feta my fav). Then the octopus and the shrimp were really good - the grilled octopus in particular. Throw in a huge Greek salad and some nice Chardonnay and you're good to go.

OK, where do I start. First of all, if you're going to enjoy this place, you've got to be in a certain mindset. Don't go expecting to be king of the world, because you're not. The rice is. Don't go expecting to fill yourself up. Depending on your budget, and how you order, you very well might leave hungry. But that's ok. Because you're gonna have a great time, and what's wrong with a little ramen after dinner anyway? Basically, go in there the first time with the mindset that you're going to a very serious/fine dining sort of place, because that's what it is. Afterwards you can decide that it's the kind of place you'll want to make your regular sushi place, but won't be able to afford to. Expect to be humbled. OK, so here are some pointers for first timers: 1) Make a reservation to sit at the sushi bar at the very least, and sit in front of the man, Mr. Yasuda if your date/time is flexible. The core of the place is in front of Mr. Yasuda, and at the sushi bar in general. That's what you're coming for. More on Mr. Yasuda later. 2) It's easy to be intimidated, but don't worry about it. Ordering at the beginning was the hardest part, but even if you make a misstep, it's ok. Mr. Yasuda will forgive you. I've read so many different things about how to order and costs and everything, I thought I had it figured out. No, I didn't. But it's really simple. For the first time, take it piecemeal. (3) Get the basic set to start, which is like less than $20 and has 8 nigiri and a half tuna-roll (which my friend said was the best tekka-maki he ever had. I agree.) This is what he'll suggest, just to get the ball rolling. He'll ask you what you don't eat. Tell him. Then he'll give you the nigiri, one by one. It will be awesome. Don't bother with soy sauce, or anything else for that matter. He's already seasoned it for you. Pay attention to the rice. Remember what I said about you not being king of the world? You're not it. But you'll start to feel like it as the meal goes on. 3) After the set is over, start looking at the list the waiters gave you at the beginning, with suggestions for that day marked in red. Start thinking of what looks good to you. Then have the chef choose 4 or 5 more nigiri for you. That's what omakase means: "you decide." It's not a pre-fixe menu. It's whatever the chef thinks is good, and thinks that you'll like. The sushi experience is all about the interaction between you and the sushi chef, and about you trusting him to make you happy. One of two things will happen. Either he'll pick what you were looking at, in which case you'll be amazed at his mind-reading abilities (this happened to us), or he'll pick something totally different. Either way, it's going to be good. Even if you don't think you like sea urchin roe, if he utters the word uni, you say "yes, please." Same goes for eel. 4) At this point it's up to you. You can ask for suggestions, you can ask him for specific things, you can ask him to choose. Whatever. At this point, you can keep going until it feels right to stop. You'll be having a grand-old time with the chef at this point, so he'll know what you like, but if something catches your eye, don't be afraid to ask for it. 5) A cool thing about the list that's in front of you. You'll always know how much each piece is, so you can keep an eye on your budget. The most expensive pieces are the different kinds (!) of toro, obviously, at $7 each. Rolls are a little more expensive, but you're not gonna go and have 5 of those at a time. Uni and other pieces are around $5. 6) About Mr. Yasuda: He's a character. Very nice, but can be a little intimidating at first. Don't worry about it. He's a talker. He'll talk a ton about his whole style, about rice, about where the fish comes from, about what sucks about most japanese restaurants, and why he's doing what he's doing. As my friend said, he's a man on a mission: to make his way of sushi, the standard way of sushi. Â According to him, his way isn't special, just the way its supposed to be. Sometimes it can be hard to understand every word, but just smile and nod, and it'll be fine. Oh, and another thing. He's a smart-ass. Seriously. He spent a good amount of time during the course of the meal busting my balls, but it was all in good fun. I wouldn't recommend this place for a date, for a few reasons. First of all, the focus isn't on the two of you, it's on the food, the chef, and you, and the interaction among them. Secondly, there's the budget thing. Any urge to impress can lead to a skyrocketing bill, and even more if you have appetizers or drinks. Ok, that's all Yelp will let me write. If you love sushi the way it was meant to be, and are prepared to humble yourself, Sushi Yasuda is the way to go.
Highly recommended!! You should try here before or after shopping in Macy's

GREAT sandwich place. Tried the Mona Lisa, 1001, and 1003. Â All were fresh and delicious. Around $6-7 per sandwich. Nice garden with seats and tables at 6th & B. cuz there's no where to eat in the deli/store.

I LOVE THIS PLACE! The food is amazing and what is best about this place is the staff, they are accommodating, wonderful people that are very attentive and understand customer service. The atmosphere is warm, inviting and welcoming!!! this is always my place to go for a business lunch/dinner. Â And now they've added breakfast! what a treat! Try the Branzino, the spreads, Cod fritters, grilled octopus (well done), Greek salad, OMG the home made soup...seafood...amazing!, Greek yogurt...I've had these all. Â There were a couple of items that were on the menu when they first open that are no longer, and wished they wouldn't of taken them off...but other then that...Delicious!!!!

Amazing environment, great drinks, food and music . Perfect to either dine with friends before heading out to party or for a date. The latin-fusion food is carefully made, organic, grass-fed and antibiotic free... And for a great price!!! If you're around the neighborhood, a must go.

Great food, super friendly owner and staff, and I love that I can also just go buy a fresh loaf of bread or a twelve pack of organic eggs to go. The only negative is that it's too popular -- however despite the crowds it remains a relaxed and laid-back place to go.

Unlike most of my reviews, I'm not going to wait a month to write this one because I want every memory of the dilectably meal to be clear in my mind... I went here last night for a date night. Â The place looked very cozy and adorable. Â Unfortunately, they made us wait about 10 minutes for our table, but granted, it was the first time we were ever on time for a reservation. Â maybe the trick is to get to the restaurant 5 minutes late. For appetizers, we got the duck meatballs and the fried calamarie. Â Both were delicious... very interesting flavors. Â A little East Asian and a little Indian. Â I felt like I was on top chef. Â I found the calamarie more impressive as the whole dish ("salad") is deep fried, but did not feel extremely heavy or gross, like most deep fried foods. For entrees, we tried the boar and the trigger fish. Â I felt that the boar was especially heavy... but the boy enjoyed it. Â Maybe I am a vegetarian at heart. Â The fish was a amazing! Â But felt a little too much like fish sticks (reminded me the of the South Park episode... "do you like fish sticks in your mouth"). Overall, great dining experience, but very much on the pricy side. Â Nonetheless, service was amazing and it felt great dining at a restaurant with a "celebrity" chef, which i don't do often. Â BTW, the Perilla 75 is very tasty!

I've been to Lomzynianka twice now, and haven't found anything on the menu that I wouldn't highly reccommend. On my first visit, I got a Polish Platter, which was a large plate filled with, among other goodies, a delicate stuffed cabbage, a sizeable piece of Keilbasa, and several fried pierogies. My friend selected a chicken cuttlet that was bigger than his plate. Both entrees were preceeded by plates full of a variety of pickled salads and slaws. Our total bill, with sodas, was less than $20 including tip. On my return, I decided to try an appetizer, and I'm glad that I did. I selected the white borscht. And, while that was quite good, it paled in comparison to what I had for an entree: the Hungarian Pancake! There was really no need to have ordered an appetizer. This entree could have easily fed two hungry adults. It consists of a dinner plate sized potato pancake, folded over and filled with a delicious beef stew. I've never had anything like it before. It would be the absolute perfect winter meal, but, even in summer was pretty damn good. I'll be back here soon for sure!
They have the best soup dumplings in town. Â The owner is Cantonese and they have a Shanghainese Chef and a Hong Kong Chef. Â Food here is made pretty good and at very reasonable prices.

We had some tasty goulash and brat worst, with Sabarsky mocha and Mozart-torte. The food was good and environment fairly nice. We did have a 30 minute wait and we were lucky because people came after us had a much longer wait. The food was good but not great - and a bit pricey for the small quantities. The goulash was more of an entrÃ©e than a meal for $16 and the bratwurst as well (boiled not roasted). The coffee was a shot of expresso with whipped cream for $8. The total for two small dinners, one coffee and one desert was $54 before tip - essentially for a snack. We might come back once a year.
great burgers. a litte sloppy but very tasty Â You can't beat the old school diner decor either. A bit pricy, but most NY diners are.

What a great surprise. Â  I was invited by a friend and his German girlfriend to have dinner at Edi & the Wolf. Â I was not looking forward to trekking to Ave C for dinner, but the trip was more than worth it. Â For starters, the venue is super. Â With no visible sign, it is hard to find and give the impression of a club or speakeasy. Â Once inside the surroundings are warm and comfortable. Â I had a seat at the bar and was offered samples of a few draft beers before making a choice; a very nice touch. The food is solid Teutonic comfort food with most of the flare in the starters. Â The short ribs, spÃ¤tzel and schnitzel were all super and solid main courses. Â We finished with a couple of desserts including a tart. They feature a great selection of beers on tap as well as a very compatible list of wines. For a casual evening, Edi & the Wolf is an excellent way to break out of old habits in more familiar neighborhoods.

Maybe this place a little overhyped? Waited Â two hours at a cafe nearby to get seated even though we showed up at around 9:30 on a Saturday morning. The pancakes were good but a little too much on the heavy flour-y side. Also wish they accepted cards!

I LOVE this place! Â Not only is the ambiance great (yes, taxidermy above the bar, old time jazz music, white candles everywhere) but they have good food. Â Set back from the street in a kind of alley felt like I was walking into a European restaurant. Â We tried everything it felt like: Â Devil's On Horseback (figs, bacons, cheese), artichoke dip (I like Houston's, is that bad?), pork and also the sea bass. Â  Try this place...but make reservations first. Â Also make sure your brother hasn't eaten beforehand for a while. Â That way he will be so hungry he orders everything and you can just sample off of his plate. Â All part of the master plan.

I really liked the atmosphere at Quaint but was thoroughly underwhelmed by the food. Though I appreciate the local sourcing and seasonal ingredients, my meal was just lacking in the flavor department. I went with a friend and together we ordered the cod and salmon entrees, along with the mesclun salad as our appetizer. I could tell that the ingredients were fresh, at least the tomatoes were- slightly crisp and sweet. The service was polite and I really enjoyed the quaint (ha! pun intended) and romantic feel of the backyard that was decorated with tiny string lights and white furniture, but were not enough to overpower the bland food.

Great place for a quick meal or steak. I come by here once in a while and am always happy with the food and service. The staff is always friendly and on top of everything. The only thing I would say is avoid going here for dinner on weekdays, its extremely crowded and filled with Wall Street brokers.

I waited for 20 minutes outside in the middle of winter (it was 25 degrees outside) and it was so worth it. Â It's way better than Lombardi's. Â  I have been to 20 pizza places in New York and Grimaldi's is easily the best.
Food was decent, nothing spectacular. But what got me was that they automatically add 18 % tip to all checks. Â That's every assumptions for a restaurant. Â  Also a reason to keep me from going back

3.5 stars. Our party of three of came to Pinto on a Thursday night after Yelping cheap Thai options south of Chelsea. When we arrived, we were happy to see that the small, well decorated restaurant was fairly bustling. It's interesting how Thai restaurants often up the ambiance factor in relatively cheap restaurants. In contrast, Chinatown joints could pretty much care less about how they long. They know the demand that exists for cheap and good food, and rarely often the dim lighting, white square-plating efforts that Thai restaurants add. Hmm. Just rambling. The Foodnalysis: - PCU (guessing that this is some type of clever acronym for Pad See Ew. ICQ, PCU! Hopefully someone out there who spent time on the internet in the 90's gets that joke) - Frankly, a little disappointing. Was too bland and served somewhat lukewarm. Guess I-don't-C-Q PCU. - Pad Thai - Sneaked a bite of my friend's entree and immediately regretted not order this. Don't you hate it when you should have ordered the classic!? The best tasting dish of our three. - Beef with Peppers - Nice, robust flavor and tender meat. Portion was small relative to the other two dishes, though. The Bottom Line: Warm ambiance, good prices for the West Village. Get the Pad Thai.

Apparently has been open about 6 months. Â Great prices for the sandwiches, made fresh to order... nice ambiance, casual with Latin music playing in the background. Â I'm a Vietnamese sandwich fanatic, and this is a great sandwich - Banh mi Zon's sandwich has the perfect interplay between the crunchy cucumber and baguette with the savory pate, pork and ham. Â (Note: I've only tried the pork patties sandwich. Â Twice in a few days (it was very tasty.)) Compared to Baoguette on St Marks, this place has much better ambiance, better flavor (I don't like Baogette's bread, too dense and chewy), and better prices. Â I would also say it's a much higher quality sandwich than Nikky's (where I first discovered Vietnamese sandwiches in NYC 5 years ago...) The fresh lemonade is delicious as well, not too sweet, just right in terms of tartness. My all time favorite is still Banh Mi Saigon Bakery, but it's often too far a trek for a sandwich. Hope my review is helpful.

My favorite THAI restaurant! Been coming here for years now. Their crispy watercress salad is the best! The tom yum shrimp soup is so fresh and with just enough tang. Love their crispy pork belly. The sautÃ©ed Chicken is so good too. The place is always packed on weekends and they don't take reservations, so get ready as there is really no place to sit around while waiting for a table. Plus they only accept CASH. We had one bad experience though. Otherwise, I would have given this restaurant a 5 star. We came on a Saturday night. My son ordered a dish which NEVER came even after we reminded the waiter TWICE! He didn't even apologize for it. I hope he's no longer there.

Char No. 4 has gradually supplanted several contenders to become what I'd call my favorite brunch in NYC. The stunning quality on repeated visits has won me over completely. I cannot imagine a better way to obliterate a hangover than glaring up at the enormous bourbon selection (one of whom is most likely the reason I feel horrible) as I sip on that spicy Chipotle Bourbon Bloody Mary (the pickle makes it) and wait for the absolute pinnacle of brunch deliciousness. Bring one other lucky soul, and order two dishes. 1. The bacon cheddar grits are a must. Pressing those perfectly poached eggs until they explode into the creamy, buttery grits and then stirring the yolks in with just a bit of homemade hot sauce...it's absurdly satisfying, and unbelievably tasty. 2. The only brunch options anywhere that can contend with those grits are (A) the Biscuits Benedict and (B) the Char Slam. With regard to (A): Hollandaise and mediocre English muffins are the downfall of most Benedicts, and Char No 4 replaces these with bacon gravy and biscuits, respectively. C'mon now. On the menu, (B) may read "sage-pork sausage patty, two fried eggs & pancakes with blueberry jam & honey-almond butter," but the check tells the truth. In fact, this is The Truth. This is a Slam worthy of Onyx. The sausage is thick and flavorful, the eggs as good as fried eggs get, and the pancakes are downright decadent. They are a mini-stack of the HUGE portion available on their own, and they are sublime. They've got maple syrup if you want it, but the fresh blueberry jam and the honey almond butter render it completely unnecessary. Add an order of the crispy potatoes with green onion & garlic to any of these, and this will be the best brunch of your life. And while people all over NYC wait in line for inferior food, if you get there by 11 am on a Saturday I'm willing to bet you can waltz right in and grab a seat at the bar.

Every experience I've had at Mominette was incredible. Â The wait staff is super adorable. As helpful as they can be, once an order was messed up and the waiter apologized and fixed it ASAP. The food is wonderful but go on an empty stomach you are going to be very tempted to eat your whole plate of super indulgent food. Â Little secret I get the Mac and cheese side and sautÃ©ed kale. Its at the bottom on the menu not really advertised which is crazy because it's to die for and a huge portion. Plus best backyard in Bushwick IMHO.
Order the Pho

Jacob's Pickles was incredibly busy when I visited at 11 am on a Sunday and rightly so. We had the Sausage Gravy Smothered Chicken, which comes with a side of grits, and one of the specials of the day--the Salmon Benedict--and they were both absolutely perfect. I was really surprised at how moist the chicken was, which really made the dish all the better, and the salmon benedict was served on their famous biscuits and with a side of potatoes. It was honestly the best benedict I've ever had. When we came at 11, the wait was an hour long for two people so we left our phone number and walked a few blocks over to Milk Bar for coffee, tea and cookies. We got a text letting us know that we had 5 minutes to come claim our table. When we left around 2, the restaurant seemed even busier, and the wait was an hour. The staff was really great. I actually visited earlier that week a little after midnight hoping to grab dinner. Unfortunately, the kitchen closes at 12, but the host was so nice and apologetic. He must've noticed how devastated I was because he offered us some pickles on the house!
waited a really long time on a table on a Friday night, but it was worth it. pretty large portions, recommend splitting plates, but the prices are pretty good.
Their congee is my favorite. The testure of the congee is perfect!

I ordered take-out from this place a few times. Decent, tasty home-cooked food. Their appetizers are tasty and delicious - empanadas with green cilantro sauce and potato wedges with spicy mayo. Their roasted chicken and shrimp with garlic sauce dishes are nice and flavorful and comes with fresh salad. This place advertises itself as fresh, cooked food. However, their chicken is already pre-made and heated up in their commercial microwaves. Â Still tasty nonetheless but a little misleading. Service is spotty - sometimes they're great and quick. Other times they're slow with orders and forget to say "thank you" more often than not (imagine complete silence as you pay the bill -awkward). I would recommend this place to friends as a nice option for late night dinners or snacks but it would not be on the top of my list.

My boyfriend and I were very excited to try Queens Comfort, so excited we waited an hour to get in. The atmosphere is fun, and the decor inspired some new decorating ideas for our apartment. Who doesn't need a painting of a raccoon or an Elvis lamp!? There is a dj in the corner, and the crowd is distinctly trendy. They have exciting menu options such as oreo mini pancakes and creme brulee waffles. Basically, this is your diets worst nightmare. The prices are a little steeper than other brunch spots in Astoria, but you are paying for the playful brunch experience and the food. My farm house hash was awesome. I loved the pulled beef, seasoning, and the potatoes. My boyfriend enjoyed the Mexican Cola, but he found his chicken and waffle to be very average. Â The donut looked amazing, but it did not live up to its appearance. We found it to be very "cake like" and lacking in strawberry/chocolate taste. Perhaps I am anti-social, but I found the seating incredibly cramped. While this may be fine for the beer garden or a bar, I would prefer a bit more space when having a leisurely brunch with my boyfriend. The groups definitely made out better with space. If you have a larger group you can get one of the nicer tables with a bit more space. They offer Harvey and Sons tea, and Stumptown Coffee for coffee drinkers. It is cash only and BYOB. Just embrace it. While the lively "line host" keeps everyone entertained with jokes and activities, we didn't feel the wait was worthwhile for brunch. I will return, but either really early for brunch or for a weekday dinner.

They bring out hummus and pita bread in the beginning...SOO GOOD!! We ordered the lamb chops and scallop/shrimp on egg pasta. The lamb chops literally melted in my mouth...really juicy (medium). The pasta was equally delicious..lots of flavor. Great wait staff, really friendly, definitely make a reservation

I wish I could give this place five stars because I wanted to love my food so much! I found this restaurant by accident out of food boredom considering I typically order food through Seamless. I searched around on Yelp for options and I found this place! It was somewhat late so I called first to make they deliver in my area and they do! SCORE! I breezed through the menu and noticed that they serve mofongo so I ordered it...chicken to be exact. With a side order of the moro del dia. I noticed time was slowly going by and considering that hadn't eaten dinner and called my order in at 9:58p my food should be on it's way any minute now. NOPE...I was wrong! It's now a little past 10:30pm so I called the restaurant and they guy told me the delivery man should be ringing my bell at any minute now. He was delayed due to the rain. Okay. No problem. Understandable! Roughly :30 minutes roll by and still...NO FOOD!!! So I call again afraid that the restaurant has now closed and my order may or may not be delivered. They check again for the delivery guy and assures me that he is near! Ten minutes later than GOD he has arrived. Once I ran into my kitchen to tear the bag open so I can eat (finally) I pull out the rice container, then the container of beans (although my moro del dia is MIXED with rice/beans) I let that slide. Now I'm anxious to pull the mofongo out the bag and instead it's a side of plantains!!! UGHHHHHHHHHHHHH I call the restaurant AGAINm now it's 11:20p I speak with the manager and he says he can have the delivery guy come back with the correct order in no time. Okay...noooooo problem. :/ When he arrives by this time I'm exhausted and don't want to eat too late considering it's damn near mid-night at this point however I'm curious to see what it taste like since I love mofongo... I cut into it...IT'S HARD AS A FUCKIN' ROCK!!! I put it in the fridge along with the sides and decide to deal with it in the morning. SO for lunch today, I heated it up and tried it again...IT'S STILL HARD AS A ROCK!!! Needless to say, I don't think I'll try this place again. I'm so disappointed.

granted, not the best neighbourhood, but it works perfectly fine for me since i spend most of my nights at issue project room (the best venue for experimental music in nyc), right next door. but this is the best italian food i've had in town. the atmosphere and decor are very pleasant and the service is impeccable. beers and wine are good and affordable. the fried seafood is awesome and comes with bits of deep fried, battered lemon slices. the seafood is so tasty that you don't even need the sauce that comes with it. their pizzas are quite tasty and their pasta dishes are fantastic. and prices are affordable, so what more could you possibly ask for, you greedy pigs?

I know, I know you all LOVE this place... you all ohhh and ahhh when you think of it and your mouths water and your eyes get big as they bring the dumplings towards your table. Well, unfortunately when I ate here I got food poisoning!! I did not even want to look at, smell or hear about Chinese food for years! Now, luckily that has passed... but I still cannot go back to Joe's. Sorry!
This place makes sexy sandwiches. I'm always a happy camper when I come here. Banh Mi fries are major.

Really well cooked yakitori, but no smokiness from binchotan. This is probably as good as it gets for grilling over gas though. My only gripe with this place is that it's going for more of a stuffy ambiance. You can't really get loud drunk here. Service is great for what they are going for, water constantly refilled, servers standing near our table at all times. But sometimes I just want to have fun. Isn't that what izakaya/yakitoris are all about?

A couple friends and I decided to hit up Fette Sau to celebrate the end of the week. Got the brisket, ribs, pork belly, some potato salad and the included rolls. Brisket was delicious, right mix of lean and fat. Ribs were good too, albeit sort of expensive. Pork belly was a little rubbery, but you definitely cannot argue with slabs of pig fat. They had the two different sauces, the spicy smokier sauce, and the normal sweet barbecue sauce. I actually liked mixing them together to reach a nice sweet and spicy medium. Potato salad left something to be desired. It was good, but a "Large" is by no means a large portion and it came a bit too vinegary for my tastes. I love the sharpness of a potato salad, but this was drenched in a sour taste. Rolls look like they could have come from the grocery, but rolls are rolls are rolls. The bar was pretty sweet though. We all got some Allagash Whites to wash down the food and it was perfect. In mason jars of course. We're in Williamsburg. To summarize: Another no frills barbecue joint in Brooklyn. High quality meats and mediocre sides. Good beer selection and a super hipster staff and vibe to the place.
Yummy! Can't resist the hawaiian shirts!

My co-worker took me and my girlfriend here for a our birthday lunch. What a great Choice! I absolutely loved it. We arrived around noon for lunch and the place was not packed which was great. We were sitted right away and waiter came right away as well. Waiter was very nice and told us about the menu and recommended a Pumpkin Beer which was delicious. For Appetizer we order the shrimp cocktail and the mac and cheese. Delicious!!!! Set the bar up for me and excited for the entree. I chose the Roast chicken which I loved. This came with potatoes and spinach and the combination was just perfect with the chicken. I was very impressed with the resturant and the service. My co-worker mentioned that it is very cool to go for dinner and when you go towards the back you can even enjoy the Billards. Which I think is very cool.

Amazing go to spot if you don't want to question if the food will be good. Â I love this place. Â Food is always amazing. Â I also have always had great service here. Â Erin or Aaron, was our waitress last time I was in. Â We were at our table foreverrrr and she was so sweet and never rushed us (even though it was close to close). Â I really love when I am not rushed or felt rushed at dinner, she was awesome. Â Pretty crowded and noisy place, so just be prepared.

Haven't been to this place in a while, but used to go often when I lived around the corner. Good food, for good prices. Most entrees are around $10. I remember liking the skirt steak dish and the fried pork chunks with corn. They also have a nice, comfy neighborhoody vibe. Only downside is that the food takes a while to get to your table.

BEST EGGS BENEDICT!! Seriously if you come here for brunch (like I did) you must get the eggs Benedict which are perfection! Everything about this dish is awesome, the biscuit is flaky and buttery and the home fries are AMAZING! I replaced the bacon with spinach and it was still fantastic. Their mimosas are also pretty good as is their coffee. The service was really good as well, we were seated pretty fast and the server was nice and helpful.

Eataly isn't exactly what I imagine Italy to really be like. It's huge, crowded, commercial (even with all of its specialty products) and chaotic (well, maybe this is actually representative parts of Italy's economy and gov't). I get that it's supposed to be a one stop shop, but is this really necessary?? It makes the entire idea of specialty a bit moot.

Came here for Easter brunch. Â Luckily most people were spending it with their families or eating elsewhere so sat down immediately. Â Tried a variety of dishes but favorites were the spicy rice cake with sausage and the short rib sandwich. Â Great meal considering how much more I spent at other NYC restaurants on my trip. Â Perhaps though the lack of wait may have skewed my opinion. Â Not sure if I would have liked it as much if I had to wait 1 hour.
Awesome food! Huge portions!! Our server Keri was fantastic!
Everything about this place is amazing

My first time here and I dined at the bar. Â  Started with a lychee mojito and roasted corn spring rolls. Â Entree was a honey ginger pork chop. Mojito was perfect. Â Roasted corn spring rolls were very good, although they were served "pre-dipped" in the dipping sauce. Honey ginger pork chop was full of flavor, but VERY thin and a bit tough. Â Fresh broccoli and tasty fluffy jasmine rice came along for the ride on the plate Typical of NYC restaurants, the diners were packed in here elbow to elbow. Beauty of a chandelier as a centerpiece, oddly placed in a mirrored glass box. Overall, a good value for the low price paid in the Hell's Kitchen area. Â I'll be back for a second try.

Gosh this place is good. Tapas style. Be prepared to spend a lot money though and make reservations! The place is small and they don't have a coat check which means you are snuggled next to everyone in the restaurant. I came here for my birthday with a party of 3. I think we split 5 or 6 dishes, but I didn't leave stuffed. Skirt steak was one of my favorites. I mean really though, everything was delicious. You can't go wrong. I got a free glass of sparkling wine with a four square check-in which was nice. I'm not sure that I would come again just because I hate spending lots of money on food and end up leaving not completely satisfied, but I'm not going to give this place less stars because of it. The food is solid. Really solid.

Delicious falafel salad bowl with fresh ingredients. There are a bunch of options to to off the salad such as himmis, Israeli salad, beets, and nyc more. My salad was delicious, healthy and filling. The guys were super friendly and helpful. There is a lot of space there as well so recommend checking it out.
Love this place! Â Try the Chicken sandwich or the Roasted Chicken. Â Those are winners every time. Â Really delicious and worth the wait.

I went to Alta for my birthday with a group of friends and it was NOT a good experience. Â I will say the food is good, but it was completely ruined by the service. Â The waitress gave us the wrong wine, which I understand happens so I was not upset, but I did want the wine I ordered. Â Since she already opened up our bottle, she said she would have to ask the manager before she gives us a new bottle. Â For some reason, the manager refused to give us what we had asked for. Â We were stuck with red wine instead of white. Â  This wasn't all. Â The bad service continued throughout our meal. Â Servers were continuously bringing out our food and practically throwing the dishes on the table. Â It would have been great if they would have told us what dishes they were bringing out instead of just throwing them in the middle of the table, but I guess that's just not how they do things.
Delilah's Steaks is a great place to eat clean food was great had the philly cheese steak of da chain
A hidden gem! Everything taste so fresh and the people that work there are very friendly. Bulgogi sandwich with a egg on top is a must!

The ambiance get a 4, the food gets a 10, overall average = 7!! Â The food here is OUTSTANDING! Â I tried nearly everything this menu had to offer, from appetizers to desserts. Â Recommendations: the Warm Feta, Tomatoes, Capers, Anchovy, Peppers, Olives, Pita Bread; Grilled Octopus, Bean Salad (SERIOUSLY good!); Meatballs, Roasted Garlic, Olives, Tomato; any of their lamb dishes; rice pudding or sesame ice cream for dessert. Â You WONT regret this experience. Â The ambiance isn't the most romantic...it's...very simple. Â Once you take a bite of the food though, it won't matter...trust me, you'll forget everything (just don't forget your company :). Â Bon apetite!

AWEESSOOMMMEEEE, I happened to be sober and it was the middle of the day when I had these amazing FRITES but I can only imagine how they taste at 3am while drunk. It's probably like eating pure 24K gold. Is that what Diddy feels like all the time? Okay I'm on a tangent. I love Pommes Frites. They have some amazing dipping sauces, everything from spicy mayo to thai peanut sauce, mango salsa, tons of stuff. I'll keep it short and sweet cause with 1000 reviews for this place you guys should be convinced you need to try it. And don't worry, it's just as good sober.

This place might be a dingy, hole in the wall, but the ramen is awesome. I got the shoyu and really enjoyed it. It's not too heavy but still has great flavor. I'd describe the soup here as tasting, "homestyle." It really taste homemade. It's not as heavy and rich as say, ippudo or santouka but it's an overall GREAT bowl of ramen. The gyoza here is also homemade and really good. YUMM.

When you first walk in you may be "underwhelmed", but give it a chance. First the service is awesome. I don't care how good a restaurant's food is; if the service sucks then the restaurant sucks.The ambience is so-so. It is small like other reviewers have said but also cozy. My friend and I started with two orders of samosas, one chicken and one vegetable. We also ordered tea which was very good. The server explained to us that traditionally they do not sweetened the tea but he was sure to give us plenty of sugar and substitutes in order for us to sweeten to our liking. He also explained the sauces that were served with the samosas. I don't know this guy's name but he knows how to treat a customer! Â I will say that the tea took too long. Â I ordered a chai tea and it took longer than a chai at Starbucks with a line! For our entrees I had the chicken tikka masala and my friend had the sookah lamb. The sauce for both dishes was soooo good. We also ordered naan bread. The rosemary naan was AMAZING. The staff and who I assumed to be the manager were very attentive and even answered questions I had about a spice that was in my rice. I felt very comfortable asking questions since there was not a condescending tone like in other establishments. I had a good time talking and relaxing with my friend. It was an amazing meal. I did not use the restroom but my friend did and she said it was very clean. It's so gross when you eat in a "nice" restaurant and the bathroom looks worse that the Port Authority. This was a solid experience and I'm so glad that we chose this place for dinner, with a little help from Yelp of course ;-). Alas I cannot award five stars. The timing of the food was not the best.
