Since our tea took so long, the apps were a bit backed up, and then the food came out. The tables are so small that it made it a bit uncomfortable. If we had time to finish our appetizers before our entrees arrived that "traffic jam could have be avoided. Also, while one of the servers was respectful to us, she did seem to have a bit of an attitude with the boss. Her mumblings and grumblings made my friend and I stop mid-sentence, look at each other and ask, " Did you hear that, too?". Â To me, this was more disturbing than the "traffic jam" mentioned earlier because it totally killed the mood. All the food was delicious, it's not a big deal if it came all at back to back. I did make one observation. The management may want to consider getting some extra chairs. Â A party of six didn't mine squeezing into a table meant for four. The staff were very accommodating and borrowed chairs from another table in order to seat them. The problem came when two more people came in and needed a table for two. While there was an empty table, there were no chairs. If they had a few extras, then they could have seated them and I wouldn't have felt like I was on display at a zoo with people staring at me while I eat. I WILL DEFINITELY BE BACK!!!!!!!!!! Everything was great! This place may be small and a little crowded at times but the food is delicious!

My grandmother only lives about 4-5 blocks away. My grandmother, being Thai, loved going to Sripraphai before it expanded. I remember going there as a child when it was extremely small and had only 3 tables, a refrigerator, poor lighting, and a place where they kept their sweets. Although the interior wasn't exactly appealing, their food was authentic and held true to Thai cuisine. They also had traditional Thai (khanom) sweets, like Khanom Chan and look choob. Ever since they expanded their restaurant, their prices rose and the authenticity of the food went down. Although the place does look nicer, the food doesn't taste like authentic Thai food at all. The food is too Americanized. Even though the place wasn't exactly somewhere you'd want to sit at and eat before, the food was delicious and used to be my family's favorite place to go to for Thai food. It's quite a disappointment really.

Been wanting to go here for quite a while, so was expecting great things Â Had the signature pork buns, but sorry, my mama ruined it for you. Â They were really good - they just didn't blow me away. Â I also had the grilled octopus with shaved fennel, which was tasty and paired it all with a nice slightly chilled red wine. Personally, I thought it was a bit expensive for what you got, but the staff is friendly and you can tell they love food. Â I heard one of the employees telling a friend about how they made the soy sauce flavored panko crumbs and it was very cool. Looking forward to trying Momofuku Ko some time.

I thought this place was absolutely amazing! We both had the $35 prix fixe menu, which is a real bargain considering the quality of the food, service, and ambiance. First, the restaurant itself is very cute. I loved the decor and the homey English-cottagey vibe (not a favorite of my husband's though). Next, the meal we had was pretty damn tasty. I had a salmon entree (from what I remember) and I couldn't find any fault with it. For dessert I had a scrumptious and delightful berry pavlova. Pavlova's are definitely a British (hence N.Z.) thing, so I was happy to have something different other than your standard chocolate lava cake. Delicious. I'll be back.

thought this place would be another tourist trap. after seeing it on the Gothamist I decided to visit with a friend. mostly community style seating, but not too uncomfortable for a hectic Saturday night. ale selections were vast and unique. I tried the refreshing Crispin ale & the server even made an effort to provide it with an adorable mason jar for convenience. the speckenwolf & famous original were both so delicious. dont forget to ask your server for their daily special. what a great place to enjoy quality ny pizza fresh from the oven to your table. can't wait to come back!

Arrived around two in the afternoon looking foward to some mac and cheese and was told wait time was 45 minutes. Â Proceeded to pass time at the nearby loehmanns so time passed quickly (actually had to get pulled out) Luckily for me I did not get a stuck up waiter so many yelpers have complained about. Â Mine was friendly and cute. Â I got the mac and cheese trio, Â tomato soup and meatballs dish. Â  Delish!! Â Im not sure what to say about the food except it was done exactly the way it should be. Â  We thoroughly enjoyed everything especially an establishment that serves fresh no nonsense dishes. Â It really is refreshing for me to find a place like this. Â Before I left I lustfully eyed the rest of the menu again so I could start planning what Â to get next.

I have a new favorite place in Brooklyn, and it's just a few blocks away. Thanks for a memorable dining experience Tom! We LOVED the many tidbits we tried on the menu. We hit a goldmine. Your chef is incredible!!! See you VERY soon!

I'm usually one for cocktails and dinners where there is usually only vegetables. That said, corner bistro is my favorite go-to bar in New York. Are the bartenders nice? not really. Is the service spotty? oh yes. But can you beat a 2 dollar beer and GOOD burger for 5 bucks in New York? The atmosphere is this bar also superb. To quote Kat H it like " that I'm-wasted-in-a-cozy-sweater feeling". Corner Bistro is just a comfortable bar: loud enough that it does not lame, but not too loud so you can have a good conversation with someone.

I love this place. First of all, the complimentary bread and olive oil dip is amazing. I usually can't stop eating it. They have a good selection of wine with one decent, really cheap option (only $14 for the bottle.) The food is great and reasonably priced too. I've gotten lasagna both times so far. I've also had the bruschetta which was on special and absolutely fantastic. The tomatoes actually tasted sweet. The atmosphere and service are great too. It's always packed in there, but they turn over tables really quickly. I've waited 20 minutes or less both times I've been, but it never felt like a long time. In the summer, they open the windows onto the street. I definitely recommend Noodle Pudding. It's a good place to go with your family, friends and guests.

It reminds me of a taverna on an island in Greece. Food is pretty good. If you love calamari then the grilled calamari is the best I have ever tasted. The tzatziki is excellent. Even when you order to go the food is still very good. You just can't go after a certain time because it gets too crowded.

Love the congee (rice porridge,jok) here at Big Wong. Â They have many varieties from pork and century eggs to dried scallops. Â I like to mix and match and they will try to discourage you saying "that is extra, will cost more", which I tell them "ok, ok, just charge me more". Â Totally worth it. Their barbecued dishes are good as well. Â Most notably the barbecued pork ribs. Yum! Â The roast duck and bbq pork is very good as well. Â  Why not get a triple combo over rice, roast duck, bbq pork, bbq ribs and a fried egg on top? Â Right, it will cost me more. Â "Just do it and charge me already". Â Ahhhh. Â Well worth it. Once you break the barrier and go often enough they know that you are a "Big Spender" now so you can order anything your heart desires even difficult combos not on the menu and they will deliver. Â But, they're gonna charge you for it. Â  Enjoy!

Great spot but their location is just hurting them soooo bad, not many people know about the place as its between Queensboro Plaza North and Astoria. Been here for dinner twice and enjoyed it both times. However, hard to see this place last long as they have Manhattan prices for their food. The food is exceptional though, but you cannot charge so much for LIC. I know people could afford it but thats not the point, you want people to come back again and again due to your location. The Burger might just be the cheapest and best thing on that menu for the price. If you Â want to impress your girlfriend or parents then this is also the spot. The food is really good, I have tried a bunch of dishes as went in a group of 6 and did a lit mix and match.
Amaaaaaaaaaazing! Best place to eat in Astoria. I want to try everything on the menu. Can't wait to go back! Â  Great service and great food. A bit pricy but it's worth it.
Amazing! Can have a drink of wine while shopping and great food choice to chose from.

The food is absolutely amazing. Fresh, well seasoned and simple. The tuna carpaccio is refreshing, fried oysters are wonderful plump fried goodness, cioppino is overflowing with different seafood including half of a lobster, the sea bass was a soft cloud of yumminess and I would even recommend the steak. I guarantee whatever you choose on the menu it will be lovely. FYI: Its BYOB and cash only.

I work around the area and my colleagues mentioned this restaurant had good food and was very inexpensive for a decent amount of food. So I decided to stop by and check it out for myself.... Appearance wise it is very elegant and everything from tables, chairs and cups are in tact although I'm not sure why the hostess is placed in the outside area where it is freezing cold where she was literally wearing a coat (that is torture! Especially in New York winter weather) I originally placed my order for take out because I was on my lunch and I planned to take it back to my job and eat it there boy was that a mistake! I only ordered a small appetizer (salchipapa) because I never have a huge appetite and because I thought it would be easy to cook and get out quickly the hostess reassured I would get my food quickly because it was so small but that was untrue because it took me 25 mins to get my food and at that point I just asked for it to be considered a stay in because I already wasted half of my lunch by just waiting. So what did I learn here? Umm, to call in advance for pick up or take out! Overall the food was good but then again it's just French fries and small bits of hotdogs. The bar area is pretty decent with many options to drink.

After giving it another shot me and that same friend have decided this restaurant just isn't for us. This time we came for dinner. They had McKenzies Seasonal Reserve hard cider which was awesome. I ordered a glass of Rose for $8 that came in the smallest wine glass I've ever seen. I decided not to order another since they weren't standard sized. They also didn't have the oysters that were listed on their menu that night. My friend ordered the butternut squash ravioli with a sage cream sauce and almonds. I love rich foods, but this was way too heavy. The ravioli was very good but the sauce completely overpowered it, and instead of a small sprinkling of almonds they threw a TON of slivered almonds in there, which texturally also made the creamy sauce more paste-like. Bizarre. The lobster mac n cheese wasn't bad, but the cheese itself was creamy to the point of being liquidy and could have been seasoned better. Same with the cream of mushroom soup, I added some pepper and that helped. We both ordered the hanger steak, mine coming with mushroom ravioli. Both of our plates came out cold. Really? On top of that our steaks were totally unseasoned. We actually added salt and pepper to them, not that it helped much. My friends asparagus were undercooked. The ravioli were fine but nothing special, although the mushrooms sprinkled on top were fresh and delicious. I said in my last review that they're trying to be an upscale diner, but just like at a regular diner you wouldn't order steak and pasta and expect it to be great. Maybe their simpler dishes are better, but for the higher prices I think I'd rather just go to a greasy spoon joint instead.

Basically, I'm tired of feeling compelled to shell out two-star reviews, so Bonnie's is going to get the benefit of my doubt, and a subsequent bonus star. I love burgers, and probably eat them in unhealthy frequency. This place is known for burgers, which in my mind means they pride themselves on a simple dish that draws a large portion of their customer base. Sounds like a good pairing for the evening. The burger was in fact a pretty good burger. It's a good size (not too huge, not too thick, not too thin, but with body) on a quality bun (so often the demise of an otherwise successful creation). The lettuce was adequate and the tomato was at least red, though tasteless due to its cold-world storage. The fries were also pretty good, and by pretty good I mean three-stars-good. The downside was the evidently undercooked state of my patty, and the absence of a good sear on the exterior. Â I ordered it medium, it was a solid medium-rare leaning towards the rare. I'm feeling generous though, and I've eaten my fair share of medium-rare burgers, so I dig in. So, all-in-all, a three-star food joint. What would normally make this a two-star review is the unbelievably poor service. Seriously, I don't expect much from a "burger joint." I don't expect essence-of-tomato when I ask for ketchup, and I certainly don't expect a well-dressed career-waiter tending to my needs. Say hi, take my order, bring me the burger, see if I need something later. Our waiter--and if you are reading this, waiter, just a small recommendation: in a dive bar (probably a former employment establishment) may accept this, but wearing a t-shirt that says COLON in huge letters across your chest when you are serving me food in a well-light space does not make for tantalizing taste buds, bud--actually walked away from me, while I was order, and attempted to finish taking my order while almost half-way across the restaurant. Me: oh, and can I have MayO on the side, PLEASE? Him: Ya Me: AND ALSO A DIET COKE?! Him: diet pepsi Me: FINE (Does mayo on the side--for my fries--and a diet coke put a tinge of homotard into myself, and this review? Maybe.) The short of it--the bus boy sucked, even for a bus boy, and the waiter was horrible in a tiny restaurant with high turnover but was never too crowded. And to end on a positive note, they have a pretty good beer list.
Our BEST dining experience in New York! Well worth the wait in line. We met some super cool people and enjoyed great food & service.

Deliciousness explosion! The french toast was out.of.this.world. My boyfriend had a pizza of amazingness that had every vegetable known to man and fried eggs on top. Come for brunch with the one(s) you love. Sink into a pillowed booth, sip your delicious coffee, and soon this super cozy space will welcomely hold you captive for the whole afternoon.

Ew...roaches! Â That's all I have to say. I went into this place to grab lunch before I went off to work--it's conveniently located right next to my bus stop. Â And there was a huge roach taking a stroll along the baseboard of the far wall, making a dash for the kitchen. Â I turned and made a dash for the exit. Â It's not surprising since they have a completely open storefront. Â But I don't like vermin garnishing my meals, and if you don't either I'd say pass.
I will die never tasting chicken and ribs this good. I mean it people. Ignore the looks of the place and TASTE their food. Wowza it is finger licking good.

My friend suggested we meet here one Monday night,his favorite bar and close to his apt so I said yes,feeling in the mood for something new. Not the bar I would have picked based on a view from outside but after half a beer it started to grow on me,very fast.Great selection of beers and at a reasonable price for the area.My friend joined me and we settled in for a good evening of different beers and good chat accompanied by a variety of musical tastes all of which I liked. My friend happened to mention at one point that he frequented the premises quite often but he hadn't actually seen our bartender before,a young twenty something very intent on her phone.At around one thirty in the am we order two more beers but about fifteen minutes later the bartender looks up from her phone and announces that we are the only reason she is still there and could we leave! No bones just goodbye. My friend always happy to please smiled paid the tab and left a healthy tip and we strolled outside.At which point I asked him did he not find what had occurred not only rude but inconvenient considering the amount of money we had spent.He did as it turned out but said again he drank there alot and likes the establishment. Fast forward a month or so.Same scenario,meet on a lonely Monday night for a few beers at his still new favorite bar,I arrive before hand and order a beer but cant quite tell if its the same girl.My friend confirms that it is when he arrives.At around one we step outside for a smoke,leaving the bar with about ten people inside.While we are smoking and talking with some new patrons to arrive from another restaurant at which they work only a block away,the ten or so people all come out of the bar pretty much at the same time and half or so stand outside saying goodnight and talking though none of them looking particularly interested in actually going home.So on a hunch I ask them if they were asked to leave...and guess what they were.Myself and friend return to the bar to finish our drinks at which point we are asked to leave.And its now we both say,in very polite terms I must add,that we are not only unhappy to be asked to leave before finishing our drinks and at a relatively early hour but a little miffed that its actually happening again and we attempt to inquire of the bartender if its a policy of the establishment to serve drinks and then ask the patron to leave.At which point we are told that not only are we completely rude but that we are now barred! I still think Momofuku Noodle House serves the best ramen in town and possibly in the country because David Chang provides a southern comfort sensibility to his ramen creations with pork belly and shredded shoulder. Surrender to your inner redneck and authenticity be damned. Ippudo's ramen, on the other hand, tastes much more Japanese and looks more like a bowl you would get at a higher-end noodle shop in the Ginza. It's not quite as satisfying, but the execution is pretty impressive nonetheless. Waiting for tables at the bar and on the sidewalk, the hipster clientele transfixed by their smartphones appear to agree if you can get their attention. Jamie W. and I waited about half an hour for a table last Saturday morning, which judging from the feedback from the preceding 27-hundred Yelpers, sounds like we scored quite a coup in terms of timing. Alas, we were seated at the kitchen counter where six stools were crowded together for the inevitable elbow jousting. Next to me, I kept feeling the snappish breeze of the giggly Asian twenty-something flipping her Farrah-like hair back for the benefit of her client... I mean her boyfriend. Regardless, we focused on the menu and ordered two appetizers. First was the $5 Tako Wasabi, which we were forewarned was purely raw (see photo). Bring it on. Fresh with a nice underlying kick due to the wasabi though the briny texture of the octopus didn't appeal much to Jamie. More unanimous praise came with the $8 Yamitsuki Goma Kyuri, a beautifully presented cucumber salad sprinkled on top with tobiko and sesame oil dressing (see photo). Very tasty although it struck both of us that the profit margin must be astronomical on this dish considering the ingredients involved. Finally the ramen. Jamie was lured by the daily special, the $15 Nakasu Kawabata Ramen, which consisted of soy-flavored ramen noodles with a chicken tonkotsu broth and topped with pork chashu, red-pickled ginger, cabbage, garlic, and scallions (see photo). It was an excellent combination of hearty flavors well worth the slurp, especially with the $2 addition of a seasoned salt-boiled egg (nitamago). Mine was even better, the $15 Akamaru Modern, which uses the original pork tonkotsu broth as the base and tops it off with their mini-meatball-shaped house miso paste (umami dama), pork chashu, cabbage, kikurage, scallions, and garlic oil. I took their advice and added not only the nitamago but also the $4 cuts of braised pork belly (kakuni) which brought the total up to $21 for a bowl of ramen albeit a fine-tasting one (see photo). Lazy bum that I am, I wished the belly was sliced rather than placed in the bowl as a mass. The ramen noodles had a nice al dente texture to them, although I have to admit I was surprised they were so thin compared to other housemade ramen I've had. No matter since the combination of savory flavors worked so well together. It's little wonder that Ippudo is such a popular chain back in Japan, and true to that aspect, the place was bustling with activity with all the sous chefs shouting "Irasshaimase!" in a typically boisterous fashion. For all the chaos and blaring music emanating from their Muzak, the service was quite courteous. FOOD - 4 stars...top-drawer albeit pricey ramen bowls with appetizers that provide the ideal complement AMBIANCE - 3.5 stars...busy as a beehive, honey SERVICE - 4 stars...cordial despite the cacophony TOTAL - 4 stars...trendy, tasty ramen for the hipsters... and the rest of us, too

Â Goes well with rice. - fried noodles are also great here, my favs are char kiew tiau (flat rice noodle), mee siam (thin rice noodle), indian mee goreng (round egg noodles - with lots of gravy) - Sarang Burong - fried mashed taro with seafood+veg inside. - Coconut or hainanese rice, i.o. of white rice For dessert, try the Coconut pudding (they serve it inside the coconut shells), peanut pancake (so buttery and crispy its so good), pulut hitam (black rice pudding/soup - best for cold days) Honestly, I am really disappointed. Â I hope this is just a temporary glitch from the recent move. Â I plan to go back in a few weeks and hope that I can say, "forget it, this place is still awesome"
Tasty. Â Not worth the long line, but if you pass by early and its empty, stop by.

Note: Review Date Aug 2012 (Dinner). I will soon post update about Brunch (was excellent) and other experiences. Pros - clam pizza came recommended on yelp and four square, very very good! Probably one of the best cooked clams ever. The pizza was crunchy and light. The scallop entree was good too. Medium rare scallops are always delicious. Service tendered was utter perfection. Con - 16oz rib eye with 4oz of fat trimmings need not be smothered with a cheese sauce that reminded me of cheddar kraft cheese. Although well cooked, I started to ponder my own mortality as I slowly finished what is surely a cholesterol filled dish. Â I am reassured however by the knowledge that the heart attack will come sooner rather than later. Confused - thrice fried spiced fries... They were heavily flavored with cumin that you can smell a mile away but you can barely taste it. It confuses the senses but it's very well fried. Update - I've become a regular patron of this place. It has come to my attention that the food is good here, but the problem all in all, is the price correlation with the food. More updated review to come. Bottom Line: A good spot if you're down for the high end business dinner type stuff.

I came here because I am trying to eat one dish from every country on the planet, including different lifestyle diets, such as gluten, vegan, raw etc. Nyonya was highly recommended on yelp and it was restaurant week, so I went for it. My boyfriend and I had the nasi lemak and a curry with rice noodles and young tofu. I liked the curry, the nasi lemak... not so much. But what the hell, right? Gotta try new things! Id definitely recommend the restaurant, because it has a very authentic malaysian vibe, but be aware that there is no outside seating... so visiting the restaurant during the cooler season might be advisable. Too many nice outdoorsy restaurants around to be stuck inside in summer!

I really wanted to give Pellegrino's Â 4 stars. This is the place where my husband and I have gone for our last few anniversary dinners. We go there because we got married in Italy and being in Little Italy - even among the tourists - brings back the fun memories from our wedding dinner. Â  The decor isn't anything spectacular. It's simple, clean, but the art reminds me of the 80's. Just a bit outdated. You don't need reservations if you dine early enough but you will most definitely need them if you venture out later. I want to say the clientele is distinctly touristy, but I'm not sure I could say so with any certainty. However, we went a few days ago for lunch and no doubt about it - tourists abound! On the upside, I've never had a bad meal here (the food is always delicious and fresh!) or experienced anything other than top-notch service. On the downside, the bathrooms are not very clean. I was sorely disappointed by this. So, it's mostly the filthy bathroom that makes me leave 3 stars when I really wanted to give Pellegrino's 4 stars. Still, it's worth it for the food and overall experience.

This place looked and sounded so promising!!! Unfortunately it was a very unappealing experience for me and my friends. Our friend was celebrating her birthday and brought our group of 7 here for a happy hour. The drinks were delicious but overpriced. I could live with that, if the bartenders weren't so incredibly rude. They were frankly a bit racist towards my African American friends, and gave everyone in the party a difficult time. We also could have lived with that as well, if the restaurant could seat us away from the bar at a table. However, every time we asked if we could be seated, either as a group or in two smaller groups, were told it wasn't possible because the restaurant was booked solid for the rest of the night. We could have lived with that if there was any evidence of that. However, the restaurant had about 80% open and free tables for the majority of hour two hour visit. I understand that large parties cannot always be accommodated, but there were literally nothing but empty seats and empty tables, and we were happy to eat a full meal at them, and leave before the reserved guests arrived... Which many never did. I would not bring my worst enemy back to this rude, racist, overpriced, under-impressive place.

Portions are huge I suggest sharing But the food is great Bloody Mary is ok had better Would go back for sure But my waitress Emily was to busy on her iPhone to pay attention to our table but hey cant have it all

i love that this place is down an alley. that whole alley has its own personality, and make freemans very unique. luckily, i came here on a sunday at 3 for late lunch and here was no wait for 3 people. usually there is a crazzzzzy wait. go me! if you are into taxidermy, this is your place. i have never seen so many stuffed animal carcases while i was eating in my life. very interesting. the brunch food was SO good, omg. devoured. i had the "Apple & Aged Cheddar Sandwich - radicchio, balsamic & mixed greens", and the "Gatsby Rickey" cocktail. tried the "Fall Vegetable Hash" and the "Smoked Trout" and it was all AWESOME. it's loud in freeman's, i was struggling to hear the table conversation. but i was kept amused by the decor and the delish food. i want to try dinner here and then i will write an update :-)
Great low key place for a cheap drink!

I was concerned about the level of noise, since this seems to be such a popular place. I came for a Sunday brunch with my family and boyfriend and the noise level was fine. I'm not going to reiterate how amazing the food is -- but the hype is so true!

I don't mind waiting at a restaurant. That being said, you will most likely wait. Sometimes not so long, sometimes very long, but the good thing is that there is a bar. The bar is fully equipped with nice eye-candy and good service. The wine is not so great if you go by the glass but it is okay. The non-alcoholic drinks are amazinggggg! So sweet and tart and bursting with flavor. THe mixed drinks are also way up there! So by the time you are seated, if you're boozed up, the food is surprisingly easy to digest. I got the steak salad, and had a try of my friend's steak (not so great), bell pepper pasta, amazing, and we also ended up ordering two bottles of wine, which was really yummy. I can't say this review is entirely valid as I was inebriated and everything tasted pretty good but I have also been there for brunch! I love going for brunch because if you go earlier than usual you will get seated very quickly and the food, regular brunch food, is super! I have to say what ties this place together is the drinks and service which are plentiful and flavorful. I really enjoy the experience of this place and will definitely go again.

Applewood is a cozy farm-to-table restaurant that really evokes intimacy with its attentive service and cramped quarters. The food was good but not memorable - I got the short ribs, which was tasty but I've had better. I certainly have had more interesting and provocative farm to table dishes at other restaurants: think Black Tree. My favorite part of the restaurant was probably the bathroom. It looked really country and had actual towels for drying your hands.

This isn't your grandfathers Thai food restaurant. This place is hip and breaks all stereotypes. The music is at times techno Asian like and really is fun while eating this awesome new fusion Thai food. There are not any standard curry dishes with the familiar coconut sauces but instead blending some not so traditional Thai spices like Turmeric and cilantro. I have ordered and enjoyed an appetizer of a type of braised beef spare rib that was so tender and delightfully spicy. The spring rolls were wonderful and filling also. I often order the Wok chili beef with turmeric which is always spicy and as I'm told by the staff, can not be toned down regarding the spiciness , so if you're not fond of spice Â don't order this dish . I have also enjoyed the Pad Kee Moa w/ beef instead of squid Â and thoroughly enjoyed my lunch. The staff is very friendly, and often fill your glass with water when you're close to running out.

This place is incredible!!! The bbq rib sandwich is amazing and I hate using the word amazing. I am from Texas and this eating this thing practically made me jizz in my pants it was that great. Some of the best food I've ever tasted. Also had the steamed pork buns which was also very very good but I am still thinking about that bbq, they should rename it BBQ Money Sammich. Don't forget to check out the milk bar at the back, the soft served ice cream is top notch.

Jimmy's may be my favorite place to eat in all of NYC. They've never disappointed and I find myself constantly salivating at the thought of eating tater heaven (a bowl of homemade tater tots topped with cheese eggs, and guac). Deep fried pickels and deep fried deviled eggs are a must as far as starters go. Their sandwiches and burgers are especially yummy; the greenpoint (a veggie burger topped with creamy spinach) remains my favorite. Do you see where this is going? I could practically recite their menu for you. Finally, this southern-styled greasy spoon is the perfect hangover remedy.

My friend came to visit from Australia and suggested brunch in LES so I wanted to take her somewhere good. Saxon & Parole had been on my list and after browsing through their brunch menu we decided to give it a try. The decor is unique, it felt warm and cozy, especially on a cold and snowy day. My friends were running late and I was worried the hostess won't seat us until everyone arrives, luckily that wasn't the case. We sat in a booth tucked in the back, which was perfect. We looked around to see what other people ordered and everything looked so good. I had my eyes set on the French toast but hubby was torn between a few items. When our friends finally came we ordered our meals, hubby had the baked eggs, my friend had poached eggs with toast and my other friend had steak & eggs. We were all happy with our order, hubby couldn't stop raving about his dish and said it was really different. It wasn't overly pricey, they have a brunch prix fixe which I thought was a good deal but none of us ordered cocktails. I would recommend this spot for brunch and may consider to come back and try their dinner.

---NOTE---I first reviewed this place back in January 2011. That review is pasted below the line, but I'll add these comments now: Piccolo Angolo is my favorite Northern Italian place in the United States. It's small and very low-key, but damn it if it doesn't pack a big punch. The staff is incredible when it comes to interacting with the customers, and for these prices this is a massive gem in the heart of New York City. [original January 2011 review below] -------------------------------------------------- Piccolo Angolo is easily one of my favorite places in New York City. It's owned by a very personable man named Angolo who knows his customers well and is always out on the floor making you feel comfortable. The food is unbelievable; they spare no effort in making each dish award-worthy and you'll be impressed each time with how they can be so consistently delicious. The house wine is also pleasantly surprising. I've had the lamb and the duck entrees and I can say that these might be my favorite lamb and duck dishes in the city. Piccolo Angolo is second to none in terms of Italian food. Lastly, to the day I die I will not stop thinking about that almond tiramisu. Personally, I love the taste of almonds and I LOVE tiramisu. The genius who put the two together needs to receive his/her Nobel Peace Prize already. Check it out when you're in the neighborhood. I would recommend making a reservation either the day before or the day of for parties greater than two; it's a popular local place and it WILL get crowded during peak hours.

Casa Enrique = classy Mexican, fit for date night or a dinner with out-of-towners. The space is white-on-white modern, and the menu has a short list of simple tacos (try the mouth watering brisket variety), classic enchiladas (green sauce had more flavor than the mole), and interesting Mexican entrees (skirt steak with roasted poblanos comes highly suggested). Extra points for being BYOB (I really hope it stays this way); it really lends to the casual feel. The quality of the food is high, the flavors are balanced albeit tempered on the spice level. If you are looking for crazy spicy hole-in-the-wall authentic style Mexican food, Casa Enrique is not the place. If you are looking for a relaxing restaurant with nicely prepared food, Casa Enrique it is.

Disappointed by food quality and quantity. Is this really an Argentine restaurant? Nothing reminded me - except maybe the saltenas? No wait. That's Bolivian. There wasn't even chimichurri sauce served with the bland steak. And the Milanesa looked nothing like you'd expect in buenos aires. Even if you out aside that this is supposed to be argentine - the food was mediocre and portions small. The best part was the dessert - bread pudding. The service was friendly, but we had to wait 30 minutes to sit down for our 8:30 reservation. The owner (?) kindly comp'ed us a glass of prosecco for the wait.

Someone posted that the steak tartare is no good but I just ate it and... AMAZING. I have eaten a lot of raw beef in my life. Cows flee upon sight of me. This stuff was super good. Also, Zucchini pasta. Good sauce, but more importantly the preparation was fab. Don't expect anything that really tastes all that much like pasta but instead get ready for one of the most awesome zucchini-based dishes since anyone ever thought zucchini could form the basis for a dish. Cocktails were also excellent. Top marks for the Louis XIV. Great atmosphere, and while sitting at the bar I keep seeing people emerge from the underground staircase behind the bar which is frankly hilarious. Will definitely be back!

A friend and I were planning to have a brunch picnic in Central Park this Saturday. Â We ran into this cute looking coffee shop after parking the car and decided to get our picnic food from here. Via Quadronno is a tiny, European style coffee shop/cafe that serves amazing coffee, espresso drinks, sandwiches, pastries, and wine. Â  We ordered two flaky sandwiches, coffee, cappuccino, and a croissant. Â Although our bill was a pricey $25 for coffee and a light meal, everything was delicious, fresh, and made from high quality ingredients. Â The soft, flaky croissant had the slightest hint of orange zest and, for lack of a more creative description, melted in my mouth. I'll definitely be heading here again on the way to another jaunt in the park.

Alright this place was on my to eat at list for about three months and FINALLY I get to try it. iv been to ippudo about 4x since this review so I have very high expectations. first off is the pork bun comparison. ippudo wins hands down. buns here have semi dry pork and they use way too much mayo. moreover it's just the bun, pork, and mixed greens... no special sauces like ippudo uses and I had to take out a good amount of mayo before I could bite in. next off I try one of their most popular ramens, a miso based one. the pork it came with were the same quality as the one in the pork bun app but they were lightly fried this time and thinner. the noodles were very good, on par with ippudo I would say, but unfortunately the broth was a bit too thick and salty. it is certainly flavorful but I would like something that did not diminish utility quite as quickly with each sip of the soup. the veges that the broth was mixed in was done excellently but given only two pieces of pork, it just didn't have the right balance. seating is extremely limited, I would recommend coming as pairs, but you must be in a party of 4 or less. ALSO NO THEY DONT TAKE CARDS. my friend had to pay for me and we didn't have the cash to tip more than 10% so the waiter held us up and asked us to go to an ATM nearby but neither me nor my friend had our debit card and we had no other money. I finally told him I would remember his name and come back w his tip next time I visit and we got to leave... I'm not gonna hold this against totto because I still think the quality is good enough for 4 stars but beware!!!!

seeing the melting of the white styro-foam box sticking on those hot dumpling freshly fried on the pan and got thrown in that box ...is kindda creep me out a bit. - like you guys eat that? isn't it chemical? If not because of this, I would have been a fan.

I'd rather eat at Vanessa's Dumpling House up the street. Yes, I realize that it is cheap and filling, but you can get cheap and filling and more delicious and spacious just a couple blocks up. I could also just be bitter because they didn't have three of the things we ordered available the day that we went: no sesame noodles, no scallion chive pancake, no sesame pancake with pork and eggs.

I always go for the ribs and pulled pork. Â Well cook and seasoned beyond perfection! Â The fried green tomatoes and sauce, Lord have mercy good! Â The greens and Mac & cheese is delicious seasoned well. Â The drinks and ice tea are hmmm delicious as well. Â The drinks are not weak! Â  Oh and try the chicken wings in sesame hoisin sauce...lick you lips good! Â I wish I could order there ice tea to go...ice cold and delicious!

I love this place. I live in the neighborhood and just starting coming here regularly last year. The food is very tasty, and the drinks just keep on flowing. The waitstaff is terrific; they often have to deal with large noisy groups of folks, but both customers and waitstaff are cheerful and respectful -- it's just a laid-back, yet energetic, noisy, friendly place. I do have to comment on "Emily S.'s" "review" of her experience last night at the Ear. I was sitting there with my friend, eating my dinner, and this group of perhaps 20 people came bombing in to the dining area. The waitstaff was trying to accommodate them, putting tables together, etc., but most of the group just kept milling about, and, frankly, d--king the staff around. They got more and more loud and belligerent, and, finally, one "bro" climbed up on a chair and started bellowing! When asked by the waitstaff to please sit down, he began to hurl verbal abuse at her. I was absolutely flabbergasted at the outrageous behavior that "Emily S." and her group exhibited. The Ear can be a noisy place, but the vibe is always sweet and gentle fun. These folks definitely came in tanked with an aggressively bad attitude. Everyone there breathed a sign of relief when they took the staff's suggestion and left.

Maybe this works better in big groups. Family size helpings means that two of us shared a huge plate of broccoli pasta. I don't think the cooks got around to cutting the florets separately so we got the equivalent of half a broccoli head cut into three. Delicate meal, this is not. But I suppose you get what you pay for so for sitting in a restaurant, well priced. Did not try anything else so this is getting a 3 ... benefit of the doubt.

This restaurant is NOT even close to authentic Colombian food. My friend invited me to what she referred to as "a great Colombian restaurant" in Brooklyn. Being that I was born and raised in Colombia, and I miss my grandma's cooking so much, she wanted to give me a taste of home and make me happy - she's so sweet. When we got there, the wait was a little long so I thought hmmm... this has got to be good. Â At the moment I did not think much of the fact that everyone there, except for me, was white! Â I ordered my favorite soda, "Colombiana" and started to get excited. I ordered the Ajiaco soup because that is such a typical dish from Bogota and I miss not having it every Sunday for lunch. When my soup came, I though the waitress was joking! It was a super yellow broth, with a piece of chicken, corn on the cob and white potatoes. Â First of all, ajiaco is not bright yellow; it is a dark yellow, moving to a very light brownish color. Second, it is a soup but not a broth; it is a very thick - so thick, that you put cream on top of it, and it does not sink (by the way I didn't get the cream). Second, you don't serve a piece of chicken; the chicken is shredded. The potatoes are not white or served whole! you have to use the yellow kind called "criollas" and wait for them to almost dissolve in the soup. And what happened with the guascas? there is no ajiaco without guascas. Â Their soup tasted like something I can make at home with Â free-range chicken for a lot cheaper. My friend ordered the "bandeja paisa" because that is her favorite dish there. I am not from Medellin, nor have I ever been there, but I have had a lot of bandeja paisa in my life and her dish was just sad. Â I really wanted to walk out, but did not want to hurt her feelings after she was being so thoughtful. Â I may just invite her to come with me to Colombia next summer and show her what Colombian food is like. Â Hell, I will take her to have ajiaco the first day!!!! So my dear American friends - when you want to try ethnic food, go to a restaurant that is filled with people from that country. In other words, if you want to try Colombian food, go to a restaurant that is filled with Colombians. That is when you get close to the original. Â Of course, if you want to taste the real thing, then you have to go that country.

Awesome. This bar restaurant is great. The food is fantastic - the brussel sprouts are super tasty and the prosciutto on grits is really great. I was super impressed with how they made simple, less luxurious food very refined. the cornbread is good, but the salted caramels were INCREDIBLE! This is a bourbon spot and the drinks are great! the hot toddy is fantastic and not too sweet. the spicy buck is also one we really enjoyed. I love the modern, but not too slick decor. The staff are super friendly, but not at all annoying - loved it!
Best Pizza! Hands down!

Tartine is a SOLID four stars. The dining room is small and fills up quickly. Â I went on a Friday night at around 7 and was seated instantly, but by the time our dinner was over there was a hefty line waiting for a table. Â I would recommend going to dinner early if you don't want to wait in line. This is a no frills dining experience. Â The tables and chairs are standard, decor minimal, paper napkins, etc. Â They don't even open your wine for you here, they just throw you a corkscrew. Â  The food was good. Â It's nothing that's going to blow your pants off, but for $30 we shared an appetizer (salmon tartar A++), an entree (beef mignonettes au poivre) and a desert.

I don't have words for how good the food here was, and it was cheap/prepared speedily. Their shawarma meat is seasoned and cooked amazingly and the vegetables and pita were stelar (the pita was also warm even though my friend and I carried out). Must eat here again.

The first four stars are given by default on the basis that The Farm hosted my favorite domestic Belgian-style brewery, Ommegang. Â The last star was for the spectacular food that was paired with the celestial beer. Witte opened up the session. Â  The BPA was paired with a lovely plantain appetizer that was garnished with lime. Â  The Rare Vos complemented a Pork Tartine that was topped with apples and served over a piece of perfectly toasted bread that absorbed the pork juices. Â Sigh. The Abbey Ale came with perfectly cooked beets and carrots over grits. Finally, the Three Philosophers supplemented the lovely Chocolate Sponge. Â Gouda Cheese and Raisin Puree were also present. Â Unfortunately, I've never been a fan. Â I can speculate that they were good. Combine the fact that Ommegang Brewery was there discussing the beer and their pairings, with the spectacular fact that Tom the Chef managed to pull off delicious food despite the voluminous crowd and you've got a great restaurant.

What luck! I stumbled into Penelope with my fiance, his brother and one of my besties on a complete and utter brainless whim. We went in because I saw the storefront, liked it; saw the name, liked it. We had been roaming around mid and lower Manhattan since 10 am, searching for apartments. And we didn't live in Manhattan at the time, mind you. We had traveled from Boston, to CT, and then into the city. We had been WALKING - no train - no taxi - since 11 am. From uptown (70's) all the way down as low as Ludlow Street in LES. I think I calculated that we had walked some odd 100+ blocks that day? And Penelope was near the end of the journey. And she did not disappoint. We shuffled in, bewildered and probably looking half-alive as I could see a somewhat concerned look on the hostess' otherwise welcoming face. We were seated immediately at a middle table. Water was provided immediately without question, along with the menus. We were given time to decide on drinks - yes please. What a surprising little beer menu they've got there! We were very pleased and impressed with the collection of local and imported brews they've got to offer. We all found something we'd enjoy. The French-American menu was quite enticing as well, an array of choices, from salads to sandwiches, soups and egg dishes. They've got non-meat options as well for the vegans and veggies. And don't skip on desert here - we tried the velvet cake and it was absolutely mouthwatering. The ambience was hip, yet relaxing and very conducive to conversation. I'd easily coin it as "cute and cozy". And you could definitely come alone with a book or computer if that's your thang. Service was fast, friendly and patient - we may not have been the "quickest" bunch to deal with as our heads were swollen with blood that had been shunted upwards from our aching feet over the miles of hot, sticky pavement. Would absolutely return and wanted to remember Penelope - which is the only reason I bookmarked her - because unfortunately, by that time in our fruitless apartment search, I knew that we would most likely not be living in the LES.

Rank: B. Name of the Game is Pasta. Good for groups - loud, fun energy in a large wooden hall style room. Food is mediocre though for the price. I can think of at least a half dozen other places I'd rather go, based on the combination of price and taste (Dell Anima, Del Posto, Maialino, Scarpetta, Convivio - before it closed, Babbo, Otto Enoteca). The prosciutto and mortadella meatballs and the tortellini panna (meat filled pasta, duck liver mousse) were two items that stood out in my mind.

I don't understand why this place has such a good review???!!!! As much as I want to give this place a higher rating, it is just average and way below expectation. The wait was 45 minutes because it is a tiny place. And it took them another 45 minutes to serve your order. My friend and I ordered deviled egg, chargrilled burger and crispy pig ear salad to share. Deviled egg is just a boiled egg with egg yolk blended in mayo and sprinkled parsley. It tastes nothing surprising as what most people said. Plus $4 for an ordinary boiled egg is just way overrated. Then the chargrilled burger tastes bland. My dad can make a better burger than them. Lastly, crispy pig's ear salad is way too sour. They must forgot and pour too much lemon/vinaigrette dressing. Also they literally served us a whole piece (uncut) pig's ear. WARNING: cutting that pig's ear is tough! Totally ruined our appetite. All in all, I do not recommend this place to anyone looking for a nice flavorful meal. Don't waste your time waiting 45mins for a table and end up with not-so-good, way overrated dishes.
Great, cheap, fresh falafel and nice salads and toppings. The service is super fast too. One of my favorites.

How can anybody "hate" this place? Sure its full of hipsters and staffed by hipsters, but they are nice, and the food is GOOD. Everything at Marlow is GOOD. Not just the biscuits, but the salads, the entrees, the pastas, etc. Sure the portions are small, and the prices are high, but did I mention that the food is GOOD?

I've been here a couple of times since it opened and can say I've never had a bad time! Â Be sure to check it out this Friday 3/25 as the Dark Horse will have live music from John Malone! Â Anyway, this place is everything I need in a bar, plenty of TV's, great service, full menu and reasonable prices. Â The guys who run this place now have done a great job. Â And the downstairs space is a great size and is perfect for parties. Â All in all just a very cool place!
Very cool ancient bar, really good basic food. Only been for lunch, turkey or angus burgers are great. Only tihng keeping it from 5 stars is they're pretty pissy about splitting checks.

The Mezes are really good and the Brussels sprouts a must. The large tables makes Ilili ideal for small groups. Go there in the evening, not for lunch. The food seems to be fresher in the evening. Staff is very friendly.

A last minute decision that turned out fantastic. Â In a rush to get to a 7:30 Broadway show, me and some friends decided to ditch our original plans and give Room Service a try. We didn't wait at all and immediately started the meal off right with the Lychee Sangria - yum and potentially dangerous! Â I usually always get Tom Yum soup, but ventured to try something new with the Dumplings and ginger broth soup. Â It was delicious and flavorful. Â  With all the choices, we decided to share a few dishes to maximize the experience. We tried the Basil Chicken, Panang Curry, and Spicy Basil Eggplant. Â All were delicious, though the Basil Chicken was not the best I've had in the city (which is disappointed, as that is my go-to dish). Â However, the Eggplant (which was in more of a black bean basil sauce) was out of this world! Â The Panang Curry was some of the best I've had...including what I had in Thailand. Ironically, the only issue I had was with the Service. We didn't get silverware, plates, serving spoons or napkins until we asked. Â And even then, they'd bring one setting for the table of 3. Â And the plates were more like coasters, instead of plates to eat dinner off of. Â It was really odd and semi-awkward service. Despite the service...With its fun vibe and delicious food, Room Service is a great place for dinner with friends or a date (its a bit dark, so keep that in mind if you are trying to figure out the 'mood' you want). Â I'd definitely go again.
Never goes wrong with these! Hirata bun & spicy miso ramen & wasabi ramen!
long line? - yes overpriced? - a little worth the wait? Â - yes! fun atmosphere? - weeeee! some advice? - get there early or wait at the bar. you're gonna have some great noodles.
Hmmmm saw an article about this place and thought it was all just a Meh experience in terms of taste... Design was awesome though.

Great brunch location. The ambiance reflected an adorable and small French cafe. This place is very tight with little very little wiggle room. I heard my neighbors Â whole convo. Anyways, the waffles and egg Benedict are the bomb. xo

I finally made it here this past weekend after wanting to come for the longest. The atmosphere is cool. It's a nice place to relax with a group of friends. I had the chicken sandwich, sweet plantains and Sangria. My bf had the guac and queso plato, Mexican corn, and spiked lemonade. Everything was tasty. I loved my sangria but the spike lemonade needed some extra spiking so I paid an extra $5 for a shot of vodka in it. For all that the bill was about $45-50 which is pretty reasonable for 2 people. My only problem was with the security patrolling the place. It was my first time so I'm not sure if anything happens in here but he was walking around the restaurant like a bouncer in a club. Made me a little uneasy because I wasn't sure if I needed to be on the look out like he was... Either way, I'll be back.

This place was recommended to me and so I had put this on my bucketlist. My friends were coming in town for the holiday weekend and so we all decided to try this place out. This place gets really busy around 12:30pm. It opens at 12pm, but didn't seem like too many people. It's rather small so I would recommend making a reservation. When I had called to confirm my reservation the day before you can tell they were super busy and it was at a decent volume of loud. As a suggestion, order about 2-3 small plates per person. We had gotten 6 plates total and it was perfect for dessert too! We got the Potatas Bravas, Bacalao Croquetas with Orange Alioli, Atlantic Calamares with Harissa and Squid Ink, Crispy Pork Belly with Peas, Honey Ham and Sweet Basil Mousse, Pork Meatballs with Fried Peppers and Marinated Sepia, and Fideos with Chorizo and Clams. For desserts, we got the bread pudding (Pudin de Pan) and the Custard (Crema Catalana con BuÃ±uelos). Both pretty good and not super sweet. Definitely would recommend this place :)

I LOVE THIS PLACE. It's busy, but the service is good and the food is DELICIOUS. I got the veal sorrentino dish, which was rich and savory. My dad got a delicious steak, and my mother got the chicken picante-SO GOOD. Their menu is pretty extensive and you can tell they source their ingredients from quality vendors. Definitely recommend going here, especially if you're looking to catch a Broadway show. Might be a tad expensive, but definitely work it.

No longer a BYOB but we saw tables with alcohol. Â I think they just posted the sign in case inspectors come, but they def. did not enforce the rule when i went . Â Places like this are hard to review because most people rate the food relative to the price. Â The appetizers were definitely good but it wouldn't have been nearly as good if it weren't that cheap. Â The dumplings were good but I feel like its a generic Chinese restaurant dumpling. Â You have to get it fried versus steamed, it does come out nice and hot. Â The avocado potato salad had chickpeas and potatoes. Â Great blend of favors and a unique dish from other asian cuisines. Â The entrees were just alright. Â The chicken curry tasted like a ketchup sauce with curry powder and the noodle soup dish was a bit bland. Â Tibetan food in generally has a ton of spices that are very colorful and smells potent but just a bit lacking in taste. Â These two dishes is exactly how it should be done but just were not for me. Â It's a simple local joint feel. Â Tightly squeezed but feels authentic.

Terrific sidewalk cafe. Had lunch with NBA Draft Comms crew working at the Barclays Center across the street. The specials were terrific. I had kale caesar salad with chicken which was moist and tasty. The service was quick and since it is on a small triangle corner the traffic was not loud. Going there again today!

I really wanted to like this place. I live around the corner and the prospect of having a solid and affordable option nearby appealed. Â I stopped in on a Saturday evening at 6:15 with no reservation. Â The place was packed, which I took as a good sign given the early hour. Â We expected a wait, but the host told us it would only be a few minutes, as a few tables had paid and were ready to leave. A table then opened up in the next five minutes, but then the host gave it to an older couple who had come in after us who also had no reservation. Â I was mildly annoyed by this, but figured other tables were opening soon so no big deal. Â Except then the other table that had paid decided to linger for another 25 minutes, during which 25 minutes my mild annoyance blossomed into full maturity. Â  The food was decidedly mediocre. Â I know the service glitch could have thrown a pallor over the entire experience, but I'm being as objective as possible. Â We had the spinach and fennel salad with sundried tomato vinaigrette, and the warm octopus and potato salad with olives and capers. Â The salad was shamefully lacking in acid. Â The octopus, however, was delicious; perfectly tender and luscious, with crisp-soft bits of potato and briny bits of olive and caper to break up the richness. Â This dish could've also used some lemon or additional acid, but overall was good. For pastas we had the spaghetti alla chitarra (being homemade, this shape is flatter than storebought and more akin to linguine) with bolognese, and the squid-ink taglioni with clams and cherry tomatoes. Both were pretty flat and lacking in depth and balance. Â The taglioni also suffered from a vaguely bad-clam flavor and we ended up leaving most of it. House red wine was a decent montepulciano and a very generous pour for $6.50. Â Service was indifferent with a dash of unfriendliness, but I got the feeling that it was just our server, as other waiters seemed perfectly nice. I feel like I should give this place another shot since it's so close and so many people like it. Â Maybe I just didn't order the right things? Â But given the number of other places to try in the city, I won't be going back anytime soon.

Dare I write yet a third review of this legendary halal cart, the first time I've done a triple-play for any business on Yelp? After all, it's been three-and-a-half years since my last report, and maybe it's the dependability that really gets to me about this nocturnal operation. It's never been about the service. It's four hard-working guys and nary a smile gets cracked among them. They're a well-oiled machine with a very fixed menu that hasn't strayed in the five years that keeps bringing Jamie W. and me back. What did change this time is that the competition moved in. Yes, there's a look-alike cart parked just a few yards away, and it was confusing to figure out which one was the authentic one. In fact, we stood in line for ten minutes before I scouted out the situation and realized we were in the wrong line. We corrected ourselves post haste and were immediately handed sharp little shopping bags with "The Halal Guys" emblazoned on them (see photo). We naively asked the young guy handing them out if this is the original cart, and without skipping a beat, he said, "There is no other cart." Wow, the power of denial. Anyway, it was nice to see the price hasn't changed, still six bucks for a rice platter, and we both went for the Chicken and Gyro combo. We got our Diet Cokes from the guy in the adjacent cart on the corner and hustled over to the wooden benches on 52nd Street since we knew they would be empty. The kids would rather eat on the concrete near the carts, but not us. No, we like setting ourselves for a little semi-private picnic even as it started to sprinkle. And the food? It's simply the best street food in Manhattan. Overstatement? No. And don't talk to me like that. In fact, I can't find a food cart in San Francisco that even comes close in terms of pure after-hours satisfaction. The hefty aluminum tin was full to the brim with shards of grilled chicken and lamb with shredded iceberg lettuce over a bed of rice and topped with soft pita slices. Glop on the mysterious "white" sauce with just dabs of the scary-hot sauce, and you have the perfect $6 meal (see photo). I don't know why I always wonder if I will finish it, because I Hoover it like nobody's business. It's just great comfort food plain and simple. I keep hoping someone will recreate it in my 'hood, but nobody has. Those lines would wrap around the block guaranteed. FOOD - 5 stars...eez steel good, eez steel real real good AMBIANCE - 3.5 stars...dining under the stars after all, but grab your bench fast SERVICE - 5 stars...who needs chit-chat?...they're buzzsaws TOTAL - 5 stars...I wouldn't change a thing about the Halal Guys

Ok, I'm officially hooked. When i first went into the venue I thought it had a peculiar smell. But that didnt deter me. I ordered the Noah's Ark (food for 2) which gives each person half a lobster, crab and shrimp roll, 2 empress claws, chips and a soda. I also ordered a NE clam chowder (yep I'm a chowder junky). Well, I heard the reviews but went in with low expectations. But man I was proved wrong! The chowder was outstanding, and the rolls were awesome. I left the place stuffed, but not too stuffed. Kudos!

It's too bad the Carmine Street location closed but this new spot is bigger and still maintains most of the original Grey Dog character. Â Others feel their system of ordering and seating is unorganized but I like it. Â It gets busy and crowded during peak times but get there during off-peak hours, and you can appreciate the good vibes.
Awesome oysters & great beer selection. Get here before 7pm and you can get their oyster & beer special for $12. Great spot to grab a bite to eat and catch up with friends.

It's Â been a while folks, but I'm back on yelp and ready to review. I have to start with Do or Dine. I have been here at least ten times and have never been disappointed. In the last year, I have made Do or Dine my go to restaurant. I have tried almost everything on their frequently changing menu and have very few complaints. The steak tartare is by far my favorite, but I have never had anything that wasn't amazing. I would recommend Do or Dine to anyone looking for a great meal in an energetic atmosphere.

I've eaten here on perhaps eight occasions and each one was terrific. Â I've done it all -- brunches were good, I've walked in and had lunch, I've had a formal dinner for two and four, and I've had a birthday party where about eight or ten of us took up a big table. In each case the food was terrific, the staff was attentive, and we've been pleased. Â It's not cheap, but it isn't pricier than it deserves. Â A great Slope restaurant and a favorite.

I was so excited when I saw that a LadurÃ©e had opened in NYC since I love the store in France. Â Unfortunately, the product here is not as good as in France, it was a real disappointment. Wow, so after seeing all the reviews on Yelp, I wasn't sure if I could believe the hype -- over 2000 reviews? Well, that being said, believe it ALL. I came here with my boyfriend for some dumplings and we were excited to try a bunch of them - we got steamed shrimp, steamed chicken, and pan fried pork dumplings. And we also got the scallion pancakes. The dumplings were all good, but definitely the best one was the pan fried pork. Was it just that it was the boy one on the menu that was pan fried and not steamed? Maybe. But regardless, it was bomb. Definitely go there to get these pork ones, even if you're not super into pork. Also - we bought all those: 1 shrimp, 1 chicken, 2 pork, and pancakes and it was all for less than 10 bucks total. And we couldn't even eat it all! Only got through about half and had leftovers for later! What a steal! Also, the shop itself is a tiny tiny tiny box, and so you kind of have to shove your way into the place, order, step out, and wait to be called. But hey, it's worth it.

Foie gras: 3 Everything else: 4 Went on a weeknight just to get the foie gras appetizer. I looove seared foie gras to death, and I thought the $28 splurge was worth it. Well... almost. Everything else was wonderful except the foie. I had two huge lobes of foie on top of a fruit puree with one dollop of fruit to the side. Somehow I didn't think this was anywhere near the best foie gras I've ever tasted. I don't think it was seared the way I liked it, I like it slightly crispy outside, with plenty of sweet sauces accompanying it. It also didn't come with bread, which is really annoying. You just can'e eat foie without some sort of carbs on the table. Foie gras: 3, even though portions were huge. I actually got sick eating it all. Besides that, the server was nice given that I only ordered one dish. I got an amuse bouche that was made of beets and horseradish foam: 2 eghh... pretty sour and gross. The bread they give you is pretty nice, you can select from several and the apple bread they give you in the beginning is pretty and tasty: 4. I didn't order dessert, but they gave us a plate of little candies. I was way too full to eat the dessert. It was strange since all I had was an appetizer... of pure fat! It came with two tiny miniature muffins, a tiny macaroon, fruit gel, truffle, and some crispy thing. Haven't eaten any yet, but I'm sure they're tasty. Then as we are leaving a lady stops us and gives me this cute little lemon loaf. Didn't eat that yet either. So overall a pleasant experience, but the foie was quite disappointing. It just didn't taste good... I don't know how else to say it. I felt kind of sick after eating the first lobe. Its sad, but I don't think i want to eat foie for another 3 months, because of this experience.

Wonderful food and amazing service! The staff pays a lot of attention to detail and makes sure to take the time to guarantee that you order something you like. This was one of my best experiences at an Italian restaurant in NYC.

Fact: Al Sharpton is probably not appetizing. He looks like he would be very salty. Fact: The Al Sharpton at Amy Ruth's is delicious! I have never had Chicken & Waffles. Why would I? I mean, who would even think that it's a good combination? Oh, how naive I have been. Wasting precious time which could've been spent eating at Amy Ruth's! The waffle was perfect: fluffy, light tasting, but able to hold onto the maple syrup without getting soaky and squishy (yes, "squishy" is a culinary term used in the description of waffles.) I had smothered chicken b/c I think chicken is dry otherwise and it was good. We didn't wait long because we missed the church and brunch rush and were too early for the dinner wait and the service was good, towards the end the waitress disappeared, which I always find annoying but I wasn't in a rush so I shouldn't complain. I also learned from the man at the door (who the hell is this guy?? doorman? host? bouncer?) that he doesn't like scary movies.

WHAT. A. DISAPPOINTMENT. We were a party of 4, all looking forward to the food here. Cozy sexy. Terrif spot to enjoy cocktails and catch up with a few calm friends. Its hella dark so if you wanna fake out your date cuz you be fugly, bring her/him here. Its not a rowdy spot so keep away, dooooshbags.
Place has been redecorated nicely! Kudos for the nice bar... colors definitely liven up the place! it's still cold....... ha.

This is the tale of two pizzas. One is vegan and one is not. One is named "In Ricotta da Vegan" and one is named "In Ricotta da Vita." I ordered the former over the phone, not knowing that the latter existed. So I'm pretty stupid for being all like "wow, no wonder other vegans flip out about this place, that looks surprisingly like animal sausage, that's kinda incredible" but then I checked the box and it says "RDV" on the side so then I'm like, cool, it must be the right thing, a few bites later decide I'm really not down with the sausage stuff (and the pizza is kind of chilly in the middle anyhow). SO SICK that night, I can't even tell ya. And then I check the online menus the next day and there it is, proof that a vegan pizza order could be very easily mixed up with a non-vegan pizza order, especially when calling in. Dude, Paulie, WTF? Bad idea. BAD, BAD IDEA. I'm open to having my mind changed about this place but I would be very, very careful and probably very annoying with the number of times I'd repeat the word "vegan" -- maybe before every single word. Strike 1 of 3 for my vegan powers... gotta be more careful or the vegan police will come... womp womp!

Three words: half-price wine (mondays and tuesdays -- bottles only, but amazing bargain). Yes, brunch is chaos. And yes, there are some misses on the menu -- calamari appetizer stuffed with odd grains, overly vinaigretted salad. But Miriam is wonderful overall. Pita is thick and meaty (not pre-sliced grocery store). The hummus is habit-forming. Fish is usually juicy and light. And if you can tolerate the stroller crowd and fight your way to a brunch table, the payoff is huge: hummus, stewed tomatoes, poached eggs, and pita to sop it all up.

I would never come back here !! The service is bad . The staff members don't care about anything . I felt like they don't like to work there . When they set up their table they literally touch the glass from top which was disgusting . I mean people will drink water . I had momo it was delicious but the sauces they have me it wasn't fresh at all . I am pretty sure it's not fresh and they are just using one sauce for different people . Suggestion they should have fresh sauces for momo it shouldn't be bubble on the top and they shouldn't serve the same one for different people . This is the reason I am giving one star .

Eastwick, you get an A- in my book. And only because you are not easily accessible by the subway and you don't offer bottomless mimosas. Everything else was top notch! Recently went here for brunch with RusBra and his mum. I was shocked because it was rather empty on a Saturday. Whatever, all the more attention for us! His mom and I both ordered the lox bagel, he got the shakshuka. All were delicious. The bergen bagel was so soft, it really sealed the deal. The shakshuka was definitely an adventurous choice for Rusbra (basically eggs in a tomato sauce), but after sneaking a bite...it was definitely a good one. The tomato sauce is almost sweet. Beware. The mimosas were also very good. Who knew that just adding a bit of strawberry would help so much? The $14 prix fixe is such a great deal here. Well worth it. I highly recommend this place for brunch. That being said, we drove here...not sure what the nearest train is. It definitely seems off the beaten path.

I was looking for a good place to eat and decided to try this based on the reveiws. I also decided for something different...I loved the pablano buger, it was loaded with roasted pepper and cheese and there sauce...juicy...delicious...my mouth waters thinking about it. Not typical burger for me. I also had their lemonade and it was a really simple lite drink...not sweet and overpowering with lemon. Overall the place is cozy...the staff was nice. I will be going back.
I've been for brunch twice. Â Latin twist on breakfast items (like eggs benedict, steak and eggs, etc). About $12, I think. Â Would definitely recommend. Service is so-so.
Sakagura has a fun atmosphere and delicious food to match! I loved my soup, and the drinks were good too. Great service to top it all off. Excellent find!

*REVIEW ON HAPPY HOUR ONLY First, get on your Yelp app and check-in so you can SPIN THE WHEEL when you come in for the chance to win a free snack or drink! Â Yay!
