The rice balls, mozzchips, and bufala mozzarella were great apps. For entrees we had the chicken parm, chicken francese, veal parm, steak, and a couple of the pastas. Everyone cleared their plates. By the end of the meal my friends and I were enamored with this place. Can't wait to come back.

Food was delicious. Â Had the classic hotdog and my girl had buffalo chicken spring rolls. Â Lots of TVs to watch the Monday night game. Â Need to light up the bottles behind the bar couldn't tell what alcohol they had. Â Would return, prices were normal for the area and the staff was very nice.

I loved the ambience at SoCo..dimly lit lights, candles on the table...so far so good. On to the food. We started with the wings, well actually my bf did...he said they were ok. I had the mussels...DELICIOUS! We shared a ceasar salad..it was...um....different. I like Kale (in my green juice) not my ceasar salad, other than Â that is was good. My salmon was cool & his steak was "ok"...he didn't finish it all...that should tell you. We live in the Bronx so I probably won't be visiting SoCo anytime soon.

This is the first place that I got NY pizza from, and it was sooooooo delicious!!! Â I mean, wow. Â The mozzarella was so fresh, and it was just so perfect. Â I tried other NY pizza since, and nothing compares. Â I think about it often since I live on the other side of the country. Â But someday.... someday.... we shall meet again. Â  PS. And as a bonus, we sat right next to Geoffrey Rush (although, I didn't know until he left and my bf pointed it out point blank--I'm horrible with recognizing celebrities).

Having only indulged in dinner, I was eager to try Paprika's brunch offerings. And after swearing off a few of my local spots for their long lines and lack of service, I pinpointed this as the locale for this past Saturday's noontime nosh. And I'm oh so happy I did. Walking in with our party of four, I was shocked to see no lines or drunken buffoonery. We were seated right away in their well-lit dining room among crimson and coral chair cushions and walls. The $13.50 brunch prix fixe menu was nothing short of divine: scrambled green eggs on a bed of polenta, apple pancakes and my personal favorite, Eggs Benedict. Their version of bene is simply perfect. Poached eggs served on a bed of thin pancetta, placed atop toasted italian bread and drizzled with a buttery fresh hollandaise. Pair it with a simple side salad of baby lettuce, tomatoes and vinaigrette and it - almost - feels healthy. Each entrÃ©e comes with a coffee and a choice of mimosa, bellini or juice. For the quality, the incredibly friendly service, price, lack of crowding and absolute convenience - this is the new brunch place to beat in my 'hood!

Great place! Really is just like being in your grandmas kitchen. Quaint and cozy. The locals know about this spot and you always wanna go after the locals go. The white borcht is delish. Had it with a side of cheese perogies. Food was great friendly staff. Its a small place so prob not the best place to go with a big crowd. Aside from that highly recommend.
The cha siew here is soo sweet and filled with flavor (most likely from the honey). It's good but there's usually a line.

I've been going to Snack for close to 5-6 years. My favorites are the avgolemono soup (I always order two), the cheese triangles, the lemon lentils, the greek salad, the beet salad, and the sandwiches. The garlic potato dip is POWERFULLY garlicky. I would order their entrees more often if they weren't so gigantic. Between the food and the cozy ambiance, I'd give it five stars but I had to take one away because: it's tiny. Five tables. About 1/3 of the time I go, I'm so hungry that I end up getting my food to go and sitting on the bench outside or near the playground. The other reason I took away 1 star is because they keep using this blond waitress that was hired last summer or spring. She's the worst. The first time I noticed her, she got my order wrong and insisted that I had ordered what she thought I did, even though I order the same couple of items and what she insisted I ordered was not one of them. Then when our food finally came, she kept coming by and trying to take away the plates even though food was still on them and my friend was still eating. The table next to us also kept saying they weren't done with their food when she tried to take away their food. She forgets orders frequently and I'm just confused about why they keep her on if she can't do her job correctly even though she's only overseeing 4 two-seat tables and 1 three-seater.

I arrived at 7pm, on a Tuesday, with a party of 5. Â We put our name down on the clipboard by the entrance and were told that it would be a 30 minute wait. Â 30 mins ain't that bad when the rewards are cheap beer and delicious yakitori. Â An HOUR passes. Â I am dying a slow death from an extreme drop in blood sugar levels. We inquired several times about the reason for the long wait. Â Apparently the restaurant wanted to seat us at this specific table in the restaurant, which had been occupied for the past few hours by four, more-than-well-proportioned women who were downing pitchers of beer like water. Â  Dear citizens of the world: Â Japanese street food = you eat, you drink, you get the eff out. Â I repeat: GET (THE EFF) OUT. Anyways, onto the food. We ordered the following dishes: 1) Mentaiko pasta dish - pasta with salmon cream... AKA delicious mayo. 2) Yakitori platter. Â It comes with a pork belly skewer, that's all you need to know. 3) Grilled Mackerel. Grilled simply. Â Very very tiny bones. Not for the lazy eaters. 4) Grilled Squid with Liver Sauce. Liver Sauce is strong, so you better love liver. 5) Tuna Sashimi. Fresh and nimble. Â Thick slices. It's a staple. 6) Kimchi Fried Rice (with bits of pork belly). HECK YES, GET IN MAH BELLY. 7) Octopus Takoyaki. Not a fan of most deep fried stuff... 8) Pork Pancake. Meh, It was too oily for my tastes... 9) Agedashi Tofu.... blurgh... I hate wasting stomach space on tofu. 10) Lastly, a pitcher of beer. Surprisingly, when split among the five of us, the bill only came out to $28 (this included tax and tip). Â Not bad for the ungodly amount of food that we had ordered. Â And guess what we did once we finished eating? We paid the check and GOT THE EFF OUT. I'd have to reiterate that you could get the same stuff in St. Mark's, too, for the same price. Â Thus, my opinion of this place remains unchanged.
Simply amazing vegan cupcakes, and a very nice person behind the counter even though we walked in right at closing time. A bit of a hike from the subway stop, but definitely worth it.

Probably the worst service I've ever received at a restaurant. We had an 8pm reservation for 2, and since we were coming from Long Island, we budgeted extra time, ending up there at 7:15. The hostesses were fine with it and said that they would seat us at the next open table, and they would call my cell phone when that happened. We figured it made no sense to leave so we grabbed a couple of beers at the bar. After finishing our beers, loitering around for another 20 mins, and then realizing it was now close to 8:30 (half an hour past our reservation), I approached the hostess and asked what the deal was, and she had no clue who I was or what I was asking about, so I refreshed her memory. Then she says she has been trying to reach me (I had no missed call on my phone, which was in my hand the entire time-I also had her confirm my number before we waited, so its my assumption that she was now lying to save face) and MIRACULOUSLY at that moment a table opened up. Hm. Funny because I read someone else's review saying something very similar. Maybe management should look into what their employees up front do. The table we were seated as was small and annoyingly right in the entryway of the bathroom. Bad luck I guess, oh well. Our waitress came over and we tried to order two flights, which she didn't think to write down until we finished telling her what we wanted. Kind of annoyed at this point since we were waiting for such a long time. We got the Swag sampler, and that came out long before we got our beers. This was pretty awesome. The swag sampler for two people included ONE HALF of a deviled egg, ONE wing, three shrimp (how generous) and a slice of a fried green tomato. Is this a joke? Am I being pranked? This is ridiculous for two people to share. Kinda fed up at this point and I want to leave, but we stayed because we finally (after 20 mins) got our drinks, and this is probably the only thing this place has going for them. Great beer selection, I even discovered a few new ones that I really like. So that was cool. Then we got our BBQ plate thingy. I ordered the Brisket, which was a-ice cold when I got it. Ok. and b-the fattiest cut of meat I've ever eaten in my life. ew. My fiance got the pulled pork sandwich. He really liked the BBQ sauce, and he says it tasted about what you'd expect from this type of place. The ribs were decent. Not the best, but not awful. We decided not to stick around for dessert, since it would probably take another hour to arrive. Overall, I'd say that this place essentially sucks ass. Service is garbage. The people working there all have a serious attitude (except for the one flamboyantly gay dude, he was pretty rad. I'd party with him.) and all think their shit doesn't stink. Their food is good if you were born and raised in the city, and never had good BBQ in your life.... just saying.
impressive food they have.

I love Cuban food; my dad, who spends a considerable amount of time in Florida, told me that a restaurant he loved down there had locations in New York, and wanted to know if we should go. What kind of question is that? We got over to Cabana last week, and we (including Girlfriend, who came along) weren't disappointed. Cabana is laid out in the uniformly upscale-NY way: low lighting, close seating, and a railroad-ish table layout. Cabana definitely has its own style, though; the decor is focused on warm colors, its louder than other restaurants, and had Latin music playing, all coming together to create an excellent weekend-night date experience (except for my father...). We were told not to make a reservation and, in spite of the crowded restaurant, were able to get a seat in about 15 minutes. After we sat down and ordered drinks (Presidente beers) our waitress began listing a huge selection of special items for the night. My father and I couldn't be distracted, though - we were here for the steak. To start, the table ordered fried calamari and fried plantains with a garlic sauce that was pretty much just chopped garlic and oil. I love garlic, so I was ecstatic, but it could be overwhelming if you're not a fan. The calamari came with a chipotle mayo dip (delicious) and a, if I'm not mistaken, teriyaki sauce, which caught me off guard. I'm still mixed on the latter. Churrasco steaks were the obvious choice for the main course, and we wouldn't have even needed the menu if Girlfriend wasn't in a steak mood. Churrasco steaks, for those unfamiliar, are flat, tender, heavily marinated in spices and [usually] lime juice. The churrasco at Cabana, was excellent, a top contender for best I've ever had, and cooked perfectly. The steaks were accompanied by yellow rice (good, standard, cone shaped) and black beans (great meaty flavor). Girlfriend got the shrimp in white wine garlic sauce which she very much enjoyed, but I can't speak to its taste (others may know: I'm allergic to shellfish. Yes, she did indeed mix our leftovers together :/). Just a note: the two appetizers and the entrees were definitely too much food for three people, so I'd downsize if I were you. After the meal, just as I was saying how I had no desire to touch any more food, the chef, who had come over to our table earlier, sent out chocolate flan (to all of us, not one for the table). I could say I love when chefs do this, but it rarely happens to me, and who doesn't? Yea, we all pretty much finished our flan. I had a great time at Cabana and, for the venue, the price didn't come out to be insane. If you like Cuban or Spanish food in general, and are looking for something a bit more than street food, Cabana is my top suggestion.

I love this place and the old school vibe it has. The same gentlemen have been working this place since I can remember and they are always really polite and welcoming. They have an awesome cuban sandwich, which is what I end up getting for the most part. I've also had the Ropa Vieja and it is delish! I definitely think it's worth a try.
Amazing food, even better service. Every time.
The Bah Kut Teh here is as good as my mom makes it back in Singapore. 5 out of 5!
Delicious, friendly, quick, cheap. Â Great merguez, okay lamb, amazing pita. Â Solid 4 stars.

This was one of the first places I fell in love with in New York. I consider french fries one of my essential food groups so when I came here, wow. First of all the french fries are fresh, made from peeled potatoes in the back room. Then there are copious amounts of sauces you dip your fries into. Some of my favorites are pesto mayo and horseradish mayo. Do not come here if you're at all full, come on a very empty stomach and whatever you do, DONT GET THE LARGE! The small is sufficent enough. You'll need to take a long walk afterwards for sure. Only downside: the limited seating inside.
Not much of a selection and the sushi was not that great.

We came here for a friends birthday brunch, mainly because they are one of few places you can reserve a table for 12 at 11am. The food was tasty, good for sharing and big groups. The only set-back was that they don't offer any non-dairy milk substitutes (which is particularly odd given BK is probably the home of Almond Milk in America). I recall perhaps one vegan friendly meal also.

I visited good ol' Ippudo Roppongi back when I was in Japan with my girlfriend. I read from CHOWHOUND that this was one of the best ramen places to visit, so after like an hour of hunting we were super famished and ready to eat. It turned out to be one of my favorite ramen experiences in Tokyo, (2nd only to Ramen Jiro Mita Honten) relatively inexpensive, and my favorite ramen using a tonkotsu broth. I took a business card which gave me the location of its New York location! Ballin'! Fast forward almost two months later, I decide to give the New York branch a shot. I've been informed by a friend of mine that the place usually had a long wait, with plenty of people standing outside waiting for nice bowl of ramen. Luckily, going in on Thursday at 5 pm me and my friend did not have that problem. We were seated immediately amongst a bunch of American waiters trained to greet us like they do in Japan, which was a nice touch if I do say so myself. Aside from that, the next thing I noticed was that the entire restaurant was pitch dark, which wasn't to my liking. Down to the nitty gritty, the food. At Ippudo, they're known for their delicious "Akamaru Modern," so I decided to give this one a shot to see how it's like here. A single bowl goes for about $14, which is like 1.5 times the price in Japan--a large blow for a destitute college student like myself. But I digress. The bowl arrived promptly (We're talking like 5 minutes) and I started chowing down. The verdict? For the most part, the broth tastes almost exactly the same as the bowl I had over at Roppongi, (Which is a good thing!) a rich, full taste... unlike any other ramen you could find in NYC. I totally recommend it for any NYC foodies. If you're a Japanese national, it'll be like a slice of home. For the rest of us Americans, it's a taste of an awesome foreign food culture, based on years upon years of refinement and technique... all boiled down into a simple bowl. It'll be the best ramen you ever spent $14 on in NYC, I assure you.

The lunch special is a good price and the food is pretty good but omg the service is soooooooo slow. There's only one waitress for the lunch shift and the poor woman is all over the place. She's also not the most attentive for being the only person on the floor, which is thoroughly annoying. I know things are slow here in LIC Â but c'mon, they really need to sort out their lunch time schedule a bit better. Or get a better multitasking waitress.

OK Pasquale your pizza is better than # 6 and you could make a case for #1! Love this place !!!!! Octopus with rocket, Amerone on sale, and possibly the best pizza in the city, noisy and fun and frozen lemonchella for desert, on the house; thanks Pasquale.

Small yet adorable restaurant. Romantic spot. Service was great. Prices are reasonable. We came as a huge party, 10 of us (all pairs, how romantic), so obviously there was a wait. That's quite all right, onto the bar next door! The hostess offered to come get us when the table was ready, how nice. Everyone loved their dishes. I had the ravioli and it certainly was delightful. The gnocci was delicious as well. Generous portions. Best quintuple date ever! I'd definitely visit Bianca again.

This place has a great ambience/atmosphere and great service. Â The drinks are really delicious too. Â I would recommend it for happy hour after work or a gathering with friends. Â It's definitely one of the better bars I've been to in NYC.
I think best korean food so far, If you guys are in a group. def. try hot pot. It will blow your mind away

Came here for our monthly friends dinner get together. Note they do take reservations of 5 or more but all people have to be present to be seated. They are kind of strict on this and you have to call them to confirm day of as well. It's a small place but service was very good. Items ordered. Cheese Fondue, didn't stand out and not too many dipping items just apples, bread, bread sticks, and potato wedges with bacon. Definitely could of had more items for the fondue. I'd skip it. The fried oysters is a must have crisp, not soggy and had a great veggie sauce underneath. Bone Marrow is probably the item to get and comes with all the fixins. A great onion marmalade, sea salt, brioche bread and huge bones filled with marrow. Mains. Fried Chicken wasn't a standout and to me the honey over flavored everything. The catfish and sea bass were the items to get. Also the sides of collards was a must have.

Definitely a nice, chill wine bar. I prefer Cali wines myself, but all of the Italian, French and Spanish wines I had were very good. They have great wine bar food! That is, the foods you crave with wine. Their cheeses are creamy fresh and sublime. Their smoked meats and pate are high quality. They have a no-nonsense kitchen in the front in full view, so you can get a feel for the freshness of everything served. There is a small area in the back with sofas that you can reserve for a group. The seating in front is a little tight, but the crowd is mellow, so it's not really uncomfortable. Good for dates, friends, or a group get-together. Jadis should not change a thing.

When the line is so long that staff members graciously hand out wine to those waiting, you know the idea of family dining just got real. Greek food to me is the perfect date night out. It has all the ingredients of quality seafood, spices, and gracious service wrapped into a pita of love that just might end the night oozing tzatziki sauce for one lucky lady. Delicious! Amazing pita and a fresh loaf of semolina soaked in olive oil and spices. While the majority of the food needs to be deboned (which you can ask the waiter to do of course), don't miss out on the pork and lamb options for a bit of land and sea (a nicer way of saying surf and turf). The greek salad is not to be skipped either as the amazing feta and tomatoes are a great predecessor to the tasty fish. Word to the adventurous: Get the octopus, it's great! Lemon, oil, and love never felt better. And if you need any more proof this place is hot: don't take a number, because they will take yours. Then 45 minutes later be prepared to return for the best meal before bed time you can get for your money's worth.

This place is okay. Â I was by myself so I only had to wait about 20 minutes for a seat at the bar. Â There are hooks under the bar, but they are awkwardly placed so no matter where I put my purse and coat, it was in someone else's way. Â I ordered the Miso Ramen with char siu pork, and shortly after I ordered, I was asked to shift one seat over to make room at the bar for a couple. Â That's totally fine, but then the cook tried to give my food to the guy who took my seat after I moved over! Â He didn't dig into it, so finally after some argument my dish was shifted over to me and I could dig in. Â I liked that the egg was medium-soft and not runny, as I've had at other ramen joints. ( Â Eavesdropped note: Â  I overheard a girl next to me ask if she could have her egg hard-cooked, and the waitress said no, there was no way to do that.) I can't speak to what's authentic, but I have been to a number of ramen joints in NYC and this place is not my favorite. Â The dish was tasty, but seemed lacking something special and umami (which was surprising to me since there was a whole scoop of miso in it). Â The pork slices were delicious, and everything about my food was good, but it wasn't the transcendent ramen experience I was looking for. Â It was also super-cramped and hot, I felt weird putting my coat on the low hook to get knocked around by my neighbor, and there were little bugs in the teensy bathroom. Â I know, it's New York, but if I have to wait 20 minutes to an hour to get in, I'd rather go to Ippudo. Â I'm glad I tried it, though.

I need to come here for brunch, because a weekday lunch was not mind-blowing as I thought it would be. =( The gnocchi was pretty good, but still not amazing-amazing. The french toast is actually very good, but I'm not much of a starch eater so after a couple of bites, I was finished. There was special of the day, which was some kind of fish with arugula (I can't even remember what it was, shows how un-amazing the dish was). The wait staff was really great though. I'd give them 5 stars alone for that alone. The entire place is quite large, and the bathroom is downstairs (don't go into the kitchen like I accidentally did. haha!)

My sister and I always come here when we are craving comfort food on a cold night. The food is hearty, tasty and very reasonably priced. Â Over the past visits, we've had keilbasa, chicken paprika, gulash, sauerbraten and bread dumplings. Nothing is terrifically inventive but it's classic and satisfying. The chicken paprika has a rich flavor and is falling off the bone. I'd be happy to have the gulash and sauerbraten again, and the keilbasa had a nice crisp skin. The bread dumplings with mushroom fricassee was bland and definitely not something I will have again. I also did not love the cheese and charcuterie plate but I am not a big fan of pate. The ambience is retro and casual, if a tad noisy, with vintage German posters and dark woods. I find the service can be inattentive and they are not so busy that it's justified. I have honestly been tempted to order 2 beers at once since I don't know when I'm going to get another. Â I find this particularly annoying since the German beer selection is not large but it is high quality, and one of the primary attractions.
Great food in a relaxed environment. We tried multiple appetizers and four different main dishes. They were of consistently great quality.

Ramen has become such a big trend in NYC. There are literally a ramen house in very corner in Manhattan. Ippudo happens to be one of the better know ramen place in the city. I've heard all the raves, and I couldn't wait to try it. My friend (who live in Chelsea) had never been here either. We came with some excitement, but left the place with slight disappointment. Although we only ordered ramen, it was the "best ramen ever," or "even great ramen." It was simply ok. The broth is definitely on the saltier side. I guess the it's really not about the food, it's about how they advertise themselves.

The quality of meat here is absolutely incredible, and the preparation is the best I've had since living in Texas. I particularly recommend the pork done ANY way. I had both spicy pulled pork sliders and roast pig. Both were delicious. On top of all this, the staff is amazing. They bent over backwards to put an unbeatable meal together, all with big smiles on their faces. The savory food and wonderful service will definitely have me coming back for more!
Absolutely love it!! We will head back again for the food, service and reasonable prices!!

Pio Pio Restaurant, 10th Ave,, NYC - On Dec. 20th, a small Xmas lunch of 5 was a fiasco. Â Poor service of Â 45 minutes for 1st course, a late service of more than 1.5 hours for lunch course. Management did not surface to address service issues, left waiter to suffer blame alone. Â Others who arrived at tables after our party were served first. Â When our table was FINALLY served, minus my entree - I was offerred another appetizer! Â They are clueless. Â  Avoid at all cost, unless you are desperate for mediocre food, i.e. Â IPeruvian cuisine - Â chicken, beef and rice with Velveeta cheese, con't waste your money. Â  This is an insult . Â I've seen more appetizing dog food.

My husband and I went here for his birthday and had the tasting menu in January 2013. The food was gorgeously presented and very tasty. Check out some of the photos I took on my blog, bigfoodsmallkitchen: bigfoodsmallkitchenblog.â€¦
It's literally the best taco spot I've ever tasted, I've eaten here a dozen times, the service is great. The street corn omg Awesome. Â Must try
Not too healthy, but tasty vegan food. I love their coconut water :) Bigger bottle is mine Clean location, but no restroom. Nice place, not many vegan places in FInancial District at all!

Dinner at Zutto was extremely tasty! I went on a Friday night around 6:30 and was quickly seated. It wasn't too crowded which was nice and our waitress was very nice. They have a great Happy Hour Menu with drink specials so we ordered the ginger wings (which were good; 5 were not enough!). We were surprised by the portion of fried rice because it was large appetizer portion and that too was good. For the entrees, we got the sushi and the parm ramen which were both really good!

Arrived with a reservation through Groupon Reserve that was supposed to give us a 20% discount. The manager refused to honor it. Wouldn't even comp a drink from bill to make up for the confusion. That was the first and last time I go to this place. Â It was a bait and switch in my opinion. The restaurant has followed up with me after I left this short yelp review (above unchanged) via phone and the comment below. Â I am curious as to how the owner was able to track down my telephone number if they had no record of our reservation. Â I am also curious about why the owner didn't mention the 'treat' he planned forus because we had already explained to the waitress that we were in a rush to make a show. Â I also agree that it is a sad state of affairs when social media is the only way to hold someone accountable for bad business and customer service.

Order delivery from here often and it's a winner in my book. Â I particularly like that the lamb gyro is real lamb and often has a few crusty bits thrown in... yum! Â Delivery is usually really quick too. Never been inside the restaurant so can't comment on that aspect.

Had dinner here with some friends. Great food, very romantic ambiance and lastly, very affordable! You can't get any better than this in the Village. Service is great as well. We ordered several pastas and pizzas and they were all great. I don't think you can go wrong in this place.

I have been to Nook twice in the past year. The food is AMAZING! The place is a really cute inside. Nice and cozy. I have to recommend the mushroom cigars as an app. One of the great things is that is is BYOB. There is a wine store around the corner on 8th ave. My only qualm about the place was that the waiter was kind of rude. He was really snotty when we were inquiring about the menu while ordering. He also seemed to want to rush us out. That aside the food is great! I cannot wait to try their brunch!

Came here on my last trip to New York and was recommended to Lombardi's. The pizza was great, try their famous white pizza and red with sausage. They were able to accommodate us right away for a table for two. Thank you! Cash only.

The hour wait is so worth it. Â This is my second time here and between Â the Banana Walnut pancakes and the Southern breakfast I fell in love. Even the orange juice, which is made in-house is amazing.

This place is named after an apple, not anything having to do with espionage (or so they want you to think). My friend recommended this place as it was nearby and offered some fresh, locally-produced food. The atmosphere is intimate, with wooden fixtures and low lighting. We shared a snack of mixed, spiced nuts which were fabulous. I ordered the Chicken and Egg Sandwich, which was a helping of dark meat chicken and a poached egg on a thick bread (something ciabatta-like). The egg seemed more fried than poached, but the chicken was tender and flavorful. Thinking about it now, it's a little weird to eat chicken and egg together, maybe. Some metaphor for the circle of life or something. And so it goes. Dessert was apple pie a la mode and some pumpkin mousse. The apple pie was fresh and warm, the mousse a little bland.

Until tonight, I had no idea this place was here, and I live like two streets away. I kind of thought the entire space had just shut down after Regina Bakery closed. Tonight my parents and I decided to try it after we'd gotten back from Manhattan and didn't want to travel too much further for dinner. P'tit Paris is definitely apropos- there's only a little bit of Paris to be found in this place. (And to a previous reviewer, yes, "p'tit" is a correct usage, it's the French equivalent of saying "li'l" instead of "little.") It wasn't crowded at all, but that could have been due to the lateness of the hour (it was almost ten) or hell, just the fact that Windsor Terrace is still kind of a wasteland. Our waiter was very friendly, although not entirely too thorough (I overheard another waiter telling someone else the specials later and I was like, "Hey, OUR guy didn't tell us about the pumpkin soup..."). We all ended up having the hanger steak. And you know, it was quite good. I like mine medium-well, and it cut really nicely, even with me forgetting I was given a steak knife until I was like a quarter of the way through it. It came with a handful of greens that had a really good mustard-y vinaigrette on them, and a ton of fries, which I wasn't as crazy about. (Particularly because they put ketchup down for the fries. If you actually go to Paris, there is no ketchup to be found anywhere. I'm just saying. I ended up soaking my fries in steak juice and eating them with my fork. Don't hate.) Even though the whole portion was really modestly sized, all of us were full afterwards. I was a *little* curious about dessert, but I hate eating dessert when no one else is like I'm seven, so I passed. Next time. However, when the waiter (a different waiter than the one who'd initially been serving us- like I said, not entirely too thorough) brought us our check, he also mentioned that there was "no such thing as no dessert," and brought out some homemade chocolate- which was freaking great. Very, very rich, and covered in powdered cocoa, but definitely dessert enough. All in all, I was pleasantly surprised- a nice restaurant, like an actual nice restaurant, in Windsor Terrace. Huh.
Came here Friday and Sunday. Â Think I found another good authentic Vietnamese restaurant. Â Still have to go back to try different dishes. Â Service is also good and fast.

I wish I lived closer to this place! I went for dinner last weekend on a deal and had a blast. They have a delicious & affordable wine selection and the best seafood around. I had the fish and chips (was feeling comfort food) and it didn't disappoint. My friend had a whole fish, which was moutwatering good. Add in some oysters, and it was one of the best meals I've had in a while. Â I'd definitely recommend Wild Edibles to fish eating friends on the East Side but warn them that the space is small!

Well, if you want half of your order forgotten and then your white rice coming out with a helping of dead fruit flies in it, by all means this is the place for you. When my girlfriend and I walked in, she was hesitant because of its B health rating. We passed it off as "just another Chinatown place", but soon realized that it actually deserved a worse grade. We won't be coming back.

The other day I rode on a chairlift out West with a guy from Scotland, and it was just fun listening to the old bugger talk. No matter what a Scot says, with that accent it sounds so elegant and charming. His description of Lagavulin 12 years as "earthy" and "smooth" made it sound like we were discussing the world economy rather than our favorite single malt scotches. On the flight back from Colorado, I read about a gastropub -- I honestly hate that term -- in the west village specializing in scotch. The place was called Highlands, and I immediately made a mental that I had to go. And soon. Last weekend I met my friend G at Highlands for a couple of drinks. G is from Delhi and only recently discovered the magic of scotch, so we sat at the bar and sampled a few of the 100 or so blends on the menu. She liked it sweet, I liked it smokey. (And that's what makes the world go around, la la la la la....) The vibe at Highlands is very cool -- very woodsy and cosy along with a deer head on the wall -- although we only stuck around for some pre-dinner drinks due to the fact that there weren't many non-meat items on the menu for my friend. Still we both loved Highlands and agreed we'd be back to sample some more scotch another time. Now, if only I had that accent...

Really seriously delicious Grandma pizza. Â When we have to stay late at work on a deadline, the team will split a pie and I'm ready to keep working til the wee hours. It's lovely to go with a group and sit outside on Stone Street as well. Â FYI-They do not do slices so be prepared to have pizza for a few days (which I would totally consider doing if I was better at eating the same thing in a row, that could be lunch and dinner for two full days at $20 total). Â  I would recommend the pepperoni or the classic. Â My biggest complaint is that they carry Pepsi products. Â Who does that? Â With pizza I either need a beer or a soda and since I rarely drink soda it should be a treat-but Diet Pepsi is just not my cup of tea. Â The goodness of the pizza keeps me coming back.

My large group had a great time here but the food was inconsistent. Â Come for the sangria, stay awhile because the atmosphere is festive, and don't be upset when your food is just mediocre. Â You can't have it all. Â At least not at Calle Ocho.

This is the chill living/entertainment room of the Village that you go to after dinner in the dining room. Â Hopefully, that analogy makes sense to the Manhattanites living in a space greater than a jail cell. Â  Starting with the ambiance, as soon as you walk through the always-crowded front shop, you enter a different world - a garden that is in bloom year round, as is the wine list. Â Italian Moscato, bottled in Italy, as opposed to somewhere in North Jersey, is my favorite. Served chilled, in a personal-sized 350 ml bottle, it complements any dessert on the menu. Â  The desserts are your basic selection - cheesecakes, chocolate concoctions like the flourless chocolate cake, and the seasonal pies. Â It's nothing to die for, but they do such a good job with the ambience and the wine selection, that I could be snacking on cheesecake I picked up from Trader Joe's and still enjoy this place. Â  During the rush, the service can get a little flaky, but that's because of you bastards reading these reviews and taking your friends here. Â  Great place. Â If there is seating room, this is a great stop.
Great environment, food was delicious, music was on point and so was the music. I definitely recommend the spot and will be there soon.

Was intrigued by the idea of vegetarian sushi and have been meaning to try this place for a long time. Finally decided to get delivery tonight and am quite happy with my experience. I ordered the Verde Salad, black bean sweet potato brownie and carrot side salad (just to meet the $15 delivery minimum - which on seamless is actually $18 total min, kinda steep) I got a call less than 5 minutes later saying the black bean brownies were sold out, so I decided to get black sesame chia pudding instead. Happy with the promptness of the call and the employee on the other line was friendly and helpful. my order arrived within the delivery limit specified (a little over 30 minutes) Â  The salad and carrot side salad were both much bigger than I expected, so I saved half for another meal. The black sesame chia seed pudding is really tasty. overall, definitely a good option for when you want something fresh and healthy that won't weigh you down (which is necessary when trying to stay awake, studying for finals) I can see myself ordering from here again

Amazing!!! Ordered combo A (crawfish and shrimp) in the spicy boil sauce...so good! Next time, I'll get only shrimp. Don't get me wrong, the crawfish was great, but the shrimp is more meaty so I prefer that. ***edit*** Returned a second time for just the shrimp. It was just as delicious as before; the only issue is that it made me really sick (flaming hot diarrhea type of sick). I wasn't feeling well the first time, but I didn't want to assume it was the delicious meal I just had. I guess it was =(

I really liked this place. it was fun to sit out on the patio. My friend recommended the chicken biscuit, and it was well worth it. the spicy sauce on the chicken blended in with the honey butter from the biscuits. I also got the mac and cheese. it was all really good. I would have come here more often if i would have known about it. we got off the L train on bedford. But it is easier to take the JMZ from Marcy Avenue. The price of the food was really cheap for NY/Brooklyn.

negative reviewers need to stfu the bbq here is awesome , better than any i've had in texas even. i LOVE the sauces, i mix the spicy w/ the reg & usually get the brisket : ) ps: if you don't want to wait forever just go on a monday or tuesday evening.. duh. of course it's gonna be busy & hard to find a seat on the weekend.

Great place, my new go to spot in the neighborhood. Â Great cocktail menu, extremely fresh seafood (love the oysters), and surprisingly for a seafood spot, they have an amazing burger. Â My favorite burger so far in greenpoint, beats out the river styx burger hands down! Also to top off the great food, love the decor, makes you feel like you're on an old sailboat.

Food & Service were wonderful! Would almost give 5 stars but we did not like the pretzel--tasted like your average pretzel and the cheese sauce was too salty along with a too salty pretzel. However the shrimp & grits and fried chicken were amazing. Â We also got the boston cream pie---omg amazing! We also got the grilled corn with cotija and corn nuts--yum! Would have loved some more spice though. would definitely return despite all the choices in NYC.

The cabbage. No one ever talks about cabbage, why would they? But seriously the cabbage served with boar belly bacon and scallion purÃ©e made my night. The wine list is interesting (all organic & additive free). I found the staff to be knowledgeable and super friendly. Really cool spot for a night of epicurean delights. Also they aren't cash only anymore! Go eat there now.

Perry Street was a very pleasant dining experience. The ambiance was "interesting" at best. Â It looked like a 1950s leftover, which went along with the waitstaff's thin black tie and white shirt look, which screamed John Foster Dulles. Â The tables were a tad close, but there was no problem with being too familiar with your neighbours. Â  The service was friendly and pleasant. The food was excellent. Â As a starter, we had a crispy (fried) calamari appetizer with a "yuzu sauce." Â The fried element of the calamari was delightfully light, although I didn't think the sauce was particularly good (and didn't really compliment the calamari). Â However, I would definitely order the pea soup next time as a starter. Â The main course was far better... both the braised short-ribs and the arctic char were divine. Â  The most important thing to remember when eating meals at Perry St. is that the combination of food is better than the sum of its parts. Â For example, the char alone tasted like a light salmon, with a passion fruit compote on the side and olives on top. Â However, when mixed together, the combination of flavors was unexpectedly delicious. Â We found the same thing with the short ribs (with asian pears and herbs). Â So... don't "compartmentalize" your meal, but instead mix it up and let the individual flavors compliment one another with explosive taste. The desserts were also wonderful. Â The chocolate pudding was decadently delicious. The bill was likewise surprisingly reasonable. Â Although I don't profess to suggest that ~$130 is cheap, for 2 people, 3 courses, and drinks, its not as bad as it could have been, particularly since Perry St. was awarded a Michelin star this year. I would recommend dinner here as a hip/trendy date place with some very good food. Â Not for the everyday diner, but well worth the visit. I don't know what the limitations (if any) there are for the $35 prix fixe menu (before 6:30) but if most of you options are available, this would be a great deal.

BEA is like a quaint and more affordable version of Isola Trattoria at the Mondrian. Â I think it's ideal for small dishes and drinks for a nice catch up session with some friends you haven't seen in a while and that's exactly what I came here for (run-on sentence much?). Â It was the perfect escape from the hustle and bustle of NY, especially during this time of the year. I ordered the pulled pork and it was surprisingly really good! Â Don't expect it to knock your socks off, but it was still tasty enough to make my eyes grow bigger after my first bite. Â As for my drink of the night, I had the Lavender Monk, which was sweet and strong - just the way I like it. Â As previous reviewers mentioned, the interior is romantic with soundless old movies projected on a brick wall. Â Service was great, as well. Â I know there are a million restaurants to try in Manhattan, but BEA is a restaurant that doesn't sacrifice the quality of food while providing an intimate atmosphere and THAT, my friends, is rare.

In addition to the requisite Big Buck Hunter, The Levee will also provide you with a selection of your favorite childhood board games to rediscover while enjoying their $4 or less non-happy hour beer options, (Yuengling), and beer and shot deals. Should your drink tastes be a bit more evolved, never fear, there is a good selection of beer on draft and in bottles, and you can count on wider array of whiskey to choose from than your average Billyburg hole. If you are so ambitious to stand up and move around while engaging in your competitive activity of choice, darts and billiards are also options, and it's dark enough in the bar to make it just short of impossible to see who wins. Downsides: the bar that extends to the back room is not so much a bar as a stand in for a bar, (I have never had any luck ordering from there), and the front counter can become a bit of a clusterfuck, being right next to the only entrance, the bathroom line, and the jute box. Otherwise, this is a solid stop on your plaid-core mustache crawl.

I left a tip a while back regarding my preference for receiving my appetizer before my entree (not at the same time), and I hear that this issue has been corrected at Station House. Â Here here! This is a cool place to drop in "for one" after work, or to come with a bunch of friends to catch "the local sports team." The staff is friendly and the chef(s) is/are creative. Â I also love the big ice cube (not cubes!) in the whiskey/scotch: nice touch! I'll definitely be back.

Found out about this place through a NY Times article, which should have mentioned that they are closed on Mondays (actually they might have). Honestly, very surprising to see a NY Times article about a small place like this so I had to try it out as I love Thai food. This place is awesome! I got 3 entrees and white rice for $7.50 plus tax and the Thai Iced Tea is only $2 (a little too much ice). The entree that stood out to me was the pork belly. It's a short hike from the train station, but after my first trip it was a lot closer than I remembered earlier. Just make sure to bring cash and you're good!
The environment is really nice and shows their great efforts to be authentic. The food here are fine for that price, not impressive but not bad. Love love the drink here: yuzusu - strongly recommend.

Their chicken sandwiches are my go to. I think I could eat it everyday if I could, without getting fat. I tried the bbq pork one but I recommend the chicken one if you're a chicken eater. I also tried the original vietnamese sandwich which was not so bad but it's not my favorites. The bread is just the way I like it, super crunchy! This place has one of the best chicken vietnamese sandwiches that I have tried and loved!

As with many NYC places we tried, Trecolori is very gluten-aware. Â They have GF pastas, know about food cross-contamination, and, according to our waiter, may even start making their GF pasts in-house soon (as with many respectable Italian restaurants on the East Coast, all their other pasta is made in-house). We went for lunch, and found the decor is simple, the atmosphere relaxed and quiet, the service attentive, and the food non-offensive and with plentiful portions. Â The red wine pairing with my particular dish (a venison goulash on GF linguini) greatly improved my meal. Â More on all of this below.... But the best aspect of our dining experience at Trecolori was our waiter, MJ. Â He was hilarious. Â Here is an example of a typical exchange: Me: "So I was thinking about maybe the LINGUINE alla VONGOLLE, or maybe ---" MJ: "No no. Â You should try the venison special. Â Very tasty. Â You can get the Vongolle anytime...why not try some venison while you can? Â How often do you have venison?" MJ didn't know that I have venison more regularly than one might think, but he seemed so confident, I let him lead me down the garden path. Â So I said: Â "Okay, I'll try it. Â And perhaps a Malbec with that ---" MJ: Â "No no. Â We have a wonderful red, our own Cabernet/Zinfandel (cuvÃ©e). Â You should try that." Me: Â "How is it? Â Is the Zin really tart?" MJ: Â "Don't worry. Â I'll take care of you. Â You'll like it." And that's pretty much how our ordering went for both my wife and I for the rest of the meal. Â MJ answered our questions, explained things patiently ("Let me tell you how this works...you get endless free olives - fresh from Italy - if you order a drink. Â If you don't order a drink, they cost $2.50...") Now...about the food. Â As I mentioned my wine really made my meal, and my wife had a similar experience. Â But the meal itself, although clearly prepared with care, wasn't all that interesting in taste, texture or presentation. Â I thought my venison goulash could have benefited from thyme, garlic or other seasoning to give it some "pop," but as it was I could only describe it as a bit plain. Â In terms of presentation it was heaped plentifully on my plate, but that was really how it looked (i.e. heaped), without garnish or arrangement. Â For the price, I think I would have preferred a little more flavor and a little more creativity. Â Perhaps the best part of the meal were those olives...they were indeed fresh, and excellent. However, with all this said, we will probably give Trecolori another try when we are Â in NYC again...especially if MJ is there to entertain us.
This place is great. Â Really actually awesome, Â Really good brunch, very nice people and adorable decor. Love the food! Â I always take people visiting from out of town here. Â Super cute!!!

After desperately wandering West Village on a Friday night with no dinner reservations, we stumbled into Barbuto and were pleasantly greeted with a 15-minute wait. The restaurant is way off to the side on Washington St, and has a grungy / upscale feel due to its huge garage door windows and concrete floors. This place is known for their roast chicken, which counts Daniel Boulud among its many fans. It's a simple roast chicken but really intensely flavored with some sort of seasoning... Portions are generous and my dinner companion essentially split this dish with me. Definitely a cozy dish appropriate for dropping temperatures. Was it worth it? It's hard to assess objectively when ANYTHING as touted as "The Best 'Insert Item Here' Ever", but considering that chicken is usually the disfavored option on most dinner menus, I think Barbuto does a good job of skyrocketing it to a headliner position.

Amazing Sushi, the freshest sashimi i have had in NY, amazing staff, incredible owner...i come here almost every single night - to work and have an amazing dinner. Â Zest Â has the best Happy hour I have ever been to at any restaurant. Truly a gem of a place that makes me sad to ever leave New York. Â Lily, Jimmy, John - you guys have made my entire experience of New York unforgettable. Â There are so few restaurants today where the owner becomes friends with all his patrons. Â Here is to hoping you open many more Zests where friends can share wonderful memories with you guys, much love, Anneli

Came here with the lady and a friend on a Saturday night for dinner. Getting in: - No reservations, walk in only - Called ahead to see if it was possible to get in. Â Mentioned what time I was shooting for and they said to stop by 30mins early. Â We did, put our name on list and went and had a drink at Uva around the corner - You get a call when your table is a few minutes from being ready Atmosphere: - Small restaurant that is fun and intimate. Â We sat at the bar which was nice Service: - Heidi served us herself. Â She was great and friendly. Â Very inviting. Food: - Fish Tacos: These were good. Â  - Paella: This was great. Â Very generous with the seafood. Â Well worth the money. Â I really enjoyed this - Mac & Cheese: Lady got this. It was very good and very heavy. Â You will need to hit the gym after this one. Â Get it with the bacon - Pasta of the day: Our friend got the mushroom pasta of the day. It was very tasty Drinks: - I stuck to beer. They have a pretty nice selection of American crafts, Belgians and UK + cider Other: - They have board games and puzzles, if that's your thing - Didn't like all the dried roses hanging upside down in the bathroom, but bathroom was clean and nice with cloth towels Overall we really enjoyed our night here. Â Had no idea a little gem like this was in the neighborhood. Â Next time we are feeling lazy and don't want to go downtown, we will stop by here.

I've spent the better part of two years being extremely envious of my friends' brunch dates at Calle Ocho... I finally make a reservation and it ends up being one of the worst meals I've had in New York City. Friends and I arrived at 12PM and were seated immediately--service started out very friendly and attentive. We got our bread basket quickly, a great variety of warm rolls with a berry flavored butter which ended up being the highlight of my experience. We ordered a selection of sangrias, most of which were quite tasty, then it was all downhill from there. I ordered the shrimp and bacon grits dish that came with two poached eggs drenched in an oily chipotle hollandaise sauce. This by far was one of the most off-putting dishes I've ever consumed a single bite of. If you read through any of my previous reviews you'd learn that I've never once left my food unloved but this was a special situation. The aroma coming off the plate was something like weird, spicy hot dogs. The shrimp and bacon seemed of a mediocre quality and the flavor of the dish was very obscure and really spicy. To add insult to food injury, the eggs had a bizarre, chewy texture on their exterior that made them inedible. I decided to abandon it altogether for the side of home fries I ordered which I then realized arrived freezing cold. I thought maybe that's how they were prepared but a few at the bottom of the dish were luke warm. My friends ordered the steak dish as well their classic benedict offering and both felt that it was passable but not enjoyable. The sausage under the poached eggs was overcooked as was the steak. Their Latin rice was okay but had a bit too much smoke for my personal taste. If I regret anything it's not selecting the salmon eggs in a corn crepe that passed us by several times and looked delectable. By the end of our meal it was impossible to get the check, even after it took us 20 minutes to flag down the waiter. I know that this place has tons of reviews saying otherwise but my point is DON'T come for the food. Sangria is fantastic... All I can hope is that I saved one person from smelling spicy, stinky hot dogs.
Very good ramen. Be prepared to wait in line. Dishes on the salty side.

It was a Wednesday night. I got to the restaurant first, so I put Â my name down and was told the wait would only be half an hour. I then went to the lounge while waiting for my friends to arrive. As soon as my friends arrived, I went to the hostess to let her know that we were all there as I was instructed earlier. She told me I should close my tab at the bar as it would just be a few minutes. My friends decided that they would wait to order their drinks at the table since we would be seated soon. We closed our tab, waited and waited. My friends were starving coming from work, so one of them went up to the hostess to check on our table status. Apparently the people at the table were taking their time even though they already paid. Fine, I understand. So we kept waiting, very patiently. Probably another 15 minutes went by, we were finally seated, in this area which probably had about 40 empty tables!!!! We were not happy. That area was sectioned off when I first got to the restaurant, and no one was sitting there. An hour later when we were seated, there were maybe one other party sitting in that section already. We were very confused. I'm not sure what the point was to make us wait an hour (while we were only told the wait would be 30 minutes) and there were all these empty tables. And if you decided to open up that section, why in the world couldn't you seat us earlier since there were so many empty tables????? What the heck Public? That was not cool.

How can you go to NYC and not have the Halal guys? Always one of my recommendations to anyone on their visit. Drunk or sober, this place is always great. I love that they're always consistent and that they're open late. I always end up catching a cab from the bars in Lower East Side just to get some before I end the night. I hear the line is ridiculous, but I haven't been there anytime before midnight!

THIS PLACE HAS THE BEST PEKING DUCK KALILA AND I HAVE EVERRRRRR TASTED!!!!!!!!!!!!!! my whole review would be complete if I just said: GET THE DUCK... but that's not really Elite behavior, now is it? But really though...... GET THE DUCK. It was so good. It was so tasty. I can't even describe it anymore... all I remembered was that I couldn't stop eating. I will now be comparing all the other duck I eat to this place. We also that the pan fried noodles and they were really good. Pretty much the same traditional pan fried noodles you can get anywhere else in chinatown. The salt and pepper pork chops & rice was good too. This place was absolutely crowded when we went, but luckily we did not have to wait that long for a table for 4. The service was fast and we never had to continue asking for things. They got our order right the first time. MUST TRY!!!

Came here for lunch and really enjoyed the food here. Â It was tasty and seemed really authentic and homemade! Â The restaurant itself is pretty small so it probably gets packed at night. What we got: Grapefruit Marguerita - a bit small but tasted very fresh Guacamole and chips - pretty good and chunky Tacos pescado - very good; fish was perfectly cooked Tacos al pastor - very good; one of my husband's favorites since he really enjoyed the pineapple/pork mixture Enchilada verde - delicious; chicken was a bit dry but the delicious mole/verde sauce made up for it Sopa de pollo - light but tasty broth but beware it's spicy! Service: Good service. Â We never felt rushed and they were very accommodating when they realized we were going to eat everything family style.

It was less than 24 hours ago that I reviewed a restaurant suggested by my roommate Elton; and between that, this post, and the other places I hear him talk about; I must say the man really knows his shit. Serious props to Elton. Anyway, we went as per his request for his birthday, and it was an amazing meal. As an enthusiast of Cuban Pete's in Montclair, NJ and all things Buena Vista Social Club / Ruben Gonzalez, personally I was thrilled to hear we were headed here. Perfect for a date or a large group (I think we were about ten), every aspect of our meal here was fantastic. The service was a little slow; but I think that just tends to be the case when you're such a large table. First off, when you walk in, it's like stepping out of Brooklyn and into Havana. (Okay, with a few of North Side's hipster eccentricities still here and there.) It's super loud in there and definitely boasts more of a party atmosphere, but sometimes I think that's almost better for a date because you have to talk that much closer. Perhaps it was just the particular live music that they had that night; very festive. It's always the best when you can watch and listen to an actual musician while you're dining. As great as the atmosphere was, the food and drink was even better. This is absolutely high-quality, gourmet cuisine. It's a given that the worse my photos are; the better the food must be, because it's that much less time I had to get the shot before a thousand hands start tearing the food to shreds, myself included. They've got tons of beer and wine; but their seasonal and standard cocktails are certainly the way to go, and pack quite a punch, making them very worth their price. The Smokey Menendez and the Dill Paloma are my favorite; el beit they contain whiskey and tequila, respectively, and Cubana Social is technically more of a rum place, given that it's a Cuban restaurant. Alas, the food. The one item I'm most excited to write about is the one thing I didn't quite manage to get a picture of. However, I thought everything was so absolutely delicious that I even included the menu below for your perusal. The great thing about going as such a large group is that you can order up a hundred and one different things; and that's exactly what we did. The duck confit empanadas (all of the empanadas really), are incredible. Everything we ordered tasted so fresh and really high quality in terms of ingredients; and that really does make all the difference. The best thing you can order, however, is the tostone tacos, which is a fish of the day (in our case, it was tuna in ceviche form), a slightly spicy cilantro aioli, and a heirloom tomato pico de gallo. Another catch of the day option is the ceviche, which they totally nailed. We must have ordered like 4 of them. The crispy avocado, while good everywhere and hard to mess up, was also really delicious. Their's was served with a guava habanero sauce, very similar to the way that it's served up at Ravi de Rossi's Cienfuegos. As for the mains; the ropa vieja was very well done; but I think myself and our friend Nick had the best entrees; we both ordered a very traditional lechon asado with lots of garlic and lime, rice and beans. It's hard to beat that kind of simple yet amazing hearty home-style meal. (PS - they also specialize in Cuban coffee.)
I had the worst $25 hamburger in my life. Â It was small and overdone. The bun was stale and tasteless. Â It's a great looking room and cool crowd but horrible food and only fair service.

do not frequent this restaurant! the front desk staff are obnoxious. the waiters are incompetent. if you ignore my advice, you will find the food is not bad, but the service will totally ruin your evening.

So I spent a week in NYC with my friends who lived in the area. They, being the tour guides for a West Coaster, were under considerable pressure to impress me of their hometown's good eats and show some East Coast pride. I'll be honest, three days in, I was starting to feel a little disappointed with the savory food choices in New York and started to just look forward to dessert time (Levain Bakery, New York cheesecake, rice pudding... New York knows what they're doing with sweets). I am pretty sure a part of my disappointment stemmed from my friends' perpetual foodie battle of "which coast is the best coast?" and being from the Los Angeles area, my heart lies firmly there. So... the scene is set up, I'm still looking for a dinner that defines NYC and heard that this was the place. I order my food and sit on the side of a street to begin my culinary adventure. WOW. I got the lamb/chicken combo plate and it was absolutely fantastic. All that hype and amazing Yelp reviews were totally on the dot. I can see why most of the other "famous food destinations" in NYC has 4 stars, yet this one remains a solid 4.5. The meat was cooked right in front of you and the meat was extremely flavorful. Despite the fact that I ate enough to last for two meals, I didn't feel heavy afterwards, as you do after you consume a greasy meal. I felt full, but satisfied. Plus, the whole experience of the food cart just defines what it's like to be a student in a big city. Anywho, I seriously considered going there one more time before I left NYC. Until next time.

This was second visit to Brooklyn crab , first visit was their first Week when they clearly did not have it together . Despite all the horrible reviews we decided to give it another try, tonight they were on their game. It was not crowded and we were seated upstairs with no wait. Perhaps enough people have been scared off so that the crowds are manageable. The steamed crab pots were good and more generous than the last visit. Service was friendly and efficient . I hope tonight wasn't just a fluke and they figured things out.
Great atmosphere. Great prices. Great experience.
Great seafood.. and one of the best Greek restaurants in NYC. There is usually a wait for dinner, but it is well worth it.
The food here is so freaking delicious. We came for Saturday brunch before hurricane Irene hit and left very full, happy campers. It's wonderful to see a neighborhood place expanding!

When I was too young to appreciate good beer or wine, my favorite thing about coming here was the view into the guy's apartment across the street. I came here on college dates to be around sexy and fake the funk through affected "mature" conversations. Since this is one of those rare places that doesn't change or disappoint through the years, I still come by when I'm in the neighborhood, now with more reliable company to enjoy the libations always gracefully recommended by the waitstaff. Â I usually forget to check on my old across-the-street entertainment.
Best brisket ever. Â  My husband's from Texas and he hasn't had brisket this good. Â  It's a little pricey but the experience is well worth it.

If you're in the mood for super fine French, the way I was when I recently went back to Balthazar after a couple of years hiatus, give this lovely and pricey bistro a chance to win your heart and you may find: That the old adage dessert should always be first is especially true when it's a caramelized banana and ricotta tart. My personal fa.vor.ite dish at Balthazar. Sweet, rich, intense flavor enveloping a subtly sweet custard. Could have three of these at a time. The lemon mousse is also divine but differently. Silky with a luscious raspberry sauce. That duck is a good thing. A great thing even, if you choose to have it with cheese and potatoes in a shepherd's pie. That probably any wine or champagne off of Balthazar's list is great to drink during and right after your meal. That the service of a perfectly fine (and I did say pricey) restaurant can vary from time to time. A cute, tall, and happy waiter one lunch and a waddling, pregnant and bitter server with a bad case of BRF the next. That a lot of background noise is somewhat forgettable when you have good food sitting in front of you. That Balthazar stays packed with tourists and New Yorkers simply because it has great food.

Carrying on our burger crawl in the city we chose B&B for this month's stop. Two of us tried the award winning Bash Burger which was mighty delish while the other had the double bacon pork burger. Tons of food as it comes with onion rings and fries (you can also get awesome rosemary tater tots instead). We share the rock shrimp fritters, the mac and cheese and the brussel sprouts with feta. Everything was really good and the service was great as well. My only comment was that it was pretty loud so don't count on intimate conversation!
Love this place. The veal meatballs are unbelievable. We come here every time we visit the city.

Meh, that's all I have to say. I came here on a friend's recommendation, but the prices that you pay for these, I don't really think it's worth it. The staff here are definitely incredibly attentive though, refilling your water even though you still have a good half a glass left, and checking in to see if everything's okay. We ordered the patatas bravas, the beef skewers, chicken empandas, and the tiger prawns (one of the specials of the night). Personally, I was most impressed with the beef skewers, they were cooked decently. Of course, I also tend to judge not just the quality, but also the amount of food that I'm getting for a price. $15 for a prawn (it was fresh alright), is a little outrageous to me, especially if it takes up just about the center of a small plate. Overally, yes I would agree it's a nice date spot if you are on a date. But to have a nice dinner with a friend, this would probably be a place to grab an appetizer before going out for a real entree. On the side note, I have also been to the Las Ramblas Street in Barcelona, Spain. The food here at this restaurant is a nice attempt, but nothing too impressive.

They only do ramen, but by george, do they do it well. Oh so so so well. Seriously, this would be 5 stars if the place was bigger so i could take more people to this wonderful little gem. The guy behind the counter was super friendly and nice. My dining partner had asked for extra noodles, and the guy said just let him know when he's ready so he would have fresh noodles. The guy was super friendly with all the patrons and the banter between the staff was pretty entertaining. Love the pork and love watching them 'brulee' it with the torch. The broth is unmatched in my opinion, as well as the rayu (spicy oil). Now, I love the spicy ramen, but the real difference between the spicy ramen and super spicy ramen isnt so much 'spicy' as it is 'peppery' as in 'black peppery'. The first time i went, my date had the super spicy, but it just tasted more like a ton of black pepper hit the bowl rather than more spiciness. In either case, the ramen is amazing. I also love that they have ramen for everyone. Dont do pork? hit up the chicken ramen. Dont do either? hello vegetarian ramen. Want toppings? well theres a whole side of the menu for you. The ramen is fantastic, the prices are great, staff is amazing. But be warned - CASH ONLY! so hit up the atm before you go!

Been here several times. Â Food always good. Brunch is very good but crowded. Â Unfortunately, the service is almost always quite poor and unattentive. They really need to improve the hiring and training

Came to chelsea market looking for something delicious eat and we ended up eating here because they were able to accomodate a large group of 8+ without a wait. The decor is very much so "cottage" on the farm style. Woody unfinished tables, dried flowers, rustic feel with dim lighting. If you want to relax and step away from the hustle and bustle of NYC, this is it! Â It's located by the restroom at Chelsea market as a point of reference. The service was good, they were really nice... which was what stood out about this place. Food came out at a good pace and they checked up on us. I would say come here for the ambiance and service, but not necessarily the food. I got a half grilled cheese and their soup of the day. Nothing really stood out flavorwise. I thought both the dishes were relatively bland. The kind of food you would eat if you had like nausea or a stomach ache... I had to add salt. The half sandwich/soup/salad is a good combo if you're not sure of what you want and need a taste. Felt pretty healthy and didn't weigh me down for the rest of the day.

We ate here on a Sunday afternoon. Found it to be a beautiful redo of an old Italian grocery. Enjoyed our window seat, especially because there was a noisy crowd at the common table in back. Enjoyed the beet salad, cheese plate and marinated olives as appetizers. Great, wood fire oven pizza and excellent salmon entree. Â Fine, attentive and helpful service. Try this spot soon.

If you like pasta then Supper is the spot to go. Everything is homemade and the lemon linguini is out of this world. The decor is charming: small worn-wooden tables and low lighting make it clear this is a member of the Lil Frankies/Frank family. The wine list is good, but like the other east village spots, they don't take reservations, so arrive early or make plans to wait.

On a cold spring night in NY, three friends and I trekked over to Joe's Shanghai hoping to saturate our ever-hungry taste buds with delicious XLB juice. The experience? Meh. The wait was an hour before we were seated at a huge table that we awkwardly shared with two other parties. Stuffing face in front of a stranger is an interesting dining experience, to say the least. We ordered two orders of XLB, Shanghai noodles, green oinion pancake, and pea sprouts. The XLB broth was not flavorful enough and the skin was too thick. The meat was just ok. The Shanghai noodles were a disappointment, lukewarm and flavorless. The green onion pancake was very greasy. They did a fine job with the veggies (pea sprouts in garlic, can't really mess that up), although they didn't have gai lan. What kind of Chinese restaurant doesn't have gai lan? Maybe I'm just spoiled by all the fresh produce in SF? Another note: 15% tip is added automatically to all checks. In any case, it was the cheapest meal I ate during my entire trip in NY, so I was satisfied (and giving it one extra star for the cheap factor). But it definitely did not live up to the Yelp reviews. Sorry, peeps!
Some dishes are pretty Good! Especially fried fish cake!
A+

A really exceptional dining experience. Â Gramercy Tavern knows both food and good service. Â  I had the $88 tasting menu and it was out of this world. Â The squash bisque was to die for. Finish dinner off with a glass of Scotch and the macaroons they bring you at the end of the meal = perfection.

A-Ma-Zing!!!!! I was treated by my brother to an omakase dinner and was simply blown away. Â I eat a decent amount of sushi & sashimi, so every piece I had was recognizable, but just perfectly fresh, well presented and better than any other fish I'd eaten. Â We kept asking for more to the point where our last order was "one or two more pieces of any fish we haven't tried", but after our waitress scanned through her list, she had to tell us we ate everything already! The restaurant is bright and open, but not at all cold or sterile. Â Service couldn't have been better. Â As everyone else has mentioned, the place is definitely expensive, our final bill (a lot of fish and 1 or 2 drinks each) came to about 200 per person.

Employees Only is known for their top-notch cocktails, but they are actually a restaurant that serves food that is just as good, or even better than their drinks. From bacon wrapped lambchops, bone marrow poppers, to steak tartare, just about anything you order will have you drooling and coming back for more. They make delicious classic cocktails with a modern twist and they can be paired to whatever you chose to eat that evening.

Okay, so the appetizers were good... pasta dishes ranged from being either too sweet or too lacking in flavor. But, above all, service is atrocious. The chubby, white (she seemed Italian) female waitress totally asked for her tip in cash since her payday wasn't for another week and a half... weird. And even after we left them tip in cash, she hurriedly grabbed our check and made rude comments loud enough for us to hear before realizing that we left the tip in cash on the table. Then she bides us goodbye in a sweet manner. MAN, SCREW YO' SHIT! Totally ruined a sub-par dining experience.

Nice restaurant and great food. Order the chefs menu, with different kind of dishes. Very tasty. Unfortunately it was very busy, so they pushed the food too quickly. Luckily we had a very friendly waitress, so we had a great night.

Overpriced for what it is. Yes, flavors are unique, but you can't charge $17 for a bowl of plain noodles with 4 small shrimp and 2 pieces of pork about the size of a quarter. Â Ps--you're all about money, not food, if your restaurant has no tables for 2 people. Â Ribs were hearty. Â Stick with corn and ribs (or just go to a BBQ :)

I loved this place. Very cute, open air, felt bustling and trendy but intimate enough for a date. Great pasta. Great champagne cocktail. Great boar and polenta special. I've also heard great things about the pasta. Our server was polite but not in our faces. I highly recommend for a small-ish group (it's not a huge place) or one-on-one.

Came here 7pm Friday evening for cuz's BD dinner. Â Sat upstairs, doors were open, no breeze, hot as balls. Â Great swamp ass by end of meal. Party of 8 requested a larger table, not granted. Â The large table next to us which was "reserved" was empty our entire meal. Â  Apps were ok: Profiteroles: not bad, not great Mussels: Salty, huge could have been from the coast of Japan...radiation Bone Marrow: ok Ceasar: ok, as it should have been Calamari: skip it Salmon Tartare: Tasty, could have been a little cooler and some crispier more delicate carb rather than bread would have been a better complement Entrees: Branzino: Maybe.. not sure as it was not the whole fish. Â Salty as balls Rabbit: Salty Ribeye: Not bad, not dry aged 30 days Linguine vongole: meh, Salty Dessert: One of each...wasn't finished off. Irish coffee was missing the Irish Atmosphere: Not bad, quiet since it was 60% empty. Service: Needs work. Â Was not asked how my food was. Â  Physical table was the kind that has the round sides that flip open to expand. Â Not enough support felt like I was eating at the bottom of a hill. Caramel at end was best part. Note: Don't be ass, toilet upstairs needs a double flush even for piss. Â Please flush for following person.

Restaurant of my dreams!!! Â Potatoes in every form? Â As you want it? Â SO IN LOVE!!! Â  Unfortunately, I'm on a diet so I cannot indulge too much. Â I came here once. Â On my birthday. Â And it was spectacular. Now I walk by every time just tormented that I cannot go inside because I know it's going to be highly delicious but also highly caloric.

After hearing much reviews about Ippudo, I decided to check this place out..all the way from California. We arrived on Friday night, party of 4 at 7pm. The wait is 2.5 hrs. Good lord. Really? We put our name down and went to eat someplace else, walked around, and came back 2 hrs later. Still waited another hour, making that a 3-hr wait for some ramen. This better be DAMN GOOD. Finally got seated, service was excellent, and the food quality was great. We ordered some of the daily specials and the famous pork buns which were all very yummy. The biggest disappointment was the ramen. Broth was good but too buttery. Are there not that many good ramen places in New York hence people line up 2+ hrs for some noodles? Sooo not worth the wait. Go on a weekday to avoid the long wait. They do have good food, service, and ambience. The food came out super quick and tasted fresh. Minus one star for the ramen being not the best ramen I've ever had and minus another star the uber ridiculous wait!
One of the top 5 or so in NYC. Their sauce is very fresh and the pizza perfectly cooked

Absolutely recommended! The amuse gueule was a fantastic little strawberry pepper gazpacho. As a salad fan I had the lettuce salad with peaches and golden zucchini which was good. However the salt and pepper shrimp with an assortment of melons were absolutely fantastic!! Best dish I had in a long time. Surprising, new and super tasty! A little spicy, perfect balance between sweet, sour and salty! Overall a very good atmosphere in the place, super sweet and caring crew. They have a little outdoor courtyard which looked cute. The chef is brilliant and creates innovative dishes.

Simply, the Best. This is my ideal bar scene - a rustic trattoria, with excellent service (with a smile). The food is amazing. Anything with "soft boiled egg" - just order it. I hate using the word 'food-gasm,' but there it is. Reccos: Ravioli w/ goat cheese and egg yolk, happy hour Pizza Carbonara (yes, w/ egg yolk), side of Mushrooms (best ever), Tonorelli pasta, and please finish with an order of tiramasu. Holy cow. Oh, forgot to mention - you have to drink a glass of red wine (petit verdot) in order to experience the sublime... Cheers.

Seriously- the best Japanese NY style place in town. In NY! Love the spicy miso ramen. They are always friendly, happy to be at work, and loving life! Good food- good vibes. stop by and enjoy the food!

Do: Come for happy hour (live music Wednesdays and Fridays) Order wine specials, THEN a bottle Try the Bacon stuffed dates and the fried olives More bacon stuffed dates Don't: Bother with entrees (unless it's the branzino) Falafel-crusted artichoke hearts-- way too much falafel! Overall: Good place for pre-BAM drinks and small plates, but for dinner I'd go elsewhere.

So far so good! Have been in the neighborhood long enough to have visited the previous incarnation of Grand Dakar. These guys have done wonders with the space - it's beautiful, much more open, and I love the bar and separate dining room. Now onto the food: I must say, I came hear because of the rumors flying about the insanely high-quality fried chicken being served at this place. Well, after going to town on their 3-piece fried chicken dinner last night, I can prove the rumors correct. I love Peaches Hothouse chicken, no doubt, but this chicken is pretty darn good! If the spicyness of Peaches' chicken is a bit overwhelming for you, this is possibly the next best thing. The skin was sooo incredibly crispy and flavorful, the chicken was so moist but not so much as to make the skin eventually soggy, and I love the vinegar and spicy sauce it comes with!
