My one gripe: no sides. It comes with a little arugula salad, but that's it. Even one side would have been nice. However, even a side, that plus the chicken will set you back $18-ish dollars, which is not too shabby in my book. This is a great new addition to the neighborhood, and I can't wait to go back and try more of their menu offerings!

Believe the hype. This place is true and real. The atmosphere is chill. Good music. Small room. Polite staff. But it's the food that keeps you. The crust is crusty. The sauce is saucy. The cheese is cheesy. Seriously, perfect sauce and crust. Â Possible best pizza in brooklyn? Â You heard it here first. Â Salad was good too. We will be back. Regularly. Welcome to the neighborhood, Emily.

wow, 493 reviews? Went in for lunch, no wait, greeted by a chorus of Japanese that just made me smile, though i didn't understand it. was seated at the end of a long table, right next to the dish pit, but with a pretty good view of the kitchen. anyway, the broth was amazing, the noodles were fantastically chewy, but the pork was very boring, and the egg had been boiled to death, and was chalky even after sitting in a bowl of soup for the duration of my meal. Also they were a little heavy handed on the ginger and sesame seeds. Â tagged for 20 bucks with a beer, but worth it. Â and for some reason i love how everybody says goodbye and thank you when you leave, its silly, but it made me smile. I'll be back.

Too often trend, style and buzz overshadow what's actually important about a restaurant; food and drink. On a quaint Elizabeth St. block, an anomaly exists; a restaurant that mergers "food destination" with just plain "destination." Public is that rare jack of all trades. Romantic date? Impress the lady friend by sneaking her off to the Monday Room, their hidden wine lounge behind the host stand, where you can conveniently cozy up in a leather banquet while enjoying a custom wine flight. Foodie friend? Don't miss the foie gras on French toast with mango chutney; its not really breakfast, dinner or politically correct but, its definitely amazing. Drinker? Their Rhubarb Mule cocktail welcomes springtime with gin, ginger, and rhubarb. Warning/Endorsement: dangerously easy to drink. All the above? Your night could end on a very good note.

Beats the hell out of Oaxaca (who closed THE DAY AFTER I bought two $5 Groupons... very sketchy). Had three tacos: Fried Avacado & Jalapeno: Amazing. Best taco I've had in a long time. Al Pastor: Very good Picadillo: Also good, plus the tortilla had been fried so it was a bit crunchier/had more structural integrity--good because the Al Pastor sprung a leak and emergency cutlery was required to get the job done. The happy hour special of $1 off tacos is a big bonus to me, because I've never acclimated to how much a taco in NY costs versus a taco in Chicago. I'll def be back to try the fried chicken, blackened catfish, brisket, and guac. And, of course, need to have a margarita next time. ALSO: They take cards!! Huge plus in a cash-only neighborhood.
Our favorite neighborhood Italian restaurant. I love the spaghetti and she loves the veal meatballs. Great service and atmosphere at reasonable price

Eataly was a fun, albeit INSANELY crowded, foray into Italian food. Eataly is basically one big temple worshipping Italian food. Â It appeared to be technically comprised of a variety of different restaurants - some dedicated exclusively to good seafood, another to good meat, another to good pasta, etc. Â We opted for the fish place, which was ridiculously tasty - the fish, which we picked out of a selection of fresh fish that day, was cooked to perfection. Wine is, as one might expect, available en masse here, as is delicious beer. Â The selection is as broad as it is tasty. The only negative: this place was CROWDED. Â To the point where it felt loud and slightly uncomfortable. Â As the entire place is basically one large open space with half-wall dividers, nothing separates you from the hundreds of other people here and the food they eat. Â It was a bit too overwhelming at times.

Jane is such a cute little spot for lunch. Â The low-key, bistro-like atmosphere is really welcoming, and the menu is packed with delicious options. Â One of my favorite items is a divine goat cheese-avocado sandwich. Â The atmosphere is relaxing, and it's fun to watch passersby on Houston Street. Â I'd highly recommend Jane for a lunch with friends or even a more casual business lunch.

What a terrific experience all around! Â We had dinner with another couple, so we each got to sample 4 apps, 3 entrees, and 4 desserts. Â Apps: Â the chili lobster was so perfectly spicy and rich in flavor; the cavatelli was pasta perfection with the balance of flavors and textures hitting the spot; the grilled calamari was ridiculous - so tender and delicate; and I had the special ravioli of the day - can you even imagine a ravioli dish topped with Midnight Moon cheese, with fresh summer peas, asparagus, snap peas, with the most heavenly fresh green sauce oozing out of the ravioli? OK, entrees - hubby and I shared the chicken under a brick which our delightful, friendly, and knowledgable waitress suggested was best shared if the other couple each ordered their own entrees but would also share the chicken. Â She was totally right. Our friends had scallops (perfectly seared and tender) and duck breast (with the most ridiculous fois gras/confit-like accompaniment, plus cherry yumminess). Â The chicken Â portion was very generous - it is, after all, an entire chicken, so we were glad to share with them in exchange for a taste of theirs! Â Chicken was so tender, perfectly charred, and served with delicious broccoli rabe and sinfully good potatoes. Â  Dessert - if you love chocolate, get the smores and the cheesecake is worth every calorie. So, part of what made the dinner delicious was the overall dining experience. Â The room was very comfortable; there is plenty of space between tables for comfort and the decor is warm and "rustic-modern" but not contrived. Â The service was exceptional - and I have to say that service counts a lot to me. Â A great dinner with snarky, uninformed, or inattentive staff loses points. Â Everyone was extremely warm and friendly but never intrusive. Â Plates were served and cleared in the correct manner (rarely see that anymore, other than the most stuffy places). Â Wine was served well; dinner plate held warm when my friend stepped away to the restroom just before the plate was served. Â Spot on, all around.

Such a delightful place to dine. A hidden gem, the dining room itself is stoic in natural prewar grandeur. The food is perfect. First course: Beet Salad is the best in the city. We each had our own as too good to share. Dinner: We had the spaetzle.. Which was light and flavorful with a hint of nutmeg and amazing creamed wild mushroom, carrot, peas and tarragon. The Wiener schnitzel was light crisp not greasy and delicate flavor served with a lingonberry sauce.. Cucumbers & Potatoes. Dessert: Chocolate Rum Cake ~ seriously perfect. Apple Strudel ~ which was better than any I've had in Germany. Layered Strawberry Elderflower Mousse Cake ~ serious Heaven and the perfect atmosphere made for most memorable evening.

I came to this place because I tried before and I liked it. However the service yesterday was terrible. So much SMOKE that my eyes were watering and many customers left! And no pico (did they tell me there is no pico, before I ordered? NO. Did they charge me less, because there was no pico? NO). I went to reliable Chipotle 3 stores down to get my pico.
I don't really like artichoke, and I don't really like white sauce. If you're like me, try the Sicilian! Oh so good.

Unfortunately, I don't think this place lived up to it's hype. The skewers were decent, but I've had much better yakitori. Since the skewers came all at once, none of it tasted hot or fresh off the grill... The asparagus wrapped with bacon was decent, and the pork neck was fatty, and chewy. The grilled shitakes were too dry, and the skirt steak, and kalbi skewers were so-so. I was not partial to the grilled eggplant with miso paste. The skewers here are nothing special; too bad since I love good yakitori. Also they don't sell grilled japanese yam. :(
The pasta was good; but everything else was just ok Plenty of friendly servers - but did not refill wine etc OK before theater Not worth more than 3 stars

This place is the new gem of the neighborhood. Â Super clean inside, easy to order, friendly and informational staff. Â Brilliant concept. Ordered: - Balkan burger; absolutely delicious and refreshing. Â Not heavy at all but way more taste and flavor than any other non beef burger I have had. Â Superb!!! - Basque Shrimp; super fresh, great flavor, well executed dish. Â A must try! Definitely giving Reviver 5 full stars and I cannot wait to try more dishes. Absolutely loved this place and will be visiting at least couple times a week. Thank you Reviver!
Great burger, horrible service. Â Downtown? Â Go to Paul's.

I have never written any reviews on here but I had a blast at Gaia and I wanted to share. I'm from Italy as well and I had many problems to find real Italian food in town and then I discovered Gaia: amazing coffee, delicious and original Italian food and a very cozy environment. The owner, Gaia, is super welcoming, friendly and I always have a good time talking to her. I think it's amazing and give it 5 stars.
Best biscuits and gravy ever! And I really like biscuits and gravy.

Good Lord, Â I'm about to betray all Vietnamese people out there by saying how delicious the sandwiches here are. Â It's like banh mi on crack. Â One of my most ardent complaints when it comes to certain banh mi's is the way the vegetables are pickled. Â It needs the right amount of crunch and sweet/sour kick to it that makes the banh mi for me. Â At Num Pang, the vegetables are cut just right: Â carrots and daikon julienned perfectly, cucumber sliced lengthwise (not too thick, not too thin) and cilantro scattered about. Â The sandwich also had enough sauce to keep it from being dry -- another downfall of some banh mi shops out there. Â  I ordered the pork belly sandwich and it was lovely. Â Just enough fat to pull this whole masterpiece of a sandwich together. Â I also had a bite from my friend's catfish sandwich (his favorite). Â I'm willing to bet everything on their menu is delicious. Â If I ever get the chance to come back to NY, I'm definitely going to be stopping by here on a regular basis because Portland, ME is in dire need of some good banh mi joints.
Try the espinacas a la crema, so good! Also the Croquettas with ham and cheese, delicious! I was bothered that they put mayonaisse apparently on everything, even the albondigas.

Best Chinese in NYC in my humble opinion - a co-worker first introduced me to the place this summer and I fell in love. The space is cramped and there is a wait but its well worth it. Everything is done well but the suckling pig is to die for - get there early for it though because they tend to run out later in the night.

For less than $20, you can probably feed up to 4 to 5 people. Â You cannot find that anywhere in Manhattan. Â The dumplings are meaty and has a good balance of chives. Â Be careful they will explode in your mouth and it is piping hot. I prefer the fried ones, that crispy skin on the bottom of the dumpling just makes it a little better. If you have a small group, just order a bunch of things for sharing. The dumplings obviously are the go to, but the pancake sandwiches are also very delicious. Â It is this crusty sesame bread that is stuffed pickled carrots and cucumbers and then you add your meat. Â We shared the duck and the pork. Great late night dining to soak up the alcohol. Â There is limited seating so have a fried stake out a table while you order.

I can't say more than a hidden gem for sure. Â The staff is attentive to say the least, every time i was 3/4 done with my water it was refilled immediately. Â I drank them down quickly just to test how attentive the staff was haha, and damn they're on point. Â The waitress was informative and helpful since the pizza isn't pepperoni its definitely an Italian named and interesting read. The pizza here is what it's all about, the ambiance is a little more upscale and trendy then what you would imagine a "Pizzabar" as, but I'm coming back when i'm in New York again.
Who else serves you cups of coffee and gingers snaps while you're waiting in line on the weekends? Â Nobody! Â That's who. 15 years of happy meals with friends at Toms and counting. Don't change!!!

lamb shank was falling off the bone and a perfect fall dish. would come back just to eat this again! monkfish was also a great fall dish, albeit much lighter and didn't stand up as well to the reasonably priced '05 bordeaux they have on the wine list

Great place for a quick bite. I love thin crust pizza so this place is a great find! For $4.00+tax, you get two slices. Their toppings are so simple and fresh! Caprese, Mushroom with truffle oil and zucchini with artichokes are all really very good. But that crunchy crust brings it home. It's light and I don't feel incredibly stuffed, which is a good thing. The place is small. It can only seat 4 ppl. So this is not the place if you plan to hang out for a while.
Brunch was mediocre. Nothing special. Service was good but the restaurant itself was not worth the 45 min wait.

The food is mouth watering. Even though it's slightly embarassing, within the first week of finding this place I went 3 times! That's a record for me. But a true testament to how delicious it is. The tejadas, yoyos, every cocktail, side, and arepa I've had is DELICIOUS - and very good pricing! My favorite items include the La del Gato arepa (guayanese cheese, avocado, and sweetened plantains), Dark & Stormy cocktail (fresh pressed ginger & rum), and the salsa on the table ( I could eat that as a meal by itself Â - it's sooooo good) Enjoy the authenticity of the food and the decor. It's hands down my new favorite spot.

So I didn't go to the original one the first time i tried..and I just didn't understand why people were raving about this and craving it..until I tried this original one. OMG. What a BIG difference!! Those fakes are no competition!!! I came here on a .. wednesday at midnight and the line was maybe 7-8 people in front of me...so I got it pretty quick. I had to get beef and chicken or lamb and chicken because if I wanted just chicken it would be a little longer as the guy says so I settled for beef and chicken. They packed 2 white sauce and hot sauce for you and cover it and stick it in a bag with a fork and napkins. These guys know how to do business and quick! The chicken and rice...I've finally figured out why people come here to eat it!! It's amazing..amazing..amazing. Okay you get the point. I will definitely have to come back and get this but I'm scared of the line. $6 for amazing rice and chicken..mmm!!!! yeah people who raved about chicken and rice was right!!!

Oh, St. Anselm. Y'all so smart! So we didn't have a reservation. (I'm not sure if they take them, actually.. Do they?) We were encouraged to go next door to Spuyten Duyvil to have a couple beers. Turns out these two spots are related. In fact, SD came before SA. Needless to say we were drunk off our faces from the delicious beer before we got to our table. Alcohol usually makes any food good but their food here is truly great. I dined on all veggie fare and was equally please with my meal as my omnivore pals. I aspire to visit this joint sober.

Soooo good, and it's a goooood amount for the price you pay too. I've been to New York quite a few times and have never had this before and I'm not sure why. Had it for the first time in June of this year and I am soooo craving it again! Be careful of imposters though. You will see a "Halal" cart on every corner or 53rd & 6th and we couldn't even tell the difference from the original and the imposters. Well, I happened to come across this article recently and wanted to share it with you all. So if you haven't tried it yet or are just craving for more.... here's how to spot the difference. Hope it helps. =) newyork.seriouseats.com/â€¦

Last night was the first time I had Brazilian food and I'm glad to say that I am not disappointed at all! It's not a bad walk from the subway, which is nice and convenient. As we were approaching the restaurant, i was a little scared because the restaurant was empty! there was only one other couple inside - this was around 6:30pm on a tuesday. Â For appetizers, we had the calamari with malagueta sauce. It was really good! the calamari was soft and yummy! as for the entrees, since i've never had Brazilian before, I decided to ask the waiter what people usually get. He suggested the fish - Corvina vatapa, it was fish served with mashed potatoes with some coconut milk with shrimps and peppers and i am very glad i took his advice. Oh before i forget, they have the best Sangria ever!!! :)

Truly mediocre in decor and food. Service prompt and polite. But veal chop was a very large breaded veal parmigiana not a veal chop in the thick usual way . The fall vegetables were dreadful. But the location near Carnegie Hall is convenient and the watery martini was watery. The Riesling was good. This is a place that once was very 'classy' and is now a stop for out oft owners
these chicken wings are shittier than the guy who owns the joint.
Small place where Â to eat but their Sicilian pizza is the best, I go there almost every weekend.

Got the Sweet Tree roll to go with Sweet Soy Mirin sauce (instead of the toasted cayenne) and it was delicious! Â I loved the combination of sweet potato and avocado on the inside, and it was even more delicious with the sweet soy mirin. Â This was my first time here and I will definitely be back to try some of their other rolls!
I always try as many empanda's as my tummy will hold. Â  Try to get here early if you want a table. Â Yummy food with a great price.

I considered coming back to this place to try out their brunch or dinner options but now that I've given it more thought, nah. Service was subpar. It wasn't busy at all on a random Tuesday for breakfast/lunch so why did it take forever to get the check? Or anything for that matter...Also thanks for letting us know that the lunch menu was gonna be available in like 10 minutes. Sarcasm. Got the omelette which tasted like an omelette you get on the plane. Bacon and chicken sausage sides were basic.
Make-your own Thai ice tea was the highlight. The sunset menu was really nice. Portions were not too much and not too little. Quiet little place. Loved it!

I have enjoy Ofrenda numerous times in the past, but this last Sunday Sep 21, I did a Birthday party for my wife and 45 People. All different backgrounds, Manhasset LI represented the USA, Germans, Colombians, Mexicans, Italians, and one Japanese The food was excellent authentic Mexican food. Fabiola was our waitresses delivering an outstanding level of service. Let's not forget the drinks from Orlando and Enrique where the hit of the night. William the GM allowed me to bring a Mariachi Band and we play music in till 2 AM. The venue turned to be more like El Tenampa in Plaza Garibaldi Mexico. And that is not easy to accomplish. Thank you berry much to the Ofrenda Team

Eh. Maybe the snow put a damper on this bars experience. I attended last night around midnight (when bars should usually be jumping) and I was faced with a thick crowd of hipsters (which I love) hugging on to the bar for dear life. It was IMPOSSIBLE to get a drink. No seriously, IMPOSSIBLE. We stood at one bar for about 15 mins...then went to the other bar in the back-- we didn't even see the bartender at that one! At one point the jukebox wasn't even playing and I found myself listening to awkward drunken conversations. I'll be honest, I love me some cheeseballs...but where the hell were they at? After my failed attempt at getting a drink, I figured I'd at least get a handful of balls (no pun intended) before jetting. My expectations for The Levee were so, so high. I'll give it another try..only because of the cheeseballs.

So in an ideal world, I would go to a restaurant, then the following morning, as I'm sipping my coffee and pretending to check my "important" work emails, I would yelp about my dining experience. Â I went to Barbuto about a week ago and I have tried to write my review a few times but I find myself not particularly inspired. I thought the service was kind of awkward. Â I came with two girlfriends and we were waiting for a third to arrive - she had told us to just sit and eat and not wait for her. Â The hostess told us we could not sit at a dining table unless we were ordering food; which is extremely reasonable, in a busy bee restaurant. Â But here, on this quiet weekday night, I could have drowned in the vast number of empty tables. Â So we had to promise that we were ordering food before we could be seated. Whatever, that was fine. Â Our waiter sort of took forever to bring our wine and food, but the ambiance was quite nice. Â I ordered the rigatoni with cauliflower and cream, which tasted good, but not particularly impressive. Â I guess I would prefer more traditional italian dishes. Oh, and the reason that we were here in the first place is because Tortilla Flats (right across the street) was closed for a private party, and we were so disappointed that we missed bingo night!
Delicious pizza Its like Goodfellas with a thin crust, but a 1,000,000 times better
Fantastic value in midtown. The black beans were excellent. Very fast service too so if you're in a hurry, this is a great option.

Ramen noodles. What's the big deal? Nothing till you try it here. Didn't think ramen noodles could taste so good. Prepare to wait during peak hours. Pro tip: get your name on the list and have them call you when your table is almost ready while you bar hop around the area.

This has been a rather unsuccessful weekend food-wise. After having a yummy giant sausage off the streets in Little Italy for the Feast of St. Gennara we walked to Vanessa's which was our original plan. Dont get me wrong, I like littel Chinese hidden restaurants, the more low key the better. But low-key and 1-dolla Dim Sum is no excuse for yuckiness. The place itself needs a good sweeping, the tables need a wipe-down and we were originally seated next to some super shady characters! Either ways I could have overlooked ALL of this if only the food was up to par. Hot and Sour Soup: COLD, gloopy, gooey, messy, took one sip and made a face and ignored it. Dumplings: not good dumplings; dumplings are supposed to be delicate, see-through pockets of fine dough that melt in your mouth, dont fall apart and have yummy fillings inside them. These are just too big, too thick and frankly just not that great. My biggest complaint: watered down chili?!?

Literally everything on their menu is fantastic. You want meat on your meat? How about some meat on that? The portions are great and well stacked, and don't limit yourself to just loving one sandwich and calling it your favorite. Try everything on their menu at least once and you'll know what I'm talking about. The smart duck is good as well as the roast beef. Half a sandwich for 5.40. Cheaper than subway and twice the meat.

A friend and I went here for dinner. It wasn't terrible. It just did nothing to distinguish itself from the hundreds of other similar places. We had soup dumplings, which were on the bland side; and some oyster mushrooms and greens, which were on the greasy side. The highlight was the sesame chicken with broccoli, which was crunchy (the chicken) and bright and crispy (the broccoli).

I had the veggie burger with a root veggie side and my girlfriend went with the Mexican burger. Â Both were cooked to perfection and the flavor was amazing. Â Great, friendly service and a wonderful ambiance. Â B&B makes a great spot for a fun date or to go out with a group of friends. Â Also has an impressive selection of wines.
I'm a huge fan of this hot spot...the food was filling, and tasty...the presentation of the food and drinks down to the coffee of was awesome..I'll definitely go back and bring hubby and friends

Welcome to the UWS Anthi's Greek Food! Â  Anthi's is a tiny, Greek take-out treasure. Â They have many tasty salads, yogurts, baklavas, etc to choose from. Â I have had their artichoke salad, which can only be described as fresh and delicious. Â Also, I couldn't help but get a taste of the mini-baklava - crispy and sweet just the way I like it! Â  On top of a wonderful selection, the man who I am guessing is the owner is super nice. Â Lastly, the serving sizes are perfectly paired with the price! Â  Excited to have them in the neighborhood and looking forward to trying many more off of their menu!
Yummy ham and cheese crepe (tastes better with mustard) with a side salad. Not too far from the high line. I'd go there again. Mom had crepe du jour with scallops and potatoes but she didn't like it.

Went there on a Group On, and the staff was very friendly. We had blood sausage, the lamb sizzler, yak momo, and 2 ginger beers. Blood sausage was awesome! Lamb sizzler was also great. Lamb was super tender and falvorful. Yak Momo was good, but don't get it steamed. Next time, we will try it fried. The yak inside was tasty, but outre wrapping was a bit odd tasting to me. They allowed us to substitute ginger beers instead of beer or wine, which was great. (And cheaper for them) The only thing keeping this from a 5-star is the way waitress disappeared when we needed check. We definitely will go back, though, and recommend you try it out. (especially the blood sausage and lamb sizzler)

Another visit to this wonderful restaurant.....one of our favourites across the globe. And another exceptional experience....so, so very good. My natural assumption is that great restaurants lose their gloss when complacency sets in and typically the high expectation morphs to disappointment and a memory...definitely not the case here. This little gem has expanded next door and the tastes, the service and atmosphere are even better than our first visit. The servers have changed over time however the service standards have not. Well, another update review and it is just continues this great story...cannot wait to come back again.

I was a bit skeptical about this place but I was pleasantly surprised. They've got outdoor seating which is a plus for me and my pooch. The salads are good but not great. Pizza is standard thin crust but solid and very tasty. I'd go back more than once!

Had the veggie burger with fries and a side of the red bean hummus. All was really good. I was particularly surprised about the hummus considering my past experiences (at other restaurants)consisted of very thick, flavorless ingredients.

It really is good. Â I'm not always a super-thin crust fan. Â I don't like charred pizza, and I like a little bit of a pillowy texture. Â Lombardi's pizza was neither charred not cracker crisp. Â It had just enough pillowy bite to be satisfying. Â On top of that, literally, the tomato sauce and mozzarella were really high quality. Â You could taste a little bit of Italy in each bite.

I would give this place 5 stars but I want to try more foods before I say anything conclusive. Â So I got the Rojak Mee because I saw the picture somebody put on yelp. Â It was freaking amazing!!!! Â LIke, holy shit! Â The picture looked good but it tasted even better. Â Aaah! Â I also got the roti canai which was freaking yummy as hell ;3 I want to go back so badly. Â When I left I kept telling my friend, "that was wonderful!"

I stopped by pommes frites during a flash flood warning so it was jammed pack and humid in this extremely TINY joint. Therefore, I took away a star because I wish this place was slightly bigger with more seating because I know it gets crowded here very easily. However the fries were really good. They were crispy but not so that you felt like you were eating burnt fries. There are a lot of options for sauces which cost $1.50 and in my opinion you don't get enough for what you pay for. But I had the mango chutney, which I highly recommend and the curry ketchup which took some time getting used to. Overall I would stop by here again to enjoy some fries with friends!
Seriously delicious brunch, and great value, too! Â Ordered the ham, gruyere, and caramelized onion scramble, and it was delicious. Â Portions are large, as well. Â Definitely recommend it!

I think I found one of the best salads in NYC, their grilled chicken Waldorf. Salads in the city are not as good as in Cali, where everything is fresh. But this salad was crisp, light, healthy and the chicken very tender. There is a heaping pile of shredded apples to keep the doctor away. I had the 24 Karat juice with beets and this funky green algae floating on top, very good. I split a wheat tomato, basil, mozzarella pizza - which was just OK (not their strongest dish). We looked around at other tables and everything looked so delicious! This is definitely going to be one of my favorite lunch places --it's a beautiful space and everything is organic! Plus you get to browse ABC carpets afterwards.

Business dinner recommended by a colleague. Delicious ginger cocktail followed by a pleasant bottle of nicely priced Cabernet. Â  Service was a bit distracted but food was solid for the most part. You could do a lot worse!

If you like rude customer service, lack luster margaritas, over priced tacos, watery guacamole, and a tight crampy space then go here!!!!!! I cannot believe this place has such a high rating I honestly feel duped!!!! I'm big on yelp and getting real reviews before I visit a place, and following these reviews were a big mistake. My boyfriend and I are Mexican food lovers and are always on the hunt to find the best guacamole. And let me tell this place by far didn't cut it. The guacamole was one of the worst I've ever tasted and was not worth the $5 bucks we paid for it nor was the tasteless margarita. I make wayyyy better guacamole and margaritas and would have rather gone to the grocery store picked up the ingredients and made my own before giving those rude disrespectful people a dime of my money. They had no respect or urgency for their customers. My boyfriend asked where the garbage was and the cashier rudely told him "over there" and rolled her eyes as if it was a dumb question. When we placed our order there was no thank you at all. I honestly feel sorry for anyone who said this place has the best tacos because clearly you have been deprived of actually tasting "good" Mexican food! If this place was the last place on earth to get food from my boyfriend and I would probably starve to death. I have zero tolerance for bad customer service period!! This place is a total fail and waste of time and money. PLEASE DO NOT GO!!!!

Really one of the worst experiences I've had food-wise at a restaurant of this calibre. One of the dishes (white asparagus) was so over salted that it was literally inedible, but the staff will argue with you and try to intimidate you into agreeing with them that it is you and not the dish that is not up to standards. The manager came around to the table to ask us to hurry up ordering (this was before the salt tide had arrived) in a very aggressive way. I felt bullied and the food was really bad actually - at a price of over $100 a head with a moderate amount of wine.

Minca is a great place for ramen -- it's pretty much what you would expect from a ramen shop tucked away somewhere less touristy in the LES, and because of its non-optimal location you'll seldom have to wait for a seat. The interior can get a bit stuffy during the summer -- perhaps they were having A/C problems when I visited -- but overall the ambience was very relaxed and felt completely unhyped.
Great food, great service, great prices!

YAY! I'm a fan of their chicken over rice! Thank you Yelp tips! I have learned early on that majority of halal carts have fatty chicken. I hate it. Just not a fan. Here, it's flaky shredded?!? I don't really know how to put it, but it's damn good. No gross fatty chicken gristle here. YAAASSSS! I get to apply my own amount of sauce. Which is always a plus! They have white sauce, hot sauce, and BBQ. When we arrived, the line was 10 people deep, but moved fairly quickly. I will assume that the rice is pre-placed in the plate (as there was a stack of them in the corner), and they just toss in your choice and a few pieces of pita bread when you order. My rice was a bit dry, but nothing more sauce can't cure. The lamb over rice is eh. The chicken is WAY better. Absolutely worth the $6.

Oh man, this place was great! I found it on here (of course) and decided to try it on a weekend stay in the city. The way that they cook the onions onto the burger makes for a delicious melding of flavor. I ate my burgers with their BBQ sauce and that made the burger perfect. I ordered a side of pickles, but they were really thick which was too much for a slider sized burger so I left them off and ate some on the side. The fries were my favorite kind which is true fries that aren't processed, but made from a cut up potato with the skin still on- reminded me of Five Guys fries. Oh and their beef is fresh ground in house! My husband had the Guinness shake. I hate beer, so I thought it was gross, but he liked it.

They probably could not have thought of a less cool name for this place. Also, what's up with the whole concept? I love potatoes, but never in my life have I thought to myself, man I could eat a whole plate of potatoes for dinner. Â  Well now if I ever have that thought I have a place to carry it out.
Best Mexican food ever!!! They have amazing tamales, quesadillas, burritos, tacos and well you get the point. Nice cozy ambience and the staff is so friendly. One of my favorite restaurants.
Consistently good food and good service. Their chicken and waffles are great. They also have Bloody Bulls if you ask

Came here with a restaurant.com gift card. Found something close to our house and as per the yelp reviews we were curious! Once was passed by we weren't to sure about the place looked sketchy. Still gave it a go. Once we entered I felt out of place and the lack of staff leaves u wondering what to do (for first timers). Once u order at the bar the staff answered any questions we might have had. We ordered some beers on tap but they weren't for us. After seeing someone with a lemonade we had to have and it is a MUST!!! Lemonade and bourbon be careful LOL We ordered the pulled pork tacos, beef tacos, corn on the Cobb and half celantro lime and half buffalo wings. Everything was amazing they BETTER NOT GET RID OF THAT COOK WHOMEVER SHE IS (forgot her name) My husband said I'm surprised there isn't a line out of the door waiting for food LOL. Don't judge a book by its cover!!!!

I kind of thought this place was stuffy. Â I didn't sit down to eat-just had a few drinks at the bar and felt the need to get out. Maybe it was due to my desire to grab some falafel across the street. Â Maybe it was due to my dirty martini being one of the weaker drinks of the night. Â I even downed my date's martini and couldn't taste a hint of vodka. Some may say that's a signature of a well made drink. Â I suppose. Â But after quaffing two martinis in under ten minutes, I thought I'd feel something. So I'll admit my review of this place isn't in-depth. Â The bartender was nice and was candid in his opinions of drinks, which I appreciate. Â I did like the old school feel of this place and have heard the burgers are amazing. I'd like to come back and eat a steak. Â I'm sure then my opinion will turn all the more favorable. Still, I think this place is A-OK.

Soooo, I've heard so much about this place and as a devout foodie, I had to check it out. Â Fortunately our wait wasn't too long, but that was the best thing about pies-n-thighs. Before I continue I should state that my palate has been trained by true southern chefs in my family, thus the bar has been set high. The food was fine, but major points were lost when I found a hair in my food. Then I ordered the apple pie with cheddar cheese, but was surprised to have a cold slice. I guess I shouldn't have assumed that they would've served it warm. I also thought that the cheese came melted on top of the pie--not so. In my opinion pies-n-thighs is overrated. The competition is tough out there and I really don't understand why this is rated as one of the best.

lunch. great service. no wait. duck over rice was yum! good portion. delicious! the kicker is that the momofuku milk bar is right across the street, so you can partake in a little bit of crack pie post-meal before you hit the gym. lol

My boyfriend and I found this place about 6 months ago and it almost immediately became our favorite go to spot for a night out and delivery. The food is incredible and when the owner tells you he only makes food his grandmothers made for him, you believe it. If possible the staff could be even better or at least on par with the incredible (and well priced) food with great service and great attitudes. My only fear about this place is that everyone in the city will know about it soon. Wishing I could keep this place all to myself.
Coban Lookchaomaesaithong and Namkabuan Rachapruikafe, both Muay Thai champions give approving thumbs up. Â Closest thing to authentic Thai food outside of Thailand.

i thought the food was absolutely delicious! i will definitely come back again, it does get pretty busy and it is extremely loud, however with the great quality of food, and happy hour it was totally worth it.

I have nothing but good things to say about this place. The decor is really well done and the service is fantastic. I will be a regular to this place for sure. I got the Oyako Don. It's like a rice grilled bowl with chicken. I loved it. It was light and very well done. It came with soup and and steamed egg custard that was delicious. The restaurant is very clean. Be aware that they close the kitchen at 10:00. I had no complaints. Check this place out.
Lovely cocktails and even lovlier atmosphere.

After getting a major dose of hype for Umami burger, I was prepared for a letdown but no. This place definitely has one of the better burgers that I have ever tasted. When comparing "chains" this place schools In and Out, Shake Shack, Five Guys and etc. I had the "original" and it was pretty much cooked to perfection, the sweetness of the bun contrasting perfectly with the parmesan chip and perfectly cooked juicy medium rare beef. The fries were cooked well and the different flavored sauces are a nice touch but the star of the show was definitely the burger. At around 12 bucks a burger, it should taste this good and it delivered. We went around 5pm on a Sunday and it was already kinda packed with a 20-30 min wait. And when we got upstairs they had a leaky air conditioner that kept on dripping AC water on me which was kinda annoying, but BURGER.

I love Lidia Bastianich. Â I love watching her cook and I love a successful attempt at trying her recipes. Â This is why I wanted to try one of her restaurants. It is packed especially before a Broadway show. Â But if you go and dine leisurely, it feel you'll get to enjoy all the food they have to offer. I almost filled up on the breadbasket. Â We wanted to try so many things, but I was really craving for pasta. Â They have the unlimited 3 daily pasta available. Â I had 3 helping and I was done. Their Â wine list is extensive with different ranges of pricing. Â I was so overwhelmed with choices, the waitress asked what our preferences were and she recommended a bunch of them. I was glad the train I needed was a nice walk away because I needed to walk off all the delicious food I packed in.
I eat here once a week. I dont need to say much more

overrated.. like some others have said, its spinach/artichoke dip on a thick cardboardy crust. Â its not a bad combination, and if you want a filling carby and gooey meal after a late night of drinking or what not, it can definitely fit the bill. Â  but its not exactly the revelation in culinary artistry that some people are making it out to be. i'd put this in the same category that i put my white castle cravings in (and i like white castle!). Â it has a unique taste and texture appeal, but after a few bites you realize 1) it may not sit too well in your stomach and 2) you're probably going to be eating more than you really should be (which is 3-4 white castle burgers, or about 1/2 - 2/3 of the slice).

I love this place. Â  My first trip here was June 2012, when I mistakenly ordered the vegetarian ramen and found it mediocre, so I didn't return for quite a while. The ramen craze hit me this past year, when I found myself constantly eating ramen: the ramen burger shop that just opened right next to my apartment, bowls and bowls of take-out ramen in the office, a revival of Shin ramen when we discovered we could buy bulk on seamless. So naturally, I went back to Ippudo - and oh it is delicious! Â The way they layer the oils within the broth is to die for. Â The quality of ingredients, whether it is cha-shu, bamboo shoots, or a perfectly boiled egg, is filled with character. Â The chewiness and freshness of the noodles paired with an extra helping of hot sauce and you've got one good bowl of ramen. In addition to ramen, I often get the shishito peppers. Â Flash fried and dipped in the bit of yuzu salt, the peppers speak of juiciness and flavor. Â I'm also crazy for the Lady M crepe cake for dessert, of which they pair the most perfect scoop of ice-cream or housemade cream. The wait can be dreadful, but the good thing is that they will call you when your table is ready, so you can wander around and drink first ("Life is short - drink alcohol first") People say Ippudo is over-rated but I just can't get over Ippudo. Â Think this is just another love story.

I've been here several times with my wife. The place is warm and inviting. I get their fish taco and the burger every time I go to breakroom. The burger is one of the best burgers I've ever had. Their tempura onion rings are one of my favorites. Great place for a quick meal!

I really want to give Pure 3.5 stars but since that isn't an option I'm just going to round down only because I felt very rushed here. I am a local and I know that everything in NY is rush-rush but the waitresses kept coming over to ask if we were done and then gave us dirty looks as we sat and talked while lingering over our meals. The food was good. The decor is super cute. Maybe it is better during lunch or an off hour when there is less of a crowd?
A Haiku: Lombardi's Pizza True coal oven perfection The sauce makes me weep

Thoroughly enjoyed my visit with my wife, Danielle and our friends Jeff and Grace to Northern Spy Food Co., we started with the Southern Fried Chicken Livers with buttermilk mint dressing with arugula salad. The best fried chicken livers I have had, simple and tasty. For dinner I had the Hudson Valley pork with lentils, cheddar, and zucchini. I found the taste of the pork to be on point, not the best pork I have ever had (I recently went to a pig roast, and the standard was set) but nevertheless delicious. Danielle got the best plate of the night, she had the Polenta & baked eggs. The dish was just the right amount of rich, and one of our first experience with baked eggs worked for us! Lastly, the goat's milk cheesecake with blueberries was not only unique, but delicious. A good indicator of how good the dessert is, it lasted all but 60 seconds on the table. Loved it and recommend it!

Food was good! Ordered crab legs-had to ask for crackers, didn't receive a small fork or knife to cut nor did we get towelettes at the end!! Server didn't speak English very well but worst part-I was scammed on total price of Bill and didn't find out until I received and alert from my bank!! Bill was $84.92 and they deducted $109.92 called my bank and they credited the amount!
Give it two stars because 1) good service and 2) kinda fun. Â But the quality of the food / seafood is really bad.... That's all. Â Maybe now is the the right season.

Found this place on yelp and so happy it steered me in the right direction once again! I was looking for a nice, chill spot to celebrate my sister's birthday that had to have good vegan options (she's a vegan). Found this place and called to see if the accept reservations (they do) and they were super friendly. They were incredibly accommodating when I asked if I could get some dessert brought out at the end of the meal- they brought together most of the staff out to sing happy birthday (really sweet! and the other diners were really cool too and joined in. Nice atmosphere). The food was REALLY good (and Im not vegan). Had the Raw Almond shake (sweet enough and delicious), black bean sweet potato cakes were great as well, veggie burger was solid, and the lasagna was savory and perfectly balanced. Huge portions too (get what you pay for!) Vegan ice cream and brownie was delicious, too. I HIGHLY recommend it!

Overrated and too crowded. While this dumpling joint probably has more table seating than any dumpling restaurant in the Chinatown/LES area (why tables are so rare at this type of place is beyond me, because some of those places certainly have enough space to fit some tables and chairs in), you probably won't get a seat because it's ridiculously crowded for what it is - a cheap dumpling joint whose food is no different from any of the other hundred cheap dumpling joints in the Chinatown/LES area. The one time I came here, I had to wait something like 20 minutes just for my order of dumplings to be ready, and by the time I got back to my seat it had been occupied by a flannel-wearing couple, despite leaving my coat on the chair. The ambiance is really not great so you probably won't want to eat here anyway - fluorescent lighting that's mostly blocked off by all the people standing around waiting for their dumpling orders. Do yourself a favor, avoid the crowds, and get cheap dumplings at...any other cheap dumpling place within a block of this place. The food will be the same, and you'll still be taking it home or eating at a counter.

If you're downtown and craving Thai food, go to Pinto. The restaurant itself has an inconspicuous awning that leads into a small, but chic/modern restaurant. The food here is awesome, and you can't get much better than their $8 lunch prefixe with generously sized entrees.

I've been back to Joya a few times, both dining in and for carry out, and the food just hasn't been up to par. The moo kraprow I had a few weeks ago was overcooked; the pork pieces were tough and dry. And the carry out tofu kraprow (I like what I like, okay?) was in a weaksauce if I've ever seen one. I've still heard that it's the best thai you can get in Cobble Hill, but I'm thinking I probably won't be back for a while.

Always been a fan of Pommes Frites. Â Always wondered whats the big deal with Belgian fries, the answer is a lot. Went in to this tiny local that looks like a tavern, and ordered a double. Then having to decide what sauce I was going to dip, the fries in. Â So I got the combo ( three sauces for $2.50). Blue Cheese Dressing because you can't go wrong with that, Wild Mushroom Mayo, and Smoked Eggplant Mayo. Sat down; as the dude brought the cone with, the immense amount of fries and the hole, which drips the oil, which their isn't really any of, and begin dipping the fries into the sauces. Blue Cheese with fries is great, the smokey flavor of the sauce is amazing with, the fries, and the wild mushroom is delicious looks like "Grey Poupon", but tastes much better. Although, Pommes Frites is tiny and seats 15 at most. Â It's always busy and the combination of the fries, and sauces make it worth standing in a really tight space.

Ippudo NY NY: East Village, Manhattan 1pm Friday 16th May 2014 Four-ish Stars There was a 35 minute wait which was always surprising for Ramen since the place is very burn and turn type of restaurant. Â The Service was great with 3 hostesses and plenty of hustling waiters, bussers, & cooks. Â We order and got our food in minutes. Â I had the Karaka Men with a Nitamago. Â  [1 being the least amount of X and 10 being the most amount of X (not the rating of)] The Tonkostu Broth: 7/10 for Fattiness; 6/10 for Soup Oil; 8/10 for flavor The Skinny Noodles: Â  5/10 for Doneness; 6/10 for flavor The Pork: 2/10 for Juiciness; 6/10 for flavor Toppings: 9.5/10 for the Soft Boiled Egg, 8/10 for the Spicy Paste; Overall it was good but not really worth the price or wait.

The staff is so friendly and so attentive. Interior: love the rustic feel and intimate settings of the table. Like many Yelpers mentioned, this place is called Feast because the idea is to share dishes together. So the setting of the restaurant features long tables/joint tables. You may even rub elbows with people you don't know. Anyway, came here with a party of 6. We were there really early on a Friday, 6pm so it wasn't packed at all. It does get very crowded by around 8pm that they had to start turning away people. So on to the food. We were able to sample everything. The menu changes based on what's in season. But this is great because you're always guaranteed to try something new and fresh. Â The menu is also broken up into tastings - so if you're a seafood lover, a lot of dishes will feature in-season fish, shellfish, etc. Here is what we were able to sample (we got extras on top of the prix fixe): Beet ravioli - goat cheese, olive crumble, orange -- Not a fan of beets but I love this combo. It's so delicate. Slices of beet envelope the olive crumble and goat cheese. LOVE this. Leek Tart - smoked shitake, frisee -- So comforting. It's salty and "meaty" from the mushroom and then the pastry is so light and buttery. My favorite item on the menu. Carrot Risotto - asparagus, crispy poached egg -- Perfectly poached egg but didn't like this dish only because I'm a carrot hater. Stuffed Artichoke - tabouleh salad -- Nothing too special Scallop sliders - celery relish, pickled mustard sea -- I didn't eat this Stuffed squash blossom - bbq pulled pork -- Ok this is SO interesting. It's a squash blossom (looks like a flower) and the inside is stuffed with BBQ pork. They fry the flower (blossom) portion. SO good! Crispy pig ears - arugula, blackberry -- Yum, who would've thought this combo would be tasty. The salty pig ears, bitter/peppery arugula and sweet blackberry just played together very well. Bacon and egg - pork belly, grits, quail egg -- I really loved the quail egg and the pork belly, but I felt like it needed a little more oopmh. Also this sits on top of a pastry tart. House charcuterie, pickles, cognac mustard -- Pickled charcuterie board of carrots, radish, beets, onions Berkshire pork tenderloin - root beer glazed apples -- Tender and very unique taste because of the root beer. I wouldn't say I liked it but it was interesting to taste. Not usually a fan of sweet and savory flavors. Potato gnocchi - mangalitsa ham, broccoli rabe -- Really enjoyed the gnocchi. So fresh and light. Stuffed cabbage - trotter fried rice -- Nothing special, least favorite Mushroom and green beans -- Very fresh green beans and the mushroom.. not sure what kind it is but so delicious DESSERTS (disclosure: not a desserts/sweets person AT ALL) chocolate profiterole - bacon brittle -- VERY interesting. I actually liked this. I'm not chef so I'll break this down in layman terms. Chocolate brownie/cake type thing, vanilla ice cream, chocolate fudge and sprinkles of fried (?) bacon. So tasty. I was shocked at the dance it did in my mouth. Beignets - truffle, caramel, jam sauces on the side -- Ate the beignets by itself, again, do not like sweets and it's very light, and crispy. Buttermilk panna cotta - summer berries chambord -- Too sweet for me. It was because of the berry mixture. Kind of like jam with berries on top of custard.

Tried the food here more than half a year ago but still memorable. Definitely a long one hour wait that night and everyone squeezed through the small one and a half foot size of a door to get in and out. When asked what entrees were not spicy, they said none. Apparently, the chef loves to put a little bit of spice in all dishes renderable of this action. So only after ordering a hot pot that I thought was not spicy, I found everything was spicy. It is wonderful for vegetable lovers though because the ratio of vegetables to meat in the hot pot is 4 to 1 --recommended try out of everything on the menu. This Japanese hot pot reminds me of a Korean ramen hot pot in Pocha 32 but both are very different in their own ways.
Better than average pizza. Not really sure what else to say lol.

I love this place!!!! The service was great and the food was delicious. They had at least 16 beers on tap and 6 bottled beers. I had the special. It was a pork pastrami with portobello mushroom, fried onion, serricha on rye bread ($11). All really good! Oh and I almost for got truffle fries ($2 extra)!!! Also really good. If youre looking for a a chill place Â to drink with tasty food... This is it!!!
Great food! Cheap easy and quick( if there's no line). Definitely must have when I visit the city.

Went for Sunday brunch and was immediately enchanted by the vibe here, which was most welcoming on a cold, damp wintery day. Â Helena who greeted us is pure joy and our wait staff, though busy, could not have been more accommodating. I wanted all Â the baked goods in the place (homemade scones, doughnuts, muffins), but held off because I had to try the sweet potato waffle with fried chicken and redeye gravy. Generally, I'm not a big redeye gravy fan, so I had it on the side. This dish is delicious and filling. Â And I thoroughly enjoyed the gravy!! Â The coffee is perc'd--can you believe it. Â Loved it. Just wish I could have eaten more. Â Go with a group who likes to share so you can sample lots of dishes. I will be back!!

Why oh why did this place have to open only a few weeks before I moved out of the neighborhood? Amazingly fresh banh mi- the pork and the sardine banh mis are to die for. The baguettes are perfectly toasted, lending that nice crunch when you bite down, with the soft interior perfectly bringing out the crisp of daikon and carrots. The spring rolls here are good, and the boba is less than thrilling, but who cares? Come for the banh mi!
I honestly LOVE this place sexy cozy gr8 service I just wish they had more wines by the class WoW Macaroni Incredible Pork with grits!! Def 1 of my Favs in the city

Love it! Â I've always liked Calle Ocho, the atmosphere, the drinks, the food but when I went last night for a friend's "Yaay, The Divorce is Final" dinner and it was amazing! Â Carolina and Andre - two servers made the evening so special for all of us. Â They kept the drinks and the food comnig and celebrated with us! Â This place is great for a group of friends to come just for drinks and appetizers, a nice dinner or a big celebration! Â  Â Oh, and we were told that they have $5 mojitos on Mondays and free Sangria (they have fabulous sangria) on Sundays.

This place has gone downhill since the last time I visited. My two friends and I went on a Tuesday night around 6pm. I was surprise to find that there was no wait for once (bad sign). The snobby waiter squeezed us into a 2ft by 2ft table meant for 2 people after we waited by the door for 5mins. There was barely any space for us to eat comfortably. I attempted to take the table next to us where no one sat in the whole time, but the waiter push it back over right away. We wait about 15mins before we got water. I was midway eating my dry corn and she decide to take our appetizer plate away and bring the tacos. The three entree plates barely fitted on our table so I left my cup of water on the table next to us. The waiter came over and attempted to take it away. She made me move it to behind the seat (who does that?). Not to mention our taco was not even warm and she was trying to rush us out of there. The waitress is really unbelievable and made uncomfortable during the whole so we ate quickly and left. You are better off just ordering your food to go next door.

I would say I'm a fan. I've been here a handful of times just to look around, grab a cappuccino, flip through the books, pick up a few things. It's totally a foodie temple for all things Italian. Their breads, produce, fresh pasta, and butcher shop all look amazing! I'm sure some of their stuff are priced slightly higher than the supermarket, but hey, go to the supermarket then, or don't buy it. You really can't beat the selection here. I haven't tried any of the restaurants in here, other than Birreria, their rooftop beer garden, so I can't say much about them. It may get crowded at times especially on the weekend, but hey, it's just like the sidewalks of New York, you're just going to have to deal with it.

I came for brunch on a Saturday. The chilaquiles were delicious. They were very busy and the service was still good. I actually sat (by myself) at the bar and watched how hard they worked to serve everyone. I love the fact that they have so many gluten free options. I can't wait to come back to this place. But I hope they put one of those contraptions up by the door to block all the cold air coming in. (Oh, and install a purse hook at the bar.) Until next time!

This is one of those places where you can't go wrong with anything on the menu. Everything I had was really well balanced in flavor. The style is tapas, small plates so I would recommend three or more plates per person. If you share everything, as you usually go, the "bites" are prepared accordingly. This is especially true (and I highly recommend this) in the chef's-choice-tasting-menu which includes 9 courses plus 2 dessert courses for $40/person. Oh and bacon bits on donuts bites, amazing. Check it out.

Try the Afton punch, so good and packs the right amount of punch. I am not convinced by the hype, I prefer a nearby restaurant/bar more than this as their selection feels very limited. Also the fact they do not have any desserts!! Why!?!?

The beautiful French speaking waitresses made up for the flimsy plastic high top chairs and tiny table space of our sort of homely makeshift terrace spot. Â  The faded peach and light blue striped umbrellas outside were like an ugly Nice tourist trap, where inside was like a more cottagey French bistrot. Â  We were craving a cheese plate and this place on an off side street was nicely quiet for prime time dining time on a Friday night. Â The place seemed very "college" but in that category - very good. Â  We just had the cheese but the menu looked good with many offerings. Good value with Euro vibe gets the fourth star.

Impressive - location, decor, service, food - the Yelp reviews as always did not let me down ... wow, the place was truly impressive. We asked the waitress what her favorite dishes were and that's what we went with...I wish I could spell it out for you but I have no clue, chicken something something and pasta something something. We also had meatballs as appetizer and a couple of beers that were local, which I absolutely loved. The prices for NYC were fair and I got exactly what I paid for - lot's of good food. I will be back - there were many more selections on that menu that sounded delicious. Last note, the restaurant was very very busy - get reservations if possible - good vibe throughout the entire restaurant.

Sorry all. Â Not quite sure what my problem was but I was less than wow'd by Amy Ruth's. All signs seemed to point to Amy Ruth's (including Yelp) whenever anyone heard that we were in Harlem. We arrived for a relatively early Sunday dinner...about 5 -ish. We were seated upstairs (as opposed to up front near the window) and it was kinda stuffy. Â I think I was still getting used to the humidity of NYC (having just come from Los Angeles) a day before. My first problem was that service was a bit slow...make that a bit too slow. Â It took a while to get our drink order (they didn't really have anything that wasn't super sweet - I'm diabetic). Â Then took a while for them to take our dinner order which can be a problem when you have a kid who is headed down the Low Blood Sugar Expressway. Â Then, they Â took a while to actually bring the food. I had the "Monte Barrett" catfish, mac n cheese and fries with a glass of water. None of it was great. Â The catfish was cooked well but was pretty bland. Â The fries were fine. And I didn't even finish the mac n cheese. A lot of my impression had to do with the AMAZING meal that we'd had at Melba's the night before. Â So, soul food as a follow up to soul food was probably a bad call. Yes, Amy Ruth's is probably much more authentic. Â I just was not impressed in any way, shape or form. Â It's not that I'm not open to soul food. Â I really do like Roscoe's Chicken n Waffles here in Los Angeles(pretty much anything on their menu)...to a much higher degree than Amy Ruth's. I certainly don't think Amy Ruth's is bad. Â It's just that, in my book, there are too many options in NYC to make Amy Ruth's my first choice.

So since this place does not accept reservations and I have come here and had been told there was over a hour wait, I decided to call ahead this, and was informed that there was no wait. I live one block up, but in the five minutes it took to walk here that no wait somehow turned into a 30 minute wait. Other than that, the service is really good and the servers very friendly. Not a huge drink list, and I think the Sapporo is kind of expensive, at $6.50 a glass when else where you can get a half pint for $2.50. The food is amazing though. All the skewers, especially the skirt steak and chicken oysters is just delicious and so juicy and flavorful. The pickled kimchi is delectable! The char grilled chicken started out sort of bland, til I realized all of the seasoning and sauce was at the bottom of the bowl, and once mixed up, with the egg as well, was also very good. As most Japanese restaurants, sitting at the bar is always fun and it is interesting to watch the chefs prepare food. Good decor and ambiance as well. Little room though, and it gets crowded, but overall good experience. Well worth future visits.

ABC Kitchen was the most creative food experience I had on this trip to NY. Â I thought it was even more creative than Blue Hill, with the same farm to table concept. Â The toast with ramps and goat cheese was a standout, along with the sugar snap pea salad. They had about 4 fish entrees, 1 fried chicken and 1 pork. Â I ended up with a pasta entree with spring vegetables and peccorino cheese that was good. The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars was that the restaurant was so noisy! Â I liked the music they played, but the volume level was more like a club than a restaurant. Then when you add in the noise generated by the patrons it was actually difficult to converse with the people at your table.

Came here around 3:30 on a sat. The wait was about 20 min. We got a small pizza with sweet Italian sausage, mushrooms and homemade meatballs. Didn't really care for the sausage. The meatballs was good. Wish we had gotten the spinach instead of the sausage. I can't say that it's the best I've had...but it's on the list of my top pizza places.

Black Label Burger. Do it. Jesse D. and I went on vacation and found ourselves at Minetta Tavern in NYC on a Wednesday night. This place is beautiful inside. It is very classy and antique looking. We sat at the bar, which was incredibly crowded. The staff handled it well and they were very friendly. The bartenders were amazing and you could tell they really feel passionately about their craft. They play the BEST tunes in here... 70's R&B was all I heard and I was super happy because it is my favorite! The best! We had seen some food show talk about how the Black Label Burger was on the best burgers in the US, so we of course HAD to try it. It was the best burger of my life. We started our meal with one of their appetizer specials. It was a ravioli thing, which was delicious, but not a do again. I wish we would have rocked the bone marrow! Then our burgers came. The burger is made of a blend of four meats, all prime grade beef. From what I've seen on TV/in articles on the internet, the meats are ribeye, NY strip, brisket, and skirt steak... ratios unknown. Gotta keep this perfect recipe a secret! It is coated in butter while cooking and topped ONLY with caramelized onions. It comes with lettuce and tomato, but leave that off. The combination of the buttery bun with the perfectly cooked meat and sweet caramelized onions is perfect and nothing else needs to be added or changed. This burger is a must. I was so happy while eating this... it was heaven. The greatest burger I've EVER had. For dessert, we had a delicious apple tart thing. It was warm and buttery and served with a side of crÃ¨me fraÃ®che. Jesse is typically not a fan of desserts, but he actually said he wanted to try to make this on his own he loved it so much. Next time I'm in NYC, I'm treating myself to another BLB from Minetta Tavern!

You could probably walk through Park Slope and lose count of the trendy Thai places you pass after only a few blocks. First off, you should have better things to be doing than counting things like a little child. Second off, very few establishments out of this Thai restaurant surplus in the area are actually any good. Song is one of these few. Mighty good, at that, as well as mighty affordable. The Homemade Chicken Curry Puffs appetizer are a clear stand-out, despite having not yet been called up for a spot on the everyday menu, but appearing rather as part of the specials (which still seems to be the same roster each day, mind you - semantics, I know). Curry is a far cry from being a buzzword for me the way prosciutto, duck, and fried are (some people have a sweet tooth, I have a really salty tooth), so I was a bit surprised myself how much I loved these hot and tasty, meat-filled pastry pockets the first time I tried them. And since then, they've remained a staple with each visit. Face your curry demons! Embrace the curry flavor! Anyway. The Fried Calamari is another worthy appetizer, for sure. You may not think much about ordering them at first. Then, you will see table after table around you with huge piles of squid goodness and be food-envied into flagging down the waiter to tack just one more item onto the bill. Lightly breaded, and served with a very nice Thai sweet chili sauce, the small, at $4.25, is more than enough for two people. And trust me - this is coming from a recovering glutton. I've been in a dark, fat place before, people. Then there's the Pad Thai. The biggest portion of Pad Thai I've ever had at any Thai joint. Seriously, I feel like a giant dump truck of noodles had to back up and unload itself onto my plate before it was brought to the table. I think the technical measurement here is a shit-ton. I don't know, I don't speak Metric system. But this shit-ton of Pad Thai is delicious, having seemingly found that wonderful, much sought-after happy medium between too soupy and not enough sauce. Plus, it's $6.95 and sure to yield leftovers for tomorrow's lunch. The staff, however, is something else. The host will barely acknowledge you, and when your table is ready, he will not say a word even when asked a direct question, he will walk no more than two steps away from the front bar, and he will simply point you to your table from across the room. He even hands the menus off to some server or busboy to bring to you well after you've been seated. Rough day at the office, I see. And while it doesn't get much better with the servers, I'm afraid, I really can't hold cold, stand-offish service entirely against Song as a whole. I've grown accustomed to the notion that the cooler-than-thou robotic antics of the staff are to be expected and it's always good for a laugh or two as part of the experience. Song is perfect for entertaining friends not from the area. Its stark yet chic interior, outdoor patio, full bar, and occasional DJ set can paint a pretty impressive picture of what the hood has to offer, if that's how you aim to show off The Slope to some new folks. That, and you won't be subjecting them to typical New York prices. Song is easily my favorite Thai restaurant in the area and certainly on the short list city-wide. You should go. I've just given you a shit-ton of reasons to get yourself there, after all.

Been wanting to try this place for a while considering that it's high on all the tourists' list of must eat in nyc. Wasn't exactly planning to eat at Grimaldi's that night but after walking the Brooklyn bridge with D and saw only 2 ppl in line, we thought hey why the hell not? usually the wait is 2 hrs! We ordered a small margarita pizza which came in 6 slices. The pizza was good but definitely had better at lombardi and john's in West village. Would eat the pizza again if there is no wait but would never ever ever stand in line for 2 hrs for this. Average at best.

I live a few blocks from cafe. This place is always crowded. Yesterday I was craving a nice dessert after dinner. And I walked in there asked if I can have dessert and latte. The waitress suggested me try the chocolate pudding... Soooo good!! I will come back for the amazing chocolate pudding again.

How can I not have reviewed Il Corallo yet?! I've been there a billion times (ok, maybe only 40) -- but I LOVE them. It's a family-run seeming restaurant. The same maitre'd at the front of the restaurant every time I come. The pastas and pizza are amazing and so affordable. Two giant pages of pasta options, so an enormous amount to choose from. I think nothing on the menu is over $16, including the seafood-heavy pastas. I mean lobster pasta for $16 -- wow. Wine too, super cheap. And the portion sizes are pretty substantial, and you should definitely have enough to take home. Absolutely nothing not to love, if you're looking for a casual low-key italian joint. One note - they won't let you sit until your full party is there, so be prepared.

I came here on Saturday night to pick up some food - really great experience. Â As soon as I walked in, someone who worked at the restaurant caught me looking confused and explained the ordering process (really easy - just walk to the back, wait in line, order delicious meat). Â There was a 20-minute wait but a waitress was walking around taking drink orders while you stood in line. Â The place is huge with lots of seating, and an awesome live band was playing. Â When it came time to order, I got the pork belly, the brisket and the baby back ribs - all were amazing. Â Perfectly tender with amazing spiced crusts. Â The potato salad was fantastic and vinegar-y, and the coleslaw was also great (not slathered in mayo like at other places!). Â The BBQ sauces were also tremendous - there is one that kind of tastes like sriracha :) Â I took my food to go, but next time I want to come here and have a few drinks, listen to some live music, and maybe dance a little :p

I thought I was over the mac and cheese trend that's been going 10 years strong in "diners" across NYC but this mac and cheese revitalized my love for cheesy carbs. First of all it's made with orzo, so there's actually more cheese than usual. That sounds bad, but it's balanced out with chopped broccoli. I'll throw broccoli in my mac and cheese at home but this is the first time I've had it in a restaurant and I respect that. It's like they aren't afraid of cooking like they're at home. Plus the truffle-cheese sauce is the most intense sauce you'll ever eat. You will scrape the bowl clean. Btw the brussels sprouts with chili jam are the best you'll ever eat. I was fighting with my date over them. The vibe is super romantic at night. Dark, quiet and cozy. Just like you want it to be.

Went here with a group on a Friday night. Made a reservation for 5 on OpenTable 1 hour prior and was seated immediately. Nice atmosphere, just busy enough to feel lively but not enough to slow down service. The build your own burger selection was awesome (brie on a burger!), as were the truffle fries. Nice selection of beers at reasonable prices. The dining area is nicely separated from the bar so it's a little quieter.

With 300 reviews, do I really need to write my own!? Â YES! Balthazar was recommended to me by one of my hipster friends, so I was a little surprised when I showed up and found such a swanky, pricey, place for brunch! Â I guess that goes to show that Balthazar appeals to all kinds. Â  I was a tourist, but I was there with a local so I'm not sure if that really counts as being overrun with tourists. Â But, who really cares...isn't all of NYC overrun with tourists? Â  Got a huge delish latte an order of eggs benedict with the smoked salmon. Â I expected it to taste different than a typical e.b. but it really tasted pretty much the same! Â Very good nonetheless! The best thing about Balthazar would have to be the ambiance and the energy.

Great ambiance. Â The place has a simple Japanese decor. Â Perfect for relax and talk with friends. Â  They serve small appetizers as well as desserts too. Â Love their tea selection. Â The menu even has a brief history and map of where each types of teas are grown. Â I like their cold sencha on a hot summer day. Â My favorite is the chocolate souffle with raspberry, so good...

I've been here before a year back and it was really good back then. Â I came with a bunch of friends for a late dinner for a 9:45 reservation. For starters, we ordered the tuna sashimi salad which was awesome. Â The tuna was fresh and the sauce was a delicious peanut buttery-sesame flavor. Â We had the gyoza afterwards which looked more like lumpias than gyozas. Â Nothing spectacular about them-they were crispy and good and the ponzu sauce was as expected. Â We ordered the dish of the cold pig's feet appetizer plate that came with a cumin-like sauce. Â I thought it was just alright. Â I'm not a big fan of cold cuts, and the sauce didn't quite mix in well with the cold cut. Â Finally, the warm pig's feet came, but this one also disappointed. Â I remembered the last time I had it, the outside was crispy. Â This time, the outside had a chewy crispy with mostly fatty and cartilage. Â I guess the sauce tasted well with it. Â  The highlight was the garlic fried rice with diced pork feet. Â I couldn't really taste the garlic, but the fatty pig's feet were good. We ordered the boiling soup that came with scallions? pork belly, bacon and peppers. Â This one was just ok because the bacon and whatever broth they pour into the pot was really salty. Â Tasted like they threw 10 MSG ramen packets into the pot. Â When the noodles were added in, I was hoping it'll help make it less salty, but it didn't. Â So disappointing.

$5 A SLICE? Â WTF. Â i am sorry, but i can make a better whole pie for myself for that money. Â c'mon for real. Â i can't believe all the hype that the hipster crowd from the boondocks of the midwest have generated for this place. Â it's only pizza for chrissakes, and for crying out loud, we're talking about brooklyn, right? Â there is good pizza all over the place. Â y'all can oggle all you want about it, wait in line for a bite and overpay for the privilege. Â i am done with this establishment, will never spend another interminable minute or small fortune for a burnt slice again.

The good: -- free flamenco show on Thursdays and Saturdays at 8pm and 10pm -- delicious food -- amazing sangria choices -- good location in the trendy East Village The bad: -- can get crowded during flamenco shows -- forget to have a conversation during the flamenco shows -- service can be average (a bit slow at times) -- can get expensive, but not too expensive

After my first visit from early on, experiencing what I considered "slow service" we made a second trip this past Monday night. Â  For a Monday at 9pm they were pretty much full and vibe was very Soho scene. Â  Wife and I split a Truffle Burger that we had read so much about and loved it. Â  Not sure how they only charge $45 given the amount of shaved truffle on top but let's hope they don't jack up the price now. Â  Also shared a chopped salad and the tuna tartare as we were not that hungry and sampled the wine on tap, which was decent, especially for only $8. Â  I see from the Yelper below he was upset because they would not take a rez but they would not take ours either. Â It's a walk-in restaurant not a burger joint a la Shake Shack or BLT Burger. Â  Sounds like you got a bad phone girl but my bet is you might be surprised if you saw it.
Best PIZZA in NYC! and that's saying a lot because there so great places to good pizza in the city. My favorite is the Hawaiian Pizza they make it's do die for!

I came here with a friend on a Friday evening. We got there a bit before 6 and the place was already half full, which was incredible since the place is quite large. We still got seated immediately one one of the tables in the back (feels a bit stuffy though, so if you can, I recommend that you either sit outside or in the front bar area). First, we ordered 4 kinds of pickles to share: special sour cukes, hot sour cukes, big dill kosher cukes and sweet & spicy carrots. They were all very delicious, despite the fact that I usually don't even enjoy pickles that much. They were quite large in portion too, so we ended up finishing less than 1/3 of it or so (But we bagged them, so no wasted pickles there!) For entree, I got the mushroom gravy smothered chicken biscuit sandwiches. It was possibly one of the tastiest things I've had in the city. The chicken was crispy on the outside and juicy and moist on the inside; the biscuit was moist and fluffy; the gravy was very rich and creamy; and the mushrooms were perfectly cooked. The cheese grits served on the side were absolutely delicious as well. I enjoyed every single bite of that dish, but I couldn't finish it because the portion is just so huge! I also got to try a bit of my friend's Turkey Leg, which was great as well: the meat was juicy and perfectly cooked, and the mashed potatoes and cranberry sauce served on the side were delicious as well. Overall, this place has some of the best southern comfort food in the city. The staff is very friendly and responsive. It's on the more expensive side, but the portion is huge enough to make up for it. The only complaint I have is that this place fills up really quickly and there is often a very long wait. I recommend that you come here early with a small group of people (or make a reservation if you have a large enough group).

The pizza's pretty good but based upon some of the other reviews here you'd think that it causes multiple orgasms upon touching your tongue, gives you the confidence to quit your shitty job as a baby-sitter to a successful Manhattanite power-couple to pursue your dream as an avant-guard spoken word performance artist and clear up that breakout of pimples on your face just in time for the weekend. It's good pizza, and "unique" because they are small just a little bit more than what one person can eat pies, but there's lots of good pizza all over New York and novelty is so whatever. What makes the place enjoyable is the ambiance the decor and outside seating area sets off. Yes, it's an interesting juxtaposition from what you'd expect, but this doesn't really surprise me as that's kind of par for the area.
