That said I've always had good service here, the beer selection if great and I recommend eating here to other people. That said I've only had the pizza here. One day, maybe after my confrontational spoken word performance art gets turned into a one-person off-Broadway hit, I'll try some of the other food that sounds delicious but I have reservations about paying that much for.

I went to Traif for the first time with my wife last night. Â  We had a 6 PM reservation, though we had to wait a few minutes because they were a bit late in opening. Â But once we made it in we had the dining experience of our lives, amazing enough that I am now more reluctant than ever to spring for fancy restaurants like Per Se, Daniel and others of that ilk. Â I am quite worried that I would pay double or triple or more and get food that is not nearly as good as this. Â  We ordered 6 savory dishes, 2 cocktails, a glass of wine and 2 desserts between the two of us, and finished every bite and every drop. Â The portions are small, and the place is consequently not as cheap as it looks (we spent almost $150 all-in between the two of us), but it was more than worth it for the quality. Â Dish by dish it was lentil soup free starter - incredible. Â  bacon-wrapped stuff dates - Absolutely amazing, nothing like this anywhere else seared scallops - merely excellent, the weakest of the bunch strawberry-cinnamon ribs - mind-blowing, best ribs of all time Maine lobster and sea urchin on potato - Awesome, even my wife loved it, and she hates seafood. Â  Short rib sliders with sweet potato fries - best of either we've ever had by far Seared foie gras, potatoes and egg - absolutely phenomenal. Bacon doughnuts, coffee ice cream - I loved it, my wife liked it. Â  key lime pie - gold standard, awesome. Â  The fact that I can remember all that we ate is amazing in itself. Â At even the best restaurants I will usually remember and talk about 1 or maybe 2 things afterward on a very good night. Â But here we had 5 or 6 plates on the same table that were that good. Â  The atmosphere is mostly fairly plain. Â It's a small place, and we ate in the very nice back "garden" room, which is enclosed during the winter. Â The service was friendly and helpful. Â But in this place, more than almost any other I have been to, it's really all about the food.

Being in The Setai (5 Star Hotel), this restaurant is the absolute perfect addition to the hotel. The stairs to walk up begin in a spiral glass staircase, which is absolutely phenomenal. Really gives you that elegant feel, then you are greeted by one of the most modern and elegant bars that are to man kind. The drinks are great, it's not so crowded and the group of people are pretty upscale. I had a table for 4 at this place with my girlfriend and another couple and can I just say the service was phenomenal? The maitre d was fantastic at explaining the menu and offering their chef's welcome. I went with the Lobster Bisque as an appetizer for the start of my 4 course meal, best Lobster Bisque I ever had. It was so rich, flavorful and bold. Continued was the ravioli and I didn't know they could make ravioli this good, you could tell it was just genuine and as close to Italy as you could get. They could have done a little better on the portions however. Next I had the foie gras as my entree and although a little more saltier than I'd like, it was pretty darn good. To finish off, I had their chocolate disc with golden flakes over pomegranate and a side of ice cream. Pretty creative. They pay pretty good attention to what the level of your drinks are, with quick refills, quick serving and retrieval of dishes. My friend flicked a crumb off the table as a joke and they promptly saw and cleaned the table. Great place!
No guacamole Unless you order a steak Not so Mexican
Went back again, it's always reliable for great dishes, attentive service, and a nice cozy atmosphere. One of my neighborhood go-to places!

I nabbed a lunchtime reservation on the Friday before Christmas and they were very accommodating when I asked to change my 2 PM reservation to 2:30 PM since we were running late. When I arrived I discovered that my lunch partner was running even LATER and the hostess politely let me know that we had to order before the kitchen closes at 3 PM. Sure - how long would it take to get from FiDi to Minetta Tavern on a Friday at 2ish in a cab? A long time, apparently! My friend finally made it through the door at 2:50 PM just as I was prepared to order for the both of us. Timing win! We were seated and our waitress rushed over to take our order. We decided to split the Bone Marrow & Black Label Burger (cooked Medium since we were told they undercook). Our waitress was one of the sweetest waitresses I've ever encountered. She checked up on us multiple times, always with a warm tone and a smile :) The food looked amazing when it came out! The portions are rather large and we never even finished our bone marrow. The burger was cooked to perfection (although to be honest I couldn't really tell the difference between the Black Label and a regular burger...) and the fries were a nice crispy golden. The place was packed when we were here and for good reason. The walls are all adorned with caricatures of celebs and the red booths added to the old fashioned atmosphere. Lovely food and service makes me a definite fan!

My coworker came into work last week raving about The Meatball Shop - she of course prefaced her detailed experience with, "yes there is veggie for you, no I didn't try it but you must go there!" So I did. Aside from Momofuku Noodle Bar, I'm not a big fan of no reservation restaurants. 1) I'm 300 points from my $50 OpenTable gift card 2) I don't have the patience to wait around. I really had a feeling this was going to be worth the wait. We arrived at 6:30 and were told it was going to be a one and a half hour wait and they took my cell # and told me they'd call me. Interesting concept - I don't have to stand on top of people waiting and I can go grab a drink down the block. So that's exactly what we did. One and a half hours later and two rounds of drinks at The Living Room, I called The Meatball Shop and was told another half hour. We slowly strolled back over and stood on top of the table that was clearly going to be ours. So yes, at 9pm we were seated after two and a half hours of waiting. This food better be worth it, is all I could think. Our waitress came over, gave us the rundown of how the menu and ordering works and we ooh-ed and aah-ed over the many options. I was a bit nervous about the veggie meatballs - she said they were bean based and had mushrooms and I was not feeling that. I just really hate mushrooms and am so particular about my veggie burgers I wasn't sure this was the right move but I was reminded that I was at The Meatball Shop and I had to try the meatballs. Their market vegetable special of the day was brussel sprouts (let the salivating begin...) with onions, apples and candied walnuts. Yes, please. Unreal. I asked the hostess (who I went from hating to loving) what she recommended I ordered and the snappy waitress jumped in and said "I'm your waitress, I can help you"...so she gave her recommendation and I didn't take it. Filled out the dry erase menu with my dry erase pen (um, love) and decided on meatballs over rigatoni with marinara sauce and obviously the side of brussel guys. Food came out fairly quickly and we all stopped talking and focused on food. I enjoyed the meatballs but can't say I'd get them again - I'm just so not thrilled with the consistency when it contains beans and mushrooms. The rigatoni was el-dente and had extra delicious sauce. But really, the highlight of the meal were the brussel sprouts. SO flavorful and perfectly cooked and just an amazing combo of ingredients mixed with it. I could have had a larger portion of that instead. My friends loved the risotto with prosciutto and all of their (actual) meatballs. They barely ate the spinach and were quite disappointed in that. I tried their mashed potatoes which were tasty as well. Oh gosh, we had to save room for dessert? We decided we all needed to try different things. I had the brownie cookie with the mint ice cream sandwich. It wasn't your typical mint, it was like a mojito. I'm not even an ice cream fan and I was really impressed by the deliciousness of this dessert. The meal was $80 for 4 of us which considering the long wait and the totally worth-wile food was completely worth it. If and when I go back, I will probably steer clear from the (veggie)meatballs and will stick to the pastas, veggies, sides and such. Highly recommend this place overall.
Always a good vibe and excellent food. Warsaw Mule followed by braised rabbit followed by fig pudding cake covered in warm salted Carmel sauce and topped with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Stellar.

First of all, I may be a bit biased because I loved Harold on Top Chef. Â That being said, I was still impressed with my meal, the restaurant, the service and basically my whole experience at Perilla because I believe it takes more than just a good chef to create an overall pleasant dining experience. I ordered the crispy calamari appetizer, the duck breast entree and the peanut butter mousse dessert (read: heaven). Â  Everything was made to perfection. The service was beyond excellent, our waiter was accommodating, informed and very attentive. Â  I wholly recommend Perilla.

We went there on Friday at around 8pm. They don't take reservation if it's less than 4 people, so we were a little worried about availability, but there are many available seats around that time. It got more crowded as the night gets darker. It was a bit loud and was hard to hear each other, but the food was delicious and service was good! I loved their mussels!

This place used to be awesome. I went to their new place and i was super disappointed. The fun vibe and the sangria bar is gone. Yes they will serve unlimited sangria but its just not the same. The food has also gone done. The burrito used to the size of a chipolte burrito and now its more like the size of a tamale and not as tastey. Why fix something if its not broken? Used to be my favorite brunch spot but i wont go back :(

What's more perfect than a piping hot bowl of noodles on a cold NYC night? NOTHING. Duh! My friend and I decided to eat here for dinner on a Friday night and we came here early. We got there about 10 minutes before they opened because it seems like a really popular place and we didn't want to risk a long wait. Despite being early, there were already people waiting in line in front of the restaurant. Though, once they opened, they seated people one after another in a timely manner. As we were being lead to our table, I noticed that there was an area where they kind of showcase the making of their noodles. There was someone there flattening the dough and probably preparing more noodles for the night. It's great to know that the noodles that they serve are hand made! I actually decided to go with their regular sized Kamo Nanban, which is their sauteed duck with green onions. As for the noodles, I decided on the udon since I like the taste of udon better than soba. This bowl of noodles was piping hot and it was such a great feeling when I'm having it on a cold night. It was wonderful. The sauteed duck was pretty good and what's great bout it is that each slice has a slither of duck fat with it, which gives it great flavor as you chew .. and chew .. The noodles itself was really delicious. It was perfectly cooked. Pure comfort. However, the broth that went with my udon was a little bit too tangy for my taste. And the price is a bit steep for udon. I understand that you're getting quality with the price but a regular sized bowl of Kamo Nanban was almost $17. Yikes! Â I've been to a restaurant before where they also had hand made udon and their prices were much less than Soba-ya's! Though, overall, it was delicious. It was great on a cold night. And I'd really recommend it.

A 24hr Latin styled eatery serving cheap sandwiches and ceviches paired with good drinks to match. It has a lovely dinner vibe but imagine it feeling very clean, the staff is helpful and check in often to make sure you are enjoying yourself. Place is great for brunch/lunch/dinner/middle of the night. I would have to recommend trying the oxtail empanadas, tuna melt, or any of the ceviches.

I LOVE chicken and waffles. I truly do. I've had it all over the country...Atlanta, Los Angeles, New Orleans, etc. So when I heard about Amy Ruth's, I knew that I had to come check it out. Walking into the restaurant, I was already feeling pretty good about the place. Sat down and was given a fantastic warm bread with butter and jam. Made my order of the "Al Sharpton", following the advice of the other yelp reviews. It took a while to get some service, but I did not mind. The food came out quickly, and what did I think upon sinking my teeth into this soul food? Fried chicken: GREAT. Waffle: meh. Honestly, it seemed kind of generic...not crispy but a little soggy. The flavor was just okay and definitely needed the syrup to give it a little something. Thank goodness for the fried chicken. My friend thought the same thing. Roscoe's Chicken and Waffles in Los Angeles is still my standard for great C&W, and Amy Ruth's just didn't quite give me the same experience. Will I go again? Maybe...if friends wanted me to go, but would I go on my own again? I don't know.
Great food, awesome staff, couldn't be happier to have stumbled upon this Brooklyn gem

the food was stellar, however trying to relay i had an allergy was nearly impossible. the message was unfortunately lost in translation. conclusion? i highly recommend, to all the non-allergy sufferers.

A neighborhood joint. Probably fine for a beer and a burger--the draft beer menu looked mighty fine. The rest of the menu was not so great. My spicy grilled squid appetizer was properly spicy and sauced, but the squid itself was rubbery without the slightest speck of char--disappointing. The mussels were plump and flavorful, but the broth was dishwater like with random pieces of chopped onion. My spouse who is pickier than I am about what she eats managed her way through the meal, but we won't be making this a regular stop though it Â is close by. Quite noisy inside, perhaps better outside when the weather permits.
you get what you expect: lots of meatballs. Â a little gimmicky, but fine in a pinch.

Halal Guys: We were in a hurry and ordered the chicken in a wrap and falafel in a wrap. Â The chicken was moist and generous, came with lettuce and white sauce. Â The falafel was flavorful but sort of dry, also with lettuce and white sauce. We also opted for containers of red hot sauce - definitely do that if you can handle hot. It was delicious with it. After finishing, we wish we had had time to order the chicken and rice plate instead because we thought the rice would have really rounded out the flavors and meal overall. Superbly priced for the quantity and quality, only $4 each. There was a somewhat intimidating line, but their system gets you in and out in a jiffy.

This is one of the original cantonese noodle place back in the days when there weren't too many around. Â The food was quick and simple, selections from noodles, roast duck, chicken and ribs, and some typical cantonese dishes. Â Given the fact that there are so many similar place like it these days, Â I've been there too many times to prove myself that I won't go back there considering the lack of hygience and service, in addtion to horrible attitude (one of the old female cashier got the nastiest attitude even though i asked politely). I mean everyone knows you goto most chinese restaurants for food, not service, but I refuse to pay for nasty attitudes. Â The reason it's getting 2 stars is the food is original, and it opens late.
my boyfriend and i tried artichoke pizza today. it was little salty and crust is too thick. since I'm a big fan of bleecker st. pizza, i was not that impressed.
I'm pretty sure they sprinkle crack in pulled pork. No seriously, easily the best pulled pork in NYC...possibly the best quick food in the ny.
It was a surprise to find this place in the Financial District on seamless. Â Their salads are great. Â I have had two and plan to get more.

Vietnamese sandwich shop with a MODERN take.. don't expect the classics start yourself a loyalty card if you think you might become a regular! ---joju monster: YUM, packed with meat & packed with flavor THEN they add an egg... half the sandwich was enough for me so i'm glad i shared with Long K.. interestingly they use BBQ pork nem nuong sausage instead of the bbq pork i'm used to ---loaded kimchi fries: nice crispiness but too overloaded with spicy mayo.. maybe ask for it on the side? ---frozen vietnamese coffee with coffee jelly: standard, nothing special but you'll need it for the food induced coma! ---vegetable spring rolls: these deep fried babies were also tasty NOTE: no minimum on credit card!! PLUS 10% student discount!
Shared the sea food linguini with white sauce. Was delicious. Lobster was slightly overcooked, otherwise would have been perfect. Nice bread choices. Way too much food for even two people.

I love this restaurant. Â It is the perfect place to unwind mid week. Â They have an insane oyster happy hour, the food is incredible, the crowd is non existent, and the service is perfect! Â The staff is very knowledgable about their menu and wine list and helped us pick the best meal! Â The must try is the polenta. Â Best polenta I've ever tasted. Â And that's no exaggeration. Â I will definitely be returning!

I cannot say enough great things about Montmartre! I recently moved to the neighborhood and this has become one of my regular spots for many reasons. The food is delicious - everything from the chicken and waffles at brunch to the mussels and the burger for dinner. Let's discuss the burger, shall we? Possibly one of the best in the city! Amazing melty goodness of perfectly flavored beef with creamy spinach and the perfect ratio of cheese on toast. A MUST. I've also indulged in the cote de boeuf dish for two and that was one of the most amazing meals I have had in a while. In warm weather their patio is one of the best in the city, a great laid back vibe, small enough for an intimate dinner with friends but large enough that you can usually get a seat with little wait. Overall the staff at this place is awesome, they make you feel like you're an old friend even if it's your first visit. Justin the host is incredibly welcoming and friendly and Matt the bar tender makes awesome cocktails. Whether you are sitting at the bar for a quick bite or in the dining room for dinner, service is top notch. Go here, now.

The food, ambience, and service here are superb. I came on a saturday night (~7PM), was expecting to wait in line, but was seated immediately (wait.. what? there was NO line??) in a cute booth with side by side seating right behind the bar. It was the perfect view - my BF and I could watch the chefs at work on their masterpieces and we had plenty of arm space. We ordered: 1) pretzel with cheese/butter dip - tasted fresh out the oven, was on the saltier side - but we just easily scrapped off the salt, and the dip was perfectly creamy 2) emmentaler sausage - comes with a sausage with cheese bits and interesting peppered flavoring, dumplings on the side, and flavored cabbage. LOVED this dish 3) Reuben sandwich - came out hot, cheesy, crunchy, and it was totes filling Heard this place expanded 2x, so maybe that explains the short wait to get seated. It looked like it fit about 50-60 ppl and accommodating to large groups too. Service is super friendly and QUICK!

Jeepney So I have a hard time to decide which Filipino restaurant is my fave. Jeepney is on the top of my list. I have never had a bad item here. Â My fave is the Bicol express. It's a juicy grilled pork loin with Filipino coconut curry on top. Served with their famous coconut rice. Nothing can compare! The burger is also one of the best in town! The meat is juicy and melts in your mouth, Served on a toasted bun with an egg on top?!?! It's amazing! Their tacilog is also really good, Grilled pork sausage links that is sweet and crunchy! Just writing this makes me hungry. Maybe I'll come here for dinner tomorrow. This place is super popular (and yes, Â they do deserve all the recognition) , so make sure you make a reservation in advance or expect to wait over an hour .

4.5 Stars Let me start by saying it's always a nice surprise when you're at the bar waiting for your table and Bobby Flay is sitting there just doing some paper work like nothing... Getting right to it, this place is damn good. Â Broke the meal down into 3 courses... 1) Started with the "Bar menu" course... sitting at a table you would think that it's only for the bar seats but it's not. Â This is a section where you order 3 items and they come out on a dish in 1-2 bite size portions (depending on how big your trap is)... Went for the Eggplant, Pumpkin Arancini and the Chorizo... Eggplant was killer, chorizo was good and Arancini was disappointing... 2) Octopus... Here's the thing... I've eaten Octopus 9,000 times (appx) and this is probably the best I've ever had... Nuff said. 3) Entree was the KALE AND WILD MUSHROOM PAELLA CRISPY ARTICHOKES... Everyone says they're known for it, so had to give it a shot, glad I did... I also tried the duck which was very good, but a little heavy on the Pomegranate for me. Service was on point as well... I appreciate that Like I said, the place is aces. Â Looking forward to my next go around.

So I went to Hagi for a Black Friday dinner for eight people. Originally, the host said 1 hour 30 minutes to be seated with everyone or 1 hour for two tables of four. Luckily for us, after waiting for 1 hr (or more like, me waiting for an hour for everyone else to come), we were all seated. My friends loved the food. The seasoning was just right and it was definitely authentic. It was nice that I could get authentic Japanese food/ tapas without going all the way down to St. Mark's. The food was delicious. The soft-shell crab was by far my favorite. The curry yaki udon was good too. Kara age and the fried squid was chewy yet tender. I highly recommend this place! Just keep in mind that you have to wait at least 30 minutes to be seated.

I really can't add much more to what's been said about Cafe Habana's grilled corn on a stick. Â It truly is a damn good, super buttery, extremely cheesy, and abundant stick of juicy white corn. Â It's a must-have when coming to Cafe Habana. For our entrees, I had the Camarones al Ajillo (shrimp in spicy garlic sauce) and the SO had the Pollo Mirador (sauteed chicken in roasted garlic sauce). Â Both of our dishes were really good. Â We were a bit hesitant when the SO's chicken dish was brought out (bland-looking chicken fillets in a white sauce), but the dish was far from bland. Â The garlic sauce was delicious. Â My shrimp was perfectly spicy and I sopped up every grain of rice in the sauce. Our wait was surprisingly only 20 minutes long on a Monday night (around 8pm). Â But New Yorkers love to eat late, because when we left at around 9:30, the line was twice as long as when we arrived. Â The service is extremely friendly, despite the constant busyness and close quarters in the restaurant. Â I know I'd go crazy working there, but all 3 servers working that night had nothing but smiles on their faces. Â I couldn't have asked for a better Cuban dining experience!

This place is really good, I've been 3 times in the past two weeks. Â It's a great addition to the dearth of food 9th Avenue and west in the mid 30's. Â The pizzas really are great. I'm docking a full two stars because of their soda and iced tea refill policy. Â Iced tea and sodas are $3.00 each - understood you need to make up the margins in food service somewhere. Â But to charge for refills - absolutely inexcusable. Â Especially when the servers ask "want a little more iced tea?"

What a fantastic place! As someone who used to live right near Greektown in Chicago, and has visited Greece, I am a bit picky about my Greek food. This place really does Greek food right- everything was delicious! The only reason they are getting four stars is that I wasn't wowed by the service. If they just take up the personality a nothc, I would give them five stars.
This was the best pizza I've had in my life. I was miserable waiting in line for nearly 2 hours, but it was all worth it in the end.

Came here tonight with the girlfriend. Very laid back atmosphere. Tiny inside, so not ideal for larger groups. Service was attentive and incredibly fast. I had the Philly Cheese Brisket Sandwich with a side of Mac and Cheese. Girlfriend had the 50/50 sandwich (half brisket, half pulled pork) with a side of the cornbread. The Philly was delicious. Definitely my favorite item of the meal, whereas my girlfriend didn't enjoy mine. The mac and cheese was ok, nothing special. My girlfriend's sandwich was also very good, but a little dry and needed some sauce. There is barbecue and other sauces available at the table. The cornbread was also pretty good, but very dry. It comes with a honey-butter, which actually tasted like honey, but in a butter form. (Many other "honey-butters" I've had in the past didn't have much, if any, honey flavor to them.) Sandwiches all come with a pickle and slaw. Neither of us liked the slaw. To go with my meal, I had their organic diet cola. It was almost as good as Diet Coke, so I was pleased. The prices were very good (under $40 for the two of us, pre-tip). From the moment we walked in, to the moment we walked out, the entire meal and all took only 35 minutes. If it was more than 5 minutes between us placing our order and having the sandwiches set in front of us, I'd be shocked. It was just that fast. We were also offered a slice of Apple Cake on the house for dessert, but we were in a hurry and declined. Nice offer though, I must say. So, if you're looking for a quick, cheap meal, Butcher Bar is a pretty solid choice in Astoria.

Came in with a friend the other day, after realizing this hidden gem had newly opened. Â Great friendly service,was waited on nearly 30 seconds after I sat down. The staff were all very courteous. The portions were huge for what you would pay for in other places. The food was fantastic. Be sure to try the tortas. I had the torta al pastor. Pork, avocado, onions and pineapple. It was delicious. Also try the agua fresca. Would definitely come here at least several times a week.

I was here last week with friends and this place has a nice quirky charm. They have a great selection of craft brews, so that's always exciting. We ordered food and it was pretty good. I got the house burger and it was huge and pretty tasty. They put sage on it, which is pretty weird, but good otherwise. My dining partners got the tomato soup with grilled cheese and the muscles with frittes and both seemed pleased.

Last week I was in NYC for several days. Wednesday night I met two of my best friends at this restaurant which was selected by one of those friends who is in the food industry in Manhattan and has a highly discriminating palate. This is one of her favorites. We had a fabulous bottle of wine recommended by the bartender. The pasta was possibly the best I have ever had. Cooked perfectly, seasoned perfectly, and gluten free option for the celiac among us. The salad with squash, ricotta , greens and the house cured meat was divine. My girlfriends had the beets in pistachios and loved it. The tartufo is everything and more that has been reported in Yelp. It was a fun scene, very hip, very New York, we had a blast plus had amazing food. Couldn't WAIT to bring my husband and daughter there for dinner Friday night! We had a reservation and were seated right away in one of those tables meant for two people and all 3 of us are large people- I'm 5'10, my husband 6 feet! I felt like I was sitting at a child's table and we were all cramped and uncomfortable. Didn't mind the close proximity to other diners but the MUSIC! What was that? It was an assault! Some kind of weird piercing rock music. Dreadful! Unfortunately the kitchen really screwed up our food order and we had to wait forever for our food. They offered us a glass of wine to compensate but we were already drinking a bottle and really were starving. Unfortunately then the food came all at once.(apps, pasta, primi-there wasn't room on the small table!) My husband was not happy and I was embarrassed Â because I had insisted we go there and had raved about it ! With all the fabulous choices in Manhattan we would have had a better experience almost anywhere. I would go back and eat at the bar again with my friends but not in the dining room-very unfortunate.

THEIR CHICKEN IS EVERYTHING YOU EVER NEED TO TRY IN LIFE. Â Seriously. It's so juicy and tender, it'll turn vegetarians into meat lovers. I came here twice was not disappointed either time. However, I would say that their special dipping sauce isn't all that "special" I liked the chicken the way it was. To compliment the chicken, you'd probably want to try their jalapeno mac and cheese. It had quite a kick, but it was a delicious kick. I went back the second time to get the regular mac n cheese and it just didn't seem something too out of the ordinary. Jalapeno Mac & Chicken- GET IT

My new favorite Indian restaurant! Busy, but worth the wait. We had the madula chicken appetizer (so yummy), chicken tikka, tandoori chicken, garlic naan, and lamb curry. Everything was delicious, and the service was friendly. Good stuff!

Great place for brunch or dinner. The bar is very pleasant to sit at and sip some good wine if you need to wait for your table. The bathrooms are interestingly located in the back of the restaurant past the kitchen, which is all open for you to look at. I kind of like that. Bathrooms are here: sitorsquat.com/sitorsquaâ€¦

We came here late, after twelve on a Saturday night. Had the pigeon ("squab", if you want to be fancy about it, but the menu refers to it as pigeon.) It was moist, very dark meat, served in a flavorful sauce. Oysters, bone marrow, beer and cocktails are also real strongpoints of Blue Ribbon.

This place is the ultimate brunch spot. Came here for Sunday brunch with my roommate and, after waiting a good 25 minutes, we sat inside their cozy yet fresh, rustic-style dining area. I got the Norwegian brunch combo, and she got the poached eggs and salmon. I loved my dish: the salmon was fresh and the hollandaise was perfect. She also loved hers, and the portions were both big enough to give you that wonderful, slightly-overstuffed brunch feeling. My only gripe was that the orange juice that comes with the brunch special is a laughable, shot-glass sized amount. Other than that, the cappuccino that's also included was good, so no complaints there. After hearing about this place for forever, I'm very glad I tried it and would definitely come back again.

Yelp says it is family friendly but it really isn't. PlAce is cramped, no kids menus and no good alternates for kids if they don't like BBQ. Service is sporadic, it took a long time for them to get us water or take our order. Yet once they brought us food, they rushed to get us out. It was busy tonight but I imagine this is pretty normal on a Saturday night. Lastly the food was very average yet pricey. 32 for a very small dish of kalbi, not much on the menu is less than 25....disappointing

Everything about this place was excellent, except the food wasn't seasonal at all. Â It was excellent food -- roast chicken, pork face, date cate -- but in the heat of July it wasn't refreshing. Â The staff obviously knows this; our menu was labeled "Winter/Spring 2013." Perfect for a drink, or a steaming dinner on a cool night.
I have to admit, I came here for a beer and not expecting much else but the burgers are surprisingly amazing!

This is the only time I don't mind getting ripped off by hipsters. Â The food is good, drinks are okay, service is AMZING. Â They take reservations for 6+, and we were seated promptly. Â This has became my go to place for fun, relaxing brunch (we even had a baby in our party and it was a-okay).

I came to the Jane for brunch on a Sunday morning. Â When the eggs benedict first arrived in my mouth, it definitely rattled my tongue and immediately notified my receptors in my brain saying, "HELLO, REALLY GOOD EGGS BENEDICT IN YOUR MOUTH RIGHT NOW". Â  I had the benedict Jane and my boyfriend had the benedict Johnny. Â The Jane comes with crab cakes and tarragon hollandaise, the Johnny comes with corn bread and sun dried tomato hollandaise. Â I love crab cakes, he loves corn bread, so it was a perfect order for us. Â  The home fries were really delicious. Â A smidgen spicy, seasoned with paprika, other spices, and finely sliced onions. Â Perfectly crispy on the outside, warm and soft on the inside. Why 4 stars since I seem to be RAVING about this place? Â I didn't have a food orgasm, so I have to reserve the 5th star for that experience. Â The Jane is definitely a great place for some good quality brunch! Â Make sure to have a reservation. Â It's loud in there, so keep conversations to a minimum, and just keep eating!

Loved this place! Went for the first time at noon on a Sunday expecting a long wait but was pleasantly surprised that the two of us were seated within 5 minutes. The interior is nicely decorated with modern clean lines, minimal but still a little stylish. Like they were trying but not trying too hard. Anyways, we ordered 2 ramens - the shiromaru and the akamaru. We both got an egg to go on top. Everything came out piping hot and absolutely delicious. The soup was flavorful and the noodles were quite chewy, almost al dente but softer. The overall taste was excellent and I would say it rivals ramen on the west coast. Will definitely be back!

This place is the best! The most welcoming, fun, carefree environment I've experienced in New York. First off, Â Sunny is the best! He made sure we had the best table in the joint and only because I think he heard it was my birthday from one of my friends in passing. From that point on, he made sure the rest of the night was nothing but a blast!!! I came in expecting to have a cocktail and a quick bite but we ended up staying all night. Sarah Elizabeth, our server, was the BEST server I've ever had in my entire life. She is so full of life, energy and such a great spirit, I could have stayed there all night. This place has the feeling of a 50's dinner in heaven. I felt like I was in a movie or musical like Grease! They made my night truly magical! Thank you to Sunny, Sarah and the HILARIOUS hosts/hostesses with mostesses who won't even wait for you to ask, but snatch the camera out of your hand to take a picture of your group. Would any other restaurant in NY do this? NO! Thank you Cafeteria! You not only made my night, but made me appreciate humanity with your humility! I'll be back to New York soon, thanks to you! XOXOXOX
Great food Great atmosphere The best crepes and sandwiches. Â We all had a great time. Â We will be back especially for the nutella crepe and the smoked salmon sandwich.

Just order 8-13 or 14 on the appetizers menu. This will give you 2 x soup dumplings (different types) 1 x scallion pancakes 1 x cold sesame noodles 1 x fried dumplings With 3 sodas this dim sum feast for 2 will set you back only $44 dollars including tip, and trust me, it's more than enough food. Don't expect this to be a romantic dinner though. I went with my fiance and they seated us after a 30 minute wait they seated us at a table with 9 other people. Everyone else finished before us and they started a 4 person cleaning the rest of the table furiously, so we finished our last dumpling and scrammed. Still a GREAT experience!! CASH ONLY!!!

Great BBQ - =) Long Waits - =( Would eat here a lot more often if I didn't have to wait hours in line. Everything is amazing but I especially like the Smoked Pork Belly I have to give them 5 stars because of the food, its worth all 5 stars, giving them less is just wrong. They definitely need to do something about the lines, seating and takeout situation.

Wow. Chef Vinny is a master. His dinner tasting menu last week was phenomenal. I can honestly say it was the first tasting menu that made me feel like I was on an exciting journey--each course so different from the next, incorporating ingredients like thistles that made me taste scallops in a whole way. Even dessert which I can usually do without could not be missed. The menu apparently changes every night so I'll be back again and again.

Amazing burritos. Similar to Chipotle in ordering style, and just as delicious. Quality ingredients, reasonable prices. I generally stick with the burrito bowl, and always opt for the $0.92 guacamole add on.

This place is amazing. Arepas are just as good as the cart. Â Staff is really fun and nice. Â The fruit juices are also great, fresh, Â and delicious. Â Arepas con queso was the real star though; it was soft, delicious and buttery and piping fresh. Â Worth the hype!
Best diner I've been to in a while! Banana walnut pancakes were off the hook! Recommend to go early. After 12 pm, line out the door!

Knowing the story of the original Grimaldi's we ventured to Patsy's new restaurant named after his mother Julianna. The food was outstanding, the service superb and to this very day pat tends to his patrons as if they were family. We were so surprised that patsy still works in the kitchen and cares so much about his product and customers. If you loved the original Grimaldi's then Julianna's will not disappoint.

This place is absolutely one of my favorite restaurants in the city. Terrific seafood at a reasonable price. It's intimate but not tiny. Â Service:The service is usually great. I've never waited more than 20 minutes for a table. Knowledgeable servers and pretty decent wine selection. Food: The salmon is excellent, as are the scallops, flounder with cheddar grits, soft shell crab, the lobster special, the buffalo shrimp is outstanding. The oyster po boy is pretty good. The scallop ceviche is outstanding. Not a fan of the lobster Mac&cheese or the lobster mashed potatoes. All in all great spot.

so good!!!!!! i love it!!!!! the must tries: pecan pie french toast and cheddar waffle. the brunch comes with rither a mimosa, juice or a bloody mary. coffee is extra. still worth it! there is a wait though. when you see a wait, you know its good. i love the place, the way it looks, the laid back sunday ambiance. only thing i found strange was that the patrons were kinda dressed up for a sunday brunch. in any case, i enjoyed my meal there. i will definitely go back!

I'm in love with the cactus tacos!!! Hand made tortillas right in front of you. Long line but moves fast. Great place to grab a nice little snack. Don't forget to add a squeeze of lime to your taco - Mmm enjoy!
Lame! Their rice is dry and their lines are long. Skip the wait and get the decent halal over moist yellow rice two blocks up at 55th and 6th ave.
always good and never disappoints. Â Stick to the basics and you'll be all good.

First time trying filipino food and it was great! Came here with a date and started off with the balut and some red wine. We were nervous about trying the balut but it just ended up tasting like hard boiled egg. The broth inside tasted like chicken broth so it wasn't as weird as I thought it would be. I had the oxtail while my date had the prawns. We loved both dishes but the peanut butter sauce mine came in was very overpowering, I would have liked for it to be a little more mild. The meat fell right off the bone and both entrees came with a side of rice. No ube ice cream, which was disappointing as I've always wanted to try it, but we did share the mango cheesecake which was small but delicious. It's not terribly pricey but probably pricey for what you are getting since everything is pretty basic. Overall, I would recommend this for filipino food but I do want to try other filipino restaurants.

Can be hard to get in on the weekends, but you can always take a vermicelli salad to go and sit in Washington Square park. Â The salads are really fresh and nice. Â Their Pho is ok, probably the best I have had in Manhattan, but still a long way from what you can get in Asia. Â Needs more herbs in it for a start.

After reading all the hypes of this place, I came for brunch. At 1pm, there was a short wait. Got the duck hash and the frittata- brussel spout w/ red onion, egg and cheese. The complimentary bread came out. I think I got cheated out of it. I got 2 carrot bread cake and 1 croissant and no side butter or jam to go with it. Sadly disappointed. Duck hash came with duck, nut, cranberry or raisin, shredded duck and 2 sunnyside egg and side potatoes. The flavor tasted like Moroccan--raisin and nut together with a protein. The duck itself was very dry but I see why people like this. It's the combination of salty, sweet, crunchy all together in a bite. $12 --- it's filling but kind of pricey. The frittata today was brussel spouts. Nothing special. Just a regular thick omelet filled with chucks of brussel spouts and cheese. After a few bites in, it gets really monotone. It also came with toast with butter and side potatoes. Side potatoes is better than the diners---baked, crunchy, and flavor okay. $9 The staff are all polite and attentive--especially if you order coffee, they come around often to refill your cup. For breakfast, this isn't worth the price. Maybe if it came with a drink and some bacon or meat then it might be worth it.

Each piece of their of cake can be considered a bit pricey, but for their huge, volumy portion, it may make sense(in fact their cake comes with 2 folks). You can't eat full meal after this. I tried the cheese cake with strawberry, and all kinds of layered cheese cake (Devil's food, carrot, chocolate mousse), and the chocolate mousse is my favorite so far. I feel like I can buy something similar to their strawberry cheese cake elsewhere... The staff there(shop) is one of the least friendly kinds(Not everybody? I was just unlucky? I always feel almost depressed with the depressed staff working there...).

The quality of food has declined since my last visit. The octopus was too soft and mushy. The spanish omelet was overcooked and I couldn't even finish it because it was so dry. The potatoes with aioli was good. The other dishes I had were not memorable. And skip the chocolate cake. The wine-soaked pear was good, but nothing special. Sucks that I have to find a new go-to tapas place with consistent quality.
Yup, It's worth it.

Sat at the bar for a quick dinner on a Saturday night. Once those waiting for dinner leave. It's actually quiet peaceful. Grilled salmon was very nice with medium doneness. Reasonable at $27. My only complaint is feeling slightly rushed by the barback. Bartender was spectacular. French press coffee was delicious. Another tip for those who prefer bottled water, they make filtered tap water in flat and sparkling. I try to avoid tap water in America, so it wasn't a choice for me.

Solid 4 stars. I actually didnt know lombardis was a famous pizza place until some1 told me so i didnt really work myself up for the hype that i now know it gets. It was really good pizza and had excellent service. However, it wasnt wow. We tried 3 pizza places in ny and this one was at the top. I would say to add extra mozzerella as a topping because the pizza would have been better with it. Get the sangria to go with it. Skip the glass and just get the whole pitcher. The glass is not enough! :)

If you haven't been here yet, GO! Best crostini and panini you'll find in Queens... nAKWJEIOJFWKLAWr wow, their stuff is something else. I would advise you to be adventurous and try something on the menu that you've never heard of. Chances are, it's going to be super delicious and amazing--totally blow your socks off.

Love this place! My friends and I came here on a Tuesday evening. We had never been here but heard about it so we stopped in after seeing a show down the street. The decor is AMAZING! To die for! The food was delicious, too! I had the Shapards Pie and it was the perfect comfort food for the cold weather we've been having. The service was great, too. Very friendly staff. Whether you live in the city or are just visiting, I would HIGHLY recommend stopping into this place! It's a true hidden gem!
Great food great atmosphere ,defiantly coming back

I like this place! Drawn in from the displays on the outside, I had to try it! I got the green tea azuka berries. The presentation was very nice, but I wish that there was a little more ingredients in it, after eating the Icecream part, there wasn't much left to go with the crepe. The flavors though were all there and quite delicious. Like some other people mentioned, it may be a little hard to eat because of the cone shape. Definitely will be some mess, so take some napkins! And look for the paypal deal online.

The food is OK for comfort food, fried chicken, pastas, etc. But the only reason I go to Junior's now is because I have a sweet tooth. Junior is an amazing man for that reason... The shakes are very good! Strawberry is the one to get - and it's very thick. The coffee is gross. Go to Starbucks across the road. The cheesecakes I must say are pretty lackluster! They're drier than most in my opinion. However, the slices of red velvet from the pick-up entrance in Shubert Alley is always a winner. Warning: everything sold here is extra extra sweet! So order water. I am ashamed to walk the streets with a bright orange Junior's bag or cup because I feel like I'm being judged as a tourist. So I walk really fast, which is good given the amount of calories I am consuming whilest I run.

Only went to cross it off my bucket list. I expected it to be extremely overrated (as most joints like this are) and I was right. The ramen was delicious, flavorful and very hot. But it's ramen. It tastes just as good anywhere. This place is generally overhyped, the line is impossible to deal with (I went at 5pm on a work day, so the wait was only about 10 minutes) and the ordering process is hoity-toity and pretentious. The spicy miso paste that you order separately gave no real spice or added flavor. Try it once to try it. Then go to a cafeteria-type place for cheaper ramen and more normal people.

My three food groups are fried, baked, sugarfied. Lucky lil' me...Pies and Thighs has all 3! Judging from my Yelp reviews and dietary choices, you would probably think that I have high cholesterol, blood pressure and triglycerides...Not yet, but Pies-N-Thighs definitely has me one step closer to clogged arteries...and loving it! Hey, you only live once, might as well eat like it. In Hipsterville, tiny little venue, but tons of seating in the back, so don't be deterred, you won't have to wait too long to be seated. Plus once you give the cute, little high-pitched voice waiter your name, you won't want to leave her hanging. I got the Turkey Pot Pie with field greens and the hot apple cider. So so good. I loved every bite. The turkey was so moist, just the right amount of crunchy topping, tons of veggies (corn, peas...)... Home-cooked heaven! Rusty got the chicken biscuit and the macaroni and cheese. The mac was ok. Very cheesy. The biscuit looked good, slathered in bright red hot sauce. But he was so infatuated with it, I couldn't get one bite in! The hot cider was perfect for a cold blistery day. It must be phenomenal with any of their deserts. We were so full though that we wouldn't dare to have gotten desert. The banana cream pie that the table next to us ordered looked heavenly though. Must go back, must go back, MUST!
The best halal cart in town. Â The best---for realz. Â But you have to go either before 12pm or after 2pm...otherwise the line will lead you around the block.
Don't see the big deal :/

I have a Thai-addiction, and so I begged my friends to go out for Thai one night. This place is AWESOME and looks so fancy. I was really surprised that the prices were moderate compared to the look and feel of the restaurant. I got the chicken Pad See Ew and it was so good. My friend got the special Pad Thai, and it looked delicious as well. Would definitely recommend it!

I'd been meaning to try this place for ages. Â It was better than I could have expected. Â A friend and I went for a late dinner on a Tuesday night and the place was packed! Even so, we were quickly seated and told the specials. Â We had a special appetizer with fried oysters and local tomato salsa, delicious. Â My friend had Ribs and I had the Tofu Steak and Eggs. Â And as a vegetarian I greatly appreciate that they apply a price adjustment for substituting tofu for steak. Â Tofu is a LOT less expensive than steak. Â It's not something you find at many restaurants. Â I cleaned my freaking plate. Â And it was not a tiny portion. Â I usually leave 1/2 - 1/4 of food on my plate as good practice for portion control at a restaurant but I just couldn't resist. Go here! You will not be disappointed!

The food is amazing! I had the lobster ravioli and was impressed. Only thing is the servings are a little small and pretty pricy, but if you're feeling in the mood to be a foodie, this is the place to go. The spicy margarita was delicious as well if you like flavorful drinks. The outside seating is nice too when the weather is good, but you're sitting kind of on top of your neighbor, so it's Euro style. Still enjoyable.

The lines here aren't nearly as long as Madison Square Park (or as the one at Citi Field). Hopefully this will relieve the crowds at the other locations without itself becoming too crowded. Currently, the wait is about 20-30 minutes (including ordering + waiting for your food). There is a good amount of seating, and the turnover is pretty quick, so you should be able to enjoy your food inside the air conditioned room. The Shackburger is delicious, and a single ($4.50) is filling. To those who want to compare it to In-N-Out, Shake Shack's patties are much thicker, so the double ($7) may be a little too much food. I love their light, potato bun, the fresh onion, tomato and lettuce, and the way they cook the juicy burgers to medium.

yummy little burgers with spicy ketchups. Â last time here i tried the bacon milk shake. Â umm for a milk shake that needed to be chewed... it was the perfect salty sweet snack to help suck down the burgers.
Their sliders are perfect. I've had the bacon ones too and they are delicious. The chipotle ketchup is top notch too.
Typical food ... over rated ...not worth the long wait.

I had high hopes for this place based on A.) the 4 star review B.) my love of unassuming neighborhood joints. Unfortunately, my hopes were dashed. The menu looked very basic but that didn't deter me because my favorite haunt in my town is a pub with a basic menu but the food is very good. Our table shared the fried oysters and the chicken fingers as an appetizer. I did not try the oysters so I can't speak about them, but the chicken fingers were underwhelming. Again....yes, I know chicken fingers are not highbrow food but sophisticated fare and well seasoned/tasty are NOT mutually exclusive the last time I checked. They get props for what appeared to be fresh chunks of chicken, but they lost points for lack of flavor. The breading was boring and the chicken didn't seem to have been seasoned. They were served with a very boring and basic dish of BBQ sauce and a boring and basic dish of duck sauce. Because pretty much EVERYONE on Yelp told me to get the burger, I did. I have no idea how a burger topped with blue cheese and grilled onions can turn out tasteless, but somehow this place managed it. Usually a burger this bland can be rescued by ketchup....nope. Had to add salt and pepper. The only good thing I can say about the burger is that it was properly cooked and it was juicy. I liked the ambiance....it was like a townie bar but cooler because it's in the Village. The folks at the bar seemed to be having a good time and the bartender appeared friendly. Our server was friendly and capable so no knocks on her. The place wasn't horrible, but it was forgettable. I am glad this was a work dinner because I would have hated to pay for such a sub-par meal.
I love love love Cafeteria. Their food is great ! 4star food in a 1 star restaurant. The salmon BLT is freakin AMAZINg as is the short rib tacos. Â fresh and GREAT!

Ok, I want to put this in perspective. I had gotten up early to go for a run, then I went for a free paddle (downtown Kayak...DO IT), then I went to a trampoline weight lifting class (yeah....I know), then started to go for another run. Only to realize that I hadn't eaten and it was 2pm. SO, I whip out my trusty Yelp app to see what was in the area, and low and behold I see a review of Mooncake from Jando S. His recommendations are GOLDEN. So basically, I knew that this was IT. It's this tiny little place, and it was so empty (how empty?), that I wasn't sure it was open. BUT, they were making fresh dumplings or things at the table. I was STARVING and THIRSTY. As requested the nice waitress brought me a pitcher of water, and humoured me when I had no idea what to order. Turns out, the pork chops with tons of salad instead of rice and a side of the grilled asparagus was EXACTLY what I needed. DELICIOUS, tons of food, and all for $15. Everything on the menu looked great, and it was all fresh. If I'm in the area again, I will DEFINITELY be going there! THANKS JANDO!

This review is way overdue, but Minca definitely deserves to be reviewed. The review below is from a blog post I wrote shortly after visiting (back when I still ate meat on occasion). ----- Minca Ramen on a Sunday. We arrived at 12:30pm and were seated immediately. It started to get a little crowded about 20 minutes later. Hidden away in Alphabet City, Minca is a teensy tiny ramen shop (even smaller than Totto Ramen). The space feels authentic and comforting. They had some weird music playing - it sounded like it should be the soundtrack for an old school Nintendo game. We grabbed one of the window seats facing E 5th St. It was beautiful out. If we can't sit outside, at least we get a view of the street. Gorgeous weather, mellow neighborhood. At Minca, you can customize your ramen with thick, thin, wavy wheat, whole wheat and bean noodles. The menu also includes noodle recommendations if you can't make up your mind. We were tempted by the gyoza, but decided to stick to ramen. Someone seated near us ordered the shrimp gyoza, and it looked pretty legit. J ordered the Spicy Vegetable Miso Ramen with wavy wheat noodles ($13), which included fried tofu and vegetables for toppings. The corn and cabbage were a little unusual, but tasty with the broth. Light spiciness, intense miso flavor. This was much more miso-flavored than some ramen places. I didn't try the wavy noodles, but J enjoyed the big mouthfuls of noodles that he could really bite into. There were a lot of noodles in that bowl. A LOT. I couldn't decide between the Minca (soy sauce, pork and chicken broth) and the Basic (salt and roast garlic, pork broth). Both had been recommended in top ramen articles on foodie blogs. I ordered the Minca Sio ($10.50), which seemed like the perfect compromise. Minca Sio has the salt and garlic flavor AND the mixed pork and chicken broth. Win, win! My ramen looked like a stick of butter had melted in the broth (in a good way). Rich, creamy broth packed with burnt garlic flavor. Minca's garlic puts Hide-Chan's black garlic to shame. Disclaimer: I'm a garlic lover, so I was in garlic heaven, but this garlicky broth is not for everyone. I'm glad I got the thin noodles. Good texture, good balance of noodles and broth. Let's talk about the char siu. Pretty sure my eyes lit up as soon as I tasted the char siu. Lightly marinated. So tender and flavorful. Oh, and the fatty bits melted in my mouth. I sometimes get weirded out by really fatty char siu (like Totto Ramen's), but Minca's char siu was delish. Huge pieces with a good balance of tender meat and fat (!!!). The broth on its own wasn't that full of porky goodness, but the generous topping of char siu definitely met my porky goodness quota for ramen. The egg was on the chewy side, seemed a little overdone. Good soy sauce flavor though.

I ate here enough times to notice when they switched the bread on me. Steak Sandwich + Corn is the only route to go. I have tried the other dishes, but they just aren't up to par for this Californification gal (where we get the best Mex/Cuban food). I am not a fan of the Ciabatta they used once on the steak sandwich. It's typically served on a baguette. Maybe they ran out? Way too much bread, not enough meat. The corn is hit or miss. Â Sometimes there is more chili than sauce. Sometimes way too much sauce and not enough chilly. I'm afraid the more popular this place gets, the less quality the food is becoming. Nonetheless, you get some bang for your buck. (especially in a pricey area) Though I've been disappointed not once, but twice...I still have faith in this quaint spicy little joint. Â Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me. Â¡Ay, caramba!

The first time we went to Di Fara's, we got lucky because it was an off time and there was hardly a wait. Â This time, on a Saturday afternoon in early May, it was about an hour and ten minutes from getting on line to getting our pie. Â That is a bit ridiculous, I have to admit, especially when your waiting time is spent standing, trying in vain to get a table, with an AC unit that has seen better days. But is it worth it? Â Absolutely! Â When I finally got my hands on our half cheese and half pepperoni pizza (with the plain being my choice), the wait was forgotten and I enjoyed some of the best pizza on the planet. Â The three cheeses, the olive oil, the San Marzano tomatoes and the fresh basil (and I usually don't even like basil) all combine into one hell of a slice. Â I so wish I did not have to get on a plane to get here. You may not share the love for Di Fara's but if you have never been and you love pizza, you need to make the trek and check it out.

First off, the b/f & I ate: Totto Spicy Ramen - it wasn't too spicy but still had kick. Totto Ramen is best described as a glamorous hole in the wall. I think it seats about 15 people at most and they don't take reservations (yes, its one of THOSE places) & I think it might be cash only (but i'm not 100% positive.) & because Manhattan thrives on mom & pop shops (especially the hole in the wall kind) that offer quality and character I can see Totto Ramen lasting against competitors. Overall, I think T.R. provides a solid ramen experience. Many have commented about the chicken broth, the no msg, the limited menu, etc but I don't think this takes away from the ambiance or the quality of the food just because its unusual in comparison to what many expect. I actually think the healthier alternatives taste just as good as the shops that add the preservatives. I actually appreciated that it wasn't too salty as a result of cooking w/out MSG. Â Other than the organic/ healthier nature of the food, the restaurant still offers a great tasting bowl with a juicy slice of pork that they slice and cooked with a butane torch right in front of you (that is, if you're sitting at the bar). That being said, you're still likely to leave hungry since they don't really fill up the bowl with much else other than a few slices of pork and a sheet of seaweed. So in regards to value I don't know if this is the best value for ramen but you certainly won't be disappointed.

Everything I've eaten so far here is good! There's usually some wait to get a seat, because it's so packed, but the wait staff is awesome and friendly (even if they're swamped), the portions are generous, and everything is tasty! The waitress once, when I was there for a dinner, haggled the kitchen about making my food gluten free, which I highly appreciated! The fries once took longer than the rest of the meal, but they comped it because of the added time, which was wonderful. I'll be going here a lot in the future.

This little gem is a work of love by owner Mario and his wife Pierina who are actively running the restaurant Â and producing first rate Italian dishes. Â We enjoyed the Calamari Fritte with Fra Diavolo sauce app and the Chicken Cacciatore and veal dish entrees. Mario's home made Italian Red wine carried us thru the meal with a smile. iL Triangolo may be small in size but its Big on great food and atmosphere. We will bring friends and return soon.

One of the best happy hours in Manhattan! Its all week from 4-7. Good service, good food + AMAZING margaritas. They don't skimp on the alcohol even during happy hour. Can't say the same for many places! Love love this place!

It was a blistery blustery night, and I just wanted to throw myself into any warm room for hot food. We wandered in and had some steamed chicken dumplings (which tasted good only with a sharp tasting sauce; the table hot sauce tasted oddly sweet). The beef pulled noodles were alright for the price range. You can get a heaping meal here for the price of a large Frappuccino, so if you're short on funds, walk down the dark and dated Doyers for these cheap eats.

Food was ABSOLUTELY amazing! Started off with a pitcher of coconut mojitos!!!! YUMMY :) As appetizers I had the Sauteed garlic shrimp and beef, chicken and shrimp skewers. I can't remember the entree but I know it was chicken breast which stuffed shrimp and mozzarella cheese and some delicious sauce and mashed potatoes. I will definitely return and recommend!

It was a long wait and that was expected. As long as you are standing with good company, the wait isn't too bad. They did misjudge our wait time by more than 45 minutes so that was slightly annoying. Overall the service was okay and the space was extremely tight. There's only one bathroom so the line build up behind it so while you are eating, there's a line of people standing behind you along the wall waiting to use the bathroom. Not exactly appetizing but that's NYC for you. Of the food we ordered, the best was indeed the pancakes. Thankfully they were my mine and I enjoyed every bite of my blueberry pancakes (I did share a bit though, promise) My sister ordered a variety of sides and they were all forgettable and bland. My brother had salmon with eggs with a side salad. Â My brother cleaned his plate so he must have enjoyed it. We both ordered milkshakes and they were delicious. Cash only! My sister said next time, we'll come for dinner to have the pancakes and not have to wait as long. Breakfast for dinner sounds great in my book especially if I can avoid a two hour+ line.

Meh. Just went here with some friends in the middle of the heat wave last week. Go on a temperate day because this place is tiny and has a hard time regulating the temperature. Â The food was great but the service kinda stunk. Â We were drenched in sweat and when asking for ice for our water got 1 small cup to share amongst 4 people. Boo!! Â Also, Yelp says this place takes credit cards but thats not true... CASH ONLY! Again, food is great but the service was sorta awful and the place was uncomfortable.

Great drinks. I've been to this spot a handful of times and you can always count on it for drinks with some friends or even a date. Great playlist too. Have yet to try the food but it looks good. Next time!

Thank you yelpers!! Without your previous reviews, I couldn't have discovered this place! I got boiled dumplings, fried rice, chow mein, fried dumplings and they were all good. All under $10.00! Will be back soon.

I'll keep it simple: the pizza is excellent but be prepared to stand in line atleast for an hour and another 30 minutes before you get your food. Service is just ok. Ambiance is none. It's a cash only place. They do not sell pizza by the slice. The medium is 6 pieces and the large is 8 pieces. The medium is pretty big and would suffice for 2 people. The take out line and the line to get a table is the same. So you really don't save any time if you decide to take out. The pizza is def. Â worth the wait. I'll go again!!!

I categorized pretty much all pizza places in FiDi as being second rate. Â Especially ones in 'gimmicky' areas. Â Stone street is a fine line between 'gimmicky' and a neighborhood feel. Â The ability to sit outside greatly amplified the already good experience and plan to go back. Margherita pizza was good and not crazy filling.

As someone originally from North Texas, I grew up with a lot of Louisiana cooking so I was looking forward to trying this place. Interior is cute and I went around Halloween and loved the extra decorations. Â  My boyfriend got the jambalaya which he was pretty happy with. Â I sampled it a bit and thought it was rather flavorful. I got the fried chicken which I was not as thrilled with as being that I was served a breast piece, it was overcooked and a bit dry inside. Â It could have been an off night however and I was hungry so I ate away. I was satisfied enough to want to return to try out their brunch soon.

First of all, you need to know that I am a Nepali, which means that I will probably have a biased opinion towards food. Second, I like spicy food, I mean spicy in Nepali (or Indian) kind of way. The place is cheap for Manhattan, but maybe not as cheap as other Nepali restaurants in Queens. My favorite place for momos (easily the most popular dish for non-resident Nepalis) is Bhim's in Queens, which is very cheap too. I liked the momo, especially the sauce. I loved the chicken chilly! The food was very spicy and very tasty. However, after recommending the place to my (Nepali) friends, they were not as impressed as I was. The owner was friendly as we had a nice chat for a while. Why go there: If you want great tasting (spicy) food, which is cheap, and is BYOB, going there with close friends can be a great experience!
Service was great. The gnocchi, chicken, bolonese Â  was amazing. Highly recommended!
What's there to say that hasn't already been said over three THOUSAND times. Â It's the best. Â PERIOD. But don't forget extra white sauce!

i hate to go against the grain here, esp since majority of the 800+ reviews for Joe's Shanghai seem to be glowing. moved near Chinatown, and found Joe's off yelp. got the infamous #1 - pork/crab buns (aka: soup dumplings). delicious, but wasn't BLOWN AWAY like everyone else seems to be. maybe there is a slight bias there, since chinese cuisine isn't my #1. also, this was my first Xiao Long Bao experience, so I also didn't have anything to compare it to. all in all, i would recommend.

When my girlfriend casually said something about Jamaican food to a Jamaican friend, the Jamaican friend insisted that we go to The Islands. Â The Jamaican friend is awesome, and I owe her a cookie. The other reviews cover most of the highlights... The Islands is a very small, quirky place with a treacherous staircase leading to a seating area that makes me feel like I've accidentally stepped into somebody's dollhouse. Â It's one of the few places in this world where I actually feel tall. I showed up with three friends at 1pm on a Tuesday, and the seating area was closed, but the gentleman at the counter let us crowd around the bar for lunch. Â We shared jerk chicken (great, though not the best I've ever had), stew chicken (jerk's mellower, gravier brother... probably the best I've ever had), goat curry (don't fear the goat--it's gamey, but really tasty), and stew peas. As soon as I ordered the stew peas, I wondered what the heck I was thinking. Â It's a bunch of beans and peas with bits of corn and carrots. Â How could that possibly be exciting? Â Actually, I really wanted to order the okra and codfish, but they were out. Â Crappy. Â So we were stuck with stew peas, as our token vegetarian entree. Crazy part is that the stew peas were ridiculously amazing, probably even better than the stew chicken or the curry goat. Â Who knew that a creamy-looking puddle of kidney beans could taste so good? Â  When I asked the server/cook what spices were in the stew peas, he said, very slowly: Â "Beans. Â Peas. Â Carrots. Â Flour. Â Pepper. Â Regular pepper. Â Jamaican pepper." I have no idea what he meant by "Jamaican pepper," but I'm definitely a fan.

Great beers on tap and fun cocktails, but otherwise pretty heavy menu full of good ole fried southern food. Â Not quite my cup of tea, but fun to take friends looking to catch up over drinks. Â Regular pickles were tasty but would not recommend the fried pickles - too battered, too oily, too hot, and too whole! Â Fried pickle slices probably would have had more of a crunchy bite and better proportions (not to mention aesthetic). Â Definitely not a (cardiac) diet friendly place...
Seriously amazing food. Order the schnitzel, get a spatzle to split and a bottle of Rotes Haus GV. It will knock your socks off.
At 1 dollar for 5 dumplings I never want a homeless person to tell me they're hungry ever again......

We loved the attentive but unobtrusive service. The food was definately good, but I didn't get the feeling that it had a "signature" theme - I could have been anywhere. I will go back. It was in a great part of town as well.

The one and only place to be if you are heading to see a show at the Bowery Ballroom! It's located right next to it - can't be any easier. One Mile House is a great craft beer spot with delicious food. The place itself is big and even has a small garden in the back. The service is friendly, polite and reasonably quick. Given that it's right next to a big venue space, this place is spacious. I noticed that the vibe changes depending on the crowd - when we went before the show, it was mellow and chill but after the show, it got loud and a little rowdy. However, as it was spacious, it didn't feel crowded with the sudden influx of people. They have an extensive draft and beer menu, as well as a cocktail list. The food menu is good too, with a good selection of vegetarian-friendly shared plates. The Mexican Flatbread had a good spicy kick to it, the Lemon Scented Artichoke-Spinach Dip with baked pita chips was heavenly, Sliders had perfectly juicy medium-rare patties and the Croquettes, while good were not as memorable. Don't even bother looking at other bars in the neighborhood when you're going to the Bowery Ballroom. This spot has it all.

Don't come to this place hungry! Â By far the longest Â line and wait for food. Â We were in a line outside the pizzeria for about an hour and a half. Â Now you ask me was it worth it? Â Heck Yah! Â It was some pretty damn good pizza! Â There were 3 extremely famished people and we ordered 2 large pizzas, 1 pepperoni and mushroom, and 1 sausage and bell peppers. Favorite thing: Pepperoni and Mushroom Least Favorite thing: waiting in line over an hour and being crammed into a table that clearly was only meant to fit 2 people. -1 star because the second pizza came out undercooked and the crust was still doughy

**This place gets an additional star for my main man chef Taquito. The Chef has a great spirit and jubilance about him and often works his magic on the noodles while singing and dancing to Michael Jackson tunes. I've had the pleasure of sitting behind him twice as he works into the night, and his cheery nature alone boosts Totto up by one more star! You really don't have a choice, but try to sit at the bar and you'll know what I mean! (photo attached) Furthermore, they've recently put up one of those protective thingies in front of the store that will keep people warm from the cold. Another nice touch for those who wait a bagillion hours in the cold to taste this yummy cuisine. Finally, next time you go, check out the staff. Is it just me or wouldn't they be a perfect cast for an EPIC samurai movie? **

This place is an EV gem. Â Took me far too long to try this place, but finally went last night. Â I am so excited to go back, as I need to try everything on the menu! Â  Our table ordered a delicious bottle of white as recommended by our server, two salads (Maroulosalata and Roka Kai Ahladia Salata Me Fistikia Aeginis [pear and arugula]), the octupus mezethe and the lamb shank. Â The salads were to die for, the octupus was tender, and the lamb was fall-off-the-bone delicious. Â To top it off, the fresh pita and red pepper hummous is unbelievable, and it magically arrives on your table! Â  Cannot wait to go back!
Nice ambiance and the fudge brownie with ice cream is HEAVEN!!!!!!!!!!!!!

The food here is incredible! Farm Fresh and always great! Now why did I give it two stars? The Hostess and the Hustle of the place. 1.) The Hostess, really hates her job and it shows. I try my hardest not to upset her, but somehow just telling her my groups name and number of people sets her off. The last visit, it was just me and my wife and she said there were two tops available right now. She told us we just had to throw out the coffee we brought in (totally understandable). So we walked outside and tossed it. We came back in and she didn't even have us on her list and now there was a wait of 1 hour--just in a 2 min walk to the trash can. 2.) Its pretty pricey for just eggs, toast and sausage. If you go there regularly between the lovely hostess and the expensive food, you feel a bit taken.

The hubs absolutely loves ramen. He would eat ramen for every meal if he could. So of course, we had to try Ippudo! We ordered the pork buns as an appetizer and they were incredible. Super tasty and I'm sure, very fattening. For our meal, I ordered the miso ramen with a poached egg. It was amazing. I really liked it. The service here is also incredible, very friendly and fast. The seating here is limited and I wouldn't recommend coming here with a large party, otherwise expect to wait at least an hour for a table. Food 5/5 Service 5/5 Atmosphere 3/5 Price 3/5 (expensive, we paid 50 bucks for 2 bowls of ramen and 2 tiny pork buns)
So rude! Not even busy but the hostess sat a bunch of people that came in after us because she had something stuck up her ass?! Prepare to wait and not be served.

Tasty bao and lots of choices. Had the pork belly, pulled pork and the colonel which was delicious! The friend chicken bao was my fave. It was fried perfectly and moist inside. It was very flavorful. The pulled pork was done well too. Pork belly was all right. Had better elsewhere.

Is this the same place I just went to last summer?! Â To say I was DISAPPOINTED, would be an understatement. Â Pickled oysters still had dirt in them, lobster and grits were unflavorful and the grits did not have any cheese in them. Â A simple Caesar's salad was bland. Â For desert, one scoop of chocolate ice cream over a hard piece of chocolate brownie ($8). Â By the time me and my other five family members left this establishment, $273.15 later, disappointed was a nice way of describing our meal. Â The outside patio area needs to be fumigated of all the flies and other bugs that we ducked and dived from while we ate. Â I try my best to support local businesses in Brooklyn, but I WILL NOT RETURN TO THIS RESTAURANT EVER AGAIN!!!! Â Restaurants have to learn how to retain customers or they will end up like "Night of the Cookers", that was once located on Dekalb Ave.

Crikey!!!! Â I'm in LOVE with this place even though there's not a koala or kangaroo in site. Â  The fare is magnificent!! Â  The grilled watermelon with pan fried squid is amazing! Â  I can't get enough. Â Really... I'm black... I CAN'T get enough. Â It's just an all-around great place to be. Â  And don't overlook the homemade sorbets... Although my dessert is hanging with all the Aussie hotties... the two Chris-es and that hunk Alan.... Oh boy watch out when Warren starts mixing his evening specials. Â  Run, don't walk to Flinders! NOW!!!!! Â A million stars for Aussie hospitality!
I think the steak is a better choice than my chorizo tacos - where's the chorizo? It's mostly potatoes

What I like about this place is that it's a diner open 24/7 but it has the feel of a classy restaurant. Dimly lit cozy and cute. The food is really good, sweet potato fries are on point not soggy like many other places. House salads are fresh, and the bread serving is enough for four people. They also have an impressive selection at the bar. Only been here for dinner but I would like to try their brunch sometime then maybe I can give them the 5 stars they deserve.

I love cha-an! The ambiance is so peaceful and calming. The waiters are experts in the teas and will guide you to the tea that will best fit how you are feeling. The green teas taste fresh and almost have a grassy nature taste to them. Sipping on their green tea was like sitting in a green valley under blue skies. But the real must have here is the sesame creme brÃ»lÃ©e. Seriously one bite changed my life. The caramel had a crunch before the soft silky cream. I've never had something so good. Eat slowly so it doesn't go away! The last bite is the saddest.

Excellent coffee and scones; their kitchen also makes wonderful hot dishes (the Egyptian Breakfast is hard to beat). The place hasriendly and courteous service; seating is a bit uncomfortable, but otherwise, it provides a warm atmosphere and yummy food.

Surprisingly, pause cafe hot coffee is superb to most others in the area. I always stop by in the mornings before work and it's strong. The workers remember you, giving it a very neighborhood-y feel. I'm also a fan of their hemp milk.

I love this place because it's a French cafe without that pretentious, frou-frou vibe that comes with other places. Â  Brunch: They do their eggs benedict just right - the hollandaise sauce is very light and compliments the eggs perfectly. Â Although the eggs benedict is my favorite brunch item here, other choices are pretty excellent as well. Â The coffee is great - on my first visit I ordered a large cafe au lait and it literally came in a bowl... totally worth the caffein jitters. Â  Dinner: Honestly, I can't say that I'm a huge fan of mussels, but I had a taste of the mussels dish with chorizo and safron broth that my bf ordered and it was pretty awesome. Â Dip your baguette in the broth and it soaks up all the rich goodness. Try it for brunch, try it for dinner, even try it for just coffee and dessert. Â Definitely an LIC favorite.

This was a great stop for a bit of GREEK yumminess!!! I emphasize the Greek because I was slightly lead to belive that this place may offer some falafel delicacies but this is a true Greek experience. The food is fresh, fantastic and a huge bargain in my book! Lunch combo was $12 and it could have been shared. The sandwiches are huge and amazing, try the Tuna. You will not be dissapointed. A winner for me ;)

I give this place 3 stars b/c, while it is a cool ambiance, fun crowd, good food and interesting/fun drinks, on a most recent trip there, the bartenders decided that they weren't happy with what I left them and took it upon themselves to up their tip on my credit card statement. Now, I know that faulting a restaurant for the poor judgement of one or two individuals isn't fair, but I warn you all to just check your credit card statements the next day to ensure this doesn't happen to you. Stealing is never ok!

Love love love this place! From the meats and cheeses to the awesome bread and pasta, any Italian food lover will die and go to heaven when the arrive in Eataly.
