Everything is so fresh and the staff is so helpful the only reason I have decided to give it 4 star (which i really rate it 4.5) is the fact of how overwhelming it is once you are inside. We had to go back the second day to really understand the layout and be able to indulge in everything Eataly had to offer. Day 2 was amazing, we were able to eat at most of the stations and also able to shop for our favorite Italian products. Eataly is a mist see when in NYC!

I can't believe i've lived in NYC for almost 5 years and this is my first time here! When i got here for brunch on Saturday around 1:30pm, there were quite a few people in line in front of us. So my gf and I just put our names down and went to get some coffee to-go at the cafe down the street. By the time we got back, they were ready to seat us, yay! Here is the rundown of what we ordered: 1. Kale Salad: Very fresh and yummy! I would go back just for this! 2. Country Biscuits with sausage gravy and poached eggs: I looove biscuits and poached eggs in general, throw some sausage gravy on top of there, what's not to love 3. Corn beef and hash: a fancier version than your standard ground corn beef with potatoes. They use thicker cuts of corn beef and home fries style potatoes and it comes with a poached egg. 4. Seltzer Coffee: If you soda and coffee had a baby, this is what i imagine it to be. Wash your meal with a glass of this and you won't regret it!
Sent my food in a container with a big hole in it. Pretty disgusting mistake. Obvious sanitation problems are a huge red flag.

Nice little space, friendly staff, promising but not quite there. Â I had fatoosh and tabooleh, both were pretty standard, lacking distinctive flavors. Â The babaghanoush was really good but the pita wasn't all that special. Â My friend had the zaatar bread which was delicious; the owner's mom supposedly sends zaatar from back home in Jordan. Â  The owner gave us a little sample of their falafel: tiny balls about the size of a ping pong ball. They were tasty and well cooked on the outside but a bit undercooked on the inside. The service was a bit confusing and strangely slow but that could just be the early jitters of a new place. Â I want to like this place but I wasn't thrilled with it; I will definitely give it another chance and will gladly change my review if given evidence contrary to my first visit. Â Good luck Ba'al!

Like everyone else said, the soup dumplings are amazing. I was also impressed by the green beans. Expect a line, so come early to put your name in. The wait on a friday night was around 45 minutes. Its good for groups because they have big tables and the food is basically served family style. The service is typical for these kinds of places, trying to get you in and out as quick as possible, be ready to order when they come to your table. Some people are annoyed by the pushy asian waiters, but I don't mind it because I think the food is worth it, and this is how most other restaurants are in chinatown. Seem to be a lot of tourists though which is annoying. If anyone has advice for a place with as good soup dumplings without the tourists, please let me know! Final note: Cash only

This place is best described as an experience! Could be considered overwhelming if you are not prepared for what you are walking into. Â It's certainly a feast for all of your senses! I love that I have the option to dine in one of the many eateries or shop at the Italian market & prepare a fabulous dish at home. The handmade fresh pasta is so amazing! I haven't had anything as fabulous since i was actually in Italy.

Deeeelicious. We both wanted pork, so that's the only sandwich we tried. It was great, and I really liked the bread. As one reviewer says, it's semolina bread, and it has a great texture. I think I'll try the catfish next time. There's hardly any seating in this place, so we just got it to go and went to Union Square to eat. I think I'll be doing that a lot this summer...

Plusses are the atmosphere - casual and homey - and the service - friendly and helpful. But the food is meh. Felafel was soggy and bland. Shwarma was limp and bland, essentially devoid of spices. And everything was smothered in way too much, unavoidable mediocre hummus. Don't bother.

Meh. I liked the noodle bar better. Diver scallop - it was ok. Steamed buns - there's a reason they serve it in all of the entities in the Momofuku Empire (even MilkBar). The pork belly is yum yum Country Ham - it was just too much ham. It's a giant 20" platter of thinly sliced ham, some red eye mayo and 2 slices of bread. We had to ask for more bread because a person can only eat so much ham alone. Seating was confusing at first - they had me walk around the looooong family style table to face my dinner companion. We went on a Monday night at around 5pm so there was no wait and we were quite pleased. I wish they served the whole roasted duck to smaller parties. It looked and smelled awesome (was saw it on the spit next door at Booker & Dax) but alas, there was only 2 of us and no way just the two of us could finish that whole duck. I found food more to my liking at noodle bar

I've been here a couple of times now and everything about it is awesome. The service, the food, the drinks, and the prices. It isn't "cheap" but for what a nice atmosphere it has and the quality of the food it is a great bang for your buck. The fries here are probably the best i've ever had. And the meatball appetizer- Mmmmm mmmmmmm. Definitely gonna be a semi regular here.

My husband and I have been wanting to try this restaurant especially with the huge rave and high reviews of this place. My sister and her fiancee went there a 1.5+ years ago and said how good it was. We decided to go altogether. All 4 of us didn't think the food was good at all. My sister and her fiancee also stated that the food was not the same when it was first opened. We ordered: 1. Lobster - the dressing took away the other ingredients on the dish. 2. Yellow Tartar - this was OK 3.Scallops - OK, nothing special. 4. Uni Toast - the toast took over the flavor of all of the ingredients in it. 5. BLT buns - too much sauce 6. Oxtail Terrine - this was kind of dry 7. Roasted Bershire Pork Belly - this was OK 8. Hanger Steak Â - tasted boiled Due to the disappointment of all 8 dishes, we decided to go somewhere else to get dessert Not planning to come back! Thanks I originally RATED them a 1 but my husband said to give it a 2, so here goes 2 STARS for this place.

Came here last night with a few friends and I wasn't impressed with the service or the food here. The yakitori was $3 a skewer which is standard in NYC and some of them were really delicious (beef tongue and gizzard) but the servers were really disorganized which ruined the whole experience. Our skewers were dumped on the table and the waiters were already walking away when they told us what was what. We were even given 4 chicken skewers we didn't order and when they figured it out, they gave it to the correct table who wanted them replaced. Can't blame them, I wouldn't want chicken skewers that were sitting at the wrong table for 5 minutes. Also we tried the chicken meatballs that were coated in sticky rice and steamed. Those were bland and needed to be doused in soy sauce for any flavor. In the end we paid $40 each for a dinner that barely filled us up.

The decor and lighting is just so inviting. Staff is professional and attentive. Food is inventive and new. Nice way to start a night in the city. Â  Overall, we had a good experience. The ingredients were all fresh and the dishes were well-composed.

We came here for a nice late lunch and they really made the experience so awesome that Maha and Mom came back again that same week. Â  We were starving and nothing says incredible service like a 3 minute wait and being whisked to a tavern table. We were served water and menus right away. Â I settled on the mussels with chorizo while maha ordered the chicken soup and dumplings. Â Mom did not feel compelled to order any of the appetizers so our concerned waiter suggested that the chef could whip together a carrot soup for her-which she did...which was AWESOME! Â The mussels were briny and fresh, complemented perfectly by the meaty salty chorizo. Â The beans were a little too plentiful but otherwise the dish was excellent. Â Maha's soup was so comforting and Mom's carrot soup was incredible. Â It was sweet with a touch of ginger, and no one would have thought they threw it together on the spot! For mains Mom and Maha had the grilled chicken, while I went for the flounder. Â The chicken was succulent and juicy, and did not even need the au jus as not one bit was dry. Â The flounder was perfectly cooked with a delicious spaghetti squash side. Â YUM! Dessert was ricotta cheesecake and sorbet, and really the sorbet was some of the best I have ever had. Â It is house made and you must not miss the grape. Â The cheesecake was rich and decadent, and the apple pie our neighbors were having was equally impressive (looking). I will definitely be back for dining room dinner service, and im sure an upgrade to a 5!
Karaka-men ramen was the perfect amount of spice and so delicious!! Service was also very welcoming!

I think we've been here around 20 times. Out of this world, amazing BBQ. The menu changes with the day/time that you come. Great beers to wash down the meat. Â We always order way too much - but it' just so hard to say no. Get there early to get the full menu, have one of you stand on line for the food while another grabs a gallon jug of beer and scopes out a space at a table. When the weather's warm, seats are perfect outside. We never both with sides more than pickles since we stuff ourselves witht he meat but they have a few good ones to offer. Of course will be back many times again.

Let me tell any one that is thinking going of going here, and is hesitant because of the color of your skin... PLEASE DO! I really do not frequent any italian establishment because of the the wave of unattentative and disrespectful waiters and staff. BUT this place by far was a eye opener for me!!!!!!!!!! the staff treated us with respect and was very helpful no other place that i have went to has been this nice to me, To me this was a like i was going to a family member's home to have dinner. Â The food was excellent! they sent out samples of other dishes to us at no charge and even supplied free desert. The agnus steak was crazy! PETER LUGER you can not even come close! Our waiter ( i gotta call him Steve's brother because we ask for steve and he said i m his brother) i didnt Â get his name... was awsome! He was so busy and was still very attentative to our needs. There was a guest by the name of Lucille... i think she frequents this place... she was a such a joy.... she showned me that even the customers are friendly at this estblishment. Â She knew all the staff and acted as if we were her her family. Lenny... i belive was the owner, was my type of guy, let me tell you... he did not flaunt his wealth, he was dressed just as a regulaur person going to get a slice of pizza... but when he introduced him self to you and made sure your table had the utmost attention, it was by far any of the resturants that i went to in my life. L and B spumoni, you are by far the best and will have my support at all times!

Great food, great prices! Â  Located between 5th and 6th avenues (closer to 6th) on 13th street, Da Andrea is a stand out in food and price, especially considering the number of Italian restaurants around the city. I love the fresh focaccia that is brought to the table shortly upon seating. Specials truly leverage what's fresh for the day - if it's available I highly recommend the (chicken or pork) ravioli. If not, I almost always go for the pappardelle with sausage ragu. Then again, don't think you can go wrong with any of the picks as nearly all the pastas are homemade. Â I usually bring my meal to a sweet close with the tiramisu - the best in the city. Â  Truly delicious food at great prices.

beautiful decor, amazing organic food, great service and unique style. I love this restaurant and wish Vancouver had more like this. The Prix Fixe menu is filling and delicious... the caramel dessert was to die for!! 5 Stars all the way! :)

I really wasn't expecting to like this place. Â I know one of the chefs here, and he can be a bit abrasive. Â Yet, that clearly has no impact on the generally good food here. Â  I went here for lunch and was warmly greeted and told that I could sit wherever I liked. Â The place is really quite homey, and there is a casual intimacy about the space that I usually never encounter in restaurants of this size. Â The menu has a limited number of selections, but I chalk that up to them wanting to do a few things well rather than any of the alternatives. Â My choice was simple enough, a meatball sandwich and a cup of coffee. Â  The sandwich was wonderful. Â The bread was really nicely done. Â It was toasted just enough to really get the appropriate texture for the sandwich. Â Within lied several heritage pork meatballs which were flavorful, and, surprisingly, not heavy at all. Â The marinara was pretty nice and not excessive in its use. Â The melted Big Ed's cheese (yay, a Wisconsin cheese) really worked nicely. Â I was pleased. Â Further, the dish even comes with a mixed green salad served on the same plate. Â That was a surprise! Â It paired quite well, tempering the heartiness of this dish. Â A skilled offering of comfort food. Â I wasn't so taken with the coffee though. Â The service was especially good which made the restaurant endearing. Â Great place! Â Definitely recommend.

This review is for a Groupon-discounted dinner at this restaurant. Mixed reviews. On the plus side, I hear breakfast/brunches are first class. the interior looks nice, it's a nice area to go out in, and the servers are courteous. On the other hand, if I had to pay the FULL menu price, I would give this place 1 star. The salmon was average; the lamb was fall-off-the-bone, soup-ready, more like a berber Tagine style, and was inexplicably served with baked beans and italian tomato sauce (It was as if a little toddler found the cupboard and disturbed mom's cooking); the tiramisu and brownie were below average; and the drink situation was pretty insulting: The Groupon title is "2 entrees, 2 drinks, and 2 desserts". Period. One of those open-ended Groupons that you get excited about because they don't limit you to certain parts of the menu or days of the week, right? Which induces you to buy the Groupon. So after announcing we had a Groupon, suddenly most of the alcohol options are not included (only beers, house wines, and sangria come with this deal)... so I reluctantly try a beer. server comes back after talking to manager... beer is no longer available. i try the next beer... same story. just so happens these are the most expensive (and best) beers on the menu. what an odd, odd coincidence. Almost incalculable, these odds. This is also known as false advertising. Another restaurant that forgot that Groupon is supposed to be an arm of marketing, and you want customers to return. Wouldn't even play by their own rules, which differed from the deal they negotiated with Groupon and thus us the customer in the first place...
The food was really good. The service was super nice as well Good place to hang out with friends. Reservation is required unless you want to wait forever.

10 course tasting menu ends up being a lot of little bites. Â A unique and fun experience seeing everything being cooked right in front of you. Â As with any 10 course tasting you're going to end up with hits and misses. Â To me the hits out shined the misses and resulted in a great culinary experience at an affordable price. Best Dishes - Crudo was light, crips and refreshing. Â The fish they used was hamachie. Â Great citrus notes and some heat but not overpowering. - Sardine was the highlight of the entire meal. Â A excellent dish that was well balanced and not fishy whatsoever. Â Great crispy counter balance but can't remember what it was, I think crispy rice. - Croquettes were amazing as many have attested to. The only dishes I didn't necessarily care for all that much was dessert and the cold soups. Â At the point dessert came I was pretty full and could probably have done with dessert at all. Â The 2 cold soups were a watermelon gazpacho and a almond soup. Â The watermelon gazpacho had a lot of heat and no taste of watermelon. Â I'm not a huge fan of cold soups. Â The almond soup had a very grainy texture to the soup and not pleasant. The techniques the chefs displayed in a wide variety of dishes, proteins and vegetables were impressive. Â Seeing them execute all of the dishes in front of you while managing the timing of dishes across the whole restaurant added to the allure of a fun and memorable dining experience.

I was looking forward to trying this place as I've heard nothing but raves for years. The place is basically a dump filled with the acrid smoke of burning olive oil from the oven. The wait was ridiculous-- nearly 2 hours and the pie was burned. Not well done, but BURNED black with a thick layer of charcoal on the entire bottom and crust. If I wasn't so famished from waiting, I'd have sent it back. That being said, the cheese and sauce topped with freshly cut basil was delicious, but the crust was inedible.

Came here last night after a random Wednesday night out and was blown away by how GOOD IT SMELLS in there. The prices are great and the falafel sandwich is bomb. I'm going back for the shwarma. I recommend using the hot sauce sparingly. That stuff will burn, but in a good way. What makes my time there particularly memorable? Seeing the guy working the register sweating balls and calling a break to rinse his entire head under the faucet. "I'm sorry," he said, "It's so damn hot in here." At 1AM on a Wednesday night? Damn right it is.

My husband was pretty excited about having a bar with a big selection of craft beers in the neighborhood, but our two experiences there have been very disappointing. Â We went there shortly after they opened and I asked the bartender to recommend something based on a couple things I told her I liked. Â She did, and it wasn't very good, but I don't fault her for that. Â However, she should have told me before I saw the charge on the bill that her recommendation was an $18 beer. Â We gave it another chance last weekend, and it was super crowded and incredibly loud on the Friday night we were there. Â My husband left a 16% tip on our bill that evening, and when the charge posted on our credit card it was for more than he left them. Â The bartender apparently decided to give herself a 25% tip. Â Ask about the cost of anything you order and keep the receipt if you go. Â Seems like they're just out to rip customers off.

The perfect date spot. Very intimate dining, so not best for groups, but they accommodate reservations ahead of time, and we saw a group of 6 seated at the window. The cheese plate is amazing. The bergere crepe is out of this world and the seguin is a close second. My boyfriend always orders and loves the pastas. Servings are enormous; come hungry.

The service was phenomenal with a great ambiance! Sangria is delicious, they have a tasty assortment of spreads and lunch options. Will be returning for sure. Great service! We were greeted and served by one of the owners which is hard to come by these days.

I was happy to see that this place had finally opened and went in to order take out this evening. Â I found it to be really cute inside and the staff seems very friendly (although there were a lot of them in there for the amount of people). Â The menu features a bunch of standard BBQ entrees and sides. I got the pulled chicken and a side of green beans. Â  My order took about 5-10 minutes to be prepared. Â Not bad at all. Â  The pulled chicken came with slaw (which was a bit too sweet in my opinion) and a couple of very new dill pickles (yum!). Â They also gave me two small containers of BBQ sauce (different kinds). Â The food was pretty good, however I think it is a bit over priced. Â My above order cost almost $17. Â Too much to spend for a dinner for one on a regular basis.

Excited to try new offerings from the chef at Zabb Elee, one of my favorite Thai places in Manhattan. The lunch offering, unfortunately, is a little watered down -- as it has to be to satisfy the bland palates of many midtown lunchers seeking sugary pad thai and vegetable curry. They should be bold and put their best food forward with their Isan dishes for lunch. I tried the moo krob over rice with chinese broccoli. It was just ok. I also had the eponymous Larb as my starter, but didn't find it special. I assume that was watered down for the lunch crowd as well. I will return and try to order off the dinner menu. However, it doesn't strike me as a dinnery kind of place, so I hope they find a way to manage while remaining true to their culinary aspirations.

I have been to Tink's several times for brunch and dinner and both were great experiences. I love the food. Not a huge portion which I like and not greasy. I would consider it upscale American style food and loved the chicken and waffles and the tacos. Tiny place, but cozy and love the decorations.
What I love about this is place is that u can play Yenga there! Its such an awesome entertainment when drinking a good beer with your friends.
This place is famouse for a reason.

Pros: extremely fiery chili sauce, generous portion with a wedge of warm pita bread. Cons: long wait Tip: Â  1. Go to whichever has the shortest line between the west and the east one. They are both run by the same, hence the same flavor. Â  2. The cart during the day is NOT the original one. The legit cart opens at 7 PM. Â  3. Get the lamb and chicken combo. Best of both worlds. Why not. Â  4. Look for the condiment container around the cart. Need more heat? More white sauce? They are all there. Hands-down THE best halal cart in Manhattan! Â  I love their chicken & lamb combo with a dash of hot fiery chili sauce. Try ONE DROP first; even one drop goes a very LONG way. Mix it well with the white sauce and the chili sauce into the rice and the meats. Jesus, I am in heaven. Just the best fix after getting crunk with ur friends! :) What I love even more is the steamed pita bread wedge that comes with it. So soft and with the green salad, you can create your own tiny wrap! ;)

I love this place. It is truly delicious. The chicken is better quality than the lamb, but I've found that it feels like there's an element missing without the lamb. Another note: going down to Central Park to eat is nice. If you walk to the park, then go straight down the steps on the right, at the entrance to the park at 59th and 6th, you'll see a nice little lake with benches. Just watch out for raccoons!

My first time here and it was ok. The wait wasn't too bad but there were only 2 of us. The ramen is too soggy for me and I'm sure I've had better ramen for less. BUT the pork buns.. they are delicious! kind of expensive for just 2 ($9), but it was something I would go back for.

There's not much else I can say that isn't already captured in the hundreds of other reviews about the Black Label Burger, but I at least wanted to be associated (however tangentially) with greatness by writing a review for Minetta. My lone suggestion is to treat the burger like steak and get a glass of full bodied red to really complete the meal.

Pleasant atmosphere and service. Â Wine by the glasses were excellent quality at reasonable price. Â Homemade pickles were tasty. Â Food was visually attractive. Â Green apple and radish salad was delicious, though the comically large hunks of radish went untouched. We waited over an hour for our food. Â When we finally inquired we were told "we make everything fresh" as if the problem were ours for expecting food any faster. Â Then moments later we were offered another story, that our food was waiting on a burger ordered well-done. Â As if it takes an hour to cook a burger well-done. 2 out of 3 main dishes were bad Â The Caputo's Fresh Linguini was undercooked, and ironically it tasted as if dried ingredients were used. Â The Berkshire Pork special featured flavorless pork swimming in a bowl of sauce of soy, sugar, and pickles. Â It tasted as disgusting as it sounds. Â The burger at least was passable. No plans to return.

Ramen-Ya in West Village is my favorite place to eat. Their broth is much creamier and tastier than IPPUDO and TOTTO Ramen ! Ramen-Ya is a new restaurant that has a great atmosphere albeit rather small in space. My favorite is their tender and flavorful CHASHU also knows as Grilled Pork). I went to Ramen-Ya last week, I tried their new ramen called the ABURA-SOBA. it is a unique creation of ramen with no soup! They have 2 kinds, one spicy and another is their traditional flavor. The traditional version uses a Kakushi-Aji, whick means "seacret ingredient" in Japanese. This is a Ramen-Ya original and never seen before in NYC!

Every time I come to NYC i have to come here... they will make a veggie platter for you (which I appericate) you can't go wrong with the whitesauce... check out the documentary I did on the 53rd and 6th Stand youtube.com/watch?v=BxJmâ€¦

The burger here is REALLY GOOD. Â It's $17, but at least you'll feel like it was well spent. Â And it comes with fries, but the really good ones, not the gross reheated ones. The place is small, and it was packed for lunch. Â If you want a table, even for lunch on a Wednesday, get a reservation. Â Not knowing this place is so popular, I sat at the bar, which was fine.

I'm glad I can now say that I've been to the 2nd oldest bar in New York City. Â We stopped in for a quick beer and had whatever the house beer was. Â Not too big of a place but great for a couple of people to hangout. Â Not a pick up spot or somewhere you can dance but I don't think that was the goal of this bar.

Been here twice already - both my experiences have been great. Â Did not try the tasting menu, and would still recommend NOT to do so. Â The food is great; love the open kitchen and love watching them cook. Â Also really like the flavors of the meals.

It was very good, I loved the decor; the restaurant was very modern with great service. I came from a evening show of the Phantom of the Opera; it wasn't to far of a walk. The tea was $4, a bit over priced for tea... but on the other hand the tea was served in this cute little cast iron tea pots. The Thai fried rice was good, the Pad Thai was the best my sister ever had and the Pad See Ew was average, and they were a little short on the vegetables. Lastly the Chicken Satay appetizer was good. There also is a full bar which may please some people.

People have said these are the best panini and cupcakes in Astoria, so I decided to try both. Â The panini was overly greasy and had way too much sauce on it. Â The cupcake was bland, flavorless, had too much frosting, and really not worth the $3.00. Â  Yet another place in Queens to avoid.

Waited for an hour and a half one evening just to sample this pizza. Â It was great. Â We tried the pepperoni and ricotta pizza as well as ordered two carafes of wine and it was surprisingly affordable. Â I've had better pizza, but that was in Naples.

I love a well done, stand-up-and-clap-yours-hands-cuz-damn-that-was-Â­good, grilled cheese as much as the next Astorian. So when I read reviews that Kickshaw has said cheesy goodness in addition to being a beer/wine/coffee place I was like 'yes, please'. So my husband and I journeyed to this lovely locale. The atmosphere is hip with great music playing in the background. It's a small place, but cozy. The woman that greeted us was nice, and all the staff were overall just swell. I ordered the cheddar and mozzarella grilled cheese and my husband ordered the Gruyere grilled cheese. Mine was just okay. The bread was spongy, and while overall it was good, I felt as if I'd just paid for something I could make at home. My husband's was also just okay. He said it tasted like eating french onion soup, not in a bad way, just not what he was expecting. He had opposite bread problems where his was so crunchy it was scratching up his mouth. Â  We also ordered the trio of dips to share and it was delicious. The only downside is they give you just a few pieces of pita bread so you run out of bread before you've finished the dips. We ordered more and were charged a dollar for it. I know it's just a dollar, but to be fair, it's also just pita bread. Give some pita love to your customers and let them eat bread. I'll have to go back and try the coffee, but I don't feel like I'd run back here for the dinner fair. Oh! And totally forgot, we got draft beers and they were like thumbs up, yes m'am good. I ordered their wheat on tap and it was awesome.
First pizzeria in the US. The original oven is still in use. Nice piece of history. Nice thin crust. Interesting white pizza. We got there for a late lunch to avoid the long lines.

I LOVE macarons and everyone knows they can cost up to $3 for ONE. These are the best macarons I've ever eaten in the states. So I didn't feel too guilty for spending the bucks. A line does form but the service is pretty quick. A good tip is to know what you want before you go in so you don't hold up the line. Best time to go is during their non-peak times and try to avoid days tourists are rampant (Fri-Sun).

Bestie & I recently shared a wonderful Sunday brunch together at CafÃ© Orlin. Â Due to the Thanksgiving Holiday weekend and our somewhat early arrival (12:30PM), we were seated within just a few minutes! Â  With two glasses of fresh squeezed orange juice on its way (always in need of our V-C), we chose three plates to share: 1) Pumpkin pancakes topped with cinnamon yogurt - super fluffy and not overly sweet; the cinnamon yogurt was a nice, unique touch 2) Â Tunisian Eggs - great dish; loved the spicy peppers and tomatoes 3) Veggie Burger with a fried egg & a side of French fries - very good veggie burger (we had it sans bun.. obvs); wish I could get my hands on a bottle of their Harissa ketchup! Â  CafÃ© Orlin is a great brunch establishment! Â I'm glad I checked it off the list.. especially with my B! :)

I booked this place for our first dinner experience in the TriBeCa area during our recent visit to NYC. I have to tell that I was a little doubtful since it was the first time I had heard of something such as a Japanese American pub. The food was very good (excellent Kobe beef buns + spicy miso ramen that the waitress recommended) and the place had a very nice laid back atmosphere that I really loved. specially in a Friday night. In the end I still didn't get quite well the "Japanese American pub" branding but the experience was very nice.
Busy place, but the staff is friendly and the most important the food is delicious.

Most. Overrated. Place. Ever. The ramen is fairly good, although for the wait, I'd say it would be wiser to go to one of the smaller places which serve equivalent, if not better, ramen. Be prepared for a long wait. Â Maybe you should bring a board game to play with that special someone you're on a date with. Or perhaps you can bring along your senior thesis, and write about 20 pages of it while you're waiting to sit. Â You could literally go to K-Mart across the street, shop for an hour, then head over to St Mark's book store & read a copy of War & Peace, and then get dessert at St Alps (why is it not saint'S alp, I always wonder). Â And you know what? Â your table at ippudo still won't be ready. Might be best to slip the sometimes obnoxious matre'd there a Franklin and hope for immediate seating.

Empanada sampler: choice of 4 empanadas for $12! The goat cheese and the guava empanadas were my favorite. My least favorite was the bacalao, but I think that's more an issue I have with salt cod. Thanks to the friendly bartender who suggested I get the sampler of 4 rather than paying more for the 3 empanadas I was trying to order.

Had heard wonderful things about this place. The wait was much longer than expected and many people had the same experience as us. The food was good, but not out of this world. great ambience, though.
Small menu, but great food at super low prices! Â It's cozy too!
The service was fantastic. Â So many great options on the menu. Â We did the summer tasting menu and were delighted with each course. Â I will definitely go back to try more of the menu.

I am so glad I said what I said about Beco. After two years of living steps away, I can honestly say that this is one of my favourite places... ever. Their brunch is incredible and I love that they serve Oslo -- the Americano wakes me up every time. And can I add that their Bloody Mary is literally the best I've ever had? I'm in love with this place, the end :)

I'm all hot and bothered, suffering from a glutton's existential angst. Have my tastebuds finally betrayed me? Or have I fallen prey to hype? A product of inflated expectations once again? Walking hungrily along 6th tonight after enjoying the fantastic play "A View From the Bridge", I sought to kill two birds with one stone with a visit to the famed Halal cart at 53rd and 6th. Yes, THAT cart. I've read much about the "living the lifestyle" and it's place in midtown lunch culture so a stop here was roughly equivalent to checking off K2 on my culinary things to do list. Well, almost but not really. Sorry to say New Yorkers, it was just okay in my books. Fill up my tummy it did but it stopped short of being epic or mind-blowing. The whole shebang of rice and meat is bland and tepid unless you throw a load of white sauce on top. And even the white sauce is not as wondrous as I imagined it to be, a ranch like derivative of yogurt and mayo. On the whole, this halal plate smells a lot better than it tastes. The chicken was finely shredded and bland while the lamb was savory with its crispy tender texture and pleasant array of gyro spices. Better flavored rice can be had at the 48th and Park XPL cart so no points in that department. But the hot sauce here is a winner in my books, it's fiery red and potent in flavor! I got a thrilling buzz in my ears as I chowed down on my halal plate thanks to this condiment, so use at your own risk! In sum, a plate of food here is a satisfying cheap meal and worth a visit if you're in the area. I'll be back, most likely after a celebratory night on the town. I'd like to test out the hypothesis whether being in a joyous and inebriated state leads to an enhanced appreciation for this food. Update: I'm a regular here now. 53rd and 6th and I have forged a beautiful relationship.

This place is pretty much perfect. Â I've been for brunch, lunch, and dinner. Â The service is great, prompt, and friendly. Â The only negative is the wait for brunch on the weekends, and they don't serve the full brunch menu on Saturdays. Â If you get there at opening (10 am) you can get a table without waiting. Â  At brunch the cheddar grits taste like less healthy delicious mashed potatoes. Â The roasted shrimp avocado tortilla is amazing. Â Most choices come with a drink and the fresh squeezed juices are great, and it's cool that they offer grapefruit. Â The coffee is served with hot milk and refills. Â  At dinner the appetizer gnocchi is very good and they have daily deals such as steak, or fried chicken and beer. Â I have never had anything not delicious on the menu. Â The salads are expensive but really good and worth it. Â  Jane is a bit expensive but worth it for a nice meal.

I can't get to this place enough. I have dragged my friends so many times, no one will listen to me say the word 'bacon' anymore. Â I'm not a bourbon fan, so for me this restaurant is all about the food. Whatever you do, get a side of bacon. Just a few bites will keep you coming back. And although this isn't the sexiest menu item in a pork-based restaurant, try the pancakes. They are easy to miss, but with a coating of marmalade and butter, you won't need any syrup.

Brunch here is tasty. Herbed Eggs - Overall a healthy and filling meal. The eggs were not as flavorful as I thought it would be. It came with only two quarters of pita bread, but the meal is large enough to not ask for more bread. The cheese is a spread with olive oil, salt and pepper. The salad is like a salsa of tomatoes and cucumber. Home Fries - Definitely get this as a side if your order doesn't already come with it. It's delicious!
Good atmosphere, good live show. Small portions. Meh food.
These soup dumplings have no competition. Hands down best in the states! Â Try the veggie duck too. It's mushrooms wrapped in tofu skin.
Fries, dips and poutine are all spot on. Fries are crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside. You can't go wrong with any of their dips, regular size is perfect for a snack or lunch :)

So, just had my first Eataly experience, and can say the place is an Italian zoo. That's a good and bad thing. Good parts, the cheese, the wine, the bread, the Italian dry goods, the sauce, the restaurants! The bad: everything is super expensive, and all of NY is there with you. Really. Everyone.

This is a typical Chinese noodle and duck place. Â It would help if you can order in Chinese. Â The waiting can be long for eat in and take out. Â There is no real order in there. Â Better to take out and just avoid the chaos.

meeting an artist friend to talk about the movement of music and its part in the direction of culture, state of society, and perpetuation of creative consciousness. Â you know, typical, casual afternoon. Â so where's the best place to do that? Â why, at a sandwich place, of course! no, this is no typical sandwich, my friend. Â what are these tantalizing bubbles of crispiness on the bread? Â they're toasted on the outside and oh-so-soft and chewy on the inside. Â dooooood. Â the cucumbers and pork belly were having a rave in my mouth with the sriracha and... is that a slice of pear? Â  it was a delectable lunch.

Gem of a find, and that's saying something in this neighborhood. Â Managed to somehow snag a last minute Saturday night reservation for 8 people. Warm and cozy setting could be ideal for either a group meal or a special date. Â Ambiance and service were tremendous. Favorites included Wild Mushroom Pizza, Squash Cannelloni and chickpea fritters. Â All three are melt in your mouth amazing. Â Marinated Artichoke Crostini was also fabulous, and also go for the Ricotta and Honey Crostini. Could have done without the roasted asparagus. Â Summer Sangria was so so, not as satisfying as the rest of the meal.

Just went for dinner - so great! It's a bit cramped but sometimes it's nice to find a hole in the wall with great food and ambiance. Sat at the bar and ordered a bottle of wine that was similar to a Sauvignon blanc and great. Then split a prosciutto mozzarella special, lobster avocado arugula salad and ravioli with asparagus. All were awesome.
Love the atmosphere! One of the coziest restaurants in the hood! The burger and fries is always a great choice!

Back when I was going to Williamsburg fairly regularly to rehearse for a play my friend was putting on (Jungle Woman of the Jungle!) we'd run our lines in a bar & then walk to Pies N Thighs afterward. Â This was back when the pies & sides were baked in the back of a nightclub & the meet was barbecued out in a parking lot, where the picnic benches were. Â I gather it has moved since there? Â Well, I just went to the Madison Square Market & saw that Pies N Thighs had a booth-- I prioritized that, you better believe it. Â I got a chicken biscuit & the coleslaw. Â Darn tasty. Â I know you wouldn't usually order coleslaw as your side-- there are plenty of other options-- but I recommend it. Â The coleslaw was named #20 in some "Essential NYC Cuisine" list, I guess-- well, it deserved it.

..i was in the area, and seen reviews on yelp. So i decided to give it a try. Place is actually pretty small, when we got there it was packed. We all ordered the chicken, we got regular, hot and extra hot..unless ur a fire breathing dragon dont get the extra hot it will melt ur face off! Chicken was actually pretty good, it had a nice little sweet taste with spice. Our sides was corn, fries, and mac & cheese (it wasnt baked) so didnt care to much for it. Came in here to check out my little bro Danny's new job. Ordered a glass of rosÃ© and some Mac n cheese. Sat at the bar. The food was delicious. The service was quick and courteous. Bree was a total delight. I like the ambiance. It's a perfect place to unwind after work on a weekday with a drink and some good food. I came during dinner but I'm really excited to try out their brunch and bring my friends. Love this place it's so cute and good! Definitely my new spot. Thanks Sugarburg!

I wanted to love you, Dos Toros. Really I did. Why? Because; -Your carnitas burrito was on-point. The rice and beans taste homemade, the pork was juicily tender, and though your method for melting cheese is unorthodox, I'll give you props for ensuring a bit of jack cheesiness in every bite. -Your super-awesome service. My burrito-makers were friendly, smiley, and genuinely seemed to enjoy being so busy (there was a line to the door when I left.) -Your restaurant is sustainable. With vegetarian fed meats, compost-able utensils and recycled (but uncomfortable looking) furniture, I can dig your eco-friendliness. ...Which is why it pains me to deduct 2 stars for wackamole. Where are the chunks of avocado, the limey zing, the spicy kick from jalapenos, or just the normal garlic, onions and salt? This guacamole had the consistency of mayonnaise and tasted just as bland. As much as I hate to admit it, Chipotle makes it better.

A friend and I are trying to eat at every branch of Joe's Shanghai. Soup dumplings are most certainly the highlight of this busy Chinatown restaurant. Come to think of it, I don't believe I've really eaten much here besides the soup dumplings. Maybe a scallion pancake or some lo mien once in a while.... But if I'm here, I'm 100% eating their delicious dumplings.

Kap-um-kap, Pig and Khao! Â This place is so wildly authentic Thai that I expected a lady-boy to jump out the back and scream "MASA-JEE!!" Â  Instead I was greeted by a bunch of hipsters in panama hats, toting liters of beer. Â I'll take the hipsters with the 40's over the lady boys with lotion any day of the week, although the owners could step it up with Chang or Singha over Tiger (my only real complaint). Nevertheless, with so much Manhattan dining awash in stale, overpriced concepts, Pig and Khao is affordable, refreshing and Southeast Asian spicy (*note that the Southeast Asian spicy is equivalent to wildly hot by American standards but by this Yelper's account, friggin' awesome). Â  Fresh chillies, limes, cilantro and mint? Â Yes, please. Â Whole fried fish you can pick apart and dress the broth over coconut rice? Â Outstanding. Â Grilled chicken with green papaya, cashews, lime, mint and all the fixins'? Â You betcha. Â This place makes me want to renounce my American citizenship, hop on the back of a tuk-tuk and celebrate Thai independence day at a full moon party with illegal firecrackers, glow-in-the-dark body paint and bad house music. Â  I'm no monk but I would definitely burn some incense at the alter to show my gratitude to the owners of this fine establishment. Â Nicely done, Pig and Khao, you've restored my faith in cool, delicious NYC restaurants without being too pretentious or too hipster-y either.
It took them a while to get our food ready but it's soooo delicious!!!!! It's a bit tiny, but the waitress was extremely nice.

Very good food at a ridiculously good price for Manhattan. The place is a bit small, but that means that you get to watch the staff prepare your food three feet in front of you. Friendly, family-run, and fast. Again, a rarity for Manhattan. Try the Spinach mushroom omelet. It was delicious.

This place is amazing!!I add 5 dollar extra tips for the restaurant but not for the service.Hope service can be improved because everybody working there seems to be hurry,which made me feel a little pushed. Remember always smile to your customers no matter you are a boss or a waiter!Glad to see Joe by the way!!Chinese food are the best of the world!!

First off the decor's amazing. Unique and handcrafted. Feels like you walked in to the 19th century dining. Their backyard is like a lush green eden. Really well done! The food is old worldy, eclectic and delicious. Took the food awhile to come but well worth it.

I don't think that Jimmy's Diner invented brunch, but we have no way to know for sure. There were 3 of us, and we ended up just ordering 3 things and splitting them, because decisions are the hard. We got chicken and waffles, Tater Heaven and biscuits and gravy. Chicken and waffles is pretty much the best food for the indecisive (because it's two things already), and Jimmy's was some of the best I've ever had. The Tater Heaven was their homemade tater-tots (more like mashed potato balls; amazing) with guacamole, eggs and cheese--also great. Biscuits and gravy also featured eggs and was gone in a matter of seconds. The service was quick and friendly, it was worth the wait in the hot sun, and the vibes were second to none. Everything was great and nothing was spared.

When I overhear someone talking about dumplings, I'm just like OH MY GOODNESS PROSPERITY DUMPLING. Not out loud, of course. Trying to not sound crazy here. I'm the type of person to venture out on a Sunday and bike ride to Chinatown from the Village specifically looking for dumplings. While trying to not get killed on the road, I almost passed this little shop. I was confused by the line going out the door. That couldn't be it.. But then I'm thinkin'---dollar for five dumplings, who WOULDN'T want in line for that?! After my first time, I have been back at least three other times for my dumpling cravings (later on deciding that biking with 3 packs of dumplings and no basket was not a good idea). I never had to wait longer than 5 minutes and when I go right up to the window, I say "two boxes," slam down my 2 Washington's, and inhale all that pork and chive goodness. With some soy sauce of course. No frills, slightly greasy, but the ultimate comfort food. The first time on a whim, I ordered the duck sesame pancake for $1.75. I felt like I was living the dream with my 10 dumplings and pancake for less than $4. Dreams do come true! Alas, the sesame pancake flopped a little when I arrived back home but the dumplings tasted great even after popping them into the microwave. I have yet to taste the soups but based on what my taste buds have confirmed so far, this quaint little shop has won me over. Much respect for all the ladies working in the back all day--you make some mean dumplings. Having worked at a Chinese restaurant, I feel your pain in slaving all day but your efforts are fully appreciated and have satisfied some Chinatown youth and a broke as hell college student. Awaiting my next adventure.. this time with a bike basket. So I can bring home 5 boxes.

The reason that I am not giving 5 start is that the waiter asked us to order whole food at once in the beginning when we wanted to take time to order food for entrÃ©e after we ordered the appetizer.

I'll sum it up for you in one statement - food was good, but service sucked. Come on, one person and a bartender for serving people? Try somewhere else.

At first glance, AmÃ©lie bears no resemblance to a French bistro. The interior of this part-restaurant, part-wine bar is a dimmed, yet alarmingly red interior. Upon entering one evening after work, my friend and I were surprised to find a bustling, clamorous crowd of people by the bar area near entrance, and it was as though had walked into a model of anachronism; shiny, modern dining tables against a seemingly rustic bar, with patrons ranging from elderly couples to young professionals. Although the initial experience was slightly jarring, we were warmly greeted by the host and shown to our seats towards the rear of the restaurant. We had our orders taken before a small bag with sliced and baked bread was placed on the table, which we nibbled at throughout the evening. Our first courses arrived quickly. I had decided on the soup of the day, which was a mushroom bisque, while my friend had decided to go with the escargot. I have to admit that I treated my soup as more of a dipping sauce than anything else. Although small in portion, it was creamy, rich, and full of flavor, and a perfect welcome to the oncoming cooler weather. I was persuaded into trying an escargot from my friend's plate, but it was cooked well and the garlic-butter sauce it came with made up most of the flavor. For my main, I had gone for the Duck Leg Confit. The protein itself was quite generous, and I could tell that the outside had been crisped to near-perfection, while the interior meat was still kept moist, which was quite a feat. Hidden beneath was a sizeable amount of mushrooms and fingerling potatoes, which had been seasoned well and deliciously flavored with the remnants of duck fat. Although somewhat tricky to eat with the bone in (I was tempted to discard any semblance of manners and eat the leg with my hands), I pretty much cleared my plate. My friend had ordered the Gratin de ravioles du Royans, which was a rather small baked pasta dish. The cheese was plentiful, though, but I didn't find it so outstanding that I couldn't replicate it myself in my own kitchen. And finally, dessert. There were only two options that night, so we decided to get one of each. My absolute favorite was the CrÃ¨me BrÃ»lÃ©e; the vanilla bean flavor was delightfully present and the caramelized sliced bananas on top created a sweet and slightly crispy exterior. Looking back, I almost wish we had not gotten the Chocolate Fondant, especially as I actually don't extensively enjoy chocolate. Flavor-wise, it was rather one-dimensional, and I had expected a slightly molten interior, which this version lacked. Service throughout the night was spot-on, which was especially noteworthy given the ratio of clients to servers during that night. For all of its flaws and its somewhat scattered personality, AmÃ©lie still strikes home on multiple counts. I look forward to returning, especially to try some of their wine selections that are proudly on display behind the bar, especially as their happy hour is one of the better deals in the city.

The lunch was terrific especially the tempura green beans. I had the mussels which were very tasty and my companion had the shrimp tacos which she liked. The menu is varied and creative. Also food is on the healthy side. Since it was around 1p.m. when we arrived there were not that many people in the restaurant so it was easy to have a conversation. Would definitely go back to try other things on the menu.
Wasn't good. Sorry. But out waited was very nice.

This is my new local spot. Great atmosphere, friendly staff, and most importantly delicious food. Probably the coolest bathroom I've seen ever too... You may want to go just for that. If you do stop in for the bathroom please order the Brussels sprouts, the burger, and the collard greens salad. Yum! I felt they deserved my review as I've been over 10 times since they opened.... This place is amazing. Everything on the menu is great. The uni croquttes and the steak tartar were fantastic! Â Dont miss out on this place.

We had a wonderful experience at Taverna Kyclades last night! We were a group of nine and we arrived around five on Saturday night and they accepted us without batting an eye. We waited for our party to arrive at the small bar area and the bartender was very helpful and let us sample the bottle of wine we wanted to order. One note, their wine list is mostly Greek. It is best to think of their food as Greek seafood rather than Greek and seafood as their menu was mainly seafood, but my lamb chops were still delicious and the whole group was satisfied with their food. I also tried the fried calamari and veggie chip appetizers and enjoyed the way they were both lightly fried. The portions were all very generous. Atmosphere is somewhat minimalist (not a super cozy, sink into the booth type place) and bright but still welcoming. It was a little loud by the time we left but it was a fun environment. Our waiter was also very kind and patient. He answered all of our questions and was very generous with his attention which we all appreciated.

Given that April Bloomfield just won the James Beard award, I think anything less than 5 stars would be inexcusable. This is less of a review of one particular experience and more of an homage to all of the experiences I've had put together. This is, hands down, my favorite restaurant in New York City. For several reasons. I've worked in 5 Star Hospitality for a long time, and one of my favorite parts about the Spotted Pig is their uncompromising commitment to quality, both of food and of experience. Part of this commitment is their refusal to acquiesce to the whims of guests. If you don't want to wait for an hour, that's fine. If you want to ask for 15 amendments to a dish because you want it a certain way, have something else. These aren't short order cooks on the line, they're culinary masters, and trust me when I say they know a hell of a lot more about what will make your tastebuds sing like a choir of angels than you do. That said, you should know what you're getting yourself into. It's a small restaurant. As such, the tables are small too. If you want space to stretch out, you'll likely be disappointed. With that in mind, every dining experience I've had has been incredibly intimate, and I've never felt like I was on top of someone else (except maybe when I was trying to get in or out of my seat). They also don't take reservations, so get there early, or be prepared to wait. Trust me when I say it's worth it. The burger is wonderful, but there are so many other incredible things on their menu it's hard to believe that's the most reviewed item here. Their burrata with wild mushrooms is to die for. The mignonette they serve with their oysters is sinfully good. Their steak with roasted beets tastes like Jesus cooked it for you himself, and as an added bonus it's very healthy. Their seasonal specials are incredible and constantly changing. The pork rillete is the stuff of my dreams. The corn soup is quite literally to die for, and it's a damn good thing I don't live in Greenwich village or it's all I would eat in the fall. Â Throw the shoe string fries (with fried garlic chips and rosemary) into the soup and it's entirely possible that your taste buds will say "We quit, because nothing you could ever give us will taste this good." They have an excellently curated wine list, and every single one of their servers, bartenders, hosts, and servers assistants knows everything about every inch of both of their menus. I've never had a bad experience, and I don't know that I ever will.

I went to Carmine's in Times Sq, NYC wit group of friends, we ordered the chicken Marsala and the lasagna. The Marsala was pretty good (could have been better), the lasagna was good. The atmosphere was great, the prices for the food were really good everything was great, but I gave the restaurant four stars because our waitress was not that great. She was extra friendly when the check came because she wanted a great tip.smh but overall I had a great time!
The Chiang Mai fries are a must-have. I also enjoyed the green curry fried rice. It's definitely a nice twist on Thai and easily one of my top 3 Thai restaurants in the city.

Some of the best bartenders in the city here. Â Everyone of them is top notch, remembers your name, and takes care of you. The food is great. Great food for a reasonable price. Â We get a banana split waffle and a croque madame both of them were awesome. Very good ice cream, homemade mayo and fries... I have belgium roots, I can tell you that the fries were as good as some places you can find over there.
Eaten here for 15 years always amazing food and attentive service. Busy during brunch but what place with good food isn't?

Very authentic place to get Katsu and curry. You can smell the curry the minute you walk in and its fabulous. Will definitely come back for more. Love their sesame dressing for the cabbage salad. It is the same as the dish I had in Asia.

Hello little orange and olive appetizer plate. Â I am a huge fan of yours. Â  While the place was definitely bustling and, sq footage-wise, it's tiny, I had a delightful meal + drinks with a friend I hadn't seen in ages. This is an amazing new addition to the neighborhood! Great ingredients, prepared fantastically. I'm in love. If you get a chance, have the pumpkin pancake special. Amazing! Even the lattes are good.

I recently transitioned to eating vegan and was in New York last week for a work trip. My sister (who lives in NYC) was nice enough to do some research on vegan places we could eat at while I was there. We tried a few different places and Ellary's Greens is definitely at the top of my list. We had a fairly big group (5 people) and they gave us a great big table at the back of the restaurant. The food and atmosphere was great and the service was really friendly. I asked our waitress for wine suggestions and she was knowledgeable. And at one point either one of the managers or owners (not sure which) came over to chat with the table which was thoughtful. We ordered Â some main dishes and sides. A few of us got the chickpea burger which was amazing. It had a little spice to it which was unexpected but tasty. We also tried the roasted cauliflower, marinated beets and brussel sprouts. All were delicious but the cauliflower was my favorite. Everything we ordered was good basically. I was the only vegan at the table and everyone else was impressed by the flavors and taste. Only one person ordered a dish with meat/dairy and everyone else tried something vegan. My favorite part of the meal was probably the desserts. Sometimes I find it hard to find really good vegan desserts that don't have a weird texture or consistency. We ordered the raw chocolate mousse, chocolate strawberry shortcake, and apple crumb (or something like that which was the special). Everything was delicious! I'm not sure I can pick a favorite from them. I'll definitely be back the next time I'm in NYC. Another plus is that everything is clearly marked as vegan, vegetarian, gluten free, etc. And if you are with a group of non-vegans there's plenty of options that have meat or fish.
Really good Japanese food! As someone whose lived in Japan, some of their more authentic dishes were THE BEST! Loved the udon with curry sauce and the green tea crepe cake!

Atmosphere was great. Â Drinks were good. Â Service was okay. Â Food was meh. This is a great place to get together with friends, especially in the summer. Â It's got outdoor seating and frozen margaritas and it's not too expensive. Â Really chill and easy place to be. Â You buy your drinks at the counter and no one bothers you. Having said that, I'm rating this at 3 stars because of the inexplicably long line for food, and the food itself. Â  Beginning with the line, there was one cashier taking food and orders for everyone there - separate line just for drinks. Â All she had to do was take your order, and your money. Â You wouldn't expect it to take too long, but it did, considering the number of people there and how standard their menu was. Â She was nice though, which might have explained why it took her so long to take an order and move on. Â Don't get me wrong, I like service and attention when I'm at that type of restaurant, but I don't want to wait on a line to get that service when I could be back at my table with my friends. And then there's the food. Â It was cold, it was a bit bland, and it just didn't look that nice. Â At least that was my impression of their tacos. Â It was only $3, but how could you get a taco wrong. Â All it has to be is fresh! Â They serve it out of a trailer to give you that street aesthetic, I suppose, but they would have been much better off hiring some real Mexican food truck guys to come in and prepare the food for their clientele. Stay for the drinks and the endless chatter with friends. Â Leave and end the chatter when you get hungry. On a side note, for those that care, they recycle, and you sort out your own trash at their recycling/compost area/station. Â It seems like every other place is concerned about being green these days, and I'm not sure if it's just a gimmick or not, but at they are doing it.

Very good soups, sandwichs, and salad at great prices. Â Go to their website to see the overwhelming number of soups that they offer, although they only have about 10-15 per day.

I have been here a few times now for lunch...I work right in the area so it's my go to lunch haunt with reps or clients...and I love it! My favorite thing here has to be the calamari! It's simply amazing...you could make a meal out of their calamari because it's soo delicious! Their menu is not as vast as I'd like...I feel like obviously you have talented chefs, why not change it up every now and again? If it wasn't for their lacking menu I'd give this place 4 stars...as of now..3.5 is where I stand :)
