Finding this place was a very pleasant surprises. I brought my mom here for her birthday without having dined here previously. Right off the bat, the service was impeccable. We had a fiasco regarding the number of people at our table and the servers were extremely accommodating despite it being the onset of rush hour. However, once that was taken care of, the food was delicious and more than plentiful.

Columbus Day weekend and we got to sit outside. We went for dessert after reading about Junior's being a good dessert place. Great atmosphere... good service and my wife loved the Plain Cheesecake. However, coffee was just ok along along with my apple pie. Apple Pie was good...Not special though. Prices were good for being do close to Times Square. However, because it was so convenient only steps from Marriott Marquis, I would come back. Number #1 reason is because I loved the outside seating area

We didn't have a reservation so we made it 10min before opening. We were seated in no time. The restaurant has nice interior design, which is not too surprising as it is part of a trendy furniture store. The atmosphere is rather classy. The food tasted amazing. This place is a must-go!

How good is Balthazar? 4 days in NYC, only 1 day in SoHo. Came here 2x on that day. Had such a great meal in the morning that I canceled the already-planned-way-in-advance dinner reservations & opted to come back to Balthazar instead. I'd definitely say this place lives up to all the hype, including the hype of prices. But whatever... I'm not in NY to save a few dollars here and there. Made Sunday brunch reservations 4 weeks in advance for a coveted 10:30am timeslot. Despite being packed, our reservation was honored exactly on time. Bravo, hostesses & TY for being respectful of your diners' time, unlike most uber-popular restos! (And please, don't even think of coming here for Sunday brunch sans resos - that'd be pure masochism.) Also, despite being packed, service was always spot-on, fast & attentive. Coffee refills happened before we ever had to ask. Everyone else has covered the oohs & ahhs around the food, so I'll just leave 3 quick tips: (1) For your sanity, absolutely make reservations not matter which meal; (2) Les huÃ®tres selection: opt for east coast ones only, save your west coast cravings for when you're on the west coast (logical, huh?); (3) Tables are very close together, so if you're even a little claustrophobic, dine only during non-peak hours. 10pm dinner on Sunday night was magical! I cannot wait to come back. Love this place!

This place is well worth the visit. We went on a Saturday night with 6 people and had reservations. We we're late though so we essentially went at 8:45 on a Friday with no reservations. I was expecting the worst or wait time. Surprisingly we only waited like ten minutes. It's a tiny place though, I highly recommend a reservation. They suggest that each person get two dishes and I agree with that suggestion. We all decided to go family style and try a lot of things. We got the prime angus sliders, buffalo tikka masala wings, pretzel crusted fries chicken, shrimp and grits, truffle or nothing, and the pizza. Everything was fantastic. I had no complaint about anything. The service was great and the atmosphere was super fun and chill. You can't go wrong if you order anything I mentioned above. I'll be back to this place for sure. One of the coolest little joints in the east village that I've eaten at in a while. Go there!!
Enjoyed the food. Â Portions were large. Â Good selection on the menu. Â I wasn't brave enough to try any of the many Peruvian drinks on the menu but the Sangria was great.
Great thin crust pizza! Â I love that they sell it by the slice. Â I've never been disappointed by any of their food and the servers are great.

A Great Round Table Dinner experience for a cousin's birthday. One more family run Italian place with an authentic tough and everything made fresh and from scratch Went there with 5 other folks who are like the best food critics in the NYC and are Restaurant Gurus. Their staff is very customer friendly and on their toes to make sure you are having good time. We tried all their major food types from veggie, poultry, seafood and meat. Everybody loved what they got. The best was the sea bass special I ORDERED. The fish literally melted in the mouth. I will recommend this place !

Came here for Sunday brunch one day when a friend and I were sitting outside across the street at Poco and had yet to see our waiter for 15 minutes (I'm sure it was just an off day; I do still love you, Poco). Â  Our hunger got the best of us and so we got up and walked directly across the street into Fonda, not knowing what to expect. Â  Compared to the bustling, dank/hipster vibe we had just left, Fonda was pretty empty and looked a bit more upscale (think high tables, white tablecloths) for the neighborhood. Â However the menu was impressive, everything looked delicious. Â We each ordered a coffee, which came out in a french press, which was surprising as well. Â Our order of guac was served with warm tortilla bread in addition to the usual chips, which was also a nice surprise. Â  All the food was great and they let us linger at our table. Had a great experience and really hope they stay; I will say that something felt a bit "off" or "missing"...not sure if it had to do with it's ambiance for the location, and the sparse attendance for brunch, or what. Â Not usually the kind of spot I think of when I'm all the way over on Avenue B. Â  Overall, I was pleasantly surprised with everything from the food, the service, the ambiance, the presentation....would definitely be interested in coming back for dinner. Â  Â I think they might fare better in a different 'hood, but it's a good option if you are that far east and want a decent meal. Salud!

picklicious good! Â The fried pickles were worth the trip to Astoria. Â Many people may not know this but there is an art to fried pickles. Â Sweet Afton has figured out the perfect combo of batter to pickle ratio using a perfectly tart pickle - add in a spicy mayo dipping sauce..yummy. Â Im a bit of a wuss when it comes to cocktails. Â They have a dirty pickle martini which was like pickle infused vodka - I think I would have enjoyed it more mixed with tonic only cause as I said i'm a bit of a wuss and it was too strong for me. Â The bar tender was super friendly as was the wait staff. Â They were crazy busy and were still all smiles.

What started as a very promising neighborhood bistro has digressed into a confused french dance club. The first few times we came here we were sooooo excited and willing to overlook growing pains. Now that they have been at it for a while we are disappointed and confused by the addition of a DJ at night, the bartender who thinks its Bungalow 8, and the overall disorganization. Our last visit my man ordered a beer, which they were out of. He then ordered a rum Daiquiri. We were the only diners in the place with a few folks at the bar. After 15 or so minutes we had no drinks and the bartender was busy chatting with his buddies at the bar, clearly not interested in making our drinks- we watched as our server handed him the drink ticket, which he glanced at and ignored. We asked what the ETA is on the drinks and our server told us that they don't have Daiquiris. So they don't "have" rum, lime, ice, a shaker and a sweetener? Rather than teach the bartender what a Daiquiri is we decided to order something they did have instead, a Margarita. We eventually got drinks after our food landed. The music was loud and a club crowd started to fill the bar area, not exactly cozy or romantic. The server seemed genuinely apologetic as he could tell we were having an annoying experience. For Bushwick if you are craving french, the food isn't terrible, and the decor is cute. Definitely not worth going out of your way for. Be warned, the service is questionable and there seems to be no management. Also, stick with wine or beer (if they have it). Hopefully Mominette can get it together, we want to love it.

We went to Casa Mono for my girlfriend's birthday on Friday night. Â Since we had no reservations, we were only able to sit on the counter which made it quite hard to have a conversation. Â Since I sat close to the kitchen, it was really annoying to keep on getting bumped by the waiters. Â Plus I was annoyed that the servers constantly kept on shoving the white wine into ice right in front of use. Overall the food was pretty good. Â It was good in the sense that it tasted good, but not good in the sense that it was authentic Spanish food. Â I've tried plenty of Spanish restaurants, and this definitely does not taste Spanish at all. Â For starters, there were no Sangrias, which I've seen throughout plenty of restaurants. Â Second there was no paella, another Spanish staple. Â The lighting was pretty dark, which made it pretty hard to see what you were eating. Â After using the Flashlight app in my phone, I've noticed that some of the food we ordered was overcooked. Â However the wine list was really good, probably one of the better ones I've seen. Â I wasn't terribly impressed with the staff either. Â I expected to have Spanish speaking waiters to ask questions about the menu (since the menu listed plenty of Spanish speaking terms). Â Given that I speak Spanish, I asked the waiter for the specifics on a specific word on the menu, and all I got was a pretty vague answer that I could have deduced myself. Regarding the food, these are the dishes we ordered: - Â Pumpkin and Goat Cheese Croquetas: - Sardinas Fritas: it was good, but it wasn't very flavorful compared to other ones I've tried. - Razor Clams a la Plancha: clam shells were all broken. - Tripe and Chickpeas with House-Made Morcilla: the morcilla was way overcooked. Â Typically you can taste the morcilla. Â This tasted more like eating chorizos. - Â Rabbit with Anticuchos and Habanero Cuajada: the habanero yogurt sauce was pretty good. - Chorizo with Spring Beans and Aged Manchego: didn't like it overall. - Grilled Oyster mushrooms: some of them were burnt. Overall, this place is great to bring a date, or if you are a fan of Spanish fushion food. Â If you are looking for an authentic Spanish restaurant, I'd suggest somewhere else.

Was in the neighborhood one night and saw the reviews on this place so figured we would give it a try. What a great choice. As we walked in we noticed that it is a very small place with just a few seats in the back, but the food is so fresh and so good! Watched them press fresh homemade tortillas right in front of us and had the best tacos I have ever had and I have had some good ones! I would definitely visit this place if I was in this neighborhood again. Not a place if you're looking for a nice sit down dinner, but if you just want some good fresh food quick, this is your place!

Had an awesome brunch at Almond today, most of it exceeding my expectations - service, ambiance. Food was ok and therefore I deducted stars from the restaurant. Service was extremely warm and welcoming, but not overly obtrusive. Â Water glasses and bread basket were always full. The bread came with two jams and a delicious sweetened butter. The waiters are friendly, cute, and patient. We never felt rushed (waiter waited for us to ask for the check) I ordered the waffles with nutella, to negate all the benefits of the morning run and it was delicious! I really enjoyed it. We also ordered the housemade pastrami & eggs and I wasn't impressed. The pastrami and home fries were good but the eggs had nothing special. My only complaint is that the tomato salsa that comes with the eggs tasted a bit old and looked soggy. Even Chipotle has better tasting tomato salsa.

Disclaimer: this is a Lunch review, for a Friday, in the Summer. Pros: One of the better ramens i've ever had. Granted, I don't really eat that much ramen but this stuff was awesome. I ordered the Shiromaru Hakata Classic, and got it with a Lunch Set includes an incredibly small salad and a bowl of rice with your choice of protein (chicken pork or eel). Honestly, I have no complains regarding the food here. Came here on a friday for lunch and we got seated soon after everyone in the party was there. Our orders didn't take too long to come out, and we all had plenty of time to finish our meals before our lunch breaks were up. Food was delicious. Everything was cooked properly, tasted great, and the broth wasn't too overpowering (i've had ramens were the broth feels like a whole can of Morton Salt was dumped into the pot). Overall a delicious meal. Cons: 4 stars because I had to spend $25 on lunch. Feels a bit touristy. Convenient from work but also close to Times Sq and Broadway and what not. Not sure what the wait is like for the dinner rush but I'm sure it's similar to the other location. Conclusion: Would I come back? For sure. Would I come back often? probably not.
Run, don't walk to Supper. Â Delicious from the get go of the oil, bean and garlic they bring along with the bread. A tell tail sign dat somepin else is comin' good. Attentive service. Bring cash.

Get the vegetarian buns!! Delicious! I did not give 5 stars as most did because I felt the food was really great, but I was not blown away. The ramen was delicious, but would I wait for an hour for ramen again there? Probably not. Would I wait TWO hours for some buns? YES. It was great to sit on the bar stools and watch the food preparation. Enjoy!

Had an early dinner here with 2 of my gfs and I have to say, it didn't live up to my expectations. I liked the comfortable and casual vibe, and the food was decent, but it just lacked punch. And in a neighborhood with so many great choices, this would just not stand out in my memory. We had the duck meatballs, lobster tagliatelle, hangar steak and cod. Plus a couple glasses of wine, espresso, sticky toffee pudding. While the duck meatballs were very good, i'm not sure I'd return just on their behalf.

The place is pretty decent. I normally come here for a quick bite/take out when I don't know what to eat for lunch. The sweet pork noodles are okay. Not amazing not terrible. Just okay. I would give this place a 3.5 or 4 but just be careful when you check out. The cashier likes to mark up the price randomly. Make sure to Â match the the prices on the bill with the menu.

FIrst night in Brooklyn. FLight is delayed and Im an hour late so I love my resys at the restaurant I wanted to go to. So after cleaning up at the hotel I decide to wander around. BBQ? perfect. I get a quarter pound of pork ribs; they come with two soft rolls, Â which really hit the spot. The guys working the counter are super nice and after some inquiring the ribs are what they seemed happiest with. Now if I had not been a on a plane so long I'd have stated for a drink. Perhaps next time when I get in the other meats too
DELICIOUS, FAST and CHEAP! I don't know what the white sauce is.. but it's delicious, watch out for the hot sauce! I had the combo platter, not sure what everything was, but it was gooood.

This place sucks. They cook nothing more than dog food(meaning it has no taste). Everything is with bread. Chicken with bread, Â hotwings with bread, egg with bread, burger with bread and the list goes on. They have burnt chicken selling to people....are you kidding me ? Yuck ! Disgusting ! I would never recommend anyone to waste there time and money to dine at this place. Very rude owner as well, avoid this place at all costs.

Wow. Â This place is awesome. Â We made reservations and was here before watching the musical memphis. [MARTINI $20 Parmesan-crusted veal cutlets sautÃ©ed with artichoke hearts and white vermouth ] I typically am never impressed with parmesean crusted anything. Â Why? Â Typically crusted items to me are a cop out on flavors because they rely on the browning of the crust paired with usually a mediocre sauce. First off, their balance of parmesean to the crust was perfect. Â As you cut the veal, the parmesean hits you (they must have used big pieces). Â With the architokes, i'm talking two huge artichoke hearts. The sauce was splendid just salty enough pulling the dish together with broccoli. Â For $20 I thought I was going to get a small portion, but it was huge. Overall. + perfect salting + nice balance + good portions + good price = 5 stars.

Oh, Eataly. You could be the greatest place on Earth if you weren't always way too crowded. Here's my advice: walk past the crowds and go straight to the Rosticceria. Get a giant sandwich, walk out of Eataly, and enjoy your sandwich in Madison Square Park. They have prime rib sandwiches every day, in addition to a different meat each day of the week (check their website for each day's selection). I strategically timed my visit for Thursday, when they have porchetta (crispy pig skin...mmm). They only give you meat and bread, no veggies and no condiments (just a drizzle of olive oil and some salt) -- but it's so good that you don't miss the other stuff.

I have been wanting to try this place since moving to Astoria. When my family came to visit, my girlfriend and I decided to take them out for a fun dinner. While we should've called ahead for a reservation since we did try to get a table for five at 8pm on a Saturday, the wait was only about 30 mins and the friendly host/manager/owner(?) was more than helpful and accommodating. Our server greeted us with a fantastically friendly attitude and smile. We didn't really know about about the food other than it was Australian and had good vegetarian/vegan options. APPETIZERS: We all split the Crab Cake, the Crostini, and Veggie Moussaka. The crab cake, holy crap. Absolutely amazing, no filler, all crab. Wonderful! The crostini was great too and easily a new favorite of mine. I was amazed with the Moussaka, I've never had it before and it was GREAT. This was enough food for five people as an appetizer round. MAINS: My girlfriend and mother had the Roasted Chicken and opted for the Kumara mash. My father and aunt got the barramundi fish with the caramelized pumpkin. And I got the Mahi fish and chips with a side of Lime rice. Everything was delicious, wonderfully prepared and more than filling. The grilled mango that came with the chicken was stellar and flavorful. The lime rice was actually a total surprise at how tasty it was, because I mean, rice isn't exciting, right? The fries were hot and salty, nice and crunchy. I admit that I DID feel slightly like a twelve year old getting a glorified chicken fingers plate for dinner, but once I had a bit of the mahi, I didn't care. It was great. The dill, something something dipping sauce was killer, they should bottle it. I didn't try the barramundi but I did try the Kumara mash and pumpkin sides and they were equally excellent. DESSERT: Didn't have any room in my stomach! DRINKS: Didn't order any. Ok, so, if you've read this far, you gather that I liked the restaurant. So to balance it out, here is my constructive criticism... The noise level. Whew. It was incredibly loud and we were all practically yelling at each other for a better part of our meal. Some sort of sound absorption or bass traps in the corners may help some of that. (I'm an audio engineer) Once the restaurant died down, we could finally hear. The service tended to lag a bit, but only because they were incredibly busy, so I can't blame them. Every time our server did arrive, she made us feel relaxed and spent as much time as we needed answering questions. We had a chance to speak with the chef and she was very humble. Her food was great. She has a very real talent. It's so awesome that Astoria has so many incredible places to eat, sometimes it makes it hard to choose. But let me make it easier for you, TRY THIS PLACE.

Came here last weekend for brunch. Â The wait was super super long. They said 30 and it was more like 45. Â After possibly eating my right hand, we finally got seated. Â The place is tiny tiny. Â Maybe 15-20 tables. Â The smell in the restaurant was overwhelming. Everything on the menu looked fantastic. Â  I had the Steak and eggs. Steak was perfectly cooked, good portion of meat, the eggs were light and fluffy --I'm not sure what they put in the eggs, but they were incredible. Â  My friend got the baked eggs and they looked delicious. Â The portions were good, the service was good and the prices were very reasonable. If only the wait wasn't so long, this would be my go-to brunch spot.

Decided to try this place based on all the positive yelp reviews - and was very pleased with my experience! Ordered a black bean burrito - which was large enough to share with another person (which I did). The tortilla was soft and the filling was delicious! The salsa and chips were also really tasty. As a CA native - I have been looking for tasty, quick, cheap Mexican food (non-chain) and this is def my new go-to place! Definitely recommend to others. Fyi - hole in the wall with 4 or 5 total seats - my friend and I were lucky enough to wrangle two ... but going forward, will generally plan to eat elsewhere.
really delicious after a night out.
Great falafel sandwich for $3! Liked the hot sauce and pickled veggie toppings... cheap and good for people watching if you sit in the window
Excellent vibe, service and food; Â I really enjoy this space.

I love this place! My best friend and I came here on one of our "foodie dates" last night to celebrate being young and alive and we both agreed that Desgustation lived up to the hype. Not surprisingly, the two of us scored the best seats in the restaurant-at the end of the bar, right in front of the chef doing the final plating. There was plenty of room and we had an awesome view of the action. Each of us started off with glasses of the $10 cava (we're celebrating, remember?), which was really delicious and came in quite large champagne glasses. For dinner we had: the roasted oysters, seasonal fish crudo, brussel sprouts, seared quail, and added on the croquetas at the last minute. Oysters were fabulous; we loved the combination with the smoked paprika and potato threads. I liked the crudo a lot, but was a tiny bit underwhelmed. The brussels, quail and croquetas were actually incredible--you don't want to miss any of these things! And you seriously cannot come here without getting the torrija for dessert. We almost made this mistake, but fortunately the chef convinced us to order it (thank you!). Also, I felt like this place was a bargain. 5 courses, dessert, and 4 glasses of wine for $100? A rarity in NYC (and one of the reasons why I love eating in the East Village).

Cheap and tasty. Â You can skip the line and get the premade stuff for cheaper, directly from the window. Â The food is wonderful, and the people are nice too. Â I forgot to bring my wallet once, and he let me take the food for free (I paid him back the next day, of course). Â  Generally, I spend around $3-5 here for lunch.

Yes, Lamazou's sandwiches are pricier than most but once you've tasted one then it will all make sense. I haven't had one that I don't love, although my favorite is the butterfly: pÃ¢tÃ©, cornichons, Munster cheese and butter (yes, butter my fellow Americans). One of those babies takes me right back to Europe, walking through parks and munching on a sandwich with REAL bread. Sandwiches, while definitely the highlight of Lamazou, aren't all they have to offer. They have every type of European cookie, snack and biscuit, also with a nice selection of deli and fine cheese. If this place ever closes, I'll be heartbroken!

I've never had such bland food in my entire life. I could have made better, actually, I have made better and I'm a lousy cook. The pizza lacked cheese and the pasta lacked taste. The only good part of the dinner was the 2 bottles of wine we had the company I was with.

Came here a few weeks ago for a Birthday Dinner and I really loved it. At first I was skeptical of the casual atmosphere, but in the end I found it really charming. It reminded me of a oceanside shack in Martha's Vineyard with its beachy decor. The food was also amazing. We started with some Blue Point Oysters, and the duo of Tartar with was really great. I had the Scallop entree with creamed spinach and loved every last bite. I'll come here again for sure.

Jane is great. Â It's very good American cuisine in a lovely, civilized atmosphere with great service (a little less so during brunch) and a welcome lack of pretension. Â  I've been here a number of times for brunch, which can get crowded and competitive after noon but the service has always been fast and professional. Â The Benedict Johnny is my standby - the chicken sausage is very good, and the country breakfast is incredibly hearty and tasty (a boy favorite). Â I'm always surprised by how good the coffee is, which is a huge plus in my book. Â (I'm even more surprised by how many good restaurants have incredibly lame coffee.) Â  Dinner is full of tasty standbys, from salads to steak frites to mussels in generous portions. Â (Another plus - restaurants that give you medium rare when you ask for it. Â Why, oh why is this so hard? Â Yay for Jane.) Â Their prawn appetizer is especially tasty. Â Desserts are lovely in the same vein - comfort food in its most flattering form - warm chocolate chip cookies, chocolate cake, etc. Â  Oh yes, item #8 (9?) in the case for Jane - even their bread basket and accompanying olive oil is extremely good. It's in the details. Jane is not going to blow your mind. Â It's not like that. Â But it is great.

I liked it alot. We crossed the Brooklyn Bridge on Foot Â to go here. i think frank sinatra used to frequent Grimaldi's as well, and i really enjoyed the sinatra memorabelia. Â we had our favorite: thin crust with pineapple, olives, ricotta, peperoni, and sausage. its a mouthful, but it is soooooo good.

An institution. Â For me, anyway. Great service (at the bar especially, but that's a personal seating preference), and the food never disappoints. Â The menu is simple but surprisingly expansive at the same time. Â  The vibe is kind of funky with a healthy dose of sophistication thrown in for good measure.

Underwhelmed with the space, menu and sadly - the food. Brunch with a party of 6 - most people got the Mediterranean or Poached Eggs With Grilled Tomato And Haloumi and the poached eggs were all cooked almost all the way through. The sandwiches looked really good - I had food envy over the egg salad sandwich (damn it! i HATE it when that happens!) The bloody Mary was just fine - nothing spesh. Super loud in this place (not from music just talking and acoustics) - everyone at the table was shouting to each other. Wouldn't return.

Came for the grand opening last Thursday--got an email saying there would be complimentary shots and dance performances. Thought it would be worthwhile to check out, given that it was right in my neighborhood. The space is lounge-y and party-appropriate. With an upstairs area, a large bar area, and a giant screen in the center, I expected there to be good drinks, good crowd, and decent food. In fact, the food exceeded my expectations (sans the ramen, see below) and I'm already looking forward to returning for the fried chicken. We got a few dishes to share, including the apple perilla leaf sesame salad and miso glazed pork belly, both of which were good. Â For fried chicken, we went with Fly the Coop wings (soy garlic), which were outstanding. Thought to myself that I needed to bring my non-Asian-date-who-enjoys-Korean-BBQ-but-hasn't-Â­tried-much-else-of-Korean-food here. Unfortunately, the joy of eating took a bit of a southern dip when we decided to add on the pot ramen to our meal. (N.B. don't order this.) It tastes exactly like Shin Ramyun made by someone who doesn't know how much water to put in the pot before boiling it (t'was very salty), not to mention at eight times what you'd pay for a package at H-Mart. Our server didn't know where the ramen came from or even whether it was fresh, dried, or packaged. Sigh. Despite this last bit though, our server, along with the other staff members, seemed to have had prior restaurant experience. Service was more or less smooth for a grand opening night. And given the location, ambiance, and FRIED CHICKEN, I will be returning.

We were in the mood for burgers, so decided to check Yelp on what's good in the area. Noticed that this spot had excellent reviews. Tried the sliders here. They were small (as expected), but pretty good. The chili fries were good (but had too many beans). Nice cheap burger spot.
LOVE the Pistachio/fennel pizza. really different from what I have tasted :)

This restaurant is AMAZING!! I first went in July for a Girls Night out. We each had a different dish - Ropa Vieja, Plantain Crusted Chicken, Skirt Steak and Pernil. All were amazing. I then went again on 9/9/11 with my husband for our 22nd wedding anniversary. The food did NOT disappoint!! EXCELLENT!! Love this place, can't wait to go again.

I really loved this place for brunch. What a unique little spot! A two story house with a rustic feel, cozy decor, and a mostly unpretentious menu. There was about a 20 minute wait at 12:30 on a Saturday, but no wait in the upstairs lounge. I had the bloody mary (a tad too chunky, but well balanced), the artichoke dip (incredible! chock full of artichokes, with an amazing cheesy crust), and the open faced omelette (don't let the egg whites fool you! the hen of the woods mushrooms give it a substantial taste). I'd come again and again for the friendly staff, the well portioned food, the reasonable prices, and the wonderful atmosphere.

worth the wait if it's your first time. lamb and rice is really, really good. but after a while you realize that you can get a gooood gyro platter elsewhere in this huge city too. [the guys on 25th and lexington are great.]

It makes me a little sad to write this but my experience at Bohemian was only ok. For the hoops you have to jump through in terms of getting a reservation and all...I expected something much more extraordinary. Ambiance: Super cute. A+ for a well decorated space, pretty bar, massaging toilet seats (didn't use them...they scare me), and skylight. Service: Pretty good and attentive, though it took FOREVER to get our cocktails! Cocktails: Decent, nothing memorable. Food: We got the uni croquette, which I thought was a very strange vessel as to put uni on. Uni is so unctuous and oily and pungent I would put it with something also pungent but citrus-y so on top of a fatty fried ball...hmm. The tofu gnocchi was also not particularly exciting and too chewy, though the dashi broth was yummy. The grilled branzino was very nice but nothing spectacular. There didn't seem any special seasoning besides S/P so while it was cooked very well I wasn't that impressed. We got a pan chicken too and was underwhelmed. Pretty good, lots of thyme, nothing Japanese or very interesting. So basically...we paid solidly for a solid meal but I feel I could've gone anywhere and had this (or cooked it myself) so...why the hype?

My bf and I were in Brooklyn for the weekend and found this place on yelp and decided to give it a try for a late dinner on Saturday night. Very cozy, small place, great atmosphere. The service was fantastic. Our waitress was very attentive. With the bread, you get butter, a cheese spread, and a pate. All excellent. A nice bonus instead of the usual butter or oil. I had the short ribs for dinner. They were melt in your mouth tender. With a fantastic flavor. The sweet garlic puree mixed in perfectly with every bite. For dessert we had the olive oil cake. It was super moist, and had just the right about of sweetness with the candied orange peel. With the check, you also get a truffle and a polenta cookie. It's these small details that make the experience that much better, and make this place stand out among other restaurants with the same caliber food. I would definitely eat here again if we're ever in the area!

This is one of my favorite neighborhood spots. I'm deeply in love with their duck meatballs but I found the serving size to be slightly inconsistent. On one occasion I came with a girl friend and we decided to share the appetizer. I was pleasantly surprised when the dish was served to us in separate portions and we got 3 meatballs and a quail egg each. Bonus points on thoughtfulness and taking the initiative! On the next occasion however, a full serving comprised of only 4 meatballs and a quail egg. Go figure! Anyway more on the food... I'm not a pork belly fan at all but have to admit that Perilla won me over with their Berkshire pork belly cooked to perfection! I also really like their black truffle and sheep's milk ravioli. My friends who had other dishes were also extremely satisfied with their dishes. Dessert was fine. I wasn't blown away but I thoroughly enjoyed my dining experiences at Perilla and will be sure to return!

Their any beef dish is to die for. Wonderful texture and flavor. Even the meals during the restaurant week were good too, which is pretty rare. Desserts were not too fancy but yummy. Always make my stomach happy. =)

I remembered a friend of mine raving about the razor clams from Casa Mono, saying if I ever went there I had to order them. And I did. The plate was playfully presented, the clams arranged like Jenga tiles. The "mantle", or fleshy part, was of course the more tender and flavorful. The 'a la plancha' technique added nice caramelization, but I found parts of the "foot" to be rubbery. Good use of garlic, herbs and finishing oil to brighten the dish. The Atlantic Calamares with Harissa and Squid Ink was definitely Iron Chef-worthy. Â The electric orange harissa oil contrasted sharply against the black squid ink backdrop. The calamari which came in two different preparations was perfectly grilled and fried. Smokiness and heat from the chilis played well with delicate flavor of squid and not overpoweringly so. Sweetbreads are best when fried and usually just with a dusting of flour. Â To my surprise the Sweetbreads with Fennel Al Mono were done almost like fried chicken; coarsely chopped nuts in the breading added a lot of crunch. The interior of the sweetbreads was soft and creamy with a subtle hint of lemon from the sauce. The braised baby fennel, however, added very little flavor to the dish. The Fois Gras with Cinco Cebollas was a beautifully layered dish of pickled onions, grilled scallions and onion halves beneath seared fois gras toast smothered in a rich sesame seed studded teriyaki sauce. Without the pickled onions, the dish may have been too sweet, but I'd still eat the fois gras and toast all day. I chose the Lamb Duo with Black Barley and Preserved Kumquats simply because I love duos and the idea of two different meat preparations on the same plate. In this case, both were loin chops, one bone in and one boneless. Both were seasoned and cooked to perfection. The black barley added a chewy texture that finished with notes of citrus. There was some sort of chickpea salad, perhaps a riff on the classic combination of lamb with yogurt, but for me was dry and uninteresting. The Tamarindo Pork Belly and Octopus with Butternut Squash was a busy dish with lots of competing elements: three blocks of pork belly, a couple random pieces of octopus and some grapefruit segments doused in a rich tamarind demi glace and dollops of squash puree. Unsure of how to eat this, I sampled all of the ingredients separately and then together in different combinations. I could appreciate the use of the grapefruit to cut the fatty richness of both the pork belly fat and the sauces, but it was unanimous at the table- the octopus was completely out of place. Which brings me to dessert and the Chocolate, Olive Oil, Sal de Mar. I loved the rustic presentation of dueling quenelles of ganache and ice cream. The olive oil flavor was astonishingly prominent, so much in fact I thought it had been drizzled over the entire dish and thought to myself, "that's so Mario Batali!" Bits of chicharron and salt flakes made the ganache even silkier in my mouth. A very well executed dish.

Decent place for brunch. The food was well made, the space not overly loud or crowded, and the servers were nice. I had the eggs Benedict, which came with Canadian bacon and home fries. The potatoes were excellent. Frittata seemed to be the most popular brunch dish.

Salt and fat is simply amazing. The food is artfully crafted and sinfully delicious. If you live in queens and have a visitor new to the city bring them here. It's an experience. The plates are small and expensive but that just makes them perfect for a special occasion. Honestly my favorite this there is not on the menu. Instead of giving you rolls before the meal they give you bacon-flavored popcorn. It's so good you'll be asking for some to take home. But don't dare eat there if you're on a diet.
Very good cheesecake!

My first trip to Red Hook! Â We came exclusively for the corn hole! Â It was a quiet, quaint way to spend a Saturday afternoon among friends. Â Service was delightful, and fast. Â After a few rounds of beer and games we dined on spinach salad, oysters and an oyster sandwich. Â Nothing was phenomenal but all was fresh and good. Â Beginning with a friendly face and ending with one always add an extra point, regardless!

This place doesn't mess around. Small menu, not many choices, so you know these guys mean business. They are good at what they do (ramen bowls) and they stick to it. Great price, friendly staff, and some of the best kimchi I've ever had. Definitely gonna go back there.

This place is a really small and cozy neighborhood spot. Â It's basically a fish market that has a few seats and a bar. Â Don't let the fish market part scare you away though- it's nothing but deliciously good smells here. Be prepared to wait. Â They don't take resys and there are probably a total of 25 seats in the whole place. Â Once you're seated, take your time. Â There's literally 2 guys running the place so you'll have to be patient about getting menus, water, drinks and food. Â This is really the main reason why this place doesn't get more stars... But anyway, the food is good here. Â The sandwiches are really solid and remind me of going to your local fried seafood joint near a beach. Â Their happy hour is great- it's $1 oysters and I even think there's a deal where you can get a dozen oysters and a beer for a very reasonable price. Â The mussels are fresh..though on a few occasions I've gotten a few cold mussels on the edge of my bowl... Ambiance-wise, it's a bit noisy and the tables are really close to each other. Â If you are sitting on the bench side and you have to go to the bathroom, forget it! Â The tables are so close to each other that you have to pull the table completely out in order to get out. Â  Basically, if you're look for a place in the neighborhood to have a casual bite with good seafood, this is perfect for that. Â It's nothing fancy, but the seafood is really fresh and very tasty. Â So, deal with the wait and deal with the small space. Â It's worth the meal. Â If you want to be some place roomier, try Mermaid Inn.

The Sangria. I could end the review just like that but I think it pisses Yelp HQ off when you post two word reviews. We had the Plato Don Carne. If you ask for extra tortillas you can get through all the beef and chicken they generously give you. My cousin liked the beef, I loved the chicken. Nice spice and flavor in that shredded chicken. Super friendly service. We happened to come on DÃ­a de Muertos, so all the staff was decked out. I only wish they had later hours. They practically had to kick us out of the joint. Now.... The Sangria. Holy crap was it good. Fruity and flavor packed, with a nice kick as well. If Â only I had known, I would have ordered a pitcher for myself and let my cousin enjoy his delicious mango/tequila concoction on his own. I see a Happy Hour trip in my future.

I came in with very high expectations, and this wonderful restaurant went beyond my expectations. I came here today for my brother's birthday celebration dinner, and they went out and sang him a happy birthday song. :) Pros: 1) Very professional staff 2) BYOB (Bring your own bottle) with no corkage fee 3) the aroma of food that hits you when you walk in is like a food lover's paradise 4) reservations were straightforward online and they call to confirm, 5) charming place which reminded my brother of restaurants in Amsterdam where he lived, 6) Food is PHENOMENAL, Tres tres bon! tres magnifique, meilleur de meilleur!!! We ordered the filet mignon and vegetable platter. Filet Mignon was exquisite per my Brother's comments and my vegetable platter was lovely. The desert of Profiterole was tres delicieux as well. HIGHLY RECOMMEND Cons (although not really a Con) 1) Was hoping to meet the charming and famed Chef himself-in addition to the french accented hostess, but to no avail. Maybe I have to come on a Friday or weekend night? 2) The location can be good and bad. It's a little ways away from the main restaurants that I'm used to eating in NY, but perhaps this out of place-ness adds to the allure and charm of the place. 3) We did wait a little longer for our entrees than I thought was necessary-at least it seemed like a good 30 minute wait. Maybe this was just due to the kitchen aromas smelling so wonderful. Overall, wonderful experience, and I have already recommended to my friends. Will definitely come back-maybe even this weekend! :) Merci beaucoup for the wonderful food and service! I wish you were in San Francisco or Los Angeles-you would do so so well there! (plus you would have a regular patron)

I've been to a few Peruvian restaurants now and this is by far the best. Every single thing we had here was incredible. We started with the shrimp and avocado appetizer and it was so unique; unlike anything I've ever had and filled with flavor. My fiancÃ© had aji de gallina which is one of our favorite traditional Peruvian dishes and it was out of this world. I had the lomo saltado. It was so flavorful. I can't wait to go again to see what the rest of the items taste like because I doubt we just happened to hit the jackpot!

Great atmosphere great service. I would recommend the pizza all of them are really good. Their platters on the other hand not worth the price subpar flavor. I would go back to this place but only for their unique pizzas.

3 1/2 stars I made a reservation for brunch here last Saturday. They wouldn't seat us until our entire party arrived (understandably), but then they put us in the middle of the communal table. I wouldn't have picked this place had I known we would have no privacy. To make matters worse, every time a waiter walked by on his/her way to the kitchen, I got nudged in the back. The food itself was very tasty (I had a brekkie sammich with duck prosciutto) and everyone found something to her liking to order. Just wish the ambience were a little nicer.

It's a British pub that serves food seasonal British & Italian. Â I came here with a good friend (hopefully more) after an off-broadway show "Sleepwalk With Me." Â This restaurant fits with the Village. Â I'd recommend the Sheep's Ricotta Gnudi with Brown Butter & Sage Lamb Heart; Chargrilled Burger with Roquefort Cheese & Shoestrings compliments of Malbec red wine. Â The burger is seasoned with Roquefort Cheese one does not need other condiments of ketchup or salt since the cheese gives it flavor. Â The shoestrings fries are seasoned with salt thus ketchup is not needed. Â Since it's themed to a British pub patrons are sitting on stools rather than actual chairs even if it's at a table or by the bar. I do not recommend this restaurant for children or for veggietarians. Â The Spotted Pig does not accept reservations or delivery or take-out. Â The name of this restaurant/bar saids it all: Â Spotted Pig which implies meat. Rather than actual business cards, Spotted Pig distributes coasters with their name, address and phone number but no web site as their indifference. I rate it four stars due to lack of space to hang coats or jackets.

Went there a few weeks ago for lunch. The portion was SOOO tiny. And I am 120% sure the chicken was cooked the night before. Service was good, which is the reason i gave it 3 stars, but I'd given them 2 if it wasn't for that.

it's weird - everything i tried here, i could say, 'hey this is good and well-made' but simultaneously thinking, 'i don't really enjoy it' needless to say an hour later at lunch Michael Psilakis gave me a free kebab sandwich amazing, dreamy space (top floor)

I came here again for dinner on a Friday night. Â The host was WAY nicer than the previous time I came around. Â The wait for 2 people around 8:30pm was stated to be 1.5 hours...but we were encouraged to have a seat at the bar, and if a spot opened up, we could order the full menu at the bar. Â We decided to do this and in about 15 minutes, we secured two spots at the bar. Â  First of all: Â Freeman's is NOT veggie friendly, there are a few options, but not extensive. Â Lucky for me, that is not a problem. I first ordered an old cuban, which is a twist on a normal mojito, and it was slurping down to the last drop good. Â It was made with dark rum and molasses syrup (!) and was just right! Â I also ordered the freeman-tini or whatever it is called - freeman's signature cocktail, and that was also very good, but really more of a "girly drink". Â  We started with two appetizers - the devils on horseback (SO FREAKING GOOD!) and the spinach artichoke dip (good, but not as good as the devils on horseback). Â We shared the fluke entree which was okay - kind of a new take on chinese food if that makes any sense. Â For dessert we ordered blueberry cobbler...again, i was AMAZED...it was SO finger licking good! Â  We closed down the bar, haha...our server/bartender Yanna was SO friendly and funny and nice to talk to. Â We talked to the host for a good 20 minutes after the restaurant closed down about celebrity sightings/etc. Â  I think this has become my new favorite restaurant in NYC :) Â hoorah!
Good food but service that is beyond terrible.

I hate to say it (updated) but the truck is better than the restaurant... is that possible? , Well, it's the reality. The restaurant is inconsistent. I have raved about it to friends and sometimes have had to explainthat the food was just not at top form. dry meats in the tacos, no special taste. Other times, friends will be so awestruck they will become immediately loyal regulars. The truck, on the other hand, is always great

This place is pretty good and the prices are great. Â I really enjoyed the torta I had. Â The chipotle chicken taco was pretty bland and pretty disappointing on the spice level. Â If I lived close, I would go all the time, but I don't and it is not worth the hour subway ride.

I can't give this more than 1 star because from start to finish the experience was a disaster. Ran out of rose, spaghetti and lobster came out with lobster covered in sauce in the shell and when I asked to have the kitchen remove the shell it was returned with part of the tail- none of the claw. That's when confusion in the kitchen began- saying their was no more lobster meat- I've never seen a lobster without claw meat- have you? Dishes were removed before everyone was done. And then they couldn't process credit cards. The overall confusion was unlike any I've seen in NY. I give it 1 star because the waitress was giving it her all and the food tasted good. The headache in the middle of the night from 1 glass of wine and the upset stomach along with the experience prevent a second star.

This little restaurant has warm inviting vibe for dinner with a cottage quaint yet updated feel. Â The place was dim but not so dark where you can't see what you're eating (hate that). Â We were seated for dinner right away on a Sunday night. Â  Fried brussel sprouts were nice and crispy. Â Griiled yellowfin tuna in curry cream sauce was really good. Â Friends got the arctic char and duck breast. Â Everyone was happy. Â I guess everyone comes here for brunch, but the dinner was pretty good.

we received a box of macaroons from a friend as a gift; and they were pretty amazing, for the most part. Â judging by the reviews, she didn't pick some of the most popular flavors. Â of the 6 flavors we had, vanilla and raspberry were the best. Â the lovely box in which the macaroons come is rather exquisite. Â and the macaroons are each so dainty and cute. Â we just scanned the reviews here, and the price is steep. Â you can't just eat one, or two, or three. Â my wife had eight in one sitting, right after lunch.

This is one of my all time favorite spots in Williamsburg! They have a really amazing atmosphere with cozy little nooks that are good for both small and large parties. The bar tenders are incredibly helpful and suggest great pairing with your meal. My personal favorite ceviche is the Salmon, it has an incredible mouth feel and flavor. The cocktails are very unique and they make a killer Michelada!! Also, their 1$ oyster happy hr is amazing and far less chaotic than Maison Premiere's (we had no wait and great service!!). Plus, the truffle oil infused popcorn will become your new addiction once you try it!

Mmmmm I was searching high and low for a tasty, chill, casual, sit down seafood restaurant - I found fish! It was exactly what I imagined it to be. It was really the $8 red white and blue special that sold me - 6 oysters with your choice of house red wine, white wine or PBR. We also got the lobster mashed potatoes $9 and the sea of fundy salmon $14. Â The salmon was delicious!! It was perfectly grilled, seasoned and cooked. Â Not over cooked nor not under cooked - which I find a lot of restaurants have problems doing. I definitely recommend it as it is the cheapest fish on the menu and it did not disappoint. Â I can only imagine how good the rest of the entrees are. We showed up at 9pm on a Wednesday and waited for about 20 minutes, they don't take reservations. Once this diet is over, I'm coming back to devour the rest of the menu!

Well, I think I found my new favorite place in Williamsburg. The place itself is very cozy with some antique decor and lighting reminiscent of the Prohibition era. The food menu has some delicious options, especially the chicken. The special cocktails are very creative and they are made with some tender loving care by the very friendly and accommodating staff here. Will definitely be coming back as often as I can. Highly recommend this place for romantic dates and small group gatherings. They also have small jazz concerts on certain nights!

Outstanding in every way! Our brunch experience at Feast was worth the trip. First of all, the decor and atmosphere is great. Every detail and design is very well thought out. The service is close to perfect and attentive. We had the Steak n Egg and Crab & Artichoke Benedict. Both dishes were interesting and prepared well. The croissants, muffin, pea and tomato soup, and quiche are all great warm ups for the main course. They know how to make a cup of coffee here! It was 11am on Sunday, so I did not have a beer. I mention this because they have a nice beer list with Founders All Day IPA, Keegan's Mothers Milk Stout, and a great Belgian beer that caught my eye. From the lighting to the business cards to the soap in the bathroom, Feast is great in every way. We will be back Â soon to enjoy dinner and beers.

simply put: tasty! went here in august for my sisters birthday and it was a great experience. the food was rich and flavorful, even the appetizers were a great crowd pleaser. i had the cavatelli, my sister had the spaghetti, my mom had the cod, i can't quite remember what my brother and dad had but i know we were all quite satisfied.

Came here on a Saturday for a lunch date. We were walking around SoHo shopping and found this little bistro to duck in to. It was pretty small, one of those places where the oversized menu took up more space then you had on the table. The service was great for a place like this, quick and painless. I ordered the penne pasta with shrimp and scallops. It was very solid, no complaints. The pasta was well cooked and the seafood was also well prepared. I should have asked for some crushed red peppers to throw on top and it would have been pretty bangin. If you're shopping in the area I definitely suggest you stop in grab a bite.

This is the best pizza in New York. If you haven't been here and loves pizza, please give it a try. Don't expect a fancy restaurant, its just a small humble place in the corner of Avenue J in Brooklyn.You also might have to wait a while to get your slice... No doubt its totally worth it! Its DELICIOUS, almost perfect. ;)

I had to give Prospect a review after an outstanding dinner last night. Â If there's one drawback to Prospect, it's that they don't have many tables, so it's hard to get a reservation, and the bar is pretty packed with those still wanting to eat or drink here. Â But walk-ins are welcome, and with no reservation available, my partner and I were Â offered seats at the chef's counter, which frankly, I prefer. Â I love to watch the kitchen in action. The five stars were earned mainly for two reasons: Â 1) the Prospect Sour cocktail was absolutely superb. Â They have a pretty decent original cocktail list and a nice wine selection by the glass, which complimented all of our dishes. 2) The Long Island Fluke was one of the best fish dishes I have had in recent memory. Â The fish was perfect, seared to a wonderful crispiness on top and flaky underneath. Â Served with what they call "flavors of New England clam chowder," it was a nice deconstruction, with some delicious clams on top of charred leeks, crispy pork belly and small round potatoes. Â Absolutely delicious when all brought together. I look forward to trying the tasting menu in the future.

I don't think that there is much more to add to the glowing reviews, but I will say that if you are only in Brooklyn for a short period of time and have to choose a place to have lunch, go here!! Especially if the weather is nice. We got lucky! The bathrooms kinda blew me away- completely Eco friendly and run on rain water....it's like you are doing your biz outside, but not really......or in the privacy of the Redwoods. The tacos are yummy- pretty generous and made outta a truck in the back. These, plus a bucket of coronas equals a pretty nice afternoon! Note: this place gets packed!!!! Arrive early and expect long lines. Go with friends, as there is picnic table style seating outside!

Everyone told me that this is the best pizza and that I had to eat there. I am a big pizza guy and I was really disappointed. I am from Miami and I have tried many pizza joints but this is not even close to my top 20. Â In fact while I was in NY I probably ate at 5 better pizza joints. First of all they are so over prized that it is not even funny. We had a big pizza w 3 toppings and it was $35. The only way I would eat this pizza again, would be if they sold it for $8. Honestly, I rather order papa johns and I don't even like pizza chains. The service was good and the atmosphere was ok but I will never eat there again. Over hyped, stay away and go eat at any other pizza place!

I came here from Manhattan in 30 degree weather and took three trains to get here. My 68 year old aunt and I ordered the drunken noodles, crispy watercress salad, coconut rice, crispy chicken with cashews, tom yum soup, lychee ice cream sorbet, green tea, ginger ale, & Thai ice tea. We had excellent service on a Sunday lunch hour. My aunt wanted three different drinks and two desserts and the waiter was speedy! Overall, my favorite has got to be the crispy watercress salad, crispy chicken with cashews and drunken noodles. The crispy watercress salad is crisp and crunchy with shrimp sauce that is very savory. As our appetizer it set the stage for the drunken noodles and chicken. My aunt had to come twice in one week because she loved the food so much. The food is reasonably priced and I am sure I will take guests here!
The best place to eat in Brooklyn, hands down! Good coffee, good service, the food is incredible, they nail it every time without fail. Thank you Five Leaves!!

Wow. So much food. For so little money. And delicious food at that. Did I mention the quantity is pretty substantial (I couldn't finish a whole one by myself!)... luckily my friend eats enough for 3 people! =) Now a falafel isn't the easiest thing to eat (so messy!)... but eating a scrumptious falafel at Mamoun's (with hot sauce) is SO worth the mess! Whether you enjoy this for lunch, dinner or a late night snack - just be prepared to wait in line!

I love the pizza here! Grimaldi's line was super long, so we went next door and decided to try Juliana's. We find out that Mr. Grimaldi himself greeted us at the door. He named the restaurant after his mother. The service was great too, one of my friend's phone battery ran out and they even charged it for us. We tried the White Pizza, Pizza Special # 4, and the Margarita. My favorite was the Margarita! Give it a try the next time you visit the Brooklyn Bridge.

I've since tried the wings (muy caliente) and I recommend them but I reeeeally dig their Beef on Weck (a Buffalo tradition). What's a weck you ask? Short for kummelweck...it's a caraway seed roll that's in perfect harmony with the thinly sliced juicy roast beef. This sucka melts in yo mouth!

Me: So the Totto/Torys/Kinnosuke group opened a ramen place called Totto Ramen. I double checked Yelp to make sure Totto is still open (Torys closed.) Totto's still open but omfg it's categorized under dim sum. Dim. Sum. W T F Him: I think they opened a place above Sakagura across from Yasuda. Him: Ramen is chinese food! Me: No. Yakitori Totto is categorized under dim sum. Him: Maybe they have gyoza Me: No they do not Him: Maybe David Chang is a partner now. Me: Does not count Dear Yelp, Why is Totto categorized under dim sum? Please fix -- it is offensive, borderline criminal. Thank you.

I've been to my fair share of Ramen Restaurants in San Francisco, but I don't think I've ever had Ramen quite like New York's Ippudo! We came here on a weekday night for a friend's birthday and had to wait for a bit, but that was fine since we grabbed a couple of drinks at the bar. They seated our large group at one of the booth tables, which comfortably seated all of us. My boyfriend and I ordered the Pork Belly Buns first, and what was absolutely amazing! It was super soft and the pork literally melted in your mouth! It's a must get when you come here. We also ordered Ramen, which the two of us shared. We would've gotten our own but we had been eating the entire day so our appetites weren't as big as we hoped. The Ramen, again, was the BEST I have tried. The noodles were perfect and not soggy, and the broth was amazing. Not bland, and not salty - but just right. Next time we're in New York, we'll definitely be back to get our own bowls!
Went there Friday night with friends Food, Drinks and Service was excellent The Mojitos are strong and tasty Will be back again soon

Good food, simple place, friendly service. We had the chasha momos (the best since Â the ones I had in Kolkata), and Chasha Shamdey. The shamdey was above average. The chicken was overcooked. The green tea ice cream was really good but the deysee was not something I would order again. It was good, but did not satisfy my palate.

I made a reservation here last Friday night for my wife's birthday. I could only get in at 5:45pm. I thought to myself, "Great. It will be us eating in an empty dining room while the waitstaff folds napkins & rushes us out the door." I couldn't have been more surprised when I got to this place. First of all, the bar was hopping. The long bar was filled with people, but not overly crowded yet. That happened around 7pm. Yes, we were there to see the 7pm crowd so you now know they didn't rush us. Back to the bar, quick service with a small, but good, selection of craft beers. I expected only Peroni or Moretti. Once seated, our waiter immediately took our orders, but didn't rush right into the specials or the menu. She gave us a chance to unwind, and get comfortable. That's when I took a look around, and noticed that the place was already filling up. There was also good music pumping through the sound system. I didn't feel like a blue-hair out for an early bird special after all. When the waiter came back, she told us the specials and took our orders. The first course came out rather quickly. Here's the rush I thought, but again I was wrong. The service and pace of the meal was executed as perfectly as the dishes we ate. They intelligently got our first course of sheep's goat ricotta and lamb meatball sliders out to us quickly because I think everyone is a bit hungry and anxious when they sit down. Those 2 dishes are a must, and really kicked off an amazing meal that unlike most Italian meals did not sit like a rock in my stomach. Nor did I feel like 6 miles at the gym the next day were necessary to remove it from my waistline. We continued after the first course to the pasta course...The pappardelle verde. It was a white bolognese. Great appearance and was good. It was the only dish that didn't wow us. It was just good. We both had fish...sea scallops which were perfect. Not a bit of grittiness. I had the roasted halibut over brussel sprouts and polenta. The fish, which was a special, was so fresh and flaky while the subtle hint of truffle in the polenta blew me away. We circled back around to the pasta again...well, just because. We were enjoying the food so much, and having such a great time that we figured why not. The ravioli. I think it's called Grandma's Ravioli. Delicious! Lamb and veal ravioli. These were the lightest, most amazing ravioli I've tasted in a long time. I can't rave enough at this place. I can't speak for the wine list as we went by the glass. I will tell you this...they let you bring your own bottle, but keep in mind they charge a $35 corking fee. That's the worst thing I can say about this place. What I thought was going to be a rushed dinner ended up being an amazing, romantic, almost 2.5 hour dining experience.

I wanted to have a better experience here, but unfortunately, a few things really brought our night down. 1. My boyfriend and I both love spicy food, so we asked for our shrimp and crawfish to be made "spicy," which isn't even the highest level of spicyness they offer (it's still a step down from "fire"). Yet our food was at a level of spicyness that almost made it inedible. It was so hard to enjoy because we were in serious pain the entire time. I actually felt my throat burning. We couldn't even eat any of the potatoes because they were so doused in the sauce of death. We tried our hardest to enjoy the food, but this seriously put a damper on the experience. 2. We got a shrimp/crawfish combination and I was disappointed to see that they only gave us one half cob of corn with it. I mean, come on, there are two of us... at least give us two pieces of corn. We had to share one sad half-cob. 3. We were told the wait would be 30 minutes and it ended up being almost an hour. 4. Our waitress didn't check on us until a good 15 or 20 minutes into the meal. If she had checked on us earlier, I would've told her how unbelievably spicy the food was, and maybe we could have gotten it re-made with a less spicy sauce, allowing us to enjoy our meals. But it was already getting late and we didn't have all night to sit and wait for her attention. Other than that, beneath the layer of deathly sauce, the shrimp and crawfish were very good. The shrimp were the plumpest I've ever had. And the whole experience is fun; the entire table is covered in paper, they put bibs on you, you get rubber gloves... it's just fun to have a super messy meal. Pretty cute place too. I might give it one more shot, but this time I'll be ordering everything "mild" or "medium." Being someone who puts crushed red pepper by the tablespoon in everything I eat, I thought I could handle my food "spicy," but either they screwed up our meals, or their concept of spicy is on a whole other level.

Good menu with a variety of very authentic dishes and everything was prepared very well. Â The Moqueca was excellent and I'm usually not a big guac fan but there's was very refreshing and had a lot of flavor. Â Pretty casual, not too expensive service made good recommendations but was very slow. Â Also note that a lot of their corn meal options are gluten free.

Stopped in here for lunch today, got the shrimp and avocado wrap, excellent. Â White peach sangria was good, refreshing, not very peachy, but had plenty of booze-soaked fruit floating about in it. The Bayou is cool, classy New Orleans, think elegant Garden District not sleazy Storyville. Â Exposed brick walls mixed with wainscoting,g audy chandeliers, movie posters of Marlon Brando and Vivian Leigh, bathrooms named Stella and Stanley, and an antique-framed portrait resembling a Frenchified version of Pope's THE RAPE OF THE LOCK. Â  The lamb and the seafood jambalaya makes me want to come back.

Ok, I admit that I have ordered the same things here over and over again, so the majority of their menu is still a mystery to me. But, the pastrami, reuben, Original NY cheesecake, and chocolate mousse cheesecake are consistently delicious. The Black and White cookie is a solid A, not the best I've ever had, but good; the only disappointing items I've had are the fries and onion rings.
Amazing shrimp tacos, the BEST I've ever had. Service is relaxed, welcoming and very kind.

I had the pleasure of coming to this place without having to wait in line (came early around noon on Saturday) so that was a good first impression. I had moderate expectations coming into this place, not having read any reviews; just word of mouth. I ordered a slice of artichoke and spinach, and a slice of crab, and boy was I pleasantly surprised. A part of me wishes that I didn't have a baby shower to go to that afternoon (which was catered by Bon Chon and Empanada Mama's) because I really did want to try a slice of Sicilian. So we're all pretty tired of new "old-timey" bars and speakeasies. It's starting to get a bit gimmicky, with bartenders wearing suspenders and secret entrances, passwords, and other Scooby-Doo type antics to get inside. I mean, we have plenty of authentic 19th century pubs in NYC, and we also have theme bars like Jekyll and Hyde and The Slaughtered Lamb, so do we really need yet another "saloon"? Turns out, yes we do, if we're referring to The Dead Rabbit. Not only is it in an historic landmarked building, but it's also been styled with care, with reclaimed wood beam ceilings and pictures of 19th-century personalities lining the walls - and not just white guys, either! The down side is that it was hugely crowded downstairs on a Thursday night. Just wall to wall people, and the music was too loud, even though it was traditional Irish folk music, but you know, even a lyre can be annoying at high volumes. I really don't understand why bars do this - it's already packed and noisy with people shouting, what's the point of blasting the music? However, there was a simple solution: the quiet upstairs "parlor." We waited about a half-hour for our party of four to be seated upstairs, and the concierge couldn't have been nicer. Once settled in the cozy parlor, we were given complimentary samples of punch in small teacups, small glasses of water, and elaborate menus bound up like a 19th century book. Certainly the most beautiful menu I have ever seen! The reason it's so long is because of the pages and pages of 19th century drinks, all of which have been carefully researched and sourced. The name of the bar comes from a famous NYC gang of the 1860s, so the drinks are from that era. Surprisingly, each drink is attributed to its original source. It's the only bar menu I've ever seen with footnotes! I know that mixology has had a revival and you can find "bespoke cocktails" as they call them, at many places (I have no idea why they are called that - every cocktail is "bespoke" i.e. made to order). But Dead Rabbit outdoes them all. Serious culinary historians would have no qualms about their menu and the historical research behind it. My companions had beer and conventional cocktails, whereas I went a more traditional route with hot whiskey toddy. I was a little surprised it was served in a stem glass, but the temperature was perfect, and it was definitely the best toddy I've had. Really took the edge of the cold that was creeping it, so I had another! I also had the Welsh Rabbit, which was okay, more like an appetizer than a hearty dish, but my British companion told me it's served differently everywhere (I was expecting toasted bread covered with a cheese-and-beer sauce, but at the Dead Rabbit, it's more like toast points with a crust of cheese). I also had the Zucchini Fritters which were delicious. I wish they served regular meals after hours, but apparently they only serve full meals at lunch. My companion had the veal meatballs, which looked quite hearty and satisfying, but alas, I am a vegetarian, and the veggy bar snack selection wasn't too expansive, but since they serve British-style food, I'm accustomed to British cuisine being veg-unfriendly. I am not exactly sure why they serve British cuisine - by the 1860s, America had its own cuisine. I really can't picture Bill the Butcher eating Welsh Rabbit. It could be that the 1860s American bar snacks would be too unpalatable - they were big on things like pigs' ears and knuckles. One warning: this place ain't cheap. I spent about $55 on two whiskey toddies and two small plates of bar snacks. However, I had a great time and I can't honestly say it wasn't worth it. I didn't feel fleeced when I left, but rather that I had paid for a truly quality experience with excellent service, fine drinks, and tasty snacks. I just hope the thrill wears off so I can check out the downstairs when it's not so crowded!

Yay!!! Awesome Italian trattoria in my hood! I've been living in HK for over 4 years and Tuesday was my first time at Tavola, shame on me. I ordered a bottle of wine form their short and not that interesting list and the bartender proceeded to open it and pour 4 glasses without so much as showing me the bottle let alone letting me taste it. It ws a mediocre Aglianaco at best and when he asked me what I thought his response to my meh was to just shrug..huh?! One of my friends had gotten there a bit early and was having a conversation with a gentleman that was eating at the bar, everything he was having looked fabulous. It turns out that he is the owner. Once we sat down he came over and told us about the olive oil and mentioned some of the specials we should order and told us that the pasta dish he was eating wasn't on the menu but the kitchen would make it for us...score!! Now I wasn't going to mention what happened next but the way the waiter handled the situation was really rude and almost ruined our night. When he came to take our order my friend told him about the pasta and asked if we could have an order of it. He very disgustingly said "I have no idea what you're talking about" My friend was insistant, even stating the ingredients and asking if the kitchen could make it and he was just as insistant "not ever going to happen" She asked if the owner was still there, our waiter said no and was completely dismissive. Well excuse us! he really was NOT nice about it. Oh well, the food was good enough to ignore his slight. We ordered a boatload off the menu. 1. Mediterranean salad - BARREL AGED FETA, PERSIAN CUCUMBERS, VINE TOMATOES - just OK 2. BURRATA WOOD FIRED RED PEPPERS, CHERRY TOMATO BASIL SALAD. IMPORTED FROM PUGLIA - excellent burrata and the bread and olive oil are fantastic 3. ORECCHIETTE ESPOSITO SAUSAGE BROCCOLI RABE ROASTED BREAD CRUMBS - I'll have to admit that they were a little skimpy on the sausage but the flavor was very good. I don't think the orecchiette was homemade but the dish was still great. 4. PIZZA DEL GIORNO - this one had meatballs, carmelized onions and a few other ingredients, pizza is definitely their strong suit. 5. MARKET FISH (DEL GIORNO) - whole branzino and I will say that this was in the top 3 best whole roasted branzino I've ever had...well done! 6. Gelato Pistachio Crushed Amaretti - I'm not usually a dessert person but this is worth ordering. There is a hard crust around a huge ball of gelato, perfect ending. 7. Tiramisu - above average. We did end up ordering another bottle of wine, the Rosso di Montalcino, and although it wasn't served at the proper temperature at least it was presented. I'm really glad I finally was introduced to this place as it's a great neighborhood spot, lively, warm atmosphere and great food. I'll be back!

Went tonight for drinks and dinner and everything was simply fabulous .... from the wine (Cabernet, which was a "special") to the cheese plate (cheese from Murray's and bread from Boulangerie!) and small plates (lamb meatballs, sliders and mushroom/Manchego quesadilla). I'm trying not to be bias but compared to Cara Cas in the East Village it was not as good. This place really needs a good sauce for the arepas like Cara Cas. Every time I'm on Ditmars there's a line of people waiting to eat here. Walking by it always smells delicious, but I hate waiting for a table, so I've been reluctant to try it out. After finally eating here, I understand why so many people are willing to wait. At the suggestion of others we order the fried calamari. It was cooked well, and the batter was crunchy without being overpowering. They bring out lemons in the beginning of the meal so I sacrificed one to adding a bit of extra zest. For our main course I had the quail and my friend had the grilled baby shark. Just to state, neither of us have ever had either of these dishes before so we had a limited frame of reference. The grilled shark honestly tasted like chicken. It wasn't a 'fishy' tasted, but tasted fresh nonetheless. The portions were absolutely huge for this dish and half of it came home with us. The quail dish came with three fully intact birds. The skin was crunchy and well seasoned, but the dish still left something to be desired. Having not eaten quail before, getting the meat off the bone proved difficult, but that is by no means a mark on the establishment. However, if you've never had quail before, I'd steer clear if you're on a date. The cake/pudding that came at the end was really good and had a touch of cinnamon which I loved. All in all, the food is really fresh and worth trying!

If you've ever wondered what real falafel should taste like, then you must try some from "The King". Just as the name suggests, these guys are the real deal. Crispy, moist, and flavorful falafel. With all the talk about falafel, yes, their shwarma is just as good! Succulent morsels of juicy lamb, chicken and beef, are placed over a bed of rice and mixed with pickled vegetables, lettuce, onions, and drizzled with yogurt and hot sauce. ( easy on the hot sauce though, no joke!) This location is the original, with a second smaller spot over on 30th ave. and 33rd street.

When I started living in NYC 5 years ago, I lived right across the street from Yasuda and came here all the time (once a week).. after having eaten in many sushi restaurants in Japan, I could def. attest that Yasuda's quality was on par with many of the top places in Japan. Sadly, it seems that Yasuda's quality has deteriorated recently, most notably this year. There were several times this year when I got a piece of fish that tasted very fishy. I've also noticed a higher than expected turnover..while restaurant turnover is completely normal, I remember that I used to see new trainees working behind other sushi chefs (rather than serving sushi up front as a sushi chef), and were required to work for the chefs for much longer before being promoted. Now it seems that more and more of the faces that I see at the sushi counter are new. The experience for me has changed, perhaps because I miss walking into a restaurant and sitting in front of my favorite chef...perhaps because the restaurant just feels very cold and corporate, or perhaps the quality just isn't on par with what it once was.
