I dont really understand how can people go to places like this living in NYC. Expensive, just normal food and deco is so ugly. I have the feeling just for the sake of being in Upper East is at least twice the price you would get anywhere else. Mediocre sandwich, mediocre tuna salad, same for a simple coffee for which u have to pay 5 buck??? Hello??

i've been going here for maybe about 18 years now. only recently have prices gone up to $2.50 for falafel and $4.50 for schwarma and it got a pretty new chalkboard menu. you dont go here for the decore though the energy level of the people waiting on line is very high. The guys putting together your sandwiches work in harmony and is quite entertaining to watch when their really busy. there are several falafel spots on the block. just look for the line of people out the door. Delicious and cheap!!!

Best burger I've ever had, though to qualify: they don't actually serve burgers. As your server will explain to you, they only use premium cuts of steak, not your regular ground beef. Consequently, they recommend you order yours medium rare, and I have to back them up. It was the juiciest, most flavorful bite of burger I've tasted, not just in NYC but anywhere. Last night I had the truffle burger, which was very saucy with good but not overwhelming truffle flavor. The rolls are stamped with what our waitress referred to as a plant-based dye stamp at the bakery. The tempura onion rings were crisp and stayed together like the best onion rings do, the fries were long and crispy on the outside, soft and tender on the inside, and the parmesan tater tots melted in our mouths. The drinks are all locally inspired and thus named. I had the market, which was super refreshing on a hot day if a little overwhelmingly fruity (should have figured that out on my own, being named after a farmers' market). People are complaining about long lines. ours was 2.5 hours on a Sunday night. Fortunately, it's in a very central village location, and they not only will text you when your table is ready and then wait for you to get there, but they have an online checking site to see how far along you are on the list. We only waited 10 minutes once we got to the place to be seated. It was so good I went for lunch today, and while there was a sizeable wait, I was seated at the bar in less than a minute. I ordered as soon as the bartender came over (Manly Burger and Truffle fries, just as good as last night), and was served in less than ten minutes. Sadly, when I ordered, the diners on either side of me had already been apologized to for their food taking so long. To all of our surprise, my food came out first, then theirs minutes later. They were so hungry that they actually finished their burgers first. When asked how they were enjoying their burgers, they said "outstanding," so I'm assuming that the food overcame the sour taste that the wait left in their mouths. The manager told them that their meals were complimentary, which was a nice gesture on the first week of business when they're just getting on their feet. No competition here, Umami is the king of burgers. Thank you for sharing, LA.

Came here for brunch, and I've got to say that the duck and waffles is truly something special. I went there a few weeks ago, and I still remember eating it and thinking "wow, this is an awesome marriage of both savory and sweet." I also had the privilege of trying the pork buns as well, and those were also awesome--practically no surprise there. Ssam bar has some really unique dishes here, and Â I think Asian Fusion Cuisine really fits the bill for this place. I would come back here again, as there were so many things I wanted to try on the menu it was really hard to narrow it down to just one.

This week we dined at Hearth for the fourth time in 12 months. For the fourth time, Heath left a lasting impression. This is our first YELP (sorry, Marco). Here's the deal, for those who do not want to read through my notes...Hens of the Woods. Again, I repeat...Hens of the Woods. Amazing. The best mushrooms we have ever tasted (4 times...). The ambiance at Hearth is attractive, well appointed and perfectly lit. The staff is attentive and kind. While the menu was simple, it is very impressive and includes local in season ingredients. The wine list was biblical--covering Old Testament and New. Simply stated, when in Manhattan, go to Hearth. Ciao!

Delicious. Each time I have been everything is great. The arugula salad is large enough to share and very fresh. The cheese plate is versatile w soft, semi SPF and hard cheese plus olives. The spaghetti with garlic and olive oil is beyond flavorful. It's almost as if the garlic is roasted in their volcanic oven. Yum. The pizza dough is delicious. Soft fresh and flavorful. The sauce is delightful. The service is friendly. They have yummy flavored Italian soda. Desserts are fresh. And cappuccino is yummy (especially if you add the cream from the tartufo). The only compliant is the bread basket. It would be 20x better if they used their own dough. The bread is sad but eatable.
I'd give it 3.5 stars, if I could. It's very good, but lagging behind the usual upscale pizza suspects.

I came here for brunch around 2pm with a friend and there was a 45 minute wait. Â We weren't in a rush so we just walked around for awhile. Â We orderd the fried chicken sandwich and the burger - both were delicious. Â The service was quick (probably because they have 45 min waits) but they did not rush us and both the host and the waitress were incredibly friendly. Â  I plan on coming back for dinner.

I came here with high expectations due to the reviews, but everything was mediocre or below mediocre. The complimentary banchan dishes were few in selections and very uninteresting. The deep fried mackerel was filled with bones and was cold. The seafood soondubu was not flavorful. I've had much better soondubu at $10/bowl in Philly than this. With mediocre food, what disappointed me the most was the horrible service. The water were not refilled until asked. When the waitress was scrapping the rice with tea to put it in the bowls, she splashed my friend a few times and failed to even apologize. When we were getting ready to leave, she sort of pushed me away and grabbed the CC receipt before I even finished putting my coat on.

So I only write reviews for places when I think the staff goes above and beyond or really sucks. Sugar Freak goes above and beyond. We came tonight-cold, rainy, just plain blah. Took 20 minutes to find parking, and when we arrived, we were told that there was a 45 minute wait. I was not happy. There was however plenty of room at the bar. I started with a sugar honey iced tea. Delicious. We ended up waiting only about 25 minutes which was awesome. We skipped apps and went straight to the entrees. I had the pulled pork and the mister had the freak special-fried chicken with Mac n cheese on top. SO FREAKING GOOD. I wasn't really a big fan of the pulled pork so when our waiter came back he felt bad and threw the dessert on the house! Everyone here is amazingly nice and the food is Delish! I will definitely be back to try more!

I havent had the pleasure of eating difaras for the past 2 months which has been terrible for me, yes thats how good this pizza is. As a pizza aficionado living in nc is tough, there is not one good pizza place. Therefore, i spend most of my time in new york. The first time I went into this place I knew it was great. Where else, can a place be this dirty and stay open? There is only one answer to that the best pizza place in the country. The 3 cheeses Dom uses on his sicilian are to die for. People, forget about the wait just judge the food. And to me, this pizza is top 5 in the country.
Great little place with friendly service. Very relaxing atmosphere. Simple and tasty dishes - will be coming back!

I've never actually stayed to eat here, but I've ordered to go several times. After a handful of some mentors of mine brought pizza from Adrienne's over, I knew I had to go there someday. None the less, there is something about New York City pizza that I miss so dearly, and this is one of them!

To find empanadas in NYC like i had in Argentina...Oh, what would I do. Â  I'd say it's a good snack if you want to try one. Â Prices are good. Â  They are decent. Â I'm afraid the problem is for those who have had them in Argentina -- there the doughy soft crust is so perfect, they are baked, not fried, the fillings delicious and they are huge! Â  I am still on the search but somehow don't think I'll ever find them here....

We accidentally stumpled into this awesome restaurant (without a reservation!). Â It was Â great and we lated realised that it's by Lidia's family!!! Â The pasta was great, especially for its tasting dinner menu where you can try various types of pasta special that they are serving. Â I am usually not a huge pasta fan, but it was so tasty that I even asked for refill!

Friendly service that is attentive and informative... Decor is simple yet welcoming. Menu is simple and filled with tasty options made with love. Burritos and tacos made like they do back in the home country... Reasonably priced and with every penny. You will not be disappointed
burger and charcuterie is good. bone marrow was cold, tasted a little stale. nick the waiter is cute and music and atmosphere is fun. Â otherwise, food is pretty mediocre.

Solid ramen, delicious pork buns, but inconsistent service. I have been to both ippudos many times. Recently I have been frequenting the hk locations more. The wait is usually less than an hour, but the service is questionable. Food: Pork buns - soft white bread, juicy pork. Can add a little less spicy mayo. Kakarumen - love the spiciness and creaminess of the broth. Pork could be a bit more tender, but overall good balance of pork, cabbage and mushrooms. Noodles are al dente. Service is generally pleasant, but our most recent waitress, radar, was awful. No smile and v short with us. I would definitely come again for the food, but request another waitress when we go back.

Stopped in after reading the rave reviews and was not disappointed one bit. Actually, this place exceeded all expectations. First off, the "A" rating on the door was a wonderful welcome sign for someone visiting from out of town... from a very foodie part of the world, PORTLAND, OR! We can't get great Indian food like this in Portland. Sad, but true. Amazing service, very warm and welcoming. Ordered tikka masala and it was incredible (not too creamy and overly buttery tasting... perfect in my opinion). Samosas, amazing and served with a trio of tasty sauces/chutney. The garlic naan was super fresh and hot out of the oven. Quite addicting. My only complaint is that I wish we had been hungrier to try more dishes. We'll be back!

For the longest time, I had a lot of reservation about Quaint. I didn't want to go back because I thought their food was tame (not lame) and uninteresting, for a relatively pricey menu. I heard that they might have reduced the prices, which I'm still not sure about, but it gave me push to try again, albeit a prolonged avoidance. Truth is, now I am quite glad that there is somewhere to go for a decent cheese burger with real fries in Sunnyside! And it's only 10 bucks! A real inch-thick patty, despite a bit heavy on the salt, it was quite juicy (I have to stress that I ordered it medium-well and it was still juicy). The bun was a bit sad and dry, but I usually don't prefer too much bread, so it sort of worked out. I really enjoyed the medium-cut fries, though I thought they were a bit cheap on the ketchup. I love loads of ketchup on my fries, whatever. I could've asked for more, the staff was attentive and friendly. The chef seems to be partial to quinoa and even offers it as a side. How cool is that? As for the classic cocktails on the menu, they serve them with a modern touch: such as Old Fashioned with muddled fruits (orange and cherries). I quite enjoyed it. I'll probably go back again when I crave for a beef burger, but I am still not sure about the other dishes, they look the same to me - tame and uninteresting. So quaint!

We went there for dinner first (could have had it during the show) and the food was good. Â The bar has a comfortable neighborhood feel to it and the bartender was alone working the bar and the tables and doing a good job of it. Â We then went to the comedy show and had a blast. Â There were about 10 comedians who did about 5-10 minutes each. Â All but one were really funny and the emcee was a riot. Â Highly recommend this for a night out.

Love this place! Our first date night with friends since the arrival of our little bean. The drinks are delicious and the mixologist( they are not just regular bartenders) are very generous with the alcohol no watered down drinks here:) oh the pumpkin ale with cinnamon around the glass rim is pure genius ( pumpkin pie kinda genius) The food.....the wings are freaking delicious I'm usually not a fan of chicken wings but the pickled pepper wing is worth reapplying your lipstick. Pork belly is the best I tried so far. My only meh moment was the truffle fries, it's just plain ole fries no truffle. But I will definitely be back here to eat my way through the menu.

This place is awesome. Service is on point and friendly, and the food is very creative and beautifully presented with the best ingredients. The ambiance was wonderful and I really enjoyed myself. I hope to come back here soon!

This place is great. Good food, good service. I got three tacos for $10. You can choose any three tacos, which is cool. I got one short rib, one chicken and one spicy pork. Beef short rib was my favorite. Pork came in second. They bring your food to the table and they even included a wet nap to clean your hands after you eat. Thoughtful. The place is pretty small. It only seats about 15. Luckily we didn't have to wait; went at lunch time. I could imagine a wait at dinner time. It's quite a trek for me to get down there from Harlem but if I'm in the area I would definitely go back.

I am somewhere between a 3 and 4 for Jolie Cantina but figured I'd round up because I think this place will be fabulous once they find their rhythm. My fiancee and I went here on Friday night since we'd heard they'd just opened and we used to go to Jolie on Atlantic. We found a great window seat at the bar and were given menus right away along with their house-made chips (though they were a bit stale) but had to wait about 10 minutes to order drinks even though the restaurant was only about 1/3rd full. Their wine menu was great and is very affordable however there was only one bartender and he seemed a bit lost but I assume its because of the new location/new bar. For dinner we shared steak tartare "a la mexicano" style, which was great! The flavors were subtle and not overtly "mexican" and served with fresh fried taquitos. Â We also shared the pork belly "chicharrones" which were more like baby pork rhinds (no skin and were crunchy like chips) but I thought they were a great snack for the bar. We shared two orders of tacos, beef tongue tacos and lobster tacos. They were both fantastic and felt fairly authentic (each on 2 small corn tortillas, with a large serving of meat and basic lettuce/onion garnish.) The meal was served with 3 sides of sauces (salsa verde, a chipotle red sauce and a mild, sweet orange sauce), all were quite nice though I would have liked a bit more heat in at least one of them as they were all quite mild for a mexican style restaurant. We didn't order dessert but had a quick look at their dessert menu which was similar to the original French Jolie menu and didn't seem to have any mexican-fusion dessert options which was suprising since the rest of the menu had very strong mexican influences. We will definitely be coming back here again soon. I believe that the minor glitches were due to the newness of the restaurant. I think Jolie Cantina will be a great addition/offering to the neighborhood and I look forward to my next visit.

i've been here one other time for a company lunch during the holidays. my memory of it was okay. i'm always wary of dining out in huge groups if the restaurant doesn't specialize in 'family style' meals. anyway, came here with one person this second time and the experience was much better. the food wasn't anything too special. actually it was very simple BUT the quality was good and they did the basics well. we had 2 glasses of wine -mussles from the brasserie menu to start (unlike many places that douse the mussles with a lot of heavy flavors in an overwhelming amount of broth, this place really let the mussles shine. it was simple and delicious. note: i am a sucker for dipping toast in broth-heavy mussle dishes, but this was yum on its own) it came with fries! -i had the miso glazed organic salmon (the salmon was cooked well. perfect medium. but i didn't really taste the miso. came with sliced snap peas, mushroom and sweet pea puree. again, simple dish. elegant. not over seasoned. good quality) -he had the grilled prime hangar steak. (perfect medium rare with grilled asparagus, and sliced potato confit. that was probably the best and simplest asparagus dish i've had. not overcooked, still had the crunch on the inside but soft and smoky on the outside. the potatoes came with a sauce that had mustard in it. DELICIOUS.) -ended with banana walnut brownie with maple bourbon ice cream. the actual brownie and banana were okay. but the bourbon ice cream was amazing! also, great attentive and friendly service!
I cant wait to go back, its my go to ramen places. The wait time we were given was pretty accurate (about 20 minutes). Â The ramen was very tasty and the pork buns were awesome!

Great place for lunch -- though usually the line is out the door and it is a little bit of a wait. They always play late 90s rap and R&B, so really the main reason I come here is to get my 4 minute fix. Oh, by the way, the burritos are tasty too.

Been meaning to write a review for awhile. Â Park Avenue Tavern is such a great spot. Â The food is delicious (crab cakes are my favorite), service is quick and friendly, and the crowd is always good. I love coming here for brunch and happy hour especially. Â Certain things are a little overpriced, but other than that, I love this spot.
Fuck the haters. This sauces are worth the wait.

Hudson Clearwater is a real special place. Â The food is fantastic, the drinks are delicious, and the place remains unpretentious. Â  I've gone several times and thoroughly enjoyed myself every time and everything I've tried off the menu has been fantastic. Â  Mark and the crew have done a great job with the place. Â Although I did notice last time I went that cocktail prices had crept up to $13, which I thought was pretty steep (especially considering that the bar tender really was nothing special).

This place is everything. I'm lucky enough to live in the same building as Eastwick and so I go there frequently, not simply out of convenience (I NEVER bought a single thing from the furniture store that inhabited the place prior to Eastwick's existence) but because the food is damn good. The owner and chef have hearts of gold. The staff are some of the friendliest in the neighborhood, running close competition with the guys who work the bodega right on the other corner. My favorite dishes are the Moroccan soup (I have probably ordered this more times than anyone else that comes here, I'm convinced), the burger with bacon, cheese, and a fried egg cooked medium, the mac and cheese, the braised short ribs. I even did the three course Thanksgiving dinner here this last thanksgiving, feasting on an amazing endive salad, a duck entree I completely demolished, and a butternut squash crumble. When I'm too sick to roll out of bed and go downstairs, Maxim hand delivers me Moroccan soup straight to my apt door. Nevermind that he doesn't do deliveries and I'm being the laziest of inconveniences by not going literally right downstairs to pick it up myself. Miss their lunch prie fixe but Love. LOVE!!!!!

This is not quite the Grimaldi's I recall from when it was Patsy's back in the 90's but it was still better than average brick oven pizza. I think they skimp a bit on the toppings (seriously, 2 baby pepperonis/slice) and the cheese is a little light, but the pizzas come out quickly and cooked perfectly. The ambiance is nice if you're a sports fan like me, with multiple TVs showing ESPN highlights and just the right amount of noise to speak loudly but not be able to hear or be heard beyond your own table. The staff seems a bit cold, but that's to be expected from most old school pizzerias. Overall, I would say this is good for a quick lunch but if you're expecting greatness and inviting friends for dinner, you're probably asking for disappointment.

Living close to Gramercy is a blessing because it allows me the luxury of walking by Maialino from time to time to see if there's a seat at the bar. When I do see a seat (or two), I walk in, grab it, order a glass of bubbly and wait for my companion (whom I've texted as I grab the seat) to arrive and join me in this completely spontaneous meal/treat. Anywho, my favorite go-to dishes at Maialino are the octopus, Maialino's very own mortadella, and almost any of the pasta dishes depending on my mood. The mortadella is basically a bologne - but a million times more delicious. Â I often imagine myself making a mortadella sandwich with 2 pieces of white Wonder Bread and wondering what it would taste like. Â I decide that with Maialino's mortadella, of course, that no condiment is necessary because it is THAT good. Â  The 'polpo', or the octopus, is succulent, charred and delicious and it's dressing of citrus and veggies make the dish perfect. My go to pasta dish is any one of their versions with sausage in it; or the carbonara, the cacio e pepe, or the bucatini all'amatriciana. Â Along with my pasta, I often order their veggie sides because whomever is cooking up the veggie sides is doing a crazy good job at it. Â You don't like your veggies? Â GET the veggies here and you'll be in love with veggies - well seasoned, garlicky deliciousness. And then - of course - you have to get their chocolate bread pudding. Moist, warm and delicious. Â The perfect ending to a fine yet simple meal. Â I never get bread pudding anywhere else after having Maialino's. Â Also, a close second is the olive oil cake. Â  In addition to the food, I think Maialino's layout, casual-vibe, it's spacious bar area and extensive 'by the glass' wine list make it a good spot for 2nd/3rd daters. Â It allows you to a) get a little more adventurous (then you were on the first date) b) get to really 'see' what your date looks like since the lighting is bright than some candle lit spot. Â If all is well, move the party to the uber sexy Rose Bar across the hallway then get FUNKY! Â yeah!!!

Ate there on the official opening day. The brisket was no-non sense. Hands down the best brisket I've ever had! The atmosphere was perfect for the food and I enjoyed the live band. The place almost had a Western movie feel to it without the swinging doors, and I loved it. BrisketTown was more of an experience than just another meal. Can't wait to go back.

YUM YUM AND YUM! Came here this weekend for brunch-we ordered just about everything. I love the peach pancakes-its not the average fruit pancakes-this was made with love and the Â Mezze from the appetizer was Oh so awesome-that day they had Ratatouille Â as Â the dip and I could've licked the whole plate-but kept it classy. AND-the plum juice sangria...I can almost taste it as I am writing this...this was one of the tastiest sangria I've had. Check em out! great spot in the slope!

Great spot. Loved it. Went for a late lunch and it was still pretty packed when we arrived. The margaritas were fantastic. Tried the guacamole and the homemade chips. Yum. Also had the steak tacos and the steak sandwich, both of which rocked. The place was a bit difficult to find as there was no sign out front when we went (we passed right by it originally). But maybe I'm not cool enough.
The food is amazing and delicious. It is also much more reasonably priced than other food carts in the area. Its a must for anyone going to that area.
Too bad you can't park anywhere! The food is the best

Walking off brunch is pretty much one of my favorite delusions ever, and one unusually balmy Saturday, I was strolling down Smith St trying to walk off the approximately 62 lb of mac & cheese I'd just consumed at Patois. Â  Â Suddenly, four words on an easel chalkboard caught my eye: Chipotle Bourbon Bloody Mary I turned to my cousin and, channeling Office Space's Lumbergh, said, "Yeeeaaaah...I'm going to have to go ahead and go in here ASAP?" Â "Here" was Char No. 4, somewhere I've been meaning to visit since before it opened, primarily because of its rumored 300 whiskeys collection. Â OK, not primarily. Â Exclusively. Â  If it weren't for Bloody Marys I'd probably never drink vodka, and with the CBBM, Char No. 4 has now made it possible for me to eliminate it altogether. Â Absolute daytime drinking perfection--spicy at first, followed by a sweet bourbon kick, and garnished with a tasty pickle. Â Also, the potent horseradish is hand-grated, as I was informed by the bartender, who proudly displayed his bandaged fingertips. Â Talk about really pouring yourself into your work! Â OK, that was a little gross. Char No. 4 is warm and welcoming, and if you sit at the bar you get to stare, mouth agape, at all that amazing bourbon. Â I mean seriously, there are so many bottles they completely fill your field of vision. Â Apparently there are public tasting events in the works, and I tried my best to plant a little seed in the management's head that the next Yelp bourbon tasting event should be held there. Â I'll keep you posted!
The ramen and pork buns and omg green tea creme brulee are the best, but the hostesses are the worst. Wish there was a takeout option but the food will always keep me coming back.

Place is absolutely amazing, from the atmosphere to the great service to the amazing menu. You must try the goat cheese balls with the lavender infused honey---crazy good. They also have a pop-rocks desert that should be at every restaurant in the city.

Champs is good for vegan food. Â That's the best i can say. Â I really want to love it but its just good. The pancakes are solid, the biscuit is decent, the soysage gravy is pretty good. Â But nothing is really great. Â The black bean burger is really bland. Â And the service is slow--last time I was there they completely forgot one of our party's order. If you aren't vegan but you want to be supportive (read: you get dragged here) stick with the batter-based stuff like waffles, biscuits, and pancakes. But you might want to dodge the chicken and waffles. Â The chicken is a pretty odd texture of you aren't used to it.

This is THE bar to go to in Queens if you're into beers. Â You won't find any Bud or Heineken here--the selection is mostly craft beers and changes constantly. Â Our server told us that they usually order only one or two kegs of a certain beer and when that's done, they move on to the next beer. Â The staff is friendly, knowledgeable and willing to answer any questions we had. Â Service can be slow but only because it's so busy in there. Â I was there on a Saturday night and despite it being super packed we only waited 20 minutes for our food order. Â Food was hit and miss. Â The ribs and pork belly were very good but the wings, though freakishly large, were boring and the brussels sprouts were bad. Â I'll definitely be back for some beers and will try some of the other items on the menu

I've not tried a lot of roasted chinese meats at other NYC restaurants, but the places I go to in Northern Virginia and Philly were better. Â I got the roast duck over rice here. Â I intended to order more food, but they had ran out of most of the things we wanted by 8p. Â The duck was fatty and cold, some of the fat had solidified on top of the skin. Â The rice was a bit dry and old, as if it had been sitting in the rice cooker for too long. Â In Philly, they will press the duck so that a lot of the fat is removed, but you still get the tasty skin flavor. Â  I would rec getting there well before closing. Â Also you should be friendly with the ppl in line with you, since you might be seated at the same table as them. Â Some of the ppl at our table balked at this, but the waiter indicated that it was near closing time and there were no free tables.

I have tried Ippudo 3 times... 2 were great and 1 was not so much... but I will explain why. The first time I visited, I thought it was the greatest ramen ever! I was greeted with random but happy shouts of Japanese from the wait and kitchen staff, and you can't help but shout at least something back. Quite comical, but adds to the environment of the restaurant. I loved the ambiance Â It was the complete ultimate UMAMI experience. I ordered the Akamaru Modern with kakuni Â (braised pork belly). The pork belly was just the right blend and texture of meat and fat and had great flavor. Another time I went with a large party and we all felt like we had umami overdose aka MSG poisoning. Literally everyone in our group of 10 felt like passing out afterwards, and boy was everyone cranky. Many people had vowed not to return after that incident, but I still held on to a glimmer of hope... I returned a 3rd time and had an experience similar to the first, so I had regained my favor in Ippudo. Overall, I still really like this ramen joint. It's a little pricey, but for the experience and quality I would say go for it!
the cubano sandwich was excellent. yucca fried fries, eh...not so much. the steamed ones looked way better. will definitely go back to try other stuff! very nice staff, and a nice establishment.
I'm glad to report that I have enjoyed the lemongrass chicken sandwich the past few times i visited. Â quality is back baby and the flavor never left. Â :-D. happy days

I wish I can rate it 3 and half stars: for all of Â the Thai restaurant choices in Manhattan, Queens and Brooklyn, it's a 4. But I am certain if this was served in Asia, it'd be a low 3 or even 2. The hype was so high that I couldn't wait to try it! The menu is definitely impressive! Some 25 pages with color coding, photos, and simple descriptions of each dish. The restaurant is spacious and clean. Cocktails mixed well. Started with tom kha gai (soup with chicken and coconut milk), the soup was unusually thick and full of chicken breast and oyster mushroom. Very lovely, but alas! It was too salty! I could not finish it. Crispy Chinese watercress salad was unique and delicious! "Salad" is a little misleading since the watercress was battered and deep fried. But fried to a crispy perfection. It's amazing how some restaurant can screw up beef satay. Not here, it was the most tender beef satay I've ever had. I was a bit disappointed with the drunken noodle. It was good but I am not sure where the "drunken" part was. Take the spicy away, the rest of the flavor was just regular. Chicken red curry: very spicy! I think the waitress even asked for mild for us. The curry tasted full flavor and not watery. I only wished they had use both white meat and dark meat. Chicken breast tend to get dry and flavorless cooked in lots of sauce or in soup. SautÃ© Chinese broccoli with crispy pork was my favorite, which is a shame since I went there for the curry. But the broccoli was not over cooked, it was still crunchy and juicy, and the crispy pork was an amazing compliment to the broccoli. I think Dennis Y (who had the luck to try the restaurant before the remodeling) might be right about its food becoming less unique and distinctive after the restaurant got popular. Or maybe I had too high of hope??

The first time I ever experienced avocado smash I made it at home, and I thought I had 'invented' it. This turned out to be inaccurate. You know who deserves to have invented it though? Dudley's. Chilli flakes in a salsa verde secreted beneath creamy avocado smeared on thick cut, seven grain bread, which can only have been fried lightly in a little salty butter... Top it off with an optional runny fried egg and you have the king of smashes. So good you'll wish you really did invent it. Â  Nice service. Sat outside on a cold sunny day. Burgers served to those around me also looked superb - lots of happy eating noises. I will be back. Often.

Lovely. Dapper. On point. The cheese and meat selection owe a visit by anyone looking to chill on a lazy weekday or after a long day at work. I have been often in on consecutive days and the cooks at the bar are worth striking a personal anecdote with... My friends grew up in the same town together. I hate French people (especially in the US) but the woman who started this place is from CA and understands the charming and sweet aspects of the culture. Love the food. Will recommend!

We schlepped over to Il Porto in the middle of a snowstorm, but no worries. The arduous walk there, during which I fell on my bum, actually added to the charm of this Italian eatery out in the middle of nowhere. When we arrived, we realized that there were actually two different rooms: a pizzeria-type room and a dining room. There were only three other couples out braving the storm, which left plenty of empty tables for us. The ambiance here is at once rustic and intimate. And even in the craziest of weathers, there was still live jazz. We started with drinks and a salad: red wine sangria and Spinaci salad (baby spinach, Bartlett pears, gorgonzola, crispy pancetta, and red wine vinaigrette). The salad was huge, extremely light, and fresh. The sangria was wine-forward (is that a thing you can say?) and chock full of alcoholic fruit. For our main course we ordered the grandma pie (thin crust, homemade fresh mozzarella, fresh tomato, basil, olive oil, grated cheese). I think this may be the best pizza I've had in New York so far, and it is DEFINITELY the best sauce. Worth falling on your bum many times over. The service was perfect. Â Friendly, prompt, not overzealous. Perfect. The price was reasonable, too. I will definitely be back for dinner and brunch (the La Fiorentina sounds fantastic).
Good pizza at a decent price, fast delivery, and the small is large!
This place is always good every time i go back. great service ,great food

Amazing! Our waiter was wonderful, attentive but not overbearing with a sense of humor and an attention to detail. The food was outstanding! I highly recommend the quinoa hushpuppies, i couldn't stop eating them! I also loved the octopus appetizer, it was cooked perfectly. Honestly everything was delicious. I kept eating way after I was full just to be sure to clean my plate. This is a great place for a special meal, I personally couldn't afford to eat here often. But next birthday or anniversary you'll be sure I'm booking a reservation!

WOW, people seriously?! Â This is considered good food?! Â I haven't been this disgusted at a restaurant ... ever I think. PORK BUNS = DISGUSTING!!! Â I've had pork buns in many different places. Â In hong Kong, in flushing queens, nyc takeout it is one of my favorite foods!!!! Â BUT...these were BY FAR the worst pork buns I've ever had hands down. Â My wife is Chinese and absolutely hates to not finish everything on her plate....after 2 bites of the pork bun she apologized and said she literally just couldn't take anymore. Â I completely agree. Â The meat was about 90% fat, I don't mean a little fat...I mean pure complete fat. Â I had to chew back vomit Â  =( Â  We both just shared a look of....what were people so happy about online?! Â  Sichuan Beef Tendon - As others have posted here online...TERRIBLE. Â Texture just miserable, spices not tasty at all. Braised Brisket - Again as others have posted here online, WAY too salty. Â And i LOVE salt. Just order a cup of water and pour the whole container of salt in to save yourself the trouble. The staff was very nice, we were seated right away, and the place looks nice. Â I just can't even begin to imagine ANYONE....let me say that again....ANNNNNNNNNYONE liking this food. Â  I'm so sorry to write a review this bad, but if I could give 0 stars I would.

I'm from Texas and maybe that's why I wasn't that impressed. I got a brisket sandwich, burnt end beans, and iced tea. We went on a Saturday night and had to wait in the line outside for about 20 minutes just to order. No biggie, if it's that good, I don't mind waiting in line. Everything looked delicious. The brisket was pretty good, but honestly, it was too dry. I slathered on their bbq sauce, which is pretty good and that helped. It just wasn't memorable. The beans had a strange kind of flavor to them- my husband thought it might have been some kind of a pickle brine or something and the beans aren't the right color for baked bbq beans- they aren't nearly as dark as they should be. They were ok. Good meal, just nothing special. I prefer Hill Country or Mabel's in Brooklyn for moist, delicious, and smoky brisket.

Yes the pizza is very good, and no, it's not worth the hassle. Went there this winter and experienced the 2 and a half hour wait for a pie. It was cold outside, but the door was left open, presumably so the people behind the counter, near the oven, would be a nice temperature., even though all the customers had to leave their coats on.This indicates their priorities, basically, they make zero effort regarding the convenience and comfort of their customers. Do yourself a favor, get a few friends, a few beers, and make some pizza from scratch at home. The pizza will be good, and you'll have a lot more fun. If you want to go out, try one of the many other fine pizza places in NYC, where they have at least an ounce of respect and appreciation for their guests.

A lot of hype for this place, noodles are not you typical ramen type, more like soba noodles. Broth is mostly if not all tonkotsu based so good luck if you don't eat pork. Place had a cold feel to it, mainly because of its big open space and long community tables, definitely not a place for a romantic dinner. Service was okay, they seated us within 10 min. After we sat down, ordered our food. It took awhile to get the servers attention again to ask something. even though it was around 2 and it wasn't as crowded. Good place to visit once for the experience but would not go back for the price.

My experience at Marc Forgione was subpar at best. Â We had a 2pm brunch reservation on a Sunday, but were still forced to wait because apparently the diners that were there before us were still "enjoying their drinks", yes, the bottomless one. Â 20 minutes flew by until we were actually seated. Â At that point, I was starving. Â For entrees we decided on the quail and waffle and the french toast w/a side of house sausage. As for the french toast, it was dry...could have spent more time in the milk & butter. Â Quail and waffle was good - but nothing extraordinary. Â Also on the dry side were the house sausage. Â The table next to us who ordered the same thing were raving about it. Â Don't.Get.It. The saving grace of the entire meal was the bottomless fig mimosa. Â  If brunch is any inkling of what's to come, I'm not interested in returning.

very good Malaysian food i ever have in NY and fair prices. we lucky get in big table for 3 people we order for 4 dish but we can't finish the food we have. very interesting for small places but busy and good service too. Try it taste good and cash only 'u'

I miss this place. Yes the wait was long, Yes the place was always crowded. Yes, sometimes I felt uncomfortable being the only black person there at times. But YES it was charming to watch the owner make his pies from scratch. YES, it smelled DIVINE when he would remove your pie out of the oven and drizzle it with oil and cut the basil leaves over the hot piping pizza. and finally YES, I loved every bite of their not too thick,not too thin crust, great sauce, great moz slices. Though I've never visited Italy, I felt this was as close to Mama's homemade pizza, I will ever get.....sigh....

Do you guys ever have trouble writing reviews for places you really really like? Â Figuring the words you write won't do the place justice? I've been to Bogata at least four or five times now and I still haven't written a review about it. Â I really have no idea what's stopped me. Â Bogata is FANTASTIC! Â One of my favorite restaurants in the city. Â It's one of those places we find ourselves at when a special occasion rolls around... birthdays, anniversaries, etc. Â  It has an amazing vibe, awesome staff, delicious food and some of the best margaritas around. -------------- Lets talk about those margaritas shall we... the frozen are my favorite...specifically the mango and passion fruit flavors. Â Absolutely perfect combination of ingredients making them sweet but not overly and just the right amount of tequila for that kick that have me ordering another, and another... Of course I do eat when I visit Bogata.... The Empanadas for one are incredible. Â If you're thinking about ordering I recommend the sampler ($15) and cutting them in half to share. Â My favorites: - Shredded Chicken - great spice! Â Dip in any of the sauces the empanadas come with, they all taste great with the spicy chicken. - Goat Cheese - combo of creamy goat cheese and queso blanco is soooo rich and soooo delish. Â Try it in the mango bbq sauce! - Guava - puree & cream cheese - who has time for churro's* and flan? Â Just bring me a round of these little guys. Â The sweet fruityness of the guava mixed with the richness of the cream cheese is soooooo good. I'm also a big fan of the following: Chipotle Salad with Plantain Crusted Chicken ($16) - it always surprised me when I go to a restaurant and have a reallllly great salad. Â It's lettuce, ya know? Â But the combination of avocado, feta cheese, diced egg, red onion, tortilla strips is great. Â Add the plantain crusted chicken, which is delish all on its own, and drizzle on some chipotle dressing and you have a killer salad. Â  The chicken especially is something special. Â The plantains give it this incredible crunch. Pernil ($16) - Ahh the pernil. Â Slow roasted pulled pork that's been marinated in Colombian beer. Â I won't lie to y'all - the pork is a little salty. Â But I suggest you ask for a side of their mango bbq, the sweet tanginess helps cut the saltiness. Â A side of the Tropical Slaw also helps cut the salt. Â The cabbage + slices of mango tossed in vinaigrette is just really good and works so well with the pork and bbq sauce. Another must try if its available is their mashed plantains. Â I've never been a big fan of plantains, unless they were in chip form, but this mashed version was wonderful. Â I wish they'd put it on the menu permanently. -------------- As mentioned briefly above the atmosphere is just great here... the place is so inviting, and so lively! Â I love the bright and colorful walls, the twinkle lights and the enclosed patio in the back. Â The staff has always been great to us too...I don't have a single complaint about this place. Oo and bonus- I found out recently that they added $3 empanadas to their happy hour menu. Â Yes! Â Looks like I won't have to wait until the next birthday to return for another awesome meal at Bogata. -------------- *In all seriousness - the Churros are really good too. Â You get four sticks and dips for $6 and they're totally worth it.

There is an uber trendy but also friendly vibe to this place. Great decor, but I'm only here for the food. It turns out both equally complement each other. The brunch menu is creative. I decided to stray from the usual omlette and instead order the grilled venison burger on a miso bun with tomato chili jam and cassava chips. Although I'm not a fan of venison (gamey flavor sickens me)...it was a pretty tasty burger. I loved the combination of this dish!

This place has a pretty friendly atmosphere and good lunch specials. Â The food was good, but nothing remarkable. Â Pasta's pretty easy to get right and really hard to make great, and here you got a pretty good dish for a pretty reasonable price. Â The brought out complimentary bread, which was delicious, but would have been even better if warmed up. Â They also brought out a pitcher of water right away, and we served ourselves (which I prefer because I drink a lot of water).

I love their duck rice- it's all about the duck. It's absolutely delicious, I always go with family and eat the same thing. The noodles are good too, but the duck is the best. The atmosphere is so-so. But it's cheap and authentic, and the food is awesome.

AMAZING food & wine! Great concept -- a different Italian grandma cooks each night. The owner is usually there pouring wine & contributing to the wonderful atmosphere. Walkable from the Staten Island Ferry. Cash only.

I have only been here for brunch, but I really like it. The atmosphere is cozy and welcoming, the food is delicious, and the prices are good. The service is a little spotty, but now that I've spent some time in Brooklyn I realize that this is just an unfortunate truth about most places. If you want more coffee, you will probably have to flag someone down. I highly recommend the croissant sandwiches and home fries, and I love that the brunch dishes come with a green salad. Omelets are great, and a friend's duck hash was really tasty. Can be pretty busy for brunch, but last time our party of three didn't have to wait at all and there were more empty tables in the back. Definitely worth checking out.
Used to be the best pizza of NY and NJ. Quality has decreased over the years, think there is new management. We'll still come here if we're in the area to and always take home a quart of spumoni.

I love this place. The drinks are good and well priced, the food is good and well priced, the service is good... what more do you want? I recommend Alfies for brunch when it's basically EMPTY. Brunch comes with a free drink (screwdrivers, mimosa, bloody mary). I also recommend getting the grilled cheese because it is the best grilled cheese I've ever had in my life. I've had it about 5 times now and it's fantastic. Â The mac n cheese is good but not great. The veggie sandwich is good but not memorable. The rosemary french fries are a freakin' dream come true.

My friend was raving about this place and took me for artichoke pizza. Â  The slice was humongous, thick, as well as greasy, but we soaked up some of the oil with napkins and proceeded to eat each of our slices. Â I enjoyed it, though I could have used more artichokes on the pizza, and we also got fried oreos from the shop next door to complete the experience :)

over rated to say the least. Â dont try the soups as they are totally watered down and not worth it. The lobster club roll was good as the bacon was crisp and delicious. Â My fiance got the regular lobster roll which was bland. My buddy ordered the lobster mac and that was pretty much totally avg at best. Â  dont order that either. Â  Ive heard that everything is good EXCEPT the lobster. Â i will be back just to try the fish and crab sangwhiches. cool atmosphere, avg drinks, and a little pricey. I dont see the crazy appeal.

this is my all-time local favorite - my go to place in the neighborhood. food is outstanding, innovative - always a great new special dish to try. great beer on tap & good wine list.... my favorite dish is the duck meatloaf followed by the pecan pie sundae for dessert.

Overall, this is a decent spot with good service and good food. The decor is a bit strange, sort of a blend of contemporary meets cafeteria (note the chairs and tables), but it's not horrible. Our server was great and knew the entire menu; we opted for the mezza royale, which was $136 for a whole bunch of food including hot and cold mezzas like fattoush and mekanek. The pitas are nice as they serve them straight out of the oven so they're still puffy; overall all of the food was good, but the fattoush, the hommus and the grape leaves were the best things served to us. The hot mezzas were decent but not outstanding. It was nice to have food served that was not over-seasoned and let the natural flavors of the main ingredients stand on their own. Anyway, worth a visit here and there for some Mediterranean fare.

BE AWARE!!!!! I don't even know where to begin with this horrible experience. I went to Empanada cafe on July 22, 2014 around 9pm. If anyone has been there, you know there is only two tables, so I order my food then sat at the bigger table with my husband. Â I am not even exaggerating this cockroach was huge to the point where I yelled and jumped on the bench. Â One of the ladies working the counter comes out holding Â a boom . Excellent place for dinner! Â We wanted seafood and the place down the block was packed and too stuffy...Oscars place wasn't far and had by far one of the best fish and chip entrees around. Â The mash of the night was amazing too!! Brussels and potatoes are my new favorite side.

I was meeting up with a few friends of mine and this place turned out to be the meeting spot. The place is decently sized and has an ample amount of seating. The pretty neat thing about this place are the tables. The wood on the top is actually recycled wood from bowling lanes. Anybody who knows how bowling lanes are made, know that they use high quality and thick wood. Needless to say, it looks great as the table top and they get a plus from me for helping out with the environment. The food itself isn't extraordinarily awesome, it's just average.... It's cooked well but a few of what I've had was dry and/or flavorless. The folks who work there are cheerful and they're happy to help out anybody who have any questions.

The day I was flying back to SF, I stopped by this Halal Cart at 4am, picked up 3 plates, got into a cab for JFK, pushed it through security, held it in my lap for the entire 5 hr flight, got back into a cab for home, called up some friend and ate it all for lunch. Yes...it's that f*cking good.

Got lucky last night after trying twice previously to get into this popular restaurant/bar. Very welcoming, even though I was accompanied by my 13year old daughter. It was very busy but the host was very accommodating and gave us a great seats at the bar. We ordered four dishes plus dessert and one glass of wine. The food was delicious and served promptly. Each dish was cooked perfectly. Overall a wonderful little eatery and bar with great ambience. Â A very cosy space, so expect to get up close and personal with other patrons.

Lovely staff. Delicious food. Amazing atmosphere. The best dish there is Jambalaya and Eggs. I am not sure why people are saying that it was not seasoned enough. I found it to be perfect. Also their coffee is good, which is important for a brunch place. Highly recommend!

This is a neighborhood gem with a killer wine list to boot. My friends and I had a great time sipping on Malbec and munching on little mushroom risotto puffs and crispy brie. The seating area in the back has couches and walls lined with board games and books; Jadis is great for both small groups and dining solo. In addition to their impressive wine selection, Jadis has small French-inspired plates as well as larger entrees and desserts. It's on a quiet strip near Rivington and Essex but it gets louder and more packed as the night goes on.

I must say, if I had to make an asian fusion sandwich, I would have to emulate the stuff JoJu serves. The sandwiches are rich in taste, full of flavor and not skimpy of product. Pair it up with some vietnamese ice coffee and you'll be rollin like lexington steele with the ladies. However, i would stay away from the joju fries. Vile.

The tacos are out of this world. More on that below. Let me first address some of the poor reviews that this place has received for their service. Dudes and dudettes: it's a taco shack with some classic Mexican extras (like bombtastic nachos and killer margs). It is nothing more. Do not come here expecting incredible speed and suave waiters. They produce cheap, savory tacos for on-a-budget hipsters who know how to eat. This is a "no soup for you" situation, not Chavella's. Deal with it. Besides, the people who work here are actually very nice. I've spoken to the manager and he's a down to earth guy. The cashiers have all been friendly, even lovely. The service can be a little slow at peak times (weekend mornings/nights, and after work hours), but, uh, doesn't that make sense? They're a small operation producing high quality, affordable, authentic tacos. AND they deliver. Take a seat (or wait for one) and chill. Trust me, those fried avocado jalapeno and hanger steak tacos coming your way are gonna be worth it. I love this place. If you find yourself on Franklin, or live near the neighborhood, shoot over for some cheap, delicious Mexican cuisine. It's a true gem in an up-and-coming part of BK.

Came here after Yelp recommended it. I'd been looking for another place since Chipotle started skimping on portions. Like the vibe and look of the shop. First impression one first bite: Very Beany First Impression on the array of selections: Not much. Once I finish this burrito I'll have more thorough idea of what I think, for now, I don't think I'll be replacing Chipotle. BUTTT tons more flavor here.

I'm vegan. It's rare, in my experience, that a trendy, tasty, highly-lauded NYC restaurant goes very far out of its way for vegan diners. In fact, I'd never expect them to, and that's totally fine with me. They do their thing, I do mine. I was looking for a good Tribeca restaurant that would both be awesome for my 3 non-vegan friends (nice ambiance, great reviews, great food) and also have some appealing vegan options for me (more than just a sad, sparse salad). This is an incredibly difficult thing to find. I checked out the Distilled menu, saw that there were ample vegan/veganiz-able dishes (that were also interesting, creative, and delicious-sounding), saw that it had a great ambiance and reviews, and booked on OpenTable for Wednesday night. At the last minute and without any expectations at all, I decided to throw into in the "additional notes" section that one of the guests is vegan. Didn't expect anyone to pay attention to that. Wouldn't be offended at all if they didn't read/consider it. No one ever does, and I know how to ask servers to hold the meat/dairy/eggs by now. We get to Distilled and order cocktails and a couple appetizers to share Â - cheese and crackers (for my non- vegan friends) and onion rings - for which I'd requested ketchup, as I don't eat the mayo-based aioli they come with. Both were delicious. We were very happy. Cue the hero of the night. Chef Shane comes over with a freshly concocted black-bean-and-herb dip with crackers, made just for me because he knew that someone at the table was vegan. Wow. I can tell you, with 3 years of vegan experience, that this never happens. We were blown away. Not only by how delicious and fresh this custom appetizer was, but because someone had actually read the OpenTable comment about having a vegan, and a CHEF(!) no less had gone out of his way to make something special for me, at no charge, without making me feel AT ALL like a burden. Insane. THEN, Chef Shane asks if he can whip me up a special vegan entree. He says I'm welcome to just order off the menu, but he'd love to throw together something special. Um, YES. This never happens. Is this real life? Then, it gets better. He sends over to our whole table a special vegan soup for each of us (yay, I don't feel like THE vegan freak!), made with cauliflower and basil and absolutely delicious, creamy (without cream), and fresh. Everyone loved it. Not just "the vegan." Just when I think I'm in heaven, he asks if we want to do shots. Yep. He brings us free moonshine pickle-backs. Can it get any better? THEN, my custom entree comes. I don't even totally remember what he said it was because I was in such awe, so I feel bad that I probably won't do his creation justice with this description...but it's something he threw together with the most amazing tender-yet-chewy mushrooms atop sauteed kale and potatoes in a gingery, miso-y broth. It was awesome. My friends loved their non-vegan entrees and desserts off the menu too! Everyone had a fantastic experience and can't wait to go back. I can't thank Shane enough for going out of his way to make me a really great meal, and for making me feel totally welcome and comfortable to boot. It was an incredible, and incredibly rare, experience to be treated this way by a restaurant and chef that don't owe it to anyone to make special vegan dishes. Usually, I feel super annoying when I ask restaurants to make things vegan, and when chefs go out of their way to do so, it feels like I'm asking for a huge favor. Here, I felt special, but not like a freak. Everyone at my table was delighted by the awesome vegan (and normal menu!) dishes he made, the pickle-backs, the thoughtful and beyond-all-expectations attention to my needs, the service, the whole experience. Thank you! Â I can't wait to return (though you don't have to bend over backwards every time...I was more than happy to just order some salads and veggies off the menu)! Usually, I only visit restaurants that aren't vegetarian/vegan specific restaurants when I'll be with friends (as I don't feel the need to force my lifestyle on them), but this is a place I feel totally comfortable returning to again and again regardless of the occasion or company.

Just had the deep fried tofu with simmered beef. The tofu was not fried and had only the texture of creamy soft tofu. When I asked if it was fried the chef and waiter were insistent that it was. I am far more offended by being castigated than I am that they still charged me for half eaten bowl of nothing special. Â Maybe I ordered wrong because other reviews are good? Â Not for me and if you like the more traditional Japanese stewed dishes you won't enjoy it either. Â Arigato gozai mashuta

A rainy day and a Rocket Pig does a delicious afternoon make. The location may be a bit hard to see if you're not paying attention. There is both Rocket Pig and an apartment building with the 463 on it. Rocket Pig is in a narrow opening to the right of the apartments at 463. Popped by and tried one of their pignic boxes and I must say I'm impressed. Yes, it's a bit steep in price at $20 but I would gladly do it again. First off, there is enough food for 2 people with moderate appetites to split one. In each pignic you get a sandwich, a huge pickle, spicy bbq sauce, and your choice of a drink, dessert, and snack. Super pleased with my box and highly recommend going with the pignic option, definitely enough food for 1-2 people depending on appetites. The sandwich had a good balance of sauce and the pork was tender, seasoned well with an appropriate level of moistness. If you are a fan of good ginger beer, they have Fentimans ginger beer! For the dessert, I STRONGLY recommend (and so did the girl working there) the chocolate hazelnut mouse cookie. They come in a package of 3.

The bf's family comes here for almost every family outing so I've been here Â quite a few times. The house salad is very tasty that dressing is killing me it gives it a nice flavor and cant decipher what they use. The pizza is good as well I would say its pretty good depending on what toppings you order. Â I wouldn't say its the best pizza ever but i've never been disappointed except when i leave hungry( he has a big family) plus the slices aren't that big. The pizza is always fresh i just wish they would put more cheese. Anyway I've liked it better to order for Â take out because the wait for this place is always ridiculous . I would say its a nice date spot or for a little group gathering with some friends.
tourist trap! can't believe so many people fall for this thick, overloaded, gross pizza when down the road you have emporio with their thin crust, woodoven cooked pizza.

OMG! Del-I-Cious! We went here with a small group and got everything on the menu. Each dish was better then last, which is hard to pull especially when you arrive hungry and leave stuffed. Great friendly service.

I was excited to try this place specializing in "hand-pulled Lanzhou beef noodle soup". Â I ordered the "house special" with oxtail, beef tendon, and some other stuff. Â Also ordered the Fujianese wonton soup and shared the steamed dumpling. Â  The noodles were pretty good, but I think mine weren't cooked long enough. Â I felt my broth was slightly bland, and the meat itself could've been better quality. Â The wonton soup was tasty, the wonton had far less skin than wonton I usually have, but were cooked perfectly, and dumplings were good. Overall, it was pretty good, not great. Â My friends love their "hot 'n spicy" beef noodle soup and always order that, so maybe I'll try that next time. With the menus posted on the wall only written in Chinese, no other decor, and the Chinese lady screeching at the cooks and customers, I had to admit a felt a little out of place when I first walked in. Â I was relieved to see they actually had menus for us ABCs =)

I don't usually order quail, but when I do, I order Momofuku's quail. Â The small dishes were all very tasty, I like the kimchi apples a lot. Â The Washburn Island oysters were really fresh. Â Not much has changed since my last visit except the prices.

We had avoided this place because many things on their menu are too heavy for a late dinner, but we returned to enjoy what ended up being an absolutely delicious meal. We shared the cauliflower soup (special that evening) and it was a perfect texture and combination of cream, but not too thick with chunks of cauliflower in it. Â We also shared the arugula salad which provides plentiful perfect bites combining fennel, apple, candied walnuts, and gorgonzola, all in a delicious honey vinaigrette. Venturing into the cocktail menu we ordered the Plum Pussy (does that mean something else in another language?!) and the Korzo Sazerac. Â The PP tasted too much like a melted lollipop, but we absolutely loved the rye whiskey-based Sazerac and had repeats on that one. All in all, a great meal at a very nice price!
Amazing food with an amazing owner who is super accomodating. Â  All the food was amazing especially the ravioli and marscapone cake. Â  Very reasonable prices for excellent food.

WHOO HOO!! Â  excellent mussel dish!! the sauce was unbelievably wonderful!!!!!!!!!! The sauce was soooo good, even after we were done with the mussels, I told the waiter to leave the sauce behind for bread dipping. Â No one believed me that the sauce was THIS good until I went here again for the second time with seven other people! hahaha! Â  Sorry, but the mussel dish is MY favorite and the funny thing is, I dont even like mussels to begin with. Â So that just leaves me with the sauce, YUMMY!!!!! Â It's made with butter, shallots, maybe some cream, spices, white wine, and probably other secret ingredients... you just cannot resist. Either way, it is THAT good! Â It was so good, forgot to take a photo of it... i was too busy eating that darn sauce... that's kind of funny. The other dishes my friends and I tried was the steak, with chimichurri sauce, YUM.
