Recently, I decided to venture back to Blend and try out their dinner menu after a not so pleasant brunch, or what they coined as 'Blunch', experience. My mind has been officially blown by Blend on the Water! And here's why: As always, the ambiance and decor of the place is breathtaking. You have the sounds of Latin music like salsa in the background while you take in the view of the Manhattan skyline as you enjoy your meal. It really feels like your at a fancy shmancy restaurant in the city. In terms of customer service 'Blend on the Water' is by far an amazing establishment that really takes into consideration the needs of their patrons. Besides your waiter/waitress, you'll have managers pass by your table and engage in conversation to see if you're enjoying your meal or just to see how you're doing. I actually had the chance to chat with Lance, one of Blend on the Water's managers, and he informed me that when I went for brunch that was their first week running that and they "worked out all the kinks". He even showed me a picture of how the same dish I order looks now and trust me what I saw in that picture looked like the real deal when it comes to mofongo. Kudos to them for actually paying attention and implementing new ideas based on customer suggestions/reviews. Now, here's what I had (& thoroughly enjoyed): Appetizers: I happen to really like their guacamole, with a couple of dashes of hot sauce, and tortilla chips. It's not lacking flavor and the tortilla chips are ALWAYS fresh NEVER stale. Of course, after my experience at the Yelp event I just had to order the tostones "nachos". What exactly is that? Twice fried plantains stacked on top of each other and topped off with cheese, guacamole, tomatoes, and just plain yumminess. These things are delicious, but WARNING you can have too much of these if you attempt to have an entire plate of this yourself. Drinks: Personally, I'm a fan of cocktails that don't have an overwhelming taste of alcohol in them. If you're like me than the pineapple mojito, which comes inside an actual pineapple, mango mojito, and coconut margarita are some good choices to take into consideration. These drinks were tasty yet refreshing. Entree: For the entree, I ordered the churrasco, medium well, which comes with a chimichurri sauce, white rice, kidney beans, and tostones. I also ordered a glass of merlot to go along with my red meat. The churrasco was cooked beautifully along with the rice and beans. I thoroughly enjoyed every last bite. After that entire meal there was no way I could fit in dessert! I still feel full reminiscing on my dinner there, but I definitely recommend EVERYONE go check out Blend on the Water whether it's with friends, a date, or family. You won't regret it.
I had the perfect evening here. Â The food was superb and the service was just what I wanted. Â This place is charming. Â I would go back in a heartbeat.

This review is for the decor of the place and the attitudes of the individuals I encountered that work here: In the aftermath of Sandy (she's a nasty BIA that wanted many people to suffer), downtown manhattan got hit hard. But apparently Chelsea was okay. This business is upstarting at an interesting time in this neighborhood, yet kind of in the Flatiron district too. I walked by this place with a friend and we liked the way it looked. Modern with a rustic, comfortable feel. Yet, we didn't see a sign. So we were very curious. We go into the place and start talking to the host, hostess, and one of the owners. The friendliness of all three of these individuals was amazing & genuine. And the owner is from the South with a very warm personality. The theme of this place: Bourbon drinks and smoked/southern dishes. I CANNOT wait to go back and try it. I am excited and there will be an update to this review. Guaranteed.

Surprisingly, the food is pretty cheap considering the quality of it. For $35 you can get a 3 course tasting which is very filling & trust me when I am say filling I mean you will be STUFFED. I also think that this deal beats restaurant week's currently priced $38 (dinner) since many of such restaurants give you small portions and just... a rather insatiable appetite. I came here for the duck confit because I love duck confit. Sadly, they did not have it since their menu is based on what ever is fresh on the market that week (which can be good or bad depending on whether or not you like the element of surprise :p). Instead, I ordered the fried pork chop which was mmm mmm good and very filling for an entree and escargot that was a tad bit salty for an appetizer. For the dessert, PLEASE trust me on this, order the bread pudding! Never have I ever tasted such a delicious, harmonious, and satisfying bread pudding. Never. I seriously enjoyed this place, but as a warning this place's menu differs from what they have online. If you see a dish you want and petit oven claims they make it, call them to just double check!
The pizza was tasty and the service was friendly. I just didn't think it was worth the trip out to Brooklyn for it. The Millennium Falco was the better of the two. Worth a visit if you're nearby.

Came in here by accident a couple of sundays ago when we couldn't get served at that pretentious German beer garden bar across the road. We had an absolute ball in here. The locals were friendly, the barman Jeff was awesome with great music and the drinks were ridiculously cheap. Forget what it looks like outside and go on in....you will have a lot of fun.

This is second review. I went there for brunch. I ordered Mexican Polenta. Spicy tomato sauce comes over square polenta. This was Â so-so, but I thought this food was unique, and other brunch menu seemed interesting, too. As for drink, I ordered mixture of cider and orange juice. It looks like Mimosa, but it tasted Â vinegary sour. I thought it was interesting. I went there on Sunday about 4:00. They serve brunch till 4:45. I want to go back there again for dinner time next time.

We ordered a margarita and staten Island pizzas which were really good and hit the spot majorly, 3 slices were more than enough per person. Will definitely come back and possibly try the artichoke pizza!! And everything else, so yummy!!

One of my favorite brunch places in New York. Sunday brunches are a great value. Benedict Jane is my favorite dish. It is quite busy but I've been with relatively larger groups and it's accommodating.

I know it is impossible for this place to be open through the winter, but I wish there was a way for their food to be available all year-round. I work about an avenue away from here, so during the Spring/Summer after work the bf and I take a nice walk to Pier i Cafe. Â The walk itself is very calming after a long day, then when we arrive we order our food, and get a table. Â Our usual order usually consists of: cheeseburgers, lobster rolls, caesar salads, and sangria -- we always get sangria ;). The view is absolutely amazing and it is just a great place to go and de-stress yourself. Â On some days they have dance classes being held on the pier where anyone is welcome to jump in. Â After eating you can chose to sit and enjoy the view which sipping on sangria, join in on the dance lessons, walk up the pier, and etc. Â There's just so many options to choose from and no choice is a bad one. On this cold winter night, I am now missing Pier i Cafe and their amazing food.

Met up with my two friends and they wanted burgers, so I of course consulted my Yelp app. Â The first place that popped up in proximity was Mark and I must say we were more than pleased with our find! Â This place is like a tiny hole in the wall, but the sliders were legit! Â They only serve sliders and fries here, oh and chili. Â But the sliders are large and a juicy and amazing. Â Also, the cheese fries are so good - they layer the cheese and so you get some with every bite. Â Not to mention the cheese is a little on the sweet side so it makes it a little more interesting. Â They have a decent beer selection... normal, dark and wheat is how I would describe it. Â We each ordered a different beer and were pleased. Â The bathrooms are surprisingly very clean. Â Hooray for sliders!

Classic 3.5 stars. It's a great clutch dining option between 30th avenue and Broadway. While my favorite 31st avenue eatery is Zenon (not meant to be a plug), Il Bambino is perfect for a carefree wine or dine night. Cheese and veggies are the stars of the paninis here, which I love though I've never wanted to eat here when I was really hungry. The Fontina is one of my favorites; Three cheese melted together, fontina (mmmmm) Mozzarella, and Pecorino, with truffle oil to add some indulgence. Another favorite would be the Bresaola which comes with Parmiggiano and arugula. WInes by the glass are fun and when the weather's decent, they have a nice patio. They had a few really good bottled beers last time I went also. ***.5 stars - any place with swine as their logo has me half won. Delicious paninis and good atmosphere make for good Astoria eating, and even better if you're searching away from the behemoth avenues of 30th ave and broadway.

It's always good to know "quick places" to eat in certain neighborhoods. I like to make mental notes of certain Starbucks, Chipotle, and Wendy's locations for those quick "grab 'n' go" moments. (Slightly shameful, but, carry on...) I have heard people sing the praises of Dos Toros in the past, and one night, I did not feel like Chipotle. (GASP.) I wanted something fresh. I walked past Dos Toros and decided to go in, expecting something awesome! I walked in and thought to myself, "Snap...this is a smaller, hipster, SoCal version of Chipotle. Ehhhh, DAMMIT." I was quickly proven wrong, thank goodness. Yes, it's the assembly line style of Chipotle, with the basic burritos, tacos, burrito bowls, and quesadillas, but...there is something infinitely better! The portions were not overwhelming. For the first time in years, I ate a burrito ("Simple" - beans and rice) and was able to finish it without feeling as though my stomach was going to violently explode within my torso. There is more simplicity to the Dos Toros line-up, which I appreciate. Seating is at a premium, with signs posting simple rules: don't sit down until you have your food, don't linger if the place is hoppin', but chizill as you please if the place is empty. Easy enough. Fair enough. Luckily, I was able to scarf with the greatest of ease without feeling rushed, despite the semi-busyness present at 7 p.m. on a Friday night. Their tacos looked wicked cute. Seeing as I WILL be patronizing this fine little establishment again, I foresee them in my future. My stomach is already dancing with glee! (Or, that could be from the beans in my burrito a few hours back. Hmmmmm...)

I've heard so much hype of this 'Best Thai Food in Queens'. Finally came here, and was pretty amused that the menu had pictures next to each dish. Some of the waitstaff actually were---wait for it---of Thai descent. Restaurant fills up pretty fast, so get here early. Ordered spring rolls which were a bit above average to me---not too deep fried as you dont feel oil bursting in your mouth as you bite into it. Instead it was crispy and fresh. Their coffee was super strong and altho I kept asking for condensed milk..they kept giving me creamer. Um okay.... Shrimp Paste Fried Rice was good, honestly it was type dry & not shrimpy enough. I think *gasp* Boon Chu made it better. BUTTTT the tom yum soup here was the best I've ever had. It wasnt too watery or artifcially spicy tasting. It tasted genuine and had loads of huge shrimp in it, I loved it. Drunken Noodles with Beef--Superb. The noodles were soft, the ingrediants really tasted fresh & perfect together. Not too spicy, and didn't taste like a whole cr@pload of MSG. This place definetly lives up to its rep. Wait staff is pretty slow & tends to ignore you though. Whomp whomp.

Ever since the first time I came here last June, I knew that Champs was something special. As a vegan with an intolerance to gluten and with a picky, omnivore boyfriend, it can be hard to find restaurants that suit our needs. However, Champs covers all the bases. . . three words: Gluten-Free Waffles. They are the most amazing things I've eaten since being gluten-free. And as for the boyfriend, he swears that the breakfast burrito cannot be vegan, cuz it's simply too good. A back-handed compliment but regardless, it's a compliment! Also, Champs gets some extra bonus points from the boyfriend because they have sriracha readily available, his favorite. Anyways, we have been here at least 5 or 6 times in the last few months for Saturday or Sunday Brunch. Yes, there is usually a wait, but it's never that long and the food is always worth it. Also, the staff is always super nice. The only negative thing I have to say about Champs is that the cash only thing is kind of annoying, but what can you do.
definitely much nicer and spacier than lower east side. the wait wasnt too bad, also the second floor is very interesting setup

I'll give this place 2 stars- Â GREAT DINE IN experience. Â Why is it lacking three stars? Â they screwed up my delivery both times. Â I'll still order... cuz its great food... Â but rice and beans when i clearly clicked on jasmine rice on Grub Hub? Â They offered a free side next time i go in but... Â i never do go in. Â for my purposes, this place gets 2 stars.

The best tacos I've had in Manhattan. Â SO delicious. Â How they prepare the meat is key to this satisfying treat. All the toppings and spices finish it off nicely. Â They have a nice kick to them too if you're into spicy food.

13 of us came on a friday night for a friend's birthday. Â  The place is a 30 seater, but it didn't feel crowded. Â  Service was excellenat. Food was great and fresh. Â The salad dressing was the disappointing honey mustard, but everything else was great. Â I got the skirt steak, and it was super tasty. Price was more than friendly, after countless of appetizer and drinks, it was a $45/person with 20% tips included.

Japanese-style cone crepes, I've been waiting for you to arrive for sooooooooooooooooooooo long. Why haven't you come to NYC sooner? As much as I love the established creperies here, they don't usually serve sugar with something called restraint. I had the Matcha Stripe even though I initially had reservations about it. I cringed to imagine how rich a crepe loaded with custard, truffle, chocolate sauce and yogurt would taste, even if it was balanced with berries and pistachios, but I ultimately succumbed to my love for green-tea-flavored anything. You ever had that type of dessert that feels heavenly from the second you take your first nip to the moment you feel it sliding down your throat? Then, when you've regretfully finished the thing, you feel this god-awful oily/sugary residual film in your mouth and at the back of your throat that makes you truly regret eating it in the first place? Well, you definitely won't feel the latter with these. True to their vision, ETC made an amazingly comforting, but delicate dessert with just the right balance of flavors and, most importantly (for me), sugar. I didn't think any single ingredient in the Matcha Stripe, not even the choco sauce or truffles, were overly sweet. And no, it wasn't the custard and yogurt masking the sugar, which brings another point: no component was overpowering the others. Wish I stopped by when they gave complimentary yuzulade. Incidentally, I did try that and the yuzu soda and they are both pretty awesome too! Nice way to wash it all down.

A really charming cafÃ©/restaurant with industrial urban design and a spacious indoor/outdoor dining area. It's huge! Had lunch here with my husband earlier today and I loved it so much it inspired my latest blog post goo.gl/m0q0V4 I am excited to see this place open in Gowanus! The menu is fairly simple with brunch items like eggs, toast and jam and lunch items like soup, salad and grilled paninis. My husband ordered the filet mignon panini and I ordered the grilled vegetable panini. We had the fried feta filo rolls as an appetizer and homemade rice pudding for dessert. Everything was delicious and prepared fresh. The chef personally brought our meal to us which I thought was a sweet touch. We asked about a liquor license and they are anticipating it soon. It would be a great place to pre-game before an event at The Bell House or a show/concert/game at Barclays. We will definitely be back!

Great place to go for a quick(ish) and delicious falafel sandwich. The prices are reasonable and the sandwiches are good. I've been here twice and both times the sandwich was on point. The falafel is freshly fried, crunchy on the outside and soft and crumbly on the inside. Very tasty. The hummus and veggies are fresh and good. A lot of people talk about Mahmoun's falafel but to be honest I think Mahmoun's pales in comparison to Nish Nush. If you work in or around Tribeca you should check this place out for a quick, reasonably priced and excellent mediterranean lunch.

If you're a New Yorker, please remember to look at reviews by New Yorker's for the most accurate description / review of this restaurant as it is in Times Square and is pretty much for tourists. Â I've definitely had better from local pizzerias. So yes, the portions are pretty large for the pasta dishes but think about it--pasta is a cheap ingredient! Â A box of pasta costs only $1 at the local supermarket. Â If you actually look at the dishes, they're not that plentiful otherwise for the most part. Â The exception here was the linguine with clam where the clams were plentiful but then the pasta wasn't which I found very odd...oh well, this dish was almost perfect. Â Next time, at least wait till the customers are out of ear-shot. Â I don't know if waiters have a designated area but if you're going to go here, avoid the waiter who looks a bit asian-caucasian mixed upstairs. Overall, I have to admit the biggest plus side to this and why they get 3 stars despite their mediocre food and service is what everyone else emphasized--it's great for large groups! Â I went with a part of 15 people including the Birthday girl so the check was split between 14 people. Â We ordered 7 dishes (including apps and dessert): fried calamari, linguine with clams, penne with shrimp, eggplant parm, chicken marsala, spaghetti with meatballs, tiramisu....and with a tip between 20 - 25% tip, it still came out to just about $20 / person which was a LOT less than I expected. Â Also, this is one of the first restaurants I've gone to where they don't add gratuity on the bill for such a large party.
Best BLT I've ever had! Fantastic!
roast duck was good but congee.... not so great :( wouldn't recommend this place.

The food was ok. I ate the daily special, the skate fish. It was too well cooked and the sauce lack subtly. Â My colleague's roast beef salad looks too large and the presentation was a bit messy. The decor is modern and good for business lunches. Service was good.

This is hands down one of my favorite restaurants in Manhattan! Â The ramen is excellent here and definitely the best I've had in the city. Â The only negative is the wait - almost always over an hour during dinner hours and pretty close to that during lunch on some days as well. Â That being said, it's definitely worth the wait!

I've been wanting to try this place for about 2 years now. I can only review the vegetarian section. It was definitely delicious. I do wish there had been more dairy free options though -- besides a salad. It was very filling. Service was quick. And the people watching was great! I'd love to come back and try one of the other sections for lunch too. If I lived in NYC, I'd be frequenting this place for regular groceries!

I expected this place to wow me with their food, but unfortunately it didnt. We had the Tom Yum soup- which was good, it had nice jumbo size shrimp... we ordered the red curry with sticky rice and pad thai. The food was good, but not as good as I thought it would be. If I was around the area, I would come for a quick eat, but would I make a special trip for this ? I think not...... sorry sripraphai! i rather go to Song in Park Slope! by the way, the "large" soup- it isnt really that large for 9 dollars.

Long wait and bit pricey overall. We ordered the pork buns and Akamaru Modern and Shiromaru Hakata Classic. Pork buns were amazing but pricey for just two pieces. Ramens were good and both very rich. If you want less rich in flavor, go for the Shiromaru Hakata Classic. I wish the noodles were a bit more cooked
Tabare is my favorite restaurant. If I could eat their tomato salad and have a glass of the Torrontes everyday, I would be living in upmost health and happiness. This place is really great.

Nice chic pizza spot. And did I mention the magic words? Brick Oven! Chill atmosphere and good service. Worth checking out. Only 4 stars because they could do with some variety in their otherwise cutting edge menu. But the inside is well put together and a great place to dine.
Service is always nice, Â and the food is even better. I love their food, Â and they have tons of veggie and vegan options. Â Always go there when I'm in the area!

We had a small rehearsal dinner here for 21 people. They have a room in the back that holds up to 23 (I think) for a fixed price. The food was amazing and the room pretty intimate (3 tables). Great option for a private event...or just dinner.

Went here after being told that it rivals the very best of the best in the Williamsburg region and beyond, and should be considered right up there at the top with the likes of Roberta's, Forcella, Best Pizza, Motorino, Zero Otto Nove, Graziella's, and Grimaldi's. The pizza did not disappoint, but it may take several more pies before a certain declaration of pizza dominance can be awarded. I had the Hellified Porkpie White, which was a white pie that had fior di latte, hot sopresata, fennel sausage, sliced red onion, sliced fresh garlic, basil, and hot honey. It all had the taste of a champion, and being a fennel sausage evangelist I was EXTRA happy during those particular bites. The hot honey, while a great idea in theory, created one of the messiest pizza eating experiences in recent memory. Hot honey, a little bit of sweet, a little bit of hot. Great idea. Though my hands were so sufficiently sticky that every time I grabbed a wine or water glass I left partial handprints in delicious honey, which remained for the rest of the meal. After my last bite I washed my hands and came back to the table. I probably won't get that again, despite it's righteous flavor. The place itself is really cool inside and in a part of Greenpoint I have come to really enjoy (suds at Broujeri Lane and Pencil Factory are a mere Vortex football throw away). Best pizza I've had in Greenpoint, out of the 1 places I have been. Great odds in their favor on that one.
the razor clams area amazing. Â had a wonderful meal here for lunch, definitely want to go back.

I don't know how I could pass by this place everyday since August and today was the first time I've eaten here! Better late than never and boy am I glad I did! The decor was beautiful especially their ceiling where an array of terracotta pots are placed to give this place the character of ancient Greece meeting modern America. Wow I am impressed! right when you sit down they offer you a plate of warm pita bread....I am a fan already. Our waiter was quite helpful with recommendations, but I was most impressed with the octopus! OMG it was so good! Tender, not chewy with just the perfect sauce/seasoning! The tzatiki dip was also yummy cause it was thick and full of yummy Greek yogurt and cucumbers :) We also got the eggplant dip which was scrumptious on its own and the meat balls and a Greek salad. The Greek salad was fresh, the feta was beautiful :) I will definitely be back in no time!

....and we didn't get the shawarma, as we were told to. Yeah, we are bad like that. But when I read the magic word "kefta" I usually have a hard time resisting the call of the lamb and beef concoction. That's how I roll. Don't come to Mamoun's for a nice sit down meal, you won't get it. There are two small tables, a napkin distributor (you *will* need it) and that's it. Tiny place that rocks the pita-ble (that would mean "that fits in a pita") fare, and offers the best hot sauce you will ever see in a joint the small. Come hungry and with a sinus infection - you'll leave happy, satisfied and definitely cleared out. Delicious.

My friend and I have severe food allergies and our waitress took this very seriously, double checking every order for the killer allergens and serving any possible dishes of death on the opposite side of the table. Â This is not an overreaction to an anaphylaxis threat. Â I've dined in many restaurants where allergies are dismissed with a hand wave and a yeah, yeah, yeah. Â Ilili clearly recognizes that it's not cool to have people dropping dead at the table. Â Those of us with allergies really appreciate this! Extraordinary food experience as well. Â Personal faves were the brussels sprouts and veal bacon slider, but I think duck shwarma won overall table choice. Â  I almost singlehandedly cleaned up both the bi laban and the beer fried kibbeh. Â Cilantro dominates both of these plates so it's probably a bad choice for soapers. Â I happen to love cilantro, but my dining companions happily passed these over to me after a taste. Â  The hummus was nothing special. Â My advice is to pass on this and try a more adventurous meat or veggie dish. Â  We came fairly late for dinner to avoid a wait. Â The adjacent bar gets a little loud, but I wouldn't mind trying it for small plates and drinks.
One of the best meals I have had... Â The grilled octopus and the salmon were exceptional. Â The apple donuts and chocolate torte were also heavenly. Â Casual dining. Â Excellent service. Â Amazing!

I want to like it and I do but I'll never go back. Beer selection is excellent. The food is good, a little pricey, but nice quality. Very quaint little bar. One star is for service and that's all I am going to say about that.

I skipped four meals--two before, two after--as part of my Gramercy experience. When you're going to Gramercy with Heather H, you do NOT eff around. Of course we sat at a center table, so that we get to see the little silverware dance they do. I'm having trouble remembering all the food we ate because it was so mind-blowingly awesome that my mind is trying to PROTECT itself from getting blown again simply by recalling the experience. Though I thoroughly enjoyed the venison, I think my favorite might have been the squab. I mean some people in our group were singing "I don't want no squab" beforehand because they were afraid of pigeons or whatever, but they tried it anyway and were totally impressed. I really liked the peanut butter semifreddo, but my fav was this thing with this red sorbet, help me out here, I don't remember exactly what it was but it was TRANSCENDENT. To Michael Anthony: Normally I don't trust people with two first names, but my hat goes off to you sir for a truly amazing experience. To Heather H: (on knees, arms raised) I am not worthy! I am not worthy! I'm dumb! I suck!

What a cute place. The line was long (but not as long as it usually is, I got that impression early on). Service was fast and we found an empty table which was pure luck. The burger was DELICIOUS (my husband and I both had the Shake burger). We also had cheese fries and the fries are easily some of the best I've ever had. On a Spring, Summer or Fall night, what a beautiful, sweet date. A must go!

How the heck did I not know abut this place until now?!? After an early evening outing of cocktails at a bar on Washington, it was time to find food. They have tables here and some people were dining in, but it's kinda smallish and likely best for the takeout crowd like me. We only ordered the wings. Saucy and delicious. I want to try more on this menu and will definitely be back. The people working at the counter were pretty nice as well and there were at least 12 people waiting while I was there. I think this place is quickly catching on.

after my roommate bragged about this place, my other roomie took her bf there... and that's when they encountered miley cyrus. Â i mean... that's when i totally had to run out the door and check this place out.. wait.. which teeny bopper is she again? i totally forgotten that the both of them had eaten here. Â we were walking around east village, deciding where to eat, when we stumbled upon this little iron clad gem, with two salt shrines bestowed upon the front door. Â odd? Â yes, but after previewing the menu, we decided it was worth checking out. izakaya style...or for grilled veggies, this place absolutely rocks! Â the food is really a 4, but my overall experience was a complete 5 for counter bar service ONLY!. Â maybe it had something to do with the fact that everything we picked was super delicious...one small plate after another. Â the finale dessert surely didn't disappoint. Â plus, the thrills of watching the chef personally hand each grilled dish you order on a paddle stick... i mean, can you heighten the experience any better? every food was perfected in its own apportioned right. Â i agree with most of the folks here, portions could possibly be a bit bigger, but too much will taint the perfect existing taste & image i have already pre-conceived about Robataya. Â I prefer small with many different samples to choose from. Â That way, I get to savor & sweet each dish in piecemeal. highlights: nama-fu (wheat gluten cake on a stick with miso & yuzu paste), tofu agedashi (light & perfectly battered in a savory thickened broth), enoki mushrooms (buttery but that's what made it taste so damn good), grilled eggplant (sticking to the basics), chu-toro (each bite was a bit of fatty heaven) i could go completely vegetarian here and be utterly content..a little biased because i'm a pescetarian...so i can live without the red meat stuff. it's important to note that their secret weapon ingredient here is noto sea salt. Â one of the highest caliber of sea salt i have ever tasted. Â my oh my, what Â a robust, rich flavor. Â perfectly accentuates the entirety of the meal. Â  note to self- MUST try the kamameshi with salmon & roe next time. Â as much as i love rice balls, anything cooked in a stone pot is a major plus.
Very cute and nice restaurant, food is good, internet is fast :) My clear fav in that area! I also love the oatmeal stout they have!

so I'm going to give this spot the benefit of the doubt because chances are I didn't do it right. not sure what my options were around midnight after traversing the brooklyn museum, yelp conveniently pointed me in the direction of kimchi kimchi bbq and friends. the place was popping to the point that we couldn't find a table (which is always a good sign walking into a new place). the menu looked exciting, which led to my potential misstep. being on a bit of a health binge, I opted against kimchi quesadilla steak fries covered in deliciousness and sauce and instead went with the kimchi bowl. come on, it's not that unreasonable. it was fine; it had a sparse amount of short rib, some decent vegetables, and a nice blend of spices. what I wasn't content about was paying $9 for it. when I throw around a ten spot on midnight grub at a quick place (healthy or not), I expect to be satiated. which I was not. alas, I may have made the wrong decision. after all, how harshly can one judge a lamborghini on its gas mileage? a fish on its spelling abilities? a late night fried dumpling taco place on its bowls? harsh enough to spend my time writing this review on the late night train home I guess.

We got here on the fly, no res. They seated us within the hour (not bad for Valentine's night). Â Had good drinks at the bar and our server was one of the best we've ever had. Â Dessert on the house. Â Can't wait to go back.
underrated. very good food in this place.
Great food, price was very good as compares to Manhattan. Â Easy to find parking spots. Online reservation made it so easy!

I came here last month on a Thursday night after an art gallery show in Chelsea. Â The ambiance is romantic so I was drawn into Porteno. Â We first sat at the bar and ordered a delicious malbec. Â Then 15 minutes later, we were seated. Service was excellent, prompt with refills and taking our order for ravioli and steak. Â The ravioli was fine but the steak was excellent, well prepared medium-rare and a tasty cut of meat. I highly recommend Porteno, it was one of the stand out Argentine restaurants in NYC.

I ordered take out at around 8 on a Thursday night. Wow was this place packed with people. Nevertheless as soon as I walked in the waiter and hostess were both very friendly and helpful. The grilled pork sandwiches that I ordered were well marinated and grilled. I would def come back again. Keep up the customer service saigon shack! It is really appreciated!
This is a hidden little place that even complete guides of New York miss on occasion. It's a lovely tea shop...perhaps not for a meal but for a snack. Must-have: Earl Grey mochi = heavenly.

While visiting NYC, this street cart was mentioned to us by a friend who said we must check it out. Â We knew this was the cart as we saw a line. Â We got the chicken and it was very tasty. Â Quite a different experience as I am not used to getting food off a street from a cart in San Diego. Â  I am glad we've tried it!

Bottom Line: Â Love this 10th avenue American hot spot with a Mediterranean twist - and love that they take reservations. Â  Tip: Â  Walk off your food coma on the Highline right across the street! Food: The team at Cookshop is committed to serving dishes (and drinks) with seasonal, local ingredients to stay true to its 1800's heritage. Â We enjoyed fresh strawberries scattered on top of our thick, not too crunchy not too wet French toast. Â The French toast had a delicious flavor, but was in a pool of a sweet butterscotch sauce which was a bit too rich for me. Â Next time I'll order it as a side dish to share with the table. The cheddar popover with poached eggs, braised leeks and cheddar was divine - just so good. Â The brioche was a perfect complement to the flavors in the dish which had just the right texture as well. Â Must have! Drink: If you're with a group, try the special cocktail mash up "Brunch Punch" (aka Pride Punch if you, like me, happen to go the day of the Gay Pride Parade). Â It is available only in pitchers for $45 and is made fresh to order. Â It is a mix of peaches, ruby red grapefruit, acai vodka, riesling, cucumber soda, and ginger beer. Â Refreshing and not too sweet but it does have a bit of a strong ginger beer taste so keep in mind if it's not your thing. For the Bloody Mary enthusiasts, Cookshop offers five unique takes on the classic brunch beverage. Â For the brave ones out there, the Hampton Shore Mary includes Citrus vodka, clam juice and fresh oyster! Atmosphere: Big airy space - even if you aren't seated outside, the natural light flows right in. Â Overall it is a casual environment with simple decor and is great for groups, families or to catch up with girlfriends. Â Also, we loved our waiter Spencer - Â he didn't rush us even with a long wait outside - and he was very helpful in our ordering decisions!

Solid new restaurant in an area that's pretty lacking in great restaurants. I really like the concept of Feast - family style dining that's customized to the size of your party. It's pretty ingenious really, a tasting menu of sorts, only much more approachable and communal. They currently offer 3 different feast menus: a vegetarian farmer's market feast, scallop feast, and nose to tail lamb feast. All of the three prix fixe menus are fairly priced, ranging from exactly $38-50 per person. The bf and I ordered their scallop feast, portioned for two, and basically let the kitchen work their magic. To start, the housemade crusty bread was surprisingly very good and still warm when it arrived at our table. I liked the hint of sourdough starter and whole wheat flour in the bread. **SCALLOP FEAST** First courses: - Scallop slider: first time I've ever had a scallop slider, though I'm not sure why more chefs do not do it. The nicely seared scallop was well-seasoned with a nice celery relish that added just enough crunch and brightness. - Ceviche: fresh and pretty fruity with zesty citrus flavor. The presentation was also nice as the ceviche was served in beautiful half shells. - Fried bay scallop: tender and nicely fried with a light breading, although the saffron mayo wasn't very prominent. - Beet ravioli: the "ravioli skin" was basically thinly sliced beets, mellowed out with goat cheese and some olive oil and citrus - an interesting take on a beet salad. Main courses: - Seared sea scallop: the addition of braised pork belly and rhubarb was definitely innovative and worked surprisingly well. I'd take this over your typical surf & turf any day. - Pot pie: Probably one of the most impressive plates of the night, in my opinion, and I'm not even a big fan of pot pie. The smoked scallop and razor clam chowder encased in light puff pastry was downright ethereal and comforting. It's also great that they leave the scallops in large chunks. - Charred asparagus: the red wine vinaigrette was not extraordinary but I can never say no to fresh asparagus. - Celery root 3 ways: another simple yet one of the more impressive bites we had - loved the puree and roasted parsnips atop a big and crispy parsnip chip. It was a perfect balance of sweet, savory, nutty, and creamy. Dessert: Vanilla yoghurt panna cotta with mango and little ginger shortbread cookies. The panna cotta was a nice texture and pretty light, though certainly not the best panna cotta I've had. My only gripe would be that their wine list is pretty limited and not the most well-curated. The only Sauvignon Blanc on their menu I had was mediocre and quite bland. The metal stools around the larger communal tables in the back are also a little uncomfortable to sit in, unfortunately. I think Feast is a fun place, possibly with a large party as the whole experience of ordering one of their prix fixe "feasts" allows for easy sharing and interactivity. Of course they also have an a la carte menu which you can order off of. But why do that when you can have 6-7 dishes for a real feast?
I was shocked that this hipsterish cafe serves the best burger and fries in Brooklyn. Try it, you'll like it!

I went to Riverpark for restaurant week with a large group of girls, and had a wonderful evening! Â I was pleasantly surprised that they were offering their entire menu (with a few supplements, of course). Service: Â Accommodating and amazing I had a reservation for 8, but then had a last minute addition. Â The manager and staff were incredibly accommodating and brought out a larger table and set up 9 chairs in an open space. Â Also, the servers were wonderful and checked in frequently. Â For hungry girls, it was amazing that our bread was always replenished! Food: Â  Our waiter for the evening mentioned the pork chop was his favorite entree item, and he was not wrong in his recommendation. Â It was cooked to perfection -- tender, juicy, flavorful -- and the accompanying brussel sprouts were also delicious. Â  I had the date pudding with yuzu ice cream, which was an interesting combination of flavors! Â  Ambiance: Getting to the restaurant was a challenge, but it is truly beautiful. Â  Definitely worth a visit :)

Love, love, love! The food was delicious and the atmosphere was great. Ask to sit in the garden, it was very cute. As far as food, we started with tomato mozzarella, cauliflower and meatballs all which were great. I do not even eat cauliflower and I think it was my favorite appetizer. For my main I got the gnocchi which was also amazing. Will definitely be going back!

I have no clue where you people even are, but when I push the buttons on my phone you bring me Cuban Sandwiches that make the rest of my afternoon happy and satisfied. Now, if you could make all that noisy ground zero construction outside my window go away, I would be in heaven.

WHAT IS ALL OF THIS HYPE?! I went there twice .. and both times were an epic fail. On my first encounter, my friend and I waited more than 2 hours on a Saturday for a damn table. The pancakes were underwhelming (Ihop makes better IMO) and the biscuits .. I gotta give it to them, it's better than Pilbury dough boy .. But no biscuit is worth 2+ hours. The second time was with my bf. Again, another 2+ hour wait on a Saturday and they seated us on that bar-styled section to the left of the door. FO'REALS?! (Excuse me as I go ghetto) Y'all made us wait 2+ hours to seat us at a table my ass can't even fit in?! I asked to the host if it was possible to get another table .. And Ms. Unibrow said, "I'm sorry, but that will take another hour." I was about to walk the hell out of this bourgeoisie establishment and settle for brunch elsewhere when the waitress kindly stepped in and offered a table. I don't know what her name is, but it was an act of grace. She took care of us, and her generous tip reflected that. Seriously .. I don't know what the hostess's problem was. By the time we were seated at a regular table, there was at least 3 empty tables sitting around for 15-20 minutes. And to the interior designers at the Clinton St. Baking Co: WHAT WERE YOU THINKING ABOUT THE TABLES TO THE LEFT OF THE DOOR? Are you feeding anorexic people? 'Cause surely no one intentionally malnourished is going to willingly stuff their face with your biscuits and pancake. With that said, go to this establishment if you enjoy aimlessly waiting around for hours only to be greeted with calorically dense subpar food. It's nothing but hype.

Good but not great BBQ. I enjoyed my food but was not blown away. I felt it was really a little over priced for what it was but i have been wanting to try Fette Sau for a long time now so i'm glad Â i finally gave it a try. I don't see myself craving it anytime soon though.
read great reviews about this place and we weren't dissapointed. Beet dip was crazy awesome!

Placed an order online and waited more than 90 minutes for delivery. Called to check on status and was placed on hold for more than 10 minutes. Called back and was told "they were busy". No apology, no discount. By the time the food came it was cold and damp. I'm sure the dine-in experience is better based on all the good reviews, but I would be weary about ordering in from these guys.
Love Fort Defiance. How can you not? Great cocktails, fresh seasonal food and a laid back vibe. A must for those who visit Red Hook.

I have to admit, I returned 5 times in 2 weeks after my first experience at Bogota. Â The service is amazing, the drinks are strong and the food is scrumptious. I usually go with a group of friends and order pitchers of Mojito's. Their Caipirinha's are dangerous- I recommend eating a full meal when ordering a pitcher of them, or you'll be seeing "Bogota Bogota Bistro Bistro" in a matter of minutes (and most likely praying to the porcelain god later on in the evening). The mojito royale is amazing, who thought mint and champagne would work so well together? Their empanadas are cooked perfectly, a bit golden brown and crispy on the crust, soft and saucy on the inside. The goat cheese and the bacalao are my favorites. Â I would try an Arepa (made with the right cheese), you won't want it any other way afterwards. If you order the patacon, ask for extra aji on the side (you'll look like a pro). I'm not a fan of their chicharrones, because I prefer the Cuban way of frying them. I also would stay away from their quinoa cakes (even if you're a veggie). Their ropa vieja is also a crowd pleaser, and the portion is massive. They play live music on Wednesdays and Thursdays, have a happy hour all night on Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday, and are always packed for dinner, doesn't that say something? They passed the best test of all: I brought my Colombian friends, and they LOVED it! Just try not to have a craving for Colombian food on a Tuesday, you'll be sorely disappointed (they're closed).

So I have to preface this review and say I've been to Belgium and have had the real deal, so my expectations were high. Â  This little joint is small, and mainly for take-out snacks unless you're lucky to grab a seat at the few tables and bar chairs that they have. Â  The fries were AVERAGE. Â Nothing special, my Mom makes better homemade fries than this place. The sauces were quite tasty though, I tried the honey mustard mayo and the curry mayo. Â The fry guy also let me and my gals sample a few of their other sauces which were phenomenal and I wish I could remember what they were :-(. I'm giving this place 3 stars for the sauces, friendly service, and large portion sizes-a small was huge! Â The fries get 2 stars-womp :-(
Enjoyed breakfast here, went with the recommended french toast which was quite good, along with standard coffee and orange juice.

Went for dinner with friends and all in all I liked it. The restuarant has a nice country home decor, which is pretty comfortable and a decent amount of seating, especially in the back. The bar is really nice and the beer list is pretty impressive. Probably around 20 craft beers from all over the country, so there is something for everyone. For food, we all shared orders of Biscuits and Fried Pickles. The biscuits weren't really that great in my opinion, and for $9 they seemed like a bit of a rip off. But I did like that they came with little squeeze bottles of honey and different preserves. The fried pickles were pretty good and I liked the mayo sauce it came with. For dinner my friends all got either the honey chicken sandwich or the gravy chicken sandwich, and they all seemed to like them a lot. I got the Turkey Leg, and it was far better than I expected it to be. Make sure you're hungry if you order it, as the leg is legitimately enormous. The mashed potatoes it comes with a good, and the cranberry sauce was great. So overall the food was really good. The only thing I didn't care for here was the service. Our waiter came by once to take our order, and then we never saw him again. No one came by to see if we wanted more drinks or water. We had to ask the guy bringing out our food to get our waiter so we could order another round of drinks. On our way out, I found that our waiter was "busy" chatting it up with the hostess in the front of the restaurant. But don't let the service stop you from trying this place, could have just been an off night.

Cute place, good food and portions. Â I would love to come back. AMBIANCE: Bright, cheery, busy, lots of stone, big window to garden, narrow space so it feels a little crowded but I like this. Â We sat at the bar -- the bar stools are amazingly comfortable due to a clever spring mechanism on the back. Â It's nice to watch the staff preparing many of the griddle items right there at the bar, also. FOOD: Good, though heavy. Â We came for brunch, had the Croque Forestier, Crepes Jambon, and asparagus with a dug egg cracked on it (and Neapolitain, I think... grated Parmesan). Â All good, though I don't know if the Croque F. needed to be completely encrusted in cheese. Â The plates are very small, but the portions fill the plates, and the food is generally heavy, so the three things we ordered fed two fairly large men. SERVICE: Folks behind the bar were very busy, so we sometimes had to ask twice to get their attention, but this did not really bother me -- food was served in good time, and questions were answered cheerfully enough. Â I suppose in an ideal world it would have been much clearer who our actual waiter was, and he would have been a little more attentive. Â  We came in around 1 pm on a Sunday, but it was pouring rain so there was no line (the place was full but there were two seats at the bar). Â By the time we left around 2:30 pm, it was starting to empty out. PRICE: Quite fair, I think. Â I guess we spent under $25 a head for brunch w/ tea and coffee.

By far my favorite spot to lunch at while around Times Square! The staff is exquisite at dealing with our every whim, while serving generous portions with a smile on their face! The smoothies are well worth it, though keep in mind they serve beer, too - which just so happens to go GREAT with the delicious meats they have. It is usually busy with non-tourists (a great thing), mostly Latinos, which speaks to the authenticity of the restaurant's food. Just keep in mind, this is not a fancy, date type place.
grea food

I used to live right next to this place. Never had a bad meal here. The filet mignon is always cooked to perfection and surprisingly inexpensive. I also love there steak sandwich. My only complaint would be about the day staff. Never really seem to have it together. Always a new, seemingly clueless girl working there. They are always very sweet though. I love the night staff! Really fun and welcoming. Great to sit at the bar, look out the beautiful little windows and have a nice glass of wine.

Whatever you get here, this place will not disappoint. The 1/2 chicken criollo is so nice and juicy. The staff are very nice and attentive. They are also very flexible with sides. Even if the menu says 'served with mashed potatoes', all you have to do is ask to get it with salad or fries instead and they gladly will do it for you. The chicken milanesa is SO GREAT! I can't get enough of it. When the dessert menu comes around, be sure to get the strawberry gelato. I haven't tasted better since Italy! All in all, a very nice spot. I'm lucky to live so close to it!

We had a nice casual lunch at Ippudo in October 2009. From everything I read, it seemed like you could wait a while there. We arrived around 11:30 and got lucky, I think. When we left the restaurant, it was wall to wall with people waiting. Of course, we had to start with the Hirata pork buns. Anything with luscious, fatty pork is probably going to be a winner with us, and these were no exception. The texture of the bun itself is almost like a sponge. That sounds really unfortunate when in fact it is quite tasty. I could see myself eating about 20 of these in one sitting given the opportunity. Afraid we would covet the other's dish, we un-creatively both ordered the Akamaru Ramen. Now, we may have ramen like that here in Austin, but I haven't found it yet. Suffice it to say, these are not the ramen I made in my college dorm room with a hot plate. A flavorful broth, noodles with a firm but not crunchy consistency plus, it included more delicious pork. What's not to love? The price point seemed a little bit high to me (around $45 for our meal and two drinks), but my husband wasn't about to complain, since it was pretty much the cheapest meal we had in New York. : )

I went there about a year ago and loved it! I returned on Saturday and mas very surprised by how the quality of the food changed. It seemed under seasoned compared to what it used to be. Sangrias were amazing, and the little bread they give you with the black bean or strawberry spread is to die for! The mojitos are some of the best I've had as well!

What a lovely find! Was in Brooklyn on Sunday morning and decided to meet some friends for brunch. After perusing the Yelp app, we decided to check out Le Barricou. It was a bit out of the way from where we were in Williamsburg, but the trip was definitely worth it. We arrived around 1 PM and had a 40 minute wait. Luckily for us, we snagged some seats at the bar and ordered drinks to pass the time (the Bloody Marys are really popular here and were quite delicious). We also spent an embarrassingly long amount of time trying to figure out what to order. Everything was crazy affordable and sounded delicious! I had the Eggs Norwegian, which were delicious. The eggs were cooked well, the salmon delicious (I could've had more salmon. Then again, I always want more salmon), the side salad refreshing, ahd the potatoes, seasoned with rosemary or thyme or something, which added an interesting flavor. I started getting full halfway through the dish, but of course, powered through. We all left feeling full and content. The service was admittedly a bit slow, but I loved the ambience and was content waiting. Would definitely come back!

Loved this place! Came in on sat night before a show up the block and were seated right away at the bar. Its Spanish tapas as if you were in Spain the the carved meat and the wines surrounding the wall. What to order.. Razor clams were fresh and in garlic perfect taste. Pulpo with fennel.. Never seen it cooked like this before very tasty. And the amazing skirt steak! Its dressed with caramelized onions and a type of pickeled sauce. There is an extra large wine selection at all price ranges $$$$.

If you like or want to try empanadas look no further - this is the place for you! An incredible selection of options. A few other tasty non-empanada options as well. Â Nummy sangria. One of the first restaurants we take people to when visiting NYC with somebody new. Only downside is very limited seating.

Holy crap, this was delicious. This was one of the best meals I've had in a long time. We got a reservation fairly easily which is such a nice change of pace for Manhattan. Â The ambiance is great...small, but great. Â It's a cozy restaurant with live music and a man making Cuban cigars in the corner. Â The only reason Cuba didn't get 5 stars is because it's a tight space, you are sitting on top of your neighbors. The service was kick ass. Â The server was nice, enthusiastic, helpful and attentive. And of course the food...delicious! Â  For starters, we had the Empanadas and the Calamari. Â SOOO good. I had a Chicken special for an entree and my boyfriend had the oxtail. Â Also, both very very good. I regret not having desert, but I will definitely be going back for that!
Great soup dumplings, shanghai beef and everything else. Wonton soup is also quite delicious!

Interesting atmosphere. Â The beef tatar was really nice. Â I enjoyed the hazelnuts. Â The chicken and veal were both satisfying entrees. Â Great wine list, although the print was really small haha. Â I wish we had had space in our stomachs for dessert!

Disappointed by the manager here. We came here tonight and everything started out lovely, and my boyfriend and I were seated at a communal table for 6 and were told beforehand that we may have to sit next to others, as it was communal. After the other parties arrived, the manager (not hostess) - the woman with dark shorter hair - came by and spoke to the party of 4 that were seated at our table, apologizing to them for having to "sit next to these two people". While it may have been an error on their end, for not reserving the whole table for the other party of 4 (what is the point of communal table seating??), there was no excuse for what came out of the manager's mouth. To make matters worse, after my boyfriend joked "sorry we are bad company", she responded with "it's probably because of your hair". We were generous with our tip, able to separate the manager from wait service, but wanted to leave immediately. On the way out, I approached the manager to let her know that we were very offended and upset with her comments. While she gave an apology, and the blame was somehow oddly redirected to the hostess who should have seated the other patrons separately (were they friends of the manager??)...this was certainly no excuse for what came out of her mouth. We will never come back. This was the one of the worst services we've ever experienced. The manager should be fired for her appalling behavior.

False advertising--Don't waste your time. After searching for a restaurant to take my Paleo friend out for his birthday, I thought Hu Kitchen was the perfect place when I saw their delicious menu on their site. Â NY1 had also featured a segment on them a few weeks ago so my friend and I decided to go for it. Imagine our surprise when we went in and found out their in-store menu is dramatically shorter than what's on their site. Â I had gotten my appetite worked up for their Beef Burger, and an employee told me it's been "a while" since they carried that. Â Another employee, who seemed to be a supervisor, said they've been "trying" to update their website but have run into IT issues. Granted, their online menu says "Menu & Prices Are Subject to Change", but wow... If you don't believe me, check out their site, then go to the restaurant. Â But you won't see me there!

Recently on a raining, summer night, some colleagues and I made our way to The Redhead to test drive what has been billed as some of the best fried chicken in the city. Why the place is The Redhead and not The Red Hen, a more apropos moniker for a chicken joint, was a question that kept us occupied during our brief wait for our table. This place doesn't take reservations, but our group of five waited just a couple of minutes at the bar for our table, most likely due to the inclement weather leaving many diners at home. The menu, just handful of appetizers, entrÃ©es and desserts, was delightfully short and sweet. We knew what we had come for and decided to split a couple of appetizers, three portions of chicken and some sides. The spicy fried peanuts and homemade chips were delicious, the crab mac 'n' cheese tasty, and the market salad refreshing, but the pasta was a little too small for the sauce, I found. The star of the meal was hands-down the succulent fried chicken in its crispy carapace served with a green salad with strawberries and some killer cornbread. Desserts were decadent and comforting as well. Following our waiter's recommendation, we ordered the insane chocolate pudding with peanut butter cookie crumbs and the strawberry shortcake. Out of the many places we dined at during a hedonist week of eating, this was by far my favorite experience over all!

Friendly and professional. This is a great place for solid food and good service. I've been here three times and had a great brunch each time. Some times a wait, but no biggie- staff is attentive and kind.
Food was great but pricey for the money. Cost us each 20+ with decent portion. Pretty crowded. But atmosphere was nice.
Had the Colonol Bao (chicken) on my way home. Tasty little bun, Â recommend getting at least 2 or a side to make a meal out of it.

If you like grilled food, you'll love Robataya. Definitely sit at the bar (not at the tables in the back) so you can watch the chefs expertly prep the food, grill it, and serve everything (including bottled beer) via long paddles, a skill in itself. We really like the grilled gingko nuts (not everyone does, but you should try them) Â This is an authentic offshoot of the Japanese restaurant of the same name (we used to live in Tokyo and love robatayaki). It's pricey but fun.
Everything was delicious! Â I had the shrimp and grits.. my sister had the salmon and spinach..my daughter had the flounder. Â Everyone's food was great. The chicken wings are very flavorful.

Before I came here, I thought I loved sushi. But now I realize that I just love soy sauce and ginger. I usually smother my sushi rolls in both. The rolls themselves are usually bland. At Beyond Sushi, however, I barely touched the ginger and soy sauce. The rolls I ordered -- Crunch n' Munch and Sweet Tree -- were so inventive and flavorful that they didn't need extra condiments. Cucumber Mint Lemonade was also delicious and refreshing. I've found a new favorite restaurant.
The stars are based on menu and deliciousness alone. I hate the hipster atmosphere, so I get take out usually. But the food is what matters. And it is goooood.

I am sorry to say that the food was nothing to brag about. We tried a few items on the menu and I was not impressed. The decor was old run down and outdated. I looked around hoping to see a celeb or two but, was disappointed. At least that would have made the night interesting. The staff were quite friendly but, not worth waiting years for a reservation as some have done.

I love this place and I wish their place was bigger. Every time I come here I wish that there was a table for me to sit at. I always end up getting it to go and just walking down Union Square stuffing myself with sushi out of the bag. Ha. I love all their rolls. I'm allergic to soy though, so that part gets a little tough. I wish they made some of their sauces with maybe cashew cream or almond cream would be a nice touch!
This is my go to place.. for brunch and for dinner. I can come here with anyone and be satisfied!
exactly the same as houstons in miami.. hawaiian rib eye is good.. have to get the spinach dip. don't get their baked potato.. it was gross!

Such a small place with outstanding cajun food amongst other things. Very hipster kind of place with a very friendly staff. Had a lamb sausage poboy! Not your ordinary sandwich but so good. It was huge and the sweet potato fries were crispy and very tasty. Mirror in the back made it look like this place was huge but to my surprise this place did not have many seats. It was a little cramped and it would be a little while to get a table for more then 2 people but the food and specialty drinks they serve makes up for all of this.

Yum! Awesome Brunch Menu- if you haven't seen it online already... not sure what you're waiting for. my new favorite bar in astoria. Â  sweet tea cocktail is perfection. Â  fried pickles will change your life!!!

Top notch breakfast nook with great food and drinks and excellent service. They were busy but we were greeted and seated immediately. The Fresh Squeezed OJ was awesome, but the fresh papaya and strawberry mix over my soft Belgian Coconut Waffles kicked this up to 5 stars for me. The 3 egg omelette comes with your choice of treats inside, and a nice big side of teeny homefries seasoned to perfection, crisp on the outside and soft on the in. While it's not as healthy as I usually eat, it's great tasting food at a nice price for what you order (large portions under $10.00.) My only regret was not ordering the alcohol drinks, as the menu was really appetizing (though they close after breakfast, so I don't know when I personally would be drinking there...)

A friend of mine and I walked by this restaurant called La Lanterna di Vittorio (129 MacDougal St, New York, NY, (212) 529-5945) that seemed cute, and decided to go in since we had been walking around for a while. The pizzas and all of the other dishes looked really nice as well, and apparently they have a garden in the back with a lot of tables. aspoonaforkandaknife.bloâ€¦

The wraps here are incredibly unique. Â The innovative ingredient combinations will have you curious at first and delighted by the end! Â It's great value to for the price and will fill you up. Food and service were very good. Menu was interesting. But, alas, we come to coffee and dessert. Lets start and end with coffee. $9.00 for coffee for two is reasonable? What if either diner wanted a different kind of coffee. $18.00 for coffee for two is ludicrous.

Excellent ramen! Â Me and my husband did a tour of the most popular ramen around NYC this winter, and this was definitely our favorite. Came here for lunch on a Saturday. Bloody mary was really spicy, almost too much horseradish for my taste. I prefer hot sauce vs horseradish in terms of what kind of spice I like in my bloody mary. Ordered the Benedict Johnny -- chicken sausage, poached eggs, and tomato hollandaise on cornbread. Definitely an interesting take. The cornbread was a bit messy, and the whole thing didn't really stay together well. But not a big deal, and it was yummy. I liked the sweet/salty/spicy combo. All in all, I liked the meal, but probably wouldn't come back. There are so many good lunch/brunch places in the city. This one was pretty decent and maybe a tad overpriced in relation to comparable offerings at other brunch places downtown. If you're in the area and looking for a place to eat, definitely stop by! Staff was really friendly, service was good, food is solid.

The wait sucks, but it's worth it. The pork buns are good. No way are they Momofuku good, but they are good. The ramen is top-knotch awesome. Waiters and waitresses chanting Japanese terms as food is coming out.

Pros: -Food portions were enormous -Great price ($9 for huge omelette) -Good service Cons: -Cash only -Small space -We went around 1030am and it was already pretty full (there was a wait starting at 1130) -The waiters were moving chairs/tables in and out of the restaurant so they left the door open. I visited our domestic mecca for macarons when I was in New York earlier this year and brought home one of their cute specialty boxes of 8. (Okay, it was probably a box of 2 by the time I returned to Los Angeles, but who's counting?) I still have it on my desk months later because the packaging is so adorable and well-done - very deserving of some excellent macarons. The flavors were delicious and spot on - just the right amount of sugar for dessert, but not overpowering with artificial, syrupy flavorings. The texture was good, though my batch felt slightly over baked and they were not as soft as I had anticipated. (Don't get me wrong, they were still SO good!) I went early enough when there was no line, but there was a semi-difficult customer with a large and specific request... so I did have to wait a little. I wasn't in any rush so I enjoyed taking my time to look at the flavors, eventually chat a bit with the helpers behind the counter, and pick out my cute little box. They even gave me a couple of free ones for waiting, which was very sweet. Delicious desserts plus great service = four stars from me!

How do I feel about this review? Drop of water, meet ocean. Anyhow, here are my heavily inflation-devalued two cents about Prosperity Dumpling: you'll have a hard time filling up your tummy for less in the city... or perhaps anywhere in a developed country. Even so, it's still not worth the stomach space. A five-minute stroll will yield you dumplings that (in my opinion) are far superior for nominally greater cost at Lam Zhou. Allow me to enumerate a sampling of reasons why their dumplings are better: 1. You get to watch as the employees hand-wrap them. Their efficiency is nearly robotic. I grew up making dumplings with my grandpa and these folks blow his speed and consistency out of the water. 2. The dumpling wrappers are much thinner and more delicate at Lam Zhou, which means a higher ratio of stuffing-to-wrapper. Ergo... less filler per dumpling.* 3. Lam Zhou's meat is actually seasoned. In contrast, at Prosperity, I added soy sauce and vinegar to my dumplings and even then, they were on the bland end. 4. Prosperity has about a half dozen seats. Not that Lam Zhou offers more, but there's at least room for a ten or fifteen people. We're talking a 100% increase here, folks. Would I come back to Prosperity? Sure. At someone else's urging. Though given my druthers, I'd pay twice as much for the dumplings at Lam Zhou any day. ----- * This is similar in comparison to crab cakes held together with breadcrumbs vs. crab cakes that are actually made of... y'know... crab. Why waste limited calories on starch? (If you'd like to weigh in on the crab cake discussion, please see G&M vs. Jerry's.)

I had to Have the Trinity Po Boy again. As I originally said.... it's my Love on a plate. There are several dishes but this one is for the seafood lovers out there. I originally chose to visit Sugar Freak because they serve dishes I have never seen or had in Queens in my 30+ years. So Danny Meyer sensed New York doesn't have enough Italian restaurants. Â What's next for him, a tapas bar? Â The interior is inoffensive, but it won't win any awards. Â I'm not sure whether a Roman would feel at home here. Â The bathroom area is downright gloomy. Â Haven't we moved past communal washrooms? Â The bar stools, with its not-quite seat backs, are uncomfortable if your ass is bigger than 12-year old's. Â Sound level is more than lively when the room is full. Â Staff is friendly, but can get inattentive when they get slammed. Â Staff also is not entirely well versed with the items on the menu. Â Granted the restaurant has been open only for one week, but one expects better from a Meyer restaurant. Â Clientele comprised mainly of couples of a certain age and local Louis Vuitton-toting yuppies holding their wine glasses by their bowls. Â  The selections of wines by the glass were good. Â The menu sources classic Roman cuisine. Â All the usual Roman suspects are there: Stracciatella Romana, Trippa Alla Trasteverina, Bucatini All'amatriciana, Coda Alla Vaccinara, all things al forno. Â I learned the hard way that the bar does not offer a full menu - only a bar menu. Â Why? Â Dunno, but the bar food is not nearly as compelling as the full menu. Â The Frito Misto and the Pollo Alla Diavola both were standouts. Â The eggplant parmigiano was over seasoned. Â The flavor of the eggplant was hidden beneath the red sauce. Â At $18, I'll take a local pizza joint's offering. Â The Carpaccio Di Polpo, an unappealing dish composed of cold boiled purple potatoes and cold braised octopus slices, was returned to the kitchen. Â The potatoes were undercooked. Â I was promised a new order, which never arrived. Â The Torta Della Nonna, actually a Tuscan dessert, was good. Â The Affogato, not so much.

Delicious food and attentive service - wonderful shrimp, tasty kohlrabi dish and terrific beet/carrot patties to start us off -

Delicious and classy. I loved dining here. It is close to home but still felt like a big night out. The drinks are wonderful and the service was warm and attentive.... but not overbearing. Would suggest as a family dinner or date night venue.
Love Buvette! Â Such a cute, cozy spot with reallllllly delightful dishes! Â Perfect for a low-key bite in the West Village!

Love this place. Great pastas, wine list, and the olive oil cake really is amazing. It's usually crowded and noisy, so not the best place for a date, but the food and service are excellent.

Been eating here almost my entire life. Got introduced when I was a but wee lad and I thank my parents for showing me this haven. I come here at least once a month, kind of my monthly pilgrimage. The times I go are usually during the slow times so I never have to wait for a table or my food. I'm given a menu and told to show myself to an empty table anywhere in the restaurant. I can see how if the pizza were made perfectly crispy I'd love this, but maybe i just got it on an off night. I'll have to give it another shot because i really do believe in this place.

First time trying NY pizza, so I have nothing to compare this with. However, my taste buds are still traumatized and drooling from the thought of this place. Extra cool points for chairs attached to the ceiling. Gimmie PIZZA... P-I-Z-Z-A

This was the first pizza place I came to when visiting New York a few weeks ago and it definitely did not disappoint. It wasn't the best pizza that I had in New York, but it's worth a trip since it's almost a landmark pizza joint. The crust was nice and thin, sticking to the traditional New York style. The sauce was good but a little bit too sweet for my liking. The cheese was fresh and delicious! Nothing kills the taste of pizza faster than overly processed cheese :/ . I just wanted a few more herbs in the sauce and this pizza would've been perfect for me, but then again, if you're into very simple flavors then this should tickle your fancy! Hah weird saying... Anyway don't get me wrong, I do enjoy simplicity in my food, but this needed just something... Oregano maybe? The place is nice and clean and the service here was awesome! Even the prices are extremely affordable.

Awesome food. Great ambience. Totally much more than I expected. I read all the great reviews and figured it was worth a shot. The place is gorgeous. Truly one of the best breakfast plates I've ever enjoyed.
so good!

I came here first in 2007 and remember it being good, but my last visit here 5 years later blew me away. We got the oysters, Pate, Brick Chicken and I had the pasta special and all were excellent. I would go back in a heartbeat except the wait is a bit long. Restaurant is pretty cute, they also sell random things and the server was amazing. I know I've walked past this place a dozen times, but never did I know what was on the inside. The place is gorgeous, the atmosphere is relaxed and friendly, and the service was outstanding. I had goat cheese wheat ravioli with butternut squash in a sage sauce, and the hubs had chicken tangine with apricots and prunes. I can't wait to go back!
excellent. get the crispy watercress salad.

I finally got a girlfriend to come with me to check out the restaurant after having bookmarked it a few months ago but our meal was terribly lackluster. We both ordered the sirloin steak medium rare. All the entrees came with two sides. The steaks came out, looking impressive, although our waiter joked that he looked for the smallest ones for us. (Or was it a joke?) My steak came out almost well done so that completely ruined the meal for me. My gf's was better but even she said that it was getting dry and tough as she ate more into her steak. Granted, we aren't at a steakhouse and we didn't order their traditional, well-acclaimed dishes, the temperature of the steak was just so off. The staff was pretty great though. We witnessed how they gave a birthday shout-out and it was the best I've seen done by a restaurant. The waiter who headlined it was very cheery and enthusiastic.

I friend of mine recommended this restaurant. He is Greek and imagined he would know what he was talking about. The next step, as always is to check the reviews on Yelp. The restaurant did not disappoint. While there were certain flaws with the restaurant, the food I tried overwhelmingly compensated for any shortcomings. My initial impression was not the best in the beginning. Being a small venue, tables are cramped together. It is not the best place to have any conversation you do not want other people to listen to. Additionally, when I attempted to order Ouzo, we were told they only had a beer and wine license, not alcohol. When we ordered, they brought out a complementary puree of lentils with warm pita. It would have been better served by giving us some hummus or even olive oil with pepper. Normally what I saw from the beginning of this meal, I would give this restaurant a maximum 4 stars. However, the rest of the meal was sublime. This is what was ordered: Htapothi Scharas- classic grilled, marinated octopus with a balsamic reduction sauce and capers Avgolemono Me Sampania- champagne avgolemono, pylos' smooth as silk classic egg-lemon soup with chicken stock and rice Arni Kotsi Me Meli, Gigantes Skordalia Kai Psiti Tomata cretan-honey braised lamb shank served with giant bean and roasted garlic puree and roasted tomato For the record, I do not like octopus. I find it to be chewy and not very flavorful. Pylos converted me. It tasted like a tender steak. It was perfectly seasoned. Â As impressed as I was with the octopus, it was the worst part of the meal. The chicken lemon soup was one of the best soups I have ever eaten. It has an amazing zest of lemon paired with a silky broth. It was so amazing, we ordered a second bowl. Incredibly, that was not the best part of the meal. I am still dreaming about that lamb shank. I was a little surprised when the silverware was brought out I was given what looked like a butter knife for the lamb. I soon discovered why. . I have eaten a lot of lamb in my life. I've also eaten lamb shank in New Zealand. However, this lamb shank is the best I have ever eaten in my life. The meat fell off the bone. It could have just used a spoon. I want to return to see if the chops are as amazing as the shank.

Have only been to the midtown location. Â Clean and super efficient. Â  The main thing are the sandwiches. Â And let me tell you....they are phenomenal. Â Absolutely amazing. Â I had Â the Their Five-Spice Glazed Pork Belly with pickled Asian pear....impossibly flavorful. Â  Â For $7.75 this is a great deal. If Pete Wells at the NYTimes wants to hand out 3 stars to outside of the box locations, I'd start with this spot.

Yum ee. I had the artisan cheese plate, the soup of the day, and shared the kale salad with my daughter. Â All huge portions and all was fabulous. Â My daughter had the house made ricotta - wow! Â A little pricey but all well worth it.

This is unbelievable. The food is outrageously cheap and totally fresh. The best way I can describe how authentic and well-done the food is here is that around 4am on weekends all the Arab party people start to form a (sometimes real long) line to get food here. I haven't been to the Middle East but I bet a few of them have and know this is the show for authentic baba etc. etc. Got a serious ganoush here the other night. For $2.50. Nuff said. I'm not going to review the East Village version of the same restaurant, just know that the vegetables at that location are usually much fresher. Other than that they are exactly the same show.

I was attracted to this food cart stand because of the long line. Â  So I decided to see what the commotion was and stood in line for it. Â I probably waited about 15min before getting this round aluminum pan filled with a couple of pita breads, lettuce and the chicken/lamb combo. Â Well I have to say that it was worth the wait and for $6, it's cheap. Â The chicken was tender and just right for taste, but what stole the show was the lamb. Â It was full of flavor and tender. Â Their white sauce (Tzatziki) is quite interesting and very tasty. Â It's lighter than most Tzatziki sauces I've had. Â They mixed it with a bit of mayo it seems. Â But it's too die for and it blended beautifully with the meat in my mouth. Â The pita bread wasn't all that special, but I could just eat the meat all day long. Â  If you like spicy food, then be sure to put some of their red hot sauce on your platter. Â A little bit goes a long way, so be prepared for fire in your mouth if you squeeze too much of it. Â It does give you that nice spicy kick to the platter. Â  This is definitely the best bang for your buck in NYC. Tip: Â The second time, I just got the lamb platter. Â You should probably get the combo platter if it's your first time. Â And try to get the exact change if you're just ordering 1-2 platters. Â The guys are super busy and they don't get to take the time to give you change if you're not ordering a lot of platters. Â And remember if you're getting it to go, they only give you 2 containers of the white sauce. Â You can squeeze as much as you want from the squeeze bottle though. Â And be sure to smother your meat w/ the white sauce.

The Momofuku cookbook was the first time I was introduced to the pork bun. Â  No, I use to have to explain, not the char sui bao from Chinatown type of pork bun but the buns that normally comes with the roast duck in Chinese banquets and filled with a tender decadent pork belly with hoisin sauce and cucumbers or green onions. Â I found the closest thing to it for the first time at Spice Kit in SF and then Chairman Bao started rolling it out in its food trucks. Â Both are very good but I knew that I had to try the OG as soon as I booked my tix.
