Â  The pork buns are bigger than the ones I found in CA so far and an order for about $11 comes with 2 buns which were decent size but not quite enough to fill you up for lunch. Â So I also split the fried duck dumplings served over sugar snap peas and accompanied with sriracha mayo. Â Be warned, although it is listed under "large plate", 5 fried duck dumplings really isn't a large plate so unless you plan on drinking the sriracha mayo, it's not going to fill you up either. Â The last item we ordered was one of the country hams which comes thinly sliced like prosciutto and served with a small piece of bread. Â  Since I was planning on going for rice pudding afterwards, it was okay that I wasn't all that full leaving there but you can easily drop $40 for lunch and still be hungry.

TERRIBLE SERVICE. Do not come here if you want to relax and have a good time. We waited over half an hour (after calling to ask if there would be available seating) and then when had JUST paid the bill, we were stared down by the waitress and the waiting customer to LEAVE. Excuse me, we have JUST paid our bill, we have been good customers, why do we need to LEAVE right now? Is this a McDonalds? Is the turn-around THAT fast? Never have I felt so insulted and so shoved out of a restaurant. The food is fine, but after being treated as such - I would rather eat at home.

I didnt' like this place (no offense Amy :). From the location (on the westside Highway), the service, the ambiance, and the food. This definitely doesn't belong in the West Village. There were 4 of us for dinner. We each had a different dish and I only liked one of them. It was way too stuffy and overpriced for the sliver of protein and piece of vegetable that was considered to be our $30 entree.

Omg memories from Summer '10 I seriously did not know they were on Yelp!!!! I believe I came here after a scavenger hunt in the city...BEST HALAL FOOD EVER!! If you are reading this...get the heck up and go...dont mind the cold!!! Seriously they give so much food and extra chicken for FREE YALL!!!! I remember there was a long line and it had to been like 12am!! I actually didnt finish it all but I gave the rest to a homeless man, I bet he was estatic! After that day, I NEVER ate halal food off any cart besides this one!!!

Legend has it that Patsy Grimaldi himself haunts the dining room in this sweet spot located steps away from Brooklyn Bridge Park. Â I heard he will even share your pie with you... but once you have had a taste, you won't even want him to.
hanger steak and duck balls were spectacular. Â alcohol is pretty expensive ($13 beers that are simply not $13). Â which is odd because the food is rather reasonable considering the high quality.
My wife and her girls all have siliac and this place is as good as it gets!

I think I had too high of expectations for this place. I got a plate to go - the sliders, one chicken, one beef - with a side of market veggies and roasted butternut squash. I also got a trailmix and a blondie to go. The food was tasty...I don't know if I would necessarily call it "healthy." I know whole foods are used, it's organic, the meat is grass-fed and hormone free - all things I value and appreciate - but I think there was more oil or butter used on the veggies than needed, I still don't know exactly what ingredients are in their slider buns, and their meat had a little too much sauce for my liking. Again, it was good, but not what I was expecting and not a place I would make my "regular" place, at least not based on the meal I had tonight. I would give it another try and get something different, maybe-- like something from their cold bar or to try their Mash bar thing people have been talking about. Maybe their organic wines are good.. Also, it was crowded with tons of students. I guess I'm getting old because A. I felt like I was in a college cafeteria, and B. I really didn't think half the people there even care about healthy, sustainable, or organic food, they care about whether or not they've tried "the new place in town." Eh, if I'm in the area I'll try it again, but I wouldn't go out of my way for it. Bummer, I really thought I'd love it.

This place in Crown Heights is pretty much the only Panamanian restaurant in NYC and according to the waitress, it's been around over 20 years. If you have had Dominican or Puerto Rican food, Panamanian food will seem a little familiar. This is the place to go to try this cuisine. Some of the things I had here were: -Hojaldres - This is a fried dough appetizer. It's very similar to Native American fry bread or funnel cake that you find on boardwalks. It is a simple, but tasty fried treat. -Carimanolas - These were actually the best part of the meal! They were extremely moist and juicy. The ground meat inside was well very seasoned and I highly recommend trying these out. If you have had the Peruvian papa rellena or Puerto Rican relleno de papa, these are very similar. -Sopa de Pata - I chose this one because I wanted to eat something that is not as common. This cow foot soup is a very hearty broth with yucca and vegetables. The cow foot doesn't sound appetizing but it's not that strange. It is actually mostly bone with pieces of gelatinous fat around it - very little actual meat on it. Taste-wise, it is actually just a so-so soup for me. -Bistec Picado - This pepper steak entree was good, but not great. It was just a bit too salty and the meat was slightly dry. It is similar to beef stew and was okay. Interesting note: While entering the nearest train station at Franklin Ave to go back, we saw the crowd of people getting off going home from work. About 60% of the people were young, white, and mostly hipsters. Crown Heights is sure changing...
Food is excellent and service was great.

I will gladly pay you in hugs for a Two 8 Two burger today. This place strikes a nice balance between burger joint and classy bar. Besides a simple lineup of tasty burgers they sport a very nice beer list as well (if you have a porter you are doing it right). I saw a lot of kids wandering around inside so I guess it's a family favorite too when dad's off the wagon again. If it's your first time get the Two 8 Two burger which has a bold and slightly smoky flavor I have yet to find in another burger due to the roasted poblano they slip into the burger. The decor is fancy-lookin and warm enough here for a casual dinner date too. Play your cards right and you might be slipping her your poblano later that night hermano.
Great late night bite. Simple menu, amazing food. The curly dude is da bomb.

The Cafeteria my wife had actually bought me to the Cafeteria. First off I had like the whole set-up. It was loud and open. I really like the outdoor seating. It was alot of people there but my wife and I was serviced real quick. The waitress was very polite and ready to take our order. It took them about 15 mins to get our food.I ordered the meatloaf and Mac and cheese. I forgot what my wife had ordered but my food was really great. The Meatloaf was very soft and tasteful and tasted like grade A Angus need. The Mac and cheese was cheesy and creamy. I remembered my wife had ordered Chicken and waffles which was delicious. So the Cafeteria gets 4 stars from me.
Great service, food, drinks, people... there really isn't much bad to say about this place. Â  I love the Daisy eggs on the brunch menu... and the black bean dip is awesome.

I regret having eaten dinner somewhere else before coming here to meet up with a friend and watch her eat. Â  The porcini mushroom pasta I tried that she ordered was one of the most delicious things to ever grace my gracious tastebuds. Â  Â Also, we accidentally ordered a $170 bottle of wine (!!!) (I pointed to a more modest $50 bottle but the waitress either needs better glasses or my fingers are too pudgy and simply covered the recession-priced vino I wanted). Â I did find it strange that they brought out a decanter and told us to wait 7-10 min before drinking. Â An incredible Italian red it was (don't remember varietal)--when we got the check I was astounded and told the waitress of the misunderstanding. Â Her manager graciously offered to split the difference with me--which I was more than willing to do, given the amazing bottle of wine we had all enjoyed. Can't wait to come back here next time I am up!
Love the RWB Special! Awesome prices, great service, cozy environment =]

Went for brunch with a friend and was very happy with the choice that we made. I ordered the chicken and waffle as it seemed like 3/4 of the customers there opted for it and felt it necessary to try it myself. My friend ordered the shrimp and grits as she had never had grits before. I normally don't finish all my food but ended up finishing up all the chicken and waffle. The chicken had a nice pretzel crust, accompanied with a chipotle honey mustard which complimented it very well. The multigrain waffle was your standard waffle. The interior of the cafe is very cozy and quaint, definitely not for those who don't like tight spaces. The brunch options also come with a mimosa and your choice of coffee or tea. Overall, I was very pleased with my meal and experience.

I came here with my aunt on a Sunday afternoon. My favorite item was the duck liver on bread. We also ordered roasted vegetables that came with three sauces on the side. My aunt ordered the soup that came with the brussel sprouts and celery. It was very tasty and tasted healthy. The sea bass we ordered here was very tender and delicious. We had one order but the chef split it up into two plates so the presentation looked wonderful. For drinks we ordered a orange spritzee cocktail and I ordered a sweet white wine. Our favorite drink however was the ginger beer. The ginger beer was sweet carbonated I felt like a party in your mouth. My aunt ordered the Honduras French press coffee. The coffee was robust spicy sweet and tropical. For dessert we had the chocolate cake with almond ice cream on the side. I wasn't too big of a fan of the chocolate cake. I had maximum one bite and it didn't capture my attention. However, I loved the almond ice cream on the side. The service here was excellent. My aunt had an iPhone 5 she needed to charge and they had a plug so she didn't have to offer her plug to get her phone charged. Ambiance has an old New York flavor to it. We went during early December so we had a tree in the background and ornaments hanging from the ceiling. Having lunch here so cozy and comforting. We enjoyed our experience here and I can see myself bringing back visitors to this place.

We went to the Meatball Shop on a Saturday night, and while it was crowded, our total wait time before being seated was only 10 minutes. Â I also think that was because we came towards the early part of the night, around 6, I saw that there was a longer line by the time we left. Â We were seated at the big communal table, and even though I would've preferred sitting at a stand-alone table, it didn't affect our dining experience at all. For dinner we got: the naked beef balls with a spicy tomato sauce and rigatoni, a spicy pork slider with creamy parmesan sauce, the special meatball slider (they have daily specials), which happened to be a buffalo chicken slider with Frank's hot sauce and blue cheese dressing, and mashed potatoes. Â All of the above were YUM. Â The meatballs are pretty sizable, so getting 3-4 is more than enough to fill you up. Â The rigatoni was al dente, and the mashed potatoes were divine. Â I might have liked the creamy mashed potatoes more than the meatballs, actually. Â Our favorite out of the meatballs we ordered was the buffalo chicken, which tasted exactly like buffalo wings in meatball form. Â But since it was a daily special, I'm not sure how often they put it on the menu. We worried it might be too little food since sliders are pretty small, but it turned out to be a good amount (though we probably could've added an extra slider or two if we were starving). Â We ordered the ice cream sandwich as well, and the good thing about it is that you can get two different cookies for the top and bottom. Â The peanut butter cookie was soft and peanut buttery. Â All in all, it was a delicious way to cap off the savory dinner. Will definitely come back, especially if we are in the area again. Â All of our food came out to around $30 (meatball entree, 2 sides, 2 sliders, dessert, 1 drink), which you can't beat.

The word is out that this is the place to go! Â I waited about an hour without a reservation to be seated on a Friday. Â The pasta dishes are amazing and reasonably priced and the chianti was excellent. Â I am not usually one to rave about Italian food I was raised all around it and never really grew to love it and feel I have seen it all before but the ravioli here with that cream sauce was phenomenal! Â The spinach gnocchi was good and the sauce was rich I just felt it lacked the sharpness of the cheese it needed a little acidity or something. Â I would come here again - with reservations. Â Also it's cash only, folks.

Oh my deliciousness! So much goodness happening in this place. I dinned here with three other ladies while visiting NYC and we had an absolutely fantastic time. Everything from the intimate, cozy ambiance, to the incredible food, to the knowledgable and friendly service - everything was outstanding. The food is AMAZING. Â We were most drawn to their appetizer list - of which we basically wanted all of them. We ordered the squash dumplings (twice) - to die for; tuna tar tar - fantastic; the burrata - wow, get it; brussel sprouts - so yummy, highly recommend; mussels - great; and oysters - great. Â Literally everything was incredible. We also had really good wine and a few of their outstanding cocktails as well. Whatever your preference is, this place has all the quality libations one could want. We were waited on by Greg (or Gregory), who was fantastic, and really did make the whole experience awesome. He was friendly and funny, but not intrusive. He was super knowledgable about the food and beverages, helped us make selections, and was enjoyable to talk to. Really, the restaurant is lucky to have servers like him because it made an already great dinner, truly fantastic. One of the best dinner's I've had in a long time. Would highly recommend to anyone looking for a beautiful, delicious and cozy dinner in NYC!

Pretty good food. I remember coming here a year ago with friends and we enjoyed it a lot thanks to its nice mix of French food and African spices. I had steak tartare this time, which was nice and flavourful with the horseradish giving it a nice spicy kick. It's a little pricy, as evidenced by the six asparaguses we got as a side dish, which cost .. six dollars. One negative aspect is its layout. Despite having a door tent to minimise the effects of the winter chill, the four tables in front of the door still manage to receive periodic gusts of freezing wind, which cools my enthusiasm for this place.. so to speak..

Meh. Really, meh. Overhyped, overpriced, overcrowded, and bland. Eataly is a large Italian market with themed sit-down eateries, and our group decided on the seafood eatery, Il Pesce. What followed was some bland, pricey seafood. For what we paid, we could've had a great, full-course dinner elsewhere. The brodetto, a medley of various mussels and clams, were good at first. Until you happened upon the sand. Lots and lots of sand. No thanks. The fish fillet was seared nicely (I don't remember the fish - trout, perhaps), but was bland. Some salt please. The pan seared whole fish was better, but again, bland. The buttered potato slices the fish sat on were delicious though. The best dish of the night was the house smoked sturgeon - a favorite of everyone's, and frankly, the only dish worth trying. To be honest, it was probably only so flavorful because it had to be cured. Everything would've been better if the food just had a bit of salt sprinkled on top. But even such a simple detail was missed. Another gripe I have with Eataly is how conformed it is to its themes. I can't get pasta with my seafood if I wanted it. It's seafood, and THAT'S IT. Want some veggies? Go over to the vegetable eatery. Pasta? Pasta eatery is on the other side. Eataly has a great selection of Italian products, but you can definitely get the same quality and variety at other gourmet markets at a cheaper price and with less frustration. For gods sakes, I can't even get coffee or dessert with my meal unless I go over to the (separate) coffee and dessert sections.

PLEASE, please, only go here when emotionally devastated or otherwise broken in spirit, otherwise the abiding vibe of being Underwhelmed will have no positive effect. Nice space - but all so, ordinary. The only bit of excitement was the Lamb Schnitzel - which was, well, nice. Oh god, please, two things - (1) If you are going to rim a cocktail glass with sugar, ensure it dries, otherwise the drink melts it into a mess that drips all over your hands; (2) whats the obsession with female nipple decor - sweet lord it nearly put me off my schnitzel - in the name of equality, a little dick wouldn't hurt Very strange place.

Melt in your mouth pork, flavorful broth, a true Japanese experience. One of the things I love about New York is that you can take these mini trips to other countries in the city. For instance, there is a little Japanese community in the Lower East Side and the streets are littered with Japanese restaurants and stores. I came across Minca on Yelp when I was searching for a delicious ramen restaurant at the last minute. It has a humble atmosphere with friendly service. The menu is limited but filled with good items. I had a pork ramen that was just absolutely delicious. The pork wasn't too fatty, and the broth wasn't too salty. Everything was cooked perfectly. I even like how the tables and chairs felt miniature like you'd see in Tokyo.

Pros (quality, speed, price) - This is a hidden gem on a block that has nothing but bakeries and hair salons. While specializing in hand pulled noodles, the restaurant-in-wall also have a good selection of toppings such as ox tail, lamb, beef, vegetarian, etc for the noodles. Once you order, you'll see one of the chefs making your noodles right in front of you, pulling fresh dough into noodles in the original Lan Zhou way. The broth is very flavorful and the noodles are perfectly cooked. They also have great fried dumplings. Unforunately they usually make large quantities at a time so sometimes you might have lukewarm dumplings. But, if you're lucky enough to get them fresh, they're amazing. Be sure to add the unique garlic vinegar sauce which adds a nice garlic flavor to the dumplings. You can also buy a bag of frozen dumplings to cook at home. Cons (cleanliness, size) - The restaurant is a hole-in-the-wall in the thick of Chinatown, so you should know what to expect before stepping into the place. It is quite dingy and although we've never seen a mouse or a cockroach, we would not be surprised to see them sometime in the future. The place is also very, very small, capable of seating a maximum of 15-20 people. They've been getting a lot of popularity lately so peak time dining tend to be shoulder to shoulder seating. We would not suggest going with more than 1 or 2 people. Recommendation: Lamb Noodles Soup, Dumplings. Comparable to: haven't found another quite like this place yet.
Excellent seafood. Fresh oysters. Friendly fast service. Went with a Home Run coupon, but will be back soon yum!

Stopped in last night before a drinking session at Fontana's across the street. This place had come highly recommended, and while I certainly can't complain about the food or the value, I found it a frustrating experience. This place was packed to the gills. There was nowhere to sit, or even stand. We ended up taking our food across the street and eating in the bar. It also took them a long time to serve us our food, which I found odd because they have these dumplings constantly on the boil. It's not quite like they're made to order. Still, the dumplings were tasty, and the price was right. I subtracted one star for the crowding and slowness.
Great food, great ambiance. Definitely will be back!

Went for brunch on a Sunday per our usual and wasn't quite sure what to expect. I was hoping for three star food not at five star prices. Needless to say when I walked in I was impressed with the decor and set up! The entrance is hidden around the corner and seems a bit frugal at first as you enter by the bar. Then turn the corner past the hostess station and the place balloons open full of rattan furniture that instantly reminds you of the last vacay to a hot spot you enjoyed. Add a mimosa to that mental image to start your brunch off just right. The food was delicious and had no complaints with the eggs benedict AT ALL! Not to mention they whet your appetite for the perfectly poached eggs that await you with some of the best breakfast breads I've found at a brunch spot. Service was attentive and not disappointing in the least.
Nothing extraordinary. Â If you want REALLY good cheescake...walk a few blocks to Carnegie Deli.

I feel compelled to write a review becasue I would really like to see this place succeed. The food at Le Barricou is really good, and yet there never seem to be enough people in there for dinner service (they seem to get more of a crowd for weekend brunch). Â Restaurants--good or bad--never seem to last more than a year on Grand Street, which is a tough location. I am still mourning the loss of Cafe Mexicano, which used to be on the same block of Grand St. I have been to Le Barricou three times. Once for brunch, and twice for dinner. The prices are reasonable, and reflect a nice mix of lower cost options and more special spluge dishes (they have some very well priced items--burgers, sandwiches, large salads etc.,--though the seafood specials are more expensive, but a good value in terms of quality and portion). It seems possible to eat well here and not spend a lot of money if you don't want to. The brunch menu is great and brunch is served with a basket of warm croissants. The eggs florentine were great, and the potatoes were really nicely spiced, browned and not at all greasy. For dinner, I second the recommendations for bouillabaise. They really do a nice bouillabase. The seafood mix changes based on the fish specials each day, and the night I ordered it the special was cod--and the stew was chock full of large, delicous pieces of cod. We also shared a fantastic beet salad. My second dinner there I ordered one of the specials--a fish sandwich with fries. The portions were generous, and the fish sandwich was fresh and really tasty--served with a very nice small salad and excellent fries. I also find the atmosphere to be really nice--maybe a little too faux Â "distressed" french country for my taste, but well done. The place is spacious and airy. It is a neighborhood place and still has an off-the-beaten path feel that is becoming rare in Williamsburg. Too bad there is back yard patio! (but they do have outdoor seating in the front of the restaurant).

OMG!!!! Â CAN I MOVE IN??!!! Â CUZ I WANNA!!! Okay...calming down *deep breath, Christopher....* I can only give four stars since I only had delivery. Â But this place is high on my list for in-person experiencing! Â We called in our order, asked for some replacements they don't usually do, they completely accommodated our requests, delivery was quick, and the food!!!! I had the Mixed Seafood Po'Boy. Â Now, I know my Po'Boys. Â I'm also a fan of a dressed, wet Po'Boy. Â These are definitely dressed...but not wet...and I am still a complete fan (I'll just have to order extra mayo next time ;-). Â The lettuce and tomatoes were very fresh. Â The seafood breading was perfect; not too light, yet not too heavy. Â Perfect for a po'boy. Â I'm not a huge fan of fried oysters, but wanted this bad boy. Â So figured I would make due. Â Whatever they do to their oysters, I LOVE IT! Â Everything was perfectly cooked, tender seafood, nice texture to the batter. My roommate got the fried chicken po'boy...that's right...the one that comes with mac and cheese on the friggin' po'boy! Â I am a mac & cheese snob...and I really like theirs! These bad boys are big! Â We both got two meals out of 'em. Â And the fresh cut fries were perfection. I'll be back to make my way through this menu! Â Just heads up that you're gonna wanna hit the ATM, as they're cash only!

Come with a group and be prepared to take home a "doggie bag" Â but you'd have to be crazy to give this food to the dogs. The chicken parm is great and the pasta is very authentic. Avoid the steak, it's overpriced but the stuffed peppers are worth it. Â Beware this place is CASH ONLY.
best soy latte and good sandwiches!
Fantastic BBQ, great cocktails. The line can suck, and it's not cheap, but you get what you pay for.

5 stars because where else in this country other than NYC can you get higher end late night snacking?!?!?! Plates that I have tried while enjoying EO's delicious drinks are: 1. Bone Marrow Poppers- If you are not afraid of pure heavenly fat, this is the dish for you. Â It comes in about 3 to 4 poppers so it's not overload if you share with others. Â I just feel overly excited whenever I know I can come here to order bone marrow at 2am. Â  2. Steak Tartare- The best tartare that you can possibly find at crack hours of going out! Â Even better they come to your table and prepare it for you, which is AWESOME for a late night bar! Â There's an option if you even want to make it spicy or not. Â This is my favorite dish here! 3. Truffle Fries- Truffle? What more can I say! I guess it depends on the night and time that you come to Employees Only. Â I have been here where it is overly crowded and you have barely any room to even walk, which sucks. Â But most of the time, I just request for a table and it hasn't been a problem. Â It is way better to grab a table and enjoy your drinks there instead of standing amongst all the tall people. Â I feel like EO isn't QUITE a speakeasy other than the mysterious EO sign at the door but it is so crowded that I feel like it is more of a lounge than anything. Â It is definitely intimate in the seating area with high ceilings. Â The staff are awesome and very catering. Â I ordered the millionaire drink which was whiskey based and I loved it. Â It did the trick. Â Prices are your standard speakeasy drinks at around $15-$19 even, not a surprise to me anymore. DEFINITE recomment for late night munchies and drinks! Â It's just too bad all the good stuff is so far away from the UES!

I give this place a 5! My friend made a reservation fro us to come in on a sat night. The food were amazinggg!!! everything pork! such a cute place too Below are a list of things that we got.. -Seaweed Salad -Some fried chicken appetizer..it comes with their special marinated dressing that is a bit sweet/savory/sourt. So good!! perfect combination. unlike other ones that can get at izakayas. -Grilled Tonsoku - omg this thing melts in your mouth. the best. i can eat 3 plates on my own no doubt. Hakana Ton ton hotpot - this is sooooooo goood!!! so much meat in it! in the end they will add in rice and egg to the broth. so much foood. Green Tea Ice Cream Sesame Ice Cream - SO GOOD Gream Tea almond tofu dessert i think those are the highlights. but everything there is gooood! our waitress was super friendly too. when we left she ran out and gave us each a piece of candy out from her pocket and told us to come back. we def. will!

One of the greatest wine lists in the city - and at retail prices. The food is also delicious - although I am not a meat lover myself, all of my carnivorous friends rave @ the steaks ! I always have whatever fish they have on the menu and have never been let down.

My girlfriend and I are Mexican foodies - this place is merely a 3 star. The tacos are small and not as flavorful as you'd hope for. The service on the Saturday night at 10PM was super slow. 20 minutes to take our drink order? Meh.

I highly recommend Piora for its food, drinks, and ambiance...just be prepared to spend some coin. You can expect apps to be in the $15-20 range, entrees in the $25 -40 (most are in 30s) and beers $8 / drinks $15+. We started with the monkey bread and burrata. Â The tomatoes were so fresh and delicious, and the burrata was soft and creamy...I just wish there was more of it. We split the bucatini, which we both thoroughly enjoyed...so much that I was wiping my plate clean with bread. For entrees, we had the lamb and the halibut. Â We really enjoyed the tomato broth that came with the halibut and just intensified the flavor. Â The lamb was cooked very well and was complimented by the fava bean puree. Service was good, very attentive...maybe even too attentive. Â Dining room is tiny but has a cool feel about it.

If there is a god of ramen, he works at Ippudo. His brother, the god of long lines, mans the door. The wait is the wait. I have as much patience as the next New Yorker, but despite it I still give it 5 stars. Come on, there are x number of seats and 5x number of customers, they can't do anything about it. You can go walk around (Amsterdam Bar & Billards is across the street for the Homers and Barts, and the Strand bookstore is blocks away for the Lisas). Just come back way before the estimated time, they sometimes seat you earlier if others ahead don't return. The servers let you enjoy your meal once you are seated, and I have never felt pressured, and our water cups are always full. Now what have you been waiting for: The pork buns - steamed warm soft asian-style buns wrapping a glove of healthy green lettuce, 2 slices of the juiciest pork belly, and special sauce. To give you an idea, I am a beef not pork person. When I eat Kobe beef I cut away the fat - yes, a shame, but I can't stomach fat. Here, I gleefully swallowed. Arteries, take one for the team. The ramen - I eat ramen about twice a week for the past 10 years. I eat it from the holes-in-the-walls to the fifty dollar bowls. Nothing I write here adequately describes the god of ramen at work. Just go. Â  The various broths - I have tried the Modern and the Special (spicy) so far. Modern is spot on - not too salty, not too sweet, and the real test is when you toss a second helping of ramen (for $2, a steal), because here is when you can tell if the stock is too weak (becomes bland) or deteriorates with temperature (flavors change). None of these occur. The broth works. The half-boiled half-egg - unsung hero, comes with Modern, or add on for $2 (or $3?). How do they get it semi-hard on the outside and semi-soft on the inside? Yes that slice of pork belly was delish, but that egg wins a Best Supporting Ingredient. And I am not even an egg fan. Verdict? I'd eat my last meal here, and happily spend 2 of my last 24 hours in line.

My husband and I stopped by SoCo last week after a few friends visited this new spot near Pratt's campus. The decor was nice and I love the cleanliness of the bathrooms. However, the food was so-so. The special of the day was Blackened Scallops and the presentation was great but the scallops were not blackened at all and actually not seasoned. I give the dish a 6 out of 10. My hussband ordered the fried chicken and red velvet waffles and did not like the waffles at all. They were chewy and just tasteless. The batter has to be changed or that dish is not going to last. However, the chicken was seasoned and fried to perfection.

I brought a girlfriend here once for her birthday and now we are no longer together... Just kidding, but your girlfriend would kill you. The service at David Burke Fabrick is absolutely atrocious. I rarely give one stars, but for this restaurant I have to give an exception. We came to David Burke Fabrick to celebrate a friend's birthday. We came in with bright smiles and left robbed our innocence. When was fine dining service at a David Burke Restaurant ever this bad? 8:30 PM - We made a reservation for 8:30 PM and arrived promptly Host - "Please go up to the rooftop bar and we will get you. Your table is currently not ready" I thought alright it shouldn't be a long wait...30 minutes later...no update...nothing...we go downstairs to find out that we had to wait an additional 30 minutes because our table was not ready. 9:30 PM - The Waiter seats us down I was asked the waiter to take our order multiple times. Looking around not sure why it took over 45 minutes to order our food. The restaurant was not packed by any means, only half full...why was it taking so long? 10:15 PM - Food Ordered Food here is mediocre. 1. Avocado Panna Cotta - $16 - Good but expensive for only a few tortilla chips 2. Grilled Skirt Steak - $29 - Probably best on the menu but very little portions... 3. Lamb chops and Ribs - $34 - Very dry and lacks juice 4. Pork shoulder Baked Can O'Rigatoni - $27 - I have no idea what I ate...not very good at all. 5. Octopus - It is okay 11:15 PM - Food Arrive And of course don't forget about getting the check because that also as you figured took a very long time. What makes fine dining great is the service and food. Neither scored highly...I am never coming back. Hasta La Vista Baby...

One of the biggest let downs of my life, I'm afraid to say. The pizza was ok just nothing compared to Grimaldi's, which does their pizza in the same style as I'm sure most people already know. Yeah it just didn't seem to deliever on the levels which Grimaldi's pizza does. The crust was over done, the sauce and mozzerella didn't seem as fresh. It was very very busy, as I'm sure it always is being so famous. So you're waiting a long time to get a seat for a pizza which doesn't seem worth it. The atmosphere is pleasant enough and the staff are nice and friendly, just the pizza lacks that special thing which makes it unique.

This is my go-to spot for brunch. Â No crowds (I'm scared that's going to change after this review, but I'm willing to share the love a little!), reasonably priced, reliably good, an incredible cup of Americano (one of the best in Nyc), and a super sweet staff to boot. One of the few restaurants in New York where the waitstaff knows my name because they're simply nice and personable. The owner is just as sweet. It's a solid choice for dinner too and has lovely ambiance at night, but I think the brunch steals the show here. My top brunch picks: Cup of americano - love at first sip The french toast - some of the best I've ever had Crostini poached eggs w/merguez - inventive and absolutely delicious Fried egg baguette - simple and good Guiness chocolate cake - the perfect ending to a great meal; homemade too! Passionfruit mojito - an anytime drink, super refreshing, super addictive If I lived near Elizabeth street, BarBossa would see me every morning. Â And simply the thought of that puts a smile on my face.

My wife and I find ourselves going a lot. In the first place the people make you feel like your part of the family. We are always welcomed when we come. The food is always good. From the specials to the staple on the menu. The roasted garlic and hot peppers are the best.

Came here with a group of friends for brunch a few weekends ago. Their brunch is a $26 prix fixe, which in usually I'm not a huge fan of. I was served things that I wouldn't have ordered otherwise, but was pleasantly surprised. The meal was well - balanced, with mindful portions, and came with a mimosa. I would return.

I loved my experience at Grimaldi's and I think it's worth the trip to Brooklyn. We came on a Sunday around 5 and waited about 20 minutes. We started with the Antipasto which was just okay- it confirmed for me that at a pizza place you should stick with pizza! My boyfriend and I shared a pie that had italian sausage on it. It was maybe the best pizza I've ever had. The ingredients were so fresh and I could literally see the guy making the pizza. I'm taking off one star for the way the tables were crammed. We were sitting next to this couple we didn't know at practically the same table- we were essentially on a double date. It was a little awkward. So, you don't really come to Grimaldi's for the date atmosphere, FYI. Also, it's cash only!

was such a delight here on a sunny Saturday afternoon. Our early arrival before 12pm meant we had the bright, open space nearly to ourselves and the full attention of a sweet, if slightly spacy server. I had the coconut brioche French toast ($12), which came in a healthy serving of three slices and fruit. I'm usually a savory breakfast girl through and through, but today this sweet concoction was the perfect counterpart to a side of spicy merguez sausage. It was a healthy serving of four slices. My friend had the green eggs with quinoa hash, which was also quite tasty. Washed down with two coffees, this was my ideal Saturday brunch situation.

Quite simply, this is where to go for great chinese. Â Why do I say , "quite simply"? Â Any yelper can throw away any notion of ambiance or a dimly lit romantic dinner. Â This is the real Chinatown. Â Lights up, no manners, and an 'get in and get out' attitude-yet the food makes up for any perceived rudeness. There will be a line. Â Go up and tell the door lady how many are in your party. Â She'll give you a number, and despite the long line, they are incredibly fast. Â You will be taken to a large table to eat with strangers unless you have a large party. Â If there is one chair available at your table? Â It will inevitably be filled by a stranger, but it was still a pleasant arrangement. When seated, expect to be yelled "DUMPLINGS?!?!" almost immediately. Â It is one of their most popular items, and why many travel to eat there. Â The crab/pork dumplings were incredible. Â In the menu they have their popular items already outlined. Â We ordered standard items (general tso's chicken and calamari with black bean), and were amazed by the freshness and overall quality of ingredients. When dinner is done, they bring free oranges for dessert, and automatically put 15% tip on your bill. Â Remember... CASH ONLY! I'd definitely go back for the food and fast pace that makes this one of the best in Chinatown.

Are you broke, yet looking for some place to eat out? Â Do you like Chinese dumplings? Â Are you looking for an eatery that's super cheap yet tastes good? Â If you answered yes to any of the questions, Dumpling House is your destination for the day. The dumplings (and other foods) here are sooooooooooooo cheap I always wonder how this place stays in business. Â The taste? Â It's actually really good! Â The restaurant is hella sketchy and dirty, but plz ignore all the ambience/decor aspects here. Â There's a line to order, but there's almost no meaning to it since you'll find people cutting in front of you if you don't watch out. Â I guess this kind of chaotic disorder is the standard for Chinatown, which can be a subtle stress. You are here for only one reason: Â Eat Dumplings.

I came here for soup before a train trip... because I can't stop thinking SOUP. Â So good! Â This place lived up to my standards--which are getting high from eating soup all the time. Â  ...and I got a free lunchtime tequila shot for New Year's Eve, so there's that.

The background story here is my gf had found out 2 days before her birthday that she had Celliacs disease (that means you cannot have anything made out of Wheat!). Well, that made me change my birthday dinner plans! Well, after some investigating i found myself making reservations at Bistangos... I am sooo grateful I did! The moment you walk in, it is intimate and quaint. The server IMMEDIATELY asked us if anyone had any food allergies. My girlfriend was self-conscious about it, but they made her feel great. They brought out Gluten Free bread which had her smile from ear to ear! Our meals were both Gluten Free. I had a the Cavatelli con Salsicca! LET ME TELL YOU... if you fed it to me in a traditional restaurant. I would have been BLOWN AWAY. Then you tell me it was Gluten Free (I ordered it Gluten Free to make her feel better!) and Oh My God! Amazing! She had the Fusilli Bistango and LOVED IT! Wine was good! But the best was that when I told the server (I forgot his name, but a nice guy that was from Greenpoint! lol) it was her birthday, he jumped right on it and surprised her with a Gluten Free Red Velvet cake that tasted perfect! So if you need a date spot, or a good spot for someone who has Celiacs... DO NOT HESITATE!! Also, this spot serves things NON GLUTEN FREE, so do not think you need to have Celiacs to only eat here! This is a legitimate restaurant in Murray Hill!

Everything was delicious. Seriously. I was with a party of seven people (two young kids) and everything was fantastic. We got items from every corner of the menu - the Mediterranean breakfast (that labne cheese!), the Malwach (wow.), steak and eggs, millet pancakes, smoked salmon sandwich... Everything was neatly presented and tasty. The brunch cocktails are a little silly (I always feel a little absurd drinking brunch cocktails) but I had a tasty Bloody Mary, and it was only $6 with the brunch special. Nobody complained about anything and everyone ate every last piece of food on their plate. The wait was impressive. I wish they were willing to take down phone numbers but the hostesses were kind enough and seated us promptly once our whole party arrived. All the more impressive since we were such a large group. Service was brisk but it was busy so I can't really blame them - at least everyone was polite and smiley. I hesitate to give anything 5-stars but honestly? I don't really want to go anywhere else for brunch. It has everything that I could ever crave from a brunch restaurant. A million varieties of eggs, pancakes, booze, coffee - and everything is (or at least appears to be, judging by all these reviews) yummy. I don't go to brunch very often so this may be "it" for me. I can't wait to go back and try everything else on the menu. Cafe Orlin truly deserves all of the hype up here on Yelp.

Always hopin' and always AWESOME!!!! Everything from the decor to the food to the drinks is just unbelievable. If you are looking for a sassy meal to impress friends and family with-this is your spot. Very NY in its authenticity, ethnicity Â and famous chef (the chef Alex Garcia is well renowned-I think he even has a show on the food network!). I wouldn't recommend Calle Ocho if you are looking for intimacy or low prices but it is worth every bit of what you pay. Try the ceviche and empanadas, paella and get yourself a glass (or a pitcher) of sangria!

This bar has been the perfect addition to the neighborhood and a nice contrast to the Murray Hill 3rd avenue bars. Great atmosphere, great food, and great staff. Nicole is one of the best bartenders out there and always makes me and friends feel very welcome. The menu is amazing too and is a major step up from typical bar/pub fare. Â I feel right at home here!

I've picked my poison and decided to write about my experience here despite the fact that once word gets, I will have to wait for a table. The chef put together an impeccable menu. Everything (I can say everything as I have tried everything) on the menu is crafted with a great level of expertise and care for each ingredient, all of which is extremely fresh. Â The menu does change occasionally but every visit we made, we were able to have: Â  Â  Â  Â  - spice rubbed chicken Â  Â  Â  Â  - pork tenderloin Â  Â  Â  Â  - PEI mussels Â  Â  Â  Â  - marbled potatoes Â  Â  Â  Â  - barley risotto Â  Â  Â  Â  - roast pork sandwich Â  Â  Â  Â  - burger Orchard is great for those looking for fresh and natural dishes. The food is prepared to be flavorful but not overpowering. They do not need to disguise their ingredients. You will not find your food overloaded with oil and grease. The decor is inviting and comfortable. Â The waitstaff is attentive and polite. Yes, we have finally found employees in a NYC restaurant that is courteous and professional. BYOB for now ... or not so you can save every inch of space in your stomach to try all of the dishes on the menu. You will not be disappointed! Very well rounded restaurant!

First off, Jean-Georges restaurant? Sold. My favorites: -the organic chicken with favas and peas -mushroom, parmesan, oregano with a poached egg on top (so amazing) -pretzel dusted calamari -crab toast with lemon aioli, -warm pork sausage with potato and mustard salad. Also, make sure you make a reservation in advance because it gets quite crowded. Â Regardless it is worth a trip and a wait. Â The service was great as well. ABC Kitchen has a nice, earthy, upscale feel to it. Â This place is known for using organic and/or local ingredients which is also a plus.

I recently went to Woorijip for a quick dinner with a few friends and found it slightly packed. The lines were quick though and I got dry noodles with beef which was cheap and quite good. My friends went for the buffet and it turned out to be quite expensive if you aren't paying attention to what you're getting (14+!!). All in all however you can get a solid meal for a very reasonable amount of money.

Had brunch here for the first time with one of my gfs and it was really nice. Â The menu was a little limited and really for my dietary restrictions (gluten free) there was only one thing I could order but it was good. Â The coffee was good as well. Â I like that there's a place like this in my neighborhood. I also like this place much better than Bliss

While I would still recommend Galli, service has definitely seen a dive since I last came. It seems like this place has gotten "big" since this summer and now feels a little cocky. Came in a bit before 8 for my 8 o'clock reservation, and hostess told us it would be a bit of a short wait since they were cleaning up the table. But we weren't seated until 8:20 and when we were seated, there were about 3 other totally empty, clean tables right next to ours. Also, they've PACKED THIS PLACE like crazy to fit in more tables, so that talking to our waiter and receving our food was very awkward because they had to reach over another table. Food and drinks were still great though, albeit on the slower end now.
Great atmosphere and excellent customer service! The food was delicious and not overpriced Highly recommend it

Yum. Just yum. I went for restaurant week, but wasn't super impressed by the options, so I just went with the ropa vieja. It. Was. So. Good. The serve the dish in an old school metal TV tray. It comes with rice, black beans, avocado, and plantains. The ropa vieja itself just falls apart all over the fork, just perfect consistency. The Sangria was also good. It tasted like fruit juice, but also made me a bit tipsy (so I know it worked). The ambiance of the place is nice, even if it is a little loud. I recommend Calle Ocho if you're up for a fun night and good food.

The interior of Church Publick is designed very nicely, and I began making this part of the happy hour rotation for those times my friends or I don't want to just go to just another plain bar in the area. They have a good beer selection here on draft, up to 22 at any given time (not infrequently they won't have anymore of what you ordered). Â There's also a full bar with a very standard selection of spirits, and a moderate wine list. Â It's a nice place to have a few drinks, but is definitely not your most budget-friendly option in the neighborhood. Â  The one time I actually ordered dinner here, I was very impressed. Â With a friend, I shared the Goat Cheese Gnocchi, and a Market Fish Special they had that night. Â Sorry, I forget what kind of fish it was...I just remember it sounding good when the waiter mentioned it. Â  Gnocchi is rarely made great in my opinion, and to my absolute surprise, they were awesome here. Â There was almost an ethereal feeling to them; light, fluffy, and just melted in your mouth. Â Goat cheese wasn't overpowering, and the parsley pesto was a nice complement. The fish that I can't name was cooked perfectly, and tasted very fresh. Â After having these two dishes, my opinion of the chef is that he/she knows exactly how to texture food so that it FEELS good as you bite into it and taste it in your mouth. Â While the fish itself was prepared just right, the flavoring on it was rather bland, and didn't do much for me. Â  I've also ordered the chips with beer and cheese fondue here a few times. Â Its pretty good, very heavy, and comes in a sizeable bowl. Â They're hard to resist when they're sitting in front of you on the table, so unless you have at least 4-5 people, you might end up feeling too full for anythign else after.

I grew up in NYC and grew up on Big Wong's. Â  They are a no frill, straight up consistent authentic chinese food place. Â Don't expect friendly service or correct orders but they will correct it. Â They will forget some things so remember to ask for it if it doesn't come. Â When we come, we like to order the following communal dishes: Â roast duck, roast pork, soy sauce chicken, chinese vegetables. Â Then we would order our own noodle, rice or congee. Â If you get congee, you must definitely get the salty fried dough for dipping. Â This is fast food and incredible food. Â  Â If you have chinese friends, make them go with you the first time, it helps to get the lay of the land. Â makes ordering easy too! Â It's super affordable. Â I'm giving it 4 stars for the food....it's chinatown so dont' expect fabulous service, just thank the lucky stars if you get food on the table. Â oh....please remember to place the tips on the table, not up front where you pay....the waiters get distraught and will run after you....it's hilarious!!!! Â oh..and if you go alone, you will be placed at the same table as strangers...no worries, just ignore each other and all will be well!
Good food and service, but crowded and cash only.

Beyond Unimpressed. First in line, waited nearly an hour while they "cleaned up and fired up the coals". Then waited nearly another hour for the pizza which was only good, not great. The waiter was offended when I asked for a time frame (this after 45 minutes) for when we might expect the pizza. He dropped it on the table and we never heard from him again. Seriously? Restaurant Abuse. I grew up in NYC so I am not thin skinned, but this is old and tired stuff. Poor service is not charming or interesting. I will NEVER go back. Meh.

Superior meatballs appetizer. Very good roasted Branzino Skewed wine selection because it is totally Italian. Â No other regions were represented in the wine list. Even though this is a premium restaurant, If you like Macallan Scotch, forget it. Â They don't carry that either. This place is so busy, I was exhausted just waiting for our with all the other people at the bar not to mention just trying to get to the table.
Looked for a place to eat and drink after getting my tattoo at Flyrite and this place was off the hook. Â Had a sample of everything and it was all YUM. Â One of my favorite spots in Brooklyn.
Love the food here! Almost all the tapas are delicous! The atmosphere is really nice here too. It gets really loud at night, but it's fun. The food is well priced too. Breakfast is delicious too!
This was great!

I've been here twice, first for take out and the second to eat in. This place does get pretty busy so be prepared to wait, though, the wait is usually 10 to 15 minutes at best. The food here is great and everything taste so well. For take out I had the steamed soy chicken which was perfect! The chicken was thoroughly cooked, darkened slightly by the soy and just the right level of salt from the soy to make it eatable alone if one wanted. For eat in, I had the Chicken Pan Fried Noodles. I tend to usually eat chicken when I'm out but wanted to try something I've never had before. The pan fried noodles comes with spinach, chicken and the pan fried noodles which is in a square shape and sauce all at the bottom of the plate. I loved the dish and would get the same thing again if I went back. The wait staff can be a more attentive, it helped my friend speaks their language to get them to come over when we needed them. As for sitting arrangements, if you don't mind sharing the table with strangers, then this is the place for you. Though if not, you might want to stay clear unless you want to give it a try. The price is CHEAP! You can't get any cheaper than this for this great food. I particularly wonder how long the prices will stay like that before the increase. As a side note, this is a CASH ONLY place! So be prepared! I'd definitely would come here again if i'm in the area.

I love their food and their service. I should write a review because they do not fully honor the Yelp deal. Â When I arrived, I was told that I wasn't allowed to order anything from the last page of the menu since I had a Yelp deal. Check out Thomas V.'s review.
Such a great deal for breakfast - 5$ or 6$ for eggs, toast, potatoes, coffee and juice -- I like the laid back atmosphere and the service was good. Will go back to try lunch sometime...

The staff was delightful; however, the food was overrated. Maybe we ordered wrong. The dessert looked amazing, but we passed. The raw diver scallops were overloaded with lime and chilies - even after we removed the lime and chilies, there was nothing special about the scallops. The ricotta ravioli was plain and the bowtie pasta with veal meatball was in a sauce that Â tasted like BBQ sauce with too much brown sugar. The restaurant is super cute. We got a table by walking in early on a Tuesday night. I really wanted to like the place....maybe next time.

Does anyone that works here have opposable thumbs? Â Whenever I open a sandwich from Tina's, the bread is either ripped, the dressing is on the up-side of the bread, and the ingredients are strewn around like the personal belongings of a philanderer, after his angry girlfriend puts them out on the lawn. Â As a part-Virgo, this consistent lack of presentation is slightly unnerving. Â  As a part-Leo, however, taste always trumps all, and in these messy sandwiches, there is always good taste.

The menu is unique. Choose your own style of meatballs, choose your sauce and select an interesting side. The restaurant is compact, but worth it. I had a beef meatball with parmesan cheese, risotto with asparagus, & parsley served under the meatballs, and a side of honey roasted carrots with walnuts, mints, and prunes. It was delicious!

Even with the lowered bar of Midtown East workday lunch, this joint probably can't compete with the rest. The food is just messy and overly salted in most cases, and for $10 a plate there should be just a bit of thought put into it, not the dirty cafeteria lunch line vibe. The food does not taste good to me, but that's a purely subjective statement. Try it out for yourself if you're in the area; it's not a big risk and you might end up liking it. I know many of my coworkers do, and I'll happily come back at some point.
gives chipotle a run for their money. love going here. so yummy!

I was first introduced to Brickyard about a year ago as a bar. Â The evening bartenders were amazingly friendly and this was always one of my favorite places to go late at night. Â Several months later I tried their food and it was fantastic. Â With great lunch specials and friendly staff this has become one of my top choices for a quick easy lunch in Hells Kitchen. Â  The truffle fries are legendary.

Ok, first off - who the F*&%! did we think we were rolling in to have dinner at 10:00pm Monday night? Â For a moment, I guess we thought we were authentic New Yorkers.....alright. Â YOU MUST EAT HERE. Â This restaurant is a national treasure. Â I had a delicious "Grey Gardens" cocktail (or three). Â My table ordered the seasonal tasting menu. Â This was one of the most phenomenal meals of my life. Â Since we didn't know when to say when, we ordered something crazy like five desserts. Â There were only three of us at the table. Â And just for asking about how ice wine is made, our server brought us all a surprise taste. Â When the check came, we were each given a delightful little package containing a fresh coffee cake muffin for the next day's breakfast. Â My gluten free world shot to $hit.....well worth every bite.
Nothing bad about it. But I certainly wasn't blown away. I guess it was just fine.

Stopped by around 2:30amish one adventurous night. We were seated instantly and the staff was pretty attentive. I had the Curry tofu soup, which was very good. The tofu was soft. A downside is, I wish they served fishcakes in their side dishes.

Delicious artichoke pizza!!! It seems like forever for them to bring out the pizza but its totally worth it and thanks to Neha S. So i finally tried the margarita pizza and not a fan so stick to the artichoke slice

I went for dinner on a rainy Monday night so there was no problem getting a table. The whole meal made me and my friend giddy. It was all so perfectly fresh and delicious. The flavors were delicate and balanced. The chicken tenders with green tea salt are mind blowing. The soba is amazing. Also, the toilet seat in the women's room is heated! My new favorite spot...

I'm always happy after eating a banh mi. SO GOOD! When you first enter the store, there's a few chairs for you to sit and eat. Then there's a small counter selling jewelry. Keep walking though; what you're looking for is in the back. The drinks and cold food are on the left side, Â along with TV displays showing the menu and prices. There's a small oven thing on the right side that holds the hot food, like spring rolls. You order at the counter, and the order usually comes right away! If it doesn't, it's a good thing because your sandwich is fresh!! My favorite is the spicy bbq pork, YUM! One sandwich is more than enough to satisfy any hunger. Plus it's only four dollars! A+ in my book!

I give four stars because it's good value for the taste and quantity and for the divey basement interior experience in midtown. Â With another friend, Â ordered and shared the hamachi sashimi, grilled squid, stewed eggplant, deep fried shrimp with mayo (very tasty and little spicy), mackerel (lightly grilled but still kind of raw, not sure?) and he had a beer and I had tea, it came out to about 20 bucks a person. Â The food was overall tasty and filling, similar in quality to taisho in the e. village.

The BEST pizza I've ever had. It's like naan covered in pizza toppings. So so good. We always get the hell infield pork pie white with post oven arugula added, and the cherry jones.. Sweet savory and a little spicy thanks to hot honey. And Paulie is the sweetest.
Worst slice of pizza in NYC, I prefer #1 NYC Pizza Tottonnos.

Wow. Who would have thought that fried bacon would go so well with powdered sugar? I didn't! I was very skeptical before I ordered, but was glad I chose that unique burger afterwards! The food here is exceptional; I've been back a few times now. Most items are a little unusual, but are always delicious! The ambiance is interesting. The restaurant is filled with old "family" photos and 1980's memorabilia and they often have an old movie playing. It's definitely worth the trip if you're into American food. BYOB!

My friend Katie is a total sucker for tartan and anything European, specifically British; Scotland is close enough in her opinion to love that too. So that's the extremely short and simple reason we wound up at Highlands on a Friday night. We decided it was high time to have a girls night, so four of us trekked in the rain to the corner of West 10th and Waverly. Obviously we grabbed the cocktail menu and went to town. Do you even know me? I ordered The Young Pretender (bourbon, Manuka honey, tarragon, lemon soda) and really loved it. I think I drank four throughout the night. I know you are judging me. But they were really good, you guys. I didn't even realize appetizers were being ordered, so stuff just started arriving at the table. I blame my drink. The Whipped Ricotta Pot came first and my god that was good. The ricotta was really light and fluffy, and had perfect accompaniments. A little honeycomb, crispy jambon and toast and I was sold. I know you will be shocked to find out I was using the toast to clean every last morsel of ricotta off my bread plate. I've got class if nothing else. Whiskey Bread also showed up and I'm no stranger to whiskey, so I dove right in. I also used this as a vessel for the ricotta, which proved an excellent choice. Take me back! As an entree (I ordered this one myself, thank you very much) I had the Braised Short Rib. It's fairly typical of me to get a braised anything, specifically short rib. I guess I'm a glutton for heavy and hearty meals. It came with potato and horseradish croquette, roasted pearl onions and brussel leaves. The onions were a little undercooked for my liking, and the potatoes were only just okay. You know what was awesome though? The brussel leaves. I was super disappointed there were only 5. Legit, five leaves on the plate. Not five brussels, five LEAVES. Weird, but so tasty. Next time I will ask for ALL the leaves, none of the potatoes or onions. Leave that other ish in the kitchen. I'm not necessarily a dessert person, so I tend to be indifferent about ordering a plate of it at the end of a rather large meal. Or any meal for that matter. But the girls wanted something and YOU GUYS: they had Sticky Toffee Bread Pudding on the menu and so I obviously raised my voice the loudest and insisted we get that. Sometimes I am really shocked I still have friends. But I have known these girls since I was...I don't know...6? So they pretty much know the drill and are very accommodating. PLUS - I didn't insist on choosing the restaurant, so I guess I'm learning? Doing better? ANYWAY. The Sticky Toffee Pudding shows up and I was really not lady like at all and similar to the ricotta, licked as much off the plate as I could without getting stares from absolutely every other patron. I love food. I almost can't help it. I would definitely go back. Although it was pretty loud, even for a Friday night and the tables are squeezed in pretty close and feels a bit cramped. And don't go for the sides...hard pass. But for all the other foodstuffs I mentioned? Worth it. And the drinks? Double worth it. It's worth noting the decor too, what with the tartan upholstered wooden dining chairs, deer heads on the wall and everything is mostly candlelight, which I like a lot. Cozy, especially on a cold rainy night for sure. I was bummed there wasn't room at the bar to hang a bit before or after dinner. Check it out, it's worth it. Let me know what you think.

Place is spot on. We went "light" last time there. 1 lb of wings- different than typical buffalo wings, in all the right ways, not over thought- spicy with lemongrass? and the burnt ends split between 2. Â Burnt ends are too saucy, but that's just personal preference. Sides of slaw, no mayo, Â and baked beans, Â spicy pickles veggies - really good, plus a beer each. Â Great set up- staff was a lot friendlier then when place first got rolling. Not pretentious or over stylized- just good food and atmosphere. Â Nice to roll in to cafeteria style service, but not rushed. Kitchen, is spotless. Â Going for brontosaurus rib next time.

i am not a HUGE red-meat eater, and this burger was awesome. so awesome in fact that i could have eaten two. have always sat outside here - they have a great (heated) deck which allows smoking, but is also spread out enough that if you aren't down with smoking its not an issue.
Juicy tender pulled pork. Smokey spare ribs. I loved it!

The food was outstandingly creative with portions that were appropriate to be able to enjoy the food without over indulging. I asked to have the menu explained to me add I was unsure of some of the ingredients and how they would be prepared. One of the chefs reviewed the menu with me and his enthusiasm and pride in the dishes offered made me want to order all of them. We ordered the kale salad the skate cheeks the bread and the squid ink pasta. Heaven on earth in a lovely cozy atmosphere. How happy I am that they came back after the flood. I will definitely return.

Cafe Ollin is a bright spot amid the sea of Mexican mediocrity here in new york. Â Authentic flavors, dishes, and ingredients make for a tasty meal from people who clearly know what constitutes good Mexican food. My all time favorite dish here is the gordita. Â It comes with pork rims. Â I have no idea what pork rims are or where on a pig the rims are, but somehow this greasy pile of meat and fresh veggies/cheese is so divine, I don't care at all. Â I'm also a fan of the tacos and tostatas with carnitas or carne asada. Â The burritos are packed with beans, rice, meat, cheese, avocados, and jalapenos, but sometimes they just don't do it for me...too ricey I think. Â Plus both ends are open, making for a slightly messy experience. Â  They would get 5 stars but the service both in the restaurant and for delivery is quite unpredictable. Â Sometimes it works perfectly. Â Other times they call to tell me they are out of something, only to replace it with the wrong item. Â I ordered two gorditas. Â They were out of pork rims. Â I asked for carnitas. Â They said ok. Â I got one chicken tostata and one chicken taco. Â We called to say that was not carnitas, nor a gordita. Â They said they were out of gordita shells. Â So they at least replaced my order with a carnitas burrito for free, but it took an hour for the delivery. Â So they try their best to make up for their errors, but sometimes it gets a little frustrating. Â  All in all, though, I will continue to frequent Ollin when I'm craving my pork rims.

For a brunch spot in Manhattan, you can't get much better than this, particularly if you're looking for above-average food that is cheaper than your regular $15 brunch spot around the block. Despite the fairly miserable weather this morning, my girlfriend and I arrived to a nearly-full restaurant around 10 this morning. You don't get too much personal space here, but it's a little better than at some other spots (like Extra Virgin) that really pack you in like sardines. Although the place was pretty packed, I felt service was a bit on the slow side...not a total dealbreaker, since we passed the time sipping on monk blend tea (this stuff is pretty good, by the way). For food, we went with one savory and one sweet dish. On the savory side, we had the baked eggs with Italian sausage. It was really good, as it adds a tomato-y Italian flair to the dish. I'm a bit unsure if I like the baked eggs that are done here better than Spoon, which does something similar but with less tomato and more potato, but both are amazing regardless. For the sweet side, I had the Texas French toast. I'm not sure what about it makes it Texan, but the toast was delicious without being too thick (as some toast is wont to be), and the fruit (a good helping of strawberries, blueberries, and bananas) and whipped cream added depth to the flavor as well. You can't go without mentioning the orange blossom syrup, though, which rocks my socks - definitely one of the best syrups I've had in a restaurant. In short, get yourself down here for brunch! It does get crowded, but not backed up to the point that spots like Penelope do in the morning. It also won't hurt your wallet as much either. While juice is a bit steep ($4.50 for a glass of fresh OJ), the standard 2 eggs with potatoes and fries costs $4(!). Yes, that's right...and that's probably cheaper than the local dive diner as well. A great find whose only downside really is not being as close to public transportation as other spots.

Decent pho (3/5) broth, but needs more noodles, and meat. Another person who ordered the same thing at our table got way more food than I did, need some consistency here. It was only 9 bucks before adding fishballs/meatballs ($2) which is pretty cheap. Sparerib on sugar cane was pretty cool to try (4/5), and the sauce definitely makes the dish. Also these guys know how to cook chicken, I had some of the juiciest chicken ever with slightly sweet flavoring on the skin from a friends dish.

People complaining about paper plates and the burger not being the best in town are missing the point. This is a great place for a super cheap burger and beer. The burger is not the best ever but it is damn good and comes up fast since it's basically the only thing on the menu. The beers are under $3 and the burgers are not much more. I was pretty broke and craving burgers with my boyfriend and I think we spent $25 for dinner and left happy. Good bang for your buck and a nice neighborhood to walk it off afterward.
Food here is amazing (especially the chicken liver bacon sandwich) as are the drinks. Staff is friendly. I will be going back probably about once a week.

Place is crowded and noisy so at the front tables you will be almost Â be playing kneesies with the next table. Â Maybe I ordered the wrong thing but the blackened catfish sandwich was so mayo laden and the bread so soggy that you couldn't taste the catfish and you feel like you put on 5 pounds. Â Subtlely in flavor is not their strong point.

Ok, the food is good, but expected. It is a Mario Batalli restaurant. Really stuck to the cheese and wine area, so I'll have to go back to check out the other stations. Went on a Sunday night, busy and a relaxed atmosphere, but honestly, I can pay for just as good wine and cheese and get a seat too. The bar top/ standing style of eating is uncomfortable and not fun when trying to take in the ambience, personally it ruined the experience to me. Plus, it's basically the market version of Otto Enoteca (exact same bar tops as in the front of the restaurant, and being that Otto is a Mario Batalli restaurant, it is clear they got the extra tables for Eataly at a good wholesale price. Sorry, but I have to keep it real. Was the food good- yes, wine- yes. Price- yes. But I've experience the exact same thing at other establishments and was able to enjoy a seated experience. This kind of reminded me of an upscale version of the Ikea food area. Plus, last I went, no one in Italy actually stands and eats. It's actually blasphemy to experience food in such a crude way. Overall, worth checking out for a casual experience, but I wouldn't make this my end all be all destination.

i stopped by this place to see what all the fuss is all about. there was a bit of a line when i got in (about 8 people in the line in front of me). one of the the first things i noticed was the cleanliness inside. it looks newer than the other vietnamese sandwich places i've been to around here. they also have a few counters to sit down at. i ordered the #1 bbq pork banh mi and a aloe drink. they were pretty organized with giving people their orders by calling out the receipt #'s. the sandwich was tasty and the bread wasn't too hard (which i hate). it was large enough for me to save the other half for later. overall, this place is pretty good. i like it a bit better than some of the other vietnamese sandwich places in chinatown, but it's no ba xuyen in brooklyn.

I came here with a few girlfriends for happy hour. House wine (Bordeaux and Riesling) and house juice (cuke, ginger, and mint) were tasty. Smoked devil eggs were also nice. Love the simple touches and rockin' ceiling. Waiters were nice, but there seemed to be too many for the crowd during this time frame. On the younger side. Would come back again to try some more food and juices!

Was told that this was a MUST while in NYC. Loved their Decor and service. We started with house cut fries. They were perfectly seasoned and hot. We shared the fried chicken and mushroom pizza. The fried chicken's batter was very light and flaky. I prefer a light batter and because it was flaky, it wasn't drenched in oil. The chicken was very tender and juicy. The pizza crust was thin and chewy. I wished the farm egg was cooked a little more. It was hard to capture the yolk since it was quite runny. Is recommend sharing and saving broom for dessert. There was quite some interesting options but unfortunately we didn't have enough room.
This place is great. Doesn't get too crowded. Good atmosphere. Great beer selection which constantly changes. I wish I still lived uptown so I could come here more often.

Ice cream sandwiches here are worthy of trying. I came here per a friend's suggestion for dessert around 10pm on a Friday night, and was surprised as to how crowded the place was. Â The trick is to skip the line and go all the way back to the take-out section, where there were only 2 people ahead of us. Â It's create your own ice cream sandwiches style, where you can choose cookies and ice cream flavors pairing. Â I had ginger cookies + vanilla ice cream because I wanted something light after a somewhat heavy dinner. Â The ginger flavor isn't too prominent and the creaminess of the vanilla ice cream helped balance out the spicy aroma. Â I highly recommend it even if you aren't usually a ginger cookie fan. Â You might be pleasantly surprised!

Don't eat the waffles! I ordered chicken n waffles of course and was disappointed when I saw these skinny little soggy wheat waffles! The chicken was good, very crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside. Interestingly it had a slight flavor of pork rinds to it which wasn't Â a bad thing in my book. I guess for a place that specializes in fried chicken I expected more.

3.5 stars. SUPER cute ambiance, lots of space to be seated, and very cool vibe. The waiter was chatty at first but later got annoyingly nosey and kept coming over to clear our stuff, ask us if we wanted more although we refused many times. A tad bit annoying. The food was good! Interesting white bean paste dip that comes with the bread basket in the beginning. AMAZING mushroom flatbread. One downside was that my friend and I had many mosquito bites after the meal! It needs attention - definitely. Nosey waiter + mosquitoes ruined it a little for me.
So good. So effing good.

Came here on a Friday night with my girlfriend. Â They were one of the few restaurants without the bothersome person standing outside by their menu trying to shuttle you in. Â The service was nothing short of exceptional. Â We had wines by the glass since we both wanted different menu items. Â She had linguine with shrimp, and I had Zuppa de pesce. Â All of the fish was fresh. Â For dessert we had flourless chocolate cake, which was amazing. The restaurant is homestyle, a great place to relax. Â There were also several large groups, but that did not delay or rush service. Â Would definitely go back again.

Best Greek Restaurant Â by a mile in the entire city. The only drawback, huge lines all the time. If you are patient enough, food is AMAZING. They always give you a complimentary desert at the end. This place rocks.
The shit
Super cute place for a date! Good portions and good service. The backyard area is great, a little buggy. Area is iffy, but classic BK, becoming gentrified.

Worth the hype. The best pizza I've ever had. I think it's the the extra olive oil in the dough which results in an almost fried bottom that sets this pie apart. Only a poser would add any toppings. Because it's in a predominately Jewish neighborhood, steer clear on Saturdays when most of the other businesses are closed and wait times are ridiculous.
Yes yes and yes. My grandmother who was born in Sicily must have started cooking for them because damn it's amazing. And super cute.

spread love, it's the Brooklyn way a wonderful lyric in the middle of gun toting Bed Stuy neighborhood. Â Kinda wants to make you trade in a Gun for a plate of food. Yes, that's how creative there choices ARE... Chicken & wafles; Grilled Squid (whole), and there popular Foie Gras Doughnut for dessert. you will end up having rich dishes indeed. Food most culinary chefs dream of and only daring tattooed cooks concoct. enjoy your plate and tell them George sent ya... Be sure to show up and stay late..

It's hard to rate a place based only on two dishes, but from what my boyfriend and I saw, it was great! I got the pulled pork sandwich, which was very nice, and he got the Korzo burger, which was FABULOUS. (I'll admit, I had dish envy.) The staff was very friendly, the draft beers were tasty, and the decor is really inviting (the space is rather small, but what can you do?) Will definitely return to try more things!

What a great brunch spot! Â The name is cute. Â The food is amazing. Â The people are friendly. Â Only thing is that it's SUCH a popular place that there are so many people jam packed into this place. Â Make reservations!!! We ordered the vanilla bean french toast for the table. Â They're sort of a must. Â The texture is kind of ridiculous. Â So tender and fluffy. Â I didn't know bread could evolve to something so beautiful. Haha Definitely check it out. Â Worth every minute of the trip.

yum yum yum and YUM. my friend and her bf who live here said i HAD TO COME here and i'm glad that we went for brunch on saturday - and thankfully she made a reservation because the place was packed! the brunch special is ideal for NYC - $25 for bottomless drinks, which were strong and great and an entree of choice. i had the OMELET DE ESPINACA, which is: an open faced spinach and oaxaca cheese omelet topped with piloncillo-sun dried tomatoes & drizzled with roasted tomatillo sauce. it was a monstrosity, and it was worth every bite. my friend had the HUEVOS RANCHEROS (her favorite - and i tried and it was definitely delicious), which is: two sunny side up eggs over a crispy corn tortilla and refried black beans covered with salsa ranchera, topped with crumbled chorizo, queso fresco and crema. her bf had the BURRITO TEXANO (didn't get a bite but looked damn good), which is: texas style breakfast taco; flour tortilla filled with eggs, chihuahua cheese, potatoes and chorizo covered in a creamy tomatillo sauce. for 1.5 hours you have a choice of drinking a frozen margaritas, mimosas, bloody mary's or house beers. let's just say we left happy. the one issue - there was a little piece of plastic in my omelet, which didn't gross me out but could have been bad. our waiter, who was great, was also new and really didn't handle the situation well. he should have alerted the manager right away before he left and handed us off to a new waiter. eventually, it got back to her and she comped us 2 meals so we only paid $27 for an amazing meal! the service really was great, they handled the issue well and the food was delicious. go here if you have the chance! i know i'll be back next time i go to nyc! OH and i checked in on yelp and got a great dessert (tres leches) for free! another reason to love it here :)

Well once again its been quite a while since my last update. But I figure the less frequently I do it the more places I have to comment about right? Personal issues aside, let me start out by saying that I've been told to come to Paprika ever since I moved to the city 3 years ago. Its somewhat of an east village Italian institution. Anyway, the opportunity to visit finally presented itself a couple weeks ago when my friend's b'day dinner reservations fell through and we were scrambling for a place to seat the 8 of us at 8pm the day of the event. Needless to say, I suggested to Paprika and I was sure happy I did. To reiterate what many on here before me have said, Paprika seems to specialize in Italian minimalist decor.
