The dining area is rather large by east-village standards and while the room is somewhat sparse in terms of ornamentation it still feels warm and inviting. Aesthetics aside, the real reason to come to Paprika is for the food. While the portions here may not be large the food was rich enough so that most of us found ourselves unable to finish. I sampled several of the different pastas, ranging from the gnocchi to the parpadella, all of which were wonderful. The food and decor coupled with warm and attentive service (they let us split the bill using 6 different cards!!) made for a great experience. My only quip would be that the vibe was a little more laid back than we were looking for (ex: romantic bordering on loungy vs. louder group atmosphere). This made for great table conversation but not necessarily the ideal situation for a group of twenty-somethings trying to celebrate a 21st birthday. All in all though, I was very pleased with my experience at Paprika and would not hesitate to return in the not so distant future.

These guys are the best - so hard working and will do anything to make you happy. The hog taco is by far the best and their pork vermicelli is amazing - always ask for it spicy, they give you the concentrated spicy sauce that is bomb. Make sure to get a stamp card - 1 stamp for every $5 spent. They're cheap but that stamps add up quickly. Lychee green tea is also extremely refreshing. LOVE THEM!

Came here last weekend and I've been kicking my self ever since for not still living here. Sweet Afton, where were you when I was an Astoria resident and needed a steady bar? huh? huh? Came here with a group of friends last weekend, and it was just a fab night at a fab bar (that I had been dying to try out). The place is rustic inside there's a large front area by the bar and tables all around, then a skinny area in back with some more tables and a little patio with a few more tables. Lively scene all over...great crowd. Unpretentious all around. Even the guy checking ID's was a sweetheart. Good waitress service too. There were 6 of us and the boys ordered $9 burgers...which I took a bite of after watching juice flow down their wrists...I couldn't contain myself. I was hell bent on getting the $5 fried pickles...oh we got them and then we got another basket and then a third. Holy moly were they good. Warm pickle on the inside beer batter doughy goodness on the outside...and a smokey sauce with a slight kick. I mean 3 baskets says it all. They use McClure's pickles from Brooklyn and they are just good on their own too! All cocktails were $9 and I was in the mood for a cocktail...first I tried the Spicy Cherry margarita...it was pretty good...the sweetness of the cherry preserves balances out the spice but I was in the mood for something tangy after that. That where the Dirty Pickle Martini comes in.......this is my new favorite drink. It's just Â pickle juice, vodka and slice of pickle. They're strong and you don't feel the onslaught coming and they have the perfect balance of flavor. I've been craving this taste combo ever since and I can't wait to go back, ASAP. I want to try everything else at this fabulous find. Must have more pickles! YUM, YUM, YUM!
Totally in love with it and have been there more than ten times!!! The same food as I had in Asia. Please don't be there because there will be longer time to wait for the seat. JK.

This place is full off racist employee. They only care about white customer. I have a $100 bill and they tried to call the cops and block me in the store thinking it was a fake. Little they know it was the new hundred dollar. Was it because I was a young rich black man and not a drug dealer.

For starters, we ordered the butternut squash soup and a side of the sweet potatoes. The soup was flavorful and creamy, but the sweet potatoes were a little too lemony? so we didn't really touch it. For entrees, we ordered the short rib which was savory and delicious and the roast chicken which was a little dry, but which had a wonderful bleu cheese sauce. For dessert, we topped off with a chocolate bread pudding which was moist and fell apart. It was pretty fluffy and was a good light dessert. Service was great from start to finish. Good date spot.

I love soup dumplings! I personally enjoy these more than the Din Tai Fung ones in Taiwan, which is blasphemy for some, but these are just... more delicious. I think they are slightly greasier, but that's probably what makes them taste so good. Please make sure you have cash, since it's cash-only. We waited about 30 minutes on a Saturday night. I didn't love the lady barking out numbers angrily, but about 20 minutes into our wait she seemed to have a change of heart and started asking for all our numbers and asked us to be patient. Once we were seated, a waiter came by very quickly to get our soup dumpling orders, so that we could get them started while we decided on what other things to eat. We got one order per person: two pork ($4.95 each), one crab ($7.95), and it seemed like just the right amount. We also got a soup to start-- super reasonable at about $5-- and each got at least a bowl's worth out of it. To try to balance it out, we got stir-fried snow pea shoots, which were the most expensive at about $14, and another appetizer. Everything came out quickly and while the place was busy, I never felt rushed. Service is about what you expect at a Chinese restaurant, though I think the servers' English here is better than usual, probably because it's such a hot tourist spot.

Found this on Yelp and lucky us! Â I would never have stopped at this place (Amsterdam & 116th) if I didn't know about it, because of the very unassuming outside and simple inside with photography on the walls. Â  Soooooo glad we went in. Â  It was a worthy find! We had the lentil soup, which came with two slices of delicious bread. Â Then we had the curry chicken salad sandwich... Just the right amount of curry (for me), bright red tomato, crisp lettuce, fresh avocado on a tasty multigrain roll. Loved it loved it loved it. Felix, one of the owners, is friendly and welcoming. Found out he is a graduate of the Culinary Institute of America and is originally from Cuba. Â He loves the food that he cooks (with Glen) and it certainly shows. Â  Fresh, delicious and satisfying. This is going on our list of places for lunch and dinner whenever we're on the upper westside. Â  Go, eat, relax, enjoy!

Mr. Sanford, whoever you are, I LOVE YOU! This place is 5 stars. No...6 stars amazing! I can't even begin to explain how awesome this is. I came here after a Pilates class in the area. I trekked in the snow here based on the awesome reviews and my desire to have as much brunch as humanly possible since I have worked weekends for years and always miss out. What a way to make up for lost time. We came in to the cute little spot and was greeted at the door by a small line and a helpful hostess. She was pleasant. Informed us of the 15 to 25 minute wait and took out name. Of course we were going to wait. I ONLY went to Pilates because it was so close to this place. As we scanned over the menu (I already had a few ideas of what I wanted based on my yelp menu stalking) we handed her back the menu and after a few minutes (definitely less than 15) we agreed to take a seat for two at the bar. Now usually I don't opt for bar seating. I just don't feel like you get the full experience of a place sitting at the bar. Bar tenders become waiters and that is totally not their forte'. Here... no such thing! The bar tender/waiters were awesome! As we sat down, first of all, the bar table is made out of this awesome soft marble that just felt so cozy leaning on. The chairs are perfect height for the bar and this super soft leather. Super comfortable. The lighting in the place is all dim and feels really intimate even at the bar. The bar tender came over right away and laid out silverware and got 2 glasses of ice cold water for us. He handed us a menu and gave us time to look it over. There wasn't a need for much time. We instantly knew what we wanted. I ordered the champagne (with 1 refill) the crab cakes egg benedict and nutella s'mores waffles to split with my friend. She ordered the steak skillet and requested they throw a splash of OJ in her champagne which they gladly did. We chatted and had a grand old time and not once did I feel like I needed to be quiet because we were seated at the bar. It was a really comfy atmosphere and no one made us feel like were were over stepping any boundaries laughing it up. When our food arrived I was in awe. The diners beside us stared as well and complimented how delicious our meals looked. I couldn't wait to dive in. The waffle looked gorgeous. This place sure knows how to make something look appetizing. My crab cake benedict looked delish as well and my friend's steak skillet came in an adorable little skillet. Now for taste. It all looked so good I didn't know where to start. Since I'm a big fan of potatoes I went with my home fries first. A nice serving of potatoes. They were sliced and had the perfect crunch to them. It came with a little container of ketchup and I usually always ask for more wherever I go but surprisingly this little serving was more Â then enough. My home fries were amazing. I watched as my friend divided our waffle. All the oweeee gooey marshmallows and nutella got all stuck to her knife and it only mad me more excited to try. She took the first bite and I knew as soon as I saw her face that this waffle was something I needed to get in to. I waited. Just to tease myself. lol I tasted my crab cake benedict and was extremely pleased with the taste. The hollandaise was amazing and the eggs were perfect. Runny but not dripping down my hand. Delicious. The crab cake was super crabby and seasoned really well. I asked the bar tender for some hot sauce to throw on top. I thought he was going to pass me the tabasco sauce which was pretty close but instead he reached under the counter and pulled out a bottle of Cholula!!! WOOT WOOT! One of my fave sauces. I HATE tabasco and I was so pleased I even had to let him know how much I appreciated this gesture. Â He let me keep the bottle close for my whole meal. He was such a great bar tender/waiter. Finally I was anxious for the waffle and with the first bite I was sold. I can TOTALLY understand why this spot is top 100 brunches in the universe. That waffle was every bit amazing and unlike anything I expected or anticipated in my life. It was the perfect amount of sweet with delicious regular waffle for homestyle-ness. It was so perfect. Every drop of my meal was fantastic and the atmosphere was friendly and cozy and super comfortable even though I was sitting at the bar. I didn't want to leave. The bathroom is a single room and it is kept clean enough for a single. I wasn't skevved out by the room at all and willingly put my purse down on the counter which usually I'm cautious about. Man oh man. I can not WAIT to come back here. I couldn't even finish my meal and I finish my meal everywhere. I was pleasantly stuffed and had a whole half of my crab cake eggs benedict to take home. I was really surprised about that. I starved myself just so I could truly enjoy all of my brunch and I could only handle half. Needless to say if you are looking for brunch THIS IS THE PLACE and the price is super reasonable.

This review is for brunch, and this is one of the BEST brunches in the Slope/Windsor Terrace area! I mean $16 for brunch with unlimited wine, mimosas, or sangria. The food is delicious! My friend loved her eggs benny, and the steak sandwich with fries and salad that I got was freakin' delicious!!! The bread was toasted perfectly, the fries were homemade, and the salad had just the right amount of dressing on it! Also, the sangria was good and it kept flowing. Our waiter was so friendly and awesome! He was always back just in time to pour another round! We loved him so we had to overtip him big time! Near the end of our meal, a baby shower group came in. I only had a couple more bites left, so, the manager came and let us know that they would need the table; he was very professional and nice about us. He carried our stuff to the bar, and they promptly filled us up with more booze and water! And even after we were done, one more for the road! That place is the best! Can't wait to go again tomorrow!

Awesome place to grab a drink in the hood on a week night, although this place is totally different on weekends and would avoid (too crowded and noisy). Â Bar tenders are cool, beer selection is great, and music selection is perfect.

okay okay i know with the way the economy is everyone is looking for ways to save money...but really???? what happened to the FRESH blueberries for the blueberry pancakes? i feel like they've switched it to canned fruit. very disappointing! it's still good, but it's no longer awesome.

Like you needed another review of this place to convince you to go and slurp your head off. Well I got the basic chicken ramen, added an egg and corn for a delicious combo. The tame broth is flavorful without being too overbearing. Honestly, you can legit see them cook and look at the clock to make sure the noodles are al dente and you can tell they take pride. The wait is redic. I went by myself and waited 20 mins lol. But so worth it. Tips: sign your name on the list on the front door. More than four people and you won't be seated together. Yes it's that small. Otherwise this place rocks!!

I forget how much I love Spanish food then I go to a place like this... Every dish was so good. Â From the simple peppers grilled with salt, through the perfectly cooked dates wrapped in bacon, stuffed with manchego cheese, the bacon perfectly crispy and scorched and smokey and the date sweet and soft, oh my god perfection--through an outstanding piece of fish with root vegetables, not to forget a heavenly crema caremel (all chased by sangria, then a glass of rioja)...this was quite the evening. Not to mention a hip setting, loud and buzzy and energetic but somehow with just the right acoustics that you can still talk to your date. Yea baby, loved this place!
Do yourself a favor and order the lemon pasta. Simple, but delicious! I'm going to try to replicate at home. Excellent service, cozy environment. Bring CASH!

cute little restaurant situated in the heart of west village. Â their garden patio is to die for....so request it and sit there before it gets too cold. Â  great selection of wine and pasta. Â i went for the fisherman's stew.... which came out in a dazzling presentation.... (the thing was bigger than the size of my head...) Â it looked like a mushroom and the bowl was covered in a dome like flatbread. Â Once you pop it, you will find seafood delights such as mussels, scallops, shrimp & clams, in a wonderful, fragrant light tomato broth. Â It was excellent. Â  the fried artichokes are a must.... a bit on the salty side...but it was crispy. Â all the pastas were a good choice and about 90% freshly homemade.

What started out as a bizarre experience at the door, waiting for someone to acknowledge our existence for over 10 minutes...quickly turned around into a fantastic hearty meal for 2. Someone eventually realized that we had been standing at the entrance and not being served. Eight or so people working the bar and yet it takes 10 minutes to get noticed at the door. Really?!!? Â It was close, as we were seconds away from leaving. Cooler heads prevailed. Anyways, the gentlemen genuinely apologized and even presented my companion and I with some delicious champagne. You are forgiven. So the reason we came here was to try the fall harvest dinner special with wine pairings. Aside from the brussel sprout salad (first course), everything was absolutely perfect, including the wines. I wish they substituted the salad for some warm soup. However, I can safely say that the roasted chicken was the most tender and flavorful chicken I have ever had. The side of sweet potato gnocchi with the pomegranate seeds completed the dish. The wine pairing was once again excellent. Finally, apple pie with a slightly stronger chocolaty tasting wine, was exactly what one needs on a cold fall evening. I am glad we stayed because the meal was as described above, amazing. The service, on the other hand, can use a bit of an upgrade.

dude. So good. Â This was probably the best meal I've had that was made in less than 5 minutes. Â Except maybe some of the stands in the night markets in Taiwan I've had. Â  Their chicken plate with rice and salad was to DIE for. Â Came here the next day for dinner again and their chicken gyro was awesomely GOOD. Â and for $5?? HELL YEAH. Definitely my meal of choice in NYC. Â Grab $5, get a plate/sandwich to go, sit, and enjoy..........mmmmmmm............. droooool. Â ask for the hot sauce. and white sauce. mix it together. drizzel over plate. experience orgasm that comes in your mouth afterwards. Â lots of carts out there claiming to be the original gyro truck but this is the real deal.

This place rocks! Very Brooklyn, and naturally very good. This place doesn't take reservations, however, we were able to score a table for 3 on a Saturday night only after 15 minutes. The ambience is wonderful esp wooden beams on the ceiling, and chalkboard lining the wall. Appetizers: Â fennel salad, and antipasti Entrees: monkfish, chicken breast and lamb ribs. I have to say they did a very good job with the chicken. I am not a chicken fan, and wow, I was impressed. The skin was nice and cripsy and the meat was juicy, flavourful and tender. The mash potatoes were out of this world and the kale was just right. The fennel salad and antipasti were both excellent. The menu is small, but really, if you can make every dish to perfection, then the eatery has accomplished its goal. and here at lot 2, they scored! Just curious: Â Is there a Lot 1?

Went here last night while in NYC for a few days of fun. ATMOSPHERE: smooth. Low lighting, great community conversations around you. Awkward: the music was a hodgepodge of everything. Would encourage more ambiance appropriate music. FOOD: Me-Flounder on bed of greens - nice and light, flavorful. WIFE-Pan Roasted chicken...prepared well, looked like avg fried chicken though much better. HOSTESS: Very Very Very nice - warm and welcoming smile. Â REVISIT AGAIN - Definitely yes.

Absolutely delicious. I think I ordered some kind of chick pea wrap (gluten free + vegan) for dinner. I will never forget the delicious raw/vegan chocolate pudding dessert I shared with a friend. To. Die. For. Do yourself a favor and go eat here :)

I really REALLY like Siggy's. I order one of 3 things everytime I order from them. Â The Greek or Beet salads and their Greek omelets. Why not 5 stars? For some odd reason they will only serve omelets at Brunch and some other special days. I guess people don't eat eggs in the afternoon or night? It's sad as I would rather order from them but I end up ordering for another place during the week as Siggy's won't make their amazing omelets during the week. Please put it on your weekday menu.
Good joint for an unpretentious breakfast. Nice little diner and they make your food right in front of you.

Mofongo. Â Just.... mofongo. Â The pollo. Â The everything. Â Everything is delicious. Â I love that I feel like I'm walking into a Puerto Rican kitchen and you have aunties in the back cooking for you. Â It's a hole in the wall and I LOVE that. Â Good food. Â Good prices.

I would say, just like Sushi Yasuda, Ippudo's is worth the wait. Â It's not as ridiculously expensive, but an appetizer, standard ramen, and dessert as well as drinks (tea) ran up to about $50. Â Still, it's pretty standard for NYC. Â If you come to NYC, be ready to throw down. Â Photos here: rammiegirl.wordpress.com . Â I can actually do a pros-cons list for this because there were only 3 things that I ordered: 1. Â Ebi-Kani (crab-shrimp) croquettes 2. Â Hakata Classic ramen, plus one egg (not recommended but my personal staple for ramen) 3. Â Hirata Milk dessert Ebi-Kani Croquettes PROS good to split for 2 (4 pieces each) goes great with the grape tomatoes awesome texture: crispy on the outside, not burnt and then soft and creamy on the inside great ratio of crab and shrimp (kani & ebi, respectively) CONS: not much, maybe price for some people but it is snow crab and it is NYC. Hakata Classic Ramen, plus egg PROS -amazing broth, very flavorful and super savory, pork based -good quantity: I'm a pretty light eater though so don't quote me on this. -request for extra ramen noodles applicable: for those of you who want extra carbs to go with that awesome soup. -egg was perfect. perfect. Â Not too salty either. CONS Personally, I'd like more pickled ginger and menma, but that's just my own preference. Â Not a carb-heavy girl here. Hirata Milk Dessert: First a brief description literally word for word: "green tea ice cream parfait with red bean, shiratama mochi, matcha (green tea) jelly, and almond-coconut milk". I think I just died retyping out that description. PROS -perfect combination of flavors and textures. -you're supposed to dump the milk into the parfait: Admittedly, I was the dumb noob who was sipping it out of the shot glass. Still tasted good though! CONS - Again, my own personal preference, but it needs more matcha jelly haha. AMAZING. Â So amazing that some of my ladies at Hopkins and I booked a trip in Jan for Ippudo's again. Â :) Cant' wait for round 2!
Delicious Mexican food. Big portions. Friendly staff. Fair prices. What else is really needed?

I love this place!! I have nothing but great things to say about this restaurant. Cute clean decor? Yes! Attentive friendly service? Yes! Fresh delicious food? Yes! Everything served in cute little dishes? Yes! Came with a friend on Monday night and got seats at the bar right away. Our server was extremely friendly, ready to offer suggestions and food descriptions, and was super on-top of refilling our water and tea. All of the entrees can be served a la carte or as a set menu which includes pickles, rice, miso soup, and a steamed egg (so good!). We had the pork katsu (panko breading, crisp and not oily) and buta yasai nabe (pork and vegetables in broth, lots of flavor). The sets are between $15-25 so the prices are great for the quality and quantity of food. Also I must note the appetizer of homemade tofu was absolutely delightful. It was silky smooth with amazingly subtle flavor. Loved it. I can't wait to come back and try everything on the menu!!

We just got the dumplings, and that is all I can review. I thought they were perfectly good- but not out of the ordinary. Â Perhaps I was not blown away by the concept of soup dumplings because I've had them before in Asia and in LA. That said, it is a nice place to vosot, and I would go back to try their other food.

Words don't do my experience here justice Mind blown every step of the way..ordered: Deviled Eggs-Proper Chicken liver spread- I don't even like liver and I loved this dish. Balsamic helps take away a lot of the gaminess of liver Oysters- fresh Burrata w/ Mushrooms- one of my favorite bites i've ever had. AMAZING Haddock Chowder- Such a well balanced bowl of soup with wide range of tastes that just work(bacon, finely chopped potatoes, basil, etc.). Best chowder I've ever had Burger- Well i feel everyone else has probably hit on this..but what i'll note is..they cook the burger exactly how you order it (for the rest of you medium-rares out there) Went on a friday night..2-hour wait which we passed with drinks and some of the appetizers mentioned above.

I told myself over two years ago that I'd never eat another Subway $5 foot long as long as I lived. It had become a problem, almost an addiction of mine while I worked in the garment district. They were cheap, loaded with mystery meat, and could become not only lunch, but dinner if I were so inclined. But after eating countless horrible Subway sandwiches I promised myself I'd never do it again, and swore that there had to be an alternative. Cut to two years later, I now live and work in Williamsburg, and I haven't had a Subway Sandwich in years. Does this mean I eat $10 lunch specials on Bedford? No. Does this mean that I pack my lunch everyday before I go to work? Seriously? It simply means I found an alternative to the ultra cheap Subway Sandwich. Except this time the food rocks, and it's even a few dollars cheaper. The $3 falafel pita is a staple not only on meatless Mondays, but for at least two other meals a week. I am actually eating one right now; the inspiration for this review obviously. But here's the thing, I have been eating this pita for almost as long as I'd been eating Subway and I've never, not a single time, been bummed about eating it. So packed with flavor compounded by the fact that you literally can't eat a cheaper meal, that each time I go there I almost feel guilty. Everything else there is very good as well, but honestly 9 times out of 10 I'm walking out of there with a $3 falafel pita and a small side of hummus. Suck on that $5 foot long. I never like you anyway. And it WAS YOU, NOT ME!
Steaks are Great there, atmosphere too, but the service is kind of bitchy! Sad!

perfect if you're in the mood for good and cheap vietnamese soup. Â pho wasn't the best I ever had but overall quite tasty-a little sweeter than im used to. friends and I split some dumplings and the duck sandwich which was really tasty. wait can be long but it does go by quickly, it's not a place you are able to really linger at

I generally don't give five stars to restaurants with no vegetarian options, but I love this place so much I don't even care. My boyfriend says all the food he's ever had here has been perfect, so I guess that fifth star is on his behalf. I love all the upstate NY paraphernalia here; the atmosphere is cool and woodsy without being overly Williamsburg about it. The people here are so nice- like, actually nice. Like Midwest nice. Dare I say Upstate nice? (I don't know, I'm a former Midwesterner). Great wine, great beer. Just a wonderful place to sit and drink and decompress.

My daughter came in from LA and we happened on this place. Everything we ordered was so tasty! The baked clams the soup the prosciutto the chicken it was not only glorious to smell but to feast your eyes on and to devour. We will be back soon.

Won't be back. Quality has fallen, now a has been.. Â Was not crowded, showed up for an early brunch. Â  Slow service, food was cold when it arrived, had to walk up to a waitor to get his attention as he was "reading a book" and did not see us waiving. Â Food was NOT what was on the menu (Breakfast Burrito did not come with black beans as mentioned on the menu), but, by the time the food arrived we were so hungry, and late, no time to complain. Â Food OK although cold. . Â I was told the bathroom really, really, really needed an update.

Can be a fairly NY-cheap breakfast for anyone in Midtown. I was under the impression, due to word of mouth, that the place would be more cozy, like an actual patisserie, but it's actually a sleeked-up modern storefront, which makes it better for seating. People were eating lunch & pastries and having coffee comfortably clustered around side-table-esque tables, and it looks like an alright place to bring your laptop/work if you just want wifi. They have Stumptown. They'll offer to warm up your pastry for you, which I recommend. The special pain au chocolat was as much as an almond croissant, so I'd say the croissant was a little annoyingly priced. Pain au chocolat, toasted, was really fun to eat, since it was flaky on top (yes), with ample crunchy almonds (yes), a doughy/chewy inside (yes), with the moderate quantity of chocolate filling melted but not runny (yes). However, don't know if this is because I'd been drinking the night before or this is indicative of the true quality, but the pastry didn't have much flavor. Definitely not half the man a Parisian pain au chocolat is. This is a good place, but maybe don't make it your go-to shop, or your "ooh, you HAVE to go to..." rec for friends. At heart, Tisserie is just...there for your convenience

went here with my fiance, i have been trying to get a reservation for a few weeks, at a norm time (not 530 and not 10 pm) so i was very excited to finally go and try this place out! we walked in and were seated by some hipsters, who were very nice, we were both amazed by the look and feel of the restaurant. Â it really is a beautiful space, its big and roomy, not typical of nyc restaurants. So to start, the bread is amazing so try not to fill up on it before your meal arrives. Â we ordered the spinage whole wheat pizza, was delish, 4 larger peices, lots of spin and perf amount of cheese. not too oily or anything at all. Fiance got the burger, it was heavenly. cooked to perfection, so juicy, and the sauce on it was so good, totally different. i just couldn't stop taking bites pf ot. Â the friees were good also, again not oily at all, and crispy. Â i kept eating his burger bc unfortunately my meal sucked! i got the crispy cod w mushrooms. it was SO bland, and it had this crispiness to it, it felt fried. Â it wasn't oily, it was just a heavy cripsy crust on such a delecate peice of fish, it didn't go at all. it woud've been good if the dish had some taste to it. it was so bland and the musrooms were just blah. i didnt like it at all. Â the service was wonderful, very attentive, friendly and knowledgeable. Â when our waitress saw that i hardly touched my meal and we split the burger (whcih was fine bc the pizza was bigger than we anticipated so we were kinda full anyway) she asked me what was wrong and i told her. she said she would let the chef know, she sounded genuine, and actually cared that i didnt like my meal. Â i thought it was great and i wish more restaurants cared about their diners' opinons. Â we ordered dessert, the pumpkin w this delish cream cheese frosting. it had the perf amt of frosting and constrated very well with the pumpkin. Â plate was scattered w pumpkin seeds too. Â i had also mentioned it was our anniversary on my open table resi, and the waitress brought out cupcakes w. a "happy anniversary" written beautifully on the plate. Â was so nice of her! we were so full at that piont, but it was such a nice thought. bottom line is the space is gorg, service was aweome, and 3 out of the 4 things we ordered were extremely well executed. woudl def go back, and def not order the cod.

Salt and Fat, Perfect! what i crave, i dont need sweet. the crack and cheese is better then prozac for turning a bad mood around. the service is also friendly and fast! Â i had the mussels which i could eat every day until i die and be happy. i just cant say enough about how awesome it was. my husband and i just ate and smilled at each other. great date night. we went on a sunday at 6:15, by 6:30 it was filled to max. but service is quick so the turn around didnt seem to awful. cant wait to go back. bacon makes the world a beautiful place. Popcorn popped in bacon fat..... my grandma would have loved it.

Came here for a friend's goodbye dinner and we had the corn chowder (delicious, nice fragrant blend curry and coconut flavors with sweet corn) the dark knight (I should've ordered that instead) and the zucchini pad thai (surprisingly tasty but disappointed because I thought that there would be actual carb noodles in my dish but wasn't. A little surprised to find a metal shaving in my food but no damage done so ill let it slide this time since I found it at home in the doggy bag). Super cute decor. Attentive service.
The pizza is unique, the sauce and cheese is almost like soup, it's so creamy. Very filling and very huge slices. There is almost no seating though. Expect to stand while eating or getting take out.

After all the hype I had to try this place. I ordered the chicken box with Mac and cheese as my side. The chicken was good nice and crispy. The biscuit was descent but not like the biscuits down south light and buttery. But it is better than a lot of places in NYC so I will order it again. I was not great fan of the Mac-n-cheese with hot sauce on top, I had better. I expected the portions to be smaller here because of the fact this is a hipster spot in Williamsburg so I can't complain about that. The prices are a little high but not that bad typical for the area. The restaurant had that down home theme, mother's kitchen theme with a hipster twist. The pies and donuts that they had sitting out there looked good definitely want to try it next time.

I loved the atmosphere here during a brunch with a friend. The staff was all so nice and very helpful. The menu is kind of a bit too foodie for me, but the stuff tasted good, nonetheless. A really cool cocktail menu too! This is definitely the place I would send anyone looking for a cool brunch spot in Astoria.
chicken & rice! white sauce (take extra to-go for leftovers/dry rice) hot sauce: a drop (the size of a penny) goes a long way! be prepared to wait (on a rather fast-moving line).

I really think this place is overrated and not worth the legendary wait for breakfast (even on a Tuesday). Â It may just be my taste buds, but I could care less for the maple butter on the wild Maine blueberry pancakes. Â Yes, the wild Maine blueberry pancakes were fluffy. Â But I would have preferred 100% maple syrup to complement them. Â I have the same problem with the sugar cured bacon. Â Its just too damn sicky sweet! Â How am I supposed to discern the succulence of the wild Maine blueberries while I am assaulting my tongue with refined sugars. Â Of course the wait was long and I cannot justify it based on the goods finally delivered. Â I agree that it is a bright, clean and nice place to eat. Â And would go there again to purchase their muffins to go. Â But if I want a really good pancake breakfast, I am sticking with Jackson Hole diner in Astoria where I get maple syrup with their larger and equally fluffy pancakes, where they serve you a complimentary small glass of fresh squeezed orange juice with breakfast between 6-11 AM, and where I will go home with a lot more money than at the Clinton Street Baking Co.
Food is amazing Staff is great A lil overpriced But all in all a great experience!
If you're craving israeli vegetarian food nish nush is your spot. Great service, fluffy pita and always delicious. Try the sabich!

The dining experience here is absolutely what you would expect from a world class 5 star restaurant. Â The apple scent upon entry is delicious. Â The restaurant is beautiful with nice domed. Food and atmosphere are amazing. Unique experience. Overall a great experience. We were seated in the lower floor so it was very quiet and the room wasn't filled at any point when we were there. We were definitely the largest party.

So I have an addiction. Â It's called the #1 at Banh Mi Saigon. Â While I've had better banh mi (for instance, Banh Mi DC or Â the Lee's franchises in So Cal), this place is the best that NY has to offer. For newbies, I would advise that you stick to the #1 on your first trip, especially if there is a long line. Â You can expect to wait slightly longer for the other sandwiches, since the ladies in the back are machine-like in cranking out the #1. Â I used to mix up my selections between the #1 and #4 (banh mi pate), but my lack of patience (and jealousy at seeing everyone enjoy their sandwiches while I fidgeted and moped) taught me to go for the numero uno, which never fails.
Always have a great time here with great food. It's a block away from me and I never get tired of it, and that's pretty rare for me! You will love it here, for a group, with a friend. or for a date.
Best authentic ramen. Â Noodles are tasty and service is great

A must when you go to NYC. This place speaks for itself. Best Chicken/lamb and rice I've EVER had. Nothing beats the white sauce and be aware that the hot sauce is really hot.There is no competition anywhere in the USA.

I really wanted to like it more. The room is lovely, the music was good and so was the wine. Â We got the tasting menu for the three of us but it was weird. We never got three plates. It was either portioned as two or one but we were charged for three people. Â The food was good but not outstanding. I'll try brunch next time.

Went back for a third time two Friday's ago. Â The even was cool and the place was still filled with people. Â We got a seat right away at a long table. Â  We ordered 1/2 a dozen blue crabs, some mac n cheese and a lobster and 2 beers. Â Everything arrived quickly, actually much quicker than expected. Â  Then, here's where the team actually did something way better than expected. Â I wound up getting a mushy lobster. Â Yeah, for the 100s of lobsters I've eaten, this has never happened. Â All within about 11 minutes at the most, we had been given a new lobster and a round of drinks. Â  We'll be sure to be back for more tasty crustaceans!

I work nearby in the theatre district and usually frequent the same few bars but am glad I went a few blocks out of my comfort zone and discovered this place!! The decor and atmosphere of the bar are excellent; very modern and trendy style without the upscale snobbiness that's usually accompanied with that. Â On the contrary, the staff there is extremely friendly and the service is excellent. The draft beer selection is fabulous: Â they have a good combination with a selection of the beers that go down easy (coors light, etc) and beers that actually have flavor. Â The sangria and all of the signature monkey drinks are awesome- Â monkey wrenches are my personal favorite!! Being that I usually get off work late, I have only had a chance to eat there a few times but everything I had was excellent. Â The duck spring rolls are incredible as well as the three different soups I tried (they have different ones on special every day). Â I also had the wings, which were awesome and accompanied by 3 different sauces to engage all your tastebuds, and tried a piece of the fig flatbread which was excellent. The three monkeys is also excellent for private parties! Â I had my birthday party here a couple months ago and one of the owners who I was in contact with in regards to planning the party, Kieron, was extremely helpful, accommodating and made the party planning process easy on my part. Â The second floor, where the party took place, is an excellent space for this kind of thing with a combination of outside and inside seating, a good sized bar and even space for dancing! All in all, this place is the full package. Â Great music, food, drinks, staff and atmosphere. Â I would highly recommend this place for dinner, happy hour, a weekend night out, a private party, or just a quick pre- or post- show drink.

five spice duck burger original burger truffle fries margarita peached high decibel atmosphere, placed our names for 20 minute wait. after 30, went back to the hostess to tell her we'll just eat at the bar, she looked as if she forgot we were even on the list. been to the los feliz location many times before always with initial amazement then later downfall. ordered the duck burger as it is only offered at this location. the first bite was pretty good, then the rich flavors and weird mixes (peach apple chutney tasted just like applesauce) became overwhelming with the palate. it was then i remembered why i never had the desire to come here.

The tapas here are great, but even more great, is the atmosphere of Yuca Bar. Â I came here on weekday evening, on a girls night out and thought that this was the perfect spot. Â The happy hour pitcher of sangria, the delicious tapas (I didnt get to try the platos fuertes), and great conversations made this a memorable, fun and returnable place in my mind.

i stumbled upon this place by accident. my boyfriend and i loved it so much i went back with a friend and the love just kept on growing. we met the owner and i had my birthday and book release party here. they are friendly, knowledgable, & the place has a great atmosphere. they have great specials and frequently have beer reps to chat with. which is great cause i am a beer nerd. in a part of town where good bars are scarce this is one of my faves.

Came here last Sunday night with my Irish friend who only ever takes me to bars with Irish bartenders. I don't know if there Is there a list out there somewhere or if he can just sense his own kind, but never the less....he finds them. Swift fit the mold. Within minutes both my friend and the barman got into a discussion which no longer sounded like English. As the drinks were refilled, their accents fell farther and farther away from anything recognizable to me. I just nodded and smiled pretending I was in on the convo. In doing so, my beer was always mysteriously full. Back to my review...the bar was cozy, the beer was good, the bartenders were friendly. I would definitely recommend Swift for a weeknight meet up spot with friends. Definitely get yourself an Irishman accessory, you won't regret it. If you don't have one, you can borrow mine.

I've recently been sampling local ramen joints and Chuko is now on the top of my list! We got there at 6:30pm on a Saturday night, expecting a long wait. The hostess took our number and said it would be around 90 minutes. So we went across the street to Weather Up and enjoyed some lovely fancy cocktails. At around 8pm the hostess called to say that our table was ready - perfect timing! I ordered the miso ramen and it was perfectly delightful, with just the right miso-y flavor and flawless noodles. My friend ordered the veggie ramen after confirming that the broth was indeed vegetarian, and she loved hers too. Highly recommend.

We had a early reservation and were seated right away. I had informed the restaurant that it was a birthday celebration and they were very nice about extending good wishes as we sat down. Service was outstanding from all. The atmosphere is that of a private club where you have been welcomed as a regular visitor . The portions are not huge but hey, this is NYC. They have a huge business whether you have 4 ounces of fish or 8. Just the reality of fine dining in this area with a restaurant with this reputation ! Go enjoy! The quality of ingredients shined through. Make your reservation well in advance and enjoy !

I went to the cafe for coffee this morning, for the second time. Â The girl who usually works there is very friendly and helpful and overall great. Â But again with the prices- I paid $2.50 for a "large" coffee that was not large in any sense of the word- maybe 8 ounces? Â I can get a bigger coffee than that for about 50 cents less near my office in manhattan, so I don't get it. Â And to add insult to injury, when I got the coffee home and drank it (I live literally across the street), it was cold and undrinkable. Â LOWER YOUR PRICES AND SERVE HOT COFFEE!!!!

YUM. Â I typically hate overpriced over-thought out food at trendy restaurants but the tasting menu at The Eddy may have changed my mind. Â Each dish was more interesting and delicious than the last. Â I literally could not pick a favorite. Â Great cocktails, great service (even with our party of 8), great atmosphere. Definitely worth my stingy dollars.
very good food and good prices

Five stars for this exact category of restaurants, not to be confused with fancy shmancy places. BUT. If you wanna have a beer or wine with a bite of simple food, it is the place to go. The bar is cosy, food and drinks are delicious and cheap. Especially nice during daytime, since it has a nice outside terrace and it is not as packed as later at night. But even if you have to wait in the line, it isn't too bad, since the bar is mostly meant for a short stay.

I've been to Good Fork multiple times and, generally, it's been a nice experience and an enjoyable menu. Â However, they're off their game when it's busy: Â that delicious dish you had on a Wednesday will take twice as long and taste half as good on a Saturday. Â The appetizers come out quickly, but you may blow through your bottle of wine before the entrees come. Â Go during the week for the best service and quality. UPDATE 4/2010 I stand by my mid-week assessment. Â I had the deliciously thin pappardelle with some reasonably-priced, barnyard-smelling gamay and it was heaven. UPDATE 8/25/10 I live in Red Hook now and go to Good Fork at least once per month. Â Each time has been a pleasure. Â I can't get enough of the dumplings and the asparagus starters. Â We always end up seeking out the wine we have at local wine stores because GF's recommendations are so spot on to our taste.

The roast duck and wonton soup is a must get. Beef chow and salty fish fried rice fun is yummy. The price has gone up a lot. The food is still amazing. There use to be a bitchy fat Chinese lady at the register but haven't seen her in a while. If she gives you an attitude curse her out and she will not try it again.

It started off fine, but as the feast came out with more dishes, it just got worst. Pasta was over cooked and tasteless. Sauteed Spinach was nothing to desire for. The pork dish was overkilled by the fruit, think was honeydew, it made the pork taste like candied flavor. It's a savory pork...not suppose to taste like dessert!!! The scallop and the salad with crispy toast were very good. We were served with a prefix menu. They didn't even tell us there is a la cart menu. We would have preferred make our own choices. There were 4 of us, maybe it'S easier for their kitchen to do prefix as everything is all pre-set up! Mistake! Now we have no desire to go back, feels like we had more not so good dishes than the good ones...

Nice little place. Â HUGE excellent selection of beer. Â I ordered the Pork Face Cuban to go. Â It was explained to me that they were prepared in advance, so they were unable to remove the pickles on my request, ok no big deal, but I had to wait almost 12 minutes for something that was pre-made, kinda strange. Â Despite the wait, and the $12 price for a decently sized sandwich, I really enjoyed the Cuban. Â The face itself was rich and fatty, salty and umami, just excellent stuff! Â Not headcheese at all, just a pile of mushy pork product that matched perfectly with the cheese and ham. Â Really enjoyed this! Â I look forward to returning to try the Grilled Cheese and other things. Â The staff was extra friendly and welcoming. Â Recommended for sure! PS: do not heed the warning of those who call this "pulled pork"... if you can't distinguish between pulled pork and pig face, you have no right to review this place.

We went for lunch on a recent Saturday. Â The menu was brief, but had several appealing choices. Â It sounds unoriginal, but I had the burger. Â It was excellent. Â The cheese (not sure what kind) and sauteed onions were perfect. Â The cheese platter our table shared to start had some great choices, but the servings were paltry. Â We had a nice pinot gris to start - it was crisp and refreshing, perfect since the dining room was warm. Â All in all, it was a really nice early summer Saturday lunch. Â Definitely would recommend.

I love lombardi's! Â The BEST thin crust pizza out there! Â I honestly think that they should open a west coast branch! Â mMmMMmmMm... Whatever it is that you decide to order, make sure you put extra pepperoni... it's SO good! Â The bread sticks are pretty huge so don't overload on these while waiting for your pizza to come out. Â Settle for the half basket because that's all you'll need. I only have two gripes with this place... CASH ONLY!!! Â Don't forget this!! Â And I've been there a couple of times where the service was slow and the wait was double the amount of time that they initially projected... 40 min instead of 20 min is quite the difference.

overall place was nice, was expecting it to be packed and it was. due to my own issue, I was late and they still seated us right away (place received cool points for that one). waitress was good and she was very attentive (another cool point). food was good, fresh, on point and so was my mimosa (a few more cool points). this kind of place is good for friends or a first day time date (icing on the cake). me and my evil foodie twin (my alter ego) will be returning to sample other items on the menu. to be continued...

We just moved to the neighborhood two days ago and Quaint was recommended highly for brunch, so we went there this morning (Sunday). Â It's so inexpensive!!! Â We were amazed - we are transplants from Minneapolis and the menu at Quaint is less expensive than all of our regular haunts in the Twin Cities. Â Talk about a pleasant surprise! Â The mimosas were only $4 (Bloody Marys too) and everything on the menu that I considered ordering to eat was well under $10. Â In the end, for two rounds of drinks (4 mimosas) and two entrees we paid $35. Â Not bad at ALL! Â You could have breakfast and a mimosa and get out of there for $10 if you wanted to. Â The food was great and the service (we sat at the bar) was prompt, but also very relaxed and nice. Â I think it's safe to say that we'll be going back next weekend. Â As brunch-loving newcomers on a limited budget (who are still acclimating to the New York prices) we are already huge fans of Quaint and their extremely reasonable prices. Â That they also have great food and nice service is almost too much to ask for.

After craving some BBQ for a few days, my boyfriend and I decided to try Mighty Quinn's. We had seen it at Smorgasborg several times, but either they had already run out of it, or the line was so long, they would likely run out by the time we reached the front. This review isn't actually for the East Village location, its for Bergen in Crown Heights. We were a little confused because we looked up the locations in Brooklyn and it listed the address for outdoor Smorgasborg, and then a location in Crown Heights. Since the Smorgasborg locations were only open on Saturday and Sunday, and this was a Tuesday night, we decided to drive to the Crown Heights location from Williamsburg. We drove by where it said the address was, and didn't see any Mighty Quinn's branding and thought either it had closed down or we were in the wrong spot. We decided to just park and walk up to the listed address and ask what happened to Mighty Quinn's. Â What we walked into was better than what we could have hoped - a giant beer hall set up with 4 Smorgasborg 'restaurants' at the end of it, serving their specialties to hungry drinkers. Â  While they were all tempting, we had come for Mighty Quinn's so we stayed the course. I had the pulled pork "naked" (no bun), and the pickled veggies that accompany the sandwich. The bf had the Burnt Ends sandwich. They were both pretty good. The Burnt Ends were quite tasty, but so rich that he couldn't finish. That would be something great to get "naked" and split between 2+ people for a taste of them, because they are great. The pulled pork was great, definitely used a wet rub as it was super moist. The sauce served with both cuts is good - nothing amazing to write about, but definitely accompanied well. The picked veggies served with everything are AWESOME! I wish I had asked for triple serving of those - pickled onions, celery, cucumbers (pickles), and red chiles. The perfect accompaniment to the meat. Â  We will certainly go back to a 'real' location so we can get the experience of the restaurant itself but this place (Bergen) was definitely cool as a beer hall (upscale) and restaurant selection. It would be a perfect Saturday or Sunday day drinking spot with friends, as they have a ton of craft beers and cocktails to choose from, and several food options.

Jacks wife Freda is a great little brunch spot in SoHo! We has to wait around 20 minutes, but it wasn't bad! The green shakshuka was good (pretty basic if you asked me -- just eggs baked with a green sauce that resembled chile verde) but the overall experience was lovely. The restaurant is small and cute, but also does not have a lot of seating. Make sure to account for the wait time!

Love this place for everything! The staff is super friendly and nice. The food is always good! They change their specials daily and they have delicious oysters! The place itself has a great atmosphere, it's very cozy and when it's dark they use candles instead of electricity, which adds up to the charm of this restaurant.
cute casual restaurant in GP. their rice ball is the best and my kids' favorite. only i wish they open on Sunday as well.

I truly don't get the hype about this place, and quite frankly i'm a New Yorker and their pizza is mediocre at best. Â But due to high expectations and the level of volume and influx of new customers they have to serve on a daily basis is overwhelming enough. Â Therefore, they lack in attention to detail and its quantity over quality. Â Our pizza was very bland, and lacked a lot of flavor. Â But I understand their business model and why it works because they get many tourists from all over the world for a one time dining experience. Â With the incredible amount of wait time and rude service from the old man at the door, needless to say, I will not be returning at all. Â And, I truly i understand their ego and the rudeness because regardless their business will flourish and the customers/tourists will always be there. Â But I doubt true locals will though, just my opinion.

BOTTOM LINE: The Dead Rabbit is a fabulous place for drinks and a horrible place to eat. It was hard to decide how many stars to give this place, because its truly a 5 for drinking and a 1 for eating, so I settled on a three and hope to give you some valuable insight into this cute FiDi speakeasy.... The Dead Rabbit is a bit hard to find, so make sure you don't miss the sign or you'll walk right by it. I loved the decor, 1800's theme, candlelit tables, and "picture book" instead of a traditional menu - Â all of these things make The Dead Rabbit very sexy and a great date place. The drinks here are just beyond :-)!!! - so many to pick from and the bartenders really know their stuff. The delicious drinks are the only real reason to stop by here...Must also mention they're pricey -- all $14 each!! On the other hand, the food was literally inedible. My boyfriend and I shared 2 specials and the Dead Rabbit Burger. The actual burger was OK, but the specials ( 1lobster mac and cheese and 1 fisherman's pie) were just GOD AWFUL. All of the food was luke warm and bordering cold (which is the first hint that things are not right with their kitchen service.) Secondly, the lobster mac and cheese was $12.00 and the serving bowl (if you can call it that) was a mini-pan the size of my palm and as shallow as 1/2 inch. It was almost hilarious how small the portions were. The fisherman's pie had no seasoning and tasted like nothing. The few shrimp/scallops it had were totally bland and the mashed potatoes were plain gross. Also, the peas were still hard and clearly were frozen, not fresh and not reheated well. Although it may seem like I'm ranting about how bad the food was here, I still urge you to consider this place SOLELY for drinks - because those were fabulous and the place is romantic!

***Restaurant Week $25 Lunch Menu*** After reading some of the negative reviews about how bad the restaurant week menu is, I didn't have high expectations for this place. I still wanted to try it out since overall it had good ratings. This was my first time trying RW by myself and can be a little nerve wrecking. The restaurant is located on the second floor and you'd have to climb the beautiful staircase up to the entrance. The ambiance was great! I loved the decor and the waiters were really attentive. They moved the table to the side so that I could get in to the chair. My glass of water was always kept full and they made sure to clear my finished dishes right away. For appetizer, I had the butternut squash soup which was delicious! I scraped everything off the plate. If I could, I would have licked everything off. The pickled squash was a nice touch to the dish. For entree, I had the chicken which was also very good. I am usually nervous about ordering chicken for RW but now after this experience, I feel more open to it. The fregola was a yummy addition to the chicken. For dessert, I had the olive oil cake with cinnamon ice cream. Like the other reviews, the cake was tasteless but with the addition of the ice cream, it was the perfect combination. Everything came and went pretty quickly. I would say that's probably my fastest meal ever. Even after a couple of days, I'm still craving their butternut squash soup and cinnamon ice cream. I would totally come here again even if it's not restaurant week.

Ate here last night, and was quite 'wowed' by the food... For primi/antipasta: Gnocchi with butternut squash, and a bitter greens salad with honey, apples, and pinenuts The gnocchi was literal HEAVEN in my mouth, HEAVEN in my belly.....in fact I've sworn to go back to Barbuto's just to consume several plates of the gnocchi as a meal...to hell with it being a Primi! My salad was excellent as well. I couldn't quite identify all the flavors, but the intensity and perfect melding of fresh black pepper and honey in the dressing was fabulous. We ordered the flank steak with chili salsa, and chicken with salsa verde, and be warned: the chicken plate is Huge with a capital "H." Both were delicious, and I think I can say that that was the most tender, juicy chicken roast I've ever had. But maybe because I'm not super-familiar with Italian cuisine, the entree's didn't seem quite Italian to me. Nevertheless, Â a meal worthwhile. Oh yes - and we still managed to have dessert: Tiramisu and Chocolate pudding. Yummy in my tummy :-) Cons: Service was slightly slow. The two ladies who sat down next to us unfortunately didn't even have their meal served until we had finished dessert (and they sat down while we were eating our appetizers/primis. Sad).

I came here in the middle of nowhere to celebrate a friend's birthday. I would readily travel the 50 minutes it takes to come here again :-) The combo plates that we got were huge, but I could just sit for three hours and eat another one. I've never had food quite like this before, but I'm a big fan now. The meat was perfectly grilled and super tender. The taste: to die for. The waiter staff: very friendly and funny. Overall, a great place to go with a large group of people.

Small/cozy restaurant and still had a 30 minute wait at 9PM at night on a tuesday! it was definitely worth it, the brussel sprouts were different and tasty. Â The chicken wings were good but not worth it for the price. Â Got the soy ramen with chicken, probably the best ramen i have had so far and their chicken was to die for. Â Chuko is my #1 ramen spot right now, better than Totto ramen.

Wow who said pepper enhances food? Â OK we have been meaning to eat here since it opened. Â Finally got around to it. Â Here goes, it is small and noisy. Â The ceiling is to low and the acoustics are horrible. The prices have gone up (watched them on the board). Â The portions are small. Â The bread really stinks. Â The main dishes were bathed in pepper, the polenta was watery. Â Do not bother.

My mouth tasted like the rusty back end of a tailpipe.....but I was still ready for what was in store. Â I was dressed in my Halloween's best on this strangely warm October 31.........ladies dressed as Gaga drafting their best poker face and Wild Things strumming along Berry and N. 6th..........wild eyed and darting for the Max that would eat them. so. Â  Turning a blind parrot eye I pass gothics and stroll gazers with gypsy eyes and lantern bags making their way towards Greenpoint as I ventured south and galivant passed lawn gnomes and the occasional werewolf hipster. Â  Finally at the Levee, (would it break?).......a flash of my I.D. and an order of the best beer ($3) my paltry checking account can buy ensued as I knew it would. Â Straight to the bathroom where I check my zombie eyes and contemplate the vampire teeth floating in the toilet water. Â I take a sip of my beer and pray to the Pumpkin god that the Pagans will take me to my seat. Â And Prince's little red corvette drifts me there from jukebox accelerations alone and I can't seem to get the miniature sized Butterfinger bars and Snickers in my stomach fast enough. Headbands and overalls all collected elbow to elbow......the lone girl without a costume but convincing us she went as an American Apparel princess.......no label...no problem. Â I strike a pose and order another beer....and another......and another. Â It's a dead man's party.......and I can't ask for more........so I leave my body and lurch out the door....the bouncer giving me a quick shove like a mummy all outstretched and persistent. I grab my cigarettes...the box ripped up from the take out put back during the last hour ago pocket chain smoke. Â 3 cigarettes left...just enough to get me through till bed. Â I pick one up and light it but there's nothing. Looking down towards the bottom of the butt I see a tiny tear and frustrated, I flick it away. Â 2 left. Â Ration time. I look left......then right.....no cabs in sight. Â I light one more and watch a bodega dim its lights for the night. Nothing good happens after 2am anyway.

Not sure what all the hoopla is about. Â I had their Chicken over rice and was not impressed to be honest. Â I hear the lamb over rice is what everyone loves this cart for. Â I'll go back and try that when the lines have died down a bit.

this is one place that def lives up to the hype! Â i went with three friends, and was able to try many items on the menu, and i cannot wait to go back! the pork meatball was my favorite, followed by chicken, and then beef, but really, all were awesome, its like picking your favorite sexual position, are there any bad ones, really??? and we also had almost all the cookie ice cream sandwich combos: meringue/caramel, brownie/mint, peanut butter/espresso, and ginger/espresso...mine was the clear winner, the meringue caramel, soo good and crispy; all the others were good, too, but i didnt love the espresso ice cream, too strong a flavor, couldnt taste much beyond burnt coffee i HIGHLY suggest coming here as often as you can, it it werent so far from home, i would prolly be a regular here!

This was the first stop for my friends from Chicago when they got off the plane. We needed a hearty meal with a modern twist. The Brooklyn Star did not fail to deliver. First - you must order the cornbread. It will take some time to reach the table, because they are always made fresh - but your patience will be rewarded. Secondly - with mixology, and drinks being the current big thing in Brooklyn, you will appreciate the breadth of the bar options. For those who prefer lighter fair: The beer list is small, but compliments most preferences. Lastly, the ambiance is top notch. The Motown tunes play at the perfect level, and add that little extra something to the meal. I will be returning here sooner rather than later.

Piacere was a true Piacere to visit for a late 4pm) breakfast/lunch today. Â Wife ran NYC marathon yesterday and we found ourselves in bed until an abrupt 1:40 phone call this afternoon. Charming interior - and, since we were understandably the ONLY patrons inside, we had the full attention of a very nice waiter and staff. For appetizers, ordered timballo di zuchinni con mozzarella, pomodoro, e basilico - as well as bruschette tartuffo which, while my wife didn't enjoy (truffles) I most certainly did. Â Ordered a second timballo to make up for wife's disdain for tartuffo! The entrees were good - she had the gnocchi/pomodoro/basilico and I had a very well done (medium rare, that is) tagliata di manzo e rosmarino with arugula and cherry tomatoes. The ONLY letdown (and this was our fault for not thinking such places existed) was that (like Costco) they were an AMEX or CASH operation. Â No lesser cards accepted here! Not to worry, the very pittoresco bathroom came complete with ATM. We'd recommend this Italian bar/bistro anytime.

Very intimate and very casual dining combined with good value Â and good food. Friendly staff and bustling crowd. I recommend. Â Love the Grilled Spicy Beef Salad and the Ratchabury Crab & Pork Dry Noodles. Steamed Vegetable Dumplings and Pad Thai Shrimp was also good.
5 stars square pied.

Fun place to go for a glass of wine and people watch. I have not sat down to eat here, but I do frequent their stand-up tables for some charcuterie and some wine. Then I grab a glass and walk around the markets usually picking up some fish and cheese to play around with at home. Yes I am a food nerd and as a wise man once said, " I always cook with wine, and sometimes I put it in my food". Think this when you wander around the aisles. Be prepared to have every sense stimulated as soon as you walk in. The tastes of salty cured meats, the smells of pungent cheese, and the sounds of young intalin guys yelling all over the place. Visually it is set up to keep you wandering. Cheers.

I don't often write reviews and normally I do so to seriously compliment a restaurant but I came here after reading the incredible reviews by Yelpers with a friend from out of town and to say we were disappointed was an understatement. We started with an appetizer which was delicious. Heirloom tomatoes, crusty bread and a little bit of oil made for a great start. I was impressed with how fresh the food was, our server was marginally pompous, but I can get over it. However, when our pasta came I was mortified to say that I had brought someone from out of town no less, to this place. I ordered a spagetti with red sauce. The pasta was not made in house, but I love red sauce (a really good one) and it was one of the few they had. I made a point to say that I was a red sauce snob and the guy said it was delicious....What I received was a bowl of pasta with a bolognese that was SO greasy that it left literally puddles of grease in my bowl. It was absolutely inedible. My friend ordered a truffle oil ravioli which was just too rich, but by no means as horrendous as what was sitting in front of me. Needless to say, I will be sticking with all of the amazing little Italian places in Brooklyn. Completely overpriced and way too hyped. One of the most disappointing meals I have had in a long time in NYC.

Best empadanas I've had... Â We had the reggeaton, spinach and cheese, shredded chicken on flour, sweet plantain with cheese.. ALL delicious.. The hazelnut cappuccino and the salpicon were to die for as well. Â We thank the "Italian" guys at Playwright Tavern who recommended this place... Super nice staff, very economic, and truly great food.
I guess they're a travelling restaurant in a way. Recently had their lunch special at Mama Joy's in Bushwick, it was so good/cheap/filling and definitely an experience. I would highly recommend!

Took the family here for the second time today -- this time for brunch which if anything was even better than the dinner. Â  Â Full brunch menu --everyone liked the waffles, french toast and omelettes. Â  I had a veggie burger the last time so there are alternatives for vegetarians. Â  Â Sometimes crowded but service is quick. Â  Certainly, the best diner in Queens.

Holy smokes do I love this place. After living in Texas for 2 years, I really appreciate a good slab of meat. The brisket and berkshire bacon are unbelievable for this side of the mason dixon line. I've tried quite a few different things off their meat and sides menu, and I have never left disappointed. They also have a nice selection of tasty sauces. This could be a good OR bad thing, but I recommend wearing clothes you plan to change out of after dinner. You'll leave smelling like meat- I promise. My only complaint is the slow slow sloooooow service. This sure ain't Texas, where the master meat cutters would have that line moving in no time. Hands down the best Texas BBQ I've had in NY.

I loved the atmosphere, the decor, the giant projection screen at the end of the room, Â especially the food..I just loved everything about it. This is my kind of place & they're hard to come by, especially in Queens. I had the Cap'n Crunch fried chicken strips that came with some sort of red chili caramel dipping sauce which was an amazing combination!! My friends both ordered the 3 cheese mac & cheese which wowed all of us. Overall this place is perfect for a date, a place to catch up with a small group of friends..I can't wait to come back!

The food is great. Four stars for the attitude of the hostess though. Oh and they don't take card which is kind of annoying in this day & age. But maple butter syrup is absolutely delicious! Do not come here without ordering pancakes!
best hotpot in nyc!!

Went for brunch on a Sunday, Blvd is a small, sweet place. Interior is nice, enjoyed the food & quick service. I will definitely be back. Just as a tip: try to get there before 1pm if going on a Sunday to avoid a wait.

Go for the ambience. Â The food is perfectly fine, but the real treat here is feeling like you've just stepped into your own personal glamorous movie set. Â  Cocktails are strong, not so refined, but definitely in keeping with the theme. Â You feel like these are drinks that would have been served at a speakeasy during Prohibition. Â Fun place to go with friends from out of town, who will feel like they got a special NYC experience (ok, forget for a minute it's a British import). Â  Don't miss the opportunity to hang out at the Gallow Green rooftop bar. Â One of the best in the city and perfect for a rendezvous of any kind. Â Go and enjoy yourself!
Had an awesome time here for happy hour. Great food/drink deals and an awesome vibe inside. Orlando at the bar is the man!

Came into (and when i say "into" i really mean outside on line with the 50 other customers in brisk feb air) Arti post-club on a sat nite/sun morning. My friend ranted and raved abt this spot so of course we checked it out. I figured from the line alone that this pizza, must 1. much like myself be thebomb.com OR 2. everyone had just finished getting high and this was their savior from the munchies ....after tasting both the artichoke and the Margarita pizza which i must say was pretty good. So i took a wild guess and decided option 2 was highly unlikely. -1 for the very rude/aloof staff. Anotha -1 for the lack of organization of it all which lead to hostile patrons and line skipping/yelling/pushing :/ that being said "i'll be back"
This is the best Mexican restaurant in Brooklyn.

Priced to titillate those accustomed to pricier neighborhood French restaurants, don't be fooled. Â This restaurant is not French. Â The leaden Gougere are a dead giveaway. Â And sadly using "Specials" to sell fish about to go bad is French, but not Senegalese.

I've been to many tapas places in NY, but this one has been one of the best so far.. Really nice tapas, good service, clean, friendly ambiance. Â The white wine sangria with berries was interesting, although I would have liked more fruit in it. Really liked the jamon serrano, gambas, croquetas de jamon and calamares fritos. Â Thought the patatas bravas could use a bit more of alioli, but otherwise, were pretty tasty. Â All in all, I would definitely go back.

Wonderful atmosphere, stellar service, well priced wine list and very good food. Â  Both of us would go back and try it again-usually one trip to a restaurant is more than enough. Pig's head-great chicken for 2-very good

My experience here was great from beginning to end. First of all, we were told the wait would be 2 hrs but were actually seated in 30 minutes. I think that was a huge stroke of luck though. A number of people probably gave up and we lucked out. We ordered the pork buns and I got myself the original ramen (don't remember the name) with some extra pork belly. The pork buns were seriously some of the best buns I've ever eaten in my life. The pork belly was tender and flavorful and was served with simply lettuce and mayo. When the ramen came, I was super stoked. The broth was delicious. You can tell that the broth was had no msg but still had TONS of flavor. It was very subtle but still tasty. The noodles were al-dente and the meats were delicious. I think I still like Ramen Dojo better in california but this place definitely comes close.

I was debating what to give Osteria Morini. Â 2 or 3 stars? Â And well, 2 it is because it was essentially a "Meh. I've experienced better" type of meal. Â Reservations were made weeks in advance, and even then, I could only snag a 930pm spot. Â I was really excited about dining here and well when Sifton's review came out last week, I was a bit worried that maybe the place wouldnt live up to the hype -- although I know that Sifton is a bit weird with his reviews. My biggest issue with Osteria Morini was the service. Â It just wasn't very good. Â Our server was fine, but I mean, the order that the stuff came to our table was just all wrong. Â I ordered a soppresata plate with some grilled bread as an appetizer. Â Literally 2 minutes later, my pasta comes. Â And what about the bottle of wine? Â Well it was AWOL for another 10 minutes or so. Â  I mean, timing is just so important when you're out to dinner. Â You want things to come out at the right time. Â I don't want my pasta to come out literally minutes after I order and while I'm still enjoying my appetizer which just came to the table. Oh, and did we get a bread basket? Â Whoops. Â Guess they overlooked that. Â And since our food came out so quickly, it was pointless to even ask for it. As for the pastas. Â Well, my tagliatelle with a ragu antica was good -- it was a pasta with meat sauce. Â It was good but nothing earth-shattering. Â I've had better at Fragole near my apartment in Carroll Gardens and at Paprika in the East Village. Â The GF had the mezzelune pasta which was essentially a ravioli-esque pasta with squash, brown butter, and amaretti. Â To be blunt, it was terrible. Â There must have been too much amaretti/Amaretto because the dish was just way too SWEET. Â There wasn't enough balance and so all you had was this sweet taste -- and as a main, it needed to be more savory. There were a few highlights of the meal though, but really, they just werent enough to make this a special dinner. Â First, my cocktail, which I had gotten at the bar because....I had to wait 30 minutes for my table even with the reservation. Â I forgot what it was called but it had brandy, rum, and a citrus twist to it. Â 14 bucks. Â The bottle of red wine we ordered was called Tre Monti and it was $45 -- it was delicious. Â The side of roasted potatoes was also great. Â And finally, since it was my GF's bday, the dessert, which was an apple tort with ice cream. Â And yes, it did have a candle on it. Overall, I don't think I'd return. Â The place was definitely happening and it was great to people-watch...but the service from the kitchen Â and some of the food was nothing special.

I gotta say, I was very impressed with Snack. Â How did I not know of this place sooner? Â Oh wait...I know. Â 'Cause it blends into Thompson St. so well that unless you know where it is, you can easily walk right by it! Â Spurred by Sam and Russ's reviews, I decided to spice up my lunch routine and grab a takeaway from Snack. Â Quick service, small location, GREAT food. Â I tried the Lamb sandwich which was not only wonderfully flavored and smelled so delicious that I had to prevent myself from just stopping in the middle of Prince St. and start my chomping. Â The only complaint one might have would be that the bread gets quite soggy 'cause of all the lamb juice drippings. Â But hey! Â I'm not complaining!

Great bourbon selection and a really friendly staff made me feel right at home well before my friends arrived or dinner was served. Â I arrived a bit ahead of schedule, to find the whole staff standing by the hostess stand, and I had to ask if they were actually open yet, but they practically cheered for me to come in and take a seat at the bar. I tried a flight of bourbons that included Buffalo trace, a bottle I keep on stand-by, and W.L. Weller, which was new to me, but entirely soothing and delightful. The crew arrived and we had a drink at the bar before getting a booth at the back. Â We weren't starving, so we shared a slew of starters (pork nuggets, bacon, crispy cheddar curds, bologna, BLT, etc.), and threw back a few more, including the Char No. 4 take on the hot toddy, made with apple cider and it was perfect to balance out the frigid January weather.

worth the wait, especially since the ramen is so authentic and you can watch them make it right in front of you if you sit at the bar. tiny place and best if you go in the winter because you walk out of there feeling satisfied, warm and fuzzy!

Veg sushi that's (buzz) lightyears above the rest. Lured by the promise of unique vegetable rolls and a Scoutmob discount, I stopped in on a Friday afternoon. Despite the warm welcome from the staff, I was turned off to discover that rolls are $6.50 and all the more happy I had the 2-for-1 coupon. But when my order of the Spicy Mang and the Shroom rolls came out, the cost of the rolls was immediately understandable by the presentation alone. Each was immaculately composed, a work of art laid out on a white canvas, and freakin' huge! All the more beautiful and decadent in taste, these rolls provide the vegetarian sushi eater with innovative flavors unmatched at your run-of-the-mill sushi bar. There was no way I could finish the large portion (2 rolls x 8 large pieces) + fresh pickled ginger and creamy wasabi. I asked for a box, and the counter guy took my plate to box up himself and even gave me new chopsticks and extra napkins without my asking. Awesome from start to finish. My one critique is that I would love a half-roll option so that I could routinely go and order two different flavor concoctions instead of maxing out on one of the jumbos they're rolling out.
Great Pizza. Â Great Place. Â Love it.

It was a long wait but I went there on Friday night so what can you do... But while waiting, me and friend had a drink at the bar. I had sake martini type that use sake and mix with fresh grape fruit. They had few more but I only tried this and also Japanese Whiskey Yamazak on the rocks!! Little bar area is small but hip with red color wall and decoration on the wall is all sorts of noodle bowls were displayed. I had akamaru and was definitely yummy but the kind of noodle was thin type ramen noodle which is common from kyushyu area or that tonkotsu kind. Even if you take time to finish it , noddle did not go soft. I finished all the soup and got super full after words.. but it was that delish! Great for quick eat in ( if there is no wait.)

We had the lamb in hand pulled noodles in soup, spicy beef and spicy lamb hand pulled noodles. Definitely recommend this place for their hand pulled noodles! The lamb noodle is in a white and milky soup,started out tasting too lamby but it got better as I go and actually had pretty nice flavor. I enjoyed their dry noodles more though because the spicy level was perfect! and there was a good amount of meat, cilantro and bok choy in there.

What else is there to say? Opened in 1936...there's a reason it hasn't closed. Service was surprisingly amazing. Better than I've had in some of the nicest restaurants in NYC. Food is exactly what you would expect and priced accordingly... definitely recommend
