Though I've been a New Yorker for the most of my life, I tend to avoid Hipster joints and most of the time, I just hate those places. They're loud, full of obnoxious and drunk people. But this place has been great for the most part. Seating is generally pretty fast, and the food is great! Still, don't bring your kids along with you.

Outdoor space is romantic and cozy. Indoor space is chic and modern. Relatively cheap prices, but 'ain't no good if the food's no good.' Food was meh. Â We ordered the chicken pad thai - way too sweet, had trouble finishing it. The chicken was cooked well though, but I'm assuming they froze their chicken so that it doesn't get overcooked. The other dish Nuur Kraprow was utterly disappointing - not spicy despite the "chili basil sauce", beef was overcooked to a point that it was inedible. See attached picture that pretty much sums up the dish.

I rave about this place. All the time. Even when I'm stuck out on the West Coast. Actually, if any of my friends are going to visit NYC, they always ask me what the sushi place is that I won't shut up about. And then they come back and they won't stop talking about it. Crap. I better stop talking about it if I don't want the secret to let out. This place is amazing. And you know it's good when it doesn't need its name splashed all around outside. This definitely isn't your 2-for-the-price of 1 or California roll joint. This is quality fish. Fresh and melt-in-your-mouth delicious. I have challenged a number of New Yorkers to find fresher sushi around. It's hard for them to try. The menu is deceptively simple. But like the decor, Sushi Yasuda is all about the no-frills approach. Don't try to hide subpar fish under a dollop of mayonnaise. Instead, the food's clean, fresh, and oh so delectable. Definitely splurge for the sashimi cuts of toro. Sure they may cost $7 per piece or more. But your mouth will be thanking you. Oh, and their negihama roll is amazing. Who knew that yellowtail and scallion could be so buttery? Even their cooked dishes are to die for. Their spider crab appetizer was seasoned to perfection, and their fillets of sea bass were cooked just right. My mom and I ordered two plates of that. Sure, their prices aren't cheap. But do you really want cheap sushi? Fish that may be a day or two old? No thanks. My mom and I consistently spend $100+ for dinner b/w the two of us. But even though I'm little, I can eat. Especially when it comes to sushi. But for those who are a little less willing to dole out the cash, they have good prix-fixe meals for lunch and dinner. I think it was 3 rolls + miso soup for $20. Not bad at all. Whenever I'm back in New York, this is the place to hit up.

This place has a wonderful ambiance, which makes up for the limited brunch menu and poor ice coffee. Â Asolutley amazing service, with very polite and attentive wait staff and amazing food. Â Try the cinnamon rolls, you won't regret it. The ambiance reminds you of your dad's study. Â I love it. Â Will definitely be back.
I come here for quick lunch or slow afternoon tea. The wait on the line is short and i can stay as long as i want its just a very convenient place, not to mention their food is great and fresh!

One word... AMAZING! Came here on a busy Saturday night and this place really exceeded my expectations. We came in with a groupon, there was a 20 minute wait the place was packed but the wait went by pretty quickly. We were seated (very small space and tables are close together) and our waitress Lauren came over to introduce herself. She took our groupon with no problems, and in addition to the groupon which included any 2 entrees, drinks and desert we got the Tuna tartare... The Tuna Tartare was one of the best I've ever had! It was covered in guacamole and had a base of beets... This combination was perfect and seasoned to perfection. For our entrees we I got the grilled tuna steak and my boyfriend got the lamb shank. The meal was exceptional and his lamb shank was so tender I didn't even have to try to put my fork in it, it just fell apart. For desert I had a warm brownie and my boyfriend got the tiramisu. The brownie was ok and the tiramisu was very good! Over all service and the food were A+ the server was so attentive and the cooks here really put passion into the food! I will definitely be back! Check this place out guys!

We have been to Chinatown restaurants many times before but never to this spot. It was a real experience--before you sit down they bring you glasses of hot tea and dealing with the waitress was also an experience--she told me I would not like a certain dish and generally she waited on us with a rather blase attitude. We had platters of chicken chow fun (which was not on the menu, only beef chow fun) and a lighly breaded fish with string beans and ordered an appetizer of what we thought was going to be a stuffed crepe, but was actually 3 vegetable rolls (which came after the entrees were served)--it was dirt cheap even though they added $1.50 because I wanted chicken instead of beef and gravy with the dish--still the meal was less than $20 for 2 persons. The food was tasty and very filling and we enjoyed it. The mistake was using the downstairs restrooms--we have been in some bad ones in Chinatown (and also in China), but these rank up there in the category of FILTHY restrooms!!

This is no doubt one of my favorite spots in the boroughs. The hipster old school steakhouse vibe is spot on. The service is great and the food is even better. And more importantly, the cocktails are proper. Some of my favorites are: The Lobster Club - it's bang'n. The Burger is one of the best in town. Period. The Butcher Steak is perfect. We make the trip from Central Harlem to this spot regularly.
cosy romantic spot for drinks inside and outside. nice to gather some friends out. that's it. the food here is a joke, the pizzas are bland and too pricey, definitely not worth it...

Vanessa's Dumpling House. Â This is probably the cheapest place you could get breakfast in New York and it's totally worth it too. Â I spent no more than $6 for breakfast and that's unheard of in New York. Â It's your typical Asian service where they don't really care for you to be there, which I absolutely love. Â It reminds me when I'm at my parents place. I had the following items: 1) Chive & Pork Fried Dumplings (#1) - This was pretty damn good. Â For $1, you get 4 dumplings. Â It has a good amount of flavor and not greasy. Â The burn parts add a crispiness to the dumplings and well worth the whole dollar I spent. Â Watch out. Â Baaallin! 2) Wonton w/ Spicy Sauce (#8) - For $4.50, you get 8 wontons. Â It comes with cilantro and green onions. Â I thought this was very flavorful, light, and spicy as hell. Â It's definitely a must try and way better than Din Tai Fung's wontons with spicy sauce. Â This had a major kick to it. Â I was literally sweating as I ate this. Â It was pretty embarrassing cause there was a cute girl sitting two seats over from me. Â I was trying to play it cool. Â However, I couldn't stop sweating so I went to buy a soda and grab some napkins to wipe my sweat. Â I ended up finishing the soda then buying another one cause was still sweating! Overall, I'm definitely coming back to Vanessa's the next time I'm in NYC and it's on my NYC must stop spots along with the Halal Guys, Prince St. Pizza and Totto Ramen. Â Lastly, they treat me like my parents as in they don't care if I'm there or not.

I could die fat and happy in Taverna Kyclades. The food is amazing, the portions big (great for groups and sharing), and the prices reasonable. The serves complimentary bread. Get the peasant salad to start and probably anything else. Haven't been dissappointed once. There wine is cheap and you can tell.but I dont really come.for.the wine. The food.steals.the show.

4 stars because it was CHEAP! The dinner set was $10 or $12? 3 course meals... where else can you find cheap food like that in the city? and actually taste GOOD!! Decor was cute, very cozy, and during the summertime, they'd open the windows, so it becomes sorta an outdoor place, but not really- more like you see the buses, cars and people walk by and breathe in the polluted air. Staff were helpful, but one note though, if you are really hungry and want a lot of food, then don't do the 3 courses, they don't give you a lot of portion, probably that is how they can keep their costs so low... but definitely a great place to go to for an early dinner!

Honestly impressed! Considered going to Chipotle but always walk by here on my way to work and it smells great and looks popular. Glad I decided to try it! I got the brisket with yellow rice, black beans, corn, squash and guac. Super flavorful! I'm impressed with how good the meat is - it really has a great smoky flavor. I was excited for the squash but thought the corn and guac were better (guac is better than chipotle's). You can get all 3 for less than chipotle charges for guac alone so I suggest going for it. Service was friendly and great!

For $4.50 a slice, the Artichoke Pizza here has a high probability of being the best pizza I've ever eaten. I'm going to give it one more taste (probably soon since I crave it already and I only had it yesterday), and if it still is, I'll up my rating to 5. To give your tastebuds a fairly accurate description of what the Artichoke Pizza tastes likes, its basically the perfect mix of Creamy, Spinach Artichoke Dip and Cheesy, Warm Pizza with a just-crisp crust... mmm. Artichoke usually also have a few other pizza choices available. I'm sure they are good too, though unless I order 2 slices (not likely given how filling one is) I don't see myself having the will power to order anything but the amazingness that is Artichoke Pizza from Artichoke Pizza. Like many wonderful places in the east village: cash only, little to no seating, potential for a long wait (esp. post drinking hours), worth it.
Really loved this place. The fish was so delicious and amazing flavors. Little pricey but worth it.
kind of cramped but there is a reason it is so busy. fantastic pizza that is fresh and not overly seasoned. the brooklyn pilsner was good too and complimented the pizza.

I've been going to Tia Pol for years - is my go-to spot. Â Everything from the patatas bravas (best I've had since I was last in Spain) to the squid cooked in its own ink, to the pork loin sandwiches are fabulous. Â I honestly think I've eaten everything on the menu at least once. Â  You'll always experience a wait on the weekends - but it passes by quickly with a glass of sangria and great company!
Great sandwiches. We do take out a few times from here. You to downstairs to order takeout. Upstairs is a bar and a more traditional sit down area. The service is quick and friendly.
This is a great little restaurant with a warm atmosphere. We were lucky enough to arrive during a coffee ceremony, so we enjoyed complementary bunna with our sampler plate.

Love Market Table. Great seasonal menu and consistently good food. We live in the neighborhood and this is our go to place if we want a nice evening out and a delicious meal. It is a bit pricey (so not our go to every night) but totally worth it when you want a solid west village dinner experience. The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, and we've never had an issue with our reservation or the staff.

What a delightful surprise! Â We stopped in for lunch because if the huge open doors allowing us to sit inside while feeling we were sitting outside. Â But the good was exceptional. Â He had the bratwurst, which was so good he never dipped into the brown mustard. Â My red cabbage salad with apples & walnuts & a lingonberry dressing was perfect & very refreshing. Â Our drinks were great, too: Â I had Katja's Tequila Daisy, with elderflower. Â Delicious! Â He had the Stiegl lager. Â Excellent! Â Then we finished with the buckwheat-almond cake with plum compote mit schlag. Â To die for! Â We love our new discovery, & will be back soon for sure, & bring friends. Â Yummy!!!!

One of my favorite low key Lunch/Dinner spots in SoHo. Very small hole in the wall Australian cafe on Mulberry. Â Everything i've had here has been really really good, it's quite surprising actually! Considering i've never been to an "Australian" cafe or restaurant before. The two things I always get here are either the Bronte Burger or the Shrimp Pasta. Â Both really really good, just depends if you're in the mood for a Burger or a Pasta. Â  The burger is not like an American style burger, it's more like a sandwich but it's delicious. Service is always super super friendly in their, and they deliver in the area as well! Highly recommended.

This place is great! Â I love the idea of bring Cali burritos to New York, because I was having the same dilemma before I found this place! THE GUAC IS SO GOOD. Â And I simply can't eat Mexican food unless its slathered in primo guacamole. Â And the cheese is melted on the tortilla before the other ingredients for a warm melted stretchy cheese effect. Â MMMMMMMM. The medium spicy sauce actually has spice, unlike every other place, where medium tastes like nothing! Â I had the pork, which was a little dry- I want to try the carne asada next time. Â  BUT MY FAVORITE THING is that they put the sour cream on from a squeeze bottle! Â I find large amounts of sour cream sickening but I still like a little bit of the flavor- so this is perfect! Â I always ask Chipotle for a "little" sour cream but they always always glob on a whole bunch! Â Yuck! I'd say the place is pretty equal to Chipotle, with some better and some worse.

Trendy, small, cozy, and delicious. This place is a little on the pricy side of things. Â People who enjoy this place, value quality over quantity. Â The ingredients are locally grown, organic, and sustainable. Â The menu is different everyday. Â Put together by the chef after a visit to the market. Â So what you get depends upon what is fresh today... literally! Anthony Bourdain filmed part of an episode of his wildly popular No Reservations show here. Â Tony praised it and ultimately questioned why he hadn't known about the great food culture of Brooklyn until now. Â Asking: "Is it too late for me?" Fun Facts: Rumor has it that the burger, which isn't on the menu, is to die for. Â Though I've never tried it and cannot confirm its existence. This is a great date spot. I've rubbed elbows with celebs here (no names thats just tacky). Â Nobody too famous, but still kind of fun when you're out to dinner.

In many ways this is like getting prison food. You stand in a long line waiting to get your tray, you point at the food you like to have and they through it directly on the tray - you pay by the weight. BUT - the food is great. We had the pulled pork shoulder, brisket and sirloin and this was some of the best BBQ I've had. You then find a vacant spot at one of the long tables and pour various BBQ sauces over the meat and you share this. Great concept, very low key, good beer and cool decor. Remember to wear clothes for outdoor as you will spend the majority of your time waiting in line outside. But it's worth the wait. The line is a bit annoying especially that once you bought the food you will have to do a new line for the beer.

This place is really good. Went there for brunch Sunday afternoon and had the Croque-Madame and it was really good really good flavors. The salad with it was good and the orange juice was fresh-squeezed. Â I couldn't resist having the poached pears crepe with home made chocolate sauce and cream for desert and it was good. I recommend this one.
I love this place. Â Fantastic sandwiches and I love all the samples in the market area of the place.

I just had my husband's 50th birthday party on Saturday. Â The food was terrific, the service was wonderful. Â Great place for a party and reasonable. Â Very well organized. Â Great parking also. Â This is my new location for my parties. Â I would recommend dinner or a party.

I went here with my friend who lives up the street and loves the place. Â The three of us were crowded onto a tiny table, which was awkward, but understandable seeing how the place was pretty packed. Â I got the obligatory corn which was pretty good, and roast pork which was tasty but a small portion. Â What I really liked was the guava margarita, yum. Â The wait staff was friendly and accommodating.

Unfortunately the fried chicken is hit-or-miss. Â Sometimes it's fresh from the fryer with firm meat and crispy skin, other times the meat's gone dry and the skin is sagging like it's been under a lamp for hours. Â I guess I was lucky the first few times I came here, but not anymore. Â There's no rhyme or reason to it either; Â it can be busy or empty, morning or night and you'd still could get either outcome. Â The credit card machine also mysteriously malfunctions on occasion. Â The waffles are still awesome and service is excellent, but the last thing I want to experience, especially in these tumultuous times, is volatile fried chicken.
I am obsessed. Link sausage is the best. Cider beer and a vast plethora of bourbon makes me feel warm and fuzzy inside.
great burgers

the husband and i decided to have a friday date night at the bounty. and we're so glad we chose this place. the ambiance - we loved the steady and relaxed vibe. the bar looked awesome and it wasn't too packed which was perfect. the service - friendly people. excellent service. the food - we got the oysters to start which were fresh and yummy. we both ordered the burger which was actually one of the best i've had in nyc. such a great surprise. so juicy and tasty. it went perfectly with the toasted brioche it was in. even the fries that went with the burger were excellent, crisp and well seasoned. we will definitely go back even just for that burger. oh and the dark and stormy was excellent too!

To be quite honest, I was planning to eat at Smith & Wollensky tonight. Â I went to S&M and find out that the waiting time will be somewhere around 35min so I decided to leave and settle with a restaurant near by. Â Now, I believe that this was fate. Â Everything happens for a reason. Â I'd have to say...WOW! Â This place is delicious!!!! Â Thanks to Smith & Wollensky for not having the table open for me when I arrived. I ordered the caprese salad and it was good. Â This was a ordinary good caprese salad. Â Then came the pasta dish (fettuccine w/chicken, mushrooms, oil, and garlic sause) that I ordered!! Â OMG, it was love in first sight and bite. Â The pasta was al-dente and with the sause it sucked in, it created a flavor that took my mind to heaven (my brain was going under the process of Big-Bang.) Â The atomosphere of this restaurant was like an at-home trattoria you'll find in the Tuscan area of Italy which made my heart relax and enjoy the food even more. Â Oh yeah, and the best part is...for NYC, the price is very sincere. Â Delicious food with a reasonable price. Â What else do you need? The only reason I didn't give this place a 5-star was because the service was sloppy and kinda slow. Â Still even with that aspect, I will still be coming back here again and again. Â Yay for this restaurant's location being near my school too :)

I nearly cried with joy when I first went here. Memories of Singapore came full on. Â Singapore Laksa (alas minus the cockles) is the real deal. Tears of joy! Char Kway Teow mnnnnn...... I have absolutely no other reason to go to Elmhurst but this place. And for it, I am willing to sit many many minutes on the subway to get a chance to eat here.

Thanks to the Yelp app and a search for "craft beer" near our current location (a little ways beyond Rockafellar Center), we came upon The Three Monkeys. I was initially a little turned off by the blow up football players outside (anticipating a sports bar) but once we walked in I was immediately a fan. Exposed brick, tasteful holiday decor and dim yet nice lighting is what we found inside. We took seats at the bar and were immediately impressed by the beer selection. I settled on the Goose Island Christmas and my boyfriend was psyched to see they had Stone's "Drink By" on draft. Unfortunately the keg was kicked about 2 ounces after the bartender started to fill his glass -- he was bummed but they were super apologetic. He went with an Old Speckled Hen on draft instead. We enjoyed our drinks without feeling urged to order another round. I made a visit to the ladies room and it was quite clean which was a bonus. The 2 beers weren't cheap but by what we had experienced in NYC at that point, they were right around average. I definitely recommend, it was enough off the beaten path to avoid that tourist trap feel yet convenient enough to the sights and to the subway to head uptown.
My life has changed. I ordered for delivery last night and it was So. Good. Will be ordering from here again ( many times) in the near future.

Dinner here was somewhat torpedoed by news of Steve Jobs' death. Consoled by melt-in-your-mouth, (tear-salt) chirashi, a double-scoop of uni, and the empathetic eyes of distant diners in the sparse, simple, cherry-wood dining area, I hoped silently that his rendition of heaven was as softly spectacular, and as quietly perfect.
The best!

Nothing fancy and served buffet style, this place is quick, reasonable and authentic Cuban. I loved the pork, and the fried plaintains were among the best I've had. There were plenty of buffet options, and meats that exceeded the stereotypical Cuban fare.

What good food, and what great service! I came here with a friend and wanted to order this noodle dish-- sorry, I forget the name, it was like a different language or something ;) -- but I was hoping it wouldn't be too spicy, because I can't abide spicy. The waiter assured me it was very mild. Well, it came, and it was burning hot! So I said, "I hate to be a pill, but can I have something else? This tastes like burning!" And they were super nice and apologized and brought me another dish, which was not spicy and very tasty. I left a very satisfied customer.

Came here for brunch on a Saturday at 11:30am - we came early since it seems like this restaurant gets pretty crowded. When we got here there was no wait and we were seated immediately. There also didn't seem to be too much of a wait when we left around 12:30 either. We didn't get anything to drink, but I did get a grapefruit juice that seemed to be freshly squeezed, which is nice. For food, we got the: oysters - they seemed to be relatively fresh but tasted like most other oysters I get pancakes - they were different than pancakes you normally get since they're made of buckwheat, but they tasted really good and fluffy poached eggs with salmon - tasted alright although we didn't expect the salmon to be cooked
Well worth the wait to sit at the bar (the best place to sit in my opinion). You can't go wrong with the black label burger or better yet, the Cote de Boeuf.
Never tried Serbian food before, so I decided it would be a good time to start. So good. Tons of flavor, great menu variety, and a lot of good meat. Delicious meat.

I never was a big fan of falafel before. Come to think of it, I am actually not sure if I have even ate a falafel before this past year.... Well, if I did, it was definitely not memorable. I've tried falafel at a bunch of places in NYC and this place has the best value proposition. It is under $3 for a FANTASTIC falafel sandwich. They give it to you piping hot. The falafel is warm and deliciously spiced. The pita is filled with lots of tahini and veggies, but the best part has got to be their hot sauce. The first time I came here I didn't realize how spicy the hot sauce was, and of course, I use hot sauce like none other and doused the whole thing with sauce. I was literally tearing up, panting, and trying my best to maintain composure as I still consumed the whole thing. I think the people at the next time got a kick out of watching me suffer. But it was SO yummy and I'd put just as much hot sauce again. There's always long lines at night, but there's pretty quick turnaround and REALLY worth it! LOVE MAMOUN'S! If I didn't crave falafel before, I now crave it ALL THE TIME.

the tori karage gave me a little stomachache, but maybe its becuase ive been eating popeyes for a long time, and my weak american stomach cant handle good fried chicken. DAMN YOU AMERICAN BELLY! the fluke carpaccio and fried persimmon were pretty amazing. especially the persimmon with plum miso paste. i do regret not getting the nabe, but maybe nexttime. also i had shochu instead of sake, because i perfer shochu. no offense, but maybe nexttime. theres nothing else that hasnt been said about this little gem in the corporate building (and no its not enron or merrill lynch).

I went out with an old friend on a Monday night, coincidentally while the Emmys were on, which I think we're the only reasons that the place was so empty. The servers gave us their full attention, giving great recommendations for food and drink. We celebrated our last hurrah before Labor Day with a ton of Rose and Blue Point Oysters. Get the seasonal heirloom tomatoes with edamame. So simple, and out of this world. I had the applewood smoked pickled muscles and toast for my entree. A very different way to try one of my favorite seafoods with a totally different flavor. After we left, I forgot my brand new sunglasses on the table and the younger waiter who I think was new chased me down the block to give them back. So sweet!
Extremely good pizza, probably the best in NYC, but outrageously expensive and difficult to get a table. Therefore, not somewhere I can frequent.

Came here for lunch on a Saturday. Â I don't have a baseline for this type of cuisine but I thought it was pretty darn authentic. Â I got the pork feet with chickpeas, one of the all day specials, not the smaller lunch special. The pork feet was soft, melt in your mouth nommmness. Â A side of yellow rice and pinto beans (comes with the special with options for the type of rice and beans that you want) helped get through the heavy meaty-ness of the dish. Â Would definitely come back to try other dishes! They had good indoors and outdoors with tables out on the sidewalks and in the alcove outside of the restaurant. Â Very quaint.

I had the fried chicken with rice & peas. Â  Great. Rice was fresh & they injected seasoning in the meat before they cooked it, resulting in a flavorful spicy chicken. Â  The jerk chicken is also great too
Your incredible falafal. I like that the staff is sometimes grumpy and impatient. It helps keep me in check. None of that matters. Your falafal...it rules.

Marietta is my go to restaurant now when there is a nice occasion. The food is so decadent and refined. My favorite is the chicken dishes, and my roommate's favorite is the salmon. For breakfast, the benedicts are amazing!

The best thing about ABC Kitchen is there are always new things on the menu that are exciting to try yet the best things always stay like the crab toast and pizzas. Food to get: -Crab Toast with Lemon Aioli (or the squash toast special if available) -Sugar Snap Pea Salad with Parmesan Dressing and Herbs -Whole Wheat Pizza: Jersey Tomatoes. Buffalo Mozzarella and Basil -Sundae: Salted Caramel Ice Cream, Candied Peanuts & Popcorn, Chocolate Sauce see pictures here: chekmarkeats.com/2011/07â€¦ Jean-George's newest local and sustainable restaurant has beautiful floral, mis-matched china and lighting that makes the room sparkle. The seasonal/rotating menu offers all kinds of unique vegetables, and the seafood is dressed in homemade sauces such as: blood-orange, lemon and carrot. Pizza has a legit, zesty tomato sauce and soft, yet crunchy pizza crust (which was consulted by Jim Lahey of Sullivan St. Bakery/ Co.). ABC gives you fancy and creative food in a hip, relaxed atmosphere suitable for "cool cats" and "oldies." Winner of the 2011 James Beard Award for "Best New Restaurant."

I went there for the first time this past Monday. Loved it. Everything from the look and feel of the place to the people who worked there. I felt like I left there having made new friends. I met Zoe who was our server and just excellent in everyway. Not to mention all the other ladies who were working that night. We sat at the Chefs counter and Chris the chef that night was super sweet, and helpful and generous. Â Lets see we ate alot. I highly recommend the Squash Salad, the Mac n Cheese, the Cauliflower and the Lamb Meatballs. We also had the pudding which I didn't need, but had no problem consuming. The music was amazing too. They were playing some throwbacks and I was tempted to return for dinner the next day. I can't wait to go back. I get why people have recommended this place to me so many times.

Definitely come here for brunch over dinner. I think the food is better and the atmosphere caters to a better brunch crowd. Extra Virgin is a cute, tucked away West Village spot with prime, outdoor sidewalk seating. The interior offers two different looks - turquoise walls and wooden paneling in one room and exposed red brick and mirrors in the other. Â The food and young crowd parallel each other creating a fun and "that's exactly what I wanted" kind of experience. Food: (for pictures of the food and scene go to my blog listed on my profile) 1. Pancakes are just as fluffy and delicious as they should be -no fancy flavored butter or overdone sauces. They offer a pancake as a side which is great if you dont want a whole short stack and also want to order eggs. 2. Eggs and omeletts are done right. Omelette of the day is always good and the frittata with basil and pesto is a nice treat! If you come here with only one other person it will be easier to get a table. They dont take reservations for brunch, but they do for dinner.

I'm in fries heaven! These little fritters are good on their own, but the different sauces add a delightful taste!!! My favorites so far have been the mango chutney and parmesan peppercorn. Poutine = Canadian delicacy of mashed down french fries with tons of gooey cheese and brown gravy. Kinda like a slightly crunchy version of mashed potatoes! YUMMY!!!
Delicious food, baby friendly, outdoor seating, live music, free tarot readings, sangria!, friendly staff... I can't complain about this place!

Bubby's Tribeca has had a fair amount of fuss made about it. It's even featured in the film adaptation of Devil Wears Prada. It seems to be like one of those really hot bands that everyone knows and likes but it's difficult to hear what everyone else is hearing. The food is rich and heavy regardless of what you order from burgers to salads to desserts. Sometimes "heavy" is exactly what you're in the mood for but variety is also appealing. It's a fairly "family oriented" diner so those with kids will feel at home. Crayons are provided for extra fun/ mess. When I feel like lashing out, I go for their meatloaf which comes with gravy, deep fried onions (which they term as "caramelized" for some reason) and 2 side dishes of your choice. No chance for dessert in this scenario but they do an awesome hot chocolate...which is, you guessed it, also heavy and rich. The decor is basic colonial/ country. The service is craptacular. The staff appear to be far more interested in hanging out at the bar with each other, chatting, laughing, joking around, rather than clearing tables. Downstairs near the bathrooms there's one of those old black & white photo booths (which I love). Not worth a trip there for the booth alone but a bit of a draw card. *Bubby's was hit with no less than 12 violations of the health code 2 weeks ago including "Rats in the food preparation area". Yum!

Took the family to Union square area to enjoy the nice weather this weekend and happen to stumble into this gem for opening day! The decor and ambiance is unheard of for a fast food restaurant - simple... clean... relaxing! Food was delicious++ we had Kebob Laffa, Veggie pita and Shawarma pita - best pita sandwiches we had in NYC so far. We shared a French toast pita sandwich for dessert... out of this world!!! -- Toasted pita bread, covered with Silan (which is "date honey" - beats maple syrup) loaded with fresh berries and vanilla ice-cream.... yum..um..mm! We'll be back for more...
Their classic Bahn Mi is really good and one of the best values in the west village for only 5 bucks. Super excited to try out their Pho as it gets colder outside.

I am a fan of the ramen, I am not a fan of the waitress who IMMEDIATELY asked me for my order as soon as I sat down. Â I had the extra spicy ramen with pork. Â My boyfriend had the extra spicy ramen with chicken. Â The pork was better, the chicken was dry. Â We added scallions and bamboo shoots, but I wished I added the poached egg! We asked for a table of 6, and given it is a small space, we accepted that they squeezed us in a table of 4. Â AS SOON AS WE SAT DOWN & GOT THE MENU (not exaggerating) the waitress came with her notepad and said "give me your order". Â I told her we just sat down, we didn't even open the menu yet.
