This place is amazing! My favorite dish was the hamburgers. They're the most flavorful burgers I've ever gotten. We actually had almost everything in the menu, and it was all excellent.

My previous experience with Peruvian food is the mom and pop fast food type places, and I must say the chicken is the bomb. Â  This is the nicest Peruvian Restaruant I have been to. Â Initially the cool design on the place gets you excited, but once you sit down the opinion changes. Â Our servers sucked! Â He was not very helpful in informing us how the menu worked as a lot of it was in Spanish. Â Had two of the people in my party not spoken Spanish it would have been even worse. The food is no better than the cheaper mom and pop Peruvian places, so your paying for the ambiance and the experience. Â If you have never tried Peruvian food and want a hip type of restaurant than this place would work. Â However, Â know that the servers are not the best around

Picked up food from here for dinner. Â Now i gotta say. Â Their burritos were REALLY Â good. Â My buddy had some spinach/feta cheese amalgamation and i had a more traditional chicken burrito with everything and hot sauce. Â  Definitely a win for having packets of Cholula sauce! Ok so i got home and unwrapped this heavy Burrito and immediately the first thing i think about is comparing it to the known standard of Chipotle. Â Why? Â B/c I've had way more Chipotle and that has become my standard to measure Burrito box against. Â And i have to say...Burrito box blows it out of the water! Â This place KILLS it! Â The meat, the cheese, the rice and beans and everything was just so fresh and had such a great flavor. Â  One can argue - "Rich - both places have fresh food how can burrito box be better?" I'll tell you. Â Not just fresh - but the way they season everything. Â It's just that good. Â I honestly don't know what they do in the back where the food is prepared but whatever they do...KEEP DOING IT!! Â It's good - it's cheap - it's got my thumbs up! TL;DR - Tasty Burritos - better than Chipotle - since Chipotle is the "benchmark" as it is neither great nor terrible.

Even Â restaurant Â looks like cozy for me . Food was insane to me delicious . Music also add charm and good vibes around it .MO MO was perfectly cook reminds me back to kathmandu . Other several dish I try also Â perfect .price was reasonable if visit again NY then I will go for it .

I like Phillip and his staff who keep this place at the top of our list when we eat out. They are always so fun. It doesn't hurt that the food is really original and super good. Since the place opened it's been steadily progressing to greater heights. Really impressive. It's sushi, but the salads are good... And it's meat but there are a lot of vegan options. You really can't go wrong here. They even have a Michelin recommendation, so clearly I'm not alone in thinking they rock.

I love Lot 2; it is by far my favorite Brooklyn restaurant. Â All of their dishes are great and usually are made with seasonal ingredients. Â All of those good reviews are spot on - Yes the chicken is amazing, Yes the burgers are the best in Brooklyn, Yes the cocktails and desserts are great. Â If you're lucky Teddy will be your waitress. Â  Sometimes you will have to sit next to someone who brought their brat kid with them.

I'm slowly working my way through Yuca in phases. My first trip to Yuca I did what any normal patron does: Took advantage of their happy hour until I was wasties. Done. Now I can say I've finally had their brunch after my boo, Kristina, suggested we meet there for Sunday morning worship*. And holy cow, I finally have a reason to live!** Their prix-fix brunch is $13.95 and includes either a mimosa, bloody mary, or screwdriver, and coffee or orange juice. Phew. I'm getting so tired of these places that make you choose between alcohol or coffee. Why can't I have both? I NEED both!*** I decided to pay an extra $1 for the Crab Cake Benedictos. To describe this brunch without coming off as overly sentimental and saccharine would be impossible. Suffice to say, I shoved this meal into my mouth with the same ferocity a child digs for dinosaurs in the backyard. I was determined. As much as I love rice and black beans, the hash browns are too good to pass up. They were phenomenal, with just the right amount of seasoning and spice. The only thing keeping this from 5 stars was the service. A tad on the slow side, and a bit negligent at times. Luckily we weren't in a rush, this being the day of rest and gluttony and all. One day I'll make it here for dinner to complete my Yuca tour. Stay tuned. __________ * Why worship something intangible when you can worship something tangible like brunch? I feel the power all right. In my gut. ** A tasteless joke. But seriously, hasn't this summer just been one long funeral? *** First World Problems.
wasn't a fan of their fries, but i loved their short rib burger. it was DELICIOUS!

Avoid going busy hours like Lunch time or after 5PM. I went around 3PM but still there was a long line. After waited for 45 minutes, I was in but I joined another people waiting in line. It was 4:30PM on Friday. Macaron is Â $2.70 each. What enjoyed the most was Rose Petal, white creaminess texture and popping scent of Rose after...it was interesting. Loved the layers of lady like experiences. Ames, The Bachelor poet, stopped in but having many sparkling eyes from girls around on him that he left after few minutes. I find him cute.

Came here to celebrate my 1 year wedding anniversary and I could not think of a more delicious restaurant to go to. The prices were decent for all the pallet tingling foods they had to offer. We went for the Prefix menu: Vellutata Â - this was amazing, the soup was sweet and the lobster was crisp, sweet and fresh. Crudo di Passera - Fluke was very fresh, the caviar and the lemon really did the job. Trofie Nero - squid ink pasta with scallops - was so delicious, my first time eating squid ink pasta and it was very flavorful. Spaghetti - had bits of crab and was such a nice spin on the normal spaghetti you would think of eating. Tagliata - Cooked to perfection - meet was very tasty and moist. Astice - Lobster again was amazing - so tasty, sweet and fresh. Crostata di Cioccolato - Amazing, I a huge dark chocolate fan - so this dessert was up my alley - they also make homemade pear sorbet that was to die for. I wish I was able to buy a tub of the pear sorbet. Torta di Olio - This was very delicious as well. But I still have favoritism with the pear sorbet Not only was he food delicious but the service was superb. I would love to go again for another special occasion. I cant wait. =) One more thing - they change there menu every season, so one can only hope to go here at least 4 times in one year.

Great value and really good food. Â Quick and attentive service, Arab music and decor just completes the place, no complaints whatsoever. Â My date and I shared the platter with 5 different salads and got a couple of extra pitas. Â Filled us both up for $15 tip and tax all included. Â Beet salad was perfect, chickpea & spinach salad was solid, hummus and labneh better than most places, grapes leaves were good. Â Pita is the star here!!
Been coming here for 8 years. It never disappoints.

Another spot on my "food bucket list" that did not disappoint. My friend and I met here at 5 on a Friday hoping to dodge the notorious crowd we had read about. Good thing we came when we did because when we left around 7 a wait was forming. First things first - the kitchen doesn't technically open until 5 but you can order chips and guac, which is pretty darn good guac. We each got the watermelon margarita, which was good but honestly a little heavy on the tequila - I've had better. Now for the main course - get the enchiladas verdes. Absolutely phenomenal, and I don't understand the reviews that say the portions here are small - this plate is huge, so if you're hungry, I highly recommend it. The taco plates were smaller (three each), so if you're looking for something lighter, my friend got the steak tacos and enjoyed them. But, back to the enchiladas! The sauce...MMMMMM. Highlight of the dish for me. Will definitely be back!

Great atmosphere. Service was friendly and polite, albeit slow; took 10 minutes before we received our coffee and beers. My burger was cooked exactly as I ordered it - medium rare - so I was surprised at how dry it was.

Yuca Bar is the quintessential hung over breakfast spot... Nice open seating area that looks out onto the street across from Thompson Square Park. Â Great pre-set menu for brunch on the weekends with your choice of breakfast+coffee+alcohol (mimosa, strong screwdriver or bloody) Definitely try the quevos rancheros, sooooo good! Â If you don't feel like breakfast, the burger with yucca fries is also quite good. Overall an awesome spot to know about and with great Latin paintings on the wall.

3.5 stars upgraded I'm baffled by the unending 5-star praise this cart gets. It's good, but not *that* good, damn!!! For instance, the super secret special white sauce is like a cross between ranch & yogurt or sour cream... And the falafel could've stood to be fresher/less hard. But... The combination of rice, lettuce, that white sauce, super-duper-make-you-sweat hot sauce & falafel was pretty effin' tasty at 2:45 in the morning. BFF & various members of our *ahem* crew visited the cart 2-3 times during our stay. The lines are long, the food is cheap ($6 for my rice combo), but it isn't quality. Tastes better the drunker you are!
chicken pot pie goodness!

I've been meaning to go to this place for half a year now and I'm so glad it was worth the while! I didn't get the tasting menu because it's all about the steak baby! How can you not get the steak when it's next to and tied with a butcher's shop?? We ordered the yuzu and mint drink - not only do they serve amazing food, but the drinks are delicious as well. We started wit the sashimi. Just kissed by fire, added with a bit of salt and wasabi and I was in heaven. My boyfriend had to get the mac and cheese and beef burger sliders. Even though that was not on my list (yes, I've been waiting to come here so long I made a list), these two are a definite must get! The mac and cheese comes with 2 piece of toasted bread that, weirdly enough, was one of the best pieces of bread I've ever had in my life. Although it was cheesy, the dish was not heavy and the mac was cooked just right. The burgers were so juicy, I was literally slurping the juices every time I took a bite. Need I say more? We also ordered the foie gras soba and steak aside, this was my ultimate favorite dish of the night. I'm so glad I read yelp reviews and ordered this because it was SO.GOOD. The noodles were the best soba I've had in NYC and the broth was light. Such a simple dish but when done right, it is truly out of this world. And finally...the beef. We ordered the 11 oz. of coulette steak that came with roasted potatoes and garlic. All I can say is, WOW. I've had better in Japan, but it's not every day I go to Japan and this was one of the best steaks I've had in NYC. It was juicy, cooked just right and flavorful. I had one of the best food moments in my life eating that dish. And what would be a great meal without dessert? I ordered the sake panecotta and my boyfriend ordered the Ugandan vanilla bean and berry with oatmeal clusters. The panecotta was delicious and silky and light but I like my desserts heavier so I ended up eating my dessert and stealing my boyfriend's. HAHA

Came for brunch on saturday, and for dinner a few months ago, the food was good. However when we came for dinner we sat at the bar and the service was fine, a little slow but alright. This weekend the waiter seemed to have an attitude. The people sitting next to us agreeed. I ordered an ice coffee and he took a good twenty min to bring it to the table, than when I asked for milk, he basically snapped at me. As cool as the atmosphere of this place is, the food is only okay and not worth the rude service.

dont know what happened to this place i just came from there i used to go there for years Â their broth Â used to bve so tasty , today perfect weather for soup so i ordered my usual and well was almost disappointed the broth was bland Â , luckily the duck wasnt , i hope this place starts doing what it used to

Another yummy cheap eat in St Marks. Try the bacon sliders, the bacon is in the pattie, it's interesting. Also, squirt on the different sauces at the table. I love the creamy Jalapeno one. I'd say a normal portion is 3 sliders.

this review has been a long time comin'. Xe May is hands down my favorite banh mi in manhattan, or at least that I've tried. It's better quality than places in chinatown, and cheaper than Num Pang (plus bigger sandwiches). I've tried almost everything on the menu and it's all super fresh, delicious, and made-to-order. Their $8 sandwich+drink+snack weekday lunch special is KILLER and their stamp cards are da' bomb (I've gone through at least three, hehe). My personal favorite is the Lam'bretta, unique and so freaking good...try it!

Amazing Mexican food that is always fresh and prepared with fresh ingredients. Priced reasonably for its size and quality. Service is good very attentive at all times. I recommend this restaurant its good food but not really a party or too loud environment if thats what you are looking for. The fish tacos are my favorite and their guacamole is the best I ever had. The Hawaiian quesadilla is another favorite! Food is a little spicy but thats expected with Mexican food.

The 5 star streak lives on. I went in fully expecting a good sandwich, and I got a mind-blowing one. Walking into the store, I was greeted by one of the two owners, who was taking a very late lunch break (I found out later, that as of now the two owners are also the only two employees). I did not catch their names, but they are both very friendly and seemed very accommodating. They have only been a open a little more than a week, and are apparently still working out some of the details (e.g. they don't really have delivery ability/manpower right now), but as far as food preparation goes, they work very fast. It's a tiny place, with seating along the walls for a handful of people (plus points for coat hooks along those seats). The menu written out in chalk is straightforward: 6-7 sandwich choices, a few different options of tacos and salads, and the option to have your pick made extra spicy. I went with the sidecar, which is the beef steak banh mi with pineapple chutney, and took the option of added spice. Certainly not a traditional banh mi, but still pretty close to the feeling you'd expect from having one, thanks to the pickled carrots, fresh cilantro and cucumbers, and chili mayo (fortunately they go light on the mayo). The meat tasted incredibly fresh and was very juicy, mixing perfectly with their pineapple chutney. It was a beautiful amalgamation of flavours sweet, sour, and hot, pushing the limits of how far these different elements might complement each other, but never overwhelming each other. Like any good banh mi, the textures of the tender meat also combine perfectly with the crunchy fresh vegetables. The bread was spot-on as well, good crust, soft, chewy, and toasted to just the right extent. These boys definitely know how to make a sandwich, and I would go as far as saying this goes in my consideration for best sandwich I have had in New York this year (and that list includes a helluva lot of great sandwiches). It also pairs very nicely with the very refreshing and soothing fresh basil soda limeade. I can't imagine how difficult it must be to open a new, small-scale eatery in this neighbourhood chock-full of amazing, well-recognized and iconic establishments. But the two young men at Xe May are doing everything right so far, and I really hope it works out for them, because the world is a better place with another option for amazing banh mi.

Cute oasis in a vast wasteland neighborhood (in terms of restaurants). Arugula salad is totally delicious and filling, too. Coffee, apparently French roast or similar, is extremely hard to bear. Nice waitstaff. Biggest negative is Upper East Side prices without accepting credit cards. Someone should inform the owner that cash is passÃ©.

I visited this small establishment this evening and LOVED it. My Dad and I ordered like 5 different tapas and all of them were great. My favorites were the squid in ink and the almond desert. We were able to sit because we got there early but I could imagine what it must be like later on... I'm going back here again very soon!

The best bahn mi I've tasted in a long time. We got the number 1 and number 5. The bread is hot crispy and fresh and they do not skimp on the ingredients. Their picked radish is the perfect taste and paired with the meats, Â it's so yummy. Def will have to return and grab another kind to try. The service is quick and friendly and the ladies behind the counter speak about 4 languages. Make sure you have cash bc it's cash only.
What can I say that hasn't already been said? We walked 5 blocks in the blizzard to get this pizza home. Can't wait to go back again.

Looking for soul food in Harlem? Amy Ruth's will satisfy! Fried whiting was great! Waffles were the best I've ever had. Sweet tea is worth tasting but if you are diabetic skip it or drink a water chaser with every sweet, delightful sip. Service was good and quick!

Super Taste is just another one of these hand pulled noodle shops that's all the rage nowadays in Chinatowns everywhere. Compared to the other shops around town this place seems to be cleaner (I'm calling you out Lamzhou) and has a specialized dish called the Mount Qi noodles. It's pretty much what I get each time I visit Super Taste, it's like a new twist on the traditional beef noodle soup. It's slightly spicy with peas and cilantro that gives it a new spin and it's a definite must try if you are tired of the typical Beef Noodle Soup that each place.

Quick seating on a Sunday morning, gorgeous little patio, friendly service, and delicious food. I am going back as soon as possible. I had the half-baked egg, which was actually two poached eggs on a piece of toast piled with wilted greens and caramelized onions topped with a smooth, creamy sauce. Hell yes.

The spotted pig is a must stop at place when one is in the village. The reason why I gave it a lower that excellent rating is because there are only a couple of dishes that I would recommend, but those two are excellent. These two are the deviled egg and the burger. The deviled egg was easily the best I have ever had, and the burger was right up there too. My friend got the suckling pig which was way to salty and certainly not worth $28. If you go the burger and egg make it worth the wait.

You guys. Â I don't like Japanese curry, never have. Â It's like a mildly spicy gravy, I'd always protest to my friends. Â And then I went to Katsu-Hama, thanks to Steph C.'s review. Â Now I've changed my mantra to I don't like bad Japanese curry. There was some contention between boy and I because he referred to Rylan C.'s remark that one should always get chicken katsu curry to judge a katsu place. Â That seems reasonable, until I chatted with the waitress and she said they specialize in pork katsu, and then explained to me the three different pork katsu options: plain, with shredded radish, and with miso sauce. Â We went with the shredded radish (oroshi hire katsu) and the hire katsu curry- usually we hedge our bets and he did want the chicken, but they specialize in pork! Â So we porked it up. Â  We were curious about the pricier Berkshire pork option, but since neither of us are katsu fanatics, we figured we wouldn't be able to appreciate the difference. Â Plus yelp helped there too. They started us with some delicious strong green tea as we were deciding at 3 in the afternoon on a Sunday, and within a few minutes of ordering we had a bowl of miso soup (comes with the oroshi hire katsu), a covered bowl of fresh rice, and a big bowl of shredded cabbage and onion. Â The salad dressing sits on the table a la ketchup and is ADDICTIVE. Â You pour it on your cabbage and onion salad and the simple crispy ingredients sing. Â There's also that chili powder stuff, some sesame seed mix, and another sauce that you have on the plain katsu sitting on the table. Â I definitely asked the waitress to explain it all to us. Â  The miso soup was probably the best I've had: big surprising chunks of hearty vegetables balanced out the salty, milky broth. Â Loved it. Â  Then came the katsus: mine was two cutlets covered in a mildly spicy, rich gravy curry filled with surprising mushrooms and onions, along with rice. Â His was two cutlets sitting on a little wire rack, covered in the grated radish, and sitting next to a huge mound of that addictive cabbage salad. Â He also got an adorable little saucer of pickles (radish and cabbage) with his. When the food came, we stopped talking and just kept eating. Â It was that good. Â Juicy cuts of pork, not greasy but beautifully crispy and fried, that curry! Â The radish! Â The CABBAGE SALAD WHICH THEY KEEP REFILLING. Â It's addictive. Â I'm going back. By the time we left at 4 the place was already filling up. Â What?

I love meatballs and I understand there aren't many restaurants that specialize in this specific delicacy, but I really don't see the big deal about this place. Let me put it this way: The restaurant is a concept, focusing on meatballs and what it can be mixed with. What it doesn't focus on is quality of the meatballs, which would explain the affordability. Dishes they have that aren't meatball, such as the Risotto, were very disappointing. They should brainstorm on how to make the meatball more delectable(less dry, more soft) than try to throw in cheap quality french cuisines. It's a small place so know that there is a 2 hour wait time, so if you're part of the super-curious, plan ahead of time.
The toppings are unique, and the slices are the size of my head. Nowhere to sit down though. Barely enough room to stand and order.

$6 feeds 2 to 3 people. What a deal! Â I wish the west coast had something like this. The Yelp reviews are right on. 1. Â Order the white sauce. 2. Â Be careful with the red sauce. It will burn your fingers , nevermind your tongue. I will be coming back on every trip to NYC. Â Best late night food ever invented.

A little less than $3 for a tiny little bite usually doesn't resonate very well with me... But, Laduree is definitely worth it! I've only had macaroons once before and they were ok, nothing to write home about, so my expectations for Laduree wasn't all that high. First bite, however, I was blown away! The consistency of these little mouthfuls of heaven were spot on, they weren't coyingly sweet, and the flavors were just.. Spot on and amazing. There wasn't a line when we went in and they didn't mind us hovering over the display for 10 minutes figuring out which ones to get. I got the chocolate, Â pistachio, vanilla, violet something, and strawberry. The violet was probably the only I thought was a little too sweet, but it had a nice floral nite to it. The pistachio is probably their most popular one and for good reason! The others were pretty good as well. 4 was definitely more than enough and I can't wait to go back and try more!

My mom loves this place and orders Hand Pulled Noodle Soup from here Â veryyy often. So it is this place that I first tried h-p'd noodle from and since then, I have been having random h-p'd noodle cravings. Anyhow, the noodle soup here is spectacular for its price because the noodles are delicious with a good amount of meat to balance it...Can't say the same about the veggies though... heh. Some things to note: -The soup definitely has some MSG because I was incredibly thirsty after. -Soups range from $4.50-$5.00 (So cheap!) -You don't have to tip, but it would be nice to seeing as the dishes are so cheap in the first place! -Order beef, it's better than lamb. -Definitely try the dumplings. While I was there, all three customers that walked in ordered dumplings....which is saying something.

Concealed in one of Chinatown's louche and malodorous alleys is a ramshackle storefront with the sign: Tasty Hand-Pulled Noodles. Â Since this is a fairly common claim for all manner of florescent-sign restaurants, I might have kept it moving to my original destination had it not been for the nothing-over-$7 menu and the respectable amount of patrons. Chinese patrons. Â That matters! I pushed the dingy glass door forward and--THUD! THUD! THUD! --there's a guy feet away from me in the kitchen slamming and pummeling a large lump of dough on a table as if the dough owed him money. I'd say the place seats no more than 15, and is fairly cramped. So if you're coming solo, which I was, chances are you'll be nudging elbows with a noodle-slurping stranger, which I was. I ordered a noodle soup with duck and broad flat noodles. Now the dough wrestler was very delicately and swiftly pulling apart the dough into noodles, his motions like an orchestra conductor in fast forward. Â With every pull, the noodles would become finer and multiply--almost enchanting to watch. The noodle soup came within minutes of my ordering it. Â The duck was delightful oily and moist, and the noodles al dente and just slightly chewy--very much to my liking! Â And, visually, it looked like something you'd get from your Chinese grandmother as the noodles had a made-from-scratch unevenness, plunked into those plastic, imitation-China, bowls. Â I slurped, chewed, and dabbed my forehead--blissfully uninterrupted. Â The broth was subtle in flavor, yet it breathed a salty whisper to the noodles. Â Again, stuff that I'm a fan of. Â I adore eating in run-down HITWs where the focus is solely on the food and this unassuming joint will definitely be getting plenty of my repeat business, $5 at a time. I ended up going for a brisk walk up Bowery after dinner, you know, just feeling happy to be alive and eat noodles that a dough-slamming conductor made.

Whoa, 19 bucks for brunch a bit pricey we thought but well worth the price.We had lobster rancheros and fried oyster omelette both delicious and the home fries were outstanding.A must try is the lobster claw bloody mary that comes with the brunch a perfect drink with along side these dishes. We are looking foward to sampleing the other dishes and to what seems like a great happy hour. Martin O.
This place is kinda awesome.

What a great spot! Â I love when restaurants care about their customers. Â I came here with a big group and they are so accommodating to all of our needs (and we have a lot of needs). The best part though was the food, super flavorful and satisfying. Â Here are all the items that everyone must try, calamari, sugar cane with bacon, mixed seafood with red spicy sauce (i dont quite remember the name).
My boyfriend is big fan of good sushi so he did some research and we ended up going. The food was great, we did try the chef choices but it was super pricy.

I don't normally like Mexican food in NYC but this place is awesome! The bartender, Orlando, makes the most delicious drinks! And he always remembers your favorite drinks. You will fall in love. Don't hesitate to come enjoy this great service and amazing good.

I was visiting from out of town, and originally disappointed because we didn't get reservations at Sushi Yasuda across the street. Â My friend had sold it as "5 stars on Yelp from over 500 people" and "must have" sushi. Â Since we had already walked all this way, we looked up and down the street and a guy standing outside this apartment building recommended us to try Sakagura. This place doesn't look like much on the outside - in fact it looks like a standard NYC apartment building. Â Which is what it is. Â We walked down to the basement of the building, and I had flashbacks of doing laundry in my college dorm all over again. Â I wouldn't be surprised if one of those doors actually led to a washer & dryer. Â Going in, I must say I had pretty low expectations - I mean I started the night thinking I would have 5 star sushi, and now I was eating in a laundromat. Â While the waiting area outside the restaurant looks like a laundromat, once you get inside the actual restaurant - it's actually quite nice and comfortable. Â Nothing fancy, but clean and mellow. Sakagara has an extensive sake selection and the waitress was pretty knowledgable and able to pick one out for us given our inability to choose one ourself. Â The food - is where they knocked my socks off. Â A nice combination of raw fish, izakaya, and just homestyle Japanese food. Â Portions are small - the two of us ordered 6 dishes and two desserts and needed to be rolled out of the restaurant. Â The specials of the day were excellent (Ankimo, and some Scallop dish) - my favorite was the Maguro Tartar. Â Make sure to save room for dessert - the Black Sesame Creme Brulee and Pear Millefeuille were SO good. We were both full when we left and were surprised at how inexpensive the meal was - $120 with tax and tip. Thanks Sushi Yasuda for squeezing us out so we could find a gem like this one! Food: 5 stars Service: 5 stars Value: 5 stars

The food is just amazing. JUST GET THE SHORT RIBS, Dont get anything else... this us to kill for and it just MELTS in your mouth. I give a 4 because there is one guy only cutting the meat while the line is 1 hour long!

I loved this place from the food to the service and the ambiance. I read and heard so much about this place that I had to try it. People call this place a hipster joint, I call it coolantic (cool and romantic) . A great place for a romantic evening. Food Cheek Corea Salad- 5 stars Â  insane and had alot of lemon which im a big fan of Hellboy pizza- 5 stars Â  Â speechless Arugala Schmoogala pizza- 5 stars Â  Waitress- 5 stars Paulie Gee- 5 Stars Â Came over to our table and was real nice and friendly. Check it out you will not be disappointed.
Very nice brunch. They really nailed down the basics. Free drink was a nice addition. Pro-tip: the place is a real hot-bed on Sundays...got very lucky with open table and didnt have to wait...

Hi-collar is a very cute coffee bar(and from what i understand at night, an alcohol bar) in the east village located on e. 10th between 2nd and 3rd. It has a long gold bar which seats about 10-15. It is clad in wood and japanese-style paneling. There are little japanese match books that dot the top of ledge above the back counter. The place was manned by two cute japanese ladies. We came on a saturday afternoon around 1-ish and was able to seat immediately. We were in a bit of a rush but needed to grab a bite to eat. Ordered the katsu sandwich and the omu rice. Also got the mizudashi iced-coffee. The katsu sandwich was very plain but also quite delicious. The pork katsu was fried and came between two slices of white bread with a remoulade on the side. The omu-rice, or omelet rice was also pretty good. it is a fluffy omelette on top of a mound of rice mixed with fatty pork and ketchup. a sausage octopus and a piece of garnish sits next to it. the fatty pork was unexpected and...well...actually not my favorite, it tasted a little bit undercooked. i love ketchup so ketchup drenched rice is good with me. overall, not a bad dish for $9 but i can see others being squeamish. the mizudashi coffee came in a little metal cup with a handle. i think metal cups are a bit of a novelty but presentation wise, it was cute and the coffee was good. smooth and not acidic. i drank it straight no sugar no milk. gf who isnt a hard core coffee drinker thought it a bit bitter. i didnt see an espresso machine anywhere so thought that was a bit funny to be missing at a coffee bar. all the parfaits looked delicious but by the end of our meal we were too stuffed to handle it. i think we made it in and out in an hour. longest part was waiting on the food as it took about 20 minutes for them to prepare the katsu sandwich and the omu rice, which i guess is acceptable. cute place. good for a lunch date. limited seating. great friendly service. definitely a place to come back to for me.

This is the review for the To-Go eatery on Elizabeth. Â  I'm sure there's some reason people come.. oh yeah it's the corn... true that, but today it was a little dryer than usual. Â Still a recommendation. Â  Counter staff was up beat and friendly - someone must have gotten laid?! Â  I kid, I kid... this place is great for a to-go spot, then sit out on the bench in the sun and have your food. Â I've sat in the restaurant and had a great time as the waitresses would dance while they worked. Â  Just temper down your expectations and you'll have some good food and a good time. Â (I know of a spot on 46th that serves a better cuban sandwich though).
really like this place and yelp takes down good reviews for no reason without a warning. Â Seems unfair-try Toby's you won't be disappointed.

It's been a while since I've been here but the vibe is still the same- classic, historical, intimate but not overbearing. The crowd is really cool and the bartenders are down to earth and not pushy or wierd. I went to the bar and ordered the Golden on draft. It was good and tasty. I'm getting more into beer because I love these sorts of places, but honestly I do miss my Sancere. What I like about this spot is the decor- brick, wood cabin like and arches. It just feels nice and warm. Had a good time and will definitely come back soon for dinner with friends.

Wayyy too salty! All I could taste was salt. I am from Texas and this place is not good Mexican- not even close. I ate it for dinner tonight and am still feeling sick that I ate it since I was so hungry. The chicken was charred. The chips full of salt- I could actually scrape it off with my fingers. That is wrong! The carnitas were way too salty too- that is all i could taste when i bite into them. Too bad I had high hopes after the reviews. If you like junk food that is not that cheap go here. Cafe Habana, Calexico cart and La Esquina are way better than this place.
Pho doesn't take 30 minutes. The food was very ok: spring rolls and pho. But the service was slow and indifferent, with the overwhelmed manager as the exception.

Everybody loves a good diner, but sometimes the ambience is lacking. Sanford's solves this problem by creating a classy atmosphere within an old dinner. Completely refurbished and contemporary. With a full wine list, gourmet bread baskets, and items like ahi tuna salad on the menu this place is anything but an old school diner.

We liked the short ribs over polenta, the tuna carpaccio, and the house made soft pretzel with mustard and pickle. The portobello mushroom salad was rather run of the mill. With it all, we had a nice pinot noir that wasn't too expensive. My favorite part was the chocolate torte, which actually had the texture of a fudgy brownie. Atop it was a scoop of mint ice cream (my favorite flavor) that actually had mint leaves in it -- loved it! Nice service and a cute, cozy atmosphere.

I don't visit New York often, but when I do, I make sure I go to Mamoun's. It's probably the most reasonable and satisfying meal you can get for under $3 in Manhattan. I've been to both locations, and they both serve a great deal. I'm talking about the $2.50 falafel sandwich. It's a pita filled with falafel, lettuce, tomato, onion and tzatziki sauce wrapped in foil. I've never had the other food but the other sandwiches are all reasonable. The baklava always tempts me. Inside, the restaurant is small with a couple of booths and a ledge on the wall with napkins and bottles of hot sauce. I think one time I got a booth seat, but I appreciate the experience of Mamoun's - waiting in a long line with a bunch of other people who have also found out about this gem. The line moves pretty quickly, and I suggest you moving quickly too when you pay, to keep the line moving. You'll get your food quickly and then, it's likely there will be no seats, so you go outside and find a place. At this particular location, I like to sit on the front stoop of an apartment across the street. Go to Mamoun's! Get a falafel! Let me know if I should give in and get dessert next time.

The food was great, the drinks were great, but I don't think they are fully prepared to accommodate large groups for celebrations. Â The food took over an hour to be served after we ordered, and to top it off, they realized they undercharged us after the most of the people left. Â They made the mistake, and then they couldn't take the hit. Â We paid over $400 with gratuity already included, and she had the odasity to ask me for $19 more after we paid the bill they gave us in full. Â She even dared to offer me the $1 change on their error. Â Really? Â A $1? Woo hoo. Â Such good food and a friendly waiter, but terrible waiting time and overall service for groups. Â So disappointed!

I went her for lunch around 12:30 on a Tuesday afternoon. Â It was empty when I arrived, but full by the time myself and my two friends left. I had the chicken club (with bacon, avocado, lettuce, tomatoe, and I added brie cheese) on a brioche bun. Â It was delicious. One friend had the derby (which was the same as my club, except in a wrap and with blue cheese). Â He seemed very happy My other friend had one of the salads and she was very satsified with hers. What really gives this place 5 stars, however, is the service. Â It's a small place and the owners come out to take your oder, give you water, etc. Â They are extremely friendly and chill people. Yes a sandwich is a little on the pricer side (9-11) typically. Â But you get what you pay for. Â Organic, local flavorful food with excellent service.
The outdoor seating is their saving grace.

On my culinary hierarchy, I rank chicken somewhere in the middle - its typically dry, tasteless, and boring. Â It really can't compete at the top of the food hierarchy with pork belly, duck breast, slow braised short ribs, or seared foie gras (not unless you count its younger sibling - the egg). Â Surprisingly, I actually bookmarked and was looking forward to Barbuto's Pollo Al Forno. Â  The chicken didn't disappoint at all. Â The skin was perfectly seasoned and crispy. Â I actually felt guilty cutting into it with a knife because I wanted an equal balance of skin and meat with each forkful (I didn't want to eat the meat with a trailing cape of skin and miss out on the goodness on the next bite). Â The meat was juicy and meaty at the same time. Â I also ordered a side of patate (potatoes with pecorino and rosemary). Â They were super crispy and mostly potato skins with some "potato meat" (I didn't really taste the pecorino or rosemary). Â By the time you're done with everything, you will feel satisfied full, not disgustingly full.

There's pretty good thin crust pizza to be had at Lombardi's, but really I only went there because it's an institution in Manhattan. Â My friend said her ex-boyfriend would drive from Queens just to have it, but honestly I wouldn't go that far for it. Â It's fine, but not transcendant. Â The sauce, cheese and crust-- nothing was particularly remarkable, in either a good or bad way. Â Maybe that's what happens after 100 years in business. The restaurant is maze-like; I think we actually passed through the kitchen to get to the annexed dining room where we ate. Â The wines by the glass are passable. Â I found it odd that they served sangria, but whatever. Â Overall, not as impressive as I would have hoped, but fine enough.

Really liked this place it definitely has that Italian charm, huge portions and I cant count how many people were ordering extra meatballs to go. Â My only con for the place is that you are literally sitting on top of one an another so you hope you are seated next to someone who isnt rude, smells etc ...No matter where you sit, the tables the bar waiting area, as well as the bar everyone is ordering food. Â  The food is worth it especially if you go with good friends/family but I definitely advise RESERVATIONS or you are waiting a long time or basically told sorry we are booked.
Stew chicken with yellow rice and black beans - 5 stars. Happy Hour $1 empanadas $3 beers! Cash only place -_-

Best Fries Ever...hmmm, not quite, but very very good. Great dining atmosphere located in one of my favorite parts of NY. I would love to come back here and try their seafood selections. I ordered the Steak Frites which were very good even though I ordered it medium and it came out well done (this was pretty wack), but the accompanied butter sauce was perfect compliment. The Balthazaar salad was really a basic salad that had incredible earthy flavors - it hit my preference for salads that focus on organic flavors as opposed to a creamy dressing. Had a bite of their cheeseburger and it was really tasty basic cheeseburger! I would actually say it was one of the better cheeseburgers I ve had, you could taste the quality of the meet.

Amazing thai food! Â  Great service, nice decor! Â We had the pad Thai rice, spicy basil chicken sautÃ© and the room service pad Thai as our main courses and chicken satay, curry puffs, and the charcoal flank steak as appetizers. Â The spicy basil sautÃ© was our favorite with the unique house pad Thai a close second. Â  Kids loved the Thai fried rice though I'd say it isn't really a kids place. Â Still really there are some amazing Thai restaurants on 9th avenue and this was a great choice among many great choices.

This has been a favorite since I moved here almost 3 years ago, and it's become my go-to place when I have out-of-town visitors. Why? Excellent service, good food, fun atmosphere. Everyone we've ever brought here has truly enjoyed the experience. I really love the chilled seafood tower - it's not cheap, but it's such a fun, interactive meal. Another favorite on the apps list is the calamari - it's sauteed with garlic in white wine, and it's to die for. It's a must-have for us every time! Usually you get fried calamari when you eat out, but this is such a wonderfully flavorful (and hopefully a little healthier) alternative! Also tried the escargot traditional (garlic, butter) - never thought I'd like eating snails, but this was great. The fried oysters, foie gras terrine, whole roast garlic, garlic shrimp and chorizo, everything has been wonderful. And they serve bread that is warm and crusty, like it's fresh out of the oven - this is great for soaking up any sauces from your apps! On the entrees list, I've tried the paella royale, which was tasty and could feed a small family, the striped bass, the lobster, sweet and spicy catfish, skate, and hanger steak, and all have been delicious. I've yet to have a bad meal here. Wine list is great, and servers all seem fairly knowledgable about the selections, which gives Blue Ribbon's service the extra edge. And last but not least, dessert - you MUST try the chocolate chip bread pudding. They put it on a griddle so that it gets a nice crust on the outside, and it's served a la mode with hot fudge. Be sure to save room for this, as it's rich and heavy, but oh-so-worth-it! We've also tried the chocolate bruno (very very rich and chocolatey), fresh berries (served w/ whipped cream), profiteroles, hot fudge sundae, and a special bread pudding that was served with a port sauce. That last one was a hit with my parents when they visited from SF. It's not cheap to eat at Blue Ribbon Brooklyn, but I know I'm guaranteed amazing service, great food, and overall, a great evening. And if you're lucky, you might spot a local celeb from the neighborhood!

I stopped by here with a friend on the recommendation of another friend. At Num Pang, they do cambodian sandwiches which are totally different than Vietnamese sandwiches in ingredients but great in their own regard and Num Pang knows their cambodian sandwiches. I'm a sucker for pork belly so I got the Five-Spice Pork Belly Sandwich ($8) with the Blood Orange Lemonade ($3). The pork belly was nice and tender, the sauce on the sandwich is to die for and the bread is perfectly toasted. The lemonade was not over-sweetened and refreshing. There is seating upstairs, but not a lot of room for large groups. Order to go and have a Num Pang outing in near by Union Square. I will be coming back here for more to try more of their sandwiches.

i love the hand pulled noodle soups here. Â you cant get a better bowl of noodle soup anywhere else and for a place that looks as hole-in-the-wall as this place does - is an unexpected delightful surprise. Â i'll choose this place over japanese ramen any day. the only thing that sucks is the service, the styrofoam cups and the cramped space. Â the pan-fried items on the menu tend to be very greasy.
Eggs Blackstone and Steak n Eggs entrees were really good! Tables for 2 are small and literally on top of each other. Service is ok

I ordered take-out tonight, and boy, was I happy I ordered from here. I'm looking for a pizza place off the Lorimer stop. Really have not found great pizza in this neighborhood. I think I can say that this is a place I would definitely order from again. A little bit about what I ordered: I ordered the Mushroom Pizza and added sausage. Their pizzas come in 12" pies. The lady who tok my order said they can also do individual slices, but who wants to do that when the pizza is so tasty? The ingredients are so fresh and delicious. I'm not sure if the mushrooms are button or sliced portabello, but they are ridiculous-marinated beautifully. The proportions are just right, and the cheese was great quality. The only thing I have an issue is how over done the crust was. I get it, it's wood-fired and there will inevitably not be a perfect crust, but the bubbles in the dough were black burnt to the point that I could not finish my crust. I wanted some kinda marinara sauce to finish it off. I'm one of those people who finish their crust because my babysitter told me and my sister when we were kids that it would make our hair grow more if we ate the crust. Tall tales neer hurt nobody, but all in all, this pizza is great, and I look forward to trying more items on the menu that I am sure will be quite delicious! The ambiance inside looked incredible war, clean, and inviting. Definitely coming back with a date or with family.
There is nothing better than a petale rose macaron! I swear. Other flavors are almost as good. The staff is great, always smiling and ready to help. They'll even let you in at 7 pm sharp.

BEAUTIFUL DINING ROOM WITH CROWDED SEATING We entered the warm glowing interior of Balthazar at 10:00 p.m. for a late dinner and it was packed; good thing we had reservations. Â We were squished into a corner booth just inches away from the other tables. The host had to actually move the table so we could squeeze into the booth. Â We were greeted by a professional server that took exceptional care of us. We ordered the following: Shrimp Cocktail--The shrimp tasted like they just jumped out of the ocean and the accompanying cocktail sauce was spiced just right. Grilled Dorade--Perfectly cooked fish on a bed of asparagus, potatoes, chanterelles, and butter. Pan-Roasted Chicken--The chicken was crispy and moist and was accompanied by beet greens, chanterelles, and spaetzle. If you want first-rate service, delicious food in a gorgeous setting, and don't mind sitting extremely close to other diners, then give Balthazar a try. Food: Â A- Service: Â A+ DÃ©cor: Â A
An oasis in a sea of meh restaurants. Great place but it's super busy. I love the decor and the numerous gluten free options on the menu. Great burgers, salads and comfort food. Highly recommended!

We sat at the communal table, and slurped a tempura eel udon, a pork belly udon, some pickles, edamame and gyoza. The food was uniformly good, the service friendly. The udon broth was very good - a depth of flavour without excessive saltiness, and the attendant noodles first class.
Mochi is good..love the salmon, Â great sake. Service is very good and nice. Small place but good enough food and staff. Good food overall.
Total over-priced tourist grub. Â Why wait, go elsewhere. Â Food is really subpar and service stinks. Â The joke is on us.

Best Pizza I've ever had, hands down. Â Something about the sauce in the pizza makes it stand out from others that I've tried. Â If you goto Brooklyn, NY check this place out. Â It's cash only, there's a significant wait in line since the place is really small.

This is my local go-to spot to reconnect with Paris! It's the kind of breezy, laid back bistro you find in la Marais, or just below Montmarte, serving a really good croque madame and strong coffee. Great backyard patio from the late spring until fall.

I'm all the way from Los Angeles. My aunt brought me to La Sirene and I have to say I have never been to a place like it. Food was perfect, dessert was perfect, service was perfect and environment was perfect. Thank you. Recommend to everyone!

Awesome! The food was fantastic and the service was friendly. Â We were there for brunch and had the Wheat Pancakes and the Steak & Eggs. Â Delicious is the only way to describe it. Â Also, try the Pomegranate and Sparkling Wine drink. Â So tasty.

Tucked away in its remote locale in the east village, supper might not be the place you stumble upon (unless you are a diligent yelper, or , driving down FDR, from which it is actually surprisingly accessible). During the summer, the prize tables are streetside in the open air - though they are scarce. The inside of the restaurant is nonetheless charming, if a tad on the cozy side (my table for 5 were awkwardly placed in an L shaped table on which we were suggested to congregate on one side, so a couple could occupy the two end seats if need be). Service, if a little slow, was courteous and knowledgable (a lot of translating service can become necessary for those not intimately familiar with the italian language or cuisine). The food is moderately priced and tasty. Drink selection hits the spot also. If you're adventurous, try the $13 "sunday" to finish things off (potentially a special when I was there so perhaps not the easiest to find). To my amazement, my two fellow diners who ordered it were licking their plates by the end, in spite of its size making that a daunting prospect at the onset. Overall, worth a redo if you feel like a trek!
So fresh, inventive and delightful cooking ! Very friendly staff ! Our favorite restaurant during our NYC trip

Great place for brunch - they offer brunch and lunch menu at the same time, love the proximity to SoHo. Of note: 1. Great coffee. 2. The two-person tables are quite long, therefore it feels as though the person across from you is a fair distance away and having to raise one's voice to hear each other is a must. Â So if you want to have a heart-to-heart, girl-talk or personal convo, expect to be sharing everything you say with tables on either side of you.

had a beef meal topping here one late afternoon, after being lost from locating another food place that i believe was in the area. the meal's great, soft, and tasty. service was also OK. this seems to be a good place for a quick lunch or dinner, based on the number of people eating alone by themselves when i was there. i'll be a customer again, anytime soon.

Gramercy Tavern is by far one of the best restaurants in Manhattan. Â I've sat in the main dining room and the tavern, and both experiences have been amazing. The food is excellent and the service is always top-notch. From the moment you walk in, people are friendly. The hosts/hostesses are not pretentious like there are in some restaurants. Instead they are approachable and warm. Five stars all the way!

Had a craving for Filipino food over the weekend other than the ones across where I live so my friends and I decided to try out Jeepney. We had everything for sharing! -Chicharong bulaklak (this does not need explaining to a pinoy PIG lover!) -A special that night: Lamb menudo in shepherd's pies' Â clothing with a huge longga on the side which was classy for a pinoy pub :D ; -Longa dog that left me wanting more (drolling while thinking about the garlic and the sauce on it) -Pinakbet (not a fan of veggies but the squash was sweet making it pleasant) -Dampa fry and the Filipino bangers (the hostess suggested and made known we could do half orders so we could taste 'em both) -Pancit malabok negra (which did make pansit look more exotic than the regular Â chowmein lookalikes) -Chori Burger with kamote fries Also had coconut flavored rice. Pops Fernandez for my drink which made me slur or twas prolly the chicharong bulaklak, can't figure. The staff explains every food that lands on the table (Awesome, gave you another good reason to take adventurous non-Filipino friends here) and we had a pretty hostess as well. Â Everything was delicious though the Longa dog I liked best. They had balut too just FYI. Subway sucks during weekends. We had reservations for 7pm, got there at 7:20... FILIPINO TIME! Â :) Group of 6. Rushing went in and the bar was packed! And seating at the back for dining was pretty small. Well NYC always has had limited space really. Wall decors are scandalous if I were to take my grandma. Overall this was a satisfying experience worthy of a next visit. Â Saving my 5th star for that.
Bomb pizza. Line's too long. And no individual slices, but the pizza is so good, it doesnt matter.

This place serves real Indian food and not the Westernized tamed spices version you are going to find at a lot of places. Â Like I can handle spicy being Asian, but the Lamb Vindaloo from here near killed me. Â I mean it was so spicy, my throat burned, my nose ran, and my ears stung. Â I confess I was a bit of a wimp and was dipping the lamb chunks in the yogurt chutney to help temper the fiery spiciness until I had to give up and immediately had to down the rice pudding dessert in order to counteract everything. Â Dairy works better than water in situations like this which is something the Indians have figured out unlike East Asians (where dairy doesn't figure at all in dishes). In any case, I have had Lamb Vindaloo at other places and they've usually been about half this level. Â The one here was literally the spiciest dish I have ever consumed in my life. Â  I also had their Chicken Tikka which was good, but also a bit spicy (also was dipped in the yogurt toward the end). Â I've never had an issue with spiciness at Asian or other Indian restaurants so I am assuming the Indian food here is a tad bit more authentic given my inability to tolerate it. Â Really, if you have doubts about your ability to handle spiciness, order a creamy spicy dish instead of the fiery enough to make all your senses shut down Lamb Vindaloo.

Really yummy! Organic eggs - very nice decor inside... and the food was very delicious - their homemade sausages are a definite to try! i also had the beet salad - which albeit was small, but still very good
Wow, super-affordable yakiniku in Midtown! They have a pretty big selection of meats and veggies, and lots of apps to choose from. We are definitely fans and will be back!

I love this place!!! Â This time around, I had the grilled skirt steak while bf had the tiger shrimp sandwich. Â Tiger shrimp sandwich was good as I remembered it, and the skirt steak was fantastic as it was cooked medium-to-medium-rare and juicy. Â The bread was toasted and crunchy, and the pickled carrots, cilantro, and cucumber added much flavors that it was an explosion in my mouth. Â Had the carrot coriander soup that was great. Â The only meh thing is the blood orange lemonade--a little sour and a little bitter and needs a little sugar. Will recommend this place to anyone who wants a low-key but delicious meal.

great spot, love the building, reminds me of lobster mecca, Gosman's, in Montauk, but in look only. Ridiculously expensive considering we were sitting at a picnic bench with paper napkins and an ineffective plastic lobster fork. 35$ for a mediocre lobster and corn on the cob in this setting is outrageous. Friendly but incredibly lackadaisical service. How many times did I beg for extra butter (and by extra I mean, like, 2 tablespoons), and by the time it arrive what little was left of my lobster was cold. And it was my birthday! I'd go back to sit and watch the sunset and have a beer, but never again to eat.

I really enjoyed Locanda Verde! It was recommended by my girlfriend's co-worker and I am glad she pushed me to go! The food is good and ambiance is very nice - a great date spot. I went at 7:30pm on a Fri night thinking that the after work crowd had left and the evening dinner people would not yet be there but I was surprised to see how full the place was. We sat at the bar and had a couple of drinks waiting for a table - I recommend a reservation. We started off with the ricotta crostini and it was excellent to the point that we have decided to go back, sit at the bar and just drink wine and have the crostini. Its a must try! For dinner I ordered a special - wild boar ragu and pasta. I wasn't crazy about this dish. It was good but not what I was expecting so I can't hold it against the place. I tried my girlfriend's pumpkin agnolotti which I thought was good as well but again pumpkin is not my thing so I wasn't crazy about it. I will definitely go back and give some other dishes another try. The food was quality and I just need to do a better job ordering!
A gastropub that delivers a good value, great selection of craft beers, and a focused but good menu of eats. Â I like the happy hour that includes $1 oysters.

I think there were three Thai restaurants in a row on this street. Â This one was the smallest and newest so we decided to try it. Â Small space, but comfortable with some good music vibe. Â Fully open front added to the open air feeling. Â We got the drunken man noodles, and the flavor was great. Â It was a little spicy, like medium, but we like the spice. Â My son got the pork chops. Â They were a little under cooked, but upon request the kitchen recooked and replated for him. Â Overall we had a great meal and would come back again.

Burrito Box is an excellent vegan-friendly place for quick, cheap, and super tasty burritos. They have classic burritos as well as some more exotic choices, not to mention their vast vegetarian selection with soy cheese and vegan sour cream. Left Terminal 5 looking for a post show snack before the long train ride home, and Bella treated us and the six others that came in behind us with kindness and hospitality despite being the jerks the show up 10 minutes before close. Sorry we were 'those guys', Bella and co-workers! Thanks for being nice anyway! Don't forget to tip!

Driest, crispiest, over-cooked medium hamburger I've ever had. I ate it and didn't complain until the end, and at that point the cook probably thinks that it was good enough if I ate most of it anyway, but I was too distracted by the meeting I was having to be interrupted by bad food. I'd heard such good things for years about this place and now that I live in the neighborhood I thought I would clearly be coming here a lot... what a let down. Boo! If a restaurant can't get something as simple as a burger right (especially with the word 'farm' in the title) it can tell you what everything else is going to be like.

Took a friend of mine here for his birthday. Â This restaurant is definitely more casual than some of the other higher end Italian in the city. Â Our server Erika was very friendly. Â We started with the polenta. Â The mushrooms were sauteed in a chicken stock, so I did not try it. Â The polenta was delicious - rich and creamy! Â I liked that since we shared it they brought it out in two separate bowls. Â I got the spaghetti that everyone raves about. Â To be honest, I think it was good, but not great. Â I think there are a lot of really great Italian places in the city that have very high quality pasta for much cheaper than Scarpetta (like becco). Â  We split the chocolate cake which was delicious - very moist and chocolate-y! Was a bit of a bummer that they didn't comp anything for his birthday (glass of champagne, dessert). Â Overall it was OK, but would be happy never returning.

Celebrated another birthday here, food was great as usual and wine was superb. What lacked this time around was service. It seemed that our waited decided that rat pack missing a member and he is too cool to serve us. I had Â to constantly chase him down, at the end of the night he left with out saying one word to us. This was bit annoying but all in all great time and all of my friends enjoyed it.

Great atmosphere, kind of a polished old-world vibe, but dozens of tables crammed cozily into the space. If you're with an adventuresome group, you can easily share small plates. After relying on Yelp reviews for so long, I figured it was finally time for me to contribute, too. As with most firsts, I wanted my first review to be special. Consequently, I chose LadurÃ©e, the most magical place on Earth...next to Disney World. Okay, so that's not really true, BUT if there weren't always so many people and there were a place to sit and savor my goodies, I'm pretty sure LadurÃ©e would be my absolute favorite place in the entire city. Every time I approach the store, I can hardly suppress the hugest grin. I'm immediately overcome by a feeling of happiness and peace, regardless of how miserable the rest of my day might have been. You may think I'm exaggerating, but then you also must not fully appreciate the awesomeness that is a LadurÃ©e macaron. After trying the macarons first at the original Paris shop, I was both ecstatic and worried when I learned that a shop was going to open on Madison Avenue. Would they be able to maintain the same great quality? Would they be just as expensive? The answer to both of those questions is yes. And even though I am not currently in a position to throw around money, I consistently and willingly shell out $20+ per visit, because let's face it, there's no way I'm leaving that place with fewer than 8 macarons, if not more. Unlike its French counterpart, the NYC location does not offer a myriad of desserts and pastries, focusing mainly on the true heart of this establishment: the macarons. I have tried macarons at other places and none of them have ever measured up to LadurÃ©e's, not even come close (at least not in New York). These classic French macarons are light and airy. Their shells are crisp (and fragile!), yet when you bite into the tiny sandwich, they have this wonderfully chewy texture that isn't dense like most other macarons I have tried. It just melts in your mouth. As for flavors, there are the original ones that can be found year-round and the seasonal ones. The salted caramel, which is fortunately a regular, makes me swoon. I don't know what it's like to be in love, but I'm pretty sure the feeling I get when I sink my teeth into a salted caramel macaron is the closest I've come. Other favorites of mine are rose, coconut, and pistachio. Honestly, it's difficult to go wrong with most of the flavors. An exception to that is the "Incroyable" almond (created in honor of Laduree's 150th anniversary), inaptly named, for it is anything but incredible. Filled with an odd marshmallowy substance instead of the usual jam or buttercream, I found it to be a poor complement to the always perfectly baked shell. It was too sweet, too sticky, and just overall unpleasant. Regardless of this little misstep, however, I feel I have no choice other than to give 5 stars to LadurÃ©e. I smiled like an idiot to myself the whole time it took me to write this review (and probably started salivating somewhere around "salted caramel"). I fear that I will go completely broke when I move to an apartment closer to LadurÃ©e in a few months' time. But at least I'll be a happy pauper.

This place gets 5 stars, and here's why. I'm a pizza freak, so when my buddy Steve took me here when I was visiting, I was excited. It has almost 1,000 reviews at the time. This was creamy and rich. A+ guys, this is my pepperoni and mushroom hot spot on the East coast for life!

Small, crowded, and slightly dirty, this might not be an ideal place for a romantic getaway, but Prosperity definitely serves up some authentic Northern Chinese homemade dumplings. Friend and I ventured off to Chinatown to reconnect with our ethnic roots when we were in NY two weeks ago. We shared an order of the pork & vegetable dumplings and a duck pancake. We waited in the constricted area for around 15 minutes as they were busily taking other people's orders with a kitchen-ful of Chinese people making delicious dumplings. By the time our food was ready, we decided to eat on the streets because the store was getting a bit too crowded and I realized that having a heater in your face wasn't actually so pleasant. I'm not sure if it was because of the wonderfully contrasting sensations of being attacked by the chilly winds while shoving steamy hot juicy dumplings down my hungry belly, or of my natural gluttony, those dumplings were homemade tastiness epitomized. So authentic, I thought I was in a Chinese province for a moment. Get the dumplings, any kind, I'm sure they're all unbelievably delicious and inexpensive. The duck pancake was a toothsome treat as well. Aromatic, crispy, and savory, these thick Chinese pancakes were covered in sesame seeds and pan fried to perfect crispiness and then filled with roasted duck and scallions. The duck meat in the pancake reminds me of Peking duck as I took another bite into the fatty duck skin. A morsel of the duck pancake made me chuckle like a happy little girl. Out of all the meals we had during our week-long visit in NYC, I can safely declare that this rustic meal I had on the streets of Chinatown was certainly the most palatally memorable.

I can understand a lack of courtesy when the place is packed, however, we went in early on a Monday evening and were alone in the restaurant when this happened- the men behind the counter were fairly awful. We asked to sample two sauces, and the man acted like we were doing him a giant injustice- he would not give my boyfriend a frite to dip into the sauce. He then acted really nasty and pretended he didn't hear when we asked for the sauce combo, When we listed the additional sauces we wanted, he literally started speaking in this super slow tone acting like we were idiots to let us know that he'd be giving us sauce in smaller cups than the free sauce that comes with each order. Feel pretty neutral about this place, I wouldn't get out of my way to go there but if someone else wanted to go, I wouldn't say no either.

I came here with my friend, and we got the three course tasting menu ($88) in the Dining Room. Nothing wowed me, and I thought all the dishes were off balance in terms of flavor. AMUSE BOUCHE: Scallop: Good. FIRST COURSE: Beef Carpaccio: Sliced wonderfully, uber thin. SECOND COURSE: Roasted and Braised Lamb: Perfectly cooked to medium rare and extremely tender. However, everything was too salty. PRE-DESSERT: Panna cotta: This was cute. It had a little happy face :) I also love panna cotta so this was a nice bite before dessert. THIRD COURSE: Upside Down Plum Cake: My friend really liked it. I thought it was too tart on the edges. I preferred my friend's chocolate bread pudding; it was very comforting and had good chocolate flavor without going overboard on sweetness or decadence. Service was very nice, and the meal was very filling. Overall though, I was extremely underwhelmed.

The bouncer really takes his job too seriously. He thinks he's standing outside of an exclusive club, and not...an empty bar. I went with a group of maybe 12 people on a weekend night, and the bouncer let some people in, and turned down others. My friend towards the front of the group wasn't let in because the bouncer didn't like the number of buttons the friend had buttoned on his shirt (!) I was with two other people at the back of the line, and as we walked up, he took one look at us from 10 feet away and said all three of us couldn't enter. I was dressed well enough as far as I could tell. Maybe it was that I had sneakers on, but it's a pub, and I'm not sure what he thought my friends did wrong. Either way, you can be this selective when an establishment is actually busy and not EMPTY, unless you want it to go out of business, which frankly would be fine with me. The fact that some of my friends couldn't get into an empty bar meant that everyone in the group left, and they permanently lost 12 customers due to rude service. Not a very good business model, I'd say. Not only that, but the bouncer kept telling my friends and I to "move across the street", implying that the bar owns the (also completely empty) sidewalk right in front of the bar, which it does not. I can stand on the sidewalk all I please. At least my friends and I had fun calling the bouncer on his bullshit and giving him a piece of our mind before we went to another bar. Don't bother with this bar, you might not be "worthy" enough for them to grant you access, even when it's empty!

Just a quick pop over the Williamsburg Bridge, and you're at Traif, a place my parents and I decided to go to, not necessarily because of previous reviews, but really because of its delightfully irreverent name. We, too, are Jews who love pork (the owner must be in this camp as well), so we had a feeling we were in for a good time. The food is incredible. Inundated with pork, as expected--and it was all fucking delicious, don't get me wrong--but I think what really rounded it all out for me were the non-pork dishes. The tuna tar tar, butterfish carpaccio and seared scallops really helped to "cut the fat" of the bacon croquettes, braised pork belly, and later, bacon doughnuts (!!). Aside from its worship of pork, the offerings at Traif are dynamic--I noticed a nice Asian influence in the mussels, cooked with soy, and the butterfish carpaccio, which was on a bed of seaweed and was topped with black sesame seeds. All in all, an amazing meal, and I would recommend it to anyone, except for vegetarians, or jews who keep kosher, of course (as if I'm recommending restaurants to vegetarians and kosher jews anyway). one more thing: EAT THE BACON DOUGHNUTS. Seriously. Don't be scared. They're fucking incredible.

I am so glad I came here...food was delicious, atmosphere was classically retro and service was great. The picture does not do it justice...this was the best trout that I have ever had - so unique, and lightly stuffed with yummy sautÃ©ed onions and the side of Brussel sprouts was out of this world with chunks of bacon. Â This place brought it!

Love at first bite. Just have trouble making up my mind which sauce to choose. Â  Also dig the small, dark, cool space in the back to rest from a day long East Village crawl. One of the best pommes frites in NYC. The owner is a genius.

What a great addition to Prospect Heights and by some of the same people that brought us Milk Bar on Vanderbilt. Â Great food, friendly and accommodating service and beautiful interior design. Â These people care a lot about delivering a great experience and it shows at every level. I only gave 4 stars because they're only serving brunch at the moment and haven't gotten their liquor license so it's a bit hard to judge the full menu but personally I can't wait to give it a try. Â  My wife and I have been twice, once with our one year old and they couldn't have been nicer about accommodating him/us. Â The coffee is unbelievable and the 4 dishes we tried were outstanding. Â My wife loved the mushroom toast and I had a hash with poached eggs and homemade sausage patties that was incredible. Let's hope this one goes the distance.

If I came here with the mindset that this was a Bar, I would give the place 4 stars. Since I came here with the mindset that it was a Restaurant, and had come here to try and satisfy a Thai food craving, I was unfortunately disappointed. The place made for a good Bar because... 1. great decor.. they have a great chandelier theme going on and do a decent job implementing their "room service" theme throughout the place 2. classy yet chill ambiance.. its chill enough for flip flops and jeans but you wouldn't feel overdressed with your party clothes on either 3. unique, tasty drinks....i devoured the guava mojito in a second. 4. attentive service.. very prompt so you're never thirsty. The food however was straight up NOT GOOD. At first I thought...oh interesting, Thai and New American together, must be a unique fusion place. Instead what they served was traditional Thai dishes, Americanized by someone New to cooking.. . guess I didn't read the Yelp labels correctly. Yes the main ingredients were there in each dish, but all the spices and herbs that make thai food, THAI FOOD, were lacking, and therefore so was the yumminess of the food. I got the penang curry and the corn spring rolls and they both could be described as such. Yet with the negative review of the food, I will be back, but next time post 10pm, after I get dinner elsewhere.

I used their new app (comes with a $3 credit!) to buy my coconut tiger shrimp sandwich (with cilantro, cucumber, pickled carrots, and chili mayo)...the process was easy and the food delicious, as always.

Yum! Â  My review is done. Just kidding, but seriously--this is a great place and my review is based solely on my experience having some wine with a friend. Â (we were not hungry enough to eat, but I will go back and add to it when I do). We arrived on a quiet Saturday afternoon and were greeted by a very warm bartender who allowed us to just sit wherever. Â He was super attentive to our needs and very kind. Â We were mulling on what wine to have when we said "could you describe the grenache?" Â  He goes, "I'll just bring you a taste and you tell me what you think." What? Â Awesome! [the grenache was amazeballs, btw] So anyway....we had a couple of glasses of wine and sadly left, but will return. Â Just great!

no fuss, no gimmicks, no attitude. just sriracha, vinegar, soy sauce, and some damn good dumplings. try them steamed, try them fried, try them all! you can probably order the entire menu and still have change left in your pocket. and with food this good, it might not be such a bad idea.
4.5 - duck over rice (or group duck dinner) makes me want to be a better man

Found this place through an eater.com recommendation for brunch. We went on a Saturday at around 11 am and the place was empty. We ordered the biscuit sandwich and the pulled pork sandwich. Both of them were absolutely amazing. The wife preferred the pulled pork sandwich. I also ordered the whiskey milk fizz which was really good. The space was really neatly laid out. The servers, while efficient, weren't the friendliest folks we ever met. Would definitely recommend for brunch.

Ahhh Laduree...finally you have blessed Manhattan with your sweetness. Only sad part is...no cafe and no yummy hot cocoa. Â :( I heard about the horrific hour wait, so I decided to play it smart and venture out during my lunch break on a Wednesday. I waited a mere 15 minutes. Pay the extra couple dollars for the adorably presh "Laudree New York" boxes. Tres chic! I had a mixture of 8 cookies stuffed into my little purple box, and each one was delish. Salted Caramel, Rose, Raspberry, Lemon....even the pistachio were all blissfully delicious. If only they had a cafe within the maison, I could then close my eyes and really feel as if I was in Paris.

A little gem in the Gramercy area... I am bedazzled! The decor is elegant yet simple. A little old fashion with the wooden tables yet the restaurant is dimly lit & there are candles are every table. Maialino reminds me of having a meal so fresh that it came directly from the farm. The octopus of the Polpi ai Ferri was crisp on the outside yet chewy & tender on the inside. For the primi, my boyfriend & I shared the Malfatti al Maialino. IF YOU DON'T GET THIS, YOU ARE MISSING OUT. BIG. TIME! I have never tasted any part of a pig so tender & juicy in my life. You don't even need a large amount to enjoy the dish - just a tidbit will do the trick. Ahhhh, braised suckling pig. How perfect you were on top on a small bed of pasta! For secondi, I had the Pollo alla Diavola. Oh my God, dear chicken, where have you been hiding all my life?! I swear Maialino has a secret to making their meats so tender & juicy. The chicken wasn't heavily flavored but it was still sooooooo. damn. GOOD! We had gotten the mushrooms as a the side. The mushrooms were also perfect. Slightly crisped but still so soft & juicy on the inside. The dessert we had was also good... I don't recall the name but it was the orange marmalade tart topped with a rich dark chocolate ice cream... Not overly sweet - just simply delish! & tart was well complimented w/ the dark chocolate ice cream. Ahhhhh... I will definitely be coming back, my dear Maialino... You are worth every penny in my wallet!

Maxican taste is rarely a found one digit here which is so bad to have at the same time.
