Taqueria Lower East Sid itself is a highly acknowledged product which can always be honored. When I went to this site for the first time, I had no clue what so ever because of the power which they offer. Thus, making this my choice was so simple and I made it so! Loving it! Making it a dream to visit!

Reasonably priced pasta. Â Some of the dishes should be a couple of dollars lower, but not bad for the neighborhood. Â Pasta's come with bread and a container of parmesan cheese. Â  Sometimes they don't prepare your pickup order until you get there and pay. Â This defeats the purpose of calling it in, and has happened to me several times. Â They recently started taking Seamless orders and this has seemed to solve my pickup debacle. Â However, there is a $20 Seamless minimum should you have your food delivered.
Cool place with a good beer selection. This place is HUGE, but it has a very cozy atmosphere. I could picture being here hangin out by the fire place with a beer on a cold winter day.

When in need of a place to go for something to eat, this may be my new "go-to" place in NY. Â They have a large selection of very fresh fish and seafood. Â You can't go wrong with anything in their menu. Â Keep in mind portions are huge. Â Friendly staff, sharp service.

I inhaled my food as soon as it came out. I ordered the Tororo, which was a simple hot soba dish with great mountain yam and nori seaweed. The soup was perfectly seasoned and tasted great. The noodles were cooked perfectly and the toppings added a nice flavor without overpowering the rest of the dish. I've got to say that their soba is really good. The regular size is the perfect amount to keep you feeling satisfied, but not full. Their tempura on the other hand is whatever. It is so overpriced and they deep fry the most random vegetables (at least in my opinion).

If you are really a big fan of thai food you have to try this place. Food is extremely delicious and so flavorful. Place is quite big and they also have an outdoors sitting area. Â For mouth watering experience you need to try this place!!

How do you like your beef tartar? The umami burger was very tasty. Â It's basically beef tartar on a gourmet bun with some delicious sauces. Â And if you don't mind dining alone, you can get seated almost immediately versus the crazy wait. However, there's a minor problem that when I want beef tartar, I want beef tartar. Â And when I want a burger, I want a b-u-r-g-e-r. Â Very tasty, but not sure what I would need to crave in order to revisit.

I had a good time overall here, minus a few mishaps like sitting too close to the stoves so hot liquids splatter onto you and the table and finding a mysterious dirty blond hair in a main course. The space here is tiny and putting mirrors on the walls does not make this place look any larger. Apparently this place does take reservations but you have to email them. I got the 7-course here ($85 currently) but a la carte is definitely available. Food: Rutabaga and green apple shooter - pretty good Vegetable muesli with Greek yogurt - ok Sweet shrimp with caviar and potato - delish Crispy kale salad (Thai/Viet style) - very good Roasted broccoli with watercress and pecorino cheese - pretty good Mushrooms with mushroom foam, spinach and poached egg - fantastic minus the hair Scottish salmon with creamed artichoke - meh Shortrib with green apple - too fatty for me Black forest cake - meh Grapefruit tart with tarragon granita - not great Banana pudding with rum - good Mascarpone cheesecake - good Pumpkin cake with maple frosting - very moist

We were standing there at 152 W 49th wondering what happened to Hagi? 152 yes.... but it says Sapporo restaurant...=T I almost let out a tear... I was on a mission, I had to eat at Hagi! After a few minutes of searching, we found a find door that led you downstairs....and there it is!!! Small room, loud, people drinking & having fun, smell of yummy japanese food fills the air..It's almost like the restaurants I went to in Tokyo except this one was missing something. The air was lacking second hand cigarette smoke...=) Almost everything we ordered was good....we ordered a few items off their specials board on the wall. One dish was a wasabi dumpling.....It was bite size so I gobbled one up immediately and started tearing! It was intense!!! So beware, take half a bite and wait if you order that dish! It's too bad we don't have any place like this in San Francisco.

The space is small but cozy. Might have trouble getting seated for dinner without a reservation and possibly lunch. The food was delicious. We went before 4pm and had unlimited sangria for $14/person. They were strong but tasty, well worth it. Strongly recommend the Ropa Vieja and the Vaca Frita as well.

Oh WOW! My type of an establishment. Â I love food and love trying different things that other people might shy away from. We came here for a brunch and i loved every second of it. Â Their bloody mary was absolutely delicious! Everything on the menu looked good too and tasted good going down :)

ilili had topped my list of restaurants to check out for a while now, based on viral buzz, critical praise, and general curiosity regarding Lebanese cuisine. The girlfriend and I decided to make Saturday date night and reservations were set. I'm happy to say that, for the most part, ilili lives up to its tremendous hype. We figured we'd order a bunch of small plates for dinner, seeing as two full pages of the menu were devoted to them. Baba Ghannouj is typical Middle Eastern crowd-pleasing fare, and I don't go wild over it like some people, but ilili's offering was probably the best I've had. We also had the Beef Fried Kibbeh, an order I could've done without, honestly. They are essentially four golf ball-sized dumplings, but man, are they heavy! Those things sank right to my stomach. The Mekanek was fantastic - a warm plate of smoky, little lamb sausages. But the standouts were the Phoenicians fries - super-salty and super-addictive - and the Duck Shawarma. I loved everything about this last dish - fresh meat, bold figs, just the right amount of green onions, and the signature garlic whip to bring it all home. Next time I find myself at ilili, I'll be sure to try some new dishes, but the fries and the duck stay put. I'm ordering them every time. I have to admit that I do have one gripe, though. While the staff was very attentive and professional, I couldn't help feeling rushed. We were already being taken care of and being checked on rather frequently, so I'm not really sure why the restaurant felt the need to send both our server and the floor manager as a tag team to our table. I think we were ready for dessert after only thirty minutes. I think we spent more time on the subway ride to the Flatiron than we did actually inside ilili. I don't think this was the relaxing dining experience I was hoping for. Delicious, yes, but relaxing, not so much. The micromanaging service here won't get me back anytime soon, but, like I said, the food will, so I'll take it. ilili didn't succeed in showing me tremendous variation between Lebanese food and other Arabic cuisine, but I can't attest to a finer Middle Eastern at-large dining experience. The decor is very modern and geometric, designed with more hard right angles than a NYC street map. The cocktails come with a price tag, but they pack a punch worth the admission to Tipsy Town, especially the From Manhattan To Beirut. Apparently, "ilili" means "tell me". Well, I tell ya - the hype is real.

I am not the biggest fan of ramen, but I still ordered the duck just to give it a try. The noodles tasted weird and a little under cooked. The "spicy" tuna maki rolls wasn't spicy at all lol. But the steamed buns with Kobe beef was really good. I was kind of disappointed because the menu was filled with basic Japanese appetizers but the choices for entree were very small. The atmosphere was nice but then once it got dark they put this oil filled candle on our table that smelled like gas. Nothing too special and don't plan on going back there. In this area there are too many better places to eat than here.

The staff is so friendly, refreshing for a quick lunch spot in midtown. Food is cheap, super quick as most is ready for you to grab and go, and delicious. Lots of pastries im interested in trying. 5 stars to the staff!
Pretty good pizza!

I avoid places in times square like the plague but a good friend of mine decided we're going to celebrate his b-day here so it wasn't a question of choice. We were a group of 10. I'll start with the good: * A really good chocolate mousse cake And now the bad: * No menus. There's a menu on the wall but a friend of ours that is shortsighted couldn't see it so he had to go with whatever people were ordering. People who sat with their backs to the menu also had a hard time. Not cool. * Cold bread served with no butter or olive oil for dipping. In one average size basket for a table of 10, so at any time if someone at one side decides they want some bread, half the people on the other side can't get to it. * I did not taste the fried calamari that was ordered for an appetizer but everyone who did agreed that it tasted very bad. I don't know how you can ruin something that's deep fried in batter, but as I said, I didn't try it. * After our round of appetizers, the crew that was sent to collect the plates before they bring out the food seemed annoyed with us not handing them the plates. One of them even yelled at a friend of mine for not noticing they're collecting the plates and not removing his cutleries. * The cheese ravioli was WAY too salty, and there wasn't enough tomato sauce to cover it all (we got a plate of ravioli with sauce only in the middle) * When it seemed like some people are done eating, the same careless crew asked one or two people sitting on one side if they're done and then took away all the plates, some of which were still half full. Other people who were still eating were surprised to find out that the central plates were gone when they got their heads up from their plates. The food was already thrown away. No one even asked us if we wanted a doggy bag. * I mentioned this was a birthday - one person got up and went to the waiter discreetly and asked him for a chocolate cake with candles for the birthday boy. When the birthday boy tried to look at the dessert menu (they brought one for the entire table), the waiter informed him that someone already ordered dessert so he should not bother, and took his menu away. By this he both ruined the surprise and left 10 people with one dessert that is meant for 2-3. * We ended up ordering another cheesecake because the first dessert was not enough for 10. The lemon cheesecake had such a bad aftertaste of lemon that no one had more than one bite and half of it was thrown away. As if all this wasn't enough (at this stage we were discussing how we would rate the place and the average score was between 5 and 6), when we tried paying with 5 credit cards, the waiter said he can't do it, as there is a maximum of three and the computer won't let him. I insisted on seeing the manager, who told me that it's their policy not to take more than three cards per party. I proceeded to explain that I don't think five cards are excessive for a party of 10 and that I expect them to figure out how to do this because this is how we're going to pay. They miraculously found a way to charge five cards, while informing us, again, that this is a one time thing and it's against their policy. I couldn't care less. If they did not add the 18% tip automatically to the bill, I'd leave around 10% or less. I'm not even complaining about the outrageous prices because it's times square and I expected to pay a lot more than what the food is really worth. I will not be returning to this place anytime soon. There are a million good Italian places in the city and there's absolutely no reason to keep going to the bad ones.

Worth the wait! Grimaldis tops Lombardis for one reason only, price! I'll say that both places have the best pizza I've ever had (better than Italy!), but grimaldis is much cheaper. Maybe its because lombardis is in little Italy and grimaldis is in Brooklyn? Idk, but the trip over to Brooklyn is worth it. The thin crust and mozzarella cheese are to d-i-e for! A MUST for every new York visit!

I work in the area and people were always talking about this place so I finally decided to come in. Wow! Indian fast food at it's finest. There is always a huge line so give yourself some extra time or call in your order, it's not that fast, lol I always get the tiger shrimp and the farmer's cheese rolls without onions. The rolls are the perfect size. I really enjoy them. Just note there is a $9 credit card minimum and a single roll is between $6-$8 so, bring cash.

I'll keep this short. I never ever ever write reviews for places, but I loved TTK so much I had to show them some love. This restaurant is amazing!!! Went there for brunch and ordered the Frisky omelette. It was AMAZING!!! I couldn't believe how delicious everything was. This place is legit and I can't wait to go back. I'm so happy they're in the neighborhood.

I came in during the lunch hour and i wanted some toppings on my chicken taboon laffa but the guy putting it together was so frustrated over the fact that i requested an extra ''fill it'' on my sandwich he actually sucked his teeth and went on to the next customer like I was nothing. Thank goodness the kind young man at cashier was attentive enough to quickly throw on gloves and easily complete my order as I requested. He even offered me a free freshly made desert as an apology for his coworker's miscue which I've buying everyday since. Despite the rude guy rushing people, My overall experience there gets a strong 4 stars due to that young man's customer first service and the food being delicious and fresh as advertised. However, I must say this place really needs to reconsider some of the people they have working in the front as they have either attitude and/or language barrier problems.
love this place. They have the best chicken sandwich !!!!

Let me tell you about two perfectly brined, juicy, tender chicken breasts. Let me tell you that they are on two thick pieces of fried buttered bread. Ham and cheese are also invited to this party, though they know they're not the star. Likewise with the delectable, stone ground mustard. And then, just when you think it can't get any more hedonistic, a perfectly cooked over-easy egg with a dash of salt and pepper. This, friends, is the Ella Fitzgerald at Hamiltons. This, friends, is the best sandwich in Brooklyn.

This is my favorite restaurant! Â Although I don't get to go here that often, but when I do go, I am HAPPY!!! This place is good for smaller groups, 4 or 5 max. Â I tried to make a reservation for my birthday, but they told me my party of 12 had to be split up into two tables. Â Of course, I didn't go cause I couldn't leave my friends behind, but believe me, I had to think twice about it because the food is THAT GOOD. The food is great and so is the service. I've only been here for dinner. Â  Appetizers: Calamari - good, not great. Â Isn't in my top five places to get calamari Mussels - we tried both the shallots and white wine sauce, as well as the chorizo and onion. Â I would have to give the upper hand to the shallots and white wine. Entrees: Grilled pork chop - OMG, it is to die for. Â The first time I had it, I was in heaven. Â However, the last time I had it, the pork chop was a bit overcooked (might have been by the size of my party - 6 and we were ordering up a storm, we didn't even have enough room on our table ;x so our entrees may have been on the grill longer since we took a while to finish our starters - calamari, mussels, fries) Linguine con vongole - was a bit spicy for my test, but that didn't stop me from finishing my plate Steaks - My go to steak at Landmarc is the strip or skirt. Â I've tried the filet as well, but I prefer the other two. Â Cooked and seasoned to perfection. Â You get to choose a sauce, but I prefer not using any. Oh, I forgot to mention the fries. Â The fries are so DELlCIOUS. Dessert: Ice cream cones - cute, but not worth it. I will definitely be coming back here soon. Â Oh, forgot to mention, another plus is there's always parking in the area. Â I normally go on Friday evenings and there's always parking, which is rare in the city.

Momo Sushi Shack is amazing. I took my boyfriend here for his birthday dinner last week and it almost felt like an adventure. Stepping out of the nearby subway, the surroundings included an incredible industrial setting. After walking a few blocks towards the restaurant we got a feel for the area and finally got seated inside the restaurant. We arrived a little early not knowing that Momo opened at 6, but that was no problem as one of the workers even let us sit a little bit early. I wish I got his name because he was so friendly! When it came time to order we got two Sapporo's, the rice croquettes, the party bomb, Hamachi roll, and the Salmon Guacamole roll. Everything was amazing, flavorful, and beautifully presented. We even asked for a second order of the spicy mc bomb. Prices are great, staff is great, no complaints! They do a great job of creating a "community" feel inside the restaurant, and I'm already awaiting my next return.

This place came recommended from two foodie friends of ours, so we decided to try it out last night. Â We were particularly excited given that it is a BYOB kind of place so we brought one of our favorite wine bottles. Â Food did not disappoint. Â The tuna tartare appetizer was particularly good and the escargot was delicious. Â There were other items on the menu that I wanted to try which I will have to save for next time. Â  The only drawback is that this restaurant is a no reservations, cash only place. Â Given the small, intimate environment of the restaurant, we were standing outside in the cold while we were waiting to be seated. Â We didn't wait long for a Saturday night (about 20 minutes), but I suggest going on an off night or for an early or late brunch if you want to try this place out.

Ok, so this is great pizza, no arguments there, but every time I pass it and want it, the place is closed. Â Also, I think it's about $5 for a slice. Â I don't care how good your pizza is... $5 for a slice??? Â  Â If you want to make the trip out there, make sure you find out their odd business hours 1st.

I've been wanting to try this place since about 2010! Â Crazy, right? Â I've just never made it until now. Â Lucky for me I was able to secure a restaurant week reservation. Â The restaurant is the next entrance to the hotel, the doorman will make sure you know where you're going and once you're inside it's definitely packed full of people. Â The space is a lot larger than expected as the space continues to the back of the building and the decor is very restoration hardware (me likes). Â  For restaurant week, they had two tasting menus, one at the normal restaurant week lunch price and the other priced as much as dinner. Â We decided to order off of both to try the best of both worlds. Â I started with the crostini di ceci, which had a bit of a kick to it. Â Then had the Taglioni neri which was light but delicious with every bite of mussel. Â For dessert I picked the olive oil cake, which came highly recommended from yelp. Â The cake was nice and reminded me of a cake I make. Â The other half ordered the octopus appetizer, which was omg, so good! Â The suckling pig with pasta as an entree, also equally as good and the semmifreddo for dessert. Â I don't eat at too many Italian restaurants b/c there's so many other great options in NY but this has definitely made it to one of my top picks. Â If only the prices were more wallet friendly. Â This kept us so full that we ended up not eating dinner that night!

It's cheap. They know how to make things Asian-grade spicy. The beef in the beef salad was not as tender or flavorful as I need it to be, but I'll forgive one flaw because everything else we ordered was packed with zest and yum. The most entertaining dish we had was the Southern Style Curry, which made us all sweat and blow our noses for the next half hour. The only thing to combat the burn is Thai iced tea, so you might want to order one in advance of a mega-spicy dish. It's nice that those clever Thai restauranteurs have a deli counter wait system, where you're given a number which is eventually shown on the marquee facing the street. But unfortunately I know of nothing fun to do in the immediate area while waiting, except to eat a pre-meal at El Mexicano across the street. p.s. - Vegetable-heads, I wouldn't trust this place to keep things fish sauce and meat-free. My guess is that they throw fish sauce into everything on autopilot.
It was ok not an A rated place

I came here for chicken and waffles at 9 AM on a Friday. Yes, any time is the right time for chicken and waffles. Smothered in butter and maple syrup, chicken as tender and juicy as can be. My stomach be growling just thinking about it.

My gf first introduced me to Galli a little over a year ago and we've been back a few times since. Â The staff has been wonderful to us. Â In addition, I believe the restaurant has a pretty cozy/intimate feel, and I especially love the exposed brick walls. Â Most importantly, the food is delicious. Â My gf has always loved the riceballs (as have I), and was pretty disappointed when she had to give them up when giving up meat. I've also tried their vodka pasta (I added chicken), as well as their chicken parm, with spaghetti and marinara sauce. Â Each time, the pasta was cooked perfectly - not too soft or hard - and the chicken was very well seasoned (I'd especially recommend the chicken parm). Â I haven't really tried their desserts yet (I'm always too stuffed from the food), but I intend to get to it one day soon.

Not sure what we were thinking trying to stroll in here w. 10 people. Â But, somehow it worked as we just waited in the corner until spots at the bar opened up. Â Beers were so cheap so it was worth waiting for the burger. Â Now, for the star of the show. Â We all had the bistro burger w. bacon and cheese. Â Tons of bacon, fresh lettuce, onions, tomatoes and a juicy burger. Â This was def very good but a bit underseasoned for me. Â I know, thats what the salt shaker is for but a finished product should always be a representation of the chef/cook and the establishment. Â Anyways, I'm glad I went as this place has been on my list for a while and now I can check it off. Â On to the next burger joint.....

got a lunch combo, katsu with egg on rice and udon. it's better than my friend's katsu with curry + udon, the pork was just too dry. I do like their noodles a lot, if only the broth had more flavor to it. Nothing special overall and the price is okay. I'd stick to onya next time.

They don't just do good cheesecake, they do good everything else! From the second we walked in the door to the second that we walked out, service was impeccable. These people know what they're doing and they are running this restaurant like a well-oiled machine. Granted we had to wait, but they told us how long (15 min) and didn't lie to us about the time. Got a great table, great waiter. Fast service. I got a turkey sandwich which was made with freshly roasted/carved turkey. Yum! My husband got a bacon cheeseburger which was delicious. Fries are thick cut and crispy. My son got a milkshake that was loaded with vanilla ice cream that had serious vanilla beans in it. It was tasty indeed. My husband got a piece of cheesecake to go - that traveled with us on the train back to Maryland. It was delicious! Very creamy. I've already told my sister to go there, the next time she visits NYC. Staff was very friendly. I will definitely go there again! I'm still dreaming of it.... :)

Opened early, this place is a nice spot for breakfast or brunch. The service was great and the atmosphere was nice, however the food was just ok for the price. Â  Note. Â I ordered a special short ribs benedict and thought that the regular eggs benedict was much better.

Tibetan food shows a major influence of Indian and Chinese methods of cooking but Yak in the other hand shows no type of excellence. i read many reviews of yak before going to eat there and thought the food would be mind blowing. i was very disheartened because i was looking for real tibetan food which reminded me of my home land. the food Chayley also known as beef tongue tasted stale and gummy. the rest of meal was very spicy and very oily or shall i say very greasy i had to order atleast 5 sodas because it was spicy. Â i know that the food is suppose to be spicy but if its to spicy the flavor of the food becomes spoiled and you cant enjoy the meal. waiters and waitress were everywher they seem to be lost but friendly. it took them about 30 min's just for them to bring out my soup. which tasted like milk and corn being warmed up . the decoration wasn't that bad. but i feel like they should reduce the spice and cook fresh food and not be giving customers stale food. after all we are paying for the food and i don't want to pay for a food that i have chances of getting sick with. the music or live band was very annoying it sounded like someone crying. they should try tib chants or inspiration songs that are more likely to smooth customers. i think i'll go back if ever decide to eat oily and very spicy food. but as for now i don't think so.
I love this place and I love its vibe. Â The cocktails are terrific, and I am grateful for the care that the mixologists put into their work. Â It's worth a try - especially on a quieter night.

This place is really hospitable. We had to wait in line for a table, which wasn't too bad because during the wait, they came by twice, once with cookies to snack on, and once with orange slices. They also gave everyone a glass of water. I got the steak and eggs. The ribeye was GREAT and cooked exactly like I ordered it, medium. The eggs were good. I also made the mistake of ordering a side of bacon. I say mistake because I thought it would have two or three pieces of bacon, not the 6-8 they brought out. While we were eating they came by with orange slices again. I also got a chocolate egg cream soda, which was really good. My food was really good, definitely worth 5 stars. My wife got the chicken chipotle omelette which is what I would get next time, simply because it is something I can't get anywhere else. My wife loved it, but couldn't finish it because of the large portion. I saw at another table someone got eggs florentine which I almost got because it looked so good. The waiter also gave us a cherry limeade on the house, which was also worth ordering. The service was great, my coffee cup was always full. We can't wait to come here again.

I sat at the bar and got a bloody mary whilst waiting for my friend to arrive. The drink was delicious and quite spicy. We got the spinach and artichoke dip to share as a starter. The texture of the dip is different than I'm used to - it's more just melted cheese on artichoke heart pieces, but I really enjoyed it this way. The pita bread went really well with the dip. I ordered the chicken pot pie and it was exactly what I needed on a cold night. It was warm, delicious and comfy. The waitress was very friendly and I enjoyed my experience here.
Nice and quiet cafe. Â I had scrambled egg. It was made fresh and fluffy.
awesome food. Â had to sit at bar because it was so busy. Â great music. Â a real pleasure to dine here.

Mediocre--lots of hype. I read quite a few reviews and decided to try Roberta's. I ordered the "Famous Original". Â First, the ingriedients are NOT certified organic, and not certain. Secondly, the pizza is like papa john style (small triangles) and not NY style pizza. Mine was priced at $13 (which is outrageous if you consider what you're getting and what you're paying for), and each additional topping ranged from $1-$4, which is incredible. Â The taste was OK. Â I will not be going back. There are far too many pizza options to settle for this over priced hype. I am happy to pay the extra cost for organic ingredients and to support local venues, this one can do Â A LOT better.

Went here for lunch and it wasn't too packed so the vibe was very relaxed and almost home-like. I ordered the rabbit crostini for appetizer and I was amazed at how flavorful and delicious it was. My main dish, which was a tagliatelli, on the other hand was just alright. I liked the atmosphere of the place; it was very casual to a point, which I'm assuming is the vibe the place is going for. I would definitely come back again for the crostini and perhaps order another dish next time.

This is my go to spot for Filipino Food in Manhattan since Elvys closed SMH :-( The lumpia shanghai are great here. Â Also I like the topsilog and longsilog and the barbeque pork and BBQ chicken. I also love the sisig, kare kare, and the crispy pata. For dessert try the halo halo, the flan is the best you can find in NYC, and the ube ice cream is so so good. Best Filipino restaurant in NYC!!!!

the ramen war continues... as a lot of reviewers have commented, the broth here is less "porky" than ippudo's. Â it gives your ramen experience a very different taste. i think i may default to ippudo's simply because it's south of 14th street. Â hey if i have to stand in line an hour for ramen, i might as well do it downtown.

Very cool atmosphere, friendly waitstaff, good food. I must admit that it might be a tad over hyped... The handrolls were small, the premixed wasabi soy had no kick (even in the most potent mix, which just tasted chalky) the guacamole roll could use more guacamole, and I'm not sure where the risotto balls really fit in the menu... I still would like to try the "bombs" which I will definitely go back for. Â In all, Momo Sushi is a great place to take your friends but I wouldn't become a regular.

What a great place. We left a well known restaurant and headed down the street exploring. We happened into carroll place and what a find. The space is great with giant candle chandeliers (how do they light them) and a classy pub feel. We only had appetizers but they were so good. Â We will be back for full meals.

I am not cool enough for Williamsburg, or most Williamsburg establishments. I find most of them over the top and packed with such vapidity to the point where I shy away from any place located anywhere even NEAR Bedford Avenue. I just can't hack it. Like I said, I'm not cool. A boyfriend wanted me to go with him to meet his sister at Rabbithole earlier this year, and I grudgingly went because I loved him. I read reviews first, and held my breath when he opened the door for me, expecting to have a Total Eclipse of the Heart while awkwardly sipping on something with a high alcohol content and wishing for it all to be over. But no! Rabbithole is a surprisingly charming treasure of a restaurant, and the romantic and elegant, yet cozy ambiance drew me right away. I can't seem to stop going back. The decor is on point, the food is delicious, and the service is... well, serviceable. I sit at the bar whenever I go, and am never disappointed by my experience here. Even when hipsters are sucking face in the corner. I have yet to be present for any specials, so I've paid full price for everything. Happily. Prices are extremely reasonable for the quality of food and the ambiance, making Rabbithole the one place I frequent that I don't intentionally go to during Happy Hour. I have ordered only one thing that I found to be "okay"-- an espresso chocolate cake. Otherwise, I find myself completely and thoroughly pleased every time I eat here. The portions are always perfect, no matter what you order. Not too much, not too little. The Earl Grey creme brulee is a must. Following my break-up with the aforementioned boyfriend, I credit sharing this with his sister on the frequent with helping me get the fuck over it. It's impossible to think about anything other than the creamy decadence of this naughty little dish while it's in your mouth. Go eat some. Now. The chocolate chip cookies, while not the most interesting offering, provide consistent comfort in their buttery, crisp-but-chewy bliss. The quinoa-rice salad ordered with grilled chicken is bafflingly tasty. I'm not even a fan of quinoa, but when I split this with a friend I find that I have to practice restraint while eating it. The steak salad is to die for, and I could eat it forever. The lamb burger, ordered medium, is the go-to for those times when you just want something amazing and filling without thinking about it. It comes with an elegant little cucumber salad that you'll be tempted to order more of. Don't-- save room for the creme brulee. The drink prices are a bit deterrent, so I find myself ordering iced tea more often than anything else. They have an inconsistently brewed jasmine green that is either okay or deliciously quaffable and perfect in every way. If I'm feeling spendy, I'll spring for the orange white wine they have, which is indeed worth the $10 or $13 per glass price tag. The service is unremarkable one way or another, which to me is A-OK. Come for the food and the ambiance and you won't be disappointed.

Went on a Monday night of a long weekend so the place was quiet, which was totally fine with me because we had plenty of bartender attention. Enjoyed my drinks - one gin with an amaro liquer and the other was a lavender infused martini. The company I was with didn't hurt - a long time friend who i hadn't seen in awhile... good place to chat and catch up. Back to the subject of bartenders, I enjoyed not only my friend's company but theirs as well. They were enjoying themselves and were amusing to interact with.

I had a chance to visit New York City the past week. I've read and heard a lot about this place. We went in relatively late on a Monday night with a group of 7. Â I was surprised to find that we were seated right away - I should note that it was the only table available, but it happened to seat up to 8. Also, luckily for us, they had one spare Bo Ssam meal left (you usually need to order in advance). We pounced on that opportunity. Â We also ordered some drinks and a few orders of the now world famous Pork Buns. The Pork Buns are famous for a reason - they are melt in your mouth good!!! Â It really is difficult to wrap your mind around how they can manage to have such a thick cut of pork melt right in your mouth like that. Â Really, really great stuff. Next came out the all of the side dishes - probably their iteration of Korean Ban Chan. Â Lettuce for wraps, Kimchi, Kimchi Puree, Red pepper paste, Scallions, Rice, Sea Salt, and a Dozen Oysters. After a few minutes of anticipation, the star of the show came out - the Whole Pork Butt. Â It was so tender and juicy...it literally fell apart on contact. Â With all of the side items, there were many different combinations to try out - all were delicious. Â However, for me, the best combo was this: A small portion or rice, Pork butt, Oyster, and Kimchi wrapped in lettuce. It was perfection. At the end of the meal I realized we just consumed a very pork-heavy meal. But they do pork right. And it was delicious. Â So who cares? Bottom line - grab a group of people and book a Bo Ssam meal. It really is that good!

I love my neighborhood, but aside from a couple of hole-in-the-wall Chinese places, I didn't think there was any vegetarian food to be had. I just found this place on Grubhub tonight, and I am SO happy. The delivery was prompt, the food so fresh- my soy chicken and vegetables Â was delicious, not oversauced or greasy, the vegetables varied and colorful and perfectly cooked, and my salad with avocado came with a fantastic side of carrot-miso dressing. I am going to eat my way through this menu! Thanks so much for an amazing dinner!

Came here on a friday night for dinner with friends and I enjoyed every aspect of El Almacen. - The decor has that hipster/old history style with lots of trinkets and random collections along the walls - The place is tightly packed, so be prepared to be sitting right on top of your neighbors. - The service was fine, nothing to rave about and nothing to complain about FOOD: Simply delicious. - The hamachi appetizer with truffle oil and the fried avocado appetizer are must orders! Both were delicious and there was enough of each for 4 people - All of the entrees were well received by my group. I loved the braised short ribs and loved how the meat melted off of the bone. The stuffed pepper was also loved and the ox tail pasta was a huge hit. If you're a meat lover, then I highly recommend you stop by El Almacen

4.5 stars. I was here twice. The first time with three friends of mine, and ordered their tasting menu, mostly seafood. Although they bring you bites, we were served a total of 13 small dishes, and got up stuff. The $40 deal is absurdly good. Spicy edamame: very interesting. Duck: very good. Sea urchin with mushroom sauce: I'm not a fan of sea urchin, but this bite was heavenly. My favorite dish of the dinner. Pork belly: even people who don't appreciate pork belly will love this, because it's not too fatty, and deliciously crisp. Ceviche (can't remember which type): just a spoonful, but very good. Vegetarian melted cheese: I wish we had chosen the meat tasting menu, because it would have beautifully complemented this dish, which was great even by itself. Octopus: the sauce was tasty, but the octopus itself very bland. Brussel sprouts: awesome. They came in a sweet sauce with grapes and were truly memorable. Merluzzo fish (not sure) in white wine sauce: super flavorful. Loved the sauce so much I wanted to lick the dish. Fried fish: the weak dish of the dinner. The fish itself was too heavy and not particularly memorabl; and it made me a little nauseous. Churros: delicious. Pan con chile and chocolate: not my thing, but it's just a matter of taste. Many people don't like the combo of tastes, so maybe they should choose a different dessert. Spicy chocolate bites: the bite from God you want to have to end a dinner in style. Overall, an amazing deal. Not everything was delicious, but the price makes it for the imperfections. Totally worth another trip, also because the service was awesome, very professional, and the place itself is very cute. My second time was epic. My gf and I were served 15 dishes, this time meat-oriented: most of them were much bigger than just tastes. Chips with cheese and hot sauce: simple, but tasty. Shrimp ceviche: kinda tasteless. Gordita with goat meat: fabulous. Duck wrapped in lettuce: deliciuos Foie gras: unreal; truly memorable; never had anything like it. Lamb tongue: so tender it could melt in your mouth. Meatballs: yummy. Corn soup: ok. Sweetbreads: together with the ceviche, the only dish that wasn't up to the level of everything else. Octopus: very tasty. Braised short rib: amazingly soft, and wonderfully complemented by the tortilla-based spread. Pork belly: fantabulous. flan with raspberry sauce: the perfect dessert to change and revive the palate; delicate, light and refreshing. Churros: fluffy and perfectly fried. Chile chocolate: great closure to an outstanding meal. We were absolutely stuffed, but as happy as we could be. Unbelievable value, especially because of the variety of meats, many of which really exotic. I can't wait to go back for more. This place is real! :)

It's just not a trip to New York without stopping at The Halal Guys cart at 53rd and 6th. I start craving the lamb platter as soon as I know I'm headed to the city... oh, such tasty goodness! And - to get a full meal (more than I can eat) for $6... rad!

Great place, with delicious food and lots of space. Â Totally unexpected in the wasteland of Times Square. Â Happy hour prices are great, but really, not THAT much of a difference for the food..50% off drinks is great though. I went with three other friends and I think we ended up paying like 160 dollars total. Â While not super pricey, for happy hour prices, I think it still ended up being a little expensive. Â  Everything, both bbq and not-bbq, was amazing. Â Make sure to get any of the several different types of kalbi, the hot oil seared salmon, as well as the hangar steak. Â Even the ramen was delicious, and it's not even a ramen joint! Â  I think if you came in with a large group, happy hour would actually be a better deal.

if your Italian friend tell you it's a great pizza, you better trust him ;) the pizza is crispy, think and you can taste the fresh mozzarella all over the pizza. the Vodka sauce on a pizza is light and tasty. don't forget the to get the bruschetta for appetizer. Friendly waiters and nice pizzeria. This is the place I diffidently go again to discover their wonderful pizza or great sandwiches again.

After moving from Texas a few years ago, I have been scouring the city for good Mexican food. Usually the versions that cross my lips are gentrified tacos and bland burritos, until now. De Mole makes great food typical of the northern states of Mexico. All of the food was fresh, tasty and extremely well prepared. Tamales were a good balance of masa and filling, the taco's are perfect size full of great fillings, the quesadillas are a fantstic "fried taco" version typical of central Mexico. Get yourself to this tiny little establishment and you will be happy.

Came in here for Sunday brunch a few weeks ago. In the grand scheme of New York City, its nothing spectacular, but a nice classic neighborhood joint offering a standard brunch menu in a friendly, trendy atmosphere. I got the smoked salmon eggs benedict, which was the most reasonably priced I had seen in the city. The discount stopped at the price however; the dish itself was quite good. I would definitely return.

I went to Cuba for lunch on Monday and the place was completely empty. My friend and I both ordered the Ropa Vieja (the braised skirt steak). The dish had a good amount of beef in it and was presented scrumptiously. The braised skirt steak was well cooked, but i felt like it was lacking a kick or something else to bring out the flavor from the tomatoes and pepper. I personally thought it was a little too much meat for lunch and didn't finish half of it. Maybe it is time to have some lunch specials at this place.

There was about a 20 minute wait for a party of 2 around 830 which wasn't bad at all. Â A lot of people were hanging around the bar watching the Yankees game. Â The atmosphere in there was louder than expected. Â Once seated, the waiter greeted us with all the specials. Â We ended up ordering the chicken wing appetizer which look cool with the little grill accompanying it. Â The new york strip steak was cooked perfectly. Â Crunchy skin with a moist, juicy inside. Â The string beans were fresh and crunchy and french fries were just right. Â My girlfriend has the sweet and spicy catfish which was pretty good. Â Skip the desert and your bill is around $70. Â Like one reviewer said, they do keep refilling your cup of water when least expected. Â I will come here again, hopefully when they have pre fixed menus.

This is a really laid back, low key, intimate place that's great for hanging with a small group of friends or a date. Fortunately I've never had an issue with finding a seat, but I can imagine this could be quite a task considering the smaller size of the place. I've never eaten here so I can't speak to the food, however the wine and beer selection is great, the bartenders are personable and nice, and the music (which I learned is an ipod), is perfect for the atmosphere.......rarely do you hear the Beatles followed by En Vogue and say "wow, that works"

You know those nights where you want to have an upscale dinner, but you unfortunately can't eat too much because your dress won't permit a muffin top? Alta is perfect for those nights. Or you know those nights where you want to treat your lady to a nice dinner, but you're severely restricted by her weird, carb-free, calorie-free diet and you're tired of eating sushi? Alta is perfect for those nights. I was first introduced to this restaurant via a date - I was having both of those aforementioned nights - and I've been coming back here ever since. This is a great spot when I wish to have a nice dinner with friends since it's so accessible to EVERYONE. Â The restaurant is conveniently located near the West 4th stop and the PATH 9th street stop. If there are availabilities in seating, request to sit upstairs. Â The view is nicer, and it's less noisy than the downstairs dining area. Â  For food, I'd recommend the following items: 1) Crispy Brussel Sprouts ($11.50) 2) Lamb Meatballs - ($9) 3) Steak Tartare ($14) 4) Braised Octopus, Carrot & Rainbow Radish Salad ($13) 5) Spaghetti Pepperoncini ($15) 6) Bacon Wrapped Dates & Olives ($7) 7) Scallop Ceviche ($8) 8) Roasted Pork Belly Confit ($18) *Drinks* 9) Ginger Mojito ($12) ... so good, I ordered 2 more glasses of this... 10) Sicilian ($12) Note: the restaurant only accepts Amex or Cash as forms of payment. Â I'd advise you to go with the Amex route, as I've never paid less $100 for a dinner here (just for myself).

Best curry I've had in a while! I didn't know this place was so popular. The food is fantastic - cheap and delicious. I would highly recommend the curry with pork cutlet. The curry is darker in color than Korean curry and is so much more flavorful. And the pork cutlet is nicely breaded and fried. It also comes with a side of salad. The only downside of this place would be the size - there are only two tables with 5 seats on each table. But that isn't a dealbreaker for me. Call ahead and take it to go to.

Mr Fishy made a bfast reservation and arrived on time. Although the restaurant was almost empty, they seated us in the worst possible spot, right by the door. We asked to be moved and they found the second worst spot, right by the waiters station where we were eye to eye with the waiter's butts (should I say eye to butt?). We asked to be moved again (in the large and empty restaurant there were plenty of choices!) and they finally gave us an ok place to sit. Not sure what motivated their behavior, but there are a lot of other restaurants to choose from in NYC, and I will not be coming back!

Went here for dessert with two friends which was the first mistake: This place is obviously a brunch place. We ended up splitting the chocolate fondue and poffertjes - both had a fine (albeit subtle) taste but the portions were much smaller than I imagined and left us unsatisfied. Granted I don't expect huge portions in New York but I did expect the fondue to be more substantial. So I wouldn't come back for dessert necessarily but I would consider getting brunch here.
I just bought a cheese pizza here, this is delicious but need to improve customer service.

Is it just us or what? Me and my family dine here and we all agree that the food is toooooooo salty! we ordered the crab toast and the lunch prix fixe menu and the meatball pasta. the crab toast is good but not like insanely or heavenly good described by other reviewers.... all the other dishes (actually include the crab toast) are super salty. I have a hard time eating my meatball pasta... and the sea salted caramel ice crea...same..it's just...OK.... only good thing is their service, very attentive and well trained... was very disappointed...maybe because i expected too much :/

I don't like writing negative reviews, but I'm going to anyway. Â Food was pretty good, but you would think this place could have figured out how to give reasonably good service after being open for so many years! I know this place has never been know for good service and you don't Â eat there for the service, but bringing out food Â in a timely manner and hot isn't too much to ask. Â When the tables around you already have their food and they sat 15 minutes after you, it is a little irritating. Â I asked 2 times about the food and was given a B.S. answer about why it came out so late. Â  Hard to understand how others got their food when a stove was supposedly broken. Also, you shouldn't have to ask for the check 3 times! Â I don't like leaving a lousy tip, but how else do you get a restaurant to improve? I like their food but won't be patronizing them again. Â Plenty of other Â Thai places in Queens that have just as good food if not better and know how to give good service. Â Try Ayada Thai instead

My girlfriend and I absutely love coming here. We always have an extremely long wait but we don't care. We just post up in the back bar area and have a thousand drinks until our name is called. What a fun atmosphere. You can also order food while you wait so if your girlfriend gets cranky when she's hungry you won't have a problem. Great drink selection, great charcuterie, cool vibe, great tunes. Now the food. Absolutely best pizza on the planet. I think all the reviews must say that. Something about their bread and toppings. Gotta stand in the front and just watch the cooks making the pizza in the oven. It's mesmerizing. Now a word to the wise: THE PASTA IS AMAZING!!! Ask which pastas are homemade and order all of them. Do not sleep. Also the ribs are shadily unreal. I hear the burger is amazing at lunch but I won't really have an opportunity to come at lunch ever unfortunately. Anyway, to the folks at Roberta's, we love you!

I don't often give 5 stars and I feel it's lame when reviewers do. Cut the crap, it should be an excellent without a doubt the best place you've been to. None of this "it was really good but...." then give them 4 to 5 Stars...4 to 5 Stars is for a restaurant that is a standout, a must go to place where you are not disappointed in the least. This place hands down deserves all 5 of my Stars. I went with 3 other friends and we each tried different sandwiches, amazing! There is a wait but it is so, so worth it. The photos uploaded by other reviewers so true! Thank you, thank you! I dream about your sandwiches and thank my waistline that I do not work near you or my hips would be in sooo much trouble. I can't wait to go back!

Came here for drinks, I like the vibe in here. It's very casual, but it gets pretty cramp since the space is small. Â As soon as you walk in, bam! the bar is right in front of you. Â If you want to get seated on a table, you have to walk through what reminds me of a hallway with tables on the left side. Â I usually love going to hole in the wall spots, but for a gastropub personally I found the place too cramp. Maybe it's just me, check it out you may have a different opinion. Â  The service was great. Â Even though the place was packed, the waitress was very friendly and came up to our group from time to time to ask if we needed anything. Â I tried the chicharon bulaklak (crispy ruffle fat). Â I'm filipino so I love the chicharon, but I found their version extremely oily to a point that it prohibited me from enjoying it. Â As for the drinks, my group got the San Miguel Beer 6 pack which cost $30 and mixed drinks for $7-9, the mixed drinks were delicous but not strong. Â Overall, I wouldn't come here only for drinks because it would only leave me broke and not even buzzed. Â I haven't tried any of their entrees so I can't say anything about that. Â I do want to try their kamayan thursday (no plates, no silverware) because basically you have to eat with your hands served in banana leaves. Â It's definitely a filipino thing which I think everyone should try, it makes the food taste even better. Â P.S You have to make reservations if you want to try kamayan thursday.

I'll preface that I have never been, and always had it delivered. Some food doesn't travel well, it just doesn't. Theirs does! My favorite lunchtime menu to order from. Pick something, anything and it will be delicious. I'm known to order the Octopus with Spinach Noodles. Tons of octopus and the green sauce is to die for.

came with groupon coupon....still end up spending waay too much. Â quality of food is less than other nearby competitive chinese fondue restaurants. Â This place has a YOUNG, HIP americanized atmosphere, thus the popularity among the young americanized asian patrons. Â For serious diners who want Â good authentic chinese fondue....SKIP IT....and go around the block instead.

Hands down one of the best falafel places in the lower east side, let alone the entire Manhattan area. **Best time to visit to avoid the rush is 4pm! P.S. Not many places to sit so go eat outside at the park nearby
Great food, especially the most decadent ricotta panna cotta. They're only losing a star because the waitress took away my daughter's coloring pages when the food came and "let me pitch these" :(

I have long wanted to try this Japanese ramen restaurant and finally was able to stop by for a visit. Like many ramen places, the line was out of this world, but as a single diner I was fortunate to grab a seat at the large communal table as soon as I arrived. The venue was larger than expected. It encompassed a wait area, an open kitchen, and several large tables surrounded by booths that reached from one wall to another. The decor was unlike many dark and eclectic ramen places I know, it was rather trendy, hipsterish, and accompanied by servers and ramen chefs who were oddly not Japanese. I started off with the Tako Wasabi ($5) that came in a small cup filled with chopped raw baby octopus served with a smudge of wasabi, salty mustard, a slice of lemon, and mint leaf. Serving was small, but the Tako Wasabi had great texture as the wasabi flavor was sharp but pleasant to complement the subtle salty lemony minty flavors in every bite. I recommend it. My ramen, Akamaru Modern ($15), consisted of tonkotsu broth, umami dama miso paste, pork chasiu, cabbage, sesame kikurage mushrooms, scallions, and garlic oil. The broth had decent flavor with enough lift coming from the cabbage and scallions, but the deep tonkotsu flavor did not render the savory creamy marble broth that I was searching for. I was hoping that the toppings could supplant the lack of depth in the broth, but the added soft-boiled egg ($2) did not have enough seasoning and the charsiu was cut rather small for the price. Service was hands-off and brief. For $17, I was expecting a lot more than what I would get from cheaper and better places such as Tsujita, Santouka, Daikokuya, Robata Jinya, and Totto Ramen. It was overall still a decent meal but the outrageous cost brought the rating down to a 3 star rating. I will be sticking to Totto Ramen on my next trip to NYC.

I would starve without this place. Â  24 hour delivery Assorted bites Assorted drinks Great sandwiches The only drawback is the guy who answers the phone can be really nasty sometimes. Â But that can all be forgotten as soon as I hear the knock on my door and my food is here! Â  I love this place!

Last night I hosted my bday dinner here for 12 which is a large feat for this tiny place. I had been here once before and really loved the atmosphere and (more importantly) the food and drinks! I called a few days in advance for a reservation and was ready to be turned down b/c the place is so small and I had already gotten a big fat no from 2 other larger places, but to my surprise they happily agreed. The also called me the day of the reservation to confirm. The waitress was very patient w/ our party as many of us had a hard time making a decision between all the yummy options, and w/ the fact that a few people showed up late. The drinks were great! Even though happy hour ended at 7 :( damn!! I had the passionfruit and mint mojito and sampled some of the lime and jalapeno caipirinha (pretty hot). The food was AWESOME! I had the crab and garlic dip and the skillet shrimp and lemon appetizers, along with the chicken and mango curry, and the chocolate Guinness cake. The apps were sooooo good, the curry was very light and not as spice-heavy as the indian type. I could only manage 2 bites of the cake as I was stuffed and my skirt was very tight, but it was not too rich or overly sweet which I really like. I also got to sample the seafood stew which was not very stew-ish and more like a heavy saute of seafood but was really good. All in all I love the portion sizes, the food is good without being overly flavored, and it's very affordable. Great place for a date or drinks!!

Dark, secretive, cozy and refined -- this place has the proper allure of a delightful little speakeasy. The drinks are kind of pricey however, so it's best to come during Happy Hour (although expect there to be a crowd).

I was excited to try Bar Bacon and went with a group on Friday night. Â  Let me say first, that the bacon I had was excellent. Â  We sat at the bar and got served pretty quickly at first. Â  My two disappointments were the food I ordered. Â I ordered the Bar Bacon cornbread. Â When It arrived there was no bacon in it. Â  I expected it to have bacon, but I guess I should have asked before ordering. Â The cornbread is not served warm and there was no butter. This tiny restaurant needs an expansion. Since the write up in magazines and the papers hipster have flooded a once peaceful hole in the wall restaurant along Forsyth Street all wanting a taste. The owner a jovial plump Chinese woman who mans the cashier at the back of the restaurant. Prior to this it was just her and one other and a cook but on a recent visit she has gained two additional help. Â Even then it is slow going if the place is packed. This is a no frills service here. It is about the food. You get greasy paper carry-out menus to order or the pictures on the wall for those who need more help. You get your own drinks from the refrigerator. The food can take a bit to come out if it is busy. If you have had similar food from the Henan region of China you will recognize it. It is spicy, lots of flavor from cumin, anise and red peppers with usual protein of lamb, chicken beef and fish. The Spicy Big Tray of chicken is exactly what it says. A tray of chicken full of a spicy oily broth abundantly flavorful and full of heat . It is plenty enough to share for two. Make sure to order the noodles as it doesn't come with it. The pancake with lamb is wonderfully delicious but filling. The ox tail soup with rice is plenty awesome for those you love gnawing on bones and sucking off the meaty morsels. For now this is my favorite Henan cuisine spot away from the other popular chain got notoriety by a certain TV host. It is a no frills all food and even the busiest they never rush you out. Chinese service with sort of a smile. I'll take it!
Love this place!!!! Peasant salad... Grilled Squid.. MMmmMM.. It is absolutely delicious!!!

My favorite Thai place in NYC. Pokpok used to be packed and it is still is, but it's not a two hour wait like it used to be. I come on weekdays and I wait for 10 min max. I kind of like the old space better but the food is as consistent. Spicy wings a must!!! Also the sticky rice, Minced duck spicy but so good, the pork neck has been change to wild boar and it's the same preparation and even better. The eggplant dish is Devine. For dessert if your mouth is burned and need a little cooling take the affogato. Will always go back there sometimes I just crave some pokpok

An epicurean delight; best restaurant in NYC hands down. The menu is a chow hound's delight. Super amazing! The ambience. The interior decorating. The service was beyond impeccable. The food...can't even begin to describe the Porcini Flan, the soups, the duck, the desserts. Stellar!

Good wine and beer selection and considering it's in NYC the price is fair.

Were here last night after reading the great reviews and was very disappointed. Â The food was good not great and our service was terrible. I've had breakfast at Balthazar a few times before heading into the office. It was pretty empty both times I went which was nice, since this place tends to attract the tourist population. Were just a buncha college kids on a budget looking for delicious drunk food. Bam. The search is over forever.
so very good. vegetarian pita. every time. the hummus is divine.

I was brought here by a friend. He's a college student fairly new to the area whose friends are all college students, so naturally I expected that this guy knew nothing what real food was. Staff was nice. Great atmosphere. Lots of seating. Chicken and waffles were good, but could have been more seasoned for my taste. Very pricy for the amount of food. The mixed drinks were not good - iced tea one was too watery and the purple drank was way to sweet.

This is a wonderful and cozy restaurant in the heart of SoHo. I had been wanting to visit for some time but the wait was always a bit long. Â I finally went with some friends and we all agreed that it was totally worth waiting for. Â  One of the best burgers in the city for sure.
i just wish that had even one vegan option on the menu. Â sure, its my choice to be vegan and i dont have to go to this restaurant, but it'd be nice. Â its not that hard.

The first time that I went here I didn't think that the food was so great, but the second time it was actually quite good and I have cravings for this food now. Â It was also very reasonably priced. Â I am definitely going back and bringing others!

We love this place. It is great, I have my fries with no added salt on top and love them. The truffle oil mayo is yummy. The house sauce has ketchup, mayo and onion. Mango curry yummy too. Oh....Em....Gee! A few of my friends had mentioned how great Uva was in the past. Update to remove a star. Food & service no longer 5 star but still good.

I'm from Seattle, where we have Thai restaurants a stone's throw away from wherever you happen to be. And I have to say, I really loved this restaurant. I'll start off with my only complaint, which is that their hours are not clear. They were still serving people 15-20 minutes before their "closing" time, which struck me as odd. It was really busy... but that's not a bad thing! Usually a sign of good food, so I was fine waiting for my food. We took our meal to go. I got Pad See Ew with calamari, which is wide noodles with various stir-fried vegetables. Calamari was cooked well, not too chewy. I was really pleased. We also ordered egg roles. Plum sauce was good, although I would've liked it to be a little tangier. Personal preference -- otherwise it was good. Nothing to blow your mind. Unfortunately, I don't remember what my brother ordered. Quick service, inexpensive, close to the theatre district and great reviews... maybe it's not something you HAVE to try while visiting New York, but if you have a thai food craving and are near the area, it's worth dropping by. Hopefully you can find a seat!
Food was good, although portions were small. Â The biggest surprise, though, is that they don't take any credit cards! Â There is an ATM machine in the restaurant, but it charges a fee of $1.75.

Decor: 4/5 -very southern feel with the white walls, large windows and dim lighting -only one washroom so there might be a wait -there are tables that can accomodate 4 and one large table that appeared to accomodate a dozen Service: 4/5 -Fairly good overall, didn't have to request for water once and the dishes came out in timely intervals Food: 3/5 -Complimentary Honey Popovers were super fluffy and to my surprise tasted better than they looked. They were cooked to a golden brown then drizzled with honey. Eat bite I couldn't help but think that I'm eating an Eggo waffle -The cornbread ($4) by itself was decent but add the chile-lime butter and wow, I could eat only cornbread the whole dinner. Yummy! -The flatbread ($12) tasted just like its ingredients: buttermilk ricotta, flowery with a hint of lemon. I wish the bread was a bit more crispy though. -Buttermilk fried chicken ($22) had a peppered seasoned skin that was thick and crispy. The white meat was surprisingly not dry but not as juicy and tender as Bobwhite. Three pieces with waffles and coleslaw for $22 is a bit fancy. I suggest spending that much at Bobwhite instead. -Duck Meatloaf ($24) was my favorite of the night. Distinct duck taste with a perfect meatloaf consistency though I couldn't help but think that when divided into four quarters, each bite was $6.

Some of the best Italian food I've had in the city. Came for my cousin's birthday dinner with his friends. The interiors were extremely nice, table setting was elegant, romantic and we had a great time being seated upstairs along with 3 other tables celebrating birthdays(which each table respectively broke into happy birthday songs at some point during the night!) We had great appetizers, including some of the best buffala di mozzarella I've tried. Bread was very good with olive oil. I had the house made gnocchi which was just melt in your mouth. The rest of the party had scrumptious lamb specials, seafood linguine etc. For dessert we tried cake and an amazing tartufo. We also had delightful bottles of Cabernet and Italian Lambrusco. Food and wine was excellent and fresh, made to order. Not to mention the exceptional service and knowledge of our waiters and sommelier was a great touch. Though pricey, I was honestly shocked at how good the service and food was in the middle Times Square, usually filled with tourist trap restaurants, and that says a lot being lined up next to Olive Gardens. I'm also a native of Manhattan. I would willingly come back again.
My girlfriend and I had dinner there and everything was great! The woman who was our waitress couldn't have been better and food was wonderful! We will be back!

Dear Hearth, I will always remember you as being the worst meal for the money, Ive had in New York, in the past ten years. The service is bad. The food, only okay and totally overpriced. The ambiance is nice, but unmemorable. Â  When I dined, with and Italian from Sardegnia, a Coffee Roaster from Seattle, and an Editor from Conde Nast, they couldn't have done any worse. Mediocre over-salted food, sloppy service and either understaffed, or the staff can't handle the frenzy of a full restaurant. good brunch. Â good bloody mary's. Â Nice decor. Very attentive service.

Grew up in Jamaica and the really good jerk chicken places are right off the side of the road. You pull up, get your jerked whatever wrapped in foil, a piece of hard-dough bread, some pepper sauce and that's heaven. Glady's is just like those roadside places...except really cutely designed, with great music, and real silverware. We had the jerked half chicken, oxtails, rice and peas and plantains. We came during lunch so maybe that's why we had to order at the counter and pick up our food on a tray cafeteria style? I assume they wait on you during dinner hours... Everything was delicious. Jerk chicken was juicy, smokey and well spiced (fear not, pepper-phobic friends, the spice level is tolerable and you can always add more heat with their table sauces); oxtails were tender and in this amazing rich sauce (a little different from my Grandma's); rice and peas were nice; and plantains, sweet and perfectly pan friend. We left full and happy. See you again, Glady's!

This is a rad neighborhood destination for good food. I love their Bloody's wiith a good breakfast... My favorite thing is that the menu changes daily which keeps it fresh and encourages me to come back for more. We try to head over at 11:30 on the weekend to beat the rush - works every time!

This is the ideal spot for a nightcap. Remember what nightcaps are? That's what Dean Martin used to say in a red silk smoking jacket in one of his cheesy 1960's comedies. It was basically a euphemism for an anticipated roll in the hay with some unsuspecting starlet who turned out to be a virgin from his hometown. That was probably Shirley MacLaine at her perky pixie peak. I don't think anybody uses that archaic term anymore, but it would fit here. I mean the libation part of the term, not the roll in the hay, as they serve these decadent $12.50 Espresso Martinis that made me feel like Lee Remick just before booze took over her life and her looks in "The Days of Wine and Roses". Too many baby boomer movie references? Sorry... My colleague Stephanie suggested coming to her favorite watering hole after our wonderful dinner at the Lion nearby. She lives just up the block, so it was the perfect place for us to chill and chat about life, work and all points in between. The space is small and low-key, and on a weeknight around 9PM, pretty darn quiet with only a few customers chatting up the bartender at the back-lit bar. We sat at a table for two, and Stephanie knew to order those martinis. Just sweet enough with an eventual horse kick. OK, we had two rounds, we just couldn't help it. Like I said, I was Lee Remick, so she must have been Jack Lemmon. I thought I'd be up all night, but the alcohol must have burned off the caffeine...that's my story and I'm sitcking to it. At least she only had half a block to walk. Cab!...CAB!! DRINKS - 4 stars...espresso martinis are not on my flexitarian diet...285 calories each...oy! AMBIANCE - 4 stars...low-key vibe makes me want to hangout for hours which we may have done...I don't remember SERVICE - 3.5 stars...the bartender came by to see if we were still conscious, I think TOTAL - 4 stars...good thing I don't live in the 'hood...I would go from "The Days of Wine and Roses" right to "Barfly"

Dining at the Ssam Bar had been one of my most anticipated events of this New York trip. This restaurant nestled on the corner of 13th and 2nd was perhaps one of the most talked about restaurants led by one of America's hottest chefs of 2009. Unfortunately the restaurant was actually a huge let down in my eyes. My friends Andrew Kwon and Louise Zhao who accompanied me for this late lunch/early dinner ultimately agreed with my assessment. Overall, the food was lackluster and it's only saving grace was the fact that the pork buns which we ordered as an appetizer was absolutely delicious and well thought out. The seasonal fried brussel sprouts which we ordered as a side to our appetizer were also good as well but tended to be overwhelmingly oily. The Bev Eggleston's pork shoulder steak was boring and poorly seasoned, the angus hanger steak with cauliflower and almonds was nothing new or innovative, and the spicy rice cakes with pork sausage and Chinese broccoli should have shamed David Chang's Korean mother. This is your take on Korea's dokboki? Come on David.

I joined Yelp today SPECIFICALLY to talk about this restaurant and how deliciously amazing the brunch is. My gf and I started off by splitting the herring, which was impeccable, served with a delicious sauce and some sort of cracker. Â We don't usually get appetizers for brunch, but we wanted to try as much as possible! For our entree, I had the Black Label burger (obviously) served medium rare, and I'm not even kidding that it was the best burger I've had in my entire life. Â The burger itself was almost crunchy on the outside, but the quality of the meat was incredibly savory. Â The bun was buttery and delicious and sopped up all the meat juice. Â Absolutely perfect. My gf had the shirred eggs, which were also delicious. Â The eggs had a great baked consistency, and were cheesy and gooey-- perfect with the bread served on the side. For dessert, we split the pots de creme, which were essentially three little pots of mousse-- chocolate, vanilla, and coffee. Â They were served with two crispy little sweet wafers that were perfect for dipping. Â All mousses were creamy and delectable. Â The perfect size, too, for something small and sweet to split after the meal. We finished off with a round of drinks. Â I had the Kentucky Dawn-- an orangey, espresso-y cocktail that was way better than it sounds. Â It almost tasted like one of those chocolate oranges, except way more refreshing. Â She had the French Toast Flip, which tasted just like french toast, except in a creamy martini form. The service was awesome-- we both agreed that our waiter was just the right amount of "there", always around when we wanted him but not annoying or trying to pressure us to order more. Â I also appreciated it that we were there lingering for two hours, and no one was asking us or hinting to leave. Â  I have to admit, the meal was a bit pricey-- $140 after tax for brunch, which is something I've never spent on a meal-- but the service, ambience, and food were worth the price tag. Â I'd gladly trade three mediocre brunches across town for one delicious brunch at Minetta Tavern. Make yourself a reservation NOW! Â The wait might be a few weeks long, but trust me.. it's worth it.

If anyone doubts the capacity to elevate ramen, you'll be made a believer at Ippudo. The great design of the space, the highly attentive service (we had 2 babies under 1 year old in tow and they offered booster chairs and other child friendly items pro actively), and the authentic vibe set the stage very early on. The pork buns were definitely flavorful but somewhat heavy handed, personally. I'm used to a hole in the wall in Chinatown churning out delicious buns for 40 cents each, but I get that it fits in with their philosophy of re-envisioning otherwise workaday eats. Our table contained aficionados so we had no doubt going with the classic ... it was aromatic, robust, and nuanced. While the portions are not for everyday, it's a fun place to take a skeptic.

Went here with my wife, my cousin, and her boyfriend on a tip that this was going to be the best burger I've ever had, and I've eaten at In N Out on the west coast, so I was pretty excited. Â We all got the kale salad and some coconut cheese bread to share for starters, and both were really solid. Â I'm not usually a big coconut fan, but this bread was delicious. Â Then, the star of the meal, the burger. Â I got mine medium rare with blue cheese, and prepped myself for an amazing burger...which it was, but definitely not the best I've ever had. Â In N Out and Burger Bar in Las Vegas were both better without question. Â I probably won't be back, but not because of anything having to do with this place, simply because it's so out of the way from where I live.

Very chill spot. Cheap beers, friendly bartender that called calling me darlin (or was it hun? can't remember) and lovely backyard space. I'm amazed it wasn't more crowded on a Friday evening, but it is somewhat out of the way.
I am neither vegetarian or Â vegan but I love ordering from here because besides being healthy the food is both tasty and fresh. I am a big fan of the chik salad and their fresh juices.

$2.50 Falefel sandwich. Â  Warning: Â Don't go here if you are on a date. OK, Ok. Let's get this out of the way. It's not very "Astoria", that's for sure, but that doesn't mean it's not something that Astoria needed. I love the Sweet Afton. Friendly and fast service (even if the asking-names-thing felt a bit forced from my server) and delicious cocktails and food. The spicy cherry margarita is not f'ing around. It will burn the crap out of your mouth and make you want more in the same sweet sip. The pickle martini is salty heaven in a glass, with a spicy kick at the end that will make you it's slave. The red lemonade was so good I had 3 when I really only meant to have 1. Get the fried pickles. Don't even think about not getting them. The burger was amazing (got the Irish Cheddar and Bacon) but I felt the bacon was slightly too smoky for my tastes.. then again, it WAS a Sunday and I'd already had a LOT of bacon that day. The macaroni and cheese my boyfriend ordered, however, I couldn't stop eating. Plus the place looks good. The only complaint I had was that it was way too bright where I was sitting in the back.. they must have read my mind on that, though, 'cause the lights were appropriately dimmed. All in all, Sweet Afton is an awesome bar worth your time. So quit whining about the Brooklynization of Astoria and just go get a drink already.

Wonderful! I've been meaning to check this place out and figured, why not on St Pat's! Cozy, warm and Irish. Beautifully poured Guinness, and great food. Prices not bad, and honestly good fare. I was pleased to see the varied clientele at 6:30 on a Monday. Wait staff was plenty attentive and the owner seated us and even brought me a beer when he saw i was getting low! I will be back!

Came here for Christmas Eve dinner. Â We were Korean food novices and the staff did their best to keep us informed. Â The meal was exquisite. Â The sea urchin course was my favorite with multiple flavors amplifying the urchin. Â The raw scallop was incredible as well. Â I loved the wagyu beef too. Â I'd never had beef that tender before. One of our party was allergic to shellfish and the chef did a completely different menu for her. Â It was just as intricate and well thought out as the original tasting menu. I loved the ambiance and the feel of the restaurant- very classy but comfortable. Â  A very well priced wine list and the sommelier was helpful but not pushy. Â It was a pricey but memorable evening.

food: friend and I ordered the escargot, chicken liver/foie gras appetizers, lamb shank and duck confit for main. escargot was a bit on the salty side but very good nevertheless. chicken liver/foie gras was delicious and faultless. bread that came along with food from the Balthazar bakery was amazing, reminded me of the good old times in Paris. lamb shank was juicy tender and flavorful. duck confit, again a bit on the saltier side, but the duck was done to perfection, the meat peeled off of the bone so tenderly, and the bed of shrooms were heavenly. we also ordered a recommended glass of rose and red, which were quite tasty too, though I have forgotten their names. service: very attentive, knowledgeable and cute. That is the waiters. Then there were the female maitre d's. I bet most of these beautiful girls are very smart in what they do, but this one girl whom I asked for the checked coats was a f***ing airhead. we had show tickets that needed to get picked up, and the dumbf%$@ forgot.
