(not on the days that maitre d' works, yes i hold a grudge) yes, and I want to try the bakery goods!

Took me 4 trips to this place to finally be able to get a slice. First time: closed Second time: closed because of extreme weather(with what he charges Â for his pizza, you would think the place would have an A/C 3rd time: closed because they ran out of dough(never heard anything so ridiculous before) 4th time: woohoooo! Finally I got a slice, and the moment I took the first bite I couldn't help but laugh and think about that famous PT Barnum quote. The pizza was garbage. Burnt, well, actually, more like charred, tasteless and just not worth even a penny. Do yourself a favor, and go to John's on Â Bleeker, or any decent pizzeria in Brooklyn(every neighborhood has at least half a dozen of them) and stay away from this shithole.

Doesn't at all live up to the hype. Small, sweaty, and pretentious. Got a drink and an app at the bar. It looked pretty disorganized back there, and the service was not great. The foie gras donut leaves much to desire. The donut was more like bread, and the jelly totally overpowers the foie gras. Could you get any more ironic than a gastropub inside a former Indian bakery that was in a Biggie video? Hipster Heaven.

Wait staff and bartender were knowledgeable, nice and actually acted like they wanted to be there - and wanted you there. Â Such a departure from most NY places. It's a "grown up" place -- kind of reminded me of a place you'd take your parents when they came to visit you at college. Â The food was good, if not life-altering.

Charming ambiance definitely make the tiny tables acceptable. Came for lunch with two others, one person was gluten free. Not too many gf options but made due with the soup of the day which was very yummy. I had the poached eggs with kale, very delicious, albeit very small portions (1 poached egg). All in all, small portions but very flavorful and delicious and the ambiance is ideal.
Leuke gezellige tent. Het gedeelte in de serre was niet bezet, dus vonden wij niet gezellig. Maar in het vaste gedeelte prima. Genoten van een heerlijke pizza en een Italiaans biertje. Aanradertje!!

Get ready for a wait...but well worth it. Â This great gluten free place is everything a celiac could want. Â Pizza and breadsticks. Â Need i say more? Â I have eaten here about 3 times so far and have loved everything I have ordered (in addition to everything my guests ordered). Â They have so many gluten free options...I could eat here everyday. Â Love love love!!!

this is really gooood bbq! worth the train ride from mahattan and walking those creepy streets it works like this: you order the meat by the weight and some sides then pay. there's a separate counter for drinks. tables are first come, first serve. if you're from hawaii skip the pulled pork-- it tastes just like kalua but w/o the smoke. the brisket, though, is insane and the ribs are just as good so be sure to order those (esp the brisket-- it was sooo tender!) we also ordered the sausage but i didn't care for it. Â we didn't have room for the pork belly but that's ok, we can get the korean kine in hawaii too, lol! a modest tray set us back $40 but it was worth every bite and we had a side of beans (it wasn't my favorite-- very strong tasting and more on the salty side) and german potato salad. the potato salad was crazy good though and i could have eaten another serving but i was just too full! we were lucky-- went on a drizzly day so there wasn't a line but it did get packed once we left. go early so you can get a table.
Really delicious burger,good for quick lunch, nice place.

The food was very good. The service was perfect. Everything was truly farm to table. Very enjoyable environment. We would definitely go back. I am very fussy and this is definitely a thumbs up are as most of his restaurants.

This is a cute little wine bar in The Village - I find the decor a bit bizarre, but the food, service, and wine were all great. They pour LARGE glasses of wine, which I love. The food is quite good: we had the beet salad, the onion and goat cheese ball (fantastic) and oysters. The bartenders are all friendly and very knowledgable about the wine and the food.

With Warren's mother in town for the Westminster Dog Show, and always presenting an interest in this place, we thought that it was the perfect time to check out Gramercy Tavern. It was a Saturday night, and after a couple of drinks at The Maritime Hotel's La Bottega Caffe, we jumped into a cab and booked it over to the Tavern at a time we thought would be reasonable to get a seat - we opted for the Tavern, instead of the dining room (where reservations are required). Once we entered, I was met by a very nice hostess who said that our table would be about two hours. Â Not to be perturbed (usually the wait times are much less), I saddled up to the bar to get us a couple of drinks that I was able to take back to the foyer and the one, lone table that we quickly snatched up. I noticed that the bar was packed, and after having some difficulty getting an arm in, a bartender immediately noticed me and took my order. Â I noticed that a lot of couples were eating at the bar - something that would probably be for the best if you were just a party of two. After about an hour of waiting, our table opened up and we were escorted into the Tavern. The Tavern (I did not see the dining room, so this is really only for the front part of the restaurant) was large with sweeping murals, flower arrangements overflowing their pots, water cans, and old, antique barrels, and bronze, candlelit scones that hung from all the walls and ceilings. Â It was dark, cozy, and immediately American. The service was fast, attentive, and the server easy to answer any questions that we may have had about the menu. I started with 5 oysters on the half shell. Â While I am not sure what variety of the oyster was I had, I knew it had to be from the East Coast - the flavor was both brine-y and smooth. Â It felt like I was eating the ocean. For my entree, I ordered the Red Snapper with braised squid, leaks and heirloom beans. Â The Snapper was cooked to perfection and the squid was sliced into long, tiny strings that almost acted as noodles in the white wine broth. Â The broth was so amazing, that I could have had that for a soup and have been satisfied. To finish off the meal, I had a glass of amaretto, on the rocks, that came in the most precious miniature wine goblet. If you are ever in the mood for a most wondrous and excessively delicious meal, than I highly suggest the Gramercy Tavern.

A-MA-ZING! Today was my second visit to Beyond Sushi and I think an addiction is developing. I've tried the Spicy Mang, Might Mushroom (my current favorite) and the Haricat. The flavors go extremely well together and the sauce they incorporate into each roll is divine. I'm not a vegan foodie but this place is beyond vegan and sushi, it's just damn good food. It'The location is awesome and the restaurant itself is very clean, has friendly staff and plays great music! A good spot to go with friends and a date. :-) Â Def a must try!

I had been meaning to try Hanco's for a while. Then I heard the piece on them on "this american life" and was compelled to try them out. Sadly I wasn't very impressed. Perhaps I had unfair hype/expectation that skewed my opinion. I got the classic and thought the texture of the meat was a little strange. The flavour was just ok. I think Nicky's makes a much better sandwich.

Amazing in every way. Â It takes a lot to get me to log in to yelp and actually review, but I just had to do if for Salinas. Definitely worth the hype. We went on a Saturday and the wait was about an hour, but they bring out little goodies for you while you wait. The French toast is fantastic, and even more fantastic are all of their flavored butters. The cherry lime rickey is delicious as well. Love!

I think this place is a solid a 4.5. Went here on mothers day 2014 and the wait was short and they seem to be efficient on rotating tables. The place is relaxed and a little tired looking. They did have an ample waiting room. We tried the house wine which was ok. I heard it might of been homemade but I couldn't tell or it could of been box. Downside here is there is no bar and no liquor. I like a drink when out and so a half point deduction. But drinks aside we are here for the food. Starting with the clams they were good but nothing more at $ 21 for an order of is 12 kind of a rip off at almost 2 dollars each for a small tiny clam. I could of had oysters at that price duh! I was impressed that the chicken was crispy and moist. It included sausage peppers onions and potatoes. Very well executed. I will definitely return to try other menu items.
If you're looking for something different, go here. Â The food is pretty good. Â But don't expect even close to a bargain. Â They're a bit pricy and cash only

Best Vietnaemse in NY. I know that's not a high bar, but this place is very much an outlier.

This was my second time here...I thoroughly enjoyed both visits and should have written a review after the first dinner. Â I would be remiss if I didn't write one now. Â Had a late night dinner there last night. Â A party of 10 at 10:30pm. Â The restaurant was more than accommodating despite the kitchen closing at 11pm. Â  As my friends and I normally do, we ate "family style", so we can try lots of goodies...and goodies did we try. Â First, we weren't really drinking because we just came from the Red Lion; however, I couldn't resist ordering the Dirty Jane. Â If you are a dirty martini lover, this drink is for you. Â I'd return to the restaurant just to have more of those. Â It was a perfect martini. Â Well blended and deliciously tart. Â  Now the food...I'll focus on our dinner from this visit (last visit I had the mussels, which were wonderful...if you're looking for classically cooked mussels in a white wine sauce, you will not be disappointed with this choice). Â Last night, we sampled the goat cheese flatbread (I could've ordered another 3 of those and still not have had enough, it was that good), the toasted ricotta gnocchi (everything, and I mean everything that you want gnocchi to be, creamy, rich, and melts in your mouth), crab cakes (well-seasoned, tangy and paired well with the chopped salad topping), pumpkin risotto (perfectly cooked with just the right amount of creamy sauce...with bacon!), the Jane burger (decadent even without the cheese), and rosemary fries (to die for). If you're ever in this neighborhood and want a drink (stop in for the Dirty Jane) or are hungry for some good eats....pick anything off the menu...seems like you're safe no matter what you order.

The service here is top-notch. Â The guys who served us were awesome; super down to earth, reliable, friendly, and at our every request. Â Among the best service I have ever gotten anywhere. Every dish we ordered was good - I have salad every day, and yet I found the arugula different and perfectly seasoned. The mixed seafood with lobster came in a huge portion and everything was delicious and flavorful. For dessert, we shared the family style strawberry shortcake which was more than enough to feed 6 of us, especially after a meal here. This place offers great value for large groups and I would definitely come back to try some of the other dishes! I would strongly recommend reservations. It was so nice to walk in and here, "come this way, your table is ready"

Me and my partner were looking for a nice place to make our wedding reception party. As soon as we got there we met the manager Giuseppe , he offered us few options of brunch with unlimited drinks. The brunch was phenomenal , the prentation was amazing and the food was delicious and fresh... like no other Italian places I've dined. The service was great and every few min there was someone that came to the table to ask if we need anything. The food that was served was in a tapas style and we got more than we paid for. The place itself Â was very clean and tastefully decorated.....nice lighting, amazing for pics. The sad part was that the two and half hours went so fast and I had to call it a day.

At the recommendation of Yelp, I went here today for lunch. Â I really love it when Yelp gets it right! The restaurant is very casual and spacious with a charming, bucolic wood motif. Â I was instantly at ease, and I found the service to be very attentive. For the appetizer, I opted for the Roti Telur which is a pastry shell filled with egg and onions and served with a curry chicken dipping sauce. Â I have to admit, that did not sound very promising. Â The waiter even informed me of the ingredients and tried to make sure if that is what I really wanted. Â I said yes, and I ended up being very happy with the choice. Â They were like bureks for vegetarians. Â They were very tasty in their own right, but the dipping sauce was just incredible. Â Rich, creamy, full in flavor -- I loved this. Â  For the entree, I had the curried beef with rice, which I was informed was equivalent to the much praised beef rendang at half the price. Â Fine, make me spend less money for the same food! Â There are only so many ways to endear me, but that's one of them. Â The stewed beef was very tasty and flavorful and was served with a very healthy portion of rice and some sliced cucumbers. Â The beef was not spicy or hot which was unfortunate because there would have been this very natural counterbalance with the cucumber. Â Nonetheless, this was a great dish as well. In every way this place exceeded my expectations. Â It easily merits 4 stars. Â But does it merit 5? Â I honestly never been to a strictly Malaysian restaurant before. Â I have seen Malaysian food at Indian restaurants and at Asian fusion restaurants. Â But given the niche nature of this cuisine and how good it was, I will go ahead and give it 5 stars, keeping in mind I am judging it among restaurants in its own class.

Its the burrito box, and they come in foil in a little tray, and the restaurant is a little bit bigger than a refrigerator box. I saw a couple guys stuffing face around lunchtime during a jog, which prompted me to stop by to grab a grilled chicken burrito for dinner. Shoulda checked yelp to see that they deliver, because i stood there for a while waiting for my food with what must have been half of the 2 Train. Not bad with the pricing though, and it was a pretty good burritto. I'd stop through again.

3.5 stars. Â Tasty, cool concept, but a little expensive for what it is and not quite crave-worthy. I ordered the Vietnamese pineapple and sweet mango chutney sauces, layered. Â Layering the sauces is cheaper and tastes good, but super messy. Â I may get sauces on the side in the future. I really wish they had more seating inside. Â The closest park is Tompkins Square, but it's at least a 10 min walk where your fries are cooling down. Â The smallest size is also definitely big enough for sharing - which is cool if you're sharing, but a bit unnecessary if you're by yourself (or visiting Pommes Frites after eating a meal). Â Overall, I like Pommes Frites, but it's not a place I'd go out of my way for.
hot popovers with honey and crunchy salt with every meal --- need i say more?? Â always good food here and a good time. Â they've been able to keep their quality up over the years, which is nice.

Peppinos in Park Slope is a friendly restaurant that makes very good brick oven pizza. The crust is exceptional if you like thin crusted pizza. The other ingredients were also quite good though we thought the sauce was a little too light and watery. All the serve staff made us feel welcome. It is a nice place for a midweek dinner.

I have never liked falafel, period. Â That being said, this place is in-****ing-credible! Â Falafel never tasted like this before and I could eat this anytime. Â Went with two friends and tried a lot of menu items. Â For the best first time experience I would suggest the falafel platter, which gives you a sampling of the three types. Â All of the other food was delicious as well. ONLY downside to this restaurant is the size. Â Very small place with just a couple bench seats. Â Other than that, it is an incredible middle eastern food experience.

Oh, how I love this place! I can always depend on this diner for my very late cravings after a long night out or even for dinner. The food is always good (the fries are great) and there is a nice wine and beer menu if you just want desert. The place was nothing special before the remodeling, but now Sanford's resembles a posh lounge instead of a local diner. The service is always excellent, but perhaps this is because I am a familiar face here. This will remain my spot, pre-party and post-party. I have lots of good memories here. One of the top diners in Queens, in my opinion.

If you arrive after 6PM, you're getting a table 4 hours later. Â Just know what you're signing up for here. Â The pizza is delicious, and I love that it's BYOB. Â The plate of extra sauce is a phenomenal idea. Â Once you get seated, the experience is great! Â They'll bring out one pie at a time so that the second (and third, and fourth) don't get soggy on your table. Â Restaurant is not too loud, and service is quite efficient. Â Can't wait to come back.

Went to Butcher Bar this weekend for dinner with a friend. We were quickly sat at a table, but the host soon realized that the table had been set aside for a party of four who were waiting. He came back and told us and was very apologetic, so we got up and went out front to wait. No big deal. They apparently have a backyard that isn't open for customers, but the host told us we could wait there if we'd prefer. We were fine out front, so we stayed there. After about five or ten minutes we got a new table. We split corn cakes and honey butter, which were delicious. I also tried the corn cakes with the original bbq sauce they had at the table, which was unusual, but it worked. I also got mac and cheese, which was even better. Perfectly cheesy and creamy. Then, I had the 50/50, a sandwich of half brisket, half pulled pork. It was fantastic. Again, I added the original sauce, which went very well with both meats. All the food was great and I had completely forgotten about the mixup earlier, but they hadn't. One of the butchers, who appeared to be in charge, came over and asked us how our food was and apologized for the inconvenience. He then insisted on giving us something for free to make up for it. We couldn't decide what to get, so he suggested ribs. A few minutes later, another butcher showed up with two ribs. He actually was bringing four, but dropped two. A couple minutes after, the first butcher was back with a plate of pulled pork to make up for the lost ribs. Both were outstanding. I then had a piece of apple pie, which was good, but forgettable. I'll probably skip it next time. Overall, great food, great service. There was an unfortunate mixup at the beginning, but everyone was friendly and they went out of their way to make up for it. I hope to be back very soon.

This is my favorite place. I come here 3/4 times a week. If I have a date, it's ngam curry. If my friends are visiting me, it's ngam pad thai. After working out, nothing sooths me like the beet ravioli. This is my HQ and I feel like I want to keep it to myself. Drop by and say hi- i'll be there.

This place awesome! I can't believe I hadn't been here prior, I live right by the place. Will be coming back often for sure. The brisket is I think the best brisket I've had in NYC, and I've been to most of the BBQ spots in the city. The Mac and cheese is ofcourse other worldly, it's the same guy who owns elbow room in Barclays. Had the collards which were also excellent. And the corn, make sure you squeeze the lime on the corn, its crazy good. My new favorite spot in the neighborhood for sure. Easy five stars.
Bumped into this place with my girlfriend. Very romantic atmosphere and classy... Definitely not your typical diner. The food here was great and the service was very nice!

Unfortunately I have to go against the grain with a review that most others will scoff at, as my experience attempting to eat here was so despicable I feel obliged to post it for others to read. Showed up at 6pm to a full restaurant. No big deal, it's a popular time for dinner. So we wait at the door, nobody but one girl working the place. Ok, it'll be slow. Eventually after 5 minutes of feeling like a fool, 3 more groups of people have crowded in behind. Finally the young woman working decides to come over and take down names... she looks at everyone and says "Who is next?" As any normal person would say who was standing at the front of the line for a while, "I was." She then looks past us and says "You were next" to the people behind us. Then she proceeds to ignore our responses saying "No, we were." She then takes down names for the people behind them before getting back to us... 3 groups are now ahead of us on the seating list, who showed up after and were standing behind us. Why? I have no idea. Giving them the benefit of the doubt, they showed up and returned with more people. Had this been communicated, I'd still be just as mad but could understand the situation. What does this mean for me as a potential customer? I could care less because I will never step foot in this place again. If you do decide to come here based on positive food reviews and are greeted with a full restaurant, do yourself a favor and choose any of the other great places around here.

I was in the neighbornood this morning and decided to drop by Petite Abeille for breakfast.....i literally walked right pass it without realizing. that is not about their food, i only had a latte, which was pretty descent. 2 stars for their hospitality department. i went there last sun (5/30). those women behind the counter were not a bit friendly. they didn't say hello when i stepped in; no thank you when i paid and left a tip. do i ask for too much? do they deserve tip for making a latte?

Pretty good chicken fingers. I tried the "naked" aka grilled ones.

It is hard to recall this precious Italian eatery as one thumbs through the Rolodex that is Batali's culinary corporation. While the diminutive restaurant on Thompson boasts an excellent menu, space is often limited. Consequently, one may find themselves propped up at the bar making their way through Roman courses that pleasingly exhibit a clever New York perspective. Mozzarella di Bufala with leeks, paired with a glass of white, served with soft, warm bread that's coddled in olive oil and fragrant leeks is a delicious way to begin your dinner. Cavatelli with octopus and calamari make way for chewy pasta immersed with the piquancy of the sea. Surprisingly, the duck at Lupa is exemplary, the skin particularly crisped, reminiscent of what makes for a prized Peking duck. Balsamic, apples, and potatoes, paired beautifully with the moist bird. Batali's always been a huge proponent of the employment of olive oil in desserts. At Otto his olive oil gelato is distinguished. At Lupa, an olive oil torta ushers olive oil's fluency as a fragrant liaison between fruit and cake.

I have ordered and sat at this place many times. Their order time is super fast. They got me my order in 20 minutes. Portions are nice and big, ingredients are fresh and delicious. This place is all-around wonderful. The interior is beautiful - urban but warm and cozy. The drinks are quality and there are reasonable wines by the bottle. The menu has lots of great choices - can definitely recommend the pÃ¢tÃ©, orecchiette, and prosciutto & arugula pizza. Enjoy!

Food to order for brunch: (to see photos go to my profile and click on the link to my blog) -Shrimp and Grits: Creamy Parmesan Grits with Shrimp Scampi & Poached Eggs -Smoked Trout Potato Hash: Bell Pepper. I'm going to agree with some general points made in other reviews: Â it's often quite busy, the staff aren't ever-present, it's cash only, and it might not be uber-authentic. Bottom line: Â It's not destination Thai, but if you want something reasonably well done and value priced, it's hard to complain if a place like this is around the corner.

I cannot wait to go back here! I usually go to Sea for thai but this has become my fav thai place now. The calamari was not good but the red curry pot, drunken noodles and another noodle dish my dad ordered was seriously good. The waiters are attentive. Lobster Joint - let's get married and have kids? Okay? Rarely do I actually venture out to Brooklyn, especially Greenpoint, given it can be quite a trek without a car. But fortunately for me, I had my fellow yelper John C drive me out there. When you first walk in, the atmosphere is extremely casual. You walk up to the counter, order what you like, they hand you a number sign and you sit wherever you like. Fortunately for us, we came in when it was relatively empty - five minutes later, the whole place was jam packed. Â We felt the Lobster Gods were looking out for us. I would say that I found the Lobster Roll to be disappointing in comparison to Luke's Lobster or Red Hook - likely because of the bread, and the lobster meat itself didn't taste that fresh. But the rest of the food well made up for it and allows me to give these five stars. The Mac N Cheese had the perfect amount of creaminess and had large chunks of lobster, while the clam steamers were fresh and steamed perfectly. I really liked the clam chowder as it wasn't super chunky and creamy - it was a little more watered (but not in a bad way) - it didn't leave you so stuffed and bloated that you didn't want to eat anything else. All in all, a great Sunday dinner.

After all the hype I had heard about Eataly, and all the positive reviews I have read, I was left feeling very unimpressed and would NOT go back. Â The best way I can describe my experience is overpriced, overcrowded, and sub par food. Â All in all, for an appetizer and two main course (no drinks) all of which were on the small size, it cost $75. Delicious and amazing.

Came here for lunch on my birthday recently and was sadly disappointed. I've always wondered about this place as my gym is nearby. I was really excited when I was researching this place right before we left for lunch, their decor (dark and brooding) was very old school and seem to suggest an awesome drinking place. When we got there, the hostess said they were all booked up and only had the bar tables, we were cool with that, and was seated. They decorated the place really well and was all Christmased up. It definitely seemed like a great place to drink as I repeat... Our waitress greeted us and took our order. I asked about their old fashion and she assured me they make a mean one. My coworker ordered a st Germain cocktail. For food, we ordered the meatballs, beets salad and the lamb chops. We didn't want to eat too much and the waitress mentioned that the entere was a decent portion to share. Pretty good so far, however this is only the beginning. We waited over twenty minutes for our drinks, which never came. Finally, a bus boy came over to deliver our meatballs. I took a bite and it was cold, also it was four tiny meatballs in a big dish. Kind of disappointing because reviews spoke well of them and if they actually came out hot, they wouldn't have been too bad. We reached out to speak to the hostess since we were sat so closed to her and because we haven't seen our waitress since she took our ordered. We explained that our meatballs were cold and that we still haven't seen our drinks and it has been over a half an hour now. Hostess explained that they only had two waitress and apologized. For a place that is all booked up, why are u shorthanded in staff? We also noticed that there was only one bartender. Manager came over shortly and apologized and took back the meatballs, we asked for the sampler instead because four tiny meatballs are not enough. Our waitress finally showed up with our drinks and a mini dirty look. Our salad and sampler platter finally came and it wasn't too bad. The sampler definitely was a better choice! Afterward our lamp chops were served and to our surprised there were three lamb chops. Pretty nice and they were delicious. Waitress came back to see if we wanted dessert and I was discourage to order in fear for how long it will take. However my coworker insisted since it's my birthday. We ordered the cheesecake, it wasn't too bad. When we finally got our check, the waitress came by tell us that they waived the dessert since it was my birthday and apologized for the wait. Although I might not be coming back here again, I have to say they definitely try to make up for their miscues. Their food weren't bad at all but I felt like they definitely needed to have more staff at lunch. For a place that not only serves the lunch crew of offices nearby and tourists, they definitely could manage their lunch time better. I had work that day and my lunch ran closed to three hours.

i have yet to find a better place for group dinners in manhattan than alta. huge menu of delicious tapas makes for a great communal experience, sharing each dish with everyone at the table. and the super yummy and really strong sangria only enhances the "communal experience." we sat in the "attic" which was weird at first because we walked upstairs and literally through the kitchen into this tiny loft-like space with just a few other tables. cozy and intimate and loud, i imagine, if you're sitting amongst loud people (like my friends). also, we had this really bizarre waitress who made intense eye contact with everyone at the table without ever breaking a smile. it was actually more humorous than annoying as the night went on because she was just so miserable. I've been here for drinks before on a Thursday night and I've got to say, I kind of like the crowd. Â People seem nice, not too annoying, yet fun. The decor is odd to say the least - randomly placed ceramic spotted pigs, but somehow it works. Â I came back to sample their lunch under the persuasion of one of my friends.. From the appetizers I tried the chicken liver toasts, deviled eggs and "roll mops" (pickled herring). Â The roll mops were the great! Â I wouldn't have thought so, but it wasn't fishy nor slimy at all. Â Very flavorful and refreshing. Â The deviled eggs were just ok. Â The chicken liver toasts were excellent - but it's definitely a heart attack on a plate. Â One bite should be enough. I got the famous Spotted Pig burger and was royally disappointed. Â It looks grand and portion is enormous, but it was just a facade. I asked for it medium, but I think it was like rare. Â Not even rare. It was still like ground meat straight from the butcher. Â Don't people usually order on the rare side b/c they want those juices following between the bun? Â Not this, it was just bright pink ground meat with no flavor and not that much juice. Â There's a heavy load of roquefort cheese on the thick burger that made it WAY too salty. Â The cheese just sort of got in the way. Â  The fries are the extra skinny kind - like potato match sticks with rosemary and too much salt. Â I'm a steak fries - tater tots - curly fries kind of girl so these extra skinny fries didn't interest me much. Â You have to stick a whole fistful in your mouth to get any sort of substance. Â Not very ladylike. I only had like 3 bites of the burger and 7 potato sticks and I decided I was no longer interested.

Stopped by here after visiting the MET on a Saturday evening. It was pretty packed but we were able to snag a table. Beers are anywhere from $7-$9 depending on the type Okay now the food: Fried Pickles 5/5 : It was an entire whole pickle fried vs the sliced up kind with a side of jalapeno mayo. Not sure how but it somehow tasted light and delicious versus heavy and fatty. Fresh, fried deliciousness! Mussels 4/5: The sauce was perfect not to salty with pork belly, garlic and pure delighfulness. The biscuit was more of a spongy consistency which is not my fave and the mussels while ample in amount were tiny. Sausage 3/5: The sausage tasted fresh and was served with three different mustard sauces, a mound of fries and sauerkraut. The only downside was it was a bit dry Mac and Cheese Side 5/5: hands down one of the best. Piping hot and stayed hot and melty the entire time served on a hot skillet crispy on the top and melty goodness as you ate further. ample serving size as well. PROS: variety, ambience, reasonable drink prices CONS: some dishes are not worth the price tag

After some drinks with friends, I wanted to grab a quick dinner to bring home and enjoy in front of the television. Â I stopped at Ellary's Greens after discovering the healthy and interesting menu online earlier that same week. Â I walked in and smiled at the wooden dÃ©cor that made me feel like I was in a treehouse. Best falafel i've ever had. Only a few seats though and the lines can be very long. Definitely worth it for the taste and price though.

Amazing place to have a quick lunch. Music in the shop should change though, hard techno is not our favorite when you have to queue ten minutes in a warm smelly place! Except from that, lovely food and correct prices

So I heard a lot about this place "It's the oldest pizza place in the US... " "It's always jammed pack etc..." "The best pizza in the world... " The first two statements are probably true. Not sure about the third. Don't get me wrong, I really liked it. Their pizza was fantastic! In my opinion it's just not the best in the world...

This place is a solid 3.5 stars. The decor is fantastic. So perfect for this time of year; it's cozy and feels like you ended up in a New England cottage in some other time in history. I had the roasted pork belly with a side of mashed potatoes. The potatoes could have used SOMETHING on them; salt or garlic or rosemary. It was completely flavorless. All the tables around us changed patrons twice throughout the duration of our dinner, and we were never approached. Also-- the crowd kinda sucks and was very uptight. It was actually quite an interesting phenomenon. Way too white for me lol. And I'm pretty white. But seriously, guys. Time to relax and enjoy dinner with friends-- Not berate the staff about wine choices and having them stand there while you taste cabs you know nothing about. You're 18 years old. Stop it. Your friends are rolling their eyes, too. I almost want to give this place 4 stars now simply because I felt bad for the wait staff.
Really good food.. I'm coming to eat here again.... Love the food..... Reminds me India!!!!!!!

Thank god that Astoria has place like this one.Quality ingredients,great bread,great selections of artisan cheeses and creativity is the wining formula.Hidden gem!
Affordable and authentic Japanese food

I've been here a couple of times, our go to place for thai in Park Slope. It's affordable, big portion size and tasty. Although , the last time I was here, I had a slight tummyache. Maybe it's not them. At least I like to believe it's not them.

Fresh organic menu which changes regularly! The drinks are fantastic and the brunch is divine. I highly recommend you make a reservation. Showing up can leave you waiting 45 minutes. Getting a reservation here is not hard

The fried chicken was simply put...the BEST I've EVER had!!! The local catch was HORRIBLE!!!! It tasted disgusting and repulsive. As if it should have been taken out with the trash 3 days prior to my arrival. I arrived with my daughter and her boyfriend as they were preparing to open. The staff was very friendly and inviting. We order the and pork belly with egg and cucumber for appetizers, and they were both awesome. Don't know how you can go wrong with pork belly, and the cucumber was served with crispy flakes on top and a special sauce. Stuck with the original ramen for dinner. A little bit expensive for what it is and how much you can get it for elsewhere, but very filling nonetheless. Also, servers here treat you like you're part of the assembly line. Appetizers shot out within minutes of ordering them, and were taken away the second the last piece was finished. Understand its a crowded restaurant and they're trying to hustle everyone through, but its almost too efficient.

Favorite tapas place in the city, hands down! Definitely a smaller place so I wouldn't recommend groups large than 4 people and definitely call ahead! Must try: + patatas bravas + croqueta del dia + garbanzos fritos + gambas al ajillo -- ask for extra bread to soak up the garlicky olive oil goodness, TRUST! + plato de quesos variados The specials we tried that night were: + brussel sprouts sauteed with serrano ham (the words "I need more brussel sprouts" had never been uttered by the likes of me until that night.) + woolly pig ham with pan con tomate The rebujito sangria is amazing with subtle notes of chamomile!

One word: Addict I went from never having a falafel in my life, to having withdraws if I go long periods w/o one of these bad boys. If you decide to try one, proceed w/ caution (esp. if you don't live in NY or tri-state area, bc you may consider coming back, just for the food here...seriously!) For such a hyped burger, the Black Label is unassuming. It stares at you, resembling a burger that you'd get for half the price at a sports bar. Â There is no foie gras, truffles, bleu cheese, or any other bells and whistles that would visibly justify the $26 price tag. Just a decent-sized thick beef patty on a brioche bun topped with caramelized onions and a mound (and I mean a hill) of beautiful frites on the side. I left the burger unadorned without any ketchup and took a bite: I did not hear angels singing that night but instead tasted a juicy, perfectly cooked dry-aged beef patty that melted in my mouth. Â The caramelized onions were like a jam that provided a not-too-sweet condiment for the fatty beef. Â However, the bun was a bit too weak for the meat as it started to fall apart about 4 bites in. Was it a unique burger worth trying once? Yes. Would I prefer that dry-aged beef in steak form instead? More often than not. But as I realized on my visit, Minetta Tavern is more than just a place with a ridiculously jammed bar scene and the $26 burger. They do onion jams very well, as in the one that complemented and almost overshadowed the bone marrow appetizer with toasted baguette points. They also do wonders with the potato: aside from their addictive frites, we ordered a side of pommes anna, which are scalloped potatoes cooked in duck fat. Their decadence made the fries taste like celery sticks and may have come close to justifying the additional $5 surcharge you incur if you want to substitute a different potato for the frites with the burger. Finally, I had the chance to look at different mains like the roasted chicken or the cote de boeuf on other tables, and they all made me want to return for a taste. Now if I could just find a way to get a table.

I was super excited to try Xixa - their sister restaurant Traif (just a few doors down) is my favorite restaurant in Brooklyn! It is a similar concept to Traif - small plates to share and combining flavors and styles that you would never think would work together, but they do and they do so deliciously. This Halal Cart defines what and how food should be cooked and served to a bunch of hungry and sometimes even intoxicated patrons after a night out in the city. Every ingredient just ties in together and makes sense -- from the rice, to the lamb, and to the sauces, it's all brilliant. I'm a huge fan and this will be a must go-to place on my next visit. Just an FYI, sometimes there is a line but it is completely worth it. For all you skeptics, don't expect gourmet or top quality food. Think of the target market this cart is trying to appeal to and then it'll make sense why they're so successful.
